items.title: PhD position in biomineralization of digitally fabricated granular materials
items.desc: Mission We are offering a challenging position as a full-time (100%) PhD Student in the Laloui Group at EPFL inLausanne. The group brings expertise in geomaterials and their mechanical behaviour to research at theinterface of material science and engineering applications. You will work on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)-funded project “DFabuLis: Digital FabricationUsing Living Systems”, conducted in collaboration between Dr. Dimitrios Terzis, Senior Scientist in the LalouiGroup at EPFL, and co-PI Prof. Benjamin Dillenburger of the Chair of Digital Building Technologies at ETHZurich. The project investigates how biologically driven mineralization can transform demolition and excavationmaterials into materials suitable for digital fabrication under ambient conditions. Digital fabrication methods, including extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying, offer opportunities to controlmaterial placement and curing, create complex geometries and reduce material consumption. Integratingbiomineralization into pumpable, extrudable and sprayable granular materials remains largely unexplored. ThisPhD will investigate the coupled biogeochemical, rheological and mechanical mechanisms governing particledeposition, mineral precipitation and hardening. Main duties and responsibilities As a PhD Student, you will be expected to: Take full responsibility for your dissertation and the progress of your research. Conduct research in close collaboration with project partners at EPFL and ETH Zurich and, whereapplicable, industry partners. Design and execute experiments, and analyze and interpret experimental results. Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present your findings at internationalconferences. Participate in teaching and supervise student projects. More specifically, within this project, you will: Investigate the rheology and processability of granular materials, including yield stress, plastic viscosity,thixotropy, water content, ageing and particle interactions. Study microbial activity and biologically driven mineral precipitation, and determine how evolving mineralphases affect mechanical hardening and material performance. Characterize the coupling between biogeochemical reactions, rheological properties and mechanicalbehaviour over space and time. Connect experimental findings to extrusion 3D printing and robotic spraying in collaboration with thedigital fabrication team at ETH Zurich. Profile An MSc degree in Civil Engineering, Materials Science and Engineering, Chemical Engineering or aclosely related discipline. A background in mechanics and the strength of solid materials, or materials science applied to the builtenvironment, is particularly welcome. Experience in rheology, granular or cementitious materials, experimental mechanics, materialcharacterization, geomechanics, mineralogy, or organic and inorganic chemistry is an advantage.Expertise across all these fields is neither expected nor required. Interest in experimental and interdisciplinary research, and in translating fundamental physical andchemical understanding into new construction technologies. Good communication skills and willingness to work as part of a team across disciplines and institutions. Enthusiasm, scientific curiosity, eagerness to learn, good organizational skills and rigor in experimentalwork. A high level of motivation for academic research. Fluency in English is essential. We offer At EPFL, we believe that people achieve great results when they feel supported, respected and enabled tosucceed. By joining our community, you will help shape the future of society through education, research andinnovation. We offer an inspiring, international and collaborative environment where your work has real impact and your ideas are valued. Combined with flexible ways of working and attractive employment conditions, weaim to create an environment where everyone can contribute, grow and make a difference. Beyond work, our campuses host a vibrant community and unique environment, enriched by initiativespromoting equality, inclusion, diversity, well-being and sustainability as well as an engaging program ofcultural, sports and community activities throughout the year. Read about our employment conditions and employee benefits. Informations The selection process involves multiple stages, and short-listed candidates will be requested to apply to aspecific EPFL Doctoral Program to qualify for a PhD at EPFL, (EDME doctoral program). Please check this page for additional information on admission. Please note that this is a separate application process necessary to be eligible to complete your PhD at EPFL. items.title: SNSF-funded PhD position in lipid metabolism
items.desc: Dysregulation of lipid metabolism plays a key role in development and progression of metabolic disorders including obesity, type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We are seeking a highly motivated and talented PhD candidate to join our multidisciplinary research team to investigate underlying mechanism associated to dysregulation of lipid metabolism in MASLD. The project aims to elucidate the mechanistic role of lipid signaling molecules in driving hepatic inflammation and fibrosis, and to identify novel therapeutic intervention. items.title: PhD Position in Accounting
items.desc: Department of Business Administration PhD Position in Accounting 60 % Start of employment : August 2027, temporary The University of Zurich invites applications for a fully funded PhD position in Accounting. The accounting group takes a rigorous, economics-based approach to research, and doctoral students are admitted to the group as a whole rather than to an individual supervisor. Applications are welcome from candidates interested in all areas of accounting, including but not limited to: Financial accounting, disclosure, and capital markets Managerial accounting, performance measurement, and incentives Corporate governance and accounting Disclosure regulation, sustainability, and real effects Interdisciplinary research at the intersection of accounting, economics, and finance All methodological approaches are welcome: analytical, archival, experimental, and field-based. Your responsibilities The appointment is at 60%. It is a salaried position, not a partial stipend. The program combines the doctoral student's own research with a rigorous international education in accounting research. The first year is devot-ed primarily to foundational coursework. From the second year, doctoral students develop their own research under close faculty supervision, alongside advanced courses and limited teaching duties, which consist of supporting courses and examinations. The program is academically oriented: it prepares students for faculty positions at leading universities and for research-oriented careers at international organizations. The position is based in an international accounting group whose research includes financial accounting and capital mar-kets, corporate governance, disclosure regulation, and sustainability. The group comprises Prof. Hui Chen, Prof. David Oesch, Prof. Evgeny Petrov, and Prof. Thomas Rauter, and it continues to grow. Doctoral students are integrated into the group's research from the start and present their work in internal and external seminars. What the position offers: Funding for the duration of the doctorate, with a salary in accordance with the University of Zurich salary scale for doctoral candidates Structured doctoral training and close supervision Financial support to present research at international conferences Place of work in Zurich, with University support for appointees of all nationalities in obtaining Swiss resi-dence and work permits Your profile Required: a Master's degree in accounting, finance, economics, statistics, or a related quantitative field, completed by the start of the position. Candidates who expect to complete their degree by August 2027 are encouraged to apply. Required: an outstanding academic record, in particular in quantitative coursework. Required: strong spoken and written English. Knowledge of German and a language certificate are not re-quired. Optional: GMAT or GRE scores. Optional: prior research experience, which is an advantage. Information on your application Applications should be submitted as a single PDF containing a CV, academic transcripts, and a statement of purpose of at most two pages via the job portal. items.title: PhD Position SNSF Project"Beyond the Gig Economy:Exploring the New Frontiers of Algorithmic Control"
items.desc: Introduction UNIL is a leading international teaching and research institution, with over 5,000 employees and 17,000 students split between its Dorigny campus, CHUV and Epalinges. As an employer, UNIL encourages excellence, individual recognition and responsibility. unil.ch/work Presentation The Swiss Graduate School of Public Administration (IDHEAP) at the University of Lausanne invites applications for a PhD position in the "Information Management" research unit headed by Prof. Tobias Mettler. IDHEAP is the largest university institute in Switzerland dedicated entirely and exclusively to the public sector. We offer excellent research support in a dynamic public policy and public administration research community and are committed to promoting the careers of young scholars. Are you interested in the future of AI and the algorithmic state? Are you enthusiastic about developing research at the crossroads between Public Management and Information Systems? Join our research team in the project “Beyond the Gig Economy: Exploring the New Frontiers of Algorithmic Control”. The project examines the implications and different design alternatives of algorithms gradually replacing human decision-making. A core problem we will explore is how social norms can be encoded into algorithmic control while enabling meaningful exception handling. The ideal candidate is therefore sensitive to technical and social questions and interested in conducting challenging empirical work in a fast-moving environment. items.title: PhD position H/F - Assessing and Explaining Deep Learning Model Compression
Industrial PhD Student in AI
items.desc: INDUSTRIAL PHD STUDENT IN AI, Sundsvall Would you like to turn deep research into real impact in the factory, in our products and in the lives of the people who use them? At Permobil, we’re looking for game-changers to join us as we innovate for individuals and develop the world’s most advanced assistive solutions. At Permobil , the people who use our products come first. Our purpose is to create advanced assistive solutions that make the lives of adults and children living with disabilities more enriching. Our people are passionate about pushing the boundaries of technology to deliver innovations that improve lives. We are a sustainable and responsible business committed to continuous improvement, and our customers can trust us to provide market-leading solutions driven by insights-based clinical data. At Permobil in Sundsvall, we design and manufacture power wheelchairs and Panthera manual wheelchairs. Sundsvall is one of our largest and most modern sites, with production, R&D and clinical research side by side. About The Role Permobil is now establishing an industrial PhD position in artificial intelligence , in close collaboration with Mid Sweden University (Mittuniversitetet) . The position is part of a four-year research project and gives you the chance to do doctoral research with one foot in academia and one foot in a real industrial environment. As Industrial PhD Student, you will be employed by Permobil in Sundsvall and admitted to the doctoral program at Mid Sweden University. You will work with the large amounts of operational and product data that our organization generates every day, and build deep knowledge about how AI can create value from it for our operations, our products and the people who use them. The research problem is deliberately open. Rather than a narrowly defined task, you get room to explore, ask deeper questions and shape the research direction together with your academic supervisors and your colleagues at Permobil. Key Responsibilities Plan and carry out doctoral research in applied AI, and complete your doctoral studies and thesis within the project period, Define and refine the research questions together with your supervisors as the project evolves, Work with real operational and product data from Permobil and turn it into new knowledge, Develop, test and evaluate AI methods, and show how they perform in a real industrial setting, Take part in doctoral courses and in the research environment at Mid Sweden University, Publish and present your results at conferences and in journals, in dialogue with Permobil and in line with the project agreement, Share insights and build competence with colleagues in Operations, R&D, Clinical and other functions at the site. Skills & Qualifications Basic eligibility for doctoral studies: a degree at advanced level, or completed course requirements of at least 240 credits, of which at least 60 credits at advanced level, or equivalent knowledge acquired in Sweden or abroad, Specific eligibility: at least 90 credits in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or closely related subjects, Good command of English, spoken and written. Swedish is an advantage, Experience in machine learning, data analysis or industrial applications of AI is an advantage, but not a requirement, Comfortable working in an international company and in a cross-functional context. Who Are You You are curious, driven and goal-oriented, with a strong interest in turning research into practical value. You like to ask the deeper question rather than settle for the first answer, and you are comfortable moving between the data, the shop floor and the clinic. You create an environment where people feel safe to share ideas, challenge assumptions and learn together. You communicate clearly, collaborate effectively with others and take ownership of your work. You share our belief in respect for people and continuous improvement. What We Offer A rare opportunity for both technical and personal development: doctoral education at Mid Sweden University combined with work on real industrial and product data at one of Permobil’s most modern sites. You get close support from supervisors at both the university and Permobil, and the chance to see your research put to use in a company with a clear purpose and a strong belief in the future. Application Process We will conduct selection continuously so send us your application today or before 20th of November at the latest! The position is based in Sundsvall, with a project period of four years. Permobil is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals. For more information about the position, please contact Mikael Boija, Senior Director Operational Excellence, mikael.boija@permobil.com For information about the recruitment process, please contact Zivile Mitkute, Talent Acquisition Partner, zivile.mitkute@permobil.com Please respect that we do not wish recruitment assistance or advertising, we decline calls from recruitment and advertising providers. More About Permobil Permobil founder Dr. Per Uddén believed that helping people achieve the greatest level of independence is a basic human right and, for over 50 years, Permobil has held fast to that belief. Permobil is a global leader in advanced rehabilitation technology, passionate about better understanding our users’ needs and improving their quality of life through state-of-the-art healthcare solutions. Today, those solutions include power wheelchairs, seating and positioning products, power assist, and manual wheelchairs. Permobil is part of Patricia Industries, a subsidiary of Investor AB, and is headquartered in Sweden. Permobil has 2 000 team members in 18 countries around the world. items.title: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time. The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data. The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project. Responsibilities Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data. Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction. Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits. Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities. Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging. Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects. Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations. Qualifications You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English. To succeed in this position, you are expected to have: A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models. Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks. A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods. Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage: Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations. Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion. Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning. Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling. Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction. Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation. At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Hans Martin Kjer, hmkj@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 16 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Compute DTU Compute – Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science – is an internationally recognised academic environment with over 400 employees and 10 research sections. We broadly cover digital technologies within mathematics, data science, computer science, and computer engineering, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, internet of things (IoT), chip design, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, social networks, fairness, and data ethics. Our research is rooted in basic research and centres on mathematical models of the physical and virtual world, as a basis for the analysis, design, and implementation of complex systems. We focus on ensuring that our research results contribute to creating a better society by supporting areas such as health, green transition, energy supply, and life science. We collaborate with universities, public and private organisations, and companies in Denmark and abroad, and through DTU’s startup ecosystem, we encourage innovation and entrepreneurship. We have a strong ethical, human, and sustainable approach that ensures integrity in our work. Therefore, we strive for and take responsibility for driving the democratisation of digital technologies, so that everyone has the opportunity to actively participate in the development, and we ensure a continued open, democratic, and inclusive society for the benefit of all. At DTU Compute, we value diversity, inclusion, and a flexible work-life balance. Read more here: www.compute.dtu.dk . DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: Promotionsstelle an der UTN im Bereich Mathematische Optimierung für Multi-Roboter-Systeme (m/w/d)
items.desc: for english version, see below - Die Technische Universität Nürnberg (UTN) bietet eine inspirierende und interdisziplinäre Forschungsumgebung mit Zugang zu modernsten Ressourcen. Sie ist der ideale Ort, um zukunftsträchtige Entdeckungen zu machen und einen bedeutenden Beitrag zu spannenden Forschungsfeldern zu leisten. Promotionsstelle an der UTN im Bereich Mathematische Optimierung für Multi-Roboter-Systeme (m/w/d) Das Department Liberal Arts & Social Sciences bietet derzeit eine Promotionsstelle (vollfinanziert, 3 Jahre, 100 %, Vergütung nach TV-L E 13) in der von Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin geleiteten Analytics and Optimization Group an. Wir suchen eine hoch motivierte und qualifizierte Person zur Verstärkung unseres dynamischen und internationalen Forschungsteams. Die erfolgreiche Bewerberin bzw. der erfolgreiche Bewerber wird Teil eines interdisziplinären Forschungsteams, das neue Ansätze für Multi-Agent Path Finding in großen robotergestützten Lagersystemen entwickelt. Die Stelle ist im Bereich der mathematischen Optimierung angesiedelt und umfasst eine enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden aus Robotik und Business Intelligence. Sie forschen unter anderem zu gemischt-ganzzahliger Optimierung für Multi-Agent Path Finding, Optimierung unter Unsicherheit und optimierungsbasierter Konfliktlösung und bringen Ihre Expertise in mathematischer Optimierung in das interdisziplinäre Team ein. Die entwickelten Methoden werden sowohl in Simulationen als auch auf realen Robotersystemen evaluiert. Eine komplementäre, im Bereich Robotik angesiedelte Promotionsstelle wird in der von Prof. Dr. Wolfram Burgard geleiteten Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Group ausgeschrieben. Weitere beteiligte Forschungsgruppen sind die von Dr. Tanja Kaiser geleitete Multi-Robot Systems Junior Research Group, die von Prof. Dr. Johannes Thürauf geleitete Discrete Optimization Group sowie die Management Intelligence Services Group der FAU unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. Freimut Bodendorf. Ihre Aufgaben: Die erfolgreiche Bewerberin bzw. der erfolgreiche Bewerber wird im interdisziplinären Projekt „Real-World Multi-Agent Optimal Path Finding under Uncertainty“ mitwirken. Zu Ihren Aufgaben gehören: Durchführung innovativer Forschung zur mathematischen Optimierung für Multi-Agent Path Finding in enger Zusammenarbeit mit einem interdisziplinären Forschungsteam. Entwicklung mathematischer Optimierungsmethoden, insbesondere gemischt-ganzzahliger Optimierungsansätze, für die Pfadplanung von Multi-Agenten-Systemen und die Lösung komplexer Konflikte in realen Robotersystemen. Entwicklung von Optimierungsansätzen unter Unsicherheit, um zuverlässige Lösungen bei unsicherem Roboterverhalten, schwankender Nachfrage und variierenden Betriebsbedingungen zu erzielen. Implementierung und rechnergestützte Evaluation der entwickelten Optimierungsmethoden, einschließlich ihrer Erprobung auf realen Robotersystemen. Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden aus der Robotik sowie der Management Intelligence Services Group der FAU, um Optimierung, Robotik und Business Intelligence miteinander zu verbinden. Veröffentlichung von Forschungsergebnissen in führenden internationalen Fachzeitschriften und auf renommierten Konferenzen sowie Präsentation der eigenen Forschung auf internationalen Konferenzen. Mitwirkung in der Lehre und Betreuung von Studierenden, z. B. im Rahmen von Lehrveranstaltungen, Abschlussarbeiten und Forschungsprojekten. Mitwirkung an Outreach-Aktivitäten und Kommunikation von Forschungsergebnissen gegenüber Wissenschaft, Industrie und Öffentlichkeit. Ihr Profil: Wir erwarten: Einen qualifizierenden Hochschulabschluss (M.Sc. oder vergleichbar) in Mathematik, Informatik, Operations Research oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet, einschließlich Natur- und Ingenieurwissenschaften Motivation, Engagement und ein hohes Maß an Verantwortungsbewusstsein Solide mathematische Kenntnisse und ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an mathematischer Optimierung Ausgeprägtes Interesse an interdisziplinärer Forschung Programmiererfahrung, z. B. in Python, C++ oder vergleichbaren Programmiersprachen Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Zusätzliche Kenntnisse oder Erfahrungen in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche sind wünschenswert: Gemischt-ganzzahlige Optimierung und mathematische Programmierung Optimierung unter Unsicherheit Optimierungssoftware, z. B. Gurobi, CPLEX oder SCIP Algorithmenentwicklung und rechnergestützte Optimierung Ausgewählte Vorteile dieser Position: Eine besondere Gelegenheit, an der Schnittstelle von mathematischer Optimierung, Robotik und Business Intelligence zu forschen, dabei fundierte Expertise in der Optimierung aufzubauen und eng mit verschiedenen Disziplinen zusammenzuarbeiten. Die Möglichkeit, neuartige mathematische Optimierungsmethoden zu entwickeln und diese an anspruchsvollen realen Multi-Roboter-Systemen zu evaluieren. Zugang zu umfassender Expertise über verschiedene Forschungsgruppen und Departments der UTN hinweg sowie zu leistungsfähigen Rechenressourcen. Attraktive Vergütung nach TV-L E 13 sowie eine hohe Lebensqualität bei vergleichsweise moderaten Lebenshaltungskosten in Nürnberg. Interessiert? Wenn Ihr Profil den Anforderungen entspricht, laden Sie bitte folgende Dokumente mit ihrer Bewerbung hoch: Ein Persönliches Motivationsschreiben (max. 1 Seite), in dem Sie die Gründe für Ihren Promotionswunsch an der UTN darlegen und weshalb Sie sich für dieses Forschungsfeld und das Department interessieren. Ein vollständiger chronologischer, tabellarischer Lebenslauf in englischer Sprache. Nachweise über Ihre Studienabschlüsse (M.Sc. sowie B.Sc.) oder gleichwertige Qualifikationen. Transcript of Records, Diploma Supplements oder Kursübersichten ihrer Studienabschlüsse (M.Sc. sowie B.Sc. oder gleichwertige Abschlüsse). Bitte beachten: Falls Sie Ihre Abschlüsse (M.Sc. sowie B.Sc. oder gleichwertige Abschlüsse) im Ausland erhalten haben, müssen Sie stets die Originalversion zusammen mit einer Übersetzung ins Englische oder Deutsche einreichen. Die Übersetzung muss von einem staatlich geprüften Übersetzer/einer staatlich geprüften Übersetzerin angefertigt worden sein und über ein offizielles Siegel verfügen. Dokumente, deren Originalsprache Englisch ist, müssen nicht übersetzt werden. Hinweise zum Motivationsschreiben: Wenn Ihr Motivationsschreiben überwiegend KI generiert erscheint, kann dies Ihre Chancen im weiteren Auswahlverfahren deutlich verringern. Wir möchten Ihre persönliche Motivation kennenlernen und verstehen, an welchen Themen Sie forschen möchten. Sollten Sie in die engere Auswahl kommen, erhalten Sie eine Einladung zu einem Interview, bei dem Sie Ihre Forschungsarbeit vorstellen können. Die Bewerbungen werden fortlaufend geprüft. Wir empfehlen daher eine frühzeitige Bewerbung. Weitere Informationen zum Bewerbungsprozess und den Aufnahmebedingungen finden Sie unter https://www.utn.de/ueber/graduate-school/promotionsleitfaden/#bewerbung Weitere Informationen zur Entgeltgruppe TV-L E13 finden Sie unter https://oeffentlicher-dienst.info/tv-l/allg/ Bitte beachten: Reisekosten und sonstige im Rahmen der Bewerbung anfallende Aufwände können nicht von uns erstattet werden. Sie haben Fragen? Bitte richten Sie alle inhaltlichen Anfragen Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin alexander.martin@utn.de Bei allgemeinen Fragen wenden Sie sich bitte an stars@utn.de The University of Technology Nuremberg (UTN) offers a stimulating and interdisciplinary research environment with access to cutting-edge resources. It is the ideal place to make groundbreaking discoveries and contribute to exciting fields of research. Doctoral researcher (Ph.D.) position at UTN with the topic of Mathematical Optimization for Multi-Robot Systems (m/f/d) The Department of Liberal Arts & Social Sciences is currently offering one opening for a doctoral research opportunity (fully funded, 3 years, 100%, pay scale TV-L E 13) in the Analytics and Optimization Group led by Prof. Dr. Alexander Martin. We are seeking a highly motivated and talented individual to join our dynamic and international research team. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers developing novel approaches to multi-agent path finding in large-scale robotic warehouses. The position is rooted in mathematical optimization and involves close collaboration with researchers in robotics and business intelligence. You will conduct research on topics such as mixed-integer optimization for multi-agent path finding, optimization under uncertainty, and optimization-based conflict resolution, and contribute mathematical optimization expertise to the interdisciplinary team. The developed methods will be evaluated in simulation and on real robotic systems. There will be a complementary position rooted in robotics available in the Artificial Intelligence and Robotics Group led by Prof. Dr. Wolfram Burgard. Further involved research groups are the Multi-Robot Systems Junior Research Group led by Dr. Tanja Kaiser, the Discrete Optimization Group led by Prof. Dr. Johannes Thürauf, and FAU’s Management Intelligence Services Group led by Prof. Dr. Freimut Bodendorf. Your tasks: The successful candidate will contribute to the interdisciplinary project “Real-World Multi-Agent Optimal Path Finding under Uncertainty”. Your responsibilities will include: Conducting cutting-edge research on mathematical optimization for multi-agent path finding in close collaboration with an interdisciplinary team. Developing mathematical optimization methods, such as mixed-integer optimization approaches, for multi-agent path planning and complex conflict resolution in real-world robotic systems. Developing optimization approaches under uncertainty to obtain reliable solutions under uncertain robot behavior, demand, and operating conditions. Implementing and computationally evaluating the developed optimization methods, including their evaluation in real-world robotic systems. Closely collaborating with researchers in robotics and FAU’s Management Intelligence Services Group to integrate optimization, robotics, and business intelligence. Publishing research results in leading international journals and conferences and presenting your work to the global research community at international conferences. Contributing to teaching activities and student supervision (e.g., courses, theses, research projects). Engaging in outreach activities and communicating research to academic, industrial, and wider public audiences. Your profile: We expect: A qualifying degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in Mathematics, Computer Science, Operations Research, or a related discipline including natural sciences and engineering Motivation, dedication, and a strong sense of responsibility A solid mathematical background and strong interest in mathematical optimization Strong interest in interdisciplinary research Programming experience, e.g., Python, C++, or related languages Proficiency in English (spoken and written) Additional experience in one or more of the following areas is desirable: Mixed-integer optimization and mathematical programming Optimization under uncertainty Optimization software (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP) Algorithm development and computational optimization Selected highlights of this position include: A unique opportunity to conduct research at the intersection of mathematical optimization, robotics, and business intelligence, while developing deep expertise in optimization and collaborating closely across disciplines. The opportunity to develop novel mathematical optimization methods and evaluate them on challenging real-world multi-robot systems. Access to broad expertise across UTN’s groups and departments, as well as computational resources. Competitive compensation according to TVL E 13, together with the high quality of living and comparatively moderate living costs offered by the city of Nuremberg. Interested? items.title: Doctorante / Doctorant CIFRE Fiabilité des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire
items.desc: Description De L'employeur Le Groupe SNCF a pour vocation de simplifier les déplacements, fluidifier le transport des personnes et des marchandises, et développer la mobilité de demain. Au sein du Groupe SNCF, la Direction Technologies, Innovation et Projets Groupe (DTIPG) est une direction de la SA SNCF chargée de l'innovation technologique appliquée aux projets stratégiques du groupe. Elle contribue notamment à concevoir un système ferroviaire plus fiable, numérique et décarboné, avec des travaux sur l'IA, les nouvelles propulsions et la localisation des trains. Dans ce cadre, le pôle RECHERCHE - DIRECTION SCIENTIFIQUE propose un projet de thèse CIFRE sur la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire , en partenariat avec le Laboratoire en Génie Industriel (LGI) de CentraleSupélec au sein de la chaire Risques et Résilience des Systèmes Complexes (RRSC) . Description Du Poste La doctorante ou le doctorant CIFRE aura pour mission de développer une méthode d'évaluation et de communication de la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques (JN) appliqués aux systèmes ferroviaires. Les principales activités seront : Comprendre et formaliser les usages des jumeaux numériques dans le ferroviaire : Analyse des cas d'usage SNCF et partenaires (conception numérique, supervision du patrimoine, planification de la maintenance, régénération du réseau). Cartographie des composants d'un JN (données, modèles sous-jacents, processus, interfaces). Réaliser un état de l'art approfondi : Revue bibliographique sur les concepts de jumeaux numériques, la qualité des données et des modèles, la confiance et la fiabilité perçue par les utilisateurs. Analyse des normes et référentiels (notamment ISO/IEC 30173:2023 et ISO 23247:2021) et des modèles de maturité (Digital Twin Business Maturity Model). Cartographier et classifier les cas d'usage SNCF : Identification des étapes de conception d'un JN et de ses niveaux de maturité. Recueil des usages métiers (par qui, pour quoi) et des limites identifiées. Analyse de la fiabilité perçue : critères utilisés, justifications, attentes des utilisateurs. Méthodes : entretiens, analyse documentaire, enquêtes auprès des équipes SNCF et des partenaires. Étudier en profondeur un ou plusieurs cas d'étude : Définition du processus complet de conception et d'utilisation d'un JN sur un cas choisi (par exemple un système de signalisation ou un sous-système d'infrastructure). Identification des étapes où interviennent les contraintes de fiabilité (collecte des données, modélisation, prédiction, décision). Modélisation du processus de conception et d'usage du JN. Méthodes : entretiens, analyse de données, modélisation de processus. Proposer une méthode de notation de la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques : Analyse des enjeux : pour qui, pourquoi et à quoi sert la notation (support à la décision, communication, gouvernance). Définition des dimensions d'évaluation de la fiabilité, éventuellement différenciées selon les types de JN (descriptif, diagnostique, prédictif, prescriptif, autonome). Choix et formalisation d'une méthodologie de notation (par exemple analyse multicritère, indicateurs composites inspirés de modèles type « nutri-score » adaptés aux JN). Expérimentation et test de la méthode sur un ou plusieurs cas d'étude ferroviaire. Conception participative avec des experts métiers et techniques SNCF. Inscrire les travaux dans un écosystème européen : Veille et participation aux travaux autour des jumeaux numériques ferroviaires dans le projet Motional du programme Europes'Rail, et le cas échéant Motional 2. Valorisation des résultats de la thèse auprès des partenaires européens (présentations, publications, contributions aux groupes de travail). Production scientifique et valorisation : Rédaction d'articles scientifiques, rapports internes SNCF, supports de vulgarisation pour les métiers. Participation à des conférences et séminaires (académiques et industriels). Profil recherché Diplômé(e) de Master 2 ou école d'ingénieur Dans Un Des Domaines Suivants (ou Apparentés) Génie industriel Modélisation et simulation de systèmes complexes Ingénierie des systèmes Mathématiques appliquées / data science avec forte appétence pour les systèmes industriels Ou formation équivalente avec solide bagage en modélisation et analyse de systèmes. Un intérêt marqué pour le système ferroviaire , ses enjeux techniques et humains, est attendu. Compétences techniques Solide maîtrise de la modélisation et de la simulation de systèmes complexes (approches systèmes, modèles de processus, éventuellement outils de modélisation type UML, SysML ou équivalents). Connaissances en ingénierie des systèmes et/ou génie industriel. Capacité à mener un état de l'art scientifique : recherche bibliographique, analyse critique d'articles, synthèse. Aisance avec les méthodes d'analyse multicritère et d'évaluation (indicateurs, agrégation, notation). Compétences en analyse de données et compréhension des enjeux de qualité des données (détection d'anomalies, données aberrantes, capteurs IoT...). Excellentes capacités de rédaction en français et en anglais (articles, rapports, documents méthodologiques). Compétences comportementales Capacité d'écoute et de dialogue avec des interlocuteurs variés (experts techniques, chercheurs, opérationnels métiers). Rigueur scientifique, sens de l'analyse et de la synthèse. Très bon relationnel et aptitude à travailler en interface entre monde académique et industriel. Autonomie, curiosité, goût pour l'innovation et la transformation numérique. Capacité à vulgariser des concepts complexes pour les rendre accessibles aux décideurs et aux utilisateurs métiers. Ce que le contrat CIFRE vous apportera Une expérience de recherche appliquée au coeur des enjeux de transformation numérique du ferroviaire : vous travaillerez sur un sujet stratégique pour SNCF et ses partenaires, à l'interface entre innovation digitale, systèmes complexes et performance du réseau. Une double immersion académique et industrielle : Au LGI de CentraleSupélec, au sein de la chaire RRSC, dans un environnement scientifique de haut niveau. Au sein de SNCF Holding - Direction Technologies, Innovation & Projets Groupe, en lien direct avec des experts du jumeau numérique, de la donnée et des systèmes ferroviaires. Un sujet fortement valorisable : Production d'une méthode de référence pour évaluer la fiabilité des jumeaux numériques ferroviaires. Contributions possibles à des projets européens (Motional, Europes'Rail) et à des groupes de normalisation ou de standardisation. items.title: PhD In Developing Multi-Intelligence Agents For Evolving Cyber-Physical-Social Systems
items.desc: About the opportunity Join Cranfield University’s Systems Realization Group (SRG) for an MSc by Research exploring Evolving Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (eCPSS) . This project combines software engineering, data science and human-centred AI to integrate existing research demonstrators into a usable, client-facing decision-support platform. SRG develops and evaluates principles and mechanisms that help engineered systems adapt to changing requirements while preserving safety, accountable human authority and sustainability. Your research will support the translation of these advances into tools that organisations can evaluate and use. Success will involve delivering a working minimum viable product (MVP), documenting its architecture and evaluating how effectively it supports users in completing tasks, understanding recommendations and tracing decisions. Responsibilities Assess existing research demonstrators and identify their integration requirements. Develop a modular software architecture and shared data interfaces. Connect components through APIs or adapters. Build a web interface that enables users to explore operational changes, compare responses and review decision rationale. Retain appropriate human approval and record decisions throughout the workflow. Evaluate integration reliability, usability, task completion and decision traceability using agreed manufacturing scenarios. Collaborate with SRG researchers and demonstrator developers. Produce technical documentation, reproducible installation guidance and an MSc by Research thesis. Qualifications A first- or second-class UK honours degree, or equivalent, in Computer Science or Data Science. Related computing disciplines with equivalent practical experience may also be considered. Strong programming skills in Python or an equivalent language, with evidence of building working software. Ability to work with APIs, structured data, databases and version control. Experience developing user-facing applications. Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work independently and collaboratively. An interest in human-centred design, accountable AI and applied research. Experience with JavaScript/TypeScript, web frameworks, automated testing, AI/LLM integration, knowledge graphs or software deployment is desirable. Prior manufacturing or healthcare experience is not required. Applicants are encouraged to share relevant projects or a portfolio/repository link. Study arrangements This is a self-funded MSc by Research opportunity , rather than a salaried position. The duration is one year full-time or two years part-time , and applications are welcome from UK and international candidates. For enquiries, contact Dr Jelena Milisavljevic Syed at jelenams@cranfield.ac.uk. View the opportunity and apply

items.title: Doktorand i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi, med fokus på ML-metoder i klimatmodellering
items.desc: Meteorologiska institutionen vid Stockholms universitet (MISU) bedriver forskning och utbildning som rör atmosfären, oceanen, och fysikaliskt-baserad klimatvetenskap. MISU erbjuder utbildningsprogram på kandidat-, master- och forskarnivå. Vår forskning söker svar på grundläggande frågor om atmosfärens och havens dynamiska, fysiska, kemiska, och biogeokemiska egenskaper av relevans för väder och klimat. Vi strävar efter en bred forskningsverksamhet inom vårt vetenskapliga område. Vi studerar frågor som sträcker sig från djuphavet till den övre atmosfären och från tropikerna till polerna. I vår forskning utnyttjar och utvecklar vi teori, statistiska metoder och numeriska modeller i nära samspel med observationer. Dessutom utvecklar och leder institutionen observationsbaserad forskning med stöd av satelliter, arktiska isbrytarexpeditioner och landbaserade instrument. MISU har cirka 60 anställda och ingår i en större forskningsmiljö som inkluderar Bolincentret för klimatforskning, Östersjöcentrum och Swedish e-Science Research Centre. Institutionen har stark internationell prägel, över hälften av medarbetarna har en bakgrund utanför Sverige och både svenska och engelska används som arbetsspråk. Vi välkomnar och värdesätter mångfald i vår arbetsmiljö. Mer information om oss finns på: Meteorologiska institutionen. Projektbeskrivning Moln och deras förändringar till följd av variationer i omgivande miljö spelar en avgörande för klimat och klimatförändringar. Upplösningen i typiska klimatmodeller är dock alldeles för grov för att de ska kunna representera processer relaterade till molnbildning explicit. Dessa processer behöver därför parametriseras, eller representeras som funktioner av storskaliga tillståndsvariabler. Sådana parametriseringar är behäftade med stor osäkerhet, och dessutom är de beräkningsmässigt kostsamma. Det här projektets fokus är att på nya sätt brygga över mellan mikroskala och global skala, för att förbättra klimatmodellers noggrannhet, effektivitet och generaliserbarhet och samtidigt utnyttja modern beräkningshårdvara. Vi kommer att undersöka hur maskininlärningsmodeller (ML-modeller) kan tränas på observationer och resultat från högupplöst modellering, som alternativ till empiriska parmetriseringar av småskaliga processer relaterade till turbulens, molnbildning och aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Specifikt ingår i uppgifterna att utveckla och träna datadrivna modeller, koppla dem till en storskalig klimatmodell, utvärdera resultaten mot mätningar och traditionellt parametriserade modeller, och att använda den ML-förstärkta modellen till att uppskatta klimatrelevans som molns effekt på strålningsbalansen, och strålningsdrivning från aerosol-moln-interaktioner. Arbetet kommer att utföras i nära samarbete med experter inom datavetenskap, inom Swedish e-Science Research Centre, och bidra till metodutveckling med bredare tillämpning än endast klimatvetenskap. Som doktorand i projektet kommer du att utveckla dina färdigheter inom atmosfärsvetenskap och klimatmodellering, men även inom datavetenskap och maskininlärning, samt kommunikation och samarbete inom och mellan discipliner. Behörighetskrav För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning krävs att den sökande har grundläggande och särskild behörighet. Behörigheten ska vara uppfylld senast vid antagning till programmet. Grundläggande behörighet har du, om du avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng (hp), varav minst 60 hp på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. För särskild behörighet krävs minst 90 hp i något av ämnena meteorologi, oceanografi, fysik eller kemi, minst 15 hp i matematik och ett självständigt arbete om minst 15 hp. Av detta skall minst 60 hp vara på avancerad nivå. Vidare krävs språkkunskaper i engelska motsvarande engelska B på gymnasiet. Allmän studieplan för utbildning på forskarnivå i atmosfärsvetenskap och oceanografi. Urval Urval bland de sökande som uppfyller behörighetskraven ska göras med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen. Enbart det förhållandet att en sökande bedöms kunna få tidigare utbildning eller yrkesverksamhet tillgodoräknad för utbildningen får inte vid urval ge sökanden företräde framför andra sökande. Beslut om antagning fattas enligt gällande delegationsordning. Vid bedömningen tas hänsyn till förtrogenhet och skicklighet inom ämnet, förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på engelska, analytisk förmåga, kreativitet, initiativförmåga och självständighet, och samarbetsförmåga. Till grund för bedömningen ligger tidigare studiers relevans, betyg på genomgångna högskolekurser (särskilt de på avancerad nivå), kvalitet och omfattning på det självständiga arbetet, referenser, intervjuer samt skriftlig avsiktsförklaring. Antagningsordning för utbildning på forskarnivå vid Stockholms universitet. Om anställningen Tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Vi erbjuder en tidsbegränsad anställning som doktorand enligt 5 kap. högskoleförordningen (1993:100). Anställningstiden får inte vara längre än vad som motsvarar utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid under fyra år. Som doktorand ska du främst ägna dig åt din egen utbildning på forskarnivå, men i anställningen kan arbete med utbildning, forskning och administration ingå i begränsad omfattning (högst 20 %). En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen förnyas därefter med högst två år i taget. Stockholms universitet värnar om att vara en arbetsplats som är fri från diskriminering och ger lika rättigheter och möjligheter för alla. Kontakt För mer information om projektet, kontakta professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. För information om forskarutbildningen, kontakta studierektor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. Upplysningar om rekryteringsprocessen och anställningsvillkor lämnas av administrativ chef, Sara Engström sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen via Stockholms universitets rekryteringssystem. Bifoga personligt brev och CV samt de bilagor som efterfrågas i ansökningsformuläret. Du som sökande ansvarar för att ansökan är komplett i enlighet med annonsen och att den är universitetet tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdag. Vi ber att du som sökande avstår från att skicka in en AI-genererad ansökan. Anvisningar för sökande finns på webbsidan: att söka en anställning. Stockholms universitet bidrar till det hållbara demokratiska samhällets utveckling genom kunskap, upplysning och sanningssökande.

items.title: Offre de thèse CIFRE Janvier/Février 2027
items.desc: Pérennisation soutenable des systèmes de production : modélisation probabiliste hybride et anticipation des risques d’obsolescence Contexte et problématique Une part importante de l’outil industriel repose aujourd’hui sur des installations exploitées depuis plusieurs décennies. Ces moyens de production associent des équipements, composants, automatismes et logiciels dont la durée d’exploitation dépasse fréquemment celle de commercialisation ou de support. L’obsolescence constitue ainsi un risque important pour la continuité de production. Elle peut résulter d’évolutions technologiques, de l’arrêt d’une référence, de la raréfaction de pièces, de la disparition d’un fournisseur, de la fin d’un support ou de la perte de compétences. Sa maîtrise constitue un enjeu de disponibilité des installations, de souveraineté industrielle et d’utilisation raisonnée des ressources. Une installation industrielle comporte plusieurs milliers de références reliées entre elles au sein d’architectures techniques et de chaînes d’approvisionnement complexes. Les informations nécessaires à l’évaluation de leur pérennité sont dispersées entre bases de maintenance, référentiels techniques, données fournisseurs, historiques d’intervention et connaissances métier. Ces informations sont hétérogènes, évolutives et souvent incomplètes. Le module de diagnostic du logiciel OBSOLIO, développé par GreenTrack Genius, évalue actuellement l’obsolescence au moyen d’un scoring expert statique. La thèse vise à dépasser cette approche pour construire un modèle capable d’actualiser et d’anticiper le risque d’obsolescence à partir des données disponibles et des connaissances métier, tout en représentant explicitement l’incertitude et les mécanismes de propagation du risque. Question scientifique centrale Comment modéliser, propager et actualiser le risque d’obsolescence au sein d’une architecture industrielle multiniveau et de sa chaîne d’approvisionnement, en présence d’informations hétérogènes et incomplètes, afin de comparer de manière explicable des stratégies de pérennisation soutenable ? Verrou scientifique et approche proposée Le principal verrou scientifique concerne la propagation probabiliste d’un risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau, depuis le composant jusqu’à l’équipement et à la ligne de production, alors que l’état de connaissance sur les différents éléments du système est incomplet et variable. Une absence d’information sur une référence, un fournisseur ou une possibilité de substitution ne peut en effet être assimilée à l’absence de risque, ni être systématiquement considérée comme une situation défavorable. La modélisation devra donc distinguer autant que possible le risque déduit des informations disponibles de l’incertitude liée à l’incomplétude de ces informations. La recherche s’appuiera sur une approche hybride associant deux niveaux de représentation. 1. Représentation des connaissances et de l’architecture industrielle Un graphe de connaissances sera utilisé pour structurer les relations entre actifs, composants, nomenclatures, fournisseurs, références de substitution, historiques et événements d’obsolescence. Ce graphe aura pour fonction de représenter la structure du système étudié et les informations disponibles. Une question de recherche portera sur la manière de transformer ou d’exploiter cette représentation pour construire les dépendances pertinentes du modèle probabiliste. 2. Modélisation et propagation probabilistes Les réseaux bayésiens constitueront le cadre principal étudié pour agréger les connaissances expertes et les observations disponibles, représenter les dépendances entre facteurs et propager l’incertitude entre les différents niveaux du système. La dimension temporelle sera introduite lorsque les données disponibles permettent de caractériser l’évolution des variables et du risque. Les extensions dynamiques des réseaux bayésiens seront notamment étudiées pour représenter cette évolution et évaluer leur capacité à anticiper une situation d’obsolescence. Le travail portera en particulier sur les méthodes d’initialisation du modèle, l’intégration de connaissances expertes, l’apprentissage à partir des historiques et la robustesse de l’inférence en présence de données manquantes. Aide à la décision et pérennisation soutenable L’objectif est de dépasser le diagnostic pour comparer des stratégies de remédiation. Les réseaux bayésiens pourront être étendus sous forme de diagrammes d’influence, intégrant variables de décision et critères d’utilité. Plusieurs stratégies seront considérées : maintien en l’état, constitution ou mutualisation de stocks, substitution, reconditionnement, reconception partielle ou renouvellement. La pérennisation soutenable sera abordée comme un problème de décision multicritère prenant en compte au minimum : la disponibilité et le risque technique ; le coût de la stratégie ; son impact environnemental ; sa faisabilité industrielle et organisationnelle. L’objectif sera donc d’identifier la solution réduisant le risque d’obsolescence mais aussi de comparer les conséquences de différentes stratégies dans le contexte propre au système étudié. Validation et résultats attendus La validation reposera sur des données industrielles historiques : données de maintenance et d’équipements, informations fournisseurs, changements de références, événements d’obsolescence et autres données de cycle de vie disponibles sur les sites étudiés. Une validation rétrospective sera privilégiée. Elle consistera, lorsque les données le permettent, à reconstruire l’état d’information disponible à une date passée, à produire l’évaluation du risque correspondant, puis à comparer cette évaluation aux événements observés ultérieurement. Les résultats seront également comparés au scoring expert actuellement utilisé dans OBSOLIO afin de mesurer l’apport de la modélisation probabiliste en matière d’anticipation, de gestion des données manquantes et d’explicabilité. La thèse devra aboutir à trois résultats principaux : un modèle formel de représentation et de propagation probabiliste du risque d’obsolescence dans une architecture industrielle multiniveau ; une méthode d’aide à la décision permettant de comparer des stratégies de pérennisation selon plusieurs critères ; un démonstrateur Python mettant en œuvre les modèles développés et permettant leur validation sur des cas industriels. Les contributions scientifiques porteront ainsi sur la représentation et la propagation d’un risque d’obsolescence dans des systèmes industriels complexes lorsque l’information disponible est distribuée, évolutive et incomplète. Les résultats auront vocation à alimenter le moteur algorithmique d’OBSOLIO, sans que le développement du logiciel constitue l’objet de la thèse. Profil recherché Le ou la candidate devra être titulaire d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master en génie industriel, ingénierie des systèmes, science des données, informatique industrielle ou domaine proche. De solides bases en probabilités, statistiques et modélisation sont attendues, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de la programmation scientifique en Python. Une connaissance des réseaux bayésiens, des modèles graphiques probabilistes ou des méthodes de recherche opérationnelle constituera un atout. Le travail nécessitera également une capacité à comprendre des architectures industrielles complexes et à travailler avec les équipes de maintenance, méthodes, achats et ingénierie. Le profil recherché doit ainsi associer compétences en modélisation et intérêt pour les problématiques industrielles concrètes. Contact : Marc.Zolghadri@isae-supmeca.fr

items.title: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d)
items.desc: Job description: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d) at the Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry The position is to be filled as soon as possible on a full-time or part-time basis for a fixed term of 36 months. Remuneration is based on the classification provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States (TV-L); placement in pay group E13 is possible, subject to the fulfillment of personal requirements. The Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry (IMB) is part of the Carl Gustav Carus Faculty of Medicine at TU Dresden. The institute’s research focuses on medical biometrics, bioinformatics, systems biology/medicine, including mathematical modelling, as well as medical informatics. In addition to these scientific activities, the IMB offers various services (e.g., consulting and education programs in the field of medical data science) for faculty and students at the Faculty of Medicine and the University Hospital. The position is part of the interdisciplinary research project “Virtual niche: Computational modelling and simulation of spatio-temporal dynamics of hematopoietic stem cells in their local microenvironment” funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The core objective of the project is the development and application of a mathematical model that describes the spatio-temporal organization of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in their local growth environment within the bone marrow. The goal of gaining a better understanding of the underlying processes is of central importance both for open questions in basic stem cell biology and for future medical applications. Your responsibilities: Development of mathematical models to describe cellular dynamics Implementation of the models in a suitable programming environment Simulation of cellular dynamics within complex 3D structures Application of the computer model as a virtual bridge between in vitro and in vivo studies Systemic analysis and interpretation of experimental data in the context of complex biological interactions Close interdisciplinary collaboration with experimental teams at TU Dresden and external partner laboratories Your Profil: University degree (M.Sc., Diplom, or equivalent) in mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering (with biological/biotechnological focus) or a related field Very good or excellent academic record Strong interest in interdisciplinary work, particularly in the application of mathematical and computational methods in biology and medicine Solid programming experience (e.g. in the statistical software R or Python) Knowledge of (stem) cell biology and experience in mathematical modelling are advantageous Reliability, creativity, flexibility, and the ability to work well in a team A cooperative, self-motivated, and goal-oriented work style Very good English skills We offer: Compensation: Based on the TV-L Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the Federal States in pay grade E13 , plus an annual bonus, provided you meet the personal requirements Vacation: 30 days of paid vacation Professional Development: Extensive internal and external training and development opportunities to continuously strengthen your skills Company Culture: We value transparency, team spirit, and shared success. Celebrate with us at company gatherings or sporting events like the Rewe Team Challenge. Mobility: A subsidy for a job ticket to make your commute eco-friendly and convenient Health: We promote your well-being with modern fitness and exercise programs at our health center, mental health programs, and a comprehensive workplace health management program. Shopping benefits: Take advantage of employee discounts at our clinic pharmacy, exclusive corporate benefits, and other shopping portals. Work-life balance: Our Family Office supports you with questions regarding daycare spots, vacation programs, and caring for family members. We also offer flexible work arrangements. For preliminary information, please contact Prof. Dr. Ingo Roeder by phone at 0351-458-6060 or by email at ingo.roeder@tu-dresden.de (Subject: DFG-virtualniche)

items.title: Doktorandin/Doktorand (m/w/d) AG Röder
items.desc: Stellenbeschreibung: Doktorandin/Doktorand (m/w/d) am Institut für Medizinische Informatik und Biometrie Die Stelle ist zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Voll- oder Teilzeitbeschäftigung für 36 Monate befristet zu besetzen. Die Vergütung erfolgt nach den Eingruppierungsvorschriften des Tarifvertrages für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) und ist bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen in die Entgeltgruppe E13 möglich. Das Institut für Medizinische Informatik und Biometrie (IMB) ist Teil der Medizinischen Fakultät Carl Gustav Carus der Technischen Universität Dresden. Die Forschungsschwerpunkte des Instituts liegen in den Bereichen medizinische Biometrie, Bioinformatik, Systembiologie/-medizin inklusive der mathematischen Modellierung sowie in der medizinischen Informatik. Neben diesen wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeitsfeldern bietet das IMB verschiedene Dienstleistungen (z. B. Beratungs- und Weiterbildungsangebote im Bereich der medizinischen Datenwissenschaften) für Mitarbeitende und Studierende der Medizinischen Fakultät und des Universitätsklinikums Dresden an. Die Stelle ist Teil des von der Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) geförderten interdisziplinären Forschungsprojekts „Virtuelle Nische: Computer-gestützte Modellierung und Simulation der zeitlichen-räumlich Dynamik hämatopoetischer Stammzellen in ihrer lokalen Mikroumgebung“. Kernziel des Projektes ist die Entwicklung und Anwendung eines mathematischen Modells, das die zeitlich‑räumliche Organisation hämatopoetischer Stamm‑ und Vorläuferzellen in ihrer lokalen Wachstumsumgebung im Knochenmark beschreibt. Das angestrebte verbesserte Verständnis der zugrundeliegenden Prozesse ist sowohl für offene grundlagenwissenschaftliche Fragestellungen der Stammzellbiologie als auch für zukünftige medizinische Anwendungen von zentraler Bedeutung. Ihre Aufgaben: Entwicklung mathematischer Modelle zur Beschreibung zellulärer Dynamiken Implementierung der Modelle in einer geeigneten Programmierumgebung Simulation zellulärer Dynamiken innerhalb komplexer 3D-Strukturen Anwendung des Computermodells als virtuelle Brücke zwischen in vitro- und in vivo-Studien Systemische Analyse und Interpretation experimenteller Daten im Kontext komplexer biologischer Interaktionen Enge interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit mit experimentell arbeitenden Teams an der TU Dresden und kooperierenden Laboren im europäischen Ausland Ihr Profil: abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (M.Sc., Diplom oder Vergleichbares) im Fach Mathematik, Physik, Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften (mit biologischem/technologischem Schwerpunkt) oder einer verwandten Disziplin sehr gute oder exzellente Studienleistungen ausgeprägtes Interesse an interdisziplinären Aufgaben, speziell an der Anwendung mathematischer/informatischer Methoden in der Biologie/Medizin solide Programmiererfahrung (z. B. in der Statistiksoftware R oder Python) Kenntnisse im Bereich (Stamm-)Zellbiologie und Erfahrungen im Bereich der mathematischen Modellierung sind vorteilhaft Zuverlässigkeit, Kreativität, Flexibilität und Teamfähigkeit kooperativer, eigenverantwortlicher und zielorientierter Arbeitsstil sehr gute Englischkenntnisse Unser Angebot: Vergütung: nach TV-L in der Entgeltgruppe E13 zzgl. Jahressonderzahlung, bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen Urlaub: 30 Tage Erholungsurlaub Weiterbildung: Umfangreiche interne und externe Fort- und Weiterbildungsangebote, um Ihre Kompetenzen kontinuierlich zu stärken Unternehmenskultur : Wir setzen auf Transparenz, Teamgeist und gemeinsame Erfolge. Feiern Sie mit uns bei gemeinsamen Veranstaltungen oder bei sportlichen Events. Einkaufsvorteile : Profitieren Sie von Mitarbeiterrabatten in unserer Klinik-Apotheke, exklusiven Corporate Benefits und weiteren Shoppingportalen. Work-Life-Balance: Unser Familienbüro unterstützt Sie bei Fragen rund um Kita-Plätze, Ferienprogramme und Pflege von Angehörigen. Zudem bieten wir flexible Arbeitsmodelle.
