items.title: Promovendus digi-, data- en AI-competenties
items.desc: De zorg van morgen wordt steeds digitaler. Maar technologie werkt pas als zorgprofessionals ermee kunnen werken. Hoe leren studenten en professionals digi-, data- en AI-competenties? En hoe bereiden we hen voor op een snel veranderende digitale wereld? Dat onderzoek jij! Aantal uur: 28 • 36 uur per week Werklocatie: Beide locaties Amsterdam UMC Contractvorm: Bepaalde tijd Salaris: € 3.217 - € 4.077 Reageer tot en met: 2 november 2026 Wat ga je doen? Je combineert literatuuronderzoek met het ontwikkelen en evalueren van leertrajecten voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je werkzaamheden bestaan uit: Je brengt de wetenschappelijke literatuur en de meest recente inzichten op het gebied van digi-, data- en AI-competenties en leren en ontwikkelen in kaart. Je schrijft een algemeen onderzoeksplan en werkt dit uit in deelstudies, inclusief de benodigde ethische goedkeuringen. Je onderzoekt modellen, methoden en technieken voor een leven lang ontwikkelen. Daarbij kijk je bijvoorbeeld naar transfer of training, simulatieleren en werkplekleren om tot schaalbare oplossingen te komen. Je ontwikkelt en evalueert leertrajecten, waaronder pilots, voor (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Je adviseert waar nodig projecten en programma's binnen Amsterdam UMC die aansluiten bij jouw onderzoek. Daarnaast schrijf je wetenschappelijke artikelen voor nationale en internationale tijdschriften. Je bundelt je onderzoeksresultaten uiteindelijk in een proefschrift en presenteert je bevindingen op nationale en internationale congressen. Ook draag je beperkt bij aan onderwijs en opleiden van studenten en medewerkers, voor zover dit aansluit bij jouw onderzoek. Wat neem je mee? We nodigen je uit om te solliciteren als je een van de volgende opleidingen hebt afgerond: Een (research)master onderwijskunde, met affiniteit met en bij voorkeur ervaring in de gezondheidszorg. Of: Een (research)master gezondheidswetenschappen, aangevuld met aantoonbare didactische ervaring of scholing. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende profiel: Je hebt aantoonbare affiniteit met onderzoek en ervaring met kwalitatieve en kwantitatieve onderzoeksmethoden. Je hebt interesse in digitalisering, data en AI in de zorg en in didactische principes zoals simulatieleren en werkplekleren, of je wilt je hierin verder verdiepen. Je bent analytisch sterk, zelfstandig en nieuwsgierig. Ook heb je het doorzettingsvermogen om een promotietraject succesvol af te ronden. Je beheerst het Nederlands en Engels goed, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Je kunt complexe onderwerpen helder uitleggen. Ervaring met lesgeven of begeleiden is een pré. Je werkt graag samen, maar kunt ook zelfstandig aan de slag. Wat bieden we jou? Je treedt in dienst bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Een contract voor de duur van 12 maanden, met de intentie te verlengen tot een totaal van vier jaar. Voor deze vacature geldt de Richtlijn Promovendi. Inschaling in salarisschaal OIO: € 3.217 tot € 4.077 bruto bij een fulltime dienstverband (afhankelijk van ervaring). Daarnaast ontvang je 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Bereken hier jouw netto salaris. Mogelijkheid tot hybride werken, waarbij je minimaal twee dagen per week op locatie werkt. Vakantie-uren: 194,4 uur per jaar bij een fulltime dienstverband en de mogelijkheid om uren bij te sparen. 100% OV-vergoeding. Kom je lopend, fietsend of met de auto? Dan ontvang je een vergoeding van €0,21 per km (voor de auto geldt een maximum van 40 km enkele reis). Kom je op de fiets? Maak gebruik van onze goede fietsregeling. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je werkt bij het Teaching & Learning Centre (TLC) van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA, bij Amsterdam UMC, locatie AMC, aan de Meibergdreef. Je maakt deel uit van het onderzoeksteam, een van de vier teams binnen het TLC. Dit kleine team bestaat uit onderwijskundig onderzoekers en innovators die samenwerken aan onderwijsvernieuwing en onderzoek. Daarnaast werk je inhoudelijk samen met het projectteam dat de leerpaden voor digi-, data- en AI-vaardigheden binnen Amsterdam UMC ontwikkelt en in de praktijk brengt. Het TLC is het expertisecentrum voor hoger onderwijs van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de UvA. Het ondersteunt de opleidingen Geneeskunde en Medische informatiekunde bij het verzorgen van hoogwaardig onderwijs. Onderwijskundig adviseurs, medical educators, trainers, onderzoekers en innovators werken er samen aan het verbeteren van onderwijs en opleiden. Het TLC maakt deel uit van de kerntaak Onderwijs & Opleiden van Amsterdam UMC en draagt bij aan de ontwikkeling van studenten en (toekomstige) zorgprofessionals. Binnen het team heerst een open en samenwerkingsgerichte cultuur. Kennis delen en samen leren staan centraal. Je werkt ook nauw samen met onderzoekers van de faculteit der Geneeskunde van de VU en met andere afdelingen binnen Amsterdam UMC. Zo draag je bij aan een groeiende community op het gebied van onderwijsonderzoek. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Je onderzoekt welke digi-, data- en AI-competenties huidige en toekomstige zorgprofessionals nodig hebben. Je brengt in kaart welke competenties al goed zijn ontwikkeld en waar nog hiaten of overlap bestaan. Op basis daarvan ontwikkel je een breed, evidence-based competentieraamwerk. Je doet voorstellen om deze competenties efficiënt te integreren in het continuüm van onderwijs en opleiden. Waar mogelijk evalueer je bestaande en nieuwe leerinterventies die aansluiten op (onderdelen van) het raamwerk. Daarbij kijk je niet alleen naar het directe leerrendement, maar ook naar de vraag of professionals de competenties op langere termijn behouden en toepassen. Je onderzoek sluit aan bij een groter project binnen Amsterdam UMC. Daarin ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en testen we al enkele jaren leerpaden voor verschillende doelgroepen. De ontwikkelde producten, zoals de ontwerpmethodiek, het eerste competentiemodel en het evaluatieproces, vormen de basis voor jouw onderzoek. Tegelijkertijd biedt deze context volop ruimte om nieuwe onderzoeksvragen te verkennen. Wil je alvast meer weten over de verschillende fases binnen het PhD-traject? Op deze pagina lees je hierover meer informatie. Laten we kennismaken De beoogde startdatum is zo snel mogelijk, in overleg. Heb je interesse? Stuur dan je motivatiebrief en cv, aangevuld met een publicatielijst indien relevant. De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken vindt plaats in de week van maandag 16 november 2026 . Tijdens deze gesprekken maak je kennis met de vice-decaan Onderwijs van de UvA, het hoofd van het TLC en de coördinerend onderzoeker van het onderzoeksteam. We vragen je om hier alvast rekening mee te houden. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Tom Broens , h oofd TLC, via t.h.broens@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Lees hier wat dit inhoudt. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

items.title: PhD AI/ML Research Engineer Intern
items.desc: Craft: Technology & Development Job Description: AI/ML Research Engineer Internship - 2027 About AI Labs at King’s AI Center of Excellence: Join AI Labs, an applied research team within King’s AI Center of Excellence, where innovation and collaboration come together to tackle complex modeling challenges and explore the latest advances in machine learning. At AI Labs, we help unlock business value through impactful research and the development of state-of-the-art solutions. Our work spans automation at scale for game levels, player experience optimization, AI trustworthiness, and the exploration of emerging technologies. Working alongside Research Engineers, ML Engineers, and Data Scientists, you will contribute to long-term research initiatives and play an important role in advancing King’s central machine learning capabilities. The Opportunity: For this internship cycle, we are looking for a motivated Research Engineer Intern with a strong interest in one of the following research themes: World Models for Gameplay and Simulation: Investigate scalable world models that learn predictive representations and dynamics from gameplay data to support simulation, planning, and downstream decision-making. Familiarity with generative modeling, latent dynamics models, model-based reinforcement learning, and self-supervised learning is desirable. Particular interest will be given to approaches that improve generalization, sample efficiency, and long-horizon prediction. Reinforcement Learning for Gameplay: Apply advanced Reinforcement Learning (RL) techniques to enhance playtesting and support the creation of more engaging player experiences. Candidates with a strong background in RL and hands-on experience with modern online and offline RL algorithms, particularly in transfer learning and robust policy generalization, are encouraged to apply. Experience with unsupervised RL, exploration and intrinsic motivation, or related approaches is highly desirable. Understanding User Behavior in Games: Leverage quantitative and qualitative methods, together with multi-modal data, to deepen our understanding of player strategies, behaviors, and skill progression. Experience combining behavioral analytics with advanced machine learning techniques to identify meaningful patterns in behavioral data will be highly valuable. This is a fixed-term internship of six months , offering the opportunity to work on cutting-edge machine learning research that contributes directly to game content and player experiences. You will gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced environment, developing solutions with real-world impact across our products and services. The role is based in our Stockholm office and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement. Responsibilities: Collaborate with researchers and engineers on projects aligned with your area of interest and expertise. Participate in the full research lifecycle, from problem definition and methodology exploration to implementation, experimentation, and evaluation. Document research outcomes and communicate progress and findings to team members and relevant stakeholders. Who You Are: Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related field. Recent graduates with relevant backgrounds are also welcome to apply. Strong foundation in machine learning, data science, and algorithm development. Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Knowledge of, or prior experience with, the research topic and methodologies relevant to the selected theme is preferred. Proficient in Python and experienced with machine learning libraries and frameworks. Hold valid authorization to work in Sweden from January 2027 onward. How to Apply: To apply for the Research Engineer Intern position at AI Labs within King’s AI Center of Excellence, please submit: 1) your CV, and 2) a cover letter outlining: Your interest in the role. Your preferred research theme. Relevant experience, including links to projects, publications, or other work where applicable. Contact details for your academic supervisor. Please ensure that all application materials are submitted before the application deadline. We look forward to hearing from you. About King With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. More information can be found at King.com or by following us on LinkedIn and @lifeatking on Instagram.

items.title: PhD Studentship: Dynamic Performance and AI-Driven Optimisation of Hybrid Energy Systems for Net Zero
items.desc: Area Foundation Eng.& Physical Sciences Location UK Other Closing Date Open Until Filled Reference ENG416 Programme Length: 4 Years Study Mode: Full-time Location: Nottingham Discipline: Engineering & Physical Sciences Start Date: December 2026 Project Overview This fully funded PhD project aims to develop and evaluate a novel hybrid energy system integrating gas turbines, low-temperature carbon capture, biomass gasification, and advanced solar thermal technologies to enable carbon-negative fuel production and grid support. The research will focus on developing intelligent energy systems capable of reducing carbon emissions, improving grid stability, and enhancing sustainable energy generation. The project combines thermodynamic modelling, transient simulation, techno-economic assessment, life cycle analysis, and AI-driven optimisation to support the UK's net-zero ambitions. Research Objectives The successful candidate will: Develop thermodynamic models of integrated hybrid energy systems. Conduct transient simulations using UK climate and grid demand profiles. Evaluate system performance under varying operating conditions. Perform techno-economic and life cycle assessments. Develop AI-driven optimisation and intelligent control strategies. Investigate opportunities for deployment across industrial applications, including steel, cement, and waste-to-energy sectors. Supervisory Team Dr Ioanna Dimitriou, University of Nottingham Dr Oliver Fisher, University of Nottingham About The Net2Zero Centre For Doctoral Training The Net2Zero CDT is a partnership between Aston University, the University of Nottingham, Queen's University Belfast, and the University of Warwick. Students benefit from: Access to world-class research facilities. Collaboration with academic and industrial partners. International networking opportunities. Training in engineering, communication, entrepreneurship, and business skills. A three-month industrial, research, or policy placement. Candidate Profile Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a First-Class or strong 2:1 degree (or equivalent) in: Chemical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Energy Engineering Process Engineering Or a closely related discipline A background in thermodynamics, energy systems, process modelling, programming, or simulation tools such as MATLAB, Python, Aspen Plus, TRNSYS, or EES is desirable. Funding Package UKRI tax-free stipend (£21,805 per annum for 2026/27) Full tuition fee support Research Training Support Grant (RTSG) Eligibility This opportunity is open to Home Fee Status candidates only. You can find the rules for home fee eligibility. Rules for home fee eligibility Academic Queries For enquiries regarding the research project, please contact: Dr Ioanna Dimitriou- Ioanna.Dimitriou@nottingham.ac.uk Dr Oliver Fisher- Oliver.Fisher2@nottingham.ac.uk Administrative Queries For enquiries regarding eligibility, funding, or the application process, please contact: Net2Zero CDT Team, Md Ashif Chy, EZ-Net2Zero-CDT@nottingham.ac.uk Email details to a friend Further details: Job Description/Role Profile View All Vacancies View Previous List

items.title: PhD Position in Entrepreneurship, AI, and Labor Market Disruption - DTU Entrepreneurship
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Are you interested in exploring the following questions? How are artificial intelligence (AI) and automation reshaping individuals' transitions to entrepreneurship? How do individuals' skills, experience, and technological readiness influence the types of businesses they create and their subsequent performance? How do these patterns vary across countries and institutional contexts? DTU Entrepreneurship invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship as part of an international research project entitled The New Landscape of Necessity Entrepreneurship: Understanding Entrepreneurial Transitions in an Era of AI- and Automation-Driven Labor Market Disruption . The project investigates how AI and automation reshape entrepreneurial transitions, with particular attention to individuals who start businesses following unemployment. The PhD candidate will join an international research team involving Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Professor Marc Gruber at École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland, and Professor John C. Dencker at Northeastern University, USA. Funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF), the project combines large-scale surveys, Danish administrative registry data, and qualitative interviews across Denmark, Switzerland, and Greece. The position offers an opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge entrepreneurship research, work with rich international datasets, and collaborate with leading scholars in the field. Responsibilities And Qualifications Your primary responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the international project, with opportunities to develop your own research questions within its overall scope. Your tasks will include: Developing research questions and theoretical frameworks concerning entrepreneurship, human capital, AI, and labor market transitions. Applying quantitative and qualitative research methods to investigate entrepreneurial transitions and outcomes. Collecting, managing, and analyzing quantitative data, including large-scale surveys and Danish registry data. Contributing to the design and implementation of surveys and qualitative interviews in collaboration with international research partners. Preparing research papers for submission to leading international academic journals. Presenting research findings at international conferences and contributing to dissemination activities targeting policymakers and other stakeholders. Collaborating with researchers at DTU, EPFL, Northeastern University, and other project partners. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with a strong interest in entrepreneurship research and technological change. We expect you to have: A Master’s degree. A strong interest in developing quantitative research and analytical skills. Excellent written and spoken English communication skills. The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment. The following qualifications would be considered an advantage, but are not required: Experience working with large-scale datasets, registry data, or longitudinal data. Experience with statistical software such as Stata or R, and familiarity with econometric techniques, including regression analysis and panel data methods. Experience with survey design, qualitative interviewing, or mixed-methods research. You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment The assessment of applicants will be conducted by Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, who will serve as the principal supervisor. We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The expected starting date is as soon as possible or as agreed with the successful candidate. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Argyro (Iro) Nikiforou, DTU Entrepreneurship, Technical University of Denmark, at argnik@dtu.dk . You can read more about DTU Entrepreneurship at www.entrepreneurship.dtu.dk . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 8 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. We enable ethically minded entrepreneurs to build solutions that benefit people, society and the world. The Center experiments with new entrepreneurial methodologies and activities to push boundaries within research and education. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: PhD Position in Secure and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning / AI (m/f/d)
items.desc: The Barkhausen Institut performs research on the latest hardware, software and communication technologies and demonstrates their application in tomorrow's society. Our goal is to build a flexible and trustworthy IoT platform based on reliable electronics and secure communication methods. The Trustworthy Data Processing group at the Barkhausen Institut is seeking a highly motivated candidate to pursue a PhD in secure and privacy-preserving machine learning and AI. At the earliest possible date we are looking for a PhD Position in Secure and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning / AI (m/f/d) The position combines academic research with practical system development, including developing new methods, implementing prototypes, and evaluating their security, privacy, and efficiency. The position will initially be filled for a period of 2 years and will be remunerated in line with TV-L E-13. The position aims at supporting further academic qualification (e.g. PhD). Your Responsibilities Will Include Conduct research in secure and privacy-preserving machine learning and AI towards a PhD. Develop and evaluate methods and prototypes and publish research findings. Contribute to collaborative research projects, including preparing project deliverables and reports. Present research findings at conferences, workshops, and project meetings. We expect the following Above-average university degree in the field of our research focus (cryptography, security, privacy) A strong academic background and relevant research experience; Programming experience and an interest in developing research prototypes; An interest in combining scientific research with practical system development. Very good written and spoken English skills We especially welcome applicants with a background in both of the following areas: Privacy-enhancing technologies, such as homomorphic encryption, trusted execution environments, and secure computation; Machine learning and AI You are interested, but you don’t think you meet all the requirements of the job posting? Then you should know: We don’t hire resumes, we hire people. We are looking for potential and want to actively foster it. That’s why we encourage you to apply! What We Provide An open and creative team Agile working hours and workflows Cross-disciplinary projects Work on future technologies Flat hierarchies for your ideas and flexible teams Our remuneration is based on the collective agreement for the federal states. If you meet all the professional requirements (diploma/master's degree), this position is classified as TV-L E 13. Depending on your professional experience, the basic monthly salary ranges between €4,629 and €6,580. We will be happy to provide more details during the interview. If you have passion for new technologies and the desire to develop the connected world of tomorrow with us, we are looking for you. Life and science are compatible at our institute. We offer a range of recognised family-friendly measures, such as part-time work, mobile working and flexible working hours that take family needs into account. We also offer support for arriving in Dresden (all formalities, apartment etc.). Application Procedure Your application should include motivation letter including a short statement outlining your research interests and relevant experience, CV, copy of university degree certificate, short summary of Master thesis. Barkhausen Institut strives for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. Severely disabled persons are given preference in the event of equal suitability. We only accept complete documents as one single PDF document by e-mail to hier . Please reference “PhD Position in Secure and Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning / AI” in the subject line. Applications that contain other file formats (e.g. Word, Excel) will not be considered in the selection process. Informal inquiries can also be submitted to the same address. If you have any content-related questions regarding the job advertisement, you can contact Maryam Zarezadeh at hier . Please apply until October 31, 2026. The data submitted by you in the course of the application procedure will be processed by the Barkhausen Institut (BI). BI shall use the data for the purposes of the application procedure. No data shall be passed on to third parties. Skills zu dieser Stellenanzeige: BI, IoT, Internet of Things, machine learning, research, AI, PhD, cryptography, security und privacy Wichtiger Hinweis Das ist eine Anzeige des Empfehlungsbund (EBND) über ITsax.de. Pensioenopbouw bij BeFrank, een modern, begrijpelijk en eerlijk geprijsd pensioen. Bekijk deze video met meer informatie over de indiensttreding bij Amsterdam UMC Research BV. Waar ga je werken ? Je maakt deel uit van het team Onderzoek van Onderwijs binnen de Faculteit Geneeskunde VU. Daarnaast neem je actief deel aan het netwerk i.o. voor onderzoek van onderwijs binnen Amsterdam UMC. Amsterdam UMC Research BV Amsterdam UMC Research BV ondersteunt wetenschappelijk onderzoek zonder winstoogmerk. Hiermee voorzien we onderzoekers in alles wat ze nodig hebben om te kunnen excelleren. Zo bieden onze principal investigators (PI's) en projectleiders begeleiding op het gebied van projectbeheer, finance en human resources. Bij medisch-wetenschappelijke onderzoeksprojecten wordt daarnaast ook ondersteuning op juridisch vlak geboden. Bekijk de video voor meer informatie. Wat ga je onderzoeken? Klinisch redeneren is de kern van het artsenvak: het vermogen om uit het patiëntverhaal, de uitgevraagde klachten, het lichamelijk onderzoek en onderzoeksuitslagen de juiste diagnose en het juiste plan te destilleren. Het is geen losse vaardigheid, maar een samenspel van veel onderdelen: fundamentele (bio)medische kennis, het verzamelen van informatie, het afwegen van diagnoses en het opstellen van beleid. Tijdens de coschappen leren geneeskundestudenten dit door te observeren, te oefenen met medestudenten en simulatiepatiënten, maar bovenal door dit daadwerkelijk uit te voeren bij de patiënt. Maar juist die leeromgeving staat onder druk. Door o.a. hoge werkdruk, fusies van ziekenhuizen, beperkte financiële ruimte, uitplaatsing naar zelfstandige behandelcentra (ZBC’s) en verplaatsing van zorg naar de eerste lijn neemt de opleidingscapaciteit van coassistenten af. Daardoor is het voor coassistenten steeds lastiger om voldoende, gevarieerde en veilige oefenmomenten met echte patiënten te krijgen. Terwijl we juist die momenten nodig hebben om artsen goed op te leiden in klinisch redeneren. Simulatie en virtuele patiënten bieden een veelbelovend alternatief om studenten in de geneeskundeopleiding voor te bereiden op het zelfstandig zien van patiënten: studenten kunnen op hun eigen niveau veilig oefenen met een breed scala aan casuïstiek, zonder risico voor patiënten, en met directe feedback. AI maakt dat nu schaalbaar. Denk aan taalmodellen die realistische patiëntcasuïstiek genereren op maat van de student, die als virtuele patiënt een anamnese kan laten afnemen, of die als tutor kan meedenken en feedback geven op het redeneerproces zelf. Maar belangrijke vragen zijn nog onbeantwoord. Welke onderdelen van klinisch redeneren leer je goed in welke vorm van simulatie (van een virtuele patiënt achter een scherm, een simulatiepatiënt van vlees en bloed, tot een teamsimulatie met acteurs), en welke leer je het best bij een ‘echte’ patiënt? Hoe realistisch en betrouwbaar is de met behulp van AI gegenereerde casuïstiek? En hoe zorgen we dat studenten zowel leren klinisch redeneren mét AI als zélf kritisch blijven redeneren? Daar ga jij als promovendus onderzoek naar doen. Laten we kennismaken Let op: voeg bij je sollicitatie ook jouw publicatielijst mee aan het einde van jouw motivatiebrief of cv (indien relevant). De eerste ronde sollicitatiegesprekken starten in de week van 26 oktober . Deze gesprekken worden gehouden met de vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU en het hoofd onderzoek van onderwijs FdG VU. Heb je nog vragen? Voor inhoudelijke informatie over deze vacature kun je terecht bij Martine de Bruijne , vice-decaan onderwijs FdG VU, via mc.debruyne@amsterdamumc.nl . Een referentiecheck en screening kunnen onderdeel zijn van de procedure. Kom je bij ons in dienst, dan vragen we voor een aantal functiegroepen standaard een VOG (Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag). Bekijk wat het inhoudt en of het voor jouw functie van toepassing is. Interne kandidaten krijgen, bij gelijke geschiktheid, voorrang op externe kandidaten. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

items.title: Wissenschaftliche/-r Mitarbeiter/-in (m/w/d) - Promotionsstelle
items.desc: Die Technische Universität Clausthal ist eine forschungsstarke Universität mit hoher nationaler und internationaler Vernetzung. Die rund 80 Professor:innen, 1.100 Beschäftigten sowie 3.000 Studierenden genießen kurze Wege, einen persönlichen Umgang und die faszinierende Landschaft inmitten des UNESCO-Welterbes Harz. Die TU Clausthal ist als größte Arbeitgeberin der Region der wichtigste Wirtschaftsfaktor und bietet kulturelle Vielfalt und Internationalität. Die TU Clausthal hat sich gesamtuniversitär dem Leitthema der „Circular Economy“ verpflichtet und verfolgt das Ziel, in Forschung, Lehre und Verwaltung am Aufbau einer nachhaltigen Gesellschaft im digitalen Zeitalter mitzuwirken. Die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik am Institut für Informatik sucht zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:einen Wissenschaftliche:r Mitarbeiter:in (m/w/d) - Promotionsstelle im Bereich neuartiger Prozessoren und KI-Beschleuniger Die Stelle ist zunächst auf die Dauer von 3 Jahren befristet (Kennziffer: CE26-1) und mit 100% der regelmäßigen wöchentlichen Arbeitszeit zu besetzen. Die Bereitschaft zur akademischen Qualifikation wird vorausgesetzt. Die Stelle ist grundsätzlich teilzeitgeeignet. Die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik am Institut für Informatik der TU Clausthal forscht im Bereich des modernen Hardware-Entwurfs, mit dem Ziel leistungsfähiger sowie energie- und ressourceneffizienter Rechnersysteme. Einen Schwerpunkt bildet die Prozessorentwicklung, von Erweiterungen der offenen RISC-V-Architektur bis zu neuartigen Prozessorkonzepten. Weitere Themen sind Hardware für neuronale Netze und Approximate Computing. Unsere Forschung umfasst die gesamte Designkette von der Logiksynthese bis zur Implementierung auf FPGAs; dabei nutzen und erweitern wir moderne Hardwarebeschreibungssprachen wie Chisel und Clash. Sie interessieren sich für Rechnerarchitektur und Hardwareentwurf und möchten promovieren? Dann unterstützen Sie die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik in einem der folgenden Themenbereiche: Prozessorentwicklung: Die Arbeitsgruppe forscht an RISC-V Prozessoren und deren Erweiterungen sowie an neuartigen Prozessorarchitekturen, die ohne klassische Register auskommen. Die Aufgaben reichen von der Konzeption bis zur ersten Hardware-Implementierung auf FPGAs. Hardware-Beschleuniger für Spiking Neural Networks: Die Arbeitsgruppe forscht an energieeffizienten Hardware-Beschleunigern für Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) und hat dafür eine eigene Architektur sowie Chisel-basierte Entwurfswerkzeuge entwickelt. Die Aufgaben reichen von der Weiterentwicklung der Architektur und der Werkzeuge bis zur Umsetzung größerer Netze und neuer Anwendungen auf FPGAs. Aufgabengebiet Forschung in einem der beiden Themengebiete mit dem Ziel der Promotion Veröffentlichung Ihrer Ergebnisse auf internationalen Konferenzen und in Fachzeitschriften Mitwirkung in der Lehre im üblichen Umfang, auf Deutsch oder Englisch Einstellungsvoraussetzungen Vorausgesetzt werden: Mit überdurchschnittlichen Noten abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master oder gleichwertig) in Informatik, Elektrotechnik, Computational Engineering oder einer verwandten Fachrichtung Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit Bereitschaft zur Kooperation mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern Hohes Engagement und Selbstständigkeit Kenntnisse in Rechnerarchitektur und im Umgang mit FPGAs Gute Englischkenntnisse wünschenswert: Kenntnisse von RISC-V, Chisel, (Spiking) Neural Networks Was wir bieten Die Möglichkeit zur Promotion in einem aktiven Forschungsumfeld, mit viel Freiraum für eigene Ideen und persönlicher Betreuung Eine abwechslungsreiche und anspruchsvolle Tätigkeit in dem lebendigen Umfeld einer Hochschule eine tarifliche Vergütung nach dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder (TV-L), sowie zum Jahresende eine Jahressonderzahlung nach dem TV-L und eine separate Zusatzversorgung als Betriebsrente (VBL), 30 Tage Urlaub sowie arbeitsfreie Tage an Heiligabend und Silvester Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie durch flexible Arbeits- und Teilzeitmodelle sowie Mobilem Arbeiten im Rahmen der dienstlichen Möglichkeiten betriebliches Gesundheitsmanagement, Angebote des Hochschulsports sowie über Corporate Benefits zukunftsorientierte Entwicklungs- und Qualifizierungsmöglichkeiten die Möglichkeit zur aktiven Mitwirkung an der Weiterentwicklung unserer Universität alle Vorteile einer Beschäftigung im öffentlichen Dienst Haben wir Ihr Interesse geweckt? Bewerben Sie sich auf unserer Homepage über den Button "Online-Bewerbung" (siehe unten). Gleichstellung mit ihren Facetten, Chancengerechtigkeit, Diversität und Familienfreundlichkeit ist der TU Clausthal ein wichtiges Anliegen. items.title: PhD position in AI and multimodal digital liver pathology
items.desc: PhD position in AI and multimodal digital liver pathology (ref. BAP-2026-622) Laatst aangepast: 10/10/26 A full-time PhD position is available for an enthusiastic and highly motivated researcher to develop artificial intelligence methods for the multimodal analysis of chronic liver disease and liver cancer. The position is based in the Govaere Research Group at the Department of Imaging & Pathology, Faculty of Medicine, KU Leuven, and is embedded in a close collaboration with Prof. Jeroen Dekervel, with co-supervision by Prof. Asier Antoranz. The Govaere Research Group is part of the […] You have strong programming skills, preferably in Python; proficiency in R is an additional asset. A solid foundation in machine learning, deep learning, statistics or data science. Motivation to work at the interface of AI, pathology and translational liver research, and commitment to completing a doctorate within four years. Excellent spoken and written English. Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary team. Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills. Desirable: Experience in computer vision, digital pathology or whole-slide image analysis. Experience with self-supervised learning, vision or multimodal foundation models, multiple-instance learning, image-omics integration or explainable AI. Familiarity with molecular or spatial-omics analysis, multimodal data integration, radiomics or MRI analysis. Prior knowledge of pathology, chronic liver disease or cancer biology; this is welcome but not required. Being eligible to apply for a FWO PhD fellowship. See following link for criteria. https://www.fwo.be/en/support-programmes/phd-fellowships/# Offer A full-time PhD position for one year, extendable after a positive evaluation, with funding foreseen for a total of four years. A multidisciplinary project with access to clinically relevant human datasets and expertise in pathology, molecular profiling, hepatology, …

PhD position: modeling menopause-related heart rhythm disorders
items.desc: Job Description Menopause induces profound electrical and structural changes in the heart, yet the mechanisms driving this transition, and the reasons it dramatically increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders in women, remain largely unexplored. In this PhD project, you will play a central role in uncovering these mechanisms by developing advanced, multi‑scale computational models of atrial electrophysiology. You will work with one of the most comprehensive and unique datasets available worldwide: high‑resolution intra‑operative electrical mapping data recorded directly from the human atria during cardiac surgery, combined with ECG, PPG, hormone profiles, and continuous vital signs. All data is collected within Erasmus MC, giving you direct access to clinicians, engineers, and the surgical team collecting the data. This means you will not rely on synthetic or incomplete datasets but you will build models grounded in rich, real-world physiology. Your task is to transform these multimodal datasets into patient‑specific “digital twins” that simulate how atrial electrophysiology evolves across the menopausal transition. You will design and calibrate mechanistic models at the cellular, tissue, and organ scale; develop numerical methods and optimization pipelines; and run large-scale simulations to reconstruct remodeling trajectories and identify the critical “breaking points” that lead to arrhythmias such as sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation. The mechanistic insights and model outputs you generate will directly feed into the women‑specific arrhythmia detection algorithms developed by our industrial partner. Your work will therefore have a clear translational pathway toward real‑world digital health solutions. Beyond modeling, you will contribute to algorithm development for arrhythmia prediction and collaborate closely with clinical researchers during patient recruitment and data collection. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining computational modeling, physiology, and real clinical data. Your work will directly advance women‑specific arrhythmia detection and care, making a scientific impact that is both academically significant and clinically meaningful. “What I enjoy most is seeing how mathematical models can reveal mechanisms that cannot be directly observed from data.” - team member The position will be available by Q4 2026. The project is funded by Health-Holland. Work environment You will conduct your research within the Translational Electrophysiology Unit of the Department of Cardiology at Erasmus MC. The group is internationally recognized for its work on cardiac electrophysiology and collaborates closely with the Department of Cardiothoracic Surgery and multiple research groups at TU Delft. You will join a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and collegial team of clinicians, engineers, and scientists who work together to understand and treat cardiac arrhythmias. The environment is dynamic, supportive, and rich in opportunities for scientific growth. Qualifications And Skills We are looking for a motivated researcher with: A MSc or MEng degree in Mathematics, Biomedical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Computational Science, or a related field. Strong interest in computational modeling, simulations, or mathematical physiology. Experience with dynamical systems, numerical simulation, or finite‑element–based modeling approaches is a strong plus. Programming experience (preferably Python, but other languages are also a plus). Affinity with clinical or patient‑related research. Excellent communication skills and ability to work in a multidisciplinary team. Strong analytical mindset and enthusiasm for scientific discovery. Terms of employment A full‑time, 4‑year PhD position. A gross monthly salary between € 3.217,- and € 4.077,- (scale OIO) based on a full-time workweek of 36 hours. A salary increase of 3.5% from May 2027, according to the collective labor agreement (CLA). Excellent fringe benefits, such as a 13th month that is already paid out in November and an individual travel expense package. Pension insurance with ABP. We take care of approximately 2/3 of the monthly contribution. Special benefits, such as an incompany physiotherapist and bicycle repairer. And there is also a gym where you can work on your fitness after work. A supportive team and excellent supervision. Opportunities to attend international conferences and courses. A dynamic research environment at the largest academic medical center in the Netherlands. More information Make this job your next career move! Apply now using the application button. For more information about the role, please contact Dr. Vehpi Yildirim, Department of Cardiology (mail (mailto:v.yildirim@erasmusmc.nl)or +31 (0)6 812 496 74), or Prof. Dr. Natasja de Groot, Department of Cardiology, Erasmus MC via mail (mailto:n.m.s.degroot@erasmusmc.nl).

items.title: Doctoral Researcher, MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design”
items.desc: MSCA Doctoral Network position “Electric solar wind sail mission design” We are now looking for two (2) Doctoral Researchers. This PhD topic is part of the “Electric solar wind sail doctors” (E-Sailors) network, funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network Programme. The E-Sailors network is designed to train the next generation of Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) scientists, developers and advocates. This particular Doctoral Researcher (DR) will work with in-orbit results of on-going missions, such as Foresail-1 p developed by Aalto University with the E-sail payload from the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI), as well as the DR will develop new and improved in-orbit E-sail experiments for future missions in lunar orbit and deep space. The DR will be enrolled at and hosted by Aalto University, Finland, with the main supervisor Jaan Praks, co-hosted by the FMI with the E-sail researcher Dr. Petri Toivanen. Research field : Space technology, payload development Supervisor : Jaan Praks Offered by : Aalto University, School of Electrical Engineering General Description Of Programme And Host The Electric solar wind Sail doctors (E-Sailors) is a challenge-based Doctoral Network that aims to bring Electric solar wind sail (E-sail) from low Earth orbit (LEO) demonstration missions to the operational environment of the solar wind. It is delivered by 8 universities in cooperation with FMI, where E-sail was invented, and 4 companies. E-sail is a highly innovative and potentially disruptive propellantless propulsion system. An operational E-sail consists of hair-thin and kilometres-long wires, or tethers, which are charged at a high voltage creating an electrostatic sheath (electric sail) which deflects solar wind particles and generates the propulsive effect in interplanetary environment. Successful and rapid development and deployment of the technology will ensure EU's leadership in the exploration and exploitation of deep space, the next commercial space frontier. The programme is designed to achieve the following training objectives for our doctoral researchers: Equip them with core scientific skills and specialised knowledge in designing experiments for demonstrating space technologies and developing space missions; Provide them with a wide range of transferrable skills, such as Open Science and FAIR, communicating science to public, advocacy, networking etc.; Develop their business and entrepreneurship skills, such as IPR management, preliminary business planning, pitching to investors, starting start-ups. Aalto University is a leading Finnish university combining science, technology, design, and business to foster innovation and multidisciplinary research. The Aalto Space Lab is a comprehensive facility dedicated to the development, integration, and qualification of small satellites and space payloads. The laboratory features an advanced electronics development environment equipped for precision soldering, calibration, functional testing, and sensor characterization. A dedicated cleanroom area supports the assembly and integration of flight hardware, ensuring high reliability and adherence to space standards. Adjacent to the electronics lab, the Space Technology Testing Laboratory provides an advanced thermal–vacuum facility that enables environmental testing of complete satellites and subsystems under simulated space conditions. This includes vacuum, thermal cycling, thermal balance, and outgassing testing, essential for qualifying hardware for launch and orbital operation. The Space Lab also offers access to a wide suite of engineering and simulation software for electronics design, spacecraft systems modelling, structural and thermal analysis, and mission performance verification. Together, these resources support the full development cycle—from early concept design and prototyping to environmental qualification and flight readiness. The Aalto Space Lab serves as a key hub for small satellite and payload research, education, and technology demonstration, supporting academic projects, collaborative research initiatives, and industrial partnerships that advance Finland’s growing role in space technology. Description Of Specific PhD Project Please indicate in your cover letter which of the two positions you are primarily interested in. Position 1: The E-Sailor 8 The E-Sailor 8 doctoral position focuses on developing advanced methods for E-sail tether deployment monitoring and safety, combining simulation, laboratory testing, and in-orbit validation. The candidate will create dynamical and photorealistic 3D models of the tether and spacecraft to support both engineering analysis and visual monitoring during deployment, working in coordination with the RT3D development led by E-Sailor 15. The research includes conducting laboratory and in-orbit experiments using data from the Foresail-1p mission, analysing tether dynamics, imaging, and operational behaviour. Based on these results, the doctoral researcher will propose and evaluate new deployment schemes and safety strategies, contributing to the reliability of future E-sail missions. The work will result in models and validated methods shared with the wider community to support ongoing and upcoming E-sail technology developments. Duration of the work contract and place of employment: The position is based at Aalto University (24 months) with collaboration at CrystalSpace (CS) (12 months), under the supervision of Jaan Praks (Aalto) and Jaan Viru (CS). Position 2: The E-Sailor 4 The E-Sailor 4 doctoral position focuses on the design and engineering of an electric sail (E-sail) payload system for nanospacecraft, with a particular emphasis on developing the payload for the ESTCube-LuNa mission. Building on previous demonstrations such as ESTCube-1, ESTCube-2, and Foresail-1p, the project aims to apply lessons learned to create a more capable and reliable E-sail payload. The work involves analysing previous mission data, defining requirements for new payloads, and designing the mechanical, electrical, and deployment subsystems for ESTCube-LuNa. E-Sailor 4 will also lead the development and testing of a prototype payload, performing functional and environmental tests to verify its performance and requirements for spacecraft integration. The research will result in three main publications covering lessons learned, design development, and prototype testing. In the final project phase, the doctoral researcher will spend 6 months at Spacecraft Anatomy (SA) to gain industrial experience in space hardware manufacturing and qualification. The project will deliver a E-sail payload prototype design and strengthen the technological foundation for future nanospacecraft missions using E-sail propulsion. Duration of the work contract and place of employment: The main supervisor of the DR at Aalto University, Finland (15 months) is Assoc. Prof. Jaan Praks. The DR will also be co-supervised by the E-sail inventor Petri Toivanen while working for 15 months at the FMI, Finland and by Dr. Iaroslav Iakubivskyi while working 6 months at Spacecraft Anatomy, Estonia. Additional details of the positions Starting date: The position is expected to start during 2026. Trial period: 6 months Target degree: Doctoral degree from Aalto University, Finland Approximate gross salary: The salary for a Doctoral Researcher at Aalto University is 3143 EUR per month, which will be adjusted according to the eligible allowances based on MSCA funding. The family allowance will be clarified with the selected candidate once their situation is defined. The salary at FMI is 2900-3200 EUR/month at the beginning of employment. The starting salary at Spacecraft Anatomy is approx. 2700 EUR/month, plus family allowance, if applicable. Requirements For PhD Position Master's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Space Technology, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or closely related field. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Research experience and independent work experience evident through technical projects, theses, publications, or technical reports. This includes the evidence of innovative thinking or novel approaches to technical problems, the ability to synthesize information from multiple sources to advance understanding and demonstrated curiosity and persistence in pursuing technical challenges. Strong academic and development track record with demonstrated proficiency in orbital mechanics and propagators (GMAT, STK, or similar), propulsion systems, spacecraft dynamics, space systems, space mission and environment analyses, cubesats, small spacecraft systems, space plasma physics, software development and version control (Git), simulation software development (experience in multiple fields are considered beneficial). Proven ability to work autonomously on complex technical problems and demonstrated problem-solving skills in technical/engineering contexts. Experience working with interdisciplinary and international teams while maintaining individual accountability, such as driving projects forward without extensive guidance. Please submit description of personal contributions and level of independence, project outcomes and impact, and references in terms of publications, theses, technical reports, simulations, analysis, code samples, or documentation (multiple references are considered beneficial). The above duties are not exhaustive; the PhD candidate may be required to undertake other tasks consistent with the role and the objectives of the E-Sailors Doctoral Network. items.title: PhD Position Video-based Hand Motion-tracking for Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis at TU Delft
items.desc: Are you passionate about human movement and developing clinical tools for understanding human movement disorders? Job Description Challenge: Over a quarter of a million people in the Netherlands alone have rheumatoid arthritis (RA) with a majority suffering from debilitating pain and inflammation that makes hand dexterity and work, at times, impossible. While anti-inflammatory and analgesic drugs are the main line of relief, new drugs and treatments are needed and being developed for long-term care. At the same time a major challenge in RA management is quantifying the effectiveness of treatments under real-world conditions. Change: We need technologies to measure and quantify changes in hand function due to daily life factors (sleep, stress, etc.…) and treatments/drugs in the home setting. These technologies would enable drug developers, physiotherapists and physicians to make objective and quantitative assessments regarding the effectiveness of treatments. Impact: Once we understand the effects of stressors and treatments on RA flare ups and hand function, clinicians will be able to more closely target treatments and plan daily routines that minimize pain and suffering from rheumatoid arthritis. We are seeking a PhD candidate for a 4-year contract to develop and apply computational models and video-based tools to capture hand movement and function with deployment in the home environment as the target. Furthermore, you will apply these tools to help us investigate the potential causes and timings of flare ups during patients’ daily lives. You will work primarily with video data, musculoskeletal models, and pose estimation algorithms. The models and algorithms you develop will be part of open source and data repositories affiliated with the broader research program and TU Delft’s commitment to Open Science. You will be an integral part of the ‘Care is coming home!’ program: a 5-year project executed by a large consortium consisting of 2 technical universities (TU Delft, UTwente), 6 hospitals (Amsterdam UMC, Erasmus MC, Leiden UMC, Maartenskliniek, Maastricht UMC, Radboud UMC), 13 companies (Able Human Motion, Biomex, Cue2Walk, DanuSports, Kinetic Analysis, Lode Holding, Madglove, ModelHealth, Moveshelf, Orikami, Sabender (Enterprising Company), Trinoma, VicarVision), 1 rehabilitation centre (Daan Theeuwes Centrum) and 5 patient organisations (Hersenletsel.nl, Hersenstichting, Parkinson Vereniging, ParkinsonNL, ReumaNederland). In total the program will encompass 9 PhDs and 5 postdocs to address the issue of translating health care to the home environment. This PhD position is hosted by the Biomechanical Engineering Department at TU Delft where you will be a part of both the Computational Biomechanics (Seth) and Neuromuscular Control (Mugge) Labs. In addition to research, there are many opportunities to develop your academic career by mentoring and teaching BSc/MSc students, presenting at international conferences, and participating in workshops/training and exchange programs abroad. Job requirements You Should Have MSc in engineering or similar discipline by the start date of the position Experience with mechanical modeling and simulation Experience in computer programming/scripting (e.g., C++, Python, Matlab, etc.) Experience collecting human experimental data (movement, video, or similar) Excellent written and oral communication skills in English The following aspects will help you stand out: Thriving in multidisciplinary environments Curiosity-driven and self-motivated working attitude Knowledge of biomechanical modeling, anatomy, vision-based motion capture, machine learning, control systems Keep in mind that this describes the background we imagine would best fit the role. If you do not meet all the requirements, but believe that you are up for the task, we absolutely want to hear your motivation and how you would fit! The PhD process is a learning experience, so let us know what you want to learn and develop as a PhD candidate. You can view the full job vacancy here. Application deadline: 21 October 2026

items.title: PhD position: modeling menopause-related heart rhythm disorders
items.desc: Job Description Menopause induces profound electrical and structural changes in the heart, yet the mechanisms driving this transition, and the reasons it dramatically increases the risk of heart rhythm disorders in women, remain largely unexplored. In this PhD project, you will play a central role in uncovering these mechanisms by developing advanced, multi‑scale computational models of atrial electrophysiology. You will work with one of the most comprehensive and unique datasets available worldwide: high‑resolution intra‑operative electrical mapping data recorded directly from the human atria during cardiac surgery, combined with ECG, PPG, hormone profiles, and continuous vital signs. All data is collected within Erasmus MC, giving you direct access to clinicians, engineers, and the surgical team collecting the data. This means you will not rely on synthetic or incomplete datasets but you will build models grounded in rich, real-world physiology. Your task is to transform these multimodal datasets into patient‑specific “digital twins” that simulate how atrial electrophysiology evolves across the menopausal transition. You will design and calibrate mechanistic models at the cellular, tissue, and organ scale; develop numerical methods and optimization pipelines; and run large-scale simulations to reconstruct remodeling trajectories and identify the critical “breaking points” that lead to arrhythmias such as sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation. The mechanistic insights and model outputs you generate will directly feed into the women‑specific arrhythmia detection algorithms developed by our industrial partner. Your work will therefore have a clear translational pathway toward real‑world digital health solutions. Beyond modeling, you will contribute to algorithm development for arrhythmia prediction and collaborate closely with clinical researchers during patient recruitment and data collection. This position is ideal for someone who enjoys combining computational modeling, physiology, and real clinical data. Your work will directly advance women‑specific arrhythmia detection and care, making a scientific impact that is both academically significant and clinically meaningful. “What I enjoy most is seeing how mathematical models can reveal mechanisms that cannot be directly observed from data.” - team member The position will be available by Q4 2026. The project is funded by Health-Holland.

items.title: PhD Candidates in advanced arc and friction stir welding processes for recycled aluminium
items.desc: About The Position The position is a 3-year doctoral research fellowship starting in 2027. The PhD candidate will be embedded in the welding and joining research activities of SFI FAST and will work closely with NTNU, SINTEF, and leading international industrial partners in the aluminium value chain. The PhD position focuses on understanding the influence of impurities coming from recycled Aluminium on the weldability of different alloys. These impurities can alter the weldability, microstructure, and performance of Aluminium welds compared to the reference alloy. Solidification and liquation cracking, pore formation, heat-affected zone softening, and degradation of corrosion resistance are some examples of possible challenges. However, the knowledge is limited about any of these possible changes. Therefore, the candidate needs to provide a thorough investigation of the welding process using conventional techniques and develop new methodologies. In addition, the welding procedure adoption to enhance the performance of the alloys based on their metallurgical characteristics shall be developed. Therefore, the candidate should have a great understanding of the welding process-microstructure-performance. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. You will be supervised by Professor Vahid Hosseini. About The Project SFI FAST (Future Aluminium Structures) is a national Centre for Research-based Innovation (SFI) funded by the Research Council of Norway and the aluminum industry. The Centre is led by NTNU in close collaboration with SINTEF and a broad consortium of 15 leading industrial partners across the aluminium value chain. FAST runs from 2026 to 2034 and represents one of Norway’s most ambitious long-term research initiatives within aluminium materials, manufacturing technologies, and circular economy. The primary objective of FAST is to establish the scientific and technological knowledge base required to enable the large-scale use of post-consumer scrap (PCS) aluminium in high-value, structural, and safety-critical products. FAST adopts a through-scale and through-process research methodology, integrating materials science, manufacturing processes, product and structural design, and lifecycle performance. A key outcome of FAST is the development of the FAST Virtual Lab, a digital framework combining experimental data, physics-based models, and data-driven methods to support design, manufacturing, and decision-making across aluminium value chains. Education and competence building are central pillars of FAST. The Centre will educate more than 18 PhD and postdoctoral researchers and over 100 MSc students, strengthening Norway’s international position in aluminium research and innovation. The two positions posted here will be among the first ones to start in the Centre. Please see the centre’s website: Future Aluminium Structures (FAST) - NTNU Duties of the position Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate Take part in the mandatory PhD research education programme Develop arc welding (GTAW and GMAW) and Friction stir welding for alloys with different impurity levels to minimize welding defects and improve mechanical and corrosion performance Develop knowledge in the influence of impurities on the weld’s physics, defects, microstructure, and performance Thermodynamic modelling of solidification and precipitation behaviour of recycled aluminium Development of weldability tests to quantify welding performance of Aluminium Alloys Advanced characterization of welded samples using Laser Confocal Microscopy, In-situ mechanical testing, SEM, FIB, and EBSD. Conduct and publish high-level research in peer-reviewed journals and international conferences Work closely with industrial and academic partners and participate in relevant SFI FAST activities, including mentoring and supervising MSc students Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant Master's degree in Mechanical engineering, Materials Engineering, Metallurgical Engineering or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. You must have an academically relevant background within fusion and solid-state welding, welding metallurgy, and material characterization Documented strong background in: Experimental welding research Material characterization and testing Excellent written presentation skills and oral English language skills The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Basic knowledge of robotic welding Knowledge of weld monitoring systems with focus on arc characteristics and thermal cycle analysis Knowledge of thermomechanical modelling of welding process Scandinavian language skills Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Highly motivated Able to work independently Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them Present and discuss your research with other professionals Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity Show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject Analyse data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed Keen interest in learning and working in teams Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We offer Exciting and stimulating tasks in a strong international academic environment SFI FAST facilities, industrial network, and a joint PhD environment An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Working capital that can be used to implement the project Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 3 years. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme through out the period of employment. items.desc: Role Description The successful candidate will join a research team working on AI-driven, simulation-based decision support for resilient and sustainable production. As a doctoral student, you will develop intelligent methods that help manufacturing companies maintain stable operations, improve energy efficiency, and adapt to disruptions and changing energy conditions. The project will combine digital twins, discrete-event simulation, predictive modelling, multi-objective optimization, and AI-based decision support to support production planning and control. The research will address production sequencing, resource allocation, energy-aware scheduling, and disruption management, with possible use of coordinated multi-agent AI systems to balance productivity, resilience, energy cost, renewable energy use, and environmental performance. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with industrial partners and is expected to contribute to both scientific knowledge and practical decision-support solutions for manufacturing. The employment comprises full-time doctoral studies, including coursework and research. This can also be demonstrated by an internationally recognized test such as IELTS (overall score of 6.5), TOEFL (total score of 90), PTE (total score of 62), etc. We will also evaluate the candidates based on the following assessment criteria: • Good ability to successfully undertake doctoral studies. • Good knowledge and experience in modeling and simulation of manufacturing systems, such as discrete-event simulation (DES). • Good knowledge and experience in machine learning, reinforcement learning, and AI-based optimization for production control. • Good knowledge and experience in multi-objective optimization and predictive modeling. • Proficiency in programming in Python, C++, or similar languages. • Ability to work independently, plan and conduct research, and achieve set goals. • Good communication and collaboration skills. • Experience in industrial collaboration, applied research, or practical implementation. In this employment, great emphasis will be placed on good knowledge and experience in modeling and simulation of manufacturing systems, such as discrete-event simulation (DES), as well as good knowledge and experience in machine learning, reinforcement learning, and AI-based optimization for production control. items.title: PhD: Impact evaluation of climate policies in agricultural and forest landscapes
items.desc: Career at WUR About Us Plenty of variety and challenges Pleasant working atmosphere Time for personal development Proper work-life balance Internationally leading Your job Have you ever wondered how we can ensure that climate mitigation and adaptation policies are fair, coherent, and effective? Are you interested in applying state-of-the-art impact evaluation techniques to analyze how climate policies affect land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity? Do you good communication skills in Spanish? Then this might be your next step! Climate change mitigation and adaptation in agriculture and forestry represent a “wicked problem”, shaped by uncertainty, conflicting objectives, institutional fragmentation and time pressure. While the EU has set ambitious climate targets for 2030 and climate neutrality by 2050, progress in agriculture and forestry remains insufficient and current policy frameworks have not yet resulted in significant climate mitigation and adaptation results, or generated the systemic transformation needed. This PhD position is part of the EU-Horizon project “ Evidence-based pathways towards fair, coherent and effective climate policies for Europe’s agriculture and forestry (PolicyForClimate) ”, which will develop tools and frameworks to enable policymakers and other stakeholders to design fair, coherent, and effective climate mitigation and adaptation policies in the EU. The project will use AI-assisted evidence synthesis, a policy-lab approach, and embedded case studies to offer a continuously updated evidence base on policy impacts, trade-offs, synergies, and spillovers. Your research will focus on developing, applying, and validating a novel mixed-methods framework for ex-post impact evaluation of climate policies in forestry and agricultural landscapes. By combining state-of-the-art econometric techniques with qualitative participatory approaches, you will empirically analyze how climate policies have affected land use, GHG emissions, and biodiversity metrics. This will require conducting systematic reviews on existing impact evaluation frameworks, run workshops and focus group discussions with various stakeholders, collect, combine, and analyze farm-level primary data and secondary spatially explicit data. Start date: February 2027. Your Duties And Responsibilities Include Conduct systematic literature reviews and workshops to develop a mixed-methods ex-post impact evaluation framework for climate policies; Apply rigorous econometric methods together with qualitative assessments, particularly from policy sciences, to evaluate the impact of specific climate policies on land cover, carbon, and biodiversity metrics; Conduct focus group discussions with various stakeholders in the EU to validate the proposed impact evaluation framework and results from the empirical analyses; Write research papers and present research findings at international academic conferences; Collaborate with our research partners and contribute to the dissemination of project results. You will work here You will be based at the Forest and Nature Conservation Policy Group (FNP) at Wageningen University . The FNP group focuses on the political, socio-economic and cultural dimensions of forests and nature. Our research addresses major challenges including biodiversity conservation, deforestation, forest transitions, climate change and landscape management in both the Global North and Global South. You will be jointly supervised by Dr. Jorge Sellare and Prof. Bas Arts from Wageningen University (WU-FNP), and by Dr. Dario Schulz (EFI) in the research group headed by Sven Wunder. Your qualities We are looking for a researcher with a strong interest in climate adaptation and mitigation policies and in exploring the underlying causal mechanisms through which they affect land, GHG emissions, and biodiversity. You enjoy working with both quantitative and qualitative data and are motivated to conduct research that combines rigorous econometric analysis with qualitative assessments and with real-world challenges facing farmers and forest owners. Fieldwork in Spain will be an important component of the PhD project, so Spanish language skills are critical. You should be enthusiastic about working with farmers and able to spend time in rural areas of Spain under fieldwork conditions. You Also Possess a successfully completed MSc degree in agricultural economics, environmental economics, environmental policy, forestry or a closely related field; affinity with applied econometrics and / or qualitative mixed methods and an interest in developing your skills in both; knowledge of GIS and spatial data analysis is an asset; good skills with statistical software such as R, Stata or Python; very good communication skills in Spanish (min. level B2); For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level . Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here . We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment . A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team. The gross salary for the first year is € 3.204,- per month rising to € 4.051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. Coming from abroad Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees. Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account, dual career programs or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.
