items.title: Akademische/r Mitarbeiter/in, Doktorand/in (w/m/d) in der Wissenschaft in Vollzeit für den Bereich NVH Fahrzeugakustik & Validierung von Antriebssystemen im Gesamtsystemverbund
items.desc: Wasserstoff gilt als einer der zentralen Hoffnungsträger für die Energiewende und wird eine Schlüsselrolle in der Defossilierung von Industrie, Mobilität und Energiesystemen einnehmen. Im Zuge der Elektrifizierung des Antriebsstrangs rücken zugleich die Schwingungs- und Akustikeigenschaften moderner Fahrzeuge stärker in den Fokus der Produktentwicklung: Während klassische Verbrennungsmotorgeräusche wegfallen, treten neue Geräuschquellen in den Vordergrund und auch der Leichtbau verändert das dynamische Verhalten der Fahrzeugstruktur nachhaltig. Ihre Forschung verbindet diese beiden Zukunftsfelder. In Ihrer Forschung befassen Sie sich zum einen mit der systemischen Analyse und Optimierung von Brennstoffzellen, Batterien und Elektrolyseuren auf der übergeordneten System- und Betriebsebene. Zum anderen untersuchen Sie das Schwingungs- und Akustikverhalten von Fahrzeugkomponenten unter anderem im Spannungsfeld zwischen NVH-Verhalten und Leichtbau. Ziel ist es, durch geeignete Betriebsstrategien Effizienz, Lebensdauer und Wirtschaftlichkeit der Energietechnologien im realen Einsatz zu maximieren und zugleich mittels gemisch physisch-virtueller Valdiderung das strukturdynamische und akustische Verhalten von Bauteilen und Fahrzeugen zu charakterisieren und gezielt zu optimieren. Neben geeigneten Simulationswerkzeugen stehen hierfür experimentelle Validierungsumgebungen auf unterschiedlichen Systemebenen zur Verfügung. Des weiteren umfassen Ihre Aufgaben die selbstständige Leitung und Mitarbeit in Industrie- und öffentlich geförderten Forschungsprojekten sowie die Beteiligung an der Durchführung von Lehrveranstaltungen. Das abschließende Ziel Ihrer wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeiten in unserem Team ist Ihre Promotion. Sie wollen durch Ihren persönlichen Beitrag in der Erforschung neuer technischer Systeme sowie Methoden und Prozesse für die Produktentwicklung der Zukunft Impulse geben und der Gesellschaft und den Unternehmen Wege weisen? Dann sind Sie bei uns im IPEK-Team genau richtig ! Als Team hochmotivierter wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeitenden gestalten wir durch unsere Forschung die Zukunft der nachhaltigen Produktenwicklung in unseren Unternehmen . Ihre Aufgaben Selbstständige Leitung und Mitarbeit in Industrie- und öffentlich geförderten Forschungsprojekten, Modellbildung und Simulation sowie experimentelle Untersuchung an eigens entwickelten, modernen Prüfständen, Betreuung von Übungen und Lehrveranstaltungen sowie Veröffentlichung wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse auf nationalen und internationalen Konferenzen sowie in Zeitschriften. items.title: PhD in Acoustic Performance of Timber Structure Connections
items.desc: Introduction Are you fascinated by improving the acoustic performance of timber buildings? Help develop advanced numerical models that predict sound transmission and bridge the gap between sustainable construction and high acoustic performance. Join this joint PhD project between TU/e and DTU! Job Description Buildings made from timber and other biobased materials generally have a significantly lower carbon footprint than conventional concrete or masonry constructions. However, lightweight timber structures often exhibit high variability in sound insulation, and poor acoustic performance remains a barrier to their wider adoption in the construction industry. A still poorly understood source of this variability lies in the connections between structural components, such as screws, nails, steel brackets, and adhesive joints. Whether a floor is screwed or glued together, and how widely spaced the fasteners are, can significantly affect how sound travels through a building. Current prediction methods largely ignore these details, while more detailed models are often too computationally expensive for practical use. Developing methods that are both physically accurate and computationally efficient is therefore the central challenge of this project. We offer a PhD position (4-year contract) within the QUIET-ARC project, a collaboration between Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e) and the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) as part of the EuroTech Universities PhD programme. As a PhD candidate in the QUIET-ARC project, you will investigate how different connection types and layouts influence sound transmission in timber buildings, develop efficient numerical simulation methods to model these effects, and quantify the uncertainty introduced by construction variability into acoustic predictions. Noise is recognised by the World Health Organisation as a major public health concern. By improving the predictive capability of computational models for timber buildings, this research supports more reliable prediction tools for sustainable constructions and contributes to the wider adoption of low-carbon building materials. The project will take place under joint supervision of dr.ir. Cédric Van hoorickx (TU/e, specializing in numerical modelling of sound transmission) and dr.ir. Jonas Brunskog (DTU, with expertise in the acoustics of lightweight structures). You will be based in the Building Acoustics research group (https://building-acoustics.net/) in the Department of the Built Environment at TU/e, and will spend approximately six months at DTU’s Acoustic Technology group in Denmark. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in acoustics, building physics, civil engineering, mechanical engineering, or related disciplines. A research-oriented attitude. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). The following experience could be considered an advantage and may be highlighted in your motivation letter: Affinity for building acoustics, vibro-acoustics, or structural dynamics Previous experience with/affinity for computational methods Previous publications and scientific communications Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. items.desc: Projet de thèse CIFRE — Apprentissage de stratégies de mémoire et de décision pour des systèmes d’IA locaux Mots-clés : Agentic systems, LLMs, persistent memory, sequential decision-making, reinforcement learning, model routing, model specialization, sovereign AI. Contexte scientifique USTS développe un projet d’IA souveraine, entièrement exécuté sur une infrastructure locale, pour permettre aux entreprises de garder le contrôle de leurs données et de leurs systèmes, tout en préservant la précision et la qualité des résultats. La thèse s’intéresse aux systèmes fondés sur des modèles de langage capables d’accomplir des tâches séquentielles : exploiter des informations, interagir avec des outils, conserver des connaissances et adapter leurs actions aux résultats obtenus. Dans ce cadre, la réussite dépend de décisions prises à différents moments de l’exécution, dont les conséquences peuvent être différées. Le choix d’une information à conserver influence les actions futures. Le choix d’un modèle détermine le coût et la qualité d’une étape. Une vérification peut éviter la propagation d’une erreur, mais consomme des ressources supplémentaires. La mémoire, les actions et l’utilisation des modèles constituent ainsi des composantes interdépendantes du processus de décision. Le problème étudié sera celui de l’apprentissage de stratégies coordonnées pour ces composantes, dans un environnement où les informations évoluent et où le calcul disponible est limité. Question scientifique et hypothèses Comment apprendre conjointement des stratégies de mémoire, d’action et d’utilisation des modèles qui maintiennent la fiabilité des tâches séquentielles lorsque les informations évoluent et que les ressources de calcul sont limitées ? Une hypothèse centrale est que l’apprentissage de ces stratégies à partir de la réussite des tâches complètes peut améliorer le compromis entre fiabilité et coût de calcul par rapport à des stratégies optimisées séparément. Cette hypothèse conduit à plusieurs questions : comment estimer l’utilité future d’une information ? Comment attribuer un échec à une décision de mémoire, à une action ou au choix d’un modèle ? Comment répartir les ressources entre génération, recherche d’information et vérification ? Dans quelles conditions les stratégies apprises restent-elles efficaces sur de nouvelles tâches ? Ces questions seront étudiées à travers des hypothèses explicites et des expériences permettant de les confirmer, de les réfuter ou d’en préciser les conditions de validité. Programme de recherche Les premiers travaux porteront sur la formalisation du système comme un problème de décision séquentielle, éventuellement partiellement observable. Il s’agira de définir les observations accessibles, les opérations de mémoire, les actions possibles et les contraintes de ressources. Cette formulation permettra d’étudier des objectifs d’apprentissage combinant réussite de la tâche, erreurs et coût d’exécution. L’apprentissage de la mémoire La recherche portera sur la sélection, la représentation, la mise à jour et la récupération des informations en fonction de leur utilité pour les décisions futures. Une attention particulière sera accordée aux informations corrigées ou devenues obsolètes, ainsi qu’aux conséquences différées des opérations de mémoire. L’attribution des erreurs et l’apprentissage des décisions Lorsque l’évaluation porte sur le résultat final, il peut être difficile d’identifier les décisions responsables d’un échec. Les travaux pourront étudier des signaux intermédiaires, des objectifs auxiliaires ou des méthodes d’attribution permettant d’améliorer l’apprentissage sans réduire l’évaluation à la qualité de chaque étape prise isolément. L’allocation adaptative du calcul Le système devra choisir quand mobiliser un modèle spécialisé, solliciter un modèle plus coûteux, rechercher une information ou vérifier un résultat. L’objectif sera d’apprendre ces choix en fonction de l’état de la tâche, de l’incertitude et des ressources restantes. Ces volets contribueront à une même problématique. Leur articulation et leur priorité seront précisées à partir de l’état de l’art et des premiers résultats expérimentaux. Recherche sur les modèles Les modèles constituent le moteur du système étudié. La thèse comprendra donc des travaux sur les modèles génératifs, les modèles de décision et leurs modalités d’apprentissage. Les recherches pourront porter sur la spécialisation de modèles locaux, la distillation de comportements ou la conception d’objectifs d’entraînement tenant compte de la réussite de trajectoires complètes. Elles examineront également la répartition des capacités entre un modèle unique et un ensemble de modèles coordonnés par une politique de routage. L’enjeu sera de déterminer quelles capacités doivent être apprises dans les modèles et quelles décisions doivent être prises au cours de l’exécution. Les architectures seront comparées en intégrant le coût de leur coordination et les interactions entre spécialisation, mémoire et décision. Évaluation et contributions attendues L’évaluation reposera sur des tâches séquentielles permettant de faire varier la durée des trajectoires, l’évolution des informations, la disponibilité des outils et les budgets de calcul. Des comparaisons avec des méthodes de référence, des études d’ablation et des évaluations sur des tâches non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage permettront d’identifier l’origine des gains et leurs limites. Les mesures porteront notamment sur la réussite des tâches, les erreurs critiques, la stabilité des résultats, la latence et les ressources consommées. Les expériences étudieront également la propagation des erreurs et la capacité du système à récupérer après une décision incorrecte. Les applications métier serviront à confronter les méthodes aux conditions d’utilisation réelles. Pour un métier et un ensemble de tâches définis, l’objectif sera d’étudier dans quelles conditions un système local peut atteindre une qualité comparable ou proche de celle de solutions généralistes accessibles au public. Cet objectif sera évalué selon des critères et une marge d’écart définis à l’avance. Les contributions attendues pourront comprendre une formulation du problème, des méthodes d’apprentissage originales et une caractérisation expérimentale de leurs propriétés, de leur capacité de généralisation et de leurs limites. Les résultats donneront lieu à des publications scientifiques et à des expérimentations reproductibles. Profil recherché Vous êtes titulaire d’un master 2 ou d’un diplôme d’ingénieur en informatique, intelligence artificielle, mathématiques appliquées ou dans un domaine proche. Vous avez de solides connaissances en machine learning et en modèles de langage, ainsi qu’une bonne maîtrise de Python et d’un framework d’apprentissage profond tel que PyTorch. Des connaissances en apprentissage par renforcement, en décision séquentielle, en statistiques ou en optimisation seront appréciées. Vous souhaitez mener un travail de recherche et avez une appétence pour les solutions d’IA et l’ingénierie nécessaire à leur expérimentation. Vous savez formuler des hypothèses, concevoir des expériences et analyser leurs résultats. Conditions et candidature Durée : 36 mois. Lieu : La Réunion. Début : à convenir avec le laboratoire d’accueil. Rémunération : ... Moyens de calcul : serveurs équipés de plusieurs GPU. Encadrement USTS : Hugo. Laboratoire d’accueil et direction de thèse : à préciser. Financement envisagé : dispositif CIFRE. Pour candidater, envoyez votre CV et un court texte présentant votre intérêt pour le sujet à recrutement@usts.ai. Vous pouvez joindre un mémoire, un article ou un projet illustrant votre expérience. Rémunération : 26 000,00€ à 30 000,00€ par an Avantages : Prise en charge du transport quotidien Lieu du poste : En présentiel

items.desc: Die Process and Data Science Gruppe (PADS) sucht kontinuierlich nach talentierten neuen MitarbeiterInnen, die an der Schnittstelle von Data Science und Process Science arbeiten möchten. Es gibt offene Stellen auf allen Ebenen (PhD, Postdoc, Software Engineer, etc.). Bei Interesse senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung bitte direkt an applications@pads.rwth-aachen.de Wenn Sie sich bewerben, geben Sie bitte relevante Informationen an und begründen Sie, warum Sie zu unserer Forschung im Bereich Process Mining beitragen können. Generische Bewerbungen werden aussortiert. Zeigen Sie, dass Sie wissen, was die Gruppe tut und was Sie zum Stand der Technik im Process Mining beitragen wollen. Bitte beachten Sie, dass das PADS-Schwerpunktkolloquium für Personen gedacht ist, die sich auf PADS-bezogene Themen spezialisieren möchten, d.h. auf Process Mining oder andere Ansätze, die Prozess- und Datenwissenschaft miteinander verbinden. Lesen Sie unbedingt das Springer-Buch "Process Mining: Data Science in Action" (ISBN: 978-3-662-49850-7) ausführlich und seien Sie darauf vorbereitet, technische Fragen zu den von Ihnen belegten PADS-Kursen zu beantworten (z.B. konkrete Modelle anhand von Daten zu erstellen). Der beste Zeitpunkt für das mündliche PADS- Schwerpunktkolloquium ist kurz vor der Masterarbeit. Studierenden mit schlechteren Noten in den BPI/APM/IDS-Kursen wird dringend empfohlen, ein anderes Schwerpunktkolloquium zu wählen oder sich sehr gut vorzubereiten. Es ist gewünscht, dass sich StudentInnen bewerben, welche Ihre Masterarbeit in unserer Gruppe schreiben möchten. Alle Stellen sind grundsätzlich Vollzeitstellen, es besteht aber auch die Möglichkeit, in Teilzeit zu arbeiten. Die Vergütung erfolgt in Anlehnung an den Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TV-L) unter Berücksichtigung Ihrer Berufserfahrung. Die RWTH ist ein Arbeitgeber der Chancengleichheit. Wir freuen uns daher über Bewerbungen von allen qualifizierten Bewerberinnen und Bewerbern, insbesondere aus derzeit benachteiligten Personengruppen. Ihre Ansprechpartnerin Frau Mara Nitschke Tel.: +49 (0) 241 8021902 E-Mail: applications@pads.rwth-aachen.de Wissenschaftliche MitarbeiterIn – DoktorandIn (PhD) Als DoktorandIn haben Sie die Möglichkeit, in einem Bereich mit vielen offenen wissenschaftlichen Herausforderungen zu forschen. Sie werden eine begrenzte Lehraufgabe haben und Bachelor- und MasterstudentInnen betreuen. In einem Zeitraum von vier Jahren erhalten Sie ausreichend Zeit, um Spitzenforschung zu betreiben und Ihre Arbeit auf den führenden Konferenzen in diesem Bereich zu präsentieren. Sie werden in einer starken und fokussierten Forschungsgruppe arbeiten, in der Sie die erforderliche Unterstützung und Rückmeldung erhalten. Nach einem PhD in PADS können Sie wählen, ob Sie eine Karriere in der Industrie oder in der Wissenschaft anstreben wollen. Der Grund dafür ist, dass Process Mining herausfordernde Forschungsprobleme bietet und gleichzeitig ein großer Bedarf an Experten besteht, die an der Schnittstelle von Prozessen und Daten arbeiten. Anforderungen Ein Master-Abschluss in Informatik oder Data Science (oder einer benachbarten Disziplin wie Operations Research, Elektrotechnik und Statistik) Sie verfügen über ausgezeichnete Sprachkenntnisse in Englisch und sind bereit, Ihre Ideen zu präsentieren. Sie sind in der Lage, Forschungsprototypen (z. B. in Java oder Python) zu entwickeln, um groß angelegte Experimente durchzuführen. Sie legen Wert auf Präzision, d. h. Sie sind bestrebt, Ihre Ideen rigoros zu präsentieren und zu prüfen. Sie kennen sich mit Process Mining aus (lesen Sie z. B. die process mining book oder den Coursera MOOC besucht "Process Mining: Data science in Action"). Sie haben ein echtes Interesse und/oder Erfahrung in den Bereichen Data Science, Process Science, Process Mining, maschinelles Lernen, Prozessmanagement und/oder Operations Research.

items.title: PhD Researcher / Doctoral Researcher (m/f/d) Bioinformatics & AML
items.desc: Department of Internal Medicine II, Research Group: Functional Genomics of Acute Leukemia (Heads: Dr. Lorenz Bastian / Prof. Dr. Claudia Baldus) The position is part of the newly established research project “LUCID-AML – Learning-based Unsupervised Clustering of transcriptomIcs to Detect developmental, functional and prognostic subtypes in AML across age”, funded by the Deutsche José Carreras Leukämie-Stiftung. It is closely linked to our DFG-funded Clinical Research Unit “CATCH-ALL: Towards a Cure for Adults and Children with Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia”, where clinical and basic researchers work together to define mechanisms of leukemogenesis and treatment resistance across age groups. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) affects people of all ages, but its incidence increases steeply in older adults, while survival decreases sharply with age. AML can be classified into transcriptomic groups that reflect cytogenetic lesions, reveal developmental origins and link leukemias to normal hematopoietic states. However, consistent subtype definitions and robustly validated tools for applying them across cohorts are lacking. The project builds on ALLCatchR and our work on machine-learning frameworks for disease classification and the identification of novel molecular subtypes in acute lymphoblastic leukemia. LUCID-AML will integrate more than 8,000 bulk AML gene-expression profiles from multiple cohorts with single-cell data, molecular genetics, diagnostic classifications, drug-response data and clinical outcomes. The project aims to establish reproducible, gene-expression-based AML subtypes while accounting for age and treatment. Further aims are to define their developmental origins and make the resulting models available as transparent, open-source tools for research and clinical diagnostics. items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Interactive and Immersive Simulation of Animal Navigation in the Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group
items.desc: Paygrade E13 TV-L Working Hours 100% (suitable for part-time) Institution Institute of Physics (School of Mathematics and Natural Sciences) Location Oldenburg (Oldb) Application Deadline 30.10.2026 First day of work 01.01.2027 Limited for 3 years About us The Quantum Biology and Computational Physics Group at the University of Oldenburg invites applications for a three-year doctoral research position at the interface of computer science, physics, and biology. The project investigates how interactive and immersive simulation can help scientists explore, experiment with, and reason about computational models of animal navigation. Animals navigate using multiple environmental and sensory cues. Computational models allow researchers to investigate possible mechanisms, test hypotheses, and predict movement patterns. This PhD will develop and scientifically evaluate interactive approaches that make such models more accessible to systematic exploration, comparison, and interpretation. Virtual and mixed reality are promising approaches, alongside conventional desktop and potentially web-based interfaces. Research questions How can researchers interactively vary model parameters, assumptions, sensory cues, and competing navigation hypotheses? Under which conditions do immersive interfaces (VR/MR) offer advantages over conventional interfaces for exploring complex navigation simulations? How can interactive representations help connect individual simulated decisions and trajectories with population-level or large-scale movement patterns? How can the scientific value of different interaction techniques be evaluated in realistic research tasks? Your tasks Develop a research framework for visualizing and interacting with computational models of animal navigation. Design and implement methods to explore parameters, manipulate assumptions, compare hypotheses, and inspect simulated outcomes. Integrate existing or newly developed navigation models and simulation data into interactive environments, potentially using Unity, Unreal Engine, or other appropriate technologies. Design and conduct evaluations with researchers to assess how different interfaces support scientific exploration, interpretation, and reasoning. Collaborate closely with scientists in physics, biology, and computer science; document and disseminate results through scientific publications and presentations. Pursue an independent doctoral research project leading to a PhD. items.title: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators
items.desc: PhD Position Experimental Analysis of Boiling Instabilities in Advanced Nuclear Steam Generators Help determine operational limits of next-gen nuclear steam generators! Job description Advanced nuclear reactor designs like the high temperature gas cooled reactor or molten salt reactor offer certain advantages compared to traditional light water reactors. One such advantage is their potential to operate with a high thermal efficiency. This advantage stems from the fact that these reactors operate at much higher temperatures, enabling superheated steam generation. Traditional light water reactors utilize so-called U-tube steam generators in which saturated steam is produced. It is well known that such steam generators suffer from spontaneous oscillations of two-phase mass flow and pressure drop on the shell side. This phenomenon is well understood in light water reactors, allowing for safe and stable operation. However, these boiling instabilities are more severe in once-through helical steam generators, as the dryout point will shift rapidly up and down along the helical tubes. This oscillating behaviour can lead to thermal fatigue of the tube walls, which can ultimately result in mechanical failure. While this phenomenon is already complex enough in and of itself, it typically coincides with parallel channel instabilities. In this project, you will develop and build a laboratory steam generator set-up to study boiling instabilities in helical tubes. In the first year, you will help design and build the set-up along with a team of skilled technicians and an energetic supervisory team. Subsequently, you will study the characteristics of the boiling instabilities within the set-up and compare them to a numerical model. Your Working Environment You will join the Process & Energy (P&E) department at TU Delft’s Mechanical Engineering faculty.Our department works along the themes of Energy, Flow and Processes. You will work together with top researchers highly skilled in thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics. Moreover, we collaborate with researchers from the Reactor Institute Delft. You will have opportunities for professional development through both technical and non-technical courses. We expect that as part of your PhD you will take the lead on interacting and collaborating with other researchers at TU Delft, with research groups at other universities, and with industry and other stakeholders. Furthermore, we expect that you have 2) A MSc. degree in either chemistry, physics or mechanical engineering or similar field. 3) Strong affinity with thermodynamics and transport equations. 4) A keen interest in the nuclear industry and its future roles in society. 5) An interest in transient modelling and analysis. 6) Good communication skills and the ability to be a team player in a highly multidisciplinary setting. items.title: PhD Position Flexibility in Nuclear Power
items.desc: PhD Position Flexibility in Nuclear Power Can nuclear- and renewable energy play nice? Job description Both Europe and the Netherlands are committed to transitioning to a CO2-neutral economy by 2050. As part of this commitment, the Netherlands has built large-scale wind park, and a significant amount of energy comes from solar power as well. While wind and solar energy help to decarbonize power generation, it also comes at a cost. Due to the intermittent availability of wind and solar energy, grid congestion can occur (which means that the grid lacks sufficient capacity to handle demand or supply of electricity). Therefore, the grid must be carefully managed. In many countries, gas power plants help manage the grid. However, since natural gas counteracts decarbonization, the question arises: “which other technologies can help reduce grid congestion? Small modular reactors (SMR) - nuclear reactors below 300 MWe – may be able to operate flexibly to help counteract grid congestion. As such reactors have less inertia, they are better suited to load-following than large-scale nuclear power plants. Even so, their ramp rates are much lower than other technologies. Through smart design of the power cycle and the inclusion of thermal energy storage, ramp rates of SMR’s can be greatly enhanced. In this thesis project, you will design advanced power cycles with or without energy storage for SMR’s to enable enhanced load-following. Using numerical techniques, you will couple transient power cycle modelling with nuclear reactor modelling to analyse any feedback to the reactor. You will run different load-following scenarios to ascertain technologically feasible enhanced ramp rates. You will be assisted by an expert supervisory team during your PhD. As the Dutch Nuclear industry is growing rapidly, and the Dutch Government has announced a significant expansion of nuclear energy, your results may actively contribute to shaping the Dutch nuclear landscape. items.title: PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN
items.desc: Job requisition Id: 16967 Job type: PhD positions Contract hours min: 38 Contract hours max: 38 Location: Leiden Applying is possible until: 12 November 2026 Teaser Text The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers capable of redefining kinase drug discovery beyond the ATP paradigm, by developing the experimental and computational tools, modular assays and workflows needed to systematically target non-conserved regulatory interfaces, such as kinase dimerization and substrate-binding sites. Proof-of-concept will be demonstrated on three representative kinases: EGFR, BRAF and the understudied “dark” kinase LTK. ANA-KIN brings together 11 beneficiaries and 9 associated partners across Europe and the USA, including Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (coordinator), University of Crete, Goethe University Frankfurt, Saarland University, EPFL, CNRS, Pompeu Fabra University, VIB, KU Leuven, INSERM and Leiden University, together with industrial partners such as AstraZeneca, Novartis, Servier and Skylight Therapeutics. The network combines chemical biology, structural biophysics (single-molecule FRET, cryo-EM, nanodiscs), AI-driven drug design and cell biology in an integrated learn–design–test loop. Twelve Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will each pursue an individual research project, benefit from co-supervision across institutions and sectors, carry out two research secondments at partner organizations, and follow a structured network-wide training program covering scientific, transferable, open-science and entrepreneurial skills. In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network. The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model predictions using second-harmonic generation (SHG)-based conformational profiling. The project will be supervised by Prof. Gerard J.P. van Westen (Leiden University), with Prof. Ruslan Efremov and Dr. Joshua Salafsky as co-supervisors. What you will do Conduct original and novel research in deep learning, AI, and cheminformatics for kinase drug discovery; Develop, benchmark and openly share models, datasets and decision-support dashboards following FAIR and open-science principles; Collaborate closely with experimental and computational DCs in the network, and carry out two research secondments abroad (VIB and Skylight Therapeutics, Belgium); Publish and present scientific articles at international journals and conferences; Participate in the ANA-KIN network-wide training events, schools and outreach activities; Contribute to educational activities; Write a dissertation. What you bring A MSc degree in Computer Science, AI, (Computational) Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, or a relevant related field; Good knowledge of and experience with machine learning and deep-learning techniques (e.g. PyTorch); Good knowledge of and experience with cheminformatics and/or computational chemistry (e.g. RDKit, molecular descriptors, docking); Interest in structural biology, protein kinases and drug discovery; affinity with peptide or biophysical data is an advantage; Highly motivated to both perform foundational research and apply the developed methods to real-world problems; creative, ‘making things work’ mentality, independent, and communicative team player; Willingness to travel and to carry out research secondments at partner institutions abroad; Excellent programming skills (preferably Python); Good academic writing skills and interest in participating in educational activities; Excellent proficiency in English (oral and written). MSCA eligibility criteria At the date of recruitment, candidates must not have been awarded a doctoral degree; Mobility rule: candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the date of recruitment. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account. Where you will work Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research Our institute is a center of excellence for multidisciplinary research on drug discovery and development. Leiden University consistently ranks within the top-20 world-wide within the subject-based QS Ranking in Pharmacology and Pharmacy. At LACDR, we develop innovative scientific concepts in fundamental and translational research underlying the discovery and optimization of drugs, and personalized medicines. We aim to optimize the route to novel drugs that are both efficacious and safe, and therefore our research focuses on drug discovery and safety, bio-therapeutics, and systems biomedicine and pharmacology. State-of-the-art expertise and infrastructures ensure that we are strategically positioned in (inter)national collaborations, thus further strengthening the development of novel concepts and their application in a clinical and industry environment. Computational Drug Discovery Research in this group, headed by Gerard van Westen, focusses on computational methods integrated in different parts of the drug discovery process. More specifically, topics include innovative treatments for cancer, kinase and GPCR drug discovery, proteochemometrics, selectivity and polypharmacology modeling, allosteric modulation, drug resistance modeling, de novo molecular design, and novel methods in the domain of machine learning. For more information see: http://www.cddl.nl Research at our faculty The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from artificial intelligence, computer science, mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and almost 6,000 students. We are located in the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry meet. For more information, see http://www.science.leidenuniv.nl . What we offer We offer a full-time appointment for 48 months as a Doctoral Candidate within the MSCA Doctoral Network ANA-KIN, starting late 2026. The appointment is initially for one year; after a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for the remaining period. Salary ranges from € 3.204,- tot € 4.051,- gross per month (pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities). Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3%), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school. As an ANA-KIN Doctoral Candidate you will also follow the network’s training program, including summer schools, workshops and an industrial immersion workshop, and your progress will be monitored by a Thesis Advisory Committee including an independent mentor. What we value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area can be made to Prof. Gerard van Westen, gerard@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact Brigitte Kraakman, b.p.m.kraakman@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application online via the blue button below. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents quoting the vacancy number and “ANA-KIN DC10”: application letter (including a statement confirming that they meet the MSCA eligibility criteria) curriculum vitae a list of grades two references (who have agreed to be contacted) Only applications received no later than November 12th can be considered. The selection procedure will take place in November. Selected candidates may be invited for an interview in the last week of November / 1st week of December, during which you are kindly requested to be available. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. items.title: PhD Researcher Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (1.0 FTE)
items.desc: Job requisition Id: 16924 Job type: PhD positions Contract hours min: 38 Contract hours max: 38 Location: Leiden Applying is possible until: 31 January 2027 Teaser Text PhD Researcher in “A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Culture: Insights from Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Southeast Asia” ( Minaret Project ), 1.0 FTE. The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) invites applications for one PhD Researcher (1.0 FTE, 4 years) from September/October 2027 – September/October 2031 to join the Minaret Project, a HORIZON Unit Grant-funded interdisciplinary and transnational research initiative, which examines the interconnection between law, religion and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies to promote democracy and good governance. The project brings together 11 universities with 15 PhD researchers across 3 work packages and 15 subprojects, with the applicant contributing to the subproject Neo-Imperialism and Constitutional Reform: The Global Dimension . This subproject examines to what extent international organizations and global governance actors act as neo-imperial forces shaping constitutional reform in North Africa and the Middle East. It will explore how donor-driven “rule of law” and “good governance” programs are developed, interpreted, and implemented in countries such as Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria. Particular attention will be paid to how the legal frameworks promoted by international actors relate to the government practices in these countries, and in particular to those embedded in local traditions and religious values. Drawing on policy-document analysis and elite interviews with a diverse range of actors -including international advisers, domestic policymakers, civil-society representatives, legal practitioners, religious scholars, and community leaders-, the study will investigate how transnational constitutional models are negotiated, adapted, resisted, or hybridized in practice. It will contribute to debates on postcolonial constitutionalism by examining the processes through which legal and governance norms circulate across borders, as well as the forms of influence, dependency, and agency that shape their adoption. Ultimately, the project seeks to develop a nuanced account of how external interventions affect perceptions of legitimacy, legal pluralism, and sovereignty in transitional Muslim-majority societies. What you will do The PhD researcher will join the Leiden-based Minaret team, working closely with two senior-researchers and two external mentors (one academic and one non-academic, associated with the project). The position provides the opportunity to conduct original empirical research on the underlying structures of constitutional reform in said countries, while also contributing to public engagement and the collaborative life of the project. All PhD researchers are required to undertake two secondments abroad with the project’s associated partners, one academic and one non-academic, of between two and six months' duration. This will not only enhance research capabilities but also equip the PhD researcher for academic and non-academic roles. Academic Research Conduct socio-legal and policy analysis with key stakeholders in selected countries. Write a doctoral dissertation and co-author academic publications based on qualitative research. Contribute to the project’s comparative framework within the subproject; within the work package (Imperial Genealogies and Constitutional Formation) and between the work packages. Communications & Engagement Present research findings at events organized by the research project, such as 3 summer schools and 4 training events. Willingness and ability to spend extended periods abroad for fieldwork and 2 secondments. Help organize international workshops, conferences, and events with academic and civil society partners. Contribute to project website and social media accounts. Where you will work The Faculty of Law is based in both Leiden and The Hague and, with over 7,000 students and approximately 600 staff members, is one of the largest law faculties in the Netherlands. The faculty is committed to innovative, multidisciplinary research and a constantly evolving curriculum that addresses key societal challenges. Our faculty is large enough to make an impact on both a national and international scale, yet small enough to offer a personal and engaging learning experience. In this way, we contribute every day to a safer and more sustainable world. Impact with law! For more information, please visit https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/law . The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) is part of the Leiden Law School. The VVI seeks to advance knowledge of the formation and functioning of legal systems in their social contexts, the impact of these systems on society and vice versa, their effectiveness in governance, and their contribution to development. The Institute adopts a socio-legal and global approach, doing research on law in the books and law in action in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. VVI staff teaches several socio-legal thematic and regional courses for both Dutch and foreign exchange students. In addition, VVI provides PhD supervision, advisory services and training courses to policy makers and practitioners. For more information, see www.vvi.leidenuniv.nl . What you bring In our team, we are looking for someone who can work independently while also contributing to a collaborative environment. Since every position is unique, we will devote careful attention to your onboarding. If some aspects of the work are new to you, we will identify what support you need and develop a tailored plan for your professional growth. We do not expect candidates to already have all the qualifications listed below. Training will be provided in areas such as socio-legal studies, research methods, and the specificities of constitutional reform in the Middle East. That said, this position will be a good fit for you if you recognize yourself in many of the following: A MSc or LLM in Anthropology, Political Science, Law, International Studies, International Relations, Development Studies, or a closely related field; Demonstrated experience in conducting empirical research, ideally in the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria); Experience working with (inter)national civil society actors; Knowledge of constitutional reform, especially in relation to religion, democracy, and governance; Familiarity with socio-legal literature and qualitative research methods; Ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary and international research team; Familiarity with one of the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria) is an asset; Knowledge of written and spoken Arabic is strongly recommended. What we offer Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development. You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University. We also offer: An employment contract for the duration of four years. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities; A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student); A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone. For more information about employment conditions, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions What we value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. Leiden University aims to be an inclusive community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to develop to their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research means inclusive education and research. Want to apply or find out more? If you want to apply straight away, click the application button. If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact Dr. Nadia Sonneveld, at n.sonneveld@law.leidenuniv.nl. You can apply until 31 January 2027; To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application in English addressed to Dr. Nadia Sonneveld using the blue button at the top of this text. Interviews are scheduled in February-March 2027. Please include with your application the following: A cover letter stating your motivation for this position; A curriculum vitae; Transcripts from your bachelors and masters degrees; A major writing sample (i.e Master’s thesis, article, or other class paper); Names of 2-3 academic references. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission The Accelerators and Communications for HPC Group leads cutting-edge research and development around accelerators/coprocessors in HPC and high-performance networking. We collaborate closely with the major vendors in the topic for HPC: NVIDIA and Intel. We organize locally international events such as the PUMPS Summer School, PATC Courses on CUDA/OpenACC, and annual hackathons, and collaborate in the organization of related international conferences and workshops such as SC, IEEE Cluster, or AsHES. The group has been recently awarded one of the prestigious ERC Consolidator Grants. We are looking to cover a PhD Student positions to work on the new hot topic of processing-in-memory applied to Homomorphically Encrypted Deep Learning Inference. Prospective candidates may take a look at the following paper to get an initial idea of our focus: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.16139 Group Web Page: https://www.bsc.es/discover-bsc/organisation/scientific-structure/accelerators-and-communications-hpc Key Duties Drive research in the above-mentioned topic, under the supervision of the Group Manager and the mentorship of a postdoctoral researcher Requirements Education MS in a related field Essential Knowledge and Professional Experience Low-level C/C++ Additional Knowledge and Professional Experience At least 2 years experience working with Processing in Memory Competences Good English Level Conditions The position will be located at BSC within the Computer Sciences Department We offer a full-time contract (35h/week), a good working environment, a highly stimulating environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure, flexible working hours, extensive training plan, restaurant tickets, private health insurance, support to the relocation procedures Duration: Open-ended contract due to technical and scientific activities linked to the project and budget duration Holidays: 22 days of holidays + 6 personal days + 24th and 31st of December per our collective agreement Salary: we offer a competitive salary commensurate with the qualifications and experience of the candidate and according to the cost of living in Barcelona Starting date: 16/11/2026 Applications procedure and process All applications must be submitted via the BSC website and contain: A full CV in English including contact details A cover/motivation letter with a statement of interest in English, clearly specifying for which specific area and topics the applicant wishes to be considered. Additionally, two references for further contacts must be included. Applications without this document will not be considered. Development of the recruitment process The selection will be carried out through a competitive examination system ("Concurso-Oposición"). items.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
items.desc: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About the Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main duties and responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants should submit a dossier including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About the University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián.

items.title: Doktorandplats - statistiker inom tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården
items.desc: Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna. Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård ansvarar för delar av läkarprogrammet. Inom forskarutbildning har vi en egen forskarskola i allmänmedicin. Vår primärvårdsforskning omfattar varierande projekt kring multisjuklighet, folksjukdomar som diabetes, nedsatt njurfunktion och psykisk ohälsa samt även pedagogiska projekt. Närmare 100 personer, av vilka cirka 30 doktorander, är anknutna till avdelningen. Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet? Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid. Forskargruppen Doktorandtjänsten finns inom forskargruppen för STEADY-CAN (Stockholm Early Detection of Cancer Study) vid Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård, Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS). Gruppen består av kliniskt aktiva forskare, statistiker och doktorander som arbetar med tidig upptäckt av cancer, i nära samarbete med Regionalt cancercentrum Stockholm-Gotland och internationella samarbetspartners. Gruppen är involverad i flera pågående forskningsprojekt, inklusive utveckling av statistiska och maskininlärningsbaserade prediktionsmodeller, longitudinell analys av blodprovsdata och registerbaserade kohortstudier inom cancerepidemiologi. Du kommer att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig grupp där statistiker, allmänläkare och epidemiologer arbetar nära varandra. I praktiken innebär det att du regelbundet diskuterar analysval med kliniker, förklarar statistiska metoder för personer utan statistisk bakgrund och själv lär dig om den kliniska vardagen i primärvården. Gruppen har regelbundna gemensamma analysmöten där du förväntas både ge och ta emot återkoppling på pågående arbete. Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter Detta doktorandprojekt kombinerar traditionell statistisk modellering och maskininlärning i tillämpad forskning kring tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården. Projektet använder data från STEADY-CAN-kohorten, som omfattar över 2,7 miljoner vuxna i Region Stockholm med länkade laboratorie-, journal- och registerdata. Under doktorandutbildningen kommer kandidaten att få bred kunskap inom överlevnadsanalys, prediktionsmodellering, maskininlärning och hantering av stora registerbaserade datamängder. Vi söker en motiverad doktorand med god bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. Den framgångsrika kandidaten förväntas ta ett stort eget ansvar genom hela projektet, med stöd från handledarna. Detta innebär konstruktion av analysdatamängder, statistisk analys och implementering av maskininlärningsmetoder, författande av vetenskapliga artiklar samt deltagande i institutionens seminarier och i nationella och internationella konferenser. Vad erbjuder vi? En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård. Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger. Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.* Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. Om du anser dig ha motsvarande kunskaper ska du följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Bedömning av motsvarande kunskaper för grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. B) Särskilt behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det särskilda behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: Intygar kunskaper i engelska (motsvarande Engelska B/Engelska 6 vid gymnasiet med godkänt betyg). Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan English language requirements for doctoral education. Kontroll av dokument Karolinska Institutet gör kontroll av dokumenten för att upptäcka förfalskningar. Karolinska Institutet förbehåller sig rätten att återkalla antagningsbeslut om förfalskningar eller oriktigheter påvisas. Inlämnande av falska handlingar är ett brott mot svensk lag och anses vara grund för rättsliga åtgärder. Färdigheter och personliga egenskaper Den sökande bör ha en gedigen bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. En examen i statistik/biostatistik eller matematisk statistik på avancerad nivå, t.ex. en masterexamen, är starkt meriterande. Utmärkta kunskaper i biostatistik och praktisk erfarenhet av överlevnadsanalys är meriterande. Tidigare erfarenhet av databehandling och statistisk analys är meriterande. Dessa erfarenheter ska företrädesvis vara från en medicinsk forskningsmiljö. Mycket goda kunskaper i statistisk programmering, företrädesvis i R, är avgörande för rollen. Erfarenhet av arbete med svenska registerdata är meriterande. Ett starkt intresse för medicinsk forskning i kombination med en passion för att tillämpa statistiska metoder för att besvara kliniskt relevanta forskningsfrågor är mycket önskvärt. Då STEADY-CAN-databasen, inklusive journal- och registervariabler och tillhörande beskrivningar, är på svenska är goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift ett krav. Handledningen och det internationella samarbetet sker delvis på engelska, varför goda kunskaper även i engelska i tal och skrift också krävs. Den sökande ska ha god kommunikationsförmåga, vilket är avgörande för att samarbeta med tvärvetenskapliga team och effektivt presentera forskningsresultat. Vi lägger mycket stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper i denna rekrytering. Den idealiska kandidaten bör vara: Självständig, strukturerad och med stark analytisk förmåga. Flexibel och ivrig att lära. Denna roll innebär kontinuerligt lärande och anpassning till nya metoder och utmaningar. Öppen för konstruktiva synpunkter och förmåga att delta i balanserad, analytisk självreflektion. Kandidaten ska även trivas med att arbeta i team och samarbeta väl med teammedlemmar med olika akademisk bakgrund. Förklara i ditt personliga brev hur du uppfyller de nödvändiga färdigheterna och egenskaperna. Villkor Doktorandplatsen innebär en anställning som doktorand under maximalt 4 år på heltid. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen i rekryteringsverktyget Varbi. Använd knappen uppe till höger och följ anvisningarna. Vi ser gärna att din ansökan är skriven på engelska, men det går också bra att ansöka på svenska. Din ansökan ska innehålla dessa dokument: Ett personligt brev och curriculum vitae Eventuella examensarbeten och publikationer Andra dokument som styrker de ovan efterfrågade färdigheter och egenskaper Dokument som styrker det grundläggande behörighetskravet (se A ovan) Dokument som styrker det särskilda behörighetskravet (se B ovan) Urval Urval bland behöriga sökande görs med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildning. En samlad bedömning av de sökandes meriter och lämplighet kommer att göras. Följande bedömningsgrunder tillämpas vid Karolinska Institutet: Dokumenterade ämneskunskaper av betydelse för forskningsområdet Analytisk skicklighet Övriga dokumenterade kunskaper/erfarenheter som kan ha betydelse för aktuell forskarutbildning Alla sökanden kommer att få information när rekryteringen är slutförd. KI tillämpar en lönestege vid lönesättning av doktorander. NVS Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård Vill du göra skillnad - och bidra till en bättre hälsa för alla? items.title: Thèse en IA, deep learning et Mathématiques appliquées
items.desc: Offre de thèse – Méta-apprentissage robuste et efficace pour la segmentation d’images médicales Lieu : Toulouse INP / IRIT, Toulouse, France Durée : 3 ans — Début prévu : 1er septembre 2027 Date limite de candidature : 23 novembre 2026 Rémunération : environ 2 800 € Nous recherchons un candidat ou une candidate motivé(e) pour développer des méthodes de méta-apprentissage capables de s’adapter à de nouvelles tâches de segmentation d’images médicales à partir d’un nombre limité d’exemples annotés. Le projet se situe à l’interface de l’apprentissage profond, de l’optimisation et de l’imagerie médicale. Le projet s’articulera autour de trois axes de recherche : Optimisation du méta-apprentissage pour améliorer la stabilité des méthodes et réduire leur coût en calcul et en mémoire. Analyse des relations entre tâches médicales pour identifier les connaissances transférables et limiter les interférences entre tâches hétérogènes. Adaptation structurée et efficace des modèles pour faciliter l’apprentissage de nouvelles tâches avec peu de données annotées. La thèse sera dirigée par le Pr Lotfi Chaari (Toulouse INP / IRIT) , avec un co-encadrement assuré par Dr Amel Aissaoui (Toulouse INP / IRIT) et Dr Alena Kopanicakova (Université de Genève, Suisse) . Une cotutelle pourra être envisagée. Profil recherché : diplôme de master ou équivalent en informatique, intelligence artificielle, mathématiques appliquées, science des données ou dans un domaine connexe ; solides compétences en programmation, de préférence en Python/PyTorch ; intérêt marqué pour les aspects mathématiques et algorithmiques de l’apprentissage ; bonne maîtrise de l’anglais écrit et oral. Une expérience en méta-apprentissage, segmentation d’images, optimisation numérique ou imagerie médicale serait appréciée, sans être obligatoire. Important — Conditions d’éligibilité au programme BEST : les candidats doivent être titulaires de leur master à la date limite de candidature, ne pas déjà détenir de doctorat et ne pas avoir résidé ou exercé leur activité principale en France pendant plus de 12 mois au cours des 36 mois précédant la date limite de candidature. Un excellent dossier académique et un fort potentiel pour la recherche doctorale sont attendus. Conditions complètes : https://doctorat.univ-toulouse.fr/cofund-best Description complète du sujet et modalités de candidature : https://docs.google.com/document/d/1YbqYcot7dJgQsgSfN68Wf6HC6IyylZbEV36gyGo5uGY/edit?usp=sharing Pour candidater : déposez votre candidature sur https://edd-projets.utoulouse.fr/ et envoyez, en parallèle, votre CV détaillé et vos derniers relevés de notes à amel.aissaoui@irit.fr and Alena.Kopanicakova@unige.ch , avec pour objet : Application – PhD in Robust and Scalable Meta-Learning for Medical Image Segmentation . Lieu du poste : En présentiel

items.title: Two PhD positions SNSF project “Governing the Party: How the Chinese Communist Party Holds Itself Together”
items.desc: Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies (IAOS), Chair of Modern Chinese Studies Two PhD positions SNSF project “Governing the Party: How the Chinese Communist Party Holds Itself Together” 80 % Start of employment 1 March 2027, temporary The Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies (IAOS) at the University of Zurich is the largest centre for research and teaching on Asia in Switzerland. Within the IAOS, the Chair of Modern Chinese Studies (Prof. Dr. Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt) works on the ideological and institutional foundations of Chinese Communist Party governance. The Chair invites applications for two doctoral positions in the research project “Governing the Party: How the Chinese Communist Party Holds Itself Together”, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). The project “Governing the Party” (SNSF, 2027–2031) takes the Chinese Communist Party seriously as an organisation. The CCP holds that the Party “leads everything” (党是领导一切的), yet how an organisation of more than 100 million members governs itself remains poorly understood. The project uses the Party's institutions as its main analytical lens without setting its ideas aside: organisational routines and ideological work are studied together, as parts of the same form of governance. It belongs to the Chair's wider research on Party governance, which concentrates on the Party below the centre, from provincial Party committees to village branches and the institutions in which the Party is present. We welcome contemporary and historical projects on the Party since 1949, using archival, documentary, ethnographic or computational methods. The research is organised around four broad areas: Forming its people: how the Party recruits, trains, evaluates and promotes its members and cadres, and what organisational life means for them. Making and enforcing its rules: how the Party regulates itself, supervises its members and handles misconduct. Producing shared meaning: how ideology is produced, recombined and put into practice across institutions and levels. Extending its organisation: how the Party builds and runs its organisations in state organs, enterprises, universities, social organisations and other institutions. These areas are an orientation, not a list of predefined topics; what matters most is an original and feasible proposal. The Chair already hosts projects on Party organisations in private and technology firms, on the regulation of cadres' work style, and on the Party's promotion of an “autonomous knowledge system”. Proposals should address distinct questions. The SNSF project funds two doctoral candidates and one postdoctoral researcher. Several team members may work in the same area, provided their questions are distinct. Your responsibilities Develop and complete an independent doctoral dissertation within one of the project's four areas of research, under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Jean Christopher Mittelstaedt Develop, with guidance, large datasets from published Chinese-language sources for the dissertation, and contribute to the project's shared analytical framework Publish findings from the dissertation in peer-reviewed journals and contribute to co-authored outputs of the project Conduct fieldwork, archival or interview research where the dissertation requires it and conditions allow Take part in the research activities of the team and present work at conferences Enrol in a doctoral programme of the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences at the University of Zurich Assist with the organisation of workshops and with limited administrative tasks of the project Your profile An excellent MA degree (or equivalent) in political science, sociology, Chinese studies, history or a related discipline, completed by the start of employment Proficiency in modern Chinese sufficient to work independently with Chinese-language primary sources A serious interest in political institutions and organisations, and the ability to engage with theory in comparative politics, political sociology, organisation studies or the study of ideology Training in at least one of the following: qualitative or interpretive methods, quantitative methods, computational text analysis. We do not expect candidates to arrive with all of these: the willingness to acquire new methods matters more than a complete toolkit at the outset Excellent written and spoken English; German is an asset but not required The ability to work independently as well as in a team, and a commitment to a shared project over four years The University of Zurich is committed to equal opportunity and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, origin or background. Information on your application What we offer Salary in accordance with SNSF guidelines Temporary employment, 48 months The possibility of applying for an SNSF mobility grant for a research stay abroad of six to twelve months during the project Regular supervision within a small team working on a shared analytical framework Funding for fieldwork, archival research, conference travel and workshops Eligibility for SNSF supplementary measures, including flexibility grants for researchers with children Employment under the policies of the University of Zurich, with its benefits for staff (continuing education, the UZH and ETH Language Center, childcare through the kihz foundation, and others) Information on your application Please submit your application as a single PDF file through the UZH job portal.
