items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Humanoid Robotics, 3D Perception and Embodied AI
items.desc: Beschreibung Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Doctoral Researcher in Humanoid Robotics, 3D Perception and Embodied AI The Advanced Manufacturing Lab (am|z) at ETH Zurich, led by Prof. Markus Bambach, is seeking a highly motivated Doctoral Researcher to conduct research in humanoid robotics, 3D perception, and embodied artificial intelligence for autonomous manufacturing. The position is embedded in an interdisciplinary research project aiming to enable humanoid robots to perceive, understand, and interact with complex manufacturing environments using novel RGB-D sensing technologies. We are looking for a candidate with a strong background in robotics, computer vision, or machine learning who is passionate about developing intelligent robotic systems and translating scientific concepts into working solutions. The successful candidate will investigate novel approaches to robot perception, simulation-to-real transfer, and autonomous manipulation, contributing to the development of intelligent humanoid systems capable of performing complex manufacturing tasks. Project background The Advanced Manufacturing Lab at ETH Zurich investigates advanced robotic technologies for flexible, intelligent, and autonomous manufacturing. This Doctoral Researcher is part of a collaborative research project focused on developing intelligent humanoid robotic systems using next-generation, single-chip RGB-D sensing technologies. The project aims to integrate novel depth-sensing hardware with advanced perception algorithms, simulation environments, and learning-based robotic control to enable autonomous and collaborative manufacturing operations. Research Activities Span Several Interconnected Areas 3D simulation and synthetic data generation: Development of realistic manufacturing environments and simulation pipelines for generating annotated RGB-D data 3D semantic perception: Development of learning-based methods for object detection, segmentation, and scene understanding using RGB-D sensor information Sim-to-real transfer: Investigation of methods for transferring perception and manipulation capabilities from simulation to physical robotic systems Autonomous robotic manipulation: Integration of perception, planning, and control for robotic handling and assembly operations Collaborative humanoid robotics: Investigation of learning-based coordination strategies, including multi-agent reinforcement learning, for cooperative manufacturing tasks Language-guided robotic actions: Exploration of approaches that enable robots to interpret natural-language instructions and translate them into executable actions The project combines fundamental research with experimental validation using physical humanoid robotic platforms and real manufacturing scenarios. The doctoral research will focus on selected scientific challenges within these areas, with opportunities to contribute to the development of a fully integrated autonomous humanoid manufacturing demonstrator. Job Description Conduct independent scientific research in humanoid robotics, 3D perception, and learning-based robotic systems Develop and evaluate novel algorithms for RGB-D-based object detection, semantic segmentation, and 3D scene understanding Design and implement realistic robotic simulation environments and synthetic data generation pipelines for manufacturing applications Develop methods for improving the transfer of perception and manipulation capabilities from simulation to real-world robotic systems Design and implement data acquisition, annotation, processing, and evaluation workflows for synthetic and real RGB-D datasets Integrate perception algorithms with robotic manipulation, motion planning, and control frameworks Investigate learning-based approaches to autonomous robotic decision-making, with opportunities to explore multi-agent coordination and language-guided manipulation Implement, test, and validate developed methods on physical robotic and humanoid platforms Plan and conduct scientific experiments, establish quantitative benchmarks, and systematically evaluate the performance of developed methods Develop reproducible research software and contribute to shared software frameworks and experimental infrastructure Publish research findings in leading international robotics, computer vision, and machine learning conferences and journals Collaborate with researchers and industrial partners involved in the project and contribute to the supervision of student research projects Profile We are looking for a highly motivated and independent researcher with strong analytical and programming skills, scientific curiosity, and a passion for intelligent robotic systems. items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Probabilistic Machine Learning
items.desc: Aalto University is a community of bold thinkers where science and art meet technology and business. We are committed to identifying and solving grand societal challenges and building an innovative future. Aalto has six schools with 14 000 students and a staff of 5000, of which more than 400 are professors. Our main campus is located in Espoo, Finland. Diversity is part of who we are, and we actively work to ensure our community’s diversity and inclusiveness. This is why we warmly encourage qualified candidates from all backgrounds to join our community. The Department of Computer Science is an internationally-oriented community and home to world-class research in modern computer science, combining research on foundations and innovative applications. With over 40 professors and more than 450 employees from 50 countries, it is the largest department at Aalto University and the leading computer science research unit in northern Europe. Computer science research at Aalto University ranks high in several international surveys (7th in Europe and 1st in the Nordics (NTU 2023); and 88th worldwide in Times Higher Education subject ranking 2025). We are now looking for a: Doctoral Researcher We are looking for a doctoral researcher(PhD student) with a strong background in probabilistic machine learning, statistics, applied mathematics, computer science, or a related field, and strong programming skills, to work on biology-informed machine learning for dynamical systems (see project description below). The position is based at the Department of Computer Science at Aalto University, Finland, within a research environment spanning the Computational Systems Biology group, the Finnish Centre for Artificial Intelligence (FCAI), and ELLIS Institute Finland. You will be supervised by Dr Julien Martinelli and Associate Professor Harri Lähdesmäki. The position offers a broad local research network in Bayesian machine learning and computational biology. Your network and team Dr Martinelli is an independent Research Fellow supported by an Academy Research Fellowship of the Research Council of Finland and develops Biology-Informed Machine Learning methods for biomedical applications. Associate Professor Lähdesmäki leads Aalto’s Computational Systems Biology group and has extensive expertise in Bayesian inference for biological systems. Project Description Ordinary differential equation (ODE) models provide interpretable descriptions of biological processes, but they are often incomplete: mechanisms may be only partly known, data are noisy and sparsely sampled, measurements vary across individuals and conditions, and some relevant biological states are unobserved. Purely data-driven models offer flexibility, but often ignore known biology and provide limited insight into uncertainty and mechanisms. These challenges motivate a broader Biology-Informed Machine Learning perspective [1]. The doctoral student’s thesis will focus on operationalising this perspective through the development of Biology-Informed Gaussian Processes (BioGPs). These are Bayesian dynamical models that combine known mechanistic components with flexible Gaussian process terms representing unknown or misspecified biology. Depending on the candidate’s interests, there may also be opportunities to connect this research with emerging foundation-model approaches for dynamical systems [2]. Key methodological questions shared across these directions include reliable uncertainty quantification, inference from heterogeneous trajectories, partial observability, and the integration of uncertain prior knowledge. A central goal will also be to go beyond trajectory prediction by coupling these approaches with methods for learning explicit, interpretable mechanistic ODEs, including their symbolic structure [3]. Lastly, recent work from the team includes nonparametric mixed-effect ODE models for population- and subject-specific dynamics [4], as well as GP-based approaches to modelling temporal single-cell data [5]. Selected references [1] J. Martinelli. “Position: Biology is the Challenge Physics-Informed ML Needs to Evolve”. In: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems. Vol. 38. OpenReview. 2025. [2] J. R. Hübers et al. “Foundation Inference Models for Ordinary Differential Equations”. In: Forty-third International Conference on Machine Learning. 2026. [3] C. Métayer, A. Ballesta, and J. Martinelli. “Data-driven discovery of digital twins in biomedical research”. In: Briefings in Bioinformatics 27.1 (2026), bbaf722. DOI: 10.1093/bib/bbaf722. [4] J. Martinelli et al. Bayesian Nonparametric Mixed-Effect ODEs with Gaussian Processes. 2026. arXiv: 2605.13088 [cs.LG]. [5] M. Y. Balik and H. Lähdesmäki. “Modeling Temporal scRNA-seq Data with Latent Gaussian Process and Optimal Transport”. In: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning. OpenReview. 2026. What We Offer The position belongs to the Aalto career system and the selected person will be appointed for a two-year fixed term appointment with an option for two-year renewal. The starting salary for the position is 3168,20 EUR per month. In addition to the salary, the contract includes occupational health benefits, and Finland has a comprehensive social security system. The annual total workload of research and teaching staff at Aalto University is 1 612 hours. The position is located at the Aalto University Otaniemi campus. Ready to apply? Please submit your application through our recruitment system Workday. The deadline for applications is 21.10.2026 at 23.59 (UTC +3). The position will be filled as soon as suitable candidate has been identified. To apply, please share the following application materials in one pdf file with us: CV Cover letter highlighting your research interests and how they align with the project (see Dr. Martinelli’s prior publications for reference) Example of academic writing (B.Sc/M.Sc thesis, project report from a course, etc.) Transcripts of MSc and BSc studies The degree certificate of your latest degree The candidates must have completed their master’s degree before the start of the contract period. Aalto University reserves the right for justified reasons to leave the position open, to extend the application period, reopen the application process, and to consider candidates who have not submitted applications during the application period. Further information Dr. Julien Martinelli, e-mail julien.martinelli@aalto.fi. HR Advisor Susanna Holma, e-mail "hr-cs@aalto.fi" (recruitment process) Want to know more about us and your future colleagues ? You can watch these videos: Aalto University – Towards a better world, Aalto People , and Shaping a Sustainable Future . And this webpage about Aalto and Finland: Why Finland? | Aalto University Check out our new virtual campus experience: https://virtualtour.aalto.fi/ ! items.title: PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys
items.desc: Cutting-edge Research for a Changing World PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys Reference code: 1057 - 2026/WD 1 Commencement date: as soon as possible Work location: Geesthacht Application deadline: November 12th, 2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. Your tasks development of physics-guided machine-learning models for composition-process-structure-property relationships in magnesium alloys combination of crystal plasticity, phase-field, precipitation, and machine-learning approaches into a unified digital twin framework implementation of simulation and machine-learning workflows in Python (e.g. PyTorch, Scikit-Learn, etc.) incorporation of experimental microstructure and texture characterization data obtained from optical microscopy, SEM, EBSD, XRD, and mechanical testing investigation of uncertainty quantification and explainable artificial intelligence methods (XAI) for materials modeling validation of computational predictions in collaboration with experimental and modeling researchers publication and presentation of scientific results in leading international journals, conferences, and workshops active contribution to the establishment of next-generation ICME and digital-twin methodologies for sustainable lightweight materials design Your profile master’s degree in mechanical engineering, materials science, computational engineering, physics, applied mathematics, data science, or a related discipline strong interest in computational materials science, digital twins, and machine learning good programming skills in Python experience with machine-learning methods and common scientific Python libraries is desirable knowledge of computational mechanics, finite element methods, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, or thermodynamic simulations is advantageous experience in analysis of experimental materials-science data is beneficial ability to work independently as well as within an interdisciplinary research team strong analytical and problem-solving skills highly proficient in spoken and written English motivation to conduct high-quality research at the interface of materials science, mechanical engineering, and artificial intelligence We offer you an exciting and varied job in a research centre with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations an International Welcome Office with guest accommodation 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day social benefits under the collective agreement for the German public sector and remuneration up to pay grade 13 (EntgO Bund) very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible working a well-connected research campus, good networking opportunities, a subsidized Deutschlandticket (job ticket) subject to certain conditions, and charging facilities for electric vehicles individual opportunities for training and development an excellent technical infrastructure and modern workplace equipment PhD Buddy Program a family-friendly working environment with childcare options, e.g. a daycare center close to the workplace workplace health promotion programmes, e.g. an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) corporate benefits a varied offer in the canteen the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range. Institute of Material and Process Design The Institute of Material and Process Design is dedicated to the sustainable and ecological development of innovative materials and manufacturing processes, especially for the transportation sector and medical technology. To this end, materials are tailored and manufacturing processes are designed to conserve resources – from the modeling of material behavior to the development of the material to the finished component. Interested? Then we are looking forward to receiving your comprehensive application documents (cover letter, CV, transcripts, certificates, etc.) until November 12th, 2026. items.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
items.desc: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos: Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants should submit a dossier including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián.

Among them, Infotainment stands out as one of the most sophisticated and customer‑visible domains, combining HMI, apps, connectivity, vehicle signals, market variants and thousands of user scenarios. This complexity demands a new generation of intelligent validation systems. To address this challenge, we are launching an ambitious PhD project focused on developing an AI‑assisted validation ecosystem for CUPRA Infotainment — an intelligent super‑agent capable of transforming how we test, analyze and improve digital vehicle experiences. items.title: Doktorand i maskinkonstruktion
items.desc: Vill du vara med och bidra till framtidens autonoma system som överträffar människors förmågor? Du kommer att tillhöra forskningsämnet maskinkonstruktion på avdelning produkt- och produktionsutveckling som tillhör institutionen för teknikvetenskap och matematik. Här bedrivs forskning inom produktutveckling, simuleringsdriven konstruktion, automation av arbetsmaskiner samt modellering & simulering. Forskargruppen består av fyra seniorer samt sex doktorander och har tillgång till relevant forskningsinfrastruktur. Forskargruppen samverkar även med andra universitet, institut och företag både nationellt och internationellt. Ämnesbeskrivning Maskinkonstruktion omfattar, för tekniska system, simuleringsdriven produktutveckling, modellering och simulering, produktutvecklingsmetodik samt produktinformationshantering. Modeller, metoder, processer och verktyg för utveckling av produkter är centrala för ämnet. Projektbeskrivning Doktorandprojektet syftar till att utveckla metoder och en modulär systemarkitektur för säker samverkan mellan autonoma terränggående arbetsmaskiner. Forskningen omfattar hur övergripande uppdrag kan brytas ned till prioriterade och samordnade maskinuppgifter, exempelvis navigering, materialhantering och inspektion. Särskilt fokus läggs på hur uppgifter kan omplaneras när omgivningen, maskinernas tillstånd eller kommunikationsförutsättningarna förändras. Projektet ska även utveckla säkerhetsfunktioner som upptäcker människor, hinder, kollisionsrisker och systemfel samt aktiverar lämpliga åtgärder, såsom omplanering, hastighetsbegränsning eller säkert stopp. Metoderna integreras i en gemensam arkitektur för planering, perception, styrning, kommunikation och säkerhet. Resultaten ska bidra till användbara metoder för kostnadseffektiv utveckling och validering av robusta, säkra och samverkande autonoma arbetsmaskiner. Arbetsuppgifter En doktorandtjänst innebär både teoretiskt och praktiskt arbete. Som doktorand tränas du i vetenskapligt arbete i form av publicering av vetenskapliga artiklar i tidskrifter och vid nationella och internationella konferenser. Du läser även obligatoriska och frivilliga doktorandkurser. Dessutom kan du få möjlighet att prova på lärarrollen. Som forskare arbetar du som en neutral part i många sammanhang vilket ger en fantastisk möjlighet att lära sig att driva utmanande utvecklingsprojekt. Arbetet kommer mer specifikt att innefatta utveckling av olika autonoma dellösningar (framförallt mjukvarumässiga) som implementeras, testas och demonstreras med hjälp av terrängfordonsforskningsplattformen AORO. Kvalifikationer Universitetsexamen (MSc eller motsvarande) inom maskinteknik, robotik, produktionsteknik eller dylikt. Du bör ha ett stort intresse, nyfikenhet och passion för forskning och vi värdesätter din personlighet och individuella egenskaper högt. Erfarenhet av arbete med kinematik, dynamik, programmering, säkerhet och CAD-modellering är meriterande. Kunskaper om AI-stödd automation är speciellt meriterande. Sökande måste behärska engelska i tal och skrift. Eftersom undervisning bedrivs inom maskinkonstruktion är det meriterande om du har erfarenhet av CAD. I utvärderingen av kandidater beaktas Luleå tekniska universitets medarbetarpolicy och jämställdhetsmål. För ytterligare information om doktorandutbildning inom maskinkonstruktion se studieplan för forskarutbildning inom teknisk fakultet. Information Anställning som doktorand är tidsbegränsad på 4 år, undervisning och annan institutionstjänstgöring kan tillkomma upp till 20 % av heltid. Tjänstgöringsort är Luleå och tänkt tillträde enligt överenskommelse. Att söka en anställning | Luleå tekniska universitet För ytterligare information är du välkommen att kontakta Professor Magnus Karlberg, 0920-49 2418, magnus.karlberg@ltu.se Fackliga kontaktpersoner Ansökan Vi ser helst att du söker befattningen via ansökningsknappen nedan där du bifogar personligt brev samt CV/meritförteckning och kopior av verifierade examensbevis. Var vänlig och märk din ansökan med referensnumret nedan. Både ansökan och examensbevis ska vara skrivna på svenska eller engelska. Sista ansökningsdag: 5 november, 2026 Referensnummer: 5393-2026

items.title: PhD Student in Machine Design
items.desc: Would you like to contribute to the autonomous systems of the future—systems capable of exceeding human capabilities? You will join the research subject Machine Design at the Division of Product and Production Development, which is part of the Department of Engineering Sciences and Mathematics. Our research covers product development, simulation-driven design, automation of mobile machinery and modelling and simulation. The research group consists of four senior researchers and six PhD students and has access to relevant research infrastructure. The group also collaborates with universities, research institutes and companies, both nationally and internationally. Subject Description Machine Design encompasses, for engineering systems, simulation-driven product development, modelling and simulation, product development methodology and product information management. Models, methods, processes and tools for developing products are important for the research subject. Project Description The PhD project aims to develop methods and a modular system architecture for safe collaboration between autonomous off-road mobile machines. The research will investigate how high-level missions can be decomposed into prioritised and coordinated machine tasks, such as navigation, material handling and inspection. Particular attention will be given to replanning tasks when environmental conditions, machine states or communication conditions change. The project will also develop safety functions that detect people, obstacles, collision risks and system faults, and initiate appropriate responses such as replanning, speed reduction or a safe stop. The methods will be integrated into a common architecture for planning, perception, control, communication and safety. The results will contribute to practical methods for the cost-effective development and validation of robust, safe and collaborative autonomous mobile machinery. Duties A PhD position involves both theoretical and practical work. As a PhD student, you will receive training in scientific research, including publishing articles in scientific journals and presenting your work at national and international conferences. You will also take compulsory and elective doctoral courses and may have the opportunity to gain teaching experience. As a researcher, you will act as an independent party in many contexts, providing an excellent opportunity to learn how to manage challenging development projects. More specifically, the work will include developing autonomous subsystems, primarily software-based solutions, that will be implemented, tested and demonstrated using the AORO off-road vehicle research platform. Qualifications Applicants must hold a Master’s degree or equivalent in mechanical engineering, robotics, production engineering or a related field. You should have a strong interest in, curiosity about and passion for research. We attach considerable importance to personal qualities and individual suitability. Experience in kinematics, dynamics, programming, safety and CAD modelling is considered an asset. Knowledge of AI-assisted automation is particularly advantageous. Applicants must be proficient in spoken and written English. As teaching is conducted within Machine Design, experience in CAD is also considered an asset. The evaluation of candidates will take into account Luleå University of Technology’s employee policy and gender-equality objectives. For further information about doctoral studies in Machine Design, please see the general syllabus for third-cycle studies at the Faculty of Science and Technology. Further information The PhD position is a fixed-term, four-year appointment. Teaching and other departmental duties may be added, corresponding to no more than 20% of full-time employment. The position is based in Luleå, and the intended starting date is subject to agreement. Applying for a job | Luleå tekniska universitet For further information, please contact Professor Magnus Karlberg, +46 920 49 24 18, magnus.karlberg@ltu.se. Union representatives In case of different interpretations of the English and Swedish versions of this announcement, the Swedish version takes precedence. Application We prefer that you apply for this position by clicking on the apply button below . The application should include a CV, personal letter and copies of verified diplomas from high school and universities. Mark your application with the reference number below. Your application, including diplomas, must be written in English or Swedish. Closing date for applications: 5 November, 2026 Reference number: 5393-2026

items.title: PhD in Machine Learning for Quantum Systems (1.0 FTE)- NL
items.desc: We are looking for PhD candidates interested in research at the intersection of machine learning (ML) and quantum many-body physics. The successful candidate will join Interpretable Machines for Physics (IMP) , a research group led by Dr. Anna Dawid. They will work on the mechanics of ML and developing new ML approaches to challenging quantum problems, with a strong focus on making these approaches interpretable, reliable, and scalable. In this position, you will learn about state-of-the-art deep learning solutions as well as the challenges of understanding neural networks. You will be given increasing scientific freedom, supported by structured mentoring, including career development plans guided by your plans after the PhD. The starting date is flexible, the latest in November 2027. The position is set in the exciting, friendly, and interdisciplinary environment of the aQa (Applied Quantum Algorithms) group, which is a team of faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and students across the Leiden Institute of Physics (LION), the Leiden Institute for Advanced Computer Science (LIACS), the Leiden Institute for Chemistry (LIC), and the Leiden Mathematical Institute (MI) at the Leiden University. What You Will Do Conducting research on the mechanics of deep learning and applications of (interpretable, reliable, and scalable) ML in quantum sciences with scientific integrity and rigor under the supervision of Dr. Anna Dawid; Assisting in relevant teaching activities; Actively participating in regular group and one-on-one meetings; Co-supervising Bachelor and Master students; Co-organizing scientific events; Presenting your research results to the scientific community at international conferences and through publications. Where you will work The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The faculty is home to more than 2,700 staff members and over 6,000 students enrolled in nine bachelor's and fifteen master's programs. We are located at the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry come together. You will be part of the Leiden Institute of Advanced Computer Science (LIACS). LIACS offers the bachelor's programs in Computer Science and Data Science/Artificial Intelligence, as well as master's programs in Computer Science, ICT in Business and the Public Sector, Media Technology, and Science Based Business. According to an independent research assessment, LIACS is one of the leading computer science departments in the Netherlands. We strive for excellence in a supportive institute where academic achievement, enjoyment, and diversity go hand in hand. We offer a clear and welcoming career path for young and talented scientists with the ambition to grow. For more information about LIACS, visit our website: www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science What You Bring Master’s degree in physics, computer science, or a closely related field; Strong interest in ML and motivation to make it interpretable and reliable; Knowledge of quantum physics and numerical methods for quantum systems or theory of deep learning is preferred; Good programming skills in Python; Proficient in spoken and written English; A team player who can communicate well across scientific fields and teams; Highly motivated and organized self-starter with an open mindset. What We Offer An full-time employment contract for the duration of initially one year. After a positive evaluation of the progress of the thesis, personal capabilities and compatibility the appointment will be extended by a further three years. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities; A salary between € 3.204,= and € 4.051,= gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours, Payscale P); A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP; Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel; Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week. Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme; If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands; A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop. What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area and position details can be made to Dr. Anna Dawid (a.m.dawid@liacs.leidenuniv.nl). If you have any questions about the procedure, please sent an e-mail to: jobs@liacs.leidenuniv.nl. Applications: Please submit your application online via the blue button in the vacancy. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents: A CV that includes names and email addresses of at least two scientists who agreed to be contacted for reference letters; A short motivation letter (1 page); Optionally, a short research statement (1 page) describing your research projects so far and what research project you would be interested in doing during your PhD. For full consideration, please apply no later than 30 November 2026 . The selection procedure will take place in December/January 2027, and selected candidates may be invited for an interview during this period.

items.title: PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN- NL
items.desc: The Faculty of Science and Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research (LACDR) are looking for candidates for a PhD Position (Doctoral Candidate 10) in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network ANA-KIN ANA-KIN is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme. Over the past two decades, small-molecule kinase inhibitors have transformed cancer therapy, yet nearly all of them target the highly conserved ATP-binding site, which limits selectivity and allows resistance to emerge. ANA-KIN aims to train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers capable of redefining kinase drug discovery beyond the ATP paradigm, by developing the experimental and computational tools, modular assays and workflows needed to systematically target non-conserved regulatory interfaces, such as kinase dimerization and substrate-binding sites. Proof-of-concept will be demonstrated on three representative kinases: EGFR, BRAF and the understudied “dark” kinase LTK. ANA-KIN brings together 11 beneficiaries and 9 associated partners across Europe and the USA, including Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (coordinator), University of Crete, Goethe University Frankfurt, Saarland University, EPFL, CNRS, Pompeu Fabra University, VIB, KU Leuven, INSERM and Leiden University, together with industrial partners such as AstraZeneca, Novartis, Servier and Skylight Therapeutics. The network combines chemical biology, structural biophysics (single-molecule FRET, cryo-EM, nanodiscs), AI-driven drug design and cell biology in an integrated learn–design–test loop. Twelve Doctoral Candidates (DCs) will each pursue an individual research project, benefit from co-supervision across institutions and sectors, carry out two research secondments at partner organizations, and follow a structured network-wide training program covering scientific, transferable, open-science and entrepreneurial skills. In this PhD project (DC10, Work Package 3 – Discovery), you will develop deep-learning architectures that integrate text-mined, cheminformatic, and biophysical descriptors to predict interface binding, allosteric signatures and resistance liabilities of kinase ligands. The models will learn jointly across peptide and small-molecule modalities and will be used to generate hybrid peptidomimetic design hypotheses. You will translate these models into consortium-wide prioritisation dashboards that support hit triage and analogue selection in the discovery campaigns of ANA-KIN, and work in close reciprocal feedback with DC9 (Saarland University) on structure-based and machine-learning pipelines. Model predictions will be validated prospectively with the experimental partners in the network. The expected results are a resistance-aware AI workflow for non-ATP interface ligands, accompanied by public models, datasets and interpretable feature maps, and prospective design case studies demonstrating improved optimisation trajectories. To reinforce structural grounding and experimental validation, you will carry out two secondments: at VIB (Belgium, Prof. Ruslan Efremov; 4 months) to extract structural classes and conformational features from cryo-EM data and use them to refine model constraints, and at Skylight Therapeutics (Belgium, Dr. Joshua Salafsky; 3 months) to test model predictions using second-harmonic generation (SHG)-based conformational profiling. The project will be supervised by Prof. Gerard J.P. van Westen (Leiden University), with Prof. Ruslan Efremov and Dr. Joshua Salafsky as co-supervisors. What You Will Do Conduct original and novel research in deep learning, AI, and cheminformatics for kinase drug discovery; Develop, benchmark and openly share models, datasets and decision-support dashboards following FAIR and open-science principles; Collaborate closely with experimental and computational DCs in the network, and carry out two research secondments abroad (VIB and Skylight Therapeutics, Belgium); Publish and present scientific articles at international journals and conferences; Participate in the ANA-KIN network-wide training events, schools and outreach activities; Contribute to educational activities; Write a dissertation. What You Bring A MSc degree in Computer Science, AI, (Computational) Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Biopharmaceutical Sciences, or a relevant related field; Good knowledge of and experience with machine learning and deep-learning techniques (e.g. PyTorch); Good knowledge of and experience with cheminformatics and/or computational chemistry (e.g. RDKit, molecular descriptors, docking); Interest in structural biology, protein kinases and drug discovery; affinity with peptide or biophysical data is an advantage; Highly motivated to both perform foundational research and apply the developed methods to real-world problems; creative, ‘making things work’ mentality, independent, and communicative team player; Willingness to travel and to carry out research secondments at partner institutions abroad; Excellent programming skills (preferably Python); Good academic writing skills and interest in participating in educational activities; Excellent proficiency in English (oral and written). MSCA eligibility criteria At the date of recruitment, candidates must not have been awarded a doctoral degree; Mobility rule: candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the date of recruitment. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status are not taken into account. Where you will work Leiden Academic Centre for Drug Research Our institute is a center of excellence for multidisciplinary research on drug discovery and development. Leiden University consistently ranks within the top-20 world-wide within the subject-based QS Ranking in Pharmacology and Pharmacy. At LACDR, we develop innovative scientific concepts in fundamental and translational research underlying the discovery and optimization of drugs, and personalized medicines. We aim to optimize the route to novel drugs that are both efficacious and safe, and therefore our research focuses on drug discovery and safety, bio-therapeutics, and systems biomedicine and pharmacology. State-of-the-art expertise and infrastructures ensure that we are strategically positioned in (inter)national collaborations, thus further strengthening the development of novel concepts and their application in a clinical and industry environment. Computational Drug Discovery Research in this group, headed by Gerard van Westen, focusses on computational methods integrated in different parts of the drug discovery process. More specifically, topics include innovative treatments for cancer, kinase and GPCR drug discovery, proteochemometrics, selectivity and polypharmacology modeling, allosteric modulation, drug resistance modeling, de novo molecular design, and novel methods in the domain of machine learning. For more information see: http://www.cddl.nl Research at our faculty The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is diverse, ranging from artificial intelligence, computer science, mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,700 staff and almost 6,000 students. We are located in the heart of the Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s largest science parks, where academia and industry meet. For more information, see http://www.science.leidenuniv.nl. What We Offer We offer a full-time appointment for 48 months as a Doctoral Candidate within the MSCA Doctoral Network ANA-KIN, starting late 2026. The appointment is initially for one year; after a positive evaluation of the progress of the research, personal capabilities and compatibility, the appointment will be extended for the remaining period. Salary ranges from € 3.204,- tot € 4.051,- gross per month (pay scale P in accordance with the Collective Labor Agreement for Dutch Universities). Leiden University offers an attractive benefits package with additional holiday (8%) and end-of-year bonuses (8.3%), training and career development. Our individual choices model gives you some freedom to assemble your own set of terms and conditions. Candidates from outside the Netherlands may be eligible for a substantial tax break. All our PhD students are embedded in the Leiden University Graduate School of Science. Our graduate school offers several PhD training courses at three levels: professional courses, skills training and personal effectiveness. In addition, advanced courses to deepen scientific knowledge are offered by the research school. As an ANA-KIN Doctoral Candidate you will also follow the network’s training program, including summer schools, workshops and an industrial immersion workshop, and your progress will be monitored by a Thesis Advisory Committee including an independent mentor. What We Value Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent. Want to apply or find out more? Inquiries about the research area can be made to Prof. Gerard van Westen, gerard@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact Brigitte Kraakman, b.p.m.kraakman@lacdr.leidenuniv.nl. To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application online via the blue button below. Please ensure that you upload the following additional documents quoting the vacancy number and “ANA-KIN DC10”: application letter (including a statement confirming that they meet the MSCA eligibility criteria) curriculum vitae a list of grades two references (who have agreed to be contacted) Only applications received no later than November 12th can be considered. The selection procedure will take place in November. Selected candidates may be invited for an interview in the last week of November / 1st week of December, during which you are kindly requested to be available. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this.

items.title: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’
items.desc: PhD position on ‘Adaptive Privacy and Differential Privacy for Energy Data’ 1,0 FTE position for 4 years. The PhD candidate will be appointed for a period of 15 months. The appointment will be extended to 4 years when progress and performance are good. A PhD training program is part of the agreement. Vacancy number: FAC/BW/26087 The Project Can you help make energy data usable without giving away sensitive information? The energy transition in the Netherlands urgently requires upgrading of the electricity grid, for instance to accommodate solar panels, wind turbines, and electric vehicles. To efficiently plan and manage these upgrades, stakeholders such as grid operators, municipalities and energy communities need to share detailed data about electricity consumption, generation and grid operation. This data sharing however is prevented by concerns on the competitively sensitive nature and privacy of data, as it reveals detailed information about households, buildings and operational assets. Synthetic data generated by generative AI-models offers a promising alternative, but preserving statistical, temporal, and physical characteristics of real energy data while protecting sensitive information are major challenges. We are offering a PhD position in the SHARE project that addresses these challenges. Research challenges As a PhD candidate, you will develop methods for adaptive privacy protection of energy data , combining differential privacy, empirical privacy attacks and privacy–utility optimisation. Your research is part of the Adaptive Privacy and Legal Compliance work package in the SHARE project. More specifically, your challenges are to: Investigate how temporal patterns, spatial information, rare events and other distinctive features contribute to re-identification and inference risk. You will work with metrics such as uniqueness, entropy, attack success rates and time-series-specific indicators. Implement and study attacks such as membership inference, reconstruction, re-identification and attribute inference to understand where information leakage occurs in both original and synthetic datasets. Investigate methods that allocate stronger protection to sensitive components and lighter perturbation to lower-risk components, thereby preserving as much analytical utility as possible. Formulate privacy protection as an optimisation problem balancing formal privacy guarantees against statistical, temporal and physical utility requirements for energy-system applications. Collaborate closely with researchers at Radboud University, who develop physics-informed generative models for synthetic energy data, and investigate approaches such as differentially private training and post-generation privacy calibration. Work closely with distribution system operator Alliander and other consortium partners to evaluate whether the developed methods provide meaningful protection while retaining the information required for practical energy-system applications. Ultimately contribute to an open-source privacy layer for the SHARE toolbox. Requirements You hold, or will soon obtain, an MSc degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related discipline. You should have: a strong background in privacy-enhancing technologies, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity or statistical modelling; strong programming skills, particularly in Python; preferably, some familiarity with deep generative models (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models) and probabilistic modelling; good written and spoken English skills; knowledge of Dutch language preferred not mandatory. Salary The salary is determined in accordance with salary scale P of Appendix A of the Collective Labour Agreement of Dutch Universities and ranges from € 3.204,-- gross per month upon commencement to € 4.051,-- gross per month in the fourth and final year, in case of full employment. The Open Universiteit provides good secondary benefits such as training, mobility, part-time employment and paid parental leave. Station The position is officially based in Heerlen. As part of the PhD project, you will mainly work at Radboud University in Nijmegen, where you will collaborate closely with the other researchers in the SHARE project. This setup enables close day-to-day collaboration with researchers working on machine learning, synthetic data and energy systems. You will be employed by Open Universiteit and supervised by Dr. Mina Alishahi as your primary supervisor, with Prof. dr. ir. Harald Vranken as co-supervisor. Information For more information about this vacancy you can contact: harald.vranken@ou.nl. Procedure Please apply to this position by sending an email to solliciteren@ou.nl, stating the vacancy number and including: your CV; a motivation letter; your MSc thesis or another representative piece of academic work, if available; contact details of two references. In your motivation letter, please briefly address the following three questions: Why are you interested in privacy-preserving machine learning and, in particular, this PhD project? Describe a research, thesis or programming project in which you worked with machine learning, privacy, cybersecurity, generative models or complex data. What was your own contribution? Provide a one-paragraph description of your MSc thesis, written for a reader outside your field. You will preferably start your employment on January 1st, 2027. Closing date: November 1st, 2026 Working at the Open University Working at the Open University means contributing to academic education for the most motivated students in the Netherlands and Flanders, as well as to scientific research with visible impact for people and society. With a broad range of bachelor’s and master’s programmes and short courses, the Open University makes lifelong learning accessible to everyone. There are no prior education requirements for bachelor’s programmes: anyone aged eighteen or older can enrol. Education is hybrid and flexible, available anytime and anywhere, at a pace that suits the student. The majority of the nearly 16,000 students combine their studies with work. This creates a valuable interaction: experiences and questions from professional practice enrich education and research and increase their societal relevance. It is therefore no coincidence that the Open University has ranked in the top three of the Dutch Keuzegids for universities for many years, and this year holds the number one position. In research, the university focuses on three central themes: healthcare, digitalisation and AI, and society and citizenship. Solutions to today’s challenges are sought across disciplinary boundaries and in collaboration with partners. The Open University employs approximately 800 staff members, has its main campus in Heerlen, and operates study centres in the Netherlands and Flanders. Its culture is people-centred, collaborative, and inclusive: an environment in which students, staff, and partners feel connected, with ample opportunities for personal development and a healthy work–life balance. Department of Computer Science You will be appointed within the Department of Computer Science of the Faculty of Science. The department’s research program “Towards high-quality and intelligent software” (2020–2025) consists of four research lines, focusing on: Techniques for quality assurance of software systems Software and computer system security, and privacy-by-design Responsible artificial intelligence, including methods and applications of AI Educational tools and computing education.

items.title: Promotion – State of Health (SoH) von Elektronik
items.desc: Unternehmensbeschreibung Bei Bosch gestalten wir Zukunft mit hochwertigen Technologien und Dienstleistungen, die Begeisterung wecken und das Leben der Menschen verbessern. Unser Versprechen an unsere Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter steht dabei felsenfest: Wir wachsen gemeinsam, haben Freude an unserer Arbeit und inspirieren uns gegenseitig. Willkommen bei Bosch. Die Robert Bosch GmbH freut sich auf deine Bewerbung! Stellenbeschreibung Du arbeitest an einem innovativen KI-basierten SoH-Konzept, das die verbleibende Nutzungsdauer von Batteriesystemen prognostiziert und nachhaltige Entscheidungen für Wiederverwendung, Reparatur und Recycling ermöglicht. Darüber hinaus entwickelst du eine umfassende Produktentscheidungsmatrix, die wirtschaftliche, technische und designbezogene Kriterien systematisch zusammenführt. Mit geeigneten Methoden, wie der hybriden Modellierung, bewertest du das von dir entwickelte SoH-Konzept und stellst dessen Praxistauglichkeit sicher. Nicht zuletzt wendest du deine Erkenntnisse auf ein Fokusprodukt an und integrierst Inspektionsdaten aus der Produktion (SPI, AOI, AXI), 0‑km‑Ausfalldaten, Zuverlässigkeitsdaten sowie Feldbelastungen. Qualifikationen Ausbildung: sehr guter Masterabschluss in Mikrosystemtechnik, Mikroelektronik, Physik oder einem vergleichbaren Studiengang Erfahrungen und Know-how: praktische Erfahrungen im Bereich der datenbasierten Modellierung (z. B. hybride Modellierung, vorausschauende Wartung / Predictive Maintenance, Anomalieerkennung) Programmierkenntnisse in Python und relevanten Bibliotheken (z. B. PyTorch) Expertise im Bereich der Zuverlässigkeit (Lebensdauer, Ausfallmechanismen, Prüfung / Testing) von Elektronik Persönlichkeit und Arbeitsweise: du zeichnest dich durch ein starkes Interesse an technischer Nachhaltigkeit aus, insbesondere an der Verlängerung der Produktlebensdauer und der Schonung von Ressourcen; zudem bringst du ausgeprägte analytische und kommunikative Fähigkeiten mit; deine hohe wissenschaftliche Neugier treibt dich an, komplexe technische Zusammenhänge zu durchdringen und innovative Lösungsansätze zu entwickeln Begeisterung: du begeisterst dich für Nachhaltigkeit und datenbasierte Modellierung Sprachen: sehr gutes Deutsch und Englisch in Wort und Schrift Zusätzliche Informationen https://www.bosch-ai.com www.bosch.com/research Die finale Vergabe des Promotionsthemas obliegt deiner Hochschule als zentrale Anlaufstelle für deine Promotion. Beginn: nach Absprache Bitte sende uns deine aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (inkl. Lebenslauf und Zeugnissen) zu. Vielfalt und Inklusion sind für uns keine Trends, sondern fest verankert in unserer Unternehmenskultur. Daher freuen wir uns über alle Bewerbungen: unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Behinderung, Religion, ethnischer Herkunft oder sexueller Identität. Du hast Fragen zum Bewerbungsprozess?
