items.title: PhD Student in Security and Privacy of Multi-Agent AI Systems
items.desc: Are you interested in doing research focused on ensuring the trustworthiness of emerging AI systems comprising multiple agents? Does it sound exciting to develop novel techniques for robust and privacy-preserving multi-agent collaboration? If so, you are welcome to apply for this position as a doctoral candidate. The project As AI agents start acting in groups, delegating, negotiating, and relying on each other's inputs and outputs, the security assumptions behind single-model systems stop holding. This project develops principled and scalable foundations for trustworthy collaboration between AI agents, sitting at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity. It is funded by the Swedish Foundation for Strategic Research (SSF) under a programme building research ties between Sweden and Taiwan, including opportunities for research visits among the participants. About Us RISE Research Institutes of Sweden AB is Sweden's research institute and innovation partner. In international collaboration with companies, academia, and the public sector, we contribute to a competitive business sector and a sustainable society. You will be part of the Cybersecurity unit at the department of Computer Science which is one of the largest technical cybersecurity groups in Sweden, conducting cutting-edge research on both fundamental and applied cybersecurity topics arising in AI, 6G, Internet of Things, etc. About The Role We are looking for a dedicated PhD student to strengthen our research in trustworthy multi-agent AI systems. Example research topics include evaluating the robustness of multi-agent systems under adversarial manipulation, designing secure and privacy-preserving multi-agent collaborative mechanisms, and verifiable decision-making under uncertainty and adversarial influence. You will be based in the RISE office at Kista, Stockholm for 4 years, and you will be enrolled as a doctoral student at a Swedish University. PhD education also involves participation in relevant university courses. Who are you? Requirements: Completed master’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, information security, mathematics, or an equivalent field (at the time of employment) Strong programming skills Good command of spoken and written English Passion for agentic AI and cybersecurity Interest in technical challenges and commitment to delivering high-quality results Meriting: Experience with research projects Demonstrated collaboration skills Demonstrated drive and independence Personal qualities: Driven by curiosity Takes initiative naturally Strong problem-solving abilities Passionate and self-motivated Employment Start date: As soon as possible or according to agreement. Salary: According to Swedish norm. Assessment Criteria: Selection for doctoral education is based on the assessed ability to benefit from doctoral education. Welcome with your application! If this sounds exciting and you want to know more, you are welcome to contact Dr. Apostolos Pyrgelis (apostolos.pyrgelis@ri.se). For further information, you can contact Prof. Shahid Raza (shahid.raza@ri.se) or the director of the RISE cybersecurity unit Andreas Aurelius (andreas.aurelius@ri.se). The deadline for applications is October 15, 2026 . Interviews will be carried out continuously during the application period. Apply as soon as possible with personal letter, cv, academic transcripts, a copy of degree diploma(s), and a copy of your passport/National ID card. Our union representatives Ingemar Petermann, SACO, +46 10 228 41 22, and Linda Ikatti, Unionen, 010-516 51 61.

items.title: CIFRE - Intégration d’architectures de qubits de spin en silicium en technologie CMOS FDSOI avancée pour le calcul quantique (F/H)
items.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. La course à la réalisation d’un ordinateur quantique démontrant la suprématie quantique s’intensifie, mobilisant de puissantes entreprises et de nombreux gouvernements, qui travaillent sur de multiples supports physiques pour encoder l’information quantique, tels que la supraconductivité, les ions piégés, le spin de l’électron dans le silicium ou encore la photonique. Au‑delà des enjeux économiques classiques, l’adoption de solutions quantiques est hautement stratégique, ouvrant la voie vers une sécurité renforcée des données et des communications. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans la feuille de route actuelle de ST, dans le cadre du contrat de collaboration avec QUOBLY, visant à produire industriellement un ordinateur quantique tolérant aux fautes (FTQC) pour des clients stratégiques. Dans cette compétition, ST et QUOBLY peuvent tirer parti de la technologie FDSOI, qui offre un environnement idéal pour isoler et manipuler le spin de l’électron utilisé dans les algorithmes quantiques. Pendant les 3 années de recherche, le doctorant devra étudier et proposer une architecture de dispositif basée sur la technologie CMOS FDSOI permettant de supporter des qubits en silicium à base de spin pour le calcul quantique. Les principaux axes de développement seront : l’architecture du dispositif (simulation 3D et réalisation des dispositifs sur silicium), l’analyse des matériaux et la caractérisation cryogénique. A propos de vos missions Réaliser une étude bibliographique exhaustive afin de situer au mieux le sujet et sa complexité. Développer des architectures de transistors à électron unique (SET) dans une technologie CMOS FDSOI avancée. Implémenter une architecture de qubit innovante (passage d’une structure linéaire 1D à une matrice 2D). Optimiser le layout des qubits en tirant parti des techniques de lithographie avancées utilisées dans les technologies FDSOI. Effectuer des simulations 3D, embarquer des structures de test et réaliser les dispositifs correspondants sur silicium. Caractériser les qubits et les SET en régime cryogénique Mener une caractérisation avancée des pièges dans les diélectriques à température ambiante et à basse température. A propos de vous Niveau Bac+5 (Master 2 ou diplôme d’ingénieur) en micro/nanoélectronique, physique des dispositifs, électronique ou physique quantique appliquée (ou formation équivalente). Bases solides en physique des semi-conducteurs, dispositifs MOSFET (FDSOI/FinFET) et compréhension d’une filière technologique CMOS. Expérience pratique en salle blanche, caractérisation électrique ou design de circuits/dispositifs appréciée. Bonnes capacités scientifiques (esprit critique, lecture d’articles) et compétences en programmation/outils numériques. Excellentes aptitudes en communication, anglais scientifique et travail en équipe interdisciplinaire. Les résultats attendus de cette recherche sont la conception, le développement et la compréhension des performances des nouvelles architectures des qubits et de SET intégrant des matériaux avancés, capables de satisfaire les exigences du calcul quantique. Contact: carlos-augusto.suarezsegovia@st.com ST est fière d’être certifiée parmi les 17 entreprises mondiales « Global Top Employers 2025 » et d’être la première et unique entreprise de semi-conducteurs à recevoir cette distinction. ST a été distinguée dans ce classement grâce à sa démarche d’amélioration continue, se démarquant notamment par son engagement en matière d’éthique et d’intégrité, de sens et de valeurs, d’organisation et de gestion du changement, ainsi que par sa stratégie commerciale et ses performances. En France, ST a également obtenu la labélisation Happy Trainee 2025. Nous cultivons un environnement de travail inclusif et diversifié, où la discrimination n’a pas sa place. Notre ambition est de recruter et de fidéliser des talents reflétant la richesse des sociétés dans lesquelles nous évoluons. Nous nous engageons à l’équité dans le développement des carrières, les opportunités professionnelles et la rémunération. Chez ST, nous encourageons les candidats qui ne remplissent pas forcément tous les critères à postuler, car nous croyons en la richesse des parcours variés et offrons de réelles opportunités d’apprentissage et d’évolution. La diversité, l’équité et l’inclusion sont des valeurs fondamentales qui façonnent notre culture d’entreprise. Pour découvrir toutes nos opportunités, rendez-vous sur st.com/careers.

items.title: Industridoktorand inom nätverkssäkerhet – Sectra Communications
items.desc: Vill du utveckla din expertis inom nätverkssäkerhet, framtida kryptografi och dataskydd samtidigt som du gör skillnad och bidrar till en säkrare värld? Sectra Communications är en ledande leverantör inom cybersäkerhet och informationssäkerhet. Här utvecklas lösningar inom kryptering och IT-säkerhet för att stärka samhällets säkerhet och skydda känslig information, både i Sverige och Europa. Forskningsavdelningen har som ansvar att utveckla kunskap, metoder och prototyper som banar väg för framtidens säkra kommunikationslösningar och cybersäkerhetsprodukter. Forskningsområdet för den här tjänsten berör skydd av nätverkskommunikation. Trots stark kryptering kan nätverkstrafik fortfarande röja känslig information genom mönster som paketstorlek, tidpunkt och frekvens, och i takt med utvecklingen inom AI blir sådana analysmetoder allt kraftfullare. Arbetet handlar om att utveckla, driftsätta och utvärdera prestandamedvetna försvar som anpassar sig efter både nätverksförhållanden och angripare, med målet att överbrygga gapet mellan forskning och praktiskt användbara lösningar för en säkrare kommunikation. Rollen I rollen som industridoktorand hos Sectra Communications kommer du att jobba i ett team med forskare och ha nära samarbete med akademiska experter globalt. Projektet utförs i särskilt samarbete med Karlstads universitet och Linköpings universitet. Vidare kommer du att: Delta i forskningsavdelningens interna projekt Arbeta i nära anslutning till våra utvecklingsavdelningar för att förverkliga forskningen Delta på konferenser för att presentera men även lyssna in på forskning Vid intresse finns även stora möjligheter till internationella resor och samarbeten. Att vara industridoktorand hos oss innebär att kombinera det bästa av två världar. Du får möjlighet att fördjupa dig i forskningsfronten och avancera inom ditt expertområde, samtidigt som du arbetar praktiskt med att omsätta forskningen i verkliga, användbara produkter. , Denna roll är en unik möjlighet som kräver engagemang och flexibilitet. Du behöver ha en positiv inställning till de utmaningar som forsknings- och industrivärlden erbjuder, och se detta som en väg till en belönande och utvecklande karriär. Vi lägger större vikt vid din potential än den kunskap och erfarenhet du besitter idag. Om du är en snabblärd person med en strävan att utvecklas kan vi lära dig det som krävs för tjänsten. För att lyckas i rollen ser vi att du har: En civilingenjörsexamen inom datavetenskap, teknisk fysik eller ett närliggande område. Flytande svenska och engelska i både tal och skrift. Ett starkt intresse för att omvandla avancerad teknologi till praktiska lösningar inom cybersäkerhet. Mycket goda akademiska resultat och en stark vilja att lära dig och behärska nya tekniska metoder. För denna tjänst behöver du ett svenskt medborgarskap då vi jobbar med säkerhetsklassad information. Vi erbjuder: Möjligheten att arbeta med teknologier som spelar en avgörande roll för samhällets säkerhet. Möjligheten att lära dig om, och driva framstegen inom, ett av de mest betydelsefulla teknikområdena i vår tid. En inspirerande och utmanande arbetsplats där du arbetar tillsammans med smarta och begåvade kollegor, både inom industrin och akademin. En organisation där du blir hörd och har en verklig möjlighet att påverka. Vi läser ansökningar löpande och kommer kalla in till intervjuer efter sommaren. Här kan du läsa mer om hur det är att jobba på Sectra, och här kan du läsa mer om vår rekryteringsprocess.

items.title: PhD Position Sustainable Generative AI for Digital Sovereignty
items.desc: Join us for this PhD project in EU Horizon €8 million initiative, to transform how generative AI is deployed across Europe for a more sustainable, sovereign and resilient future. Job Description Generative AI is widely expected to become a central element of digital transformation. Its flexibility and adaptability give businesses in many sectors an opportunity to innovate rapidly, respond to changing conditions, and lower barriers to automation. For society to benefit from these advancements, organisations need to maintain control over sensitive information and critical decision-making tools. Reducing dependence on external providers strengthens digital autonomy, while more efficient ways of running AI help align technological progress with environmental and energy targets. By designing systems that are sustainable, sovereign, secure, and efficient at the same time, this PhD project will support Europe’s broader ambitions for responsible technological leadership. Position Overview: This PhD position is aimed at candidates with a Master’s degree in computer science/engineering, AI, data science, or related fields, with a strong interest in generative AI. The successful candidate will be based at the Department of Engineering Systems and Services (ESS) at Delft University of Technology under the supervision of Dr. Aaron Ding, Dr. Marcela Tuler de Oliveira, Prof. Dr. Marijn Janssen. This PhD project involves close collaboration with partners from the EU Horizon project, and candidates will have the opportunity to engage with interdisciplinary teams involved in the project. Key Responsibilities: To conduct an in-depth evaluation of existing foundation models to assess their suitability in the digital industries, automotive and healthcare domains. Design sustainable inference strategies and framework towards the computing continuum. Collaborate with experts from the f-inference consortium to design, develop, test and refine the design strategies and framework. Work independently and contribute collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team environment. Project Impact: This project will democratise the access to advanced Generative AI technologies through practical tools that help businesses, particularly SMEs, adopt state-of-the-art AI models. The outcomes are expected to enhance competitiveness, support sustainable innovation, and contribute to a more inclusive digital transition across Europe. Job Requirements MSc in computer science/engineering, AI, data science, or related fields. Strong analytical skills A strong interest in interdisciplinary research, and the use of AI in inter-oranisational context Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a dynamic, multidisciplinary environment. Excellent command of English TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Technology, Policy & Management The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Technology, Policy and Management. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information For more information about this vacancy, please contact Aaron Ding (aaron.ding@tudelft.nl). For more information about the application procedure, please contact Olivie Beek, HR-advisor (recruitment-tbm@tudelft.nl). Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: your CV motivation letter official list of all courses followed during your BSc and MSc studies with grades your MSc thesis If the applicants are selected for an interview, they will be asked to provide contact details of two referees with their consent. The start date is flexible, but foreseen for summer/fall 2026. Screening starts as applications come in. You can address your application to Aaron Ding. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

items.co: Fraunhofer Institute for Production Technology IPT
items.title: Doktorand IT (m/w/d)
items.desc: Die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft (www.fraunhofer.de) ist eine der weltweit führenden Organisationen für anwendungsorientierte Forschung. 74 Institute entwickeln wegweisende Technologien für unsere Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft - genauer: 30 000 Menschen aus Technik, Wissenschaft, Verwaltung und IT. Am Fraunhofer-Institut für Produktionstechnologie IPT in Aachen gestalten wir mit mehr als 450 Mitarbeitenden die Produktion der Zukunft - digital, nachhaltig und resilient. In der Abteilung »Produktionsqualität und Messtechnik« trägst du maßgeblich dazu bei, innovative Hardware- und Softwarelösungen für die Produktion von morgen zu entwickeln. Dabei verbinden wir moderne Mess- und Sensortechnik mit Datenanalyse und Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) sowie Steuerungs- und Automatisierungstechnik. Die Einsatzgebiete reichen von der Qualitätssicherung und Prozessüberwachung bis hin zur intelligenten Steuerung und Optimierung komplexer Produktionsprozesse in unterschiedlichsten Branchen Dabei bildet die gezielte Erfassung und Verarbeitung von Mess- und Produktionsdaten die Grundlage für eine höhere Produktqualität, stabile Prozesse und eine effiziente Produktion. Aufgaben Entwicklung und Integration innovativer Mess- und Automatisierungslösungen für industrielle Produktionsprozesse Erarbeitung technischer Lösungsansätze in den Bereichen Sensorik, Systemsteuerung sowie Daten- und Signalverarbeitung Entwicklung von Hard- oder Software zur Erfassung, Verarbeitung, Vernetzung und Visualisierung von Mess- und Produktionsdaten Anwendung von Datenanalyse, Machine Learning und Künstlicher Intelligenz zur Prozessüberwachung, Qualitätssicherung und Optimierung Akquisition, Koordination und Bearbeitung von nationalen und internationalen Industrie- und Forschungsprojekten im Team Präsentation deiner Forschungsergebnisse bei Auftraggebern sowie auf internationalen Konferenzen und Fachtagungen Qualifikationsprofil Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master, Diplom) im Bereich Maschinenbau, Elektrotechnik, Automatisierungstechnik, Informatik, Physik oder in einer verwandten Fachrichtung Begeisterung für technische Systeme und innovative Technologien in der Produktion Interesse an einem oder mehreren Themenfeldern wie Sensorik, Datenanalyse, KI, Steuerungstechnik oder Automatisierung Gute Kenntnisse in einer oder mehreren Programmiersprachen, beispielsweise Python, C++, C# oder MATLAB, sind von Vorteil Gute analytische Fähigkeiten und Freude an interdisziplinärer Projektarbeit Eigeninitiative, Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Spaß an Teamwork Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Wir bieten Ein engagiertes Team mit offener, wertschätzender Arbeitskultur Verantwortungsvolle Aufgaben in hochinnovativen Forschungs- und Entwicklungsprojekten Enge Zusammenarbeit mit renommierten Industriepartnern aus unterschiedlichen Branchen Ein hochmoderner Maschinenpark mit Edge-Cloud-Technologien und 5G-Infrastruktur Flexible Arbeitszeiten und Unterstützung bei der Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Privatleben Individuelle Weiterbildungs- und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten Möglichkeit zur Promotion an der RWTH Aachen in einem selbst entwickelten Forschungsthema Ein exzellentes Netzwerk aus Wissenschaft und Industrie mit hervorragenden Karriereperspektiven Attraktive Zusatzleistungen wie Deutschlandticket-Zuschuss, Mitarbeitendenrabatte und attraktive Benefits Warum Fraunhofer IPT? Bei uns verbindest du wissenschaftliche Exzellenz mit praxisnaher Forschung. Du entwickelst Technologien, die unmittelbar in industriellen Anwendungen zum Einsatz kommen, übernimmst früh Verantwortung in Industrie- und Forschungsprojekten und schaffst gleichzeitig die Grundlage für deine wissenschaftliche Karriere - bis hin zur Promotion. Die nachhaltige Erhöhung des Anteils von Frauen in der Wissenschaft ist unser erklärtes Ziel. Mit unserem Karriereprogramm »Fraunhofer TALENTA« bieten wir Berufseinsteigerinnen und Young Professionals zusätzliche Qualifizierungs- und Vernetzungsangebote sowie den nötigen Freiraum zur Gestaltung ihres Karrierewegs. Wir wertschätzen und fördern die Vielfalt der Kompetenzen unserer Mitarbeitenden und begrüßen daher alle Bewerbungen - unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung sowie persönlicher Orientierung und Identität. Schwerbehinderte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt eingestellt. Die wöchentliche Arbeitszeit beträgt 39 Stunden. Die Stelle kann auch in Teilzeit besetzt werden. Die Stelle ist zunächst auf 2 Jahre befristet. Es besteht die Möglichkeit der Verlängerung. Anstellung, Vergütung und Sozialleistungen basieren auf dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TVöD). Zusätzlich kann Fraunhofer leistungs- und erfolgsabhängige variable Vergütungsbestandteile gewähren. Bereit für Veränderung? Dann bewirb Dich jetzt online und mache einen Unterschied!

items.title: CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship
items.desc: 🎓 PhD Opportunity | Artificial Intelligence in Childhood Leukaemia Research 🔬 Interested in using AI and data science to advance childhood cancer research? The Leukaemia Research Cytogenomics Group (LRCG) at Newcastle University is recruiting a PhD student through the Cancer Research UK (CRUK) Black Leaders in Cancer PhD Scholarship Programme, with applications now open for the 2027 intake. This exciting project will focus on developing and evaluating trustworthy synthetic healthcare data using statistical methods, machine learning and generative AI, drawing on a national dataset of more than 20,000 childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients. The research aims to support more robust, reproducible and privacy-conscious approaches to childhood leukaemia research, with the potential to improve our understanding of treatment pathways and patient outcomes. 🔬 Project focus: Developing and comparing statistical, machine-learning and generative AI approaches to synthetic healthcare data generation. Evaluating the preservation of clinically important patterns, treatment pathways and outcomes, including rare events such as relapse. Assessing data utility, privacy, fidelity, fairness and clinical validity. Exploring the use of synthetic data for methodological research, hypothesis generation and reproducible analysis. 🌍 What the scholarship offers: Fully funded 4-year PhD, including stipend and tuition fees (Home fee status). Mentoring and leadership development opportunities. Networking through Black in Cancer and the Windsor Fellowship. A supportive and diverse research environment. Opportunities for research placements and community engagement. 👩‍💻 Who should apply? We welcome applicants with backgrounds in statistics, data science, biostatistics, epidemiology, computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related quantitative disciplines. As part of the CRUK Black Leaders in Cancer Programme, we particularly encourage applications from talented Black students who are passionate about advancing cancer research and addressing inequalities in healthcare. 📍 Location: Newcastle University, UK 👨‍🏫 Primary Supervisor: Dr. Amir Enshaei 📅 Application deadline: 4 December 2026 🎓 Start: 2027 intake 🔗 Find out more and apply: https://www.ncl.ac.uk/cancer/training/studentships/cruk-black-leaders-phd/ For informal enquiries, please contact Amir Enshaei (Primary Supervisor). Join us in advancing AI-driven research to improve outcomes for children with leukaemia! #PhDOpportunity #PhDStudentship #BlackLeadersInCancer #CancerResearch #ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning #DataScience #ChildhoodLeukaemia #SyntheticData #NewcastleUniversity

items.title: Ingénieur Doctorant CIFRE
items.desc: Job Description Summary Activités contribuant à la conception et au développement de produits, de solutions et de systèmes de paliers magnétiques actifs. Inclut les activités liées à l’amélioration technique des produits et composants existants Influence la qualité de son propre travail et du travail des collègues de son équipe. Exécute les tâches opérationnelles/techniques standard généralement soumises à des instructions et à des routines professionnelles. Une certaine latitude est accordée pour réorganiser l'ordre des tâches en fonction de l'évolution des situations professionnelles. Job Description Rôles et responsabilités Définit la configuration physique optimum pour convertir les mouvements mécaniques développant un système électrique alimenté pour produire de l'électricité.Concerne la configuration des appareils et systèmes électriques, en particulier des générateurs principaux, des dispositifs électroniques de puissance, des appareillages de commutation, des transformateurs, des barres omnibus, des câbles, des matériaux non conducteurs et des concepts complets d'intégration du système. Élargir la connaissance de sa propre discipline technique pour exécuter la politique/stratégie. Peut inclure des rôles de soutien dans des domaines de connaissances techniques spécialisés. Poursuivre son acquisition de connaissances et de compétences de haut niveau. Compréhension de base des principaux facteurs opérationnels ; utilise cette compréhension pour accomplir son propre travail. Bonne compréhension de la manière dont le travail de sa propre équipe s'intègre aux autres équipes et contribue à son domaine. items.title: PhD Position 100% – AI Literacy & Regulatory Learning (m/w/d)
items.desc: Your tasks Examine how AI-literacy frameworks cultivate individual and organisational absorptive capacity in public bodies and support regulatory learning. Use case studies and pre/post assessments to measure how literacy interventions affect evidence generation, procurement choices, escalation paths and the circulation of lessons across units and agencies. Build an inventory and typology of AI-literacy frameworks, validate interventions, report on literacy effects, and develop guidance for integrating literacy with procurement and review cycles. Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team; prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials; complete a doctoral thesis and related publications. Participate in REGULAIRE training, network reviews, dissemination, practitioner engagement, summer schools and monthly paper development seminars. Secondment Within the position, a secondment to a partner organization is planned. Supervision Primary supervision by Prof. Aurelia Tamò-Larrieux (HSG), co-supervision by Ass. Prof. Sandra Cortesi, plus a sectoral mentor at the secondment host. The secondment provides direct insight into the design and evaluation of AI-literacy initiatives in a public administration. Your profile Master's degree (or equivalent qualification giving access to doctoral studies at the University of St. Gallen) in public administration, political science, learning sciences, information systems, communication, law, or a related social science/interdisciplinary field, completed by the start date. Skills or demonstrable interest in case studies and intervention research, including pre/post assessment designs. Strong interest in AI literacy, public administration, AI governance and interdisciplinary research. Excellent written and spoken English; reliable, independent and analytical working style. Willingness to engage in international mobility and network-wide activities, including the planned secondment. Fulfilment of the doctoral admission requirements of the University of St.Gallen and the MSCA eligibility conditions. Eligibility Applicants may be of any nationality and must not hold a doctoral degree at the start of MSCA employment. Applicants must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: they must not have resided or carried out their main activity in Switzerland for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date (subject to the standard MSCA exclusions). Applicants must be eligible for timely enrolment in the relevant doctoral programme at the University of St.Gallen. The Institute of Law and Economics (ILE-HSG) conducts research at the interface of law (tax law and public law) and business (corporate governance, reporting and tax & trade). www.ile.unisg.ch . We offer A doctoral position within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network REGULAIRE, with an international cohort of 15 doctoral candidates across ten European universities. Cross-institutional supervision, network-wide methods training, three residential summer schools, monthly paper development seminars and practitioner engagement. A stimulating interdisciplinary research environment at the University of St.Gallen with opportunities to contribute to national and international research and policy networks. A planned three-month intersectoral secondment as part of the doctoral project. The opportunity to complete a doctoral thesis and develop an independent research profile in AI governance, law and technology, and regulatory learning. Documents Motivation letter; CV; academic credentials/transcripts; at least two reference letters; a short research proposal engaging with the doctoral project. Apply Apply on the portal of the University of St. Gallen Application Deadline 07.11.2026 We are looking forward to your online-application stating the job ID apply here Inspirational Work Environment At the HSG, as Europe's leading business university, we operate in an entrepreneurial environment where you will meet highly qualified, ambitious experts - both regionally and internationally. For example, you benefit from a modern IT infrastructure and, in our library via HSGswisscovery, from nationwide access to the wealth of scientific information available. Executive Education We support internal and external executive education opportunities. Our internal executive education programme offers you a practical, dedicated and didactically mature transfer of knowledge in the form of seminars, e-learning, coaching and collegial advice. We support task-specific external training and executive education financially as well as with regard to the time required. Network We promote our culture of cross-functional collaboration and create space for forging valuable relationships - also with external partners. Regular exchanges and internal events help to strengthen these relationships and make them long-lasting. Family & Career We provide our employees with flexible work time models with a variable number of hours per week. As a family-friendly employer, we offer part-time positions, 16 weeks of maternity leave and a subsidised crèche, as well as support with childcare during the vacations. Equal Opportunities The University enables equal opportunities for all employees and students. This applies to degree courses and work, as well as academic careers, university management positions and the reconciliation of studies, work and private commitments. We are committed to this with various measures in the areas of teaching, research, administration and the Presidency. Fit and Healthy We help you stay fit and healthy. In addition to our diverse range of sports activities at the university, most of which are free of charge, and campaign weeks for corporate health management, we also offer you fruit in the workplace. In our canteen you will find a wide selection of freshly prepared meals - from vegetarian to fish dishes - at discounted prices. Further information on working at the HSG can be found here. University of St.Gallen «A place where knowledge is created» - As one of Europe's leading universities of economics and business administration, the University of St.Gallen (HSG), Switzerland, is committed to the education of over 10'000 students. The HSG is one of the largest employers in the region and provides an attractive and innovative environment for more than 3'800 researchers, educators and professional staff.

It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. items.title: Doktorandplats - statistiker inom tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården
items.desc: Vid Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS) bedrivs världsledande forskning inom åldrande, demens, epidemiologi och vårdvetenskap. Forskningen sträcker sig från grundforskning på molekyl- och cellnivå till kliniska studier och forskning på samhällsnivå. Vid NVS genomför cirka en tredjedel av KI:s studenter sin utbildning på grund- och avancerad nivå. Institutionen med cirka 540 anställda och en omsättning på 530 miljoner miljoner år 2023, består av sju avdelningar och finns på Campus Flemingsberg och Campus Solna. Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård ansvarar för delar av läkarprogrammet. Inom forskarutbildning har vi en egen forskarskola i allmänmedicin. Vår primärvårdsforskning omfattar varierande projekt kring multisjuklighet, folksjukdomar som diabetes, nedsatt njurfunktion och psykisk ohälsa samt även pedagogiska projekt. Närmare 100 personer, av vilka cirka 30 doktorander, är anknutna till avdelningen. Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet? Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid. Forskargruppen Doktorandtjänsten finns inom forskargruppen för STEADY-CAN (Stockholm Early Detection of Cancer Study) vid Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård, Institutionen för neurobiologi, vårdvetenskap och samhälle (NVS). Gruppen består av kliniskt aktiva forskare, statistiker och doktorander som arbetar med tidig upptäckt av cancer, i nära samarbete med Regionalt cancercentrum Stockholm-Gotland och internationella samarbetspartners. Gruppen är involverad i flera pågående forskningsprojekt, inklusive utveckling av statistiska och maskininlärningsbaserade prediktionsmodeller, longitudinell analys av blodprovsdata och registerbaserade kohortstudier inom cancerepidemiologi. Du kommer att ingå i en tvärvetenskaplig grupp där statistiker, allmänläkare och epidemiologer arbetar nära varandra. I praktiken innebär det att du regelbundet diskuterar analysval med kliniker, förklarar statistiska metoder för personer utan statistisk bakgrund och själv lär dig om den kliniska vardagen i primärvården. Gruppen har regelbundna gemensamma analysmöten där du förväntas både ge och ta emot återkoppling på pågående arbete. Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter Detta doktorandprojekt kombinerar traditionell statistisk modellering och maskininlärning i tillämpad forskning kring tidig upptäckt av cancer i primärvården. Projektet använder data från STEADY-CAN-kohorten, som omfattar över 2,7 miljoner vuxna i Region Stockholm med länkade laboratorie-, journal- och registerdata. Under doktorandutbildningen kommer kandidaten att få bred kunskap inom överlevnadsanalys, prediktionsmodellering, maskininlärning och hantering av stora registerbaserade datamängder. Vi söker en motiverad doktorand med god bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. Den framgångsrika kandidaten förväntas ta ett stort eget ansvar genom hela projektet, med stöd från handledarna. Detta innebär konstruktion av analysdatamängder, statistisk analys och implementering av maskininlärningsmetoder, författande av vetenskapliga artiklar samt deltagande i institutionens seminarier och i nationella och internationella konferenser. Vad erbjuder vi? En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård. Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger. Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.* Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. *Om du anser dig ha motsvarande kunskaper ska du följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Bedömning av motsvarande kunskaper för grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå. B) Särskilt behörighetskrav Du uppfyller det särskilda behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du: - Intygar kunskaper i engelska (motsvarande Engelska B/Engelska 6 vid gymnasiet med godkänt betyg). Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan English language requirements for doctoral education. Kontroll av dokument Karolinska Institutet gör kontroll av dokumenten för att upptäcka förfalskningar. Karolinska Institutet förbehåller sig rätten att återkalla antagningsbeslut om förfalskningar eller oriktigheter påvisas. Inlämnande av falska handlingar är ett brott mot svensk lag och anses vara grund för rättsliga åtgärder. Färdigheter och personliga egenskaper Den sökande bör ha en gedigen bakgrund inom statistik/biostatistik. En examen i statistik/biostatistik eller matematisk statistik på avancerad nivå, t.ex. en masterexamen, är starkt meriterande. Utmärkta kunskaper i biostatistik och praktisk erfarenhet av överlevnadsanalys är meriterande. Tidigare erfarenhet av databehandling och statistisk analys är meriterande. Dessa erfarenheter ska företrädesvis vara från en medicinsk forskningsmiljö. Mycket goda kunskaper i statistisk programmering, företrädesvis i R, är avgörande för rollen. Erfarenhet av arbete med svenska registerdata är meriterande. Ett starkt intresse för medicinsk forskning i kombination med en passion för att tillämpa statistiska metoder för att besvara kliniskt relevanta forskningsfrågor är mycket önskvärt. Då STEADY-CAN-databasen, inklusive journal- och registervariabler och tillhörande beskrivningar, är på svenska är goda kunskaper i svenska i tal och skrift ett krav. Handledningen och det internationella samarbetet sker delvis på engelska, varför goda kunskaper även i engelska i tal och skrift också krävs. Den sökande ska ha god kommunikationsförmåga, vilket är avgörande för att samarbeta med tvärvetenskapliga team och effektivt presentera forskningsresultat. Vi lägger mycket stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper i denna rekrytering. Den idealiska kandidaten bör vara: Självständig, strukturerad och med stark analytisk förmåga. Flexibel och ivrig att lära. Denna roll innebär kontinuerligt lärande och anpassning till nya metoder och utmaningar. Öppen för konstruktiva synpunkter och förmåga att delta i balanserad, analytisk självreflektion. Kandidaten ska även trivas med att arbeta i team och samarbeta väl med teammedlemmar med olika akademisk bakgrund. Förklara i ditt personliga brev hur du uppfyller de nödvändiga färdigheterna och egenskaperna. Villkor Doktorandplatsen innebär en anställning som doktorand under maximalt 4 år på heltid. Ansökan Du söker doktorandplatsen i rekryteringsverktyget Varbi. Använd knappen uppe till höger och följ anvisningarna. Vi ser gärna att din ansökan är skriven på engelska, men det går också bra att ansöka på svenska. Din ansökan ska innehålla dessa dokument: - Ett personligt brev och curriculum vitae - Eventuella examensarbeten och publikationer - Andra dokument som styrker de ovan efterfrågade färdigheter och egenskaper - Dokument som styrker det grundläggande behörighetskravet (se A ovan) - Dokument som styrker det särskilda behörighetskravet (se B ovan) Urval Urval bland behöriga sökande görs med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildning. En samlad bedömning av de sökandes meriter och lämplighet kommer att göras. Följande bedömningsgrunder tillämpas vid Karolinska Institutet: - Dokumenterade ämneskunskaper av betydelse för forskningsområdet - Analytisk skicklighet - Övriga dokumenterade kunskaper/erfarenheter som kan ha betydelse för aktuell forskarutbildning Alla sökanden kommer att få information när rekryteringen är slutförd. KI tillämpar en lönestege vid lönesättning av doktorander. NVS Avdelningen för allmänmedicin och primärvård Vill du göra skillnad - och bidra till en bättre hälsa för alla? items.desc: Tecnun - Escuela de Ingeniería-Universidad de Navarra Tecnun-Escuela de Ingeniería , perteneciente a la Universidad de Navarra , se propone contribuir a la formación profesional, científica y humana de los futuros ingenieros. Desde su creación, en la primavera de 1961, mantiene un equilibrio entre la docencia, la investigación y el servicio a la sociedad, haciendo que estas actividades se complementen entre sí. Actualmente dispone de dos campus : la sede más antigua, ubicada en el campus universitario del Bº de Ibaeta, está integrada por los edificios de laboratorios, el edificio docente y de representación concluido en 1989, y un edificio multiuso, levantado en 1996. La otra sede se encuentra en el Parque Tecnológico de Miramón e integra las aulas y laboratorios de investigación de las áreas de Electricidad, Electrónica y Comunicaciones. Descripción de la oferta Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants Should Submit a Dossier Including: Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI
items.desc: The Human Centered Computing Section at the Department of Computer Science, Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen invites applicants for a PhD fellowship on Street-level Bureaucracy of Regulatory Implementation for AI. The start date is expected to be 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position This doctoral position is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Project description The PhD student’s research is expected to conduct in-depth qualitative studies of how EU digital regulation (e.g., AIA, DSA) is technically and organisationally implemented in SMEs developing AI-related technologies. The goal is to map developers’ translation of regulatory guidance into product and service design and compares implementation strategies across sectors. This project offers a focused route into human-centred computing, sociotechnical research and the study of regulation in practice. You will join an international cohort, receive supervision across institutions and take part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The PhD student to be recruited in this call is expected to define their PhD project within the scope of the overall project and collaborate with the larger project team. Description of the scientific environment The position will be within the Human Centered Computing section (HCC). The Human Centered Computing section is a highly interdisciplinary group that conducts research within the areas of Human-Computer Interaction, Computer Supported Cooperative Work, Ubiquitous and Pervasive Computing, Digital Fabrication and related fields. Our section aspires to be a top research environment that bridges technology, theory, and empirical studies. The Human Centered Computing research environment at the University of Copenhagen is internationally leading, as evidenced by it’s ranking as second in Europe according to CSRankings. Further information about research at the Department is available here: https://di.ku.dk/english/research/ . This position will be co-supervised by Irina Shklovski (email: ias@di.ku.dk ) and Naja Holten Møller (email: naja@di.ku.dk ) at the University of Copenhagen in the Department of Computer Science, Human-Centered Computing section. The PhD will be conducted in collaboration with Joris Van Hoboken, Professor of Information Law, with special emphasis on Law and Digital Infrastructure at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Faculty of Law, University of Amsterdam Who are we looking for? Applicants should hold a MSc degree or equivalent in Computer Science, Data Science, HCI, Critical Data Studies, STS, Law and Policy or a related field. Good written and oral English skills are a requirement. Previous scientific publications (if any) and relevant work experience is encouraged Applicants must be willing to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities The ideal candidate would have an educational background or prior work experience in technology development, prior experience in qualitative research and fieldwork in organisations, and some understanding of European regulatory and policy concerns around AI systems. The PhD programme You can undertake the PhD programme as: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish Master’s degree. Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme equivalent to a Danish Master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the position, i.e. HCI or CS. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Additional qualifications for the MSCA PhD REGULAIRE is funded by the European Commission’s Marie Skłodowska-Curie programme and to be eligible for this funding you must meet the following criteria: You must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to your recruitment; You must work on the project full-time. Please ensure that this information is clear on your CV. Researchers can be of any nationality. Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as a PhD fellow is full time, on site in Copenhagen, and for maximum 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific position formulated by the applicant. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme Carry out a research project with increasing autonomy from your supervisors Collaborate with researchers both within the research group, and with external project partners Author scientific papers aimed at high-impact venues Participate in the research and training activities with the REGULAIRE network Disseminate research nationally and internationally Attend PhD courses on general skills development such as academic writing, as well as relevant specialised courses such as REGULAIRE summer and winter schools Conduct a change of scientific environment in the form of a secondment with a relevant standards organisation and an extended visit with one of the REGULAIRE academic partners Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project We are looking for the following qualifications: Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD position Relevant educational background Relevant publications Relevant work experience Other relevant professional activities Good written and oral English language skills Application and Assessment Procedure Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. Please include : Cover Letter detailing your motivation and background for applying for this PhD position; Research Statement detailing your desired research focus and goals for the PhD studies within the scope of the specified position. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research direction within technology governance you wish to explore, including: specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature, and the potential impact and applications ; Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position; Original diplomas for Bachelor’s and Master’s degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted; Publication list (if available); Names and contact details of three references. Application deadline: The deadline for applications is November 22 , 23:59 GMT +1 . We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements. The further process After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by unbiased expert assessors. You will be notified about whether your application will be selected for assessment. The assessors will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessments. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/. Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in December Questions For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact ias@di.ku.dk General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position. Vi søger svar og løsninger på fælles problemer og gør ny viden tilgængelig og nyttig for andre. items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology at the University of Oulu (Finland)
items.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are currently looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland. The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) . The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities. The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education. About the job As a doctoral researcher, you will: Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning. Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities . Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers. Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities. Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners. Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results. In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Qualifications To succeed in the position, we expect from you: A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline. A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values. Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research. Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research. Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments. Additional merits considered an advantage Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education . Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers . Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design . Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning . Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments. Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage). What we offer? The support of an experienced and enthusiastic project team of where you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and close-ones in settling into Oulu. We have a HR Excellence in Research -quality label which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, excellent education system, and competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Salary The position is fixed-term for three years as soon as possible or starting from January 2027. The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (maximum of 50% of the job-specific component). Starting gross salary will be approx. 2300-2600 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6 months is applied in the position. How to apply? Interested? If yes, please apply by 15.11.2026 (23:59 Finnish local time) through our recruitment system. The application should be written in English and include the following: Cover letter CV following the guidelines of the Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity Certificates/Diplomas Contact information of two persons available for recommendation The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-site or remote interview. All applicants will be notified during the selection process. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, such as people of different ages, genders and lingual, cultural or minority groups. Contact Information If you have any further questions, please contact D r. items.title: Doctorat (H/F) en Web Sémantique et Intelligence Artificielle
items.desc: L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Laboratoire d'Informatique, Signaux et Systèmes de Sophia Antipolis Type de Contrat CDD Doctorant Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 06903 VALBONNE Durée du contrat 36 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration 2300,00 € mensuel Date limite de candidature : vendredi 6 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Sujet De Thèse Dans le cadre du projet ANR DIVA, cette thèse se concentrera sur la modélisation sémantique et la représentation en graphes de connaissances de l’activité analytique des utilisateurs, ainsi que sur l’étude d’approches neuro-symboliques pour apprendre et raisonner sur ces représentations. L’objectif est ainsi de poser les fondations nécessaires à la prédiction de comportements et, à terme, au développement de mécanismes de recommandation et d’adaptation des visualisations explicables et contrôlables. Malgré des travaux importants sur la capture et la visualisation des traces d'activité des utilisateurs, les représentations existantes sont généralement propriétaires ou ad hoc [1], ce qui limite le raisonnement automatisé, l'interopérabilité et la réutilisation à long terme. Les graphes de connaissances (GC), fondés sur les normes du Web sémantique telles que RDF, RDFS et OWL, offrent une alternative prometteuse pour représenter l'activité des utilisateurs sous forme de données liées et riches sur le plan sémantique [3]. Ils permettent notamment de structurer et intégrer des données d'activité hétérogènes, tout en fournissant des mécanismes standardisés d'interrogation et de raisonnement. Cette représentation constitue ainsi un support pertinent pour l'application de méthodes d'IA visant à identifier des comportements analytiques et à en prédire l'évolution, tout en conservant une représentation explicite et interprétable des connaissances. S'appuyant sur des travaux antérieurs (par exemple, UI2Ont [4] et DIVA [5], et des ensembles de données ouverts sur l'activité des utilisateurs [6], cette thèse de doctorat vise à développer des modèles sémantiques et des approches neuro-symboliques pour la représentation et l'analyse de l'activité utilisateur. Elle s'articule autour des objectifs suivants : Modélisation sémantique de l'activité de l'utilisateur : Développer un cadre unifié, fondé sur des vocabulaires RDF, pour représenter l'activité multimodale de l'utilisateur sous forme de GC, en intégrant et structurant les données hétérogènes générées lors de l'exploration visuelle, notamment les interactions de l'utilisateur, le suivi du regard et les verbalisations. Découverte et prédiction du comportement exploratoire de l'utilisateur : Étudier des méthodes neuro-symboliques permettant d'exploiter les GC pour découvrir et prédire des comportements exploratoires, en combinant apprentissage automatique et raisonnement symbolique afin d'identifier des modèles comportementaux interprétables. Raffinement dynamique et validation des modèles comportamentaux : Étudier des méthodes de raffinement incrémental des modèles et règles comportementaux au cours de l'exploration, et évaluer leur qualité, leur interprétabilité et leurs capacités prédictives dans différents scénarios d'utilisation. Plan de travail : La thèse débutera par une revue de l’état de l’art, suivie du développement et de la validation du modèle sémantique et des pipelines de construction des graphes de connaissances. Les travaux porteront ensuite sur la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires à l’aide de méthodes neuro-symboliques, puis sur leur raffinement dynamique et incrémental. Les approches développées seront évaluées sur des données réelles et donneront lieu à des publications scientifiques ainsi qu’à des contributions open source. Les livrables attendus sont : L1. Modèle sémantique et extension de DIVA-O pour l’activité utilisateur multimodale. L2. Pipeline de construction et d’enrichissement des graphes de connaissances. L3. Méthodes neuro-symboliques pour la découverte et la prédiction des comportements exploratoires. L4. Méthodes de raffinement dynamique des modèles comportementaux. L5. Évaluation expérimentale des modèles et méthodes proposés. L6. Publications scientifiques et ressources open source. Références Bibliographiques [3] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces – Yet Another User Interface Description Language?,” 2011. [4] H. Paulheim and F. Probst, “UI2Ont—A Formal Ontology on User Interfaces and Interactions,” in Semantic Models for Adaptive Interactive Systems, T. Hussein, H. Paulheim, S. Lukosch, J. Ziegler, and G. Calvary, Eds., London: Springer, 2013, pp. 1–24. doi: 10.1007/978-1-4471-5301-6_1. [5] A. Menin and C. Faron, “DIVA: An Ontology-based Approach to Model User Activity within Visualization Systems,” in SAC 2026 - 41st ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing, Thessaloniki, Greece, Mar. 2026. doi: 10.1145/3748522.3779893. [6] S. Mohseni, A. Pachuilo, E. H. Nirjhar, R. Linder, A. Pena, and E. D. Ragan, “Analytic Provenance Datasets: A Data Repository of Human Analysis Activity and Interaction Logs,” Jan. 16, 2018, arXiv: arXiv:1801.05076. doi: 10.48550/arXiv.1801.05076. Votre Environnement de Travail Cette thèse est accueillie par le laboratoire I3S du CNRS à l’Université Côte d’Azur. Plus précisément, le/la doctorant(e) rejoindra l’équipe Wimmics (Inria, Université Côte d’Azur, CNRS, I3S), qui mène des recherches à l’interface entre intelligence artificielle et Web, notamment autour des graphes de connaissances, de la représentation et du traitement sémantique des données, et des méthodes d’IA pour les données du Web. Cette thèse s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR JCJC DIVA, qui vise à étudier comment l’activité des utilisateurs avec des systèmes de visualisation interactifs peut être capturée, représentée et exploitée afin de mieux comprendre et, à terme, accompagner leurs processus d’analyse. Le projet part du constat que les interactions des utilisateurs avec les visualisations constituent une source riche d’information sur leurs processus analytiques, leurs stratégies et leurs objectifs, mais que les approches existantes reposent souvent sur des représentations ad hoc, limitant leur interopérabilité, leur réutilisation et le raisonnement automatisé [1], [2]. DIVA vise ainsi à développer des approches sémantiques et neuro-symboliques pour représenter l’activité des utilisateurs et identifier des comportements analytiques à partir de leurs traces d’interaction avec le système, des données biometriques, ainsi que des verbalisations sur leur raisonnement. Références [1] K. Xu, A. Ottley, C. Walchshofer, M. Streit, R. Chang, and J. Wenskovitch, “Survey on the Analysis of User Interactions and Visualization Provenance,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 39, no. 3, pp. 757–783, 2020. [2] F. Yanez, C. Conati, A. Ottley, and C. Nobre, “The State of the Art in User‐Adaptive Visualizations,” Comput. Graph. Forum, vol. 44, Dec. 2024, doi: 10.1111/cgf.15271.
