items.title: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience
items.desc: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience We are looking for a PhD candidate to join the Multimodal Imaging in Clinical Neuroscience department at the Institute of Neuroscience and Medicine – Medical Imaging Physics (INM-4). You will work in the field of translational neuroscience and precision psychiatry under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar. The brain mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders are poorly understood, and treatment choices are largely symptom-based. In this project, you will use multimodal neuroimaging and computational neuroscience to study how brain networks change in these disorders. The aim is to identify imaging biomarkers that could support earlier diagnosis, predict disease trajectories at an individual level and help match treatment to the patient. A key resource is our MINDset platform (Multimodal Imaging Infrastructure for Neuroscience Data Science), which consolidates over 1,000 multimodal datasets from clinical studies, including structural and functional MRI, PET, EEG, fNIRS, neuropsychological and clinical measures, and digital phenotyping. Vertragsart: Vollzeit Angebot Team & Environment: You will work in a motivated and interdisciplinary team including psychiatrists, neuroscientists, physicists, engineers, and data scientists Research & Infrastructure: You will have access to advanced neuroimaging infrastructure and training in structural and functional MRI, multimodal imaging, connectomics, and computational neuroscience Networking & Exchange: You will participate in (international) conferences and project meetings, actively building your scientific network through collaborations involving Forschungszentrum Jülich, RWTH Aachen University, Ulm University, Bezirkskrankenhaus Günzburg and LVR-Klinik Cologne Supervision & Support: We will accompany your doctoral studies with continuous, expert guidance from your academic supervisors Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar Work-life balance: Optimal conditions for balancing work and private life, as well as a family-friendly company policy. The option of flexible working (in terms of location) is generally available after consultation and in line with upcoming tasks and (on-site) appointments Annual Leave: You get 30 days of annual leave Fixed-term: The position is limited to 3 years Fair remuneration: Depending on your existing qualifications and the tasks assigned to you, you will be classified in pay grade 13 (65 %) of the TVöD-Bund (Collective Agreement for the Public Service). In addition to the basic salary, there is an additional year-end bonus under the collective pay agreement amounting to 75% of a monthly salary, as well as capital-forming benefits. All information on the TVöD-Bund collective agreement can be found on the BMI website. The monthly salaries in euros can be found on page 74 of the PDF download Support for international employees: Our International Advisory Service makes it easier for international employees to get started In addition to exciting tasks and a collegial working environment, we offer you much more: https://go.fzj.de/benefits Aufgaben The successful candidate will have the opportunity to combine prospectively acquired data with existing multimodal datasets and contribute to replication studies, biomarker development, machine learning applications, and analyses of individual disease trajectories. Your tasks will include: Integrate multimodal neuroimaging datasets from MRI, PET, EEG, and fNIRS studies Characterize brain networks using graph-theoretical methods and structural and functional connectivity analyses Apply multivariate statistical modelling and machine learning to multimodal datasets Investigate individualized imaging biomarkers relevant to diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring Coordinate longitudinal studies involving psychiatric patients and healthy controls, including recruitment, scheduling, and neuropsychological and psychopathological assessments Coordinate and supervise MRI data acquisition; maintain standardized acquisition protocols and data quality Manage and curate imaging data in accordance with established standards (e.g., BIDS) Profil Excellent university degree (Master) in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, medical physics, psychology, cognitive science, computer science, physics, data science, or a related discipline A strong interest in translational psychiatry, neuroimaging and computational neuroscience, and a motivation to work in an interdisciplinary research environment Programming experience in MATLAB and/or Python, alongside strong analytical and problem-solving skills Experience with structural and/or functional MRI; familiarity with packages such as SPM, FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI, MRtrix, CONN, or similar tools is desirable Knowledge of neuroimaging preprocessing, quality control, graph theory, connectomics, multivariate statistics, or machine learning is an advantage Very good command of written and spoken English with extensive vocabulary is required (at least B2 level according to the CEFR), ideally supported by a certificate confirming the language level German language skills at B1 level are desirable Über uns We welcome applications from people with diverse backgrounds, e.g. in terms of age, gender, disability, sexual orientation / identity, and social, ethnic and religious origin. A diverse and inclusive working environment with equal opportunities in which everyone can realize their potential is important to us. The following links provide further information on diversity and equal opportunities: https://go.fzj.de/equality and on specific support options for women: https://go.fzj.de/womens-job-journey. International applicants can find more information here: https://go.fzj.de/job-journey-internationals

items.title: PhD in Data- and AI-based solutions to improve child health and outcomes through housing
items.desc: Sustainability, in its broadest definition, is the cornerstone of research and education in the Department of Built Environment. We take the lead in (re)shaping the built environment to be future-proof, safe, healthy, inclusive and respectful of planetary boundaries. We house the entire spectrum of technology, engineering, design, and human behavior disciplines in the built environment, with world-class experimental facilities at all scales. This allows us to address societal challenges from a uniquely integrated perspective. Introduction Are you a graduate in exact sciences, engineering or econometrics, passionate about using data and AI to improve people's lives?Eindhoven University of Technology is looking for a PhD candidate to develop innovative data-driven solutions that predict and optimise the impact of housing improvements on children's health and wellbeing. Job Description Millions of children, even in high-income countries, are born and grow up in homes with poor insulation, inadequate heating, or insufficient ventilation, affecting their health and development. While housing upgrades are often motivated by sustainability and affordability goals, we focus on their potential benefits for future generations. How does inadequate housing during pregnancy and early childhood affect children's health and development? Which housing upgrades offer the greatest benefits? And how can behavioural modelling, big data and AI help shape healthier, more equitable homes? These are the questions your PhD research will tackle. You will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers and practitioners, working at the intersection of housing, public health, climate adaptation, and social equity. Combining medical and behavioural insights, large-scale data analysis, computer vision and advanced statistical methods, you will be tranforming complex unstructured housing and health data into predictive models. The results will feed into a digital tool to predict and optimise the impact of housing upgrades across different scenarios, helping housing providers and municipalities create healthier, more resilient homes for families. This research is part of the NWO-funded research programme Homes for Upcoming Generations, which brings together social scientists, medical doctors, building engineers and industry partners. As a PhD candidate, you will be part of the TU/e's internationally renowned Urban Systems and Real Estate group (Department of the Built Environment), conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of urban systems, real estate, data science, and smart technologies. The four-year program combines advanced training with impactful research, offering strong support for professional development through courses, seminars, and international conferences. You will collaborate closely with scientific partners at Erasmus Medical Centre, Erasmus University Rotterdam, VU University Amsterdam, as well as societal partners including housing providers, municipalities and engineering bureaus. A proven experience of programming in Python and working with (big) data. Having working experience at a European research institute or a European university is an advantage. Strong demonstrable analytical skills and proficiency in English (spoken and written). Affinity with collaboration with industry, ability to bring together fundamental and applied research. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). items.title: PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point ultrasound'
items.desc: Jouw functie Ultrasound and tomosynthesis are the most prevalent modalities used for breast imaging, and each has its specific advantages and disadvantages. Ultrasound uses sound waves to create a cross-sectional image of the tissue and has excellent depth resolution, but limited resolution in directions perpendicular to the transmitted ultrasound lines. Tomosynthesis uses x rays to create a pseudo-3D representation of the breast with high in-plane spatial resolution, but low out-of-plane (depth) resolution. Therefore, both techniques are complementary to each other. We plan to develop a joint system that will use the information from each modality to improve the image quality of the other, yielding not only a multi-modality imaging system, but a joint imaging system. The combination of tomosynthesis and ultrasound into a single joint imaging system will yield improved images from two independent and complementary sources, with inherent spatial correlation, allowing for improved lesion detection, even in dense breasts, and the direct multi-modal assessment of suspicious lesions. For this multi-disciplinary project, we will be working in collaboration with the Advanced X-ray Tomography Imaging (AXTI) lab of our Department, who will be developing the X-ray aspects of this system (see accompanying vacancy). In this project, you will focus on 3D ultrasound by using an ultra-wide ultrasound transducer that is mounted in a paddle required for acquisition of tomosynthesis data. In this way, a 3D ultrasound dataset can be acquired that can be used to improve the x-ray data by using the high-axial resolution US data. Additionally, the ultrasound data can be improved by using the high-resolution x-ray data. You will develop and validate these methods using both digital and physical phantoms, working towards first patient images at the end of the project. All of this will be in collaboration with a PhD student focusing on the x-ray aspects of the project, and industry partners to facilitate the translation of these methods into clinical evaluation. Tasks will also include presenting at international scientific conferences and writing papers on the newly developed methods and study results. PhD candidate 'Development of an integrated system for breast cancer imaging | focus point X-ray' Jouw werkplek Nijmegen and the Radboudumc Nijmegen is the oldest Dutch city with a rich history and one of the liveliest city centers in the Netherlands. Radboud University has over 17,000 students. Radboud University Medical Center is a leading academic center for medical science, education, and health care with over 10,000 staff and 3,000 students. Department of Medical Imaging The Department of Medical Imaging is one of the most active research departments of the Radboudumc. More than 200 researchers are continuously striving to optimize healthcare. Close cooperation between preclinical researchers, radiologists, and clnicians gives a fantastic opportunity to implement new imaging techniques in clinical practice, and you will be working directly in this field. Medical Ultrasound Imaging Center: MUSIC The MUSIC laboratory works on the development, optimization, and clinical evaluation of new ultrasound imaging methods. For that, MUSIC collaborates with major vendors of ultrasound equipment. The focus of MUSIC is on development of high end ultrasound solutions for improved diagnosis of breast cancer, carotid diseases, and liver steatosis. Additionally, AI-driven handheld ultrasound solutions are developed for improving diagnosis in low resource settings, and by general practitioners and doctors in child consultation centers. For this, the group has researchers with various backgrounds, from engineering to medical doctors, providing wide-ranging expertise in image reconstruction and processing, deep learning and other AI methods, and analysis, along with the design and performance of patient trials. The laboratory works closely with radiologists and industry. Jouw profiel Requirements You should be a creative and enthusiastic researcher with a MSc degree in physics, mathematics, engineering, Technical medicine, or similar. Experience or interest in physics modeling, inverse problems, and/or image processing, and affinity with biomedical research. Experience in programming in python, C/C++, Matlab, or similar. Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken. Goed om te weten The following should be included in your application : CV, letters of motivation, list of completed courses and grades, and reprints or, preferably, links to your thesis or any scientific publications or reports that you have written. The first job interviews will take place on 2 November 2026 . Please take this into account. All additional information about the vacancy can be obtained from Prof. Chris de Korte. This position requires a Certificate of Conduct (VOG). We are recruiting for this position ourselves. Unsolicited marketing is not appreciated, but do feel free to share the vacancy in your network! More than 100 researchers are continuously striving to optimize healthcare. items.title: PhD Autonomous & Decentralized Air Traffic Management
items.desc: Functieomschrijving Background Air Traffic Management (ATM) and Communications, Navigation, and Surveillance (CNS) systems form the operational foundation of civil aviation. Current operations depend heavily on centralized ground facilities and satellite services for surveillance and management. This system is vulnerable for a range of disruptions including infrastructure failures, GNSS outages or cyber incidents. These vulnerabilities can degrade or even halt civil aviation. Project ORION (Onboard Resilient Infrastructure-free Operational Network) investigates an alternative ATM/CNS architecture designed to function without reliance on ground- or space-based infrastructure. By utilizing an aeronautical ad-hoc network for communication, relative positioning, and surveillance, ORION aims to enable aircraft to self-organize and maintain safe separation thus ensuring a minimum service level even during (large scale) disruptions. Project description This PhD project is fundamentally multidisciplinary. As a PhD candidate, you will design, model, and evaluate a decentralized ATM/CNS architecture. The research focuses on determining how core traffic management functions can be sustained through cooperation using an aeronautical network when centralized ground and satellite services are unavailable. In the first phase of the research, you will determine a set of use cases and design the underlying aeronautical ad-hoc networking concept layer to enable direct airborne data exchange, cooperative relative localization, and cooperative surveillance. Next, building on this network layer, you will formulate distributed algorithms for fundamental traffic management functions, including aircraft-as-a-sensor (mesh network), separation assurance, conflict detection and resolution, and traffic sequencing. Finally, to evaluate the operational feasibility of the architecture, you will implement the models within an ATM simulation platform, such as the open-source simulator BlueSky. For this you will extend the platform to include the ad-hoc networking functionality. Using this environment, you will stress-test the system under severe disruption scenarios by comparing the overall performance directly against conventional centralized ATM/CNS operations. This will provide evidence of the performance of the models for the various use-cases. Your profile Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field; Strong analytical and mathematical foundation, with experience in or a keen aptitude for complex systems modelling and distributed systems; Multidisciplinary mindset with the ability to bridge distinct domains: connecting operational ATM concepts with distributed network protocols and algorithm design; Strong background in programming, using Python or other relevant programming languages; Good scientific reporting and communication skills in written and spoken English. What we offer you You will receive a 4-year research contract from NLR and will join the Air Traffic department. In addition, you will be enrolled in the Doctoral Education programme of the Graduate School at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). During this period, you will work closely with NLR colleagues in Amsterdam and with academic supervisors from TU Delft. Your working week will ideally be divided into: 2 days in Amsterdam, 2 days in Delft, and 1 day from home. In addition, we offer: No fewer than 45 days off (with full-time employment); A fixed end-of-year bonus of 8%; A contribution towards your healthcare costs; Extra paid parental leave; The possibility to work from home where possible. Would you like to know more? Please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/en/ae/research/ae-graduate-school for more information on the graduate school. For more information about the recruitment procedure, contact Pien Moller (recruiter) via pien.moller@nlr.nl. Would you like to apply? Great, we are curious about you! Send your motivation letter and CV via the apply button ! A pre-employment security screening (VGB-C) is a requirement. For more information about the screening, please visit the AIVD website. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. items.title: PhD Position in Bidirectional Power Converter Design and Control for Data Centers
items.desc: The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Introduction Data centers are the backbone of the digital economy, but their exponential growth in energy consumption-driven by AI and machine learning workloads-demands transformative solutions. The next-generation of data centers will be based on Solid-State Transformer, which enables energy distribution with higher efficiency, grid-friendly data center operation and etc. This PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of power electronics, control systems, and grid integration, with direct collaboration with Delta Energy System GmbH, a global leader in power conversion for data centers. Your research will focus on power electronics converters for SST, focusing on the DC-DC stage. Job Description As a PhD candidate in the Electromechanics and Power Electronics (EPE) group at TU/e, you will with solid-state transformers (SST) for datacenter, focusing on the DC-DC stage. Your research will address the critical challenges of power density, efficiency, and grid stability in modern data centers, focusing on the converter design and advanced control/modulation strategies to achieve high performance and high controllability. Additionally, the design should be validate with experimental results. Your work will directly contribute to the sustainability of AI infrastructure by enabling data centers to efficiently integrate renewable energy sources, support grid stability, and reduce their carbon footprint. With access to cutting-edge tools and industrial collaboration, you will have the opportunity to shape the future of power electronics for data centers. Job Requirements A master's degree (or equivalent university degree) in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Control Systems, or a related field. A research-oriented attitude with strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interest in collaborating with industrial partners. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Based on our candidate assessment, the following skills are valuable: Required: Demonstrated knowledge in power converter topologies (e.g., DC-DC, AC-DC, multilevel converters). Familiarity with control theory (e.g., classical control, state-space methods, model predictive control). Experience with simulation tools (MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, or similar). Understanding of grid integration challenges (e.g., power quality, stability, renewable energy interfacing). Advantageous: Hands-on experience with prototyping and experimental validation of power converters. Affinity with embedded systems (DSP, FPGA) for real-time control implementation. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. Information Do you recognize yourself in this profile, do not hesitate to apply directly through our web platform. For additional information please contact: dr. Levy Costa, l.costa@tue.nl. Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video. Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page. Application We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a: Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and qualifications for the position. A factual, position-focused curriculum vitae, including a list of your publications and the contact information of three references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application. Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications. We look forward to receiving your application and will screen it as soon as possible. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled. Please note You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. items.title: 3 PhD Candidates in Material Science and Energy Engineering
items.desc: Career Vacant positions Job vacancy 3 PhD Candidates in Material Science and Energy Engineering SINTEF Industry, Department of Metal Production and Processing (MPP) & Department of Sustainable Energy Technology (BET) and announce three PhD candidate position within the field of Energy engineering and material science. The position is within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidates will be employed by the Casting, Forming, and Recycling and Solar Energy and Materials research groups during the doctoral project, enrolled by the doctoral program at Brunel University of London , and have supervisors both at SINTEF and Brunel, College of Engineering, Design and Physical Science. As part of the MSCA Doctoral Network programme, the successful candidate will undertake a secondment with one of the project's industrial partners. This position’s scope is Integrated Modelling of Thermal Energy Flows, Waste Heat Recovery, and High-Temperature Heat Pump Deployment in Industrial Clusters. Development and Validation of Modular Digital Twin Frameworks for Industrial High-Temperature Heat Pump Integration Developing Decarbonisation Pathways for Industrial Heat Through High-Temperature Heat Pumps, Renewable Energy Integration, and Thermal Storage The activity is coordinated within the MSCA-DN by the Brunel University of London. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 6 partners and 12 Associated partners across Europe. The project aims to undertake cutting-edge multidisciplinary research and development to make a step change in the understanding of Industrial High Temperature Heat Pump (IHTHP) technology, both at the overall system and component levels while addressing sustainability, economic social impact and energy policy aspects to support realising its potential to provide a breakthrough towards full industrial heat decarbonisation helping to achieve the 2050 net-zero emissions targets. The topics hosted by SINTEF is "Mapping Industrial Energy Flows and Developing Decarbonisation Pathways for IHTHP Integration" and focus on developing data-driven strategies for industrial heat decarbonisation by mapping energy flows, integrating HTHPs with low-carbon technologies, and creating decision-support databases for system design and sustainability assessment. "Development of Digital Twin Frameworks for Predictive Modelling and Optimisation of IHTHPs" and focus on developing and validating digital twin frameworks for the integration and optimisation of IHTHPs in high-temperature industrial processes, enhancing the understanding of industrial energy flows and optimisation strategies, and enabling factory-wide digital energy management systems to support industrial digitalisation, energy efficiency, and decarbonisation. "Grid integration and sector coupling challenges of electrifying industrial heat using IHTHPs" and focus integrating IHTHPs, renewable energy, and thermal storage to enhance grid flexibility, support industrial decarbonisation, and enable scalable low-carbon heat solutions. The project combines engineering analysis with industrial implementation perspectives, including decision-support methodologies, stakeholder engagement, business case development, techno-economic assessments, innovation management, and pathways for industrial adoption of low-carbon technologies. SINTEF MPP & BET and HeatMinds partners have extensive expertise in Industrial High Temperature Heat Pumps (IHTHPs), thermal systems engineering, energy systems modelling, thermal heat storage, digital twin, waste heat recovery and utilisation, process metallurgy, industrial decarbonisation, data analytics and digitalisation, and socio-economic analysis. The project includes international secondments at academic and industrial institutions and close collaboration with the related PhD positions at Brunel. Contacts Topic 1 and 3 Morten Ingar Onsøien and Sarina Bao Topic 2 and 3 Gaute Stokkan and Eivind Johannes Øvrelid Work place: SINTEF Trondheim and Nordland (secondment partners). Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondments with HeatMinds partners. Participate in conferences, workshops and training activities. Adjust project focus as the PhD progresses if needed. Complete doctoral education. Participate actively in the Casting, Forming, and Recycling and Solar Energy and Materials two research groups. Required selection criteria Relevant Master's degree in Material Science, Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Process Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Sustainable Energy Systems, Industrial Ecology, Technology Management, Engineering Management, Systems Engineering, Industrial Digitalisation, or similar. Experience with data analytics, decision-support systems, digitalisation, industrial management, innovation management, technology transfer, project portfolio management, or industrial transformation projects is considered an advantage Degree completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential. Excellent written and spoken English. Applicants must meet one of the following English language requirements: IELTS 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in all components), PTE Academic 59 (minimum 59 in all subscores), BrunELT 6.5 (minimum 6.0 in all components), or TOEFL iBT 5.0 (minimum 4.5 in all subscores). Further details on accepted qualifications can be found on Brunel University's English Language Requirements page. MSCA Mobility Rule At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date. Preferred selection criteria Experience with one or more of energy engineering, material science, thermal energy systems, industrial energy systems, process systems engineering, sustainable energy technology, industrial ecology, energy and environmental engineering, industrial decarbonisation, energy Informatics, and mechanical engineering Experience with one or more of energy flow modelling, process integration modelling, techno-economic modelling, energy system modelling. Familiarity with one or more of industrial waste heat, including energy flow mapping, integration of high-temperature heat pumps (HTHPs) with low-carbon technologies, and development of decision-support databases for system design and sustainability assessment. Candidates with experience in technology management, industrial transformation, digitalisation, data analytics, or technology commercialisation are encouraged to apply. Ability to work independently and collaboratively in international interdisciplinary teams. To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. We offer Exciting research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network. Dynamic, creative and inclusive work environment. Access to cutting-edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. The employment period is 3 years, conditioned on external funding through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services for both SINTEF and Brunel; Eksportkontroll – DEKSA . Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria, will not be able to be employed. The application must include: Motivation letter (max. 1 page) CV Copies of diplomas and transcripts (Bachelor’s and Master’s) Bachelor’s and Master’s diplomas/transcripts Master’s thesis or draft (if recently submitted) Names and contact information of two references Applications without required documentation will not be considered. Documents must be in English. Applicants are requested to indicate in their application which of the three proposed SINTEF PhD research topics they wish to pursue. Unit SINTEF Industry Work place Trondheim Application due 15/11/2026 Questions regarding the position Eivind Johannes Øvrelid Senior Research Scientist Morten Ingar Onsøien Research Manager Gaute Stokkan Research Manager Sarina Bao Senior Research Scientist SINTEF Industri er ett av fem institutt som utgjør SINTEF. Med over 620 medarbeidere, er vi det største instituttet. Vi legger grunnlaget for fremtidens bærekraftige industri. Med vår flerfaglige kunnskapsbase og avanserte laboratorier som fundament, utvikler vi - i tett samarbeid med våre kunder og samarbeidspartnere - teknologi og tverrfaglige løsninger med stor påvirkning på samfunnet innen et bredt spekter av markeds- og fagområder, for eksempel: Sirkulær økonomi, batterier, hydrogen, CCS, materialvitenskap og -teknologi, nanoteknologi, nanomedisin, sol, vind, bioteknologi, metallproduksjon, prosessteknologi, lavutslippsproduksjon av olje og gass og industriell økonomi og optimering. About SINTEF SINTEF is one of Europe’s largest research institutes, offering specialist multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of technology and the natural and social sciences. SINTEF is an independent foundation that since 1950 has generated innovation by means of research and development projects for the private and public sectors both in Norway and overseas. SINTEF has 2,100 employees from 80 countries and an annual turnover of more than NOK three billion. SINTEF invests any profits into further research and innovation. Our vision: Technology for a better society.

items.title: PhD in Sociology of Law – Securitisation of Religion in Hybrid Regimes
items.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. PhD Position in Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Cultures – Securitisation of Religion in Hybrid Regimes: Insights from Central Asia and North Africa Project description This doctoral project investigates how governments in Uzbekistan and Egypt mobilise religious narratives to justify security policies and governance strategies. The doctoral candidate will analyse how religion becomes embedded within state security frameworks and assess the implications of these processes for citizenship, constitutional legitimacy, and state-society relations in hybrid political regimes. To read more about the MINARET project please see: https://www.norca.lu.se/minaret https://www.soclaw.lu.se/en/article/major-eu-grant-lund-led-phd-programme-islamic-legal-cultures Tasks and responsibilities As a doctoral student, you will be admitted to doctoral studies in sociology of law and employed at Lund University. You will: Conduct independent research within the scope of the project. Undertake multi-sited fieldwork in Central Asia and North Africa (Uzbekistan and Egypt) and two mandatory secondments (one academic, one non-academic) abroad. Participate in training events, workshops, and conferences organized by the MINARET Doctoral Network. Collaborate with international supervisors and peers. Contribute to departmental activities, including teaching and seminars (up to 20% of working hours). If selected for the position, you will join NORCA – Nordic Central Asian Studies (www.norca.lu.se) research environment at the Sociology of Law Department, led by Rustamjon Urinboyev who will also serve as your principal supervisor. You will be given sufficient time, guidance, and resources to develop your individual research project, aligned with the overall MINARET project's aims. Doctoral Programme in Sociology of Law The doctoral programme in sociology of law comprises 240 credits (equivalent to four years of full-time study) and concludes with a public defence of the doctoral thesis. You will primarily engage in doctoral studies and work on your dissertation within the field of sociology of law. You will also actively participate in the department’s research environment. In addition to research, the position may include teaching and administrative duties, up to a maximum of 20% of the working time. The working language is primarily English, but you are expected to acquire basic knowledge of Swedish during the employment period. More information about the doctoral programme is available at: https://www.soclaw.lu.se/en/research/doctoral-studies/phd-handbook General Requirements The requirements for admission to third cycle courses and study programs (in accordance with HF, Chapter 7, Section 35) are that the applicant; meets the general and specific entry requirements that the higher education institution may have laid down, and is considered in other respects to have the ability required to benefit from the course or study program. A person meets the general entry requirements for third cycle courses and study programmes if he or she: has been awarded a second cycle qualification prior to the employment decision, has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. Specific Requirements A completed degree at the advanced level in Sociology of Law or another subject deemed relevant by the employer. Doctoral candidates cannot have been awarded a doctoral degree and/or completed more than four years of full-time equivalent research experience. In line with the eligibility criteria and on Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme, doctoral candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (i.e. work, studies) in the hosting country for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. For further information on eligibility criteria and on Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks in general, please refer to: Doctoral Networks - Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions. A minimum of 240 credits, of which at least 60 must be at the advanced level. At least 30 credits in Sociology of Law or a related subject at the advanced level, including a thesis of at least 15 credits. Excellent ability to express yourself in spoken and written English. Strong motivation and ability to work independently under pressure. Good collaboration and communication skills. Merits Knowledge of legal sociology, Islamic legal culture, security studies and hybrid and authoritarian governance literature. Experience with qualitative research methods and fieldwork. Self-motivated, perseverant, and strong writing skills. Collaborative and independent working style. Knowledge of the legal and political contexts of Central Asia, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is considered an asset. What we offer A full-time, fixed-term employment for four years. Competitive employment package. Joint supervision and intersectoral placements. Comprehensive training in research methods, ethics, Open Science, and transferable skills. Assessment Criteria Regulations for employment as a doctoral student can be found in the Higher Education Ordinance. Only those admitted to third-cycle studies may be appointed to a doctoral position. In the recruitment process, primary consideration will be given to the applicant’s ability to benefit from the doctoral programme. The research plan, as well as previous theses and published material in Sociology of Law or related subjects within social sciences or law, are important documents for assessing this ability. In addition to pursuing their own doctoral studies, the incumbent may be required to perform duties related to education, research, and administration in accordance with specific provisions in the Higher Education Ordinance. Excellent ability to express oneself in speech and writing is of great importance. As doctoral studies in Sociology of Law are highly demanding, the candidate must be strongly motivated and able to work independently under pressure. items.title: PhD in Machine Learning in Medicine
items.desc: About us You will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Lisa Koch, head of the Machine Learning in Medicine Lab (www.mlm-lab.ch). Our research group develops trustworthy machine learning towards clinical use. Our methodological interests include uncertainty quantification, robustness and reliability, representation learning, probabilistic modelling, and causal machine learning, with applications in biomedical imaging, wearable and tabular data. We publish at leading machine learning and medical imaging venues, collaborate closely with clinicians at Inselspital, Bern University Hospital, and maintain close links to research groups across Switzerland and internationally. We are a small and collaborative team and value regular interactions. Bern offers a strong and growing medical AI community and an excellent quality of life. About the project Chronic diseases often develop gradually over years, and their trajectories vary widely between individuals. Understanding this progression is key to early detection and timely intervention. Large multimodal health datasets combining medical imaging, wearable sensor data and clinical measurements now make it possible to study disease progression from multiple perspectives. The goal of this project is to develop machine learning methods that learn from multimodal health data to characterise and model disease progression. Methodological focus areas the candidate may explore include: Multimodal representation learning across imaging, time series and tabular data Disease progression modelling from cross-sectional and sparse longitudinal data Causal machine learning to disentangle disease progression from treatment effects Learning with missing modalities and irregularly sampled signals Fairness and bias in multimodal models across demographic subgroups The candidate We are looking for a curious and motivated PhD candidate with a keen interest in doing machine learning research in the healthcare space. You should hold a Master's degree in a quantitative discipline such as computer science, machine learning, statistics, biomedical or electrical engineering, or similar. You have solid knowledge of the foundations of machine learning, are willing to dig deep to understand a problem, and have strong analytical skills. You have practical experience implementing and evaluating machine learning models in Python. Experience processing biomedical data (imaging, wearable, tabular) is a plus. Application and Contact Applications received by 30 November 2026 will receive full consideration. After the deadline, we may continue to review applications until the position is filled. Applications should include your CV, full transcripts (BSc and MSc), and a cover letter (max 1 page) telling us about your motivation and something you are particularly proud of or passionate about. items.title: BHF 4-Year PhD Studentships in Cardiovascular Research (Prevention)
items.desc: University of Cambridge, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College London and University of Oxford. Applications are invited for 10 funded 4-year PhD studentships starting in October 2027, as part of the British Heart Foundation (BHF) doctoral training programme focused on preventing cardiovascular disease through innovative, data-driven approaches. This interdisciplinary PhD programme brings together leading researchers from the University of Cambridge, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College London, and the University of Oxford. Students will be trained to work at the intersection of population health, systems biology, and data science/AI, combining expertise across these fields to tackle one of the most pressing challenges in global health. By harnessing large-scale multimodal data and emerging technologies, students will develop new approaches to understand, predict, and prevent heart and circulatory diseases. Students will be based in one of the following institutes: Cambridge (5 studentships), Edinburgh (2 studentships), Imperial (1 Studentship) or Oxford (2 studentships) while benefiting from training, co-supervision, and collaboration across the partner institutions. Projects will span a range of topics including health data science, AI and machine learning, multi-omics, epidemiology, and translational cardiovascular research. Students will be part of a cohort-based programme, gaining access to shared training activities, collaborative networks, and state-of-the-art data resources across the multi-institute partnership. This four-year PhD programme combines interdisciplinary training with in-depth research. In year 1, students will undertake training courses and research rotations (at their host institution) before selecting their PhD project and supervisory team. In years 2-4, students will carry out their PhD research with interdisciplinary supervision. Additional opportunities will include advanced training courses, programme-wide workshops and symposia, and optional placements with our academic or industry partners, including EMBL-European Bioinformatics Institute, Wellcome Sanger Institute, AstraZeneca, Novo Nordisk, Genomics Ltd, Owlstone Medical, ThermoFischer Scientific and Flagship Pioneering. The co-leads of the programme are: Cambridge - Professor Angela Wood Edinburgh - Professor Nicholas Mills Imperial - Associate Professor Michela Noseda Oxford - Professor Sarah Lewington Eligibility Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a first or upper second-class undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline such as statistics, mathematics, computer science, data science, engineering, bioinformatics, epidemiology, biomedical sciences, genetics, public health, or another quantitative or biomedical field, and may also hold a Master's degree in a related subject. Applicants should also demonstrate strong analytical skills, experience working with data or computational methods, and an interest in interdisciplinary research. Strong communication and teamwork skills are essential, and international applicants may need to provide evidence of English language proficiency. Funding The studentship provides: University tuition fees (UK home rate only) A tax-free stipend at the BHF rate Research training and support We invite applications from students who meet the UK residency requirements (home fees). International students who confirm that additional costs of all overseas tuition fees will be covered through other scholarships or funding schemes will also be considered. How to apply Please do not use the University application portals. To apply, please email bhfphdadmin@medschl.cam.ac.uk with the following documents. Curriculum vitae (CV) Two letters of recommendation from your referees, signed Transcripts A cover letter (maximum 2500 characters) outlining your suitability for the PhD programme and indicating your preferred host institutions in order of preference. Please list only institutions that you would be willing to attend if offered a place, even if they are not your first choice. Evidence of competence in English - If required - please see our Competence in English guidance for more information. AI must not be used when writing personal statements and CVs. This prohibition covers the use of AI to help your use of English. Using AI in your application ' Postgraduate Study Application deadline: 8th December 2026 Please quote reference RH51427 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

items.title: Phd candidate - Generative Agent-Based Modeling for Climate Policy Design
items.desc: Tecnun - Escuela de Ingeniería-Universidad de Navarra Tecnun-Escuela de Ingeniería , perteneciente a la Universidad de Navarra , se propone contribuir a la formación profesional, científica y humana de los futuros ingenieros. Desde su creación, en la primavera de 1961, mantiene un equilibrio entre la docencia, la investigación y el servicio a la sociedad, haciendo que estas actividades se complementen entre sí. Actualmente dispone de dos campus : la sede más antigua, ubicada en el campus universitario del Bº de Ibaeta, está integrada por los edificios de laboratorios, el edificio docente y de representación concluido en 1989, y un edificio multiuso, levantado en 1996. La otra sede se encuentra en el Parque Tecnológico de Miramón e integra las aulas y laboratorios de investigación de las áreas de Electricidad, Electrónica y Comunicaciones. Descripción de la oferta Fully Funded PhD Opportunity at TECNUN, the School of Engineering of the University of Navarra, Spain We are seeking a highly motivated PhD Researcher to join our team for a 3- to 4-year fully funded PhD opportunity. The successful candidate will work at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, and Policy Modelling to build advanced decision-support tools for climate action and disaster resilience. The candidate will be part of the Resilience research group at TECNUN, which focuses on understanding and strengthening the resilience of communities, cities, and organizations in the face of disruptions and crises. The group combines engineering, data-driven approaches, and decision-support methodologies, with research spanning areas such as urban resilience, crisis management, infrastructure, and emerging technologies such as AI and LLMs. The PhD candidate will join this research environment under the supervision of Professor Josune Hernantes and Dr. Sahar Elkady. About The Project This PhD project focuses on developing a novel decision-support framework that combines Generative Agent-Based Modelling (GABM) with Simulation Optimization. The primary goal is to simulate how diverse societal stakeholders (e.g., citizens, businesses, and public authorities) interact, perceive, and respond to climate-related policies. By integrating LLM-driven generative agents into an optimization loop, the project aims to help decision-makers design robust policies that balance environmental targets with public acceptance and social legitimacy. Main Duties And Responsibilities The PhD candidate will conduct research leading to the development of their doctoral thesis, with the aim of disseminating their findings through high-quality publications in highly ranked, internationally recognized journals. The candidate will be expected to take an active role in the development and execution of research projects related to their research topic, as well as contribute to the preparation and submission of research proposals and funding applications. The candidate should also be willing to actively participate in seminars, workshops, meetings, and other activities organized by the Department and the research group. As part of the responsibilities established in the PhD student agreement, the candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching activities, including serving as a teaching assistant in selected courses and proctoring examinations. These responsibilities are intended to provide the candidate with broader academic and professional development alongside their research activities. Requisitos Provisions relating to positions as PhD Research Fellows can be found in the Applied Engineering program web page. Education: MSc degree in Computer Science, Operations Research, Data Science, Industrial Engineering, Computational Social Science, or a closely related field. Technical Skills: Solid background in computational modelling, simulation, or optimization techniques. Programming proficiency in Python (experience with LLM frameworks, prompt engineering, or agent-based frameworks is a strong plus). Familiarity with machine learning, Large Language Models (LLMs), or natural language processing. Soft Skills: Strong analytical problem-solving abilities, excellent writing skills for scientific publications, and the ability to work independently within a multidisciplinary team. We recognize that candidates may have different academic and professional backgrounds. If you do not meet all of the requirements but believe that your skills, experience, and motivation make you a strong potential candidate, we still encourage you to apply. We look forward to hearing from you. Application Applicants Should Submit a Dossier Including Detailed Curriculum Vitae including all the relevant projects/publications. Certificates and transcripts of the bachelor's and master's degrees. Applicants with foreign higher education must attach an official description of the grading system used at the issuing institution. One-page summary of MSc’s thesis The names and contact details of two references. A one-page document answering the following questions (Please describe any relevant academic, research, or practical experience, including optimization, mathematical modelling, simulation, or related methods): What is your experience with ABM? What is your experience with LLM and Software Engineering? What is your experience with Operations Research? For further information or queries, please contact Sahar Elkady at selkady@unav.es. About The University The University of Navarra is an international University committed to quality teaching and excellence in research. It occupies the 3rd position in the Europe Teaching Ranking 2019 by Times Higher Education and Elsevier. The University was founded on the basis of Catholic principles by St. Josemaría Escrivá and is a corporate work of Opus Dei. It supports the professional development of its faculty and staff, promotes cultural engagement and social outreach through collaboration with NGOs and charitable organizations, and encourages service-learning initiatives. Employment opportunities are offered fairly, with all qualified candidates considered equally. The School of Engineering (TECNUN) is home to approximately 1,200 students and is located in Donostia-San Sebastián, a vibrant and picturesque city on Spain’s northern Basque coast. As an academic institution, TECNUN conducts fundamental research across a broad range of engineering disciplines while also fostering strong links between academic research and real-world applications. In this context, TECNUN collaborates closely with CEIT, a non-profit applied research Centre founded by the University of Navarra in 1982. This partnership facilitates the transfer of scientific knowledge into innovative technological solutions and strengthens the connection between fundamental research, applied research, and industrial needs. For further information about the School of Engineering, the University of Navarra, and the city of Donostia-San Sebastián, please visit the following websites: University of Navarra (UNAV), TECNUN – School of Engineering, and Donostia-San Sebastián.

items.title: R&D Engineer (PhD Student)
items.desc: At ABB , we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world. This position reports to: Technology Manager __ Your Role And Responsibilities We are now looking for an R&D Engineer to join our team at High Power Motors & Generators division in Helsinki, Finland. In this role, you will work as a PhD student for a predefined project and as a part of our Research & Development (R&D) team. As a PhD student, you will pursue your doctoral thesis at Aalto University’s Department of Electrical Engineering and Automation, the Research Group of Electromechanics. This is an excellent opportunity for a freshly graduated M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering to complete their PhD funded by industry. In this R&D Engineer role, you will have the opportunity to contribute to ABB’s success with technology, software, product, and system development. Each day, you will identify and implement innovative solutions to relevant problems. This is a fixed-term role until spring 2030. The role requires physical presence in Helsinki, Finland. The position is within a project focused on integrating recyclability into the design of permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) rotors through multi-material topology optimization. The research addresses the reduction of heavy rare-earth elements in NdFeB magnets, and the development of magnet encapsulation methods for safe disassembly and reuse. The project also includes prototyping, experimental validation, and a comprehensive life-cycle assessment (LCA) and life-cycle cost analysis (LCC). You will be mainly accountable for: Working as an independent and reliable contributor in your PhD project with supervision Performing various tasks in the assigned project (e.g., electrical machines, software), from building concepts, gathering requirements to designing, implementing, integrating, testing Publishing research results in high-impact journals and completing doctoral coursework as required by Aalto University Our team dynamics You will join our Design and Method Development team, where you will be able to advance your project with the support of your supervisor and the whole team. Qualifications For The Role In order to be selected, you must be qualified for doctoral studies at Aalto University (more information available at Aalto’s website: Aalto Doctoral Programme in Electrical Engineering) Completion of your Master of Science of Electrical Engineer with grades qualifying for doctoral studies You have a solid background in electromagnetic design and analysis of rotating machines, especially PMSMs You are familiar with numerical methods for finite element simulations You are interested in programming and have good knowledge of a relevant programming language (Python, MATLAB, or equivalent) You are highly motivated to pursue doctoral research in electrical machines at ABB and at Aalto University You are at ease communicating in English at an advanced academic level Familiarity with topology optimization or structural optimization methods is an advantage You hold current VISA/work permit to work in Finland/EU What's in it for you? A funded fixed term doctoral position with ABB employment, while receiving support and contacts from both the industry and university. Benefits Our culture and benefits reflect our values: courage, care, curiosity and collaboration. The most appreciated benefits according to our personnel are at the moment, e.g. an annual performance bonus, employee share acquisition program, continuous learning opportunities, and other wellbeing and family benefits. More About Us The Large Motors and Generators Division offers a comprehensive product portfolio of large AC motors and generators. The Division’s induction, synchronous and special design motors and synchronous generators power critical applications across industry, infrastructure and marine transportation. Combining the best available materials with superior technology, the large motors and generators are designed to operate efficiently and reliably, even for challenging processes or applications and to have low life cycle costs. If you have questions, please contact Technology Manager Jan Westerlund, tel. +358 50 3323795. Apply for the position by October 18th, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application. Building a cleaner, smarter future takes all kinds of minds: the curious, the courageous, and the creative. That's why we welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences. Ready to make an impact? Apply today or visit https://www.abb.com to learn more about the impact of our solutions across the globe.

items.title: PhD: 3D-Aware Multi-Object Tracking
items.desc: At IDEMIA, we aim to offer our employees, a dynamic and exciting environment where you have opportunities for career growth and professional development. Internal mobility is a great way for you to energize your career and to build your personal brand. It’s also a great way to explore other functions, professions or countries as IDEMIA operates in different businesses and in 50+ locations around the world. Purpose IDEMIA and Télécom Paris are opening a CIFRE PhD position to address a key challenge in modern multi-object tracking (MOT): how can we design more robust tracking systems in the presence of severe and prolonged occlusions? While current tracking methods have achieved impressive performance, occlusion remains one of the main sources of identity switches, missed detections, and fragmented trajectories, particularly in crowded and unconstrained environments. We are seeking to develop an improved tracking system by exploring the hypothesis that 3D-aware and amodal representations can provide the missing information required to maintain object identity through occlusion. The PhD will investigate how reasoning about the full, potentially occluded extent of an object (amodal tracking) and/or its position and structure in 3D space (3D-aware tracking) can be integrated into a tracking architecture. Particular attention will be given to challenging real-world scenarios involving dense crowds, frequent occlusions, and complex interactions. While the initial focus will be on single-camera tracking, the development of multi-camera tracking systems is of interest, with the objective of exploiting complementary viewpoints and cross-camera geometric consistency to improve identity preservation. The resulting technologies could support IDEMIA's broader biometric and video-security applications, including public-space surveillance, critical infrastructure protection, smart cities, border control, and access management. Key Missions Investigates and develops robust, efficient, and real-time multi-object tracking (MOT) algorithms, with a focus on end-to-end MOT architectures such as MOTIP2 and pedestrian tracking in challenging occlusion scenarios. Explores amodal and 3D-aware representations to enhance tracking performance while addressing the computational and resource constraints of edge devices. Designs experimental methodologies and benchmarks to evaluate proposed approaches against state-of-the-art MOT methods and real-world datasets. Contributes to the design, implementation, and validation of prototypes, with an initial focus on monocular tracking and future extensions toward multi-camera tracking. Keeps up to date with advances in computer vision, multi-object tracking, amodal perception, and 3D scene understanding, identifying and transferring relevant innovations to industrial applications. Communicates research findings to the IDEMIA and Télécom Paris research and engineering communities, contributing to scientific publications and papers submitted to leading computer vision and machine learning venues. Profile & Other Information Solid foundations in deep learning, particularly transformer architectures (attention mechanisms, DETR-style query-based models). Experience with computer vision tasks: object detection, tracking, and/or 3D/geometric vision (depth estimation, neural scene representations). Proficiency in Python and PyTorch. Familiarity with vision-language / foundation models (CLIP-like contrastive models, open-vocabulary detectors) is a plus. Seize all the opportunities of our fast-paced environment. Expect the unexpected.

items.title: Wissenschaftliche:r Mitarbeiter:in / Doktorand:in für Natural Language Processing (NLP) und kausale KI (m/w/d)
items.desc: Als Deutsche Zentrale Fachbibliothek für Technik und Naturwissenschaften sichern wir mit unseren zukunftsweisenden Dienstleistungen die infrastrukturellen Voraussetzungen einer qualitativ hochwertigen Informations- und Literaturversorgung für Forschung in Wissenschaft und Industrie. Mit dem Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) arbeiten wir daran, den Austausch und die Nutzung wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse im digitalen Zeitalter zu revolutionieren. Die Technische Informationsbibliothek (TIB), Programmbereich D, Open Research Knowledge Graph, sucht für die Forschungsgruppe Data Science & Digital Libraries (Prof. Dr. Sören Auer) zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:n Wissenschaftliche:n Mitarbeiter:in / Doktorand:in für Natural Language Processing (NLP) und kausale KI (m/w/d) Die Stelle ist für die Dauer der Projektlaufzeit von drei Jahren befristet. Die Einstellung erfolgt vorbehaltlich der finalen Bewilligung der Mittel durch den Drittmittelgeber Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Die regelmäßige Wochenarbeitszeit beträgt 39,80 Stunden (Vollzeit). Der Arbeitsplatz ist grundsätzlich für Teilzeitbeschäftigung geeignet. Mobiles Arbeiten ist unter Berücksichtigung dienstlicher Erfordernisse in begrenztem Umfang möglich. Die Eingruppierung erfolgt in die Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. Ihre Aufgaben Die Stelle ist Teil des Projekts EcoAIRE - AI-assisted hypothesis assessment in invasion biology and the restoration of freshwater ecosystems under fragmented and heterogeneous ecological evidence im Förderprogramm Leibniz-Kooperative Exzellenz. Das Projekt verbindet die Expertise der TIB in der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache und der wissenschaftlichen Wissensrepräsentation mit der ökologischen Expertise des Leibniz-Instituts für Gewässerökologie und Binnenfischerei (IGB) sowie der Expertise des Deutschen Forschungszentrums für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) in der kausalen Modellierung. An der TIB liegt Ihr Forschungsschwerpunkt auf der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache zur Extraktion wissenschaftlicher und kausaler Informationen. Sie entwickeln Methoden, die wissenschaftliche Evidenz in strukturierte, maschinenverarbeitbare Repräsentationen von Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Unsicherheiten und kausalen Zusammenhängen überführen. Dabei geht Ihre Forschung über die Extraktion einzelner Fakten hinaus: Sie modellieren, wie wissenschaftliche Befunde zusammenhängen und unter welchen Bedingungen wissenschaftliche Aussagen gelten. Darauf aufbauend erforschen Sie kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern. Dazu gehören Simulationen, interventionsbasierte Schlussfolgerungsverfahren und die Bewertung von Hypothesen unter veränderten Bedingungen. Ihre Tätigkeit umfasst Sie entwickeln ein multimodales Rahmenwerk, das heterogene wissenschaftliche Wissensquellen - darunter Publikationen, Bilder, ergänzende Informationen, Datensätze und weitere Forschungsartefakte - in strukturierte Repräsentationen zur Hypothesenbewertung integriert und dabei die Herkunft der Informationen nachvollziehbar berücksichtigt. Sie entwickeln sprachmodellbasierte und agentenbasierte Methoden, um Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Evidenz, Unsicherheiten sowie kausale oder mechanistische Zusammenhänge quellenübergreifend zu extrahieren, zu vereinheitlichen, aufeinander abzustimmen und zusammenzuführen. Sie erforschen kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern, um Interventionen zu simulieren und zu untersuchen, inwieweit sich Hypothesen auf veränderte Bedingungen übertragen lassen. Sie entwickeln Evaluationsrahmenwerke, die unterschiedliche Qualitätsaspekte der KI-gestützten Hypothesenbewertung erfassen. Dazu gehören Verfahren auf Grundlage fachlicher Expertenbewertungen sowie Ansätze, bei denen große Sprachmodelle als Bewertungsinstanz eingesetzt werden („LLM-as-a-judge“). Sie veröffentlichen Ihre Forschungsergebnisse auf Konferenzen und in Fachzeitschriften mit Peer-Review-Verfahren in den Bereichen NLP, Semantic Web, künstliche Intelligenz und maschinelles Lernen. Zudem wirken Sie an Projektberichten und der Verbreitung der Forschungsergebnisse mit. Ihr Profil Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master oder gleichwertiger Abschluss) in Informatik oder einem eng verwandten Fachgebiet, beispielsweise Künstliche Intelligenz (Artificial Intelligence), maschinelle Sprachverarbeitung (Natural Language Processing), maschinelles Lernen (Machine Learning), Data Science oder Computerlinguistik. Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Forschung oder Softwareentwicklung mit Python sowie praktische Kenntnisse moderner Methoden der Softwareentwicklung, beispielsweise Git-basierter Zusammenarbeit, automatisierter Tests und reproduzierbarer Experimente. Nachweisbare praktische Erfahrung mit transformerbasierten Modellen und großen Sprachmodellen, einschließlich der Nutzung von Frameworks wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers oder vergleichbaren Technologien für NLP-Anwendungen. Die Einstellung erfolgt vorbehaltlich der finalen Bewilligung der Mittel durch den Drittmittelgeber Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Die regelmäßige Wochenarbeitszeit beträgt 39,80 Stunden (Vollzeit). Ihre Aufgaben Die Stelle ist Teil des Projekts EcoAIRE - AI-assisted hypothesis assessment in invasion biology and the restoration of freshwater ecosystems under fragmented and heterogeneous ecological evidence im Förderprogramm Leibniz-Kooperative Exzellenz. Das Projekt verbindet die Expertise der TIB in der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache und der wissenschaftlichen Wissensrepräsentation mit der ökologischen Expertise des Leibniz-Instituts für Gewässerökologie und Binnenfischerei (IGB) sowie der Expertise des Deutschen Forschungszentrums für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) in der kausalen Modellierung. An der TIB liegt Ihr Forschungsschwerpunkt auf der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache zur Extraktion wissenschaftlicher und kausaler Informationen. Sie entwickeln Methoden, die wissenschaftliche Evidenz in strukturierte, maschinenverarbeitbare Repräsentationen von Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Unsicherheiten und kausalen Zusammenhängen überführen. Dabei geht Ihre Forschung über die Extraktion einzelner Fakten hinaus: Sie modellieren, wie wissenschaftliche Befunde zusammenhängen und unter welchen Bedingungen wissenschaftliche Aussagen gelten. Dazu gehören Simulationen, interventionsbasierte Schlussfolgerungsverfahren und die Bewertung von Hypothesen unter veränderten Bedingungen. items.title: PhD Autonomous & Decentralized Air Traffic Management
items.desc: Functieomschrijving Background Air Traffic Management (ATM) and Communications, Navigation, and Surveillance (CNS) systems form the operational foundation of civil aviation. Current operations depend heavily on centralized ground facilities and satellite services for surveillance and management. This system is vulnerable for a range of disruptions including infrastructure failures, GNSS outages or cyber incidents. These vulnerabilities can degrade or even halt civil aviation. Project ORION (Onboard Resilient Infrastructure-free Operational Network) investigates an alternative ATM/CNS architecture designed to function without reliance on ground- or space-based infrastructure. By utilizing an aeronautical ad-hoc network for communication, relative positioning, and surveillance, ORION aims to enable aircraft to self-organize and maintain safe separation thus ensuring a minimum service level even during (large scale) disruptions. Project Description This PhD project is fundamentally multidisciplinary. As a PhD candidate, you will design, model, and evaluate a decentralized ATM/CNS architecture. The research focuses on determining how core traffic management functions can be sustained through cooperation using an aeronautical network when centralized ground and satellite services are unavailable. In the first phase of the research, you will determine a set of use cases and design the underlying aeronautical ad-hoc networking concept layer to enable direct airborne data exchange, cooperative relative localization, and cooperative surveillance. Next, building on this network layer, you will formulate distributed algorithms for fundamental traffic management functions, including aircraft-as-a-sensor (mesh network), separation assurance, conflict detection and resolution, and traffic sequencing. Finally, to evaluate the operational feasibility of the architecture, you will implement the models within an ATM simulation platform, such as the open-source simulator BlueSky. For this you will extend the platform to include the ad-hoc networking functionality. Using this environment, you will stress-test the system under severe disruption scenarios by comparing the overall performance directly against conventional centralized ATM/CNS operations. This will provide evidence of the performance of the models for the various use-cases. Your profile Master’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, or a related field; Strong analytical and mathematical foundation, with experience in or a keen aptitude for complex systems modelling and distributed systems; Multidisciplinary mindset with the ability to bridge distinct domains: connecting operational ATM concepts with distributed network protocols and algorithm design; Strong background in programming, using Python or other relevant programming languages; Good scientific reporting and communication skills in written and spoken English. What we offer you You will receive a 4-year research contract from NLR and will join the Air Traffic department. In addition, you will be enrolled in the Doctoral Education programme of the Graduate School at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft). During this period, you will work closely with NLR colleagues in Amsterdam and with academic supervisors from TU Delft. Your working week will ideally be divided into: 2 days in Amsterdam, 2 days in Delft, and 1 day from home. In Addition, We Offer No fewer than 45 days off (with full-time employment); A fixed end-of-year bonus of 8%; A contribution towards your healthcare costs; Extra paid parental leave; The possibility to work from home where possible. Would you like to know more? Please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/en/ae/research/ae-graduate-school for more information on the graduate school. For more information about the recruitment procedure, contact Pien Moller (recruiter) via pien.moller@nlr.nl . Would you like to apply? Great, we are curious about you! Send your motivation letter and CV via the apply button ! A pre-employment security screening (VGB-C) is a requirement. For more information about the screening, please visit the AIVD website. Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated.
