items.title: PhD Position - Translational Neuroscience
items.desc: We are looking for a PhD candidate to join the Multimodal Imaging in Clinical Neuroscience department at the Institute of Neuroscience and Medicine – Medical Imaging Physics (INM-4). You will work in the field of translational neuroscience and precision psychiatry under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar. The brain mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders are poorly understood, and treatment choices are largely symptom-based. In this project, you will use multimodal neuroimaging and computational neuroscience to study how brain networks change in these disorders. The aim is to identify imaging biomarkers that could support earlier diagnosis, predict disease trajectories at an individual level and help match treatment to the patient. A key resource is our MINDset platform (Multimodal Imaging Infrastructure for Neuroscience Data Science), which consolidates over 1,000 multimodal datasets from clinical studies, including structural and functional MRI, PET, EEG, fNIRS, neuropsychological and clinical measures, and digital phenotyping. Your Job The successful candidate will have the opportunity to combine prospectively acquired data with existing multimodal datasets and contribute to replication studies, biomarker development, machine learning applications, and analyses of individual disease trajectories. Your tasks will include: Integrate multimodal neuroimaging datasets from MRI, PET, EEG, and fNIRS studies Characterize brain networks using graph-theoretical methods and structural and functional connectivity analyses Apply multivariate statistical modelling and machine learning to multimodal datasets Investigate individualized imaging biomarkers relevant to diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring Coordinate longitudinal studies involving psychiatric patients and healthy controls, including recruitment, scheduling, and neuropsychological and psychopathological assessments Coordinate and supervise MRI data acquisition; maintain standardized acquisition protocols and data quality Manage and curate imaging data in accordance with established standards (e.g., BIDS) Your Profile Excellent university degree (Master) in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, medical physics, psychology, cognitive science, computer science, physics, data science, or a related discipline A strong interest in translational psychiatry, neuroimaging and computational neuroscience, and a motivation to work in an interdisciplinary research environment Programming experience in MATLAB and/or Python, alongside strong analytical and problem-solving skills Experience with structural and/or functional MRI; familiarity with packages such as SPM, FSL, FreeSurfer, AFNI, MRtrix, CONN, or similar tools is desirable Knowledge of neuroimaging preprocessing, quality control, graph theory, connectomics, multivariate statistics, or machine learning is an advantage Very good command of written and spoken English with extensive vocabulary is required (at least B2 level according to the CEFR ), ideally supported by a certificate confirming the language level German language skills at B1 level are desirable Our Benefits for You Team & Environment: You will work in a motivated and interdisciplinary team including psychiatrists, neuroscientists, physicists, engineers, and data scientists Research & Infrastructure: You will have access to advanced neuroimaging infrastructure and training in structural and functional MRI, multimodal imaging, connectomics, and computational neuroscience Networking & Exchange: You will participate in (international) conferences and project meetings, actively building your scientific network through collaborations involving Forschungszentrum Jülich, RWTH Aachen University, Ulm University, Bezirkskrankenhaus Günzburg and LVR-Klinik Cologne Supervision & Support: We will accompany your doctoral studies with continuous, expert guidance from your academic supervisors Prof. Dr. Irene Neuner and Dr. Ravichandran Rajkumar Work-life balance: Optimal conditions for balancing work and private life, as well as a family-friendly company policy. The option of flexible working (in terms of location) is generally available after consultation and in line with upcoming tasks and (on-site) appointments Annual Leave: You get 30 days of annual leave Fixed-term: The position is limited to 3 years Fair remuneration: Depending on your existing qualifications and the tasks assigned to you, you will be classified in pay grade 13 (65 %) of the TVöD-Bund (Collective Agreement for the Public Service). In addition to the basic salary, there is an additional year-end bonus under the collective pay agreement amounting to 75% of a monthly salary, as well as capital-forming benefits. items.desc: Das Institut für Medizinische Informatik und Biometrie (IMB) ist Teil der Medizinischen Fakultät Carl Gustav Carus der Technischen Universität Dresden. Die Forschungsschwerpunkte des Instituts liegen in den Bereichen medizinische Biometrie, Bioinformatik, Systembiologie/-medizin inklusive der mathematischen Modellierung sowie in der medizinischen Informatik. Neben diesen wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeitsfeldern bietet das IMB verschiedene Dienstleistungen (z. B. Beratungs- und Weiterbildungsangebote im Bereich der medizinischen Datenwissenschaften) für Mitarbeitende und Studierende der Medizinischen Fakultät und des Universitätsklinikums Dresden an. Die Stelle ist Teil des von der Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) geförderten interdisziplinären Forschungsprojekts „Virtuelle Nische: Computer-gestützte Modellierung und Simulation der zeitlichen-räumlich Dynamik hämatopoetischer Stammzellen in ihrer lokalen Mikroumgebung“. Kernziel des Projektes ist die Entwicklung und Anwendung eines mathematischen Modells, das die zeitlich‑räumliche Organisation hämatopoetischer Stamm‑ und Vorläuferzellen in ihrer lokalen Wachstumsumgebung im Knochenmark beschreibt. Das angestrebte verbesserte Verständnis der zugrundeliegenden Prozesse ist sowohl für offene grundlagenwissenschaftliche Fragestellungen der Stammzellbiologie als auch für zukünftige medizinische Anwendungen von zentraler Bedeutung. items.title: Doctoral Researcher (Ice Crystal Surface Roughness and Atmospheric Optics) / Väitöskirjatutkija (Ilmakehän jääkiteiden pinnankarheuden ja optiikan tutkimus)
items.desc: Tampere University and Tampere University of Applied Sciences create a unique environment for multidisciplinary, inspirational and high-impact research and education. Our university community has its competitive edges in technology, health and society . www.tuni.fi/en The Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics group, part of the Aerosol Physics Laboratory at Tampere University, is recruiting a Doctoral Researcher to join CRYSTAL, a European Research Council (ERC)-funded project that pioneers the use of advanced 3D nano-printing in atmospheric science. CRYSTAL addresses a major unresolved question: how nano- and microscale surface roughness changes the way atmospheric ice crystals scatter sunlight and how cirrus clouds are represented in climate and satellite-observation models. Job Description As a doctoral researcher, you will investigate the optical response of realistic ice crystal surface roughness using nano-printed test surfaces. Your main responsibility will be to plan and participate in the optical characterization of these surfaces and to analyse polarization-resolved measurements of their bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF). The work combines optics, precision measurement, surface characterization, programming and quantitative data analysis. You will contribute to selecting and preparing representative ice crystal surface morphologies for nano-printing and to assessing the quality of the fabricated samples. You will develop robust data-processing and quality-control routines and determine how the measured scattering depends on roughness scale, surface anisotropy, illumination and observation geometry, and polarization. In collaboration with the project's postdoctoral researcher, you will test physically based surface-scattering descriptions, including Harvey-Shack theory and ABg-type parameterizations, against the laboratory measurements. The resulting parameterized optical description will support modelling of atmospheric ice crystals and, ultimately, improved interpretation of cirrus-cloud observations from next-generation satellites. Requirements Applicants must hold an internationally recognized Master's degree in experimental physics, optics, photonics, atmospheric science or another relevant field by the starting date. You should be motivated by experimental research and interested in working across the boundaries of atmospheric science, optical measurement and surface technology. The most important qualifications are hands-on experience with optical or other precision laboratory measurements and strong programming and data-analysis skills in Python, MATLAB or comparable tools. Previous experience with light-scattering or BRDF measurements, gonioreflectometry, surface metrology, microscopy, nano-fabrication, ice-particle optics or cloud microphysics is an advantage but not required. Excellent English and constructive teamwork are essential; Finnish is not required. We offer You will receive structured doctoral training and close scientific supervision while developing expertise in experimental atmospheric optics, surface scattering and advanced measurement methods. You will work closely with the project's postdoctoral researcher, experienced researchers in the group and international collaborators. As your project progresses, you will take increasing responsibility for experiments, data analysis, scientific publications and presentations at international conferences. We offer a fixed-term Doctoral Researcher position for 3.5 years. The preferred starting date is 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible by mutual agreement. A trial period of six months applies to all our new employees. The salary will be based on both the job requirements and the employee's personal performance in accordance with the Finnish University Salary System. A typical starting salary for a Doctoral Researcher is around EUR 3,000 per month. The Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics group has a long record of developing optical instruments and measurement methods for aerosol and cloud research, supported by an extensive international collaboration network. Within Tampere University's Aerosol Physics Laboratory, the ERC-funded CRYSTAL project offers a distinctive interdisciplinary environment connecting atmospheric science, experimental optics, nano-fabrication and computational light scattering. As a member of staff at Tampere University, you will enjoy a range of competitive benefits, such as occupational health care services, flexible work schedule, versatile research infrastructure, modern teaching facilities and a safe and inviting campus area as well as a personal fund to spend on sports and cultural activities in your free time. Please read more about working at Tampere University and information about Tampere University as an employer. You can also find more information about us and working and living Tampere by watching our video: Tampere Higher Education Community - our academic playground. Finland is among the most stable, free and safe countries in the world, based on prominent ratings by various agencies. Tampere is the largest inland city of Finland, and the city is counted among the major academic hubs in the Nordic countries. Tampere region is the most rapidly growing urban area in Finland and home to a vibrant knowledge-intensive entrepreneurial community. The city is an industrial powerhouse that enjoys a rich cultural scene and a reputation as a centre of Finland’s information society. Tampere is also surrounded by vivid nature with forests and lakes, providing countless opportunities for easy-to-access outdoor adventures and refreshment throughout the year. Read More About Finland And Tampere City Visit Finland This is Finland Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment: Welcome to Finland Visit Tampere How To Apply Please submit your application through our online recruitment system. The closing date for applications is 18th of Oktober (23:59 EET / UTC +2). Please write your application and all accompanying documents in English and attach them in PDF format. Applications Should Include The Following Documents Curriculum Vitae according to TENK guidelines List of publications according to Academy of Finland guidelines Contact information for two referees Motivation letter describing your relevant experience, research interests and motivation for doctoral research on ice crystal surface roughness, optical measurements and atmospheric light scattering For More Information, Please Contact Emma Järvinen, emma.jarvinen@tuni.fi Tampereen yliopisto ja Tampereen ammattikorkeakoulu muodostavat yhdessä Suomen toiseksi suurimman monitieteisen, innostavan ja vaikuttavan tutkimus- ja oppimisyhteisön. Korkeakouluyhteisömme osaamiskärjet ovat tekniikka, terveys ja yhteiskunta. Lue lisää: www.tuni.fi Tehtävänkuvaus Tampereen yliopiston Aerosol and Cloud Particle Optics -tutkimusryhmä etsii väitöskirjatutkijaa Euroopan tutkimusneuvoston (ERC) rahoittamaan CRYSTAL-hankkeeseen. Innovatiivisessa hankkeessa tuodaan edistynyt 3D-nanotulostus ilmakehätieteeseen ja tutkitaan, miten jääkiteiden nano- ja mikromittakaavan pinnankarheus vaikuttaa niiden optisiin ominaisuuksiin. Väitöskirjatutkijan päätehtävänä on tutkia realistisia jääkiteiden pintarakenteita jäljittelevien nanotulostettujen testipintojen optista vastetta. Työhön kuuluu polarisaatioherkkien BRDF-mittausten suunnittelu ja toteutukseen osallistuminen, mittausaineistojen laadunvarmistus ja analyysi sekä fysikaalisten pintasirontamallien testaaminen yhdessä hankkeen tutkijoiden kanssa. Tehtävä täytetään 3,5 vuodeksi. Toivottu aloitusajankohta on 1.1.2027 tai mahdollisimman pian sopimuksen mukaan. Edellytykset Hakijalla tulee olla soveltuva ylempi korkeakoulututkinto ja sujuva englannin kielen taito. Arvostamme erityisesti käytännön kokemusta optisista tai muista tarkkuusmittauksista sekä hyviä ohjelmointi- ja data-analyysitaitoja. Kokemus valonsirontamittauksista, BRDF-mittauksista, pintamittauksista, mikroskopiasta, nanovalmistuksesta tai ilmakehän jäähiukkasista katsotaan eduksi. Hakijan tulee pystyä työskentelemään yhteistyössä kansainvälisessä ja monitieteisessä tutkimusympäristössä. Hakuohjeet Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävästä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta. Jätäthän hakemuksesi yliopiston sähköisellä hakulomakkeella (linkki löytyy tämän ilmoituksen alta). Hakuaika tehtävään päättyy 18.10.2026.

items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology at the University of Oulu (Finland)
items.desc: Login and apply Faculty of Education and Psychology The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are currently looking for a Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland. The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) . The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities. The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education. About The Job As a doctoral researcher, you will: Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning. Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities. Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers. Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities. Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners. Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results. In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence. Qualifications To succeed in the position, we expect from you: A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline. A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values. Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research. Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research. Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments. Additional Merits Considered An Advantage Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education. Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers. Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design. Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning. Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments. Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage). What we offer? The support of an experienced and enthusiastic project team of where you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. items.title: Ph.D. Cadidate (m/f/d)
items.desc: The Institute for Medical Informatics and Biometry (IMB) is part of the Carl Gustav Carus Faculty of Medicine at TU Dresden. The institute's research focuses on medical biometrics, bioinformatics, systems biology/medicine, including mathematical modelling, as well as medical informatics. In addition to these scientific activities, the IMB offers various services (e.g., consulting and education programs in the field of medical data science) for faculty and students at the Faculty of Medicine and the University Hospital. The position is part of the interdisciplinary research project “ Virtual niche : Computational modelling and simulation of spatio-temporal dynamics of hematopoietic stem cells in their local microenvironment” funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). The core objective of the project is the development and application of a mathematical model that describes the spatio-temporal organization of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in their local growth environment within the bone marrow. The goal of gaining a better understanding of the underlying processes is of central importance both for open questions in basic stem cell biology and for future medical applications. items.desc: About The Position Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? Do you have a background in electrical power engineering, operations research, or a related field, and are you interested in energy systems and markets? As a PhD candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, both in and outside academia. The Department of Electric Energy (IEL) at NTNU is seeking a highly motivated candidate for a full-time (100%) PhD position for 3 years as part of the Norwegian Centre on AI for Decisions. You will join the research group Electricity Markets and Energy System Planning (EMESP) at IEL, where we foster an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment. Our work environment is defined by its friendly and supportive atmosphere, with regular gatherings such as professional meetings within the research group, weekly colloquia, shared lunches, and “Friday coffee” sessions to end the week. These formal and informal events offer opportunities to share ideas, celebrate milestones, and build relationships. PhD candidates also organize social activities open to everyone interested, fostering a welcoming and inclusive community. Your immediate Line Manager will be the Head of Department. About The Project The position will be part of AID, the Norwegian Centre on AI for Decisions, an interdisciplinary national AI centre led by NTNU and SINTEF. AID brings together academic institutions, research organizations, and more than 50 professional organizations. Its primary objective is to advance AI for decision-making through fundamental research and real-world use cases, ensuring that AI-enhanced human decisions and autonomous systems are effective, safe, and trustworthy in sectors critical to society. This PhD project will contribute to AID by developing trustworthy AI-supported methods for long-term hydropower scheduling. Hydropower plays a central role in the Nordic power system, and deciding when to use or store water is becoming increasingly important as the energy system faces more uncertainty from weather, renewable generation, market developments, and future electricity demand. These decisions depend on uncertain inflows, future electricity prices, reservoir levels, cascade constraints, and the nonlinear relationship between water release and electricity production. Improving such decisions is essential for efficient renewable energy use, energy security, and the reliable operation of hydro-dominated power systems. The project will focus on how AI can support advanced optimization models for hydropower and energy-system planning. In particular, the research will investigate how the future value of stored water can be represented more accurately when hydropower production is nonlinear and when short-term operational conditions influence long-term reservoir decisions. In line with AID’s research areas, the project will emphasize trust, knowledge embedding, generalization under uncertainty, and human-interpretable decision support. The PhD candidate will develop and validate a hybrid methodology that combines established stochastic optimization with AI-based learning. The aim is not only to develop new algorithms, but also to understand how AI can be used safely and reliably in decision-support tools for the energy sector. The enhanced framework will be tested on Nordic hydropower use cases, including long-term and medium-term hydropower scheduling, multi-reservoir cascade operation, hydropower participation in energy and reserve markets, and planning under high renewable variability. In this way, the project responds to the growing need for safe and trustworthy AI tools in demanding, decision-critical systems. The PhD candidate will be hosted in the Electricity Markets and Energy Systems Planning (EMESP) group at the Department of Electric Energy, NTNU. The main supervisor will be Professor Hossein Farahmand, with co-supervision from experts in stochastic hydropower optimization and AI for decision-making, including Professor Arild Helseth, Associate Professor Jayaprakash Rajasekharan, Professor Sebastien Gros, and Research Manager Signe Riemer-Sørensen, depending on the final methodological focus of the PhD project. Duties of the position Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above Participate in activities of the EMESP research group Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum 30 ECTS Contribute to publications in relevant journals and to popular science dissemination Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions Career-enhancing work, which is in addition to the research project and doctoral education, may be offered to a candidate who demonstrates clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department determines there is a need. Examples of career-enhancing work include, but are not limited to, contributing to teaching, laboratory and exercise teaching, supervision, and examination work within the employee's areas of competence. Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must have a relevant Master's degree in either electrical power engineering, computer science, control engineering, chemistry, managerial economics with strong quantitative skills, or physics or mathematics with a specialization in operations research. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master's students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than autumn 2026. You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education, i.e., by having relevant work experience and/or published/publishable scientific papers. You must meet the requirements for admission to the Faculty's Doctoral Programme. Experience with optimization modelling and numerical optimization tools, such as JuMP, Pyomo, Gurobi, CPLEX, HiGHS, or similar frameworks and solvers, will be considered an important qualification. You must have English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale B2 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Applicants who are not native English speakers are encouraged to document their English language proficiency. This can be done through an approved English language test. One of the following test scores could be documented for this purpose: TOEFL internet-based test (iBT) - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 79 - 101. IELTS - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 5.5 - 6.0 Cambridge English - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 160 - 179. Further assessment of both written and oral English language skills, as well as the ability to communicate fluently, will be conducted throughout the selection process and during any interviews for all applicants. PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Work and/or research experience in electricity markets, hydropower scheduling, energy system modeling, and operations research or optimization. Very good programming and modeling skills, preferably in Julia, Python, or a similar programming language. Knowledge and/or experience with Machine Learning, Reinforcement Learning, AI-based time-series forecasting English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale C1 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). See which scores are equivalent to the C1 level here. Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), the candidate is expected to: demonstrate strong motivation, curiosity, and a learning-oriented mindset work independently, take initiative, and maintain good structure and discipline in their work communicate effectively and collaborate well with supervisors and peers show resilience and work constructively when facing challenges or setbacks demonstrate integrity and a strong sense of responsibility in their research conduct Emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. items.title: PhD in Quantum Computing for Power Systems
items.desc: At AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from December 1, 2026, or as soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years. Your work tasks This PhD position focuses on the application of quantum computing to computational challenges in power systems with high shares of renewable energy. You will investigate quantum and hybrid quantum–classical methods for power system analysis and optimization, with emphasis on their practical performance and suitability for real-time applications. Your work will include formulating representative power system analysis and optimization problems, developing and implementing quantum and hybrid quantum–classical solution methods, and comparing their performance with relevant classical approaches. You will also evaluate the developed methods through numerical studies and real-time power system simulation. The research will involve scientific programming, analysis and documentation of results, and dissemination through peer-reviewed publications and international conferences. The position is offered within the Center for Research on Microgrids, and the PhD student will be affiliated with the Electric Power Systems and Microgrids section at AAU Energy. Your competencies The applicant must have a relevant educational background in electrical engineering, energy engineering, computer science, or a closely related field. You should have a solid foundation in mathematical modelling and numerical methods, together with experience in scientific programming, preferably in Python. Knowledge of power system analysis and optimization (e.g., power flow and optimal power flow), as well as experience with quantum computing methods and algorithms (e.g., HHL or variational quantum linear solvers for linear system problems, and QAOA or quantum annealing for optimization problems), is expected. Experience with real-time power system simulation using platforms such as RTDS or OPAL-RT would be an advantage. Previous peer-reviewed journal publications at the intersection of quantum computing and power and energy systems would also be considered an advantage. You should be motivated to further develop your expertise across both power systems and quantum computing. You should be able to organize and conduct research independently, document and communicate your methods and results clearly, and discuss technical challenges constructively with colleagues. The position requires both independent research and collaboration with researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds, as well as good written and spoken English. Qualification requirements PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. Who we are AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real world energy challenges. Aalborg University has been ranked as the best university in Europe within energy research and is among the very best universities worldwide in this field. At AAU Energy you will be part of a top international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges such as the green transition and future energy systems. The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and with diverse national and disciplinary backgrounds, which creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as working language in both research and teaching, which supports the integration of international colleagues. We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes). You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk. How to apply Your application must include the following: Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position Curriculum Vitae (CV) Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) Other relevant documents The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost. Further information Read more about our recruitment process here. The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts. Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not. The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science Salary and terms of employment The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”. There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position. Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

items.title: BHF 4-Year PhD Studentships in Cardiovascular Research (Prevention)
items.desc: University of Cambridge, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College London and University of Oxford. Applications are invited for 10 funded 4-year PhD studentships starting in October 2027, as part of the British Heart Foundation (BHF) doctoral training programme focused on preventing cardiovascular disease through innovative, data-driven approaches. This interdisciplinary PhD programme brings together leading researchers from the University of Cambridge, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College London, and the University of Oxford. Students will be trained to work at the intersection of population health, systems biology, and data science/AI, combining expertise across these fields to tackle one of the most pressing challenges in global health. By harnessing large-scale multimodal data and emerging technologies, students will develop new approaches to understand, predict, and prevent heart and circulatory diseases. Students will be based in one of the following institutes: Cambridge (5 studentships), Edinburgh (2 studentships), Imperial (1 Studentship) or Oxford (2 studentships) while benefiting from training, co-supervision, and collaboration across the partner institutions. Projects will span a range of topics including health data science, AI and machine learning, multi-omics, epidemiology, and translational cardiovascular research. Students will be part of a cohort-based programme, gaining access to shared training activities, collaborative networks, and state-of-the-art data resources across the multi-institute partnership. This four-year PhD programme combines interdisciplinary training with in-depth research. In year 1, students will undertake training courses and research rotations (at their host institution) before selecting their PhD project and supervisory team. In years 2-4, students will carry out their PhD research with interdisciplinary supervision. Additional opportunities will include advanced training courses, programme-wide workshops and symposia, and optional placements with our academic or industry partners, including EMBL-European Bioinformatics Institute, Wellcome Sanger Institute, AstraZeneca, Novo Nordisk, Genomics Ltd, Owlstone Medical, ThermoFischer Scientific and Flagship Pioneering. The Co-leads Of The Programme Are Cambridge - Professor Angela Wood Edinburgh - Professor Nicholas Mills Imperial - Associate Professor Michela Noseda Oxford - Professor Sarah Lewington Eligibility Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a first or upper second-class undergraduate degree (or equivalent) in a relevant discipline such as statistics, mathematics, computer science, data science, engineering, bioinformatics, epidemiology, biomedical sciences, genetics, public health, or another quantitative or biomedical field, and may also hold a Master's degree in a related subject. Applicants should also demonstrate strong analytical skills, experience working with data or computational methods, and an interest in interdisciplinary research. Strong communication and teamwork skills are essential, and international applicants may need to provide evidence of English language proficiency. Funding The Studentship Provides University tuition fees (UK home rate only) A tax-free stipend at the BHF rate Research training and support We invite applications from students who meet the UK residency requirements (home fees). International students who confirm that additional costs of all overseas tuition fees will be covered through other scholarships or funding schemes will also be considered. How to apply Please do not use the University application portals. To apply, please email bhfphdadmin@medschl.cam.ac.uk with the following documents. Curriculum vitae (CV) Two letters of recommendation from your referees, signed Transcripts A cover letter (maximum 2500 characters) outlining your suitability for the PhD programme and indicating your preferred host institutions in order of preference. Please list only institutions that you would be willing to attend if offered a place, even if they are not your first choice. Evidence of competence in English - If required - please see our Competence in English guidance for more information. AI must not be used when writing personal statements and CVs. This prohibition covers the use of AI to help your use of English. Using AI in your application ' Postgraduate Study https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/apply/how/ai-postgraduate-applications Application deadline: 8th December 2026 Please quote reference RH51427 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

items.title: PhD in In-Operando Diagnostics of Li-ion and Post-Li-ion Batteries Using Acoustic Technology
items.desc: At AAU Energy, a PhD stipend position is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from 15 November 2026 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years. Your work tasks Battery performance assessment and diagnostics rely today on standardised electrical measurements complemented by post-mortem analysis. None of these methods is suited for in-operando diagnostics, as they are either destructive or require the battery to be taken out of its daily operation. Acoustic techniques, based either on passive listening to acoustic emissions or on active ultrasound signal injection, have recently been proposed as an alternative; however, further research is needed to establish the relationship between materials degradation and the sensed acoustic signals. The aim of this PhD project is to establish a mechanistic understanding of the coupling between battery ageing mechanisms and measured acoustic signals, and to translate this understanding into a diagnostic method applicable to both Li-ion and post-Li-ion chemistries. You will start by reviewing the state of the art in acoustic-based battery diagnostics, and you will then design and build a set-up for sensing acoustic emissions in coin cells. Using this set-up, you will carry out degradation tests over a wide range of operating conditions with simultaneous acoustic and electrical measurements, and you will analyse how the acoustic signatures relate to the electrical ones and to the underlying degradation mechanisms. On this basis, you will develop an acoustic-based, physics-validated model for battery diagnostics; the resulting algorithm is targeted to be at least 25% more accurate than conventional impedance-based estimation and at least 50% less energy demanding than traditional diagnostic approaches. While most of the experimental work will be carried out at coin-cell level, a proof of concept at single-layer pouch-cell level is expected, which will facilitate further demonstration towards innovation. The work will be supported by critical analysis of the results, benchmarking against the state of the art, and high-quality publications and conference presentations. In addition to the research activities, you will contribute to teaching and to the supervision of student projects, as well as to broader dissemination activities within the department. The position is offered in relation to the research group Batteries, and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for Power Electronics Systems Integration and Materials. Your competencies We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate who is eager to work at the intersection of battery testing, sensing instrumentation and signal processing, and who enjoys combining fundamental understanding with hands-on experimental work. The ideal candidate is curious and persistent in the laboratory, excels at troubleshooting, can plan and execute experiments independently, and motivated to collaborate closely with colleagues in an international and interdisciplinary environment. Applicants must hold an M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering, energy engineering or mechatronics. Experience with one or more of the following will be considered an advantage: electrical characterisation of batteries, acoustic or ultrasonic sensing and laboratory instrumentation, and signal processing and data-driven modelling (e.g., in MATLAB or Python). Experience with Problem Based Learning (PBL) is required, as the PhD student will be involved in the supervision of BSc and MSc student projects. Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken, are required, as the project will be carried out in an international research environment. Danish language skills are highly desirable and will support co-supervision of BSc student projects; however, they are not a formal requirement. Qualification requirements PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution. Who we are AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real world energy challenges. Aalborg University has been ranked as the best university in Europe within energy research and is among the very best universities worldwide in this field. At AAU Energy you will be part of a top international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges such as the green transition and future energy systems. The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and with diverse national and disciplinary backgrounds, which creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as working language in both research and teaching, which supports the integration of international colleagues. We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes). items.title: PhD Position in Space Law and Artificial Intelligence
items.desc: Who sets the rules when AI turns Earth Observation data into decisions about security, resilience and society? Join us as a PhD researcher and help shape the unique intersection of space law and artificial intelligence. You will conduct doctoral research within EO-TRUST, a €1 million multidisciplinary project funded by the Dutch Research Council (NWO), led by Dr Ioana Bratu. Your research will examine the legal and ethical dimensions of AI-enabled Earth Observation, focusing on how space law, AI regulation and related legal frameworks address questions of resilience, responsibility and trustworthy use of satellite data. You will work in a multidisciplinary environment connecting law with Earth Observation, artificial intelligence and computer science. Your duties conduct independent doctoral research on the legal and ethical governance of AI-enabled Earth Observation map and analyse applicable legal frameworks, including international space law, the EU Space Act, the EU AI Act and relevant security and military law conduct doctrinal and empirical research, including interviews and engagement with governmental, regulatory, academic and industry stakeholders contribute to academic publications, policy outputs, conferences, workshops and the development of principles for responsible and explainable AI-enabled Earth Observation contribute to the activities of Amsterdam Law & Technology Institute and Amsterdam Space Law & Sustainability Center. Your profile a completed LL.M. or equivalent master's degree in law, preferably with a specialisation or demonstrated interest in technology (AI) law, space law, military law, international security, international humanitarian law, EU law or public international law strong academic research and legal analytical skills, with an interest in collaborating in a multidisciplinary environment knowledge of, or a demonstrable interest in, the legal and regulatory implications of space activities and artificial intelligence experience or an interest in empirical legal research and in working with stakeholders from government, industry and technical disciplines excellent written and spoken English and the ability to communicate legal research clearly to both academic and non-academic audiences As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset. We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore, we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements. What do we offer? A challenging position in a socially engaged organisation. At VU Amsterdam, you contribute to education, research and service for a better world. And that is valuable. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of minimum € 3.204 (Scale 85 PhD.) and maximum € 4.051 (Scale 85 PhD.) gross per month, on a full-time basis. This is based on UFO profile PhD candidate. The exact salary depends on your education and experience. a position for at least 0.8 FTE. Your employment contract will initially last 1 year. Afterwards, the possibility of expansion to a total of 4 years. the possibility to engage and collaborate with industry and governmental stakeholders as part of the EO-TRUST project. For example, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on industry expertise at Caeli BV, as an intern. you will benefit from international insights offered by a renowned Advisory Board, as part of the EO-TRUST project. Members include representatives from ESA, the European Commission, EUSPA, the European Parliament, top AI policy & governmental advisors and space law advisors and academics. If you choose to work 40 hours, you have 96 extra holiday leave hours on an annual basis. items.title: Wissenschaftlerin/ Wissenschaftler (Doktorandin/ Doktorand) (m/w/d) im Institut für Nutztiergenetik
items.loc: Neustadt am Rübenberge, Lower Saxony, Germany
items.desc: Das Friedrich-Loeffler-Institut gehört zu den weltweit führenden Forschungsinstituten auf dem Gebiet der Tierseuchen, des Tierschutzes, der Tierhaltung, der Tierernährung und der Nutztiergenetik. Es gehört zum Geschäftsbereich des Bundesministeriums für Landwirtschaft, Ernährung und Heimat (BMLEH) und unterrichtet und berät die Bundesregierung auf diesen Gebieten. Das Institut für Nutztiergenetik am Standort Neustadt am Rübenberge sucht zum 1. Januar 2027 für die auf 3 Jahre befristete Projektstelle eine/ einen Wissenschaftlerin/ Wissenschaftler (Doktorandin/ Doktorand) (m/w/d) Das Projekt widmet sich der Erhaltung alter, bedrohter Hühnerrassen und unterstützt die fachliche und konzeptionelle Weiterentwicklung der Forschung am FLI in diesem Bereich. Es wird im Rahmen des Bundesprogramms Nutztierhaltung (BUNTH) durch das BMLEH gefördert. Die Bundesanstalt für Landwirtschaft und Ernährung (BLE) übernimmt die Projektträgerschaft. Die Stelleninhaberin/ der Stelleninhaber übernimmt bei der Mitwirkung an der Erhaltung und Rekonstitution alter, bedrohter Hühnerrassen im Rahmen des Forschungsprojekts „FrostyBird“ folgende Aufgabenschwerpunkte Durchführung molekularbiologischer und zellbiologischer Laborarbeiten, insbesondere DNA- und RNA-Extraktion, qualitativer und quantitativer PCR, Fluoreszenz- und Konfokalmikroskopie, Durchflusszytometrie, Immunhistochemie und Zellkultur Durchführung von Brutverfahren, Embryonenkultur und reproduktionsbiologischen Techniken beim Huhn, einschließlich der Spermagewinnung Mitwirkung bei der Betreuung der Projekttiere sowie Erhebung und Auswertung von Gesundheits- und Tierwohlindikatoren Auswertung, Aufbereitung und Präsentation der im Projekt gewonnenen Daten. Neben der Veröffentlichung der Forschungsergebnisse in begutachteten englischsprachigen Fachzeitschriften sowie Präsentation auf nationalen und internationalen wissenschaftlichen Tagungen incl. des Wissenstransfers ist die Erstellung von Zwischen- und Abschlussberichten und die Öffentlichkeitsarbeit Inhalt der Projektarbeit. Anforderungen abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (Master oder vergleichbar) Agrarwissenschaften, Veterinärmedizin, Biologie oder einer verwandten lebenswissenschaftlichen Fachrichtung Zum Interesse an der Erhaltung tiergenetischer Ressourcen sowie an reproduktionsbiologischen, molekularbiologischen und zellbiologischen Fragestellungen beim Huhn sowie die Bereitschaft zur praktischen Arbeit mit Hühnern und zur Einarbeitung in die im Projekt eingesetzten Untersuchungs- und Reproduktionstechniken wären Von Vorteil Praktische Erfahrung mit molekularbiologischen oder zellbiologischen Methoden Arbeitserfahrung mit Geflügel, insbesondere in den Bereichen Haltung, Reproduktionsbiologie oder Geflügelmedizin einschließlich der Kenntnis der tierschutzrechtlichen Rahmenbedingungen für die Haltung und wissenschaftliche Nutzung von Tieren Kenntnisse in der statistischen Datenauswertung, vorzugsweise mit R Führerschein der Klasse B Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie ein sicherer Umgang mit gängigen MS-Office-Anwendungen sind Voraussetzungen für die erfolgreiche Aufgabenerfüllung. Eine selbstständige, sorgfältige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise sowie ausgeprägtes Organisationsvermögen in Verbindung mit einer guten Kommunikationsfähigkeit und Freude an der Zusammenarbeit in einem interdisziplinären Team unterstützt die wirksame Projektarbeit. Eine vorhergehende berufliche Ausbildung im einschlägigen Assistenzbereich wäre für einen schnelleren Projekteinstieg hilfreich, jedoch nicht erforderlich. Neben einer anspruchsvollen und abwechslungsreichen wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeit in einem interdisziplinären Umfeld mit einem hochmotivierten Team bieten wir: eine 36-monatige Beschäftigung nach dem Tarifvertrag des öffentlichen Dienstes eine Vergütung mit 65% der Entgeltgruppe 13 TVöD- Bund, Tarifgebiet West eine ausgezeichnete Forschungsinfrastruktur für die Durchführung Ihres Promotionsvorhabens vielfältige Möglichkeiten zur fachlichen und überfachlichen Weiterbildung im Rahmen unserer FLI-Graduiertenschule. Unser Institut engagiert sich für ein familienfreundliches Arbeitsumfeld durch flexible Arbeitszeiten ohne Kernarbeitszeiten. Zu unseren Sozialleistungen gehören ein betriebliches Gesundheits- und Wiedereingliederungsmanagement, eine betriebliche Sozialberatung, eine betriebliche Altersvorsorge sowie vermögenswirksame Leistungen. Der Standort Neustadt am Rübenberge (Liegenschaft Mariensee) ist gut an den ÖPNV angebunden und unterstützt das Deutschlandjobticket. Wir leben ein diverses und weltoffenes Miteinander. Das Friedrich-Loeffler-Institut verpflichtet sich zur Inklusion. Menschen mit Schwerbehinderung werden bevorzugt berücksichtigt. Bei gleicher Eignung finden die durch die Behinderung bestehenden gesundheitlichen Einschränkungen keine Beachtung. Entsprechend unserer internationalen Ausrichtung begrüßen wir die Bewerbung von Menschen aller Nationalitäten und Ethnien. Nähere Auskünfte erteilt Frau Dr. Altgilbers: Tel.: 05034 871 5239, E-Mail: stefanie.altgilbers@fli.de. Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung. Bitte schicken Sie Ihre aussagekräftigen und vollständigen Unterlagen bis zum 01.11.2026 ausschließlich als ein PDF-Dokument mit dem Betreff „ Stelle 112/26 “ und unter Angabe Ihres frühestmöglichen Eintrittstermins per E-Mail an 112.26@fli.de. Alternativ können Sie Ihre Bewerbungsmappe auch mit der Post an das Friedrich-Loeffler-Institut, Referat Personal, Südufer 10, 17493 Greifswald - Insel Riems schicken. Bitte beachten Sie, dass unvollständige Unterlagen zum Ausschluss aus dem Bewerbungsverfahren führen können. Eine Eingangsbestätigung sowie die weitere Kommunikation während des Ausschreibungsverfahrens erfolgen per E-Mail. Bitte überprüfen Sie Ihre Spamfilter-Einstellungen!

items.title: PhD position in Geoscience Education Research
items.desc: Novo Nordisk Foundation Centre for University Science Education (NNF-USE). The Department of Science Education invites applications for a three-year PhD position in geoscience education research, commencing on April 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is part of the research work package “Disciplinary Writing Practices in the AI Era: Enhancing Learning in the Geosciences” at NNF-USE, led by Professor Kristine Harper. The PhD will be part of the research group on University Science Education, which hosts several other scholars working on higher education discipline-based educational research (DBER). NNF-USE, led by Professor Jenny Dauer, also partners with scholars from two other Danish universities (University of Aarhus, University of Southern Denmark) as well as those from abroad. Project Description Writing is key to disciplinary learning, development and knowledge production. The role of writing in disciplines, however, remains understudied and underutilized in university science education. Particularly in Geoscience Education Research (GER), disciplinary writing often serves merely as an assessment tool, rather than a vehicle for learning. As emerging GenAI technologies fundamentally disrupt writing practices, there is an urgent need to understand the role of writing in disciplinary learning and examine how extant and emerging GenAI technologies interact with disciplinary teaching practices, writing norms, and student learning. This work package examines the role of disciplinary writing in teaching and learning within geology. It explores how writing serves as a learning tool for both acquiring scientific knowledge and developing disciplinary ways of thinking and being in the world as a geologist – examining how students’ writing practices change and how perceptions of authorship, expertise, and disciplinary norms are evolving in the AI era. The aim is to generate knowledge about how writing can be better integrated in teaching and learning at different levels of university geology education and practice, harnessing the potentials of AI tools without undermining core educational goals. We seek a candidate for an exciting research project focused on scientific writing’s connection to learning in all levels of university geoscience education. The project aims to explore how university students and faculty members currently experience disciplinary writing in relation to their studies and teaching, respectively, how that is changing or might change as large-language models become more sophisticated over time, and what those changes mean or could mean for professional disciplinary development. The project could be designed to provide insights into how faculty members currently do or do not use writing as a teaching and learning tools in their instruction, how it might be better incorporated into teaching, and the outcomes for both teachers’ perceptions of the effectiveness of including disciplinary writing in their teaching and student outcomes. There will be considerable room to shape and adapt this PhD project to the academic background and interests of the PhD candidate. The project can include a range of methodologies, including, but not limited to, literature reviews, surveys, classroom observations, interviews with faculty and student focus groups, teaching experiments and testing of implementation strategies in the classroom. The PhD project should be relevant to university geoscience education in a Danish context. The final project design will be determined in consultation with the supervisors after the appointment. Who are we looking for? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate with a strong background in a geoscience (e.g., geology, meteorology, oceanography, physical geography) and interest in geoscience education and its roles in undergraduate and graduate instruction. In particular, we are looking for the following competencies and experience. It is required that applicants: Hold a master’s degree by 1 April 2027 (see specifications below) in an appropriate geoscience discipline (see above) or in geoscience education, with a bachelor’s degree in an appropriate geoscience discipline. Are comfortable working in research groups and are interested in collaborative work. Are very interested in pursuing geoscience education research. Have excellent written and oral English skills. It is advantageous if applicants: Have expertise in geology, since that will be the focus for the undergraduate education part of the project. Have experience and/or training in qualitative research methods. Have Danish language skills or are willing to adapt to an environment where Danish is often used. About the Department of Science Education The Department of Science Education aims to open up science and mathematics for all through research that enhances education, communication, and public engagement. The Department brings together expertise from the sciences, social sciences, and humanities to lead internationally in science and mathematics education, digital education, history and philosophy of science, and science communication. The Department currently employs approx. 100 persons – many of whom are international. We offer a vibrant interdisciplinary research environment and an attractive and friendly work environment for all employees, and we are determined to support PhD students, postdocs, and assistant professors in building of a foundation for their future career within and outside academia. It is a hallmark of our research to unite strong fundamental and applied research, with high impact in society. A large part of the Department’s teaching activities concerns the mandatory university pedagogical training and competence development for teaching faculty at the Faculties of Science and Health. You may read the Department’s strategy towards 2030 and you may read about the USE Center here: https://use.ku.dk/. You may read more about the department in general here: https://www.ind.ku.dk/english/ Copenhagen is one of the 10 most livable cities in the world with a rich culture within music, theater and associations (https://www.visitcopenhagen.com). Life for families is made easier by a publicly supported daycare and health care system, dual career opportunities, maternity/parental leave and six weeks of annual vacation. International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark at https://workindenmark.dk/. Useful information is also available at the International Staff Mobility (ISM) office at the University of Copenhagen (https://ism.ku.dk/). ISM offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen. The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background. The PhD programme Qualifications needed To be eligible for the PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g., in a geoscience or in geoscience education. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. Terms of employment Employment as a PhD fellow is full time and for a maximum 3 years. Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant. The terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. Responsibilities and tasks Carry through an independent research project under supervision at the host institution Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities (corresponding to approx. 1/2 FTE) Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals Write and defend a PhD thesis based on your project Your supervisor will be: Professor Kristine Cecile Harper, Department of Science Education, University of Copenhagen, kch@ind.ku.dk, +45 3533 0710. Application and Assessment Procedure Applications should include a PhD project proposal with clear and relevant research questions that link to the proposed research design and methodology. In the evaluation of the application, emphasis is placed on the relevance of the research question to the research project within which it will be rooted as well as the originality of the project and the suggested research design and methodology. Further criteria are: The project´s ability to relate the proposal to existing geoscience education research The project’s plan to make the project relevant to geoscience education research and for knowledge transfer through education, dissemination, or development activities. The PhD candidate’s reflections on ethical aspects specifically related to the proposed project. Your application including all attachments must submitted electronically by clicking Apply for position below. Applications must be made in English. Please include: Letter of application, including your motivation for applying for the specific PhD project. Proposal for a PhD project related to the research area described above. The proposal may not exceed six-pages in length. Please use this template. Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position Original diplomas for completed Bachelors and Masters education and transcripts of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. Publication list (if possible). Application deadline : November 29, 2026 23:59 GMT +1 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline and not to consider applications that do not meet the above-mentioned requirements. The further process After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessment committee. You will be notified whether you qualify to proceed beyond the assessment stage. The assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessment committee will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/. Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in January 2027. Questions For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor, Kristine Cecile Harper, kch@ind.ku.dk. General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/. The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position. Københavns Universitet giver sine knap 10.000 medarbejdere muligheder for at udnytte deres talent fuldt ud i et ambitiøst, uformelt miljø. Vi sikrer traditionsrige og moderne rammer om uddannelser og fri forskning på højt internationalt niveau. Vi søger svar og løsninger på fælles problemer og gør ny viden tilgænge

items.title: PhD-student in cellular neuroscience
items.desc: Your function Project description: Our ability to walk, talk and form memories requires that neurons in our brain form, maintain and adapt billions of synaptic connections to establish functional neuronal circuits. It is unclear how neurons supply the protein complexes required to build these synapses in the right time and place. This project aims to provide a molecular understanding of how synapses are formed with spatiotemporal precision. While protein synthesis was long considered to occur exclusively in neuronal cell bodies, recent research from our group and others has revealed that mRNA localization allows neurons to rapidly synthesize new proteins at defined subcellular locations. Indeed, hundreds of mRNAs are found at synapses. However, we do not know how these mRNAs are precisely captured and translated at specific sites, and how this contributes to the formation of functional synapses. Synapse formation is initiated by the interaction between cell surface proteins on both sides of a synapse. My lab has recently uncovered that specific cell surface proteins bind mRNAs and translational machinery in neurons. This provides a powerful way for neurons to regulate the localization and selective translation of mRNAs. The aim of this NWO-funded project is to investigate this exciting new mechanism and examine how mRNA capture and translated are regulated and contribution to synapse formation and function. In this project, you will use and develop genetic and imaging tools established in the Koppers lab together with live-cell imaging and functional assays to: Unravel the molecular mechanisms of synaptic mRNA capture and translation during synapse formation Control synaptic mRNA localization to modulate synapse formation. The work will be carried out in rodent neurons in culture and human iPSC-derived neurons. You will be part of international research networks and exploit a variety of techniques and analysis tools available. All the core methodology, cell models, equipment, analysis software and viral vectors are available from the start of the project. You will be trained on site and in specialized courses on campus. Your duties: As a PhD candidate your main tasks and responsibilities are: Imaging of mRNA, translation and receptors at synaptic sites in cultured rodent and human iPSC-derived neurons Investigate and control the dynamics mRNAs and ribosomes by developing novel genetic and imaging tools with live-cell and super-resolution imaging Performing functional assays to study synapse formation and function Publishing analyses in peer-reviewed journals and provide progress reports to funding sources Contributing to teaching activities (~10% of your time), including supervision of BSc and/or MSc students during internships Presenting your work to the international research community Your profile We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with: a Master degree in life sciences, biomedical sciences or biophysics with neuroscience specialization Hands-on experience with molecular and cellular neuroscience, especially the methods and/or models listed above Hands-on experience with imaging is an advantage You are fluent in English (written and spoken) and have good communication skills As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset. We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements. What do we offer? A challenging position in a socially engaged organisation. At VU Amsterdam, you contribute to education, research and service for a better world. And that is valuable. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of € 3.204,00 (PhD) and maximum € 4.051,00 (PhD) gross per month in the fourth year, for a full-time employment an employment contract of initially 1 year. If there is sufficient perspective, this will be extended to a total of 4 years. Your dissertation at the end of the fourth year forms the end of your employment contract. We also offer you attractive fringe benefits and arrangements. Some examples: A full-time 38-hour working week comes with a holiday leave entitlement of 232 hours per year. If you choose to work 40 hours, you have 96 extra holiday leave hours on an annual basis. For part-timers, this is calculated pro rata. 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% end-of-year bonus contribution to commuting expenses solid pension scheme (ABP) a wide range of sports facilities which staff may use at a modest charge About us The Functional Genomics department is made up of an enthusiastic, international team of young professionals, employing a wide range of experimental approaches—from molecular genetics to behavioral analyses (see http://www.cncr.nl/departments/). You will work closely with PhD students, postdocs, and analysts. The department has an informal, friendly atmosphere, and communication with colleagues is open and approachable. The working language is English. Faculty of Science Working at the Faculty of Science means collaborating with students, lecturers and researchers who are focused on their field, yet have a broad view of the world. We are proud of a positive and inclusive workplace culture within the faculty, where we work together with great energy and a pragmatic attitude to tackle social challenges. From forest fires to big data, from obesity to malnutrition, from helium to the universe and from genetics to medicine: our education and research cover the full breadth of science, from molecules to mankind.
