items.title: PhD Candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making
items.desc: PhD Candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making Job description Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics, in collaboration with Sciensano, the Belgian institute for health and a leading public-health research organisation, is looking for a PhD candidate in Network Modelling for Food Safety and Regulatory Decision-Making. Sciensano brings established expertise in food safety, food contaminants, exposure assessment, risk analysis, and scientific evidence generation for public authorities. The collaboration connects methodological research at Maastricht University with Sciensano’s policy-facing work supporting food safety assessment and risk-manager decision-making at Belgian and European levels. The position focuses on the development of new multi-layer network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data. The aim is to support evidence generation for contaminant risk assessment, food safety monitoring, and regulatory decision-making. The PhD candidate will conduct original methodological research while working in close connection with public-health and regulatory questions. The project offers a distinctive opportunity to develop rigorous computational models in a setting where scientific evidence, regulatory judgement, and societal impact are closely connected. The project This PhD project develops new multi-layer network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data. The project addresses an open methodological challenge: how to specify, estimate, validate, and interpret network models that can support evidence generation for contaminant risk assessment and regulatory decision-making. The project focuses on the development of network-based models for analysing complex relationships in food safety data, including information relevant to contaminants, consumption patterns, exposure assessment, and regulatory prioritisation. The methodological contribution lies in developing models suited to this type of heterogeneous and relational data, rather than simply applying existing algorithms to a new domain. The work builds on Sciensano’s established activities in food safety, exposure assessment, and contaminant risk analysis. Sciensano’s work supports science-based policy, legislation, and decision-making by risk managers at Belgian and European levels. This collaboration gives the project a strong societal and institutional grounding, while preserving a clear methodological research ambition. The precise modelling choices and empirical focus will be developed as part of the PhD trajectory, in close dialogue with the supervisory team and Sciensano researchers. The candidate will be supervised by a team from Maastricht University’s School of Business and Economics and Sciensano, combining SBE’s methodological expertise with Sciensano’s expertise in food safety, while drawing on both institutions’ experience with regulatory decision-making. The candidate will: develop new network modelling approaches for structured food-safety data; work on model specification, estimation, validation, interpretation, uncertainty assessment, and robustness analysis; analyse heterogeneous data relevant to food safety, contaminants, consumption patterns, exposure assessment, and regulatory decision-making; investigate how network models can support contaminant risk assessment, monitoring prioritisation, and evidence generation for food safety authorities; implement computational methods in reproducible research workflows; publish research in international peer-reviewed journals and present findings at academic conferences; collaborate with researchers from Maastricht University, Sciensano, and relevant academic or policy-facing partners; complete a doctoral dissertation within the agreed timeframe. Candidate profile We are looking for a candidate with a strong quantitative and computational background who is motivated to develop rigorous modelling approaches for societally relevant regulatory questions. The candidate should have: a completed or near-completed master’s degree in a relevant field, such as computer science, data science, applied mathematics, statistics, econometrics, operations research, physics, computational social science, systems science, or a related quantitative discipline; demonstrated experience with programming for data analysis or computational modelling, preferably in Python, R, Julia, or a comparable language, and willingness to further develop skills in writing reproducible, modular, and maintainable research code; a foundation in at least one relevant methodological area, such as network modelling, statistical learning, machine learning, probabilistic modelling, complex systems, or computational modelling, together with the ability and motivation to develop the specialised network-modelling expertise required for the project; an interest in structured, relational, and heterogeneous data; the ability to formulate research questions with both methodological and applied relevance; strong analytical skills and the capacity to work independently; strong written and spoken English communication skills, preferably at C1 level or higher according to the CEFR, with the ability to explain technical concepts to interdisciplinary academic, public-health, and policy-facing audiences; ability and willingness to work in an interdisciplinary environment involving methodological, food-safety, public-health, and regulatory expertise. Experience with food safety, contaminant risk assessment, exposure assessment, nutrition, toxicology, public health, or regulatory science is welcome but not required. Domain-specific knowledge can be developed during the project in collaboration with Sciensano. A strong technical profile and an interest in food safety decision-making are more important. The starting date is negotiable, but ideally the position would start in January 2027. Employment conditions At Maastricht University, the PhD candidate will work in an international, open, and engaged academic environment. The position offers: a 18-month contract, 1.0 FTE, with the prospect of a 2,5 year extension based on mutual satisfaction; a gross monthly salary between €3,204 and €4,051, based on full-time employment of 38 hours per week; 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus; 29 vacation days, based on full-time employment, four additional days off, and the possibility to accrue up to 12 extra days through compensation hours; flexible working hours, a home office allowance, and the option to work from home; supervision by researchers from Maastricht University and Sciensano; the opportunity to develop new methodology in network modelling, computational analysis, and structured food-safety data; close collaboration with Sciensano, a public-health institute with established expertise in food safety, exposure assessment, contaminant risk analysis, and scientific evidence generation for public authorities; access to doctoral training, research seminars, methodological expertise, and professional-development opportunities; opportunities to publish in international journals and present at academic conferences; an interdisciplinary research environment combining methodological rigour with public-health and regulatory relevance; a solid pension plan via ABP, company fitness schemes, and access to various university sports facilities; an inspiring work environment in the heart of Europe. Find out more about the PhD journey at Maastricht University, from starting your research to completing your PhD and beyond. As a PhD candidate, you will be automatically enrolled in one of our Graduate Schools. Find out more about our Graduate Schools. Further information For questions about the scientific content of the project, the research environment, or the collaboration between Maastricht University and Sciensano, please contact: Rui Jorge Almeida via rj.almeida@maastrichtuniversity.nl Mirjana Andjelkovic via Mirjana.Andjelkovic@sciensano.be For questions about the application procedure or employment conditions, please contact: Miranda Van den Beuken via miranda.vandenbeuken@maastrichtuniversity.nl Application procedure Applications should include: a motivation letter describing the candidate’s interest in the position and fit with the project; a curriculum vitae; transcripts or a list of completed courses and grades; a writing sample, such as a master’s thesis, research paper, or technical report; if available, examples of programming, modelling, or data-analysis work; the names and contact details of at least two academic referees. In the motivation letter, candidates are encouraged to explain how their methodological background could contribute to the development of multi-layer network models for food safety and regulatory decision-making. Prior experience in food safety or public health is not required, but candidates should be willing to engage with domain experts and policy-facing research questions. Applications should be submitted no later than 18 November 2026. Please note that incomplete applications will not be considered. The vacancy is open for internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritised. At Maastricht University, we prefer to contact potential candidates directly. We therefore kindly ask that no agencies or intermediaries submit offers or approaches. Apply now via the button below. We look forward to getting to know you! About the School of Business and Economics (SBE) SBE is an international faculty for economics, business, and policy. We combine academic depth with societal engagement. Our education is small-scale and interactive. Our research focuses on themes such as sustainability, inclusion, and digital transformation. Together, we work on impactful solutions for the world of tomorrow. About Maastricht University At Maastricht University, we collaboratively seek solutions to help move the world forward. We do this with 23,300 students and 5,400 employees across 5 regional locations, 6 faculties, and more than 70 research institutes. We encourage you to push boundaries and discover new opportunities for yourself and the world around you. Together, we can find the answers for tomorrow. The vacancy is open for internal and external candidates. In case of equal qualifications, internal candidates will be prioritized. At Maastricht University, we prefer to contact potential candidates directly. We therefore kindly ask that no agencies or intermediaries submit offers or approaches. Maastricht University is committed to promoting and nurturing a diverse and inclusive community. We believe that diversity in our staff and student population contributes to the quality of research and education at UM, and strive to enable this through inclusive policies and innovative projects led by teams of staff and students. We encourage you to apply for this position. items.title: PhD in Energy-Efficient Sensors and Computing Hardware from 2D Materials
items.desc: The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Introduction Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region. Job Description In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware. What you'll contribute to Specifically, you will: develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities; optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration; develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors; engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance; characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance; publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences; supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects. Your research environment You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab (NanoComputing Research Lab), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities. What we're looking for A master’s degree in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field, with a solid foundation in semiconductor materials and device physics, and prior experience in the growth of nanomaterials (preferably 2D materials using CVD), nanofabrication processes such as atomic layer deposition, lithography, etching etc., and 2D material transfer process. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field. A research-oriented attitude. Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and mentor bachelor/master’s students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. items.title: PhD Position
items.desc: About the position 3-year 100% PhD position is available at the Department of Pediatric Research, OUS Rikshospitalet for a highly motivated and skilled PhD student on a project funded by South-Eastern Norway Regional Health Authority. The position is available from 23rd November 2026. Neonatal cholestasis is a condition with impaired bile flow causing accumulation of bile acids and bilirubin, liver damage and debilitating pruritus. Reduction in bile to the intestine results in malabsorption, reduced weight gain, vitamin deficiency and changes in microbiota. Both genetic and environmental factors can result in cholestasis. About the Department / Research Group Professor Runar Almaas (Pediatric hepatology) at PFI, OUS is leading the project. The PhD candidate will be supervised by him and by Co-supervisor Barbora Smolkova (PhD) and senior researcher Gareth Sullivan. The group is using induced pluripotent stem cells for making liver organoids and a major part of the work will be related to this model. Oslo University Hospital is a workplace with great diversity. We believe this is crucial for solving our tasks in the best possible way. We want this diversity to be reflected among the applicants for our positions, and we encourage all qualified candidates, regardless of background, to apply! Key information Application deadline: 15.11.2026 Employer: Oslo universitetssykehus HF Town/city: Oslo Title: PhD Position Positions: 1 Full-time/part-time: Full-time Employment type: Contract Percentage of full-time: 100 Webcruiter ID: 5194655530 Start date: 23.11.2026 End date: 09.11.2029 Social sharing : Share on x Share on LinkedIn Share on Facebook Share by email Duties and responsabilities What Tasks and Responsibilities Are Associated with the Position? To reveal mechanisms of cholestasis and pruritus and to investigate novel potential treatments we are using liver organoids derived from disease-specific induced pluripotent stem cells. iPSC-derived liver organoids are a unique model that can mimic key features of the human liver and can be used to study liver development and disease. In these project liver organoids will be used for studying protein trafficking, effect of modulating factors and potential drugs. Qualifications Master degree (or equivalent) in medicine, biomedicine, biotechnology, or molecular biology Good practical skills in various extraction, quantification, and analysis of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) and proteins including qRT-PCR, ddPCR, and Western blotting are advantages Skills and prior experience in cell cultivation and handling is an advantage experience in other relevant molecular biology techniques including gene editing using CRISPR/Cas9 technology, next-generation sequencing, etc is an advantage Experience in scientific writing / presentation is an advantage Good written and oral communication skills in English Practical Information We request that relevant documentation be attached to the application. Please note that all documents should be in English or a Scandinavian language. Personal qualities We are looking for a highly dedicated, reliable and highly motivated candidate with great working capacity We expect scientific curiosity and understanding about the nature of scientific thinking You have a strong interest in completing your tasks in structured way. You are able to design, plan, perform, and analyze experiments in an innovative way The candidate is expected to work together with engineers and other scientists in a team. Ability to work independently, but with good communication skills is preferred. We can offer 100% position for three years granted Ambitious project and interesting scientific topic. An emerging and rapidly developing area of research Training in advanced methods and models. Encouraged supervision and cooperation team A friendly and international environment A favorable pension arrangement and attractive welfare arrangements In accordance with the OUS’s equal opportunities policy, we invite applications from all interested individuals regardless of gender or ethnicity Address: Oslo universitetssykehus HF, Rikshospitalet, Sognsvannsveien 20, 0372 Oslo, Norway Open directions (in new tab) Contacts Runar Almaas Head of Department Phone: +4741321932 About the employer Oslo University Hospital is a highly specialized hospital in charge of extensive regional and local hospital assignments. As Scandinavia’s largest hospital, we carry out more than 1.2 million patient treatments each year. The hospital has a nationwide responsibility for a number of national and multi-regional assignments, and has several national centers of competence. Oslo University Hospital is responsible for approximately 50 percent of all medical and health care research conducted at Norwegian hospitals, and is a significant role player within the education of a large variety of health care personnel.

items.title: PhD Research Intern
items.desc: Job description Company and benefits Social Impact & Sustainability Job ID 41745 Join the leader in entertainment innovation and help us design the future. At Dolby, science meets art, and high tech means more than computer code. As a member of the Dolby team, you’ll see and hear the results of your work everywhere, from movie theaters to smartphones. We continue to revolutionize how people create, deliver, and enjoy entertainment worldwide. To do that, we need the absolute best talent. We’re big enough to give you all the resources you need, and small enough so you can make a real difference and earn recognition for your work. We offer a collegial culture, challenging projects, and excellent compensation and benefits, not to mention a Flex Work approach that is truly flexible to support where, when, and how you do your best work. Internship: Development and On-Device Deployment of an Autoregressive Model for Real-Time Speech Restoration and Dialog Enhancement Start: Open Duration: 3 months (full-time) or 6 months (part-time) Location: Stockholm Speech restoration and dialog enhancement are critical components in modern audio experiences, especially in noisy environments or legacy content with degraded quality. Current systems often rely on non-causal, server-side models that require full audio context, limiting their use in real-time or on-device applications. With recent advances in autoregressive language modeling and efficient deep learning deployment, there is growing potential to develop low-latency, high-quality speech enhancement systems that operate in real time and even on consumer devices. This internship aims to design and implement an autoregressive, large language model (LLM)-based architecture for speech restoration and dialog enhancement. The model will be trained to reconstruct clean speech from degraded inputs by leveraging both acoustic and linguistic context. It will be evaluated against Dolby’s current best multimodal system, focusing on perceptual quality, intelligibility, and latency. A key objective is to explore the feasibility of deploying the model on-device through techniques such as model compression, quantization, pruning, and compilation using modern inference frameworks. Candidate requirements Master’s or Ph.D. student in Machine Learning, Signal Processing, Computer Science, or a related field. Hands-on experience with PyTorch. Interest in model optimization for edge deployment using tools such as Triton Inference Server, ONNX, TensorRT, or similar frameworks. Prior experience in this field is a plus. Experience fine-tuning LLMs is a plus. Knowledge of audio-language modeling is a plus. Dolby Hiring Entity: Gävlegatan 12A 113 30 Stockholm, Sweden

items.title: Doctoral student in Industrial Design with focus on strategic design
items.desc: Lund University was founded in 1666 and is repeatedly ranked among the world’s top universities. The University has around 46 000 students and 8 500 staff based in Lund, Helsingborg and Malmö. We are united in our efforts to understand, explain and improve our world and the human condition. Lund University welcomes applicants with diverse backgrounds and experiences. We regard equality, equal opportunities and diversity as a strength and an asset. Description of the workplace The position is located in the division of Industrial Design at the Department of Design Sciences at LTH, Lund University. Design Sciences is an interdisciplinary department that integrates design, technology, and people in its research and education. As a doctoral student you will become part of an interdisciplinary research environment and work alongside doctoral students, senior researchers and teaching staff within Industrial Design and the wider Department of Design Sciences. Being a doctoral student As a doctoral student, you are both admitted as a student and employed at Lund University. You will be trained in a scientific approach. In short, you will be trained to think critically and analytically, to solve problems independently using the right methods, and to develop an awareness of research ethics. In addition, you will have the opportunity to work on projects, to develop your leadership and pedagogical skills. Throughout your studies, you will be guided by supervisors. Doctoral studies end with a thesis and a doctoral degree. More about being a doctoral student at LTH on lth.se. Subject and project description Research in Industrial Design investigates how design shapes and responds to technological, environmental and societal change. It develops and critically examines design knowledge, methods and practices, with the aim of understanding how design can contribute to meaningful and responsible transformation. Our research combines scientific and artistic approaches and is often conducted in collaboration with academic, industrial and public-sector partners as well as communities and third-sector organizations. The research environment encompasses sustainable design; emerging technologies and AI; design strategy, management and innovation; design practice and methods; and critical and participatory perspectives on design and design education. This doctoral position has a particular focus on strategic design. The research will investigate how design can operate as a strategic capability in organizations and society and contribute to processes of innovation, transformation and value creation. Possible areas of inquiry include how design capabilities are developed and embedded in organizations; the role of design and design approaches in enabling organizational change; design in complex settings; systemic design; and user and citizen engagement in strategic design processes. The research may also investigate futures-oriented approaches, including designerly ways of navigating complex and uncertain societal, technological and environmental conditions. Within this overall research area, the doctoral student will develop and refine the specific research direction and project in dialogue with the supervisors. The project is expected to combine theoretical inquiry with empirical research and may incorporate experimental, participatory or practice-based design approaches where relevant. Work duties You will primarily devote yourself to your doctoral programme. You will develop and conduct an independent doctoral research project. Your work will include formulating research questions, reviewing and developing relevant theoretical perspectives, designing and conducting empirical studies, analysing research material, communicating findings through academic publications and conferences, and completing a doctoral thesis. You will also be expected to participate actively in the research environment of the Division of Industrial Design and the Department of Design Sciences and to engage with relevant academic and external research partners. Additional duties include participation in teaching and other departmental work (however, a maximum of 20% of working hours). The position requires regular on-site presence at Lund University in Lund to carry out the work and participate fully in the research environment. Qualifications To be eligible for admission and employment as a doctoral student, you must fulfil the requirements below. Admission requirements A person meets the general admission requirements for third-cycle courses and study programmes if the applicant: has been awarded a second-cycle qualification, or has satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the second cycle, or has acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad. A person meets the specific admission requirements for third cycle studies in Industrial Design if the applicant has: at least 30 higher education credits relevant to the subject area, of which at least 15 credits must be at an advanced level, or an in-depth study of at least 20 higher education credits at an advanced level relevant to the subject area, or a degree in fine arts, engineering, Master's or Magister's degree relevant to the subject area. Additional requirements In order to complete the doctoral programme in question, the following are also required: Knowledge and skills relevant to industrial design and to the proposed area of doctoral research. Ability to to independently formulate and address research problems. Analytical skills and the ability to engage critically with theoretical perspectives and empirical material. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English. Other qualifications (advantages) For the doctoral programme in question, the following are considered as other qualifications: Experience of conducting empirical, practice-based or participatory research. Experience of interdisciplinary or multidisciplinary work. Experience of managing complex projects involving multiple actors or perspectives. Experience of using design methods and practices as part of research or inquiry. Experience of collaboration with academic, industrial, public-sector or other societal actors. Experience of communicating research or complex design work to different audiences. Consideration will also be given to the applicant's ability to take initiative, work independently, collaborate with others, and develop and complete a long-term research project. We offer Lund University is a public authority which means that employees get particular benefits, generous annual leave and an advantageous occupational pension scheme. More about working at Lund University on lu.se. About the employment The employment is a fixed-term employment at full time, starting on 2027-01-01 or soon after. Third cycle studies at LTH consist of full-time studies for 4 years. In the case of teaching and other departmental duties, the employment is extended accordingly. Doctoral studentships are regulated in the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100), chapter 5, 1-7 §§. More about terms of employment for doctoral students on Lund University’s Staffpages. Other This doctoral position is funded by the Ingvar Kamprad Design Foundation (IKDF). How to apply Applications must be written in English and include: CV A cover letter describing your reasons for wishing to undertake a PhD in Industrial Design, your interest in this position, and how your academic, professional and/or personal experiences have shaped your research interests and prepared you for doctoral studies. Copies of degree certificates and transcripts confirming that you meet the general and specific admission requirements; A research statement (maximum 1,500 words) describing the research questions, problems or phenomena within Strategic Design that you are interested in exploring, why you consider them important, and how you might approach investigating them. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and ability to formulate a potential direction for doctoral research; it is not expected to constitute a fully developed research proposal. A portfolio or selection of work samples demonstrating relevant design, research, or professional work. These may include design projects, research projects, publications or other written work, collaborative or community-based projects, or other work relevant to the position. For collaborative work, clearly describe your own role and contribution. Contact information for three references and Any other documents you wish to be considered. We welcome your application. LTH is Lund University’s Faculty of Engineering. At LTH we educate people, build knowledge for the future and work hard for the development of society. We create space for brilliant research and inspire creative advancements in technology, architecture and design. We have nearly 12,000 students. Every year, our researchers – many of whom work in world-leading profile areas – publish around 100 theses and 2 000 scientific findings. In addition, a number of research results and degree projects are transformed into innovations. Together we explore and create – to benefit the world. We kindly decline all sales and marketing contacts. items.title: PhD en modélisation spatio-temporelle d'événements extrêmes (incendies de forêt)
items.desc: Introduction Institution d’enseignement et de recherche de premier plan au niveau international, l’UNIL compte près de 5’000 collaboratrices et collaborateurs et 17’000 étudiant·e·s, réparti·e·s entre le campus de Dorigny et les sites du CHUV et d’Epalinges. En tant qu’employeur, elle encourage l’excellence, la reconnaissance des personnes et la responsabilité. unil.ch/travailler Présentation Un poste de doctorant·e en modélisation spatio-temporelle d'événements extrêmes (incendies de forêt) financé par le Fonds national suisse de la recherche scientifique (FNS) est à pourvoir dans le laboratoire de la Dre Marj Tonini à l'Institut des dynamiques de la surface terrestre (IDYST), Faculté des géosciences et de l'environnement (GSE), Université de lausanne (Unil), en collaboration avec la prof. Valérie Chabez-Demoulin (co-requérante principale), professeure de statistique à la Faculté des hautes études commerciales (HEC Lausanne), Unil. Le laboratoire développe des approches innovantes en apprentissage automatique et en statistique pour l'analyse de données environnementales complexes présentant des dimensions spatiales et temporelles. Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e pour rejoindre ExtFire, un projet financé par le FNS qui vise à développer le premier cadre paneuropéen combinant la théorie des valeurs extrêmes (TVE) non stationnaire, l'inférence causale et l'apprentissage profond sensible aux queues de distribution, afin de quantifier et de prédire le risque d'incendies extrêmes de manière reproductible et transférable. Outre les deux requérantes principales, l'équipe d'ExtFire réunit trois partenaires externes aux compétences complémentaires : le prof. Marco Turco (Université de Murcie, Espagne) apporte une expertise spécialisée dans les interactions entre feux et climat ; Le Dr Paolo Fiorucci (CIMA Research Foundation, Italie) apporte son expertise en simulation de la propagation des feux ; et le Dr Erwan Koch (Expertise Centre for Climate Extremes, Unil) fournit son expertise en TVE spatiale et en champs aléatoires max-stables. La personne retenue rejoindra le laboratoire de la Dre Tonini à l'IDYST et travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le·la postdoctorant·e recruté·e dans le cadre du projet ExtFire, bénéficiant de l'expertise et du soutien de l'ensemble de l'équipe ExtFire. Informations liées au poste Entrée en fonction : 1er janvier 2027 ou à convenir Durée du contrat : 1 an, renouvelable jusqu'à 4 ans Taux d'activité : 100% Lieu de travail : Université de Lausanne - Quartier Unil-Mouline - Bâtiment Géopolis Vos activités La personne retenue développera des travaux de recherche conduisant à un doctorat en sciences de l'environnement sous la direction principale de la Dre Marj Tonini. Le·la doctorant·e contribuera à ExtFire en développant le coeur du projet. Les tâches principales comprennent : Harmoniser et intégrer de grands jeux de données ouverts sur les incendies, la météorologie et la surface terrestre au sein d'une infrastructure de données paneuropéenne cohérente ; Développer des modèles statistiques et spatio-temporels pour caractériser les incendies extrêmes, tels que ceux présentant de très grandes surfaces brûlées ou une propagation rapide ; Constituer les jeux de données et les modèles d'apprentissage automatique de référence utilisés pour évaluer les prédictions d'événements extrêmes ; Appliquer des méthodes d'IA explicable (p. ex. SHAP) pour identifier les principaux facteurs environnementaux des incendies extrêmes selon les régions ; Rédiger des articles scientifiques, présenter les résultats lors de conférences internationales et participer à l'enseignement en tant qu'assistant·e (environ 10% du temps). Votre profil Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e motivé·e présentant le profil suivant : Volonté d'élaborer une thèse en modélisation spatio-temporelle d'événements extrêmes (incendies de forêt) ; Master en sciences de l'environnement, géosciences, statistique, mathématiques appliquées, physique, informatique ou dans un domaine quantitatif étroitement apparenté, avec de solides résultats académiques ; Expérience pratique de l'apprentissage automatique, idéalement de l'apprentissage profond (p. ex. PyTorch, TensorFlow), et familiarité avec l'IA explicable ; Solides bases en statistique et en analyse de données (p. ex. probabilités, régression, séries temporelles ou statistique spatiale). La connaissance de la théorie des valeurs extrêmes est un atout ; Solides compétences en programmation en Python et/ou R, attestées par une expérience du traitement et de l'analyse de grands jeux de données (p. ex. données climatiques ou de télédétection maillées, formats NetCDF/raster) ; Maîtrise de l'anglais, à l'écrit et à l'oral, avec la capacité de rédiger des rapports scientifiques. La connaissance du français est un atout ; Une expérience avérée en analyse quantitative ou en modélisation des dangers naturels (p. ex. incendies de forêt, inondations, glissements de terrain, séismes) attestée par un mémoire, un projet ou une publication, est un atout. Vos avantages Nous offrons un environnement de travail dynamique et inclusif, favorisant un fort esprit de communauté et offrant un soutien dédié au développement d'une carrière académique. Les membres de notre équipe font partie de réseaux de recherche internationaux, et les doctorant·e·s sont encouragé·e·s et soutenu·e·s dans leur participation à ces réseaux, y compris à des conférences et ateliers. Le poste est financé par le FNS, avec un salaire conforme aux barèmes salariaux du FNS et de l'Unil, ainsi que des fonds dédiés aux conférences, ateliers et séjours de recherche. Diverses possibilités de formation complémentaires sont également disponibles à l'Unil ou auprès d'autres organisation qui promeuvent la recherche doctorale. Un cadre de travail agréable dans un environnement académique multiculturel et diversifié. Des possibilités de formation continue, une multitude d'activités et d'autres avantages à découvrir. Davantage d'informations sur unil.ch/travailler Pour tout renseignement complémentaire Dre Marj Tonini - marj.tonini@unil.ch Votre dossier de candidature Délai de postulation : 01.11.2026 Nous vous prions de bien vouloir nous transmettre les documents suivants en un seul fichier PDF : Lettre de motivation (1 page maximum), présentant votre motivation et expliquant en quoi votre parcours et votre expérience répondent au projet. Curriculum Vitae, incluant une liste de publications, le cas échéant. Copies des diplômes et titres académiques, des relevés de notes et du mémoire de master. Noms, adresses e-mail et numéros de téléphone de deux personnes de référence. Court descriptif (1 page maximum) d'un projet antérieur impliquant l'analyse quantitative ou computationelle de données environnementales ou relatives aux dangers naturels (p. ex. votre mémoire de master, un projet de recherche ou un stage), précisant votre contribution personnelle et incluant un lien vers votre code (p. ex. GitHub), si disponible Il ne sera pris en compte que les candidatures adressées par le biais de ce site. Nous vous remercions de votre compréhension. Remarques L’UNIL s’engage : Pour l’égalité, la diversité et l’inclusion au sein de sa communauté ; À garantir un environnement ouvert, respectueux et propice à l’épanouissement ; À offrir des conditions de travail favorables à la conciliation des différentes sphères de vie ; À soutenir la relève scientifique. unil.ch/egalite unil.ch/familles unil.ch/graduatecampus

items.title: AstraZeneca-Funded Non-Clinical PhD Studentship (Fixed Term): Physics-Guided Representation Learning for Drug Discovery
items.desc: Applications are invited for a four-year, AstraZeneca-funded PhD studentship in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics, commencing in October 2027. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof Sergio Bacallado (University of Cambridge), Dr Dino Oglic (AstraZeneca), and Dr Jon Paul Janet (AstraZeneca). The studentship offers an opportunity to conduct cutting-edge research at the interface of statistical machine learning, molecular simulation and drug discovery. Project description The project, entitled Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection , aims to develop novel machine-learning methods for predicting molecular binding affinities and supporting decision-making in drug discovery. Free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations provide valuable information about how strongly candidate drug molecules bind to their biological targets, but these calculations are computationally expensive. This project will investigate how machine-learning models can extract richer information from FEP data and experimental measurements, combining physical principles with modern representation-learning techniques. The research will involve developing and evaluating new statistical and machine-learning methods, with access to both public benchmark datasets and AstraZeneca's industrial drug-discovery expertise and data. Candidate requirements Applicants should have, or expect to obtain, a first-class or upper second-class honours degree (or equivalent), normally following four years of university study. We welcome applicants with backgrounds in Mathematics, Statistics, Machine Learning, Scientific Computing, or any closely related discipline. Experience with computational chemistry would be desirable but is not essential . We particularly welcome applications from candidates with strong mathematical or machine-learning backgrounds who are interested in applying their expertise to problems in drug discovery. Funding The studentship provides funding for four years , covering a maintenance stipend and University tuition fees at the UK/Home rate. The studentship is open to candidates eligible for Home-fee status. International candidates may also be considered, provided that additional funding can be secured through scholarships or other approved funding schemes to cover the difference between Home and international tuition fees. This difference cannot be covered through student self-funding. Training and supervision The student will benefit from joint academic and industrial supervision, participating in the research activities of the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics and collaborating closely with AstraZeneca researchers to gain exposure to industrial applications of artificial intelligence in pharmaceutical development. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the University of Cambridge Postgraduate Applicant Portal , selecting the course PhD in Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics : https://www.postgraduate.study.cam.ac.uk/courses/directory/mapmpdpms/apply Applicants should indicate Dr Sergio Bacallado as their proposed supervisor and use the following project title: Physics-Guided Representation Learning from Free Energy Perturbation Data for Affinity Prediction and Candidate Down-Selection. Applications should include the supporting documentation required by the University, including academic transcripts, a CV, two references, and the relevant research summary and reasons for applying. The deadline for applications is 6 January 2027 (23:59 UK time) . Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview in January 2027 . Informal enquiries about the project are welcome and may be addressed to Dr Sergio Bacallado at sb2116@cam.ac.uk . The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society.

items.title: PhD Quant
items.desc: Overview We are seeking an exceptional Quant Researcher to join a highly collaborative and research-driven systematic investment team. This role is ideally suited to candidates completing or recently having completed a PhD in a quantitative discipline such as Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering, Machine Learning, Operations Research, or a related field. You will be responsible for identifying, researching, and developing predictive signals and systematic trading strategies across global financial markets. The successful candidate will combine strong theoretical foundations with practical programming expertise to transform complex datasets into innovative investment insights. Key Responsibilities Conduct original quantitative research to identify alpha-generating opportunities across global markets. Develop predictive models using advanced statistical techniques, machine learning methods, and data-driven approaches. Analyse large, structured and unstructured datasets to uncover patterns and investment signals. Design, implement, and evaluate systematic trading strategies through rigorous backtesting and validation frameworks. Collaborate closely with quantitative researchers, portfolio managers, and engineers to move research ideas into production. Improve existing models through ongoing performance analysis, monitoring, and refinement. Research and evaluate new datasets, alternative data sources, and novel modelling techniques. Build scalable research tools and infrastructure to support efficient strategy development. Present research findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders in a clear and concise manner. Stay at the forefront of developments in statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, and quantitative finance. Required Qualifications PhD (completed or near completion) in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering, Machine Learning, Econometrics, Operations Research, or a related quantitative discipline. Outstanding academic record from a leading university. Strong background in probability, statistics, optimisation, machine learning, or related quantitative methods. Excellent programming skills in Python, C++, Java, or a similar language. Experience working with large datasets and conducting empirical research. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Ability to communicate complex concepts effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. Demonstrated intellectual curiosity and a passion for solving challenging quantitative problems. Preferred Experience Research experience in machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, statistical modelling, time-series analysis, optimisation, or artificial intelligence. Publications in leading academic conferences or journals. Experience with distributed computing, high-performance computing, or large-scale data processing frameworks. Exposure to quantitative finance, systematic investing, or algorithmic trading is advantageous but not required. Familiarity with cloud computing, data engineering, or production-grade software development practices. What We Offer Opportunity to work alongside world-class researchers, engineers, and investment professionals. Access to extensive datasets, cutting-edge technology, and substantial computational resources. A highly collaborative, intellectually stimulating research environment. Direct impact on live investment decisions and trading strategies. Exceptional opportunities for learning, development, and long-term career progression. Competitive compensation package, including performance-based incentives.

items.title: Funded PhD Position in Multi-Agent AI and Distributed Optimization for Resilient Cyber-Physical Systems
items.desc: Funded PhD Position in Multi-Agent AI and Distributed Optimization for Resilient Cyber-Physical Systems. Universidad Rey Juan Carlos, Móstoles, Madrid, Spain. Competitive funding for three years We are seeking a motivated PhD candidate to join our Artificial Intelligence Group (GIA) and conduct research at the intersection of multi-agent systems, mathematical optimization and machine learning. Under the supervision of Prof. Marin Lujak , the successful candidate will investigate how autonomous agents can adapt both their operational decisions and their coordination mechanisms as demands, resources and communication conditions change. The research will draw on two complementary projects: CEFIR: intelligent coordination of waste-collection fleets, integrating operational data into dynamic task allocation and vehicle routing. CRISIS: coordination of resources during floods and wildfires, addressing uncertainty, disrupted communications and time-critical decisions. The thesis will develop a focused scientific contribution within this programme, combining methodological advances with evaluation against concrete operational challenges. Its precise scope will be defined with the selected candidate, taking their background and research interests into account. Your research activities Formulate mathematical models for multi-agent coordination, resource allocation and routing, and develop distributed or decentralized solution methods. Investigate which decisions require revision after a disruption and how agents should adapt their information exchange and coordination structure. Explore how learning and optimization can work together to improve decisions while respecting operational constraints. Implement algorithms and design reproducible computational experiments using simulation and digital twins. Contribute to scientific publications and collaborate with academic and project partners. Candidate profile We welcome applications from candidates with: A Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics or a related discipline. Solid foundations in mathematical modelling, algorithms and optimization. Good programming skills, preferably in Python. Proficiency in written and spoken English. Intellectual curiosity, analytical rigour and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Experience with Gurobi, multi-agent systems, distributed computing, simulation or machine learning would be an advantage. What the position offers The position combines three years of competitive funding with scientific supervision and opportunities to develop original research connecting AI and Operations Research in a competitive international environment. The candidate will work on problems arising in industrial fleet management and crisis response, with opportunities to collaborate with industrial and academic project partners and contribute to scientific publications. How to apply Please email one PDF containing your detailed CV, a motivation letter and academic transcripts to marin dot lujak at urjc dot es . Email subject: PhD application – CEFIR/CRISIS Your motivation letter should explain your relevant experience, your interest in the position and the research questions you would like to explore. Links to research code or publications are welcome, if available. About the university @Universidad Rey Juan Carlos (URJC) is the most modern public university and one of the largest in the Madrid region in Spain. As a part of the EULIST Alliance, its teaching and research span multiple disciplines, with international collaboration across academic institutions, industry and public organizations to address scientific and societal challenges. Please share this opportunity with students and colleagues who may be interested. #PhDPosition #FundedPhD #ArtificialIntelligence #DistributedAI #MultiAgentSystems #OperationsResearch #Optimization #URJC

items.title: PhD Candidate in AI Driven MAC Control for Integrated Terrestrial NTN 6G Networks
items.desc: About The Position Are you motivated to pursue a doctoral degree and contribute to cutting-edge research at the intersection of artificial intelligence and next-generation wireless communications like 6G? The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU has a vacancy for a PhD candidate in AI‑Driven & Self-healing MAC Control for Integrated Terrestrial-NTN 6G networks. The position is fully funded and will run for four years (100 % employment), including teaching duties. Your immediate leader is the Head of the Communication Technology Unit at the department of Information Security and Communication Technology. The workplace will be located in Trondheim. About The Project Future 6G and beyond communication systems are expected to integrate terrestrial cellular networks with non-terrestrial platforms, including Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Satellites, High Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS), and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). While such integrated networks can provide ubiquitous connectivity and improved resilience, they also introduce significant challenges due to highly dynamic radio environments, heterogeneous backhaul infrastructures, mobility, resource constraints, and service disruptions. The core research focuses on the MAC layer and its techniques – the candidate will design, implement and evaluate an AI-driven MAC-control framework that self‑heals in integrated terrestrial-NTN (LEO, HAPS, UAV) 6G networks. The work will be hands-on and system-oriented; a closed-loop, verifiable prototype will be built, tested under realistic degradations and examined for different metrics such as latency, reliability, fairness and SLA‑violation. For example, the candidate will do some of the tasks including: AI-driven Link Adaptation and MAC control – develop AI-based mechanism that proactively anticipate and respond to rapidly changing conditions in integrated terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (LEO satellites, HAPS, and UAVs) and to cascading radio access networks (RAN) failures/degradations. AI-Driven self-healing MAC – develop algorithms and techniques at the MAC layer for fast anomaly detection, failure prediction, autonomous recovery, and performance resilience. Service-aware MAC layer techniques – develop novel MAC-layer mechanisms that integrate queueing theory, traffic modelling, machine learning, and network-performance prediction for improving latency, reliability and fairness to support mission‑critical services. The proposed algorithms and mechanisms will be implemented and validated on the B5G Lab infrastructure at the IIK department, NTNU. The lab provides industry‑grade 5G equipment, open‑source RAN stacks, programmable OpenFlow/P4 switches and AI‑Boxes for fast inference, together with NetFPGA/DAG hardware for sub‑millisecond failure detection and a Timeseries‑DB/Grafana monitoring platform for closed‑loop testing. One or multiple satellite ground stations (e.g., Starlink, OneWeb) will be installed and connected to the core network soon to support NTN testing. Duties of the position Complete all the doctoral courses work, a condition to obtain the doctorate degree Carry out high‑quality research within the scope described above Publish enough scientific results in recognized venues and contribute to research disseminations Actively participate in the Networking Research Group and its activities Engage in international activities (conferences, research stays at foreign educational institutions) Teach and support learning activities in courses related to communications and networking Required Selection Criteria You must have a relevant master’s degree in wireless communications and mobile networks, computer networks and distributed systems, telecommunication engineering, computer science with a networking focus, or equivalent, with a strong background in theory, ML/AI, and mathematics Your master’s degree must correspond to a five-year Norwegian degree, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level Master students can still apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position, and no later than 1st of August 2027 You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background (not worse than C), you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. A scientific proposal (max. 1000 words / 3 pages) You must meet the requirements for admission to the PhD program in Information Security and Communication Technology. Applicants who do not master a Scandinavian language and are not native English speakers must provide evidence of good written and spoken English language skills. The following tests can be used as such documentation: TOEFL: 600 (paper-based test), 92 (Internet-based test). IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted). CAE/CPE: grade B or A PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNU's guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria High skills in applied mathematics, problem mathematicalising and solving Practical experiences with networked systems and multi-vendor softwarized environments Experience with 5G radio access and core testbeds including open-source solutions Relevant publications and dissemination will be considered an advantage Experience in teaching, preferably on master level Good oral and written presentation skills in Norwegian/Scandinavian language Personal characteristics We Are Seeking Applicants Who Are Highly motivated by fundamental research of practical relevance Well organized and have interest beyond their own research Capable to work independently with clear goals and plans to achieve them Eager to present and discuss their research with other professionals Eager to disseminate research results in both local and international venues In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal suitability, as well as motivation, in terms of the qualifications specified in the advertisement. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Access to the B5G Lab’s state‑of‑the‑art infrastructure Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 4 years for the doctoral work including teaching duties. Integrated PhD study candidates are welcome to apply. For more information on the Integrated PhD program you may check here. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD program in Information Security and Communication Technology within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral program throughout the period of employment. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to be in conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed. About The Application The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. The Application Must Include Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees Curriculum Vitae (clear, up to date) Copy of Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be presented before taking up the position A scientific proposal (max. 1000 words / 3 pages, written in English) including a brief problem formulation, research questions, theoretical perspective, methodological approach, and an initial progress plan for the project Your motivation letter (max. 400 words/1 page, written in English) Names and contact information of three relevant references Publications or other relevant research work (e.g., conferences, journals) (if applicable) Certificates or other relevant documentation (e.g., hands-on work with 5G network) (if applicable) Link(s) to public GitHub (or similar) repositories or other code portfolios demonstrating relevant programming experience (e.g., in C++ and/or Python) (if applicable) If all or parts of your education have been completed abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation. When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications

items.title: Doctoral researcher in AI for Science
items.desc: About Us The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character. The Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) at the University of Luxembourg contributes multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine. Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the IAS Audacity project AI4TECS, which investigates how advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques can enable real‑time identification and treatment of emerging contaminants (ECs). AI4TECS aims to develop the first AI‑powered system that integrates real‑time EC identification using non-target high resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) data, toxicity prediction, and transformation modelling into an early‑warning monitoring framework. Your role Conducting excellent collaborative research within the project AI4TECS. The person will pursue three core research directions: Developing a foundation model capable of identifying ECs directly from complex LC‑HRMS data Designing hierarchical graph‑based models to predict toxicity under uncertainty by linking molecular‑level and system‑level knowledge Advancing causal inference methods to predict transformation products (TPs) under varying treatment conditions Writing a doctoral dissertation in computer science Publishing research findings in leading international conferences and high‑impact journals in AI, machine learning, and environmental sciences Presenting results at scientific meetings, workshops, and project events, contributing to the visibility and impact of the AI4TECS project Potential participation in teaching activities The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary project team with expertise spanning environmental chemistry, AI, and water‑treatment engineering. Collaboration is central to the project’s design. Throughout the project, the candidate will work closely with a second doctoral researcher to be recruited within the Environmental Cheminformatics Group (ECI) at LCSB. The ECI PhD candidate will perform prioritized Non-Targeted Assessment (pNTA) across diverse water matrices and case studies, while the AI4Science PhD (this position) will develop machine‑learning models that learn from and build upon these pNTA results. The successful candidate will be employed at the Department of Computer Science of the University of Luxembourg (UL) and have access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources suitable for large-scale machine-learning and foundation-model experiments. They will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jun Pang and Dr. Zhiqiang Zhong. For further information about the position, please contact Prof. Dr. Jun Pang and Dr. Zhiqiang Zhong (firstname.lastname_AT_uni.lu). Your profile A Master’s degree in computer science or a closely related field Solid background in AI, with particular interest or experience in foundation models, e.g., representation learning, large‑scale pretraining, and graph machine learning, e.g., GNNs, graph representation learning, hierarchical or probabilistic graph models Strong analytical and problem‑solving abilities, with enthusiasm for developing novel computational methods Excellent programming skills and familiarity with modern deep learning frameworks Strong interest in interdisciplinary research, and the ability to engage meaningfully with collaborators from environmental chemistry and water‑treatment engineering Operational Language Requirements: Excellent command of English is required Academic Eligibility (Thesis): Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission – Doctoral Candidates. We offer A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure A partner for society and industry. items.title: Doktorand Conversational Banking mit Agentic AI (m/w/d)
items.desc: Für unser Geschäftsfeld Data, Security and Identity im Tribe Analytics (DSIANA) suchen wir dich in Vollzeit als Doktorand (m/w/d) Conversational Banking mit Agentic AI in Karlsruhe. Deine Tätigkeit ist dem Squad Data Ignite zugeordnet. Hier arbeitest du mit deinen Kolleg*innen standortübergreifend und mit vielfältigen, teilweise englischsprachigen Schnittstellen zusammen. Beachte: Diese Stelle ist für die Dauer von 3 Jahren befristet. Hinweis: Damit deine Bewerbung berücksichtigt werden kann, ist es erforderlich, dass du deine vollständigen Bewerbungsunterlagen zusätzlich an Prof. Dr. Alexander Mädche am KIT per E-Mail (alexander.maedche@kit.edu) schickst. Deine Aufgaben mit Perspektiven Du arbeitest an deiner Doktorarbeit im Bereich Agentic Enterprise Systems mit dem Fokus auf Conversational Banking und wirst betreut von Prof. Dr. Alexander Mädche am human-centered systems lab (h-lab) des Instituts für Wirtschaftsinformatik (WIN) am Karlsruher Institut für Technologie (KIT) (https://h-lab.win.kit.edu/). Die Promotion ist primär in der Wirtschaftsinformatik verortet und hat interdisziplinäre Bezüge zu den Disziplinen der Mensch-Computer-Interaktion und der Künstlichen Intelligenz. Du entwickelst innovative Prototypen im Kontext Conversational Banking unter Verwendung von Agentic AI und Knowledge Graphs auf Databricks. Du evaluierst diese Prototypen wissenschaftlich und überführst erfolgreiche Konzepte in den produktiven Einsatz. Du gestaltest Lösungen, die perspektivisch in unsere Data Intelligence Platform sowie unsere Omnikanalplattform integriert werden. Dafür arbeitest du themenbezogen eng mit weiteren Bereichen zusammen, u. a. mit dem Corporate AI Office und der Omnikanalplattform für das Banking. Du engagierst dich in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Forschenden am h-lab des KIT sowie innerhalb der Genossenschaftlichen Finanzgruppe, um innovative Lösungen für Conversational Banking mittels neuer Design-Methodiken zu entwickeln und den Wissenstransfer von der Forschung in die Praxis aktiv zu gestalten. Du präsentierst deine Forschungsergebnisse auf (inter-)nationalen Fachkonferenzen und veröffentlichst in renommierten Journals. Du bist Teil eines agilen, interdisziplinären Teams und gestaltest gemeinsam mit dem h-lab am KIT die Zukunft datengetriebener KI-Lösungen im Banking. Deine Persönlichkeit mit Profil Du hast ein überdurchschnittliches Masterstudium der (Wirtschafts-)Informatik, des Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung abgeschlossen. Du verfügst über fundierte Kenntnisse in Python und SQL sowie erste Erfahrungen in der Entwicklung von Business Intelligence Anwendungen (z. B. Dashboards, Conversational BI). Du kennst dich mit Databricks aus – Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Notebooks, MLflow – bzw. bist bereit, dich hier einzuarbeiten und hast ebenfalls erste Berührungspunkte mit Conversational UIs, Design-Methodiken, LLMs, Agentic-AI-Architekturen oder Knowledge Graph/Semantic-Layer-Konzepten. Du verfügst über verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse (mind. C1) sowie gute bis sehr gute Englischkenntnisse (mind. B2) für Publikationen und die Zusammenarbeit mit dem KIT. Du denkst offen und gleichzeitig konzeptionell und analytisch. Ein starker Forschungsgeist zeichnet dich aus, mit dem du dich kontinuierlich weiterentwickelst. Dabei hast du den produktiven Praxisbezug immer im Blick. Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, teamorientiert und kommunizierst sicher – im agilen Team wie im akademischen Umfeld. Du bist zu regelmäßiger Präsenz in Karlsruhe (voraussichtlich 2 Tage am KIT, 2 Tage bei Atruvia) bereit. Unsere Vorteile auf einen Blick Neben einem attraktiven Tarifgehalt und 30 Tagen Urlaub bieten wir dir folgende Benefits: Flexibles Arbeiten: Wir arbeiten in einem ausgewogenen hybriden Mix aus Remote Work und Anwesenheit in modernen Bürowelten (Activity Based Working). Work-Life-Balance: Mit unseren individuellen Arbeitszeitmodellen wie z. B. Teilzeit, der Wahlmöglichkeit in Vollzeit zwischen 30-40 h und unserem Lebensarbeitszeitkonto (Sabbatical und/oder Freistellung vor Rentenbeginn) findest du den passenden Ausgleich. Vereinbarung von Privatleben und Karriere: Wir bieten dir ein Familienbudget und unterstützen in besonderen familiären Situationen wie z. B. der Pflege von Familienangehörigen. Individuelle Benefits: Neben einer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge (bezuschusste BAV), hast du die Wahl zwischen Bike-Leasing, IT-Hardware-Leasing, vermögenswirksamen Leistungen und/oder einem zusätzlichen Freistellungstag sowie weiteren Optionen. Onboarding: Eine geführte und individuelle Einarbeitung mit Pat*in sowie regelmäßige Feedbackgespräche mit deinem People Lead unterstützen dich bei deinem Ankommen. Zudem begrüßen wir dich bei unserer Willkommensveranstaltung #enter. Gesundheitsmanagement – Health, Family and Life: Mit unseren Angeboten begleiten und unterstützen wir dich u. a. durch Kooperationen mit der Familiengenossenschaft und voiio.
