items.title: Phd
items.desc: Tilburg University | Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences | Department Intelligent Systems (DIS) are looking for a PhD-Researcher and Lecturer (1.0 fte, six years) PhD-Researcher and Lecturer (PhD+) Department Intelligent Systems (DIS) Location: Tilburg Contract size: 1.0 fte (40 hours per week) Full-time gross monthly salary: A minimum gross salary of €3706 per month up to a maximum of € 4599 in the 6th year. For the duration of 12 months, you are entitled to an allowance. The amount is the difference in salary of scale 10 level 0 and scale PR level 0. Contract duration: 12 months, followed by a 5-year contract (after positive assessment) Intended start date: February 1, 2027 Your position The Intelligent Systems (DIS) department at Tilburg University invites applications for a 6-year position. The successful applicant for this position would spend 60% of their time as a PhD student and 40% as a lecturer. The candidate’s educational tasks include leading practical sessions, grading assignments and exams, and (eventually) supervising thesis students. The PhD project would be determined jointly by the successful applicant and the supervision team. The research will broadly focus on the use of artificial intelligence for cybersecurity, targeting applications such as intrusion/vulnerability detection and root-cause analysis. The focus will be on using AI to help human analysts make the right decisions. Please see the homepage of Prof. Sicco Verwer (https://www.tilburguniversity.edu/nl/medewerkers/s-e-verwer) for more information on possible research topics. Your profile Master’s degree in computer science, mathematics, machine learning, cybersecurity, or related field. If you expect to obtain your degree before February 2027, you are also eligible. Knowledge of artificial intelligence, machine learning, data mining, and/or cybersecurity. Excellent knowledge of English and good academic writing skills. Dutch proficiency is preferred but not necessary for the role. Our offer Tilburg University offers excellent benefits in a pleasant working environment: Employment of 1.0 fte (40 hours per week). The selected candidate will receive a contract for 12 months followed by a 5-year contract (after positive assessment). A minimum gross salary of €3706 per month up to a maximum of € 4599 in the 6th year. For the duration of 12 months, you are entitled to an allowance. The amount is the difference in salary of scale 10 level 0 and scale PR level 0. Vacation pay of 8% and a year-end bonus of 8.3%. Over 8 weeks of vacation leave. Hybrid working with home working allowance (€2 p/day) and internet allowance (€25 p/month). Reimbursement sustainable commuting: walking, cycling, and public transport. Options model for additional leave, pension, a bicycle or personal training. Moving allowance (subject to conditions). 30% rule for international employees (if applicable). Pension through ABP. Ample training offer: personal development, leadership, education, research or language courses. Inclusive work culture: everyone welcome, equal opportunities. A green, inviting campus that’s easily accessible by public transport. For more information, please see our website and the CLA Dutch Universities. Want to know more? Would you like to know more before applying? Feel free to contact Prof. Dr. Sicco Verwer (Professor of AI for Cybersecurity), via S.E.Verwer@tilburguniversity.edu, or dr. Drew Hendrickson (Head of Department DIS), via A.Hendrickson@tilburguniversity.edu. Want to apply? We kindly invite you to apply before December 1; this can only be done online . Address your cover letter to Prof. Sicco Verwer and attach your resume. We look forward to your response. The letter selection will take place on December 2. You will be notified as soon as possible thereafter. The first selection interviews will take place in December 2026. The selection committee consists of: Prof. Sicco Verwer, Professor of AI for Cybersecurity, Dept. Intelligent Systems Dr. Peter Hendrix, Academic Director of MSc CSAI and AI & Cybersecurity programs Dr. Görkem Saygili, Track Coordinator for AI & Cybersecurity program You will ideally start working for Tilburg University on February 1, 2027. This vacancy has been published simultaneously internally and externally. In case of equal suitability, our preference is for an internal candidate. It is possible a screening for knowledge security may be considered necessary as part of the evaluation of candidates. About Tilburg University Tilburg University is the university in the humanities and social sciences. Ever since our foundation in 1927, we have been committed to a just, inclusive, and sustainable society. With leading research and inspiring education, we contribute to the interpretation and, where possible, solutions to current societal issues, from climate change to digitalization Our community is personal, engaged, and small-scale. On our green, compact, and vibrant campus there is room for encounter, collaboration, reflection, and personal growth. Read more about Tilburg University. Working at Tilburg University means working in an inclusive team with attractive employment conditions. At Tilburg University, you will receive ample opportunities to strengthen your talents and develop your career, in a warm working atmosphere where we attach great importance to the following values: curious, connected, caring, and courageous. About the Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences (TSHD) Research and education at the Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences (TSHD) focuses on humans, technology, culture, and their interactions in a globalizing digital society. From the interplay of our disciplines, our research and education focuses on the development of artificial intelligence and interactive technologies, their influence on communication, culture and society, and moral and existential challenges that arise. The School of Humanities and Digital Sciences consists of six Departments: Communication and Cognition, Computational Cognitive Science, Intelligent Systems, Culture Studies, Philosophy, and the Tilburg Center of the Learning Sciences. Collaboration across disciplines is encouraged among both researchers and students. With this approach, we nurture a way of thinking that takes into account different perspectives and the diverse, sometimes conflicting needs and interests of people and society. At TSHD, we foster a culture of integrity, trust, diversity and inclusion, and constructive and critical dialogue. All members of our community are recognized and valued for their unique contributions. University College Tilburg, with its interdisciplinary Liberal Articles and Sciences program, holds a unique position within the School. This collaboration with other Schools also includes the disciplines of economics, law, and the social sciences. Read more about the Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences (TSHD). About the Research Center for Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence The Research Center for Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence at Tilburg University is part of the Tilburg School of Humanities and Digital Sciences. The center consists of reseachers from two departments, Intelligent Systems and Computational Cognitive Science. The group is responsible for the Bachelor and the Master program Cognitive Science & Artificial Intelligence, the master track on AI & Cybersecurity, is co-responsible for the university-wide data science Master program Data Science & Society, and is affiliated with the Jheronimus Academy of Data Science (http://www.jads.nl). Researchers in the Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence center have access to computer clusters, experimental lab facilities, and the virtual and mixed reality DAF Technology Lab and its sensing technologies (https://www.tilburguniversity.edu/campus/experiencing-virtual-reality/ ). Moreover, researchers play an important role in Mind Labs (http://www.mind-labs.eu ), an initiative that fosters collaborations between knowledge institutions and corporations in the field of interactive technologies and behavior.

items.title: PhD Position in Accountable and Responsible AI
items.desc: Are you eager to conduct high-impact research spanning computer science, economics, law, and the creative industry—while living in Amsterdam, a dynamic city renowned for its high-quality life and its thriving AI and creative sectors? Working at the UvA Join Us! A fully funded four-year Ph.D. position is available in the Complex Cyber Infrastructure research group at the University of Amsterdam. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) becomes deeply embedded in our society, the urgency to warrant its responsible and accountable use is increasing. Examples include the control that creative industry actors need to manifest when using AI pipelines in the (moving) image industry. This PhD project aims to focus on the emerging field of Accountable and Responsible AI, with the goal of advancing knowledge and practice at the intersection of AI research, creative industry practices, and societal regulatory expectations. Two projects underpin this position: SafeGenAI – a creative industry endeavour to enable creative industry actors to safely use GenAI tools; and LLM4LM – a large consortium addressing the legal-tech challenges in cross-organisational multi-domain agentic solutions. The candidate will not only have a chance to contribute to shaping the next generation AI systems within the creative industry and logistics practices, but also potentially to design more transparent, fair, and compliant ones with evolving societal and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will be embedded in a team that will help transfer fundamental research results into the creative industry and legal practices, respectively. Moreover, they will be working closely with the supervision team, as well as the other PhD students and postdocs in the research group. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do In this context, you will investigate the following key challenges: Opacity in GenAI inferencing: How can the inferencing and reasoning processes of GenAI systems be made sufficiently transparent and traceable to support accountability in high-stakes professional contexts? AI legal compliance-by-design: How can GenAI systems be built to satisfy the requirements of the regulations such as the EU AI Act — including transparency, human oversight, and risk management — while remaining practically useful in domain-specific workflows? SMEs lack the expertise to navigate complex regulatory environments: How can domain-specific structured knowledge be integrated into GenAI systems to ground their outputs, reduce hallucination, and support trustworthy decision for non-expert users? What We Ask Of You Your experience and profile: MSc in CS, AI or a closely related field. Strong interest in Interest in finance and financial services is a plus.; previous experience in these fields is a plus. Enthusiasm for the research process: studying research papers, solving complex problems, applying creative thinking, evaluation, reflection and disseminating findings via writing and oral presentations. The ability to critically analyse abstract models as well as concrete implementations. The ability to work individually as well as effectively in a team Fluency in written and spoken English This Is What We Offer You A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 18 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is as soon as possible. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3,204 to € 4,051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile PhD Candidate is applicable.. A favourable tax agreement, the ‘30% ruling’, may apply to non-Dutch applicants. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. We also have an extensive secondary benefits package. Your place at the UvA You will work in this team The Faculty of Science has a student body of around 8,000, as well as 1,800 members of staff working in education, research or support services. Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, be it elementary particles, the birth of the universe or the functioning of the brain. The mission of the Informatics Institute (IvI) is to perform curiosity-driven and use-inspired fundamental research in Computer Science. The main research themes are Artificial Intelligence, Computational Science and Systems and Network Engineering. Our research involves complex information systems at large, with a focus on collaborative, data driven, computational and intelligent systems, all with a strong interactive component. The Complex Cyber Infrastructure (CCI) group is part of the Informatics Institute at the University of Amsterdam. CCI focuses on the complexity of human-made systems on all scales. Cyber Infrastructure is rapidly evolving from relatively simple fixed components to programmable and virtualized objects with many degrees of freedom, owned, operated and governed by different entities in multiple administrative domains interacting on the Internet. Harnessing this complexity in a transparent, trustable way for safe and secure data processing is a major research topic that defines the focus of CCI research. The challenges are addressed by combining methods and results from research into sustainable and sovereign distributed data processing, programmable networks, policy reasoning and normative control, and software (language) engineering. Want to know more about our organisation? Read more about working at the University of Amsterdam. About The Faculty Of Science Researchers and students at the Faculty of Science are fascinated by every aspect of how the world works, whether it concerns elementary particles, the birth of the universe, or how the brain functions. The Faculty has a student population of approximately 8,000 students, as well as 1,800 staff members working in education, research, or support services. Important to know Your application & contact If you feel the profile fits you, and you are interested in the job, we look forward to receiving your application. You can apply online via the red button. We accept applications until and including 15 November 2026. We plan to organise multiple rounds of interviews. Therefore, due to time sensitivity the vacancy will be closed if a suitable candidate is selected before 15 November 2026. Applications should include the following information (all files besides your cv should be submitted in one single pdf file): a detailed CV including the months (not just years) when referring to your education and work experience; a letter of motivation; a list of publications; the names and email addresses of two references who can provide letters of recommendation. A knowledge security check can be part of the selection procedure. (for details: national knowledge security guidelines). Only complete applications received within the response period via the link below will be considered. If you have any questions or do you require additional information? Please contact: Dr. Ana Oprescu, Assistant Professor Complex Cyber Infrastructure, a.m.oprescu@uva.nl Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. Diversity, Equity & Inclusion As an employer, the UvA maintains an equal opportunities policy. We value diversity and are fully committed to being a place where everyone feels at home. We nurture inquisitive minds and perseverance and allow room for persistent questioning. With us, curiosity and creativity are the prevailing culture. Studies show that women and members of underrepresented groups only apply for jobs if they meet 100% of the qualifications. Do you meet the educational requirements but not yet all of the requested experience? The UvA encourages you to apply anyway.

items.title: Professional Doctorate Candidate in the maritime field (Practice Based Research Promovendus)
items.desc: Location Amsterdam Salary € 4.427,- to € 6.677,- Employment 32 – 40 hours Contract Temporary 1 year contract, with extension option of 3 years to finalise the professional doctorate time-frame In the maritime sector, there is a need for academic and more practice-based research to reinforce each other to make the sector safer and more sustainable. Technological solutions are offered from academia. However, without a deep understanding of the everyday practice of the sector, there might be doubt that the full potential of these developments can be realised. The Professional Doctorate-program can bridge this gap by making knowledge practically applicable. The Professional Doctorate is the practice-oriented equivalent of PhD tracks at universities where the candidate conducts research at a university of applied sciences at the highest level. We are looking for candidates who recognise themselves in one or more of the following profiles: Managers and senior professionals working in private/public organisations in the maritime domain. Academic staff working at universities of applied sciences/ universities looking for a further step in their research career. Where else than at AUAS … Can you research predictive maintenance from a financial, environmental and operational perspective Are you making a contribution to a safer and more sustainable sector by combining academic and practice-based research Do you have the opportunity to work in a practice-oriented equivalent of University PhD tracks at a university of applied sciences, in Amsterdam Do you want to know if this job is right for you? Call or send a WhatsApp message to Konstantinos Stamoulis, Professor Aviation Engineering, 06- 21155138 or Hubert Schaafsma, Maritime Studies, 06- 11719290 and get in touch! Here's How You Will Make a Difference You conduct practice-oriented research that contributes to the sustainability, safety and competitiveness of the maritime sector. In particular our group is engaged in multiple (inter-) national research projects which include the topic of predictive maintenance. In such an approach, maintenance takes place when it is beneficial from a financial, environmental and operational perspective. During your Professional Doctorate route you follow support courses to further develop yourself and your research skills. As a member of our multidisciplinary team you are supervised by a professor and fellow researchers. Your Other Perks A gross monthly salary between € 4.427,- and € 6.677,- (VSNU profile Researcher 3 scale 11), based on a full-time appointment and depending on education and experience. An end-of-year bonus of 8.3% and holiday allowance of 8% of your gross annual salary. 10.7 holiday weeks per year with a 40-hour working week. Entitlement to various types of leave, such as (un)paid parental leave, care leave, adoption and foster care leave and various other arrangements. A travel allowance for your commute, an NS-Business Card, your own AUAS bicycle or a tax incentive to purchase your own bicycle. If you are unable to use personal or public transport to travel to work, e.g. because of a disability, we will explore alternate possibilities together. Plenty of development opportunities, e.g. via our own AUAS Academy. Discounts on various facilities, such as books, cultural courses, soft- and hardware and a number of insurances. A strong focus on your job satisfaction, work-life balance and vitality. For example, you can participate in various sports activities for AUAS staff or via the USC sport centre. You can also visit our (career) coaches and use various online tools to benefit your mental health. A good pension scheme via the ABP pension fund. A monthly internet allowance, a laptop and smartphone on loan. Last but not least: a chance to work in a dynamic and pleasant environment with wonderful colleagues. You and your colleagues can also get together outside work, e.g. in one of our communities such as HvA Alumni, HvA United, JongHvA and FEM IT. Have a look at our employment conditions here and learn more about the tailor-made opportunities we offer. What You Bring To The Table At AUAS, no two employees are the same. No matter who you are, you are sure to be a valuable addition to our team. You are independent, persistant, curious, have a collaborative spirit and a drive to improve practice. You also possess: A completed university (or university of applied sciences) master’s degree in the maritime/naval engineering field or in another relevant field, e.g. mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, computer science, or similar with a research topic relevant for this project; Demonstrable coding skills, preferably in Python and affinity with statistics and data-driven modelling; Affinity with machine learning, preferably in the field of prognostics and health management (PHM), with experience working with time-series data is highly desirable. Prior industrial experience in maintenance and repair, preferably in the maritime/aerospace domain is a plus; A demonstrable good command of the English language (at least level C1). Dutch is a plus; Demonstrable research and publication experience is a plus. Become our new Professional Doctorate Candidate in the maritime field: Upload your CV and letter of motivation via the application button. We will get back to you within two to three weeks, so keep an eye on your inbox. For more information about the application procedure, you can send an email to vacatures@hva.nl. We apply the AUAS Job Application Code to this vacancy’s recruitment and selection process. No (recruitment) agencies please. Creating tomorrow at the Faculty of Technology At the Faculty of Technology, students, teachers, researchers and external partners work intensively together on current issues in society. Consider challenges such as the climate, sustainability, housing shortage, transport and health. Together with our partners, our education and research makes a substantial contribution to technical and technological solutions for social issues of today and the future. All our employees contribute to this from their own expertise and thus literally lay the foundation for the developments of tomorrow!

items.title: PhD in Energy-Efficient Sensors and Computing Hardware from 2D Materials
items.desc: Introduction Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region. Job Description In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware. What You'll Contribute To Specifically, you will: develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities; optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration; develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors; engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance; characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance; publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences; supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects. Your research environment You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab (NanoComputing Research Lab), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities. What we're looking for A master’s degree in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field, with a solid foundation in semiconductor materials and device physics, and prior experience in the growth of nanomaterials (preferably 2D materials using CVD), nanofabrication processes such as atomic layer deposition, lithography, etching etc., and 2D material transfer process. Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field. A research-oriented attitude. Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and mentor bachelor/master’s students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). items.title: PhD Position in Foil Drone
items.desc: Pioneering the future of maritime surveillance? Join as a PHD to research and advance autonomous, wind-powered drones, featuring tethered hydrofoils for indefinite ocean monitoring. Job Description Are you ready to shape the future of autonomous maritime security? We are looking for a highly motivated and talented PhD Candidate to spearhead advanced research on the FoilDrone system—an innovative, future-proof maritime surveillance concept. Project Context & Mission Maritime domain awareness is a critical global priority. Traditional surveillance options face major trade-offs: airborne drones offer high speed but suffer from critically low endurance (6 to 22 hours), while unmanned surface vessels (like the Saildrone) boast long endurance but travel at very low speeds (3 to 5 knots) and cannot see over the horizon. The FoilDrone system bridges this market gap by combining an aerial Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) rotating-wing sailplane with a submerged, tethered hydrofoil. completely eliminating propulsion power consumption during operations. Key Responsibilities & Research Focus As a PhD candidate, you will take ownership of the next phase of FoilDrone research. You will take the design from conceptual idea towards physical implementation through independent research, simulation and experimentation. Your core duties will include: Advanced Multi-Body Dynamics & Control: Deepen and expand simulation models linking the aerial vehicle to the submerged hydrofoil via a flexible tether. Refine independent controllers to ensure stability during critical transitions (transit, deployment, sailing, and recovery). Aerodynamic & Hydrodynamic Optimization: Investigate the complex interactions of fixed wing drone, cabels, and hydrofoils. Optimize aerodynamic and hydrodynamic efficiencies across varying sea states and wind disturbances. Experimental Validation: Translate theoretical models into physical hardware. Collaborate with technical staff and student teams to design wind-tunnel experiments, tow-tank tests, and open-water flight trials to validate structural integrity, deployment mechanisms, and control strategies. Academic Contribution: Publish high-impact scientific papers in leading international journals, present findings at global aerospace and marine conferences, and assist in supervising Master's and Bachelor's student thesis projects. What We Offer A fully funded, multi-year PhD position within a world-leading aerospace research environment. Access to state-of-the-art simulation tools, testing facilities, and prototyping equipment. Opportunities to collaborate closely with pioneers in UAV technology, maritime sensors, and renewable energy systems. A vibrant, international, and inspiring workplace dedicated to creating innovative drone solutions that work in the real world. If you are eager to push the boundaries of aerial-marine robotics and make a tangible impact on global maritime safety, we invite you to submit your application Job Requirements Educational Background: Hold a Master of Science degree in Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, Control Systems, or a closely related discipline. Technical Expertise: Strong background in flight dynamics, multi-body system modeling, guidance, navigation, and control (GNC). Simulation Skills: Demonstrated proficiency in numerical simulation environments (such as MATLAB/Simulink, Python) for aerial or underwater systems. Research Drive: Passion for academic research, experimental verification, and autonomous systems, with a proven ability to publish findings in peer-reviewed journals. Collaboration & Communication: Excellent English written and verbal communication skills, with a collaborative mindset to work alongside interdisciplinary academic and industrial partners. Practical Experience: Demonstrated hands-on experience in building, assembling, or maintaining (fixed-wing) unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and/or marine hydrofoil systems, including composite manufacturing and mechanical integration. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Aerospace Engineering The Faculty of Aerospace Engineering at Delft University of Technology is a leading international community where innovation in aerospace meets global challenges. Our support and scientific staff, including PhD candidates, postdocs, and students, largely work together on three main themes: the energy transition, sustainable aerospace, and safety and security, with the aim of tackling climate change and contributing to the independence and security of Europe. When you join us, you become part of a diverse, collaborative, and forward-thinking environment where your ideas and perspectives are valued. Our work extends beyond the lab—into field labs, innovation hubs, and partnerships with other faculties, research institutes, governments, and industry, both locally and globally. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and welcoming workplace, assisted by an active Diversity & Inclusion team. This includes tangible support such as funding for extra personnel for family and caregiving responsibilities, mentoring programmes, and initiatives that promote cultural exchange and integration. You don’t just join our faculty — you join a community where you can thrive, grow, and help shape the future of aerospace. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Aerospace Engineering. items.title: PhD in AI enabled prediction of pollen season magnitude for next generation forecasting
items.desc: Some features of our web site require JavaScript to function properly. Please enable JavaScript in your browser. Position PhD in AI enabled prediction of pollen season magnitude for next generation forecasting Employer University of Birmingham Birmingham - research that matters At Birmingham, you’re free to pursue your own independent research, while building the skills and confidence to make an impact on global society. A platform for significant, pioneering research, Birmingham is a hub for innovation, delivery and academic rigour. We focus on global issues, with a collaborative, cross-disciplinary culture. Combined with modern facilities and academic expertise, it’s an approach that shapes and inspires all our teaching, creating and learning. Homepage: https://www.birmingham.ac.uk Location Birmingham, United Kingdom Sector Academic Relevant divisions Atmospheric Sciences (AS) Biogeosciences (BG) Type Full time Level Student / Graduate / Internship Salary A fully funded 3.5-year PhD studentship, including a tax-free stipend at the UKRI rate (currently £21,805 per year for 2026/27), tuition fees, and £8,000 for research and training. International applicants are eligible to apply, with international tuition Preferred Education Master Application deadline 6 January 2027 Posted 19 October 2026 Job Description PROJECT HIGHLIGHTS Work directly with the UK Met Office on next-generation operational pollen forecasting Develop novel AI and machine-learning methods to predict pollen season magnitude months in advance Join an interdisciplinary team spanning environmental science, mathematics and artificial intelligence Overview Understanding and forecasting airborne pollen is essential for improving operational environmental prediction across the UK. While daily pollen forecasts have improved substantially in recent years, one of the greatest remaining challenges is predicting the overall magnitude of each pollen season. For example, total birch pollen concentrations can vary by a factor of eight between consecutive years, driven by complex interactions between previous-season pollen production, meteorological conditions during the preceding summer, and weather during the flowering season itself. These processes remain poorly understood and are not currently represented within operational forecasting systems. This project will harness a unique UK-wide pollen reanalysis (2000–2025), developed by the UK Met Office under the stewardship of Co-I Lucy Neal, together with long-term pollen observations and meteorological datasets, to develop next-generation machine learning approaches for predicting seasonal pollen magnitude. The resulting models will improve understanding of the environmental drivers of interannual variability while providing practical tools to enhance the operational Met Office NAME pollen forecast. With only 8 active regulatory-grade pollen monitoring sites across the UK, equivalent to approximately one site per eight million people, long-term pollen observations are extremely sparse. The pollen reanalysis provides an unprecedented spatially and temporally complete dataset for developing and validating artificial intelligence methods. The student will investigate how biological memory, antecedent weather conditions and environmental variables combine to determine pollen production, developing interpretable machine learning models capable of predicting seasonal severity months in advance. This PhD will be embedded in a vibrant interdisciplinary research environment at the University of Birmingham, combining expertise in environmental science, artificial intelligence and applied mathematics. Joint supervision from Environmental Sciences, the School of Mathematics, and the UK Met Office will provide outstanding training in machine learning, environmental modelling and operational forecasting. The research will directly address a major limitation in current pollen forecasting systems, delivering new scientific understanding alongside AI tools with clear operational impact for the UK Met Office and wider environmental forecasting community. items.title: Doktorand i produktionsutveckling med inriktning mot laserbaserade slitbeläggningar
items.desc: Vill du utveckla slitstarka material som minskar industrins beroende av volfram? Forsknings-ämnet produktionsutveckling vid Luleå tekniska universitet söker en doktorand till projektet Gröna karbider. Du kommer att arbeta med laserbaserad beläggning och experimentell processutveckling, från pulver till utvärderad beläggning, i en forskargrupp med kompetens inom laserteknik, pulverframställning och materialkarakterisering. Ämnet ingår i avdelningen produkt- och produktionsutveckling vid institutionen för teknikvetenskap och matematik. Här får du arbeta i en internationell forskningsmiljö med tillgång till laserlaboratorium och dialog med industrin. Läs mer om forskningsämnet produktionsutveckling Ämnesbeskrivning Produktionsutveckling omfattar såväl enskilda processer och tekniker för tillverkning, som utformning av hela system för industriell produktion. Ett viktigt område är laserbearbetning. Projektbeskrivning Gröna karbider utvecklar volframreducerade slitmaterial som alternativ till gjuten volframkarbid, cast tungsten carbide (CTC), för stål- och gruvindustrin. Målet är att utveckla och demonstrera minst tre material med mekaniska egenskaper jämförbara med CTC. Projektet omfattar materialdesign, framställning av sfäriska pulver genom atomisering, laserbeläggning på stål samt utvärdering av egenskaper och cirkularitetspotential. Doktorandarbetets tyngdpunkt ligger på sambanden mellan pulvrets egenskaper, beläggnings-processens parametrar och den färdiga beläggningens mikrostruktur och slitprestanda. Du arbetar tillsammans med forskare inom produktionsutveckling och materialteknik. Arbetsuppgifter Arbetet omfattar experimentell forskning och analys med stöd av relevant teori. Du kommer framför allt att: Planera och genomföra laserbaserad pulverbeläggning på stål samt undersöka hur lasereffekt, bearbetningshastighet och pulvertillförsel påverkar resultatet. Utveckla och anpassa försöksuppställningar, pulvertillförsel och rörelsebanor samt använda processövervakning för att förstå och förbättra processen. Medverka i pulverframställning och pulverkarakterisering samt utvärdera beläggningarnas mikrostruktur, fasbildning, bindning mot substratet, hårdhet och nötningsmotstånd. Analysera och dokumentera försöksresultat, bidra till projektets hållbarhetsbedömningar och presentera resultat i vetenskapliga publikationer och vid konferenser och industridialoger. I forskarutbildningen ingår även doktorandkurser och arbete med doktorsavhandlingen. Under-visning och annan institutionstjänstgöring kan ingå. Kvalifikationer Grundläggande behörighet har den som har avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, fullgjort minst 240 högskolepoäng varav minst 60 på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Därutöver ska kraven på särskild behörighet i den allmänna studieplanen för produktionsutveckling vara uppfyllda. Relevant utbildningsbakgrund är civilingenjörs- eller masterutbildning inom maskinteknik, produktionsteknik, materialvetenskap, fysik eller ett närliggande tekniskt område, alternativt en utländsk utbildning som bedöms motsvara behörighetskraven. För arbetet krävs god förmåga att kommunicera på engelska i tal och skrift. Du ska kunna arbeta systematiskt med tekniska frågeställningar, analysera resultat och dokumentera ditt arbete. Du behöver kunna ta ansvar för egna uppgifter och samarbeta i en forskargrupp. Meriterande erfarenheter: Experimentellt arbete med laserbaserad metallbearbetning, särskilt pulverbaserad Directed Energy Deposition (DED) eller laser cladding. Utveckling av försöksuppställningar och systematisk parameteroptimering inom tillverkningsteknik. Processövervakning och analys av mätdata, exempelvis med höghastighetsfilmning, termografi eller pyrometri. Robot- eller CNC-programmering för tillverkningsprocesser. Pulverhantering, jämförelse av pulveregenskaper eller utvärdering av återanvänt pulver. Materialkarakterisering, metallografi eller mekanisk provning av metaller eller slitbeläggningar. Urvalet görs med hänsyn till förmågan att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildningen, enligt den allmänna studieplanen. Vid bedömningen av projektanknutna meriter läggs särskild vikt vid dokumenterad experimentell erfarenhet av laserbaserad metallbearbetning och processutveckling. Erfarenhet från examensarbete, praktik och anställning kan beaktas. Du behöver inte ha samtliga meriterande erfarenheter För ytterligare information om specifik doktorandutbildning se studieplaner för forskarutbildning inom teknisk fakultet Information Anställning som doktorand är tidsbegränsad på 4 år, undervisning och annan institutionstjänstgöring kan tillkomma upp till 20 % av heltid. Tjänstgöringsort: Luleå. Tillträde: 1 januari 2027. För varje tjänst anges ett preliminärt lönespann som baseras på befattningens krav, ansvar och marknadsläge. För ytterligare information är du välkommen att kontakta Professor Johanne Mouzon, 0920-49 1960, johanne.mouzon@ltu.se Fackliga kontaktpersoner Ansökan Vi ser helst att du söker befattningen via ansökningsknappen nedan där du bifogar personligt brev samt CV/meritförteckning och kopior av verifierade examensbevis. Var vänlig och märk din ansökan med referensnumret nedan. Både ansökan och examensbevis ska vara skrivna på svenska eller engelska. Sista ansökningsdag: 9 november, 2026 Referensnummer: 5143-2026

items.title: SD-25045 – DOCTORAL RESEARCHER - IN HONG-OU-MANDEL INTERFERENCE AND ENTANGLEMENT WITH COLOUR CENTRES IN SILICON CARBIDE
items.desc: Temporary contract | 14+22(+12) months | Belval Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a Research and Technology Organization (RTO) active in the fields of materials, environment and IT. By transforming scientific knowledge into technologies, smart data and tools, LIST empowers citizens in their choices, public authorities in their decisions and businesses in their strategies. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? You will be part of the LIST Materials Research and Technology department, where you will carry out your work in the Quantum Materials Group, led by Dr. Florian Kaiser. Quantum technologies have the potential to revolutionise the world in many aspects. Quantum colour centres in in wide bandgap semiconductors have recently emerged as a promising platform, since they can incorporate quantum systems, which can be scaled up by industrial processing. Along these lines, we have recently shown that individual colour centres can be integrated into silicon carbide nanophotonic waveguides with little-to-no degradation of spin-optical coherences. These finding define the strategy for developing a scalable quantum technology architecture. Our strategy is to use multiplexed and integrated colour centres for quantum communication tasks. Key here is to generate entanglement between colour centres based on spin-photon entanglement, as well as Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. With this milestone demonstration, we strive to kickstart subsequent developments towards a quantum internet architecture. The objective of this PhD thesis is to support our work towards optical interference between colour centres, i.e., Hong-Ou-Mandel interference. The initial part of this thesis comprises setting up our new optical cryostat platform, which is based on a combination of standard confocal microscopy, and interferometry. In the second step, you will benefit from our ongoing activities towards quantum photonic silicon carbide chips in which we generate colour centres in fibre-coupled waveguides. You will determine the ideal pulsed excitation schemes for colour centres, considering spectral, temporal and polarization filtering. Subsequently, you will characterise the photon quality depending on experimental parameters, and implement initial two-photon inteference experiments outside of the cryostat, followed by a fully-on-chip demonstration inside the cryostat. If time permits, this project can be further extended to the generation of entanglement between two colour centre chips located in two different cryostats. Is Your profile described below? items.title: PhD Candidate in Modelling Marine Larval Dispersal and Spatial Population Genetics and Demography
items.desc: About The Position A fully-funded PhD position in modelling marine larval dispersal and spatial population genetics and demography is available at the Department of Biology, Norwegian University of Science & Technology (NTNU) under the supervision of Associate Professor Scott Burgess. NTNU’s Department of Biology hosts internationally leading research activity in ecology, evolutionary biology, physiology, marine science and technology, and cell & molecular biology. As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. About The Project The PhD position is aligned with a research program that has the overall aim of providing new understanding of the processes that affect marine larval dispersal and gene flow, how we measure it with genetic data, and how we use that information to predict the genetic and demographic responses of spatially structured marine populations to environmental variation and change. Specifically, the primary focus of the PhD will be to understand how complex coastlines, ocean circulation, and biology (e.g., reproductive systems and phenology, larval behavior and survival) interact to affect the spatial structure of the genetic and demographic properties of marine populations. There is flexibility, and an expectation, for candidates to develop their own line of research within this broad scope. For example, projects could focus on combining simulations using spatial-genetic-demographic individual based models (e.g., using the software SLiM), machine learning approaches, and genomic data to estimate larval dispersal distances from the spatial structure of genetic genealogies across the genome, and the genetic relatedness among individuals; or develop and use biophysical models (hydrodynamics + particle tracking) to understand the demographic and genetic dynamics of marine metapopulations and adaptation to environmental change. The PhD position provides an exciting opportunity to gain broad experience and expertise working at the interface of population genetics and demography, oceanography, and computer science. It will provide broad training in research skills, and will suit a candidate who is curious and is motivated to undertake high-level research to gain skills in computational methods and software tools to understand large, complex biological data. The position will be hosted within a dynamic international research group based at NTNU, with strong links to local and international collaborators. There will be opportunities for conference and workshop participation. The project supervisor will be Associate Professor Scott C. Burgess (Department of Biology, NTNU). Your immediate leader will be the head of department. Duties of the position Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate. Learn and apply advanced statistical and computational methods to analyze genetic data generated from simulations, outputs from biophysical models, or empirical genomic data to answer questions in spatial population genetics and marine metapopulation dynamics. items.title: PhD position (all genders) in Computational Neuroscience and NeuroAI
items.desc: Main tasks Over the past decades, neuroscience has made remarkable progress in characterizing the architecture of biological neural networks. We now possess increasingly detailed descriptions of synaptic connectivity, cellular composition, laminar organization, mesoscale topology, and large-scale connectomes across multiple species. Across these diverse levels of organization, common structural principles have begun to emerge, including modularity, core-periphery organization, asymmetric reciprocity, and multi-scale network organization. Yet, despite this wealth of anatomical knowledge, a fundamental question remains unresolved: how do these structural features shape neural computation? Which aspects of biological connectivity are essential for flexible, robust, and adaptive information processing, and which are simply byproducts of development or evolution? This PhD project aims to bridge this gap by combining computational and network neuroscience with artificial intelligence to investigate how biologically inspired connectivity principles influence computation in recurrent neural networks. Research Environment The Institute of Computational Neuroscience is a small, active and internationally diverse group working at the interface of computational neuroscience, network science, neuro-inspired artificial intelligence and clinical neuroscience. The successful candidate will be jointly supervised by Prof. Claus C. Hilgetag and Dr. Fatemeh Hadaeghi. About The Project A central methodological framework will be recurrent neural networks and reservoir computing models. Our goal is to uncover how biological wiring and functional organization can inform artificial neural network design and to translate these insights into models that operate effectively with low-precision (binary or ternary) weights. Main Aims Are To Explore bio-inspired backbones for unimodal temporal learning Develop modular and core-periphery architectures for multimodal learning Explore Scalability and real-world application. The work will involve close interaction with a strong computational and network neuroscience team at our institute. The position provides substantial scope for scientific initiative and intellectual ownership. The successful candidate may also contribute to the development of related research proposals and future funding applications. The position is funded through third-party research funding, comprises 65% of the regular weekly working hours, and provides the opportunity for obtaining the academic qualification of a PhD. Your Profile Master’s degree or equivalent qualification by the starting date in a relevant field such as computational neuroscience, computer science, physics, mathematics, biomedical engineering or a related quantitative discipline Independent scientific thinking and productivity The ability and interest to understand complex mathematical or computational concepts Fluent written and spoken English, enabling full participation in scientific discussions, presentations and academic writing Prior experience with recurrent neural networks (RNNs), including reservoir computing or state space models, is advantageous Strong analytical and computational skills, including proficiency in Python; Prior practical experience in areas directly related to the project is advantageous Scientific initiative, quantitative aptitude and willingness to learn (Evidence of scientific independence may include an ambitious Master’s project, publications or preprints, conference contributions, contributions to scientific software, open-source work or other substantial independent research activity.) Please explain: what scientific or technical question you addressed what your own contribution was what difficulties you encountered and how you dealt with them what the project ultimately produced or taught you This description is intended to help us understand how you approach scientific problems and how much intellectual ownership you have taken in previous work. items.title: PhD Candidate in Cybersecurity Challenges in Maritime AI
items.desc: About The Position Digitalization and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming society, and the integration of AI into the maritime industry represents a digital shift that will redefine today’s operations. The maritime industry is increasingly embracing AI, enabling a broad digital transformation. At the same time, the use of AI introduce new cybersecurity challenges that need to be understood and addressed to enable secure and trustworthy AI technology. This PhD project will investigate cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain. The project will have an interdisciplinary approach, combining insights from information security, artificial intelligence, maritime operations, and data engineering. The research may address cybersecurity risks related to the data used to develop AI models, the models themselves, or their integration and use in maritime applications. Relevant research topics may include cybersecurity risks related to training data and AI models, data poisoning and manipulation, privacy and confidentiality, secure data sharing, and methods for assessing the security and trustworthiness of maritime AI technology. The specific research questions and methodological approach will be further developed based on the candidate’s background and interests, relevant maritime AI use cases, and collaboration with industry partners. This position offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of cybersecurity, AI, and maritime operations in close collaboration with academic and industrial partners. The research is expected to contribute new knowledge and approaches for understanding and addressing cybersecurity challenges associated with the development and use of AI in the maritime domain. Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. About The Project The candidate will work in a multidisciplinary research environment located at the heart of the maritime industry in Ålesund. Working at the NTNU department of ICT and Natural Sciences ensures close contact with the industry and research communities. The PhD project will be part of the Norwegian Maritime AI Center that aims to accelerate operationalization of AI in the maritime value chains. The center shall position the maritime sector for accelerated and successful use of AI. The demand for safe and sustainable maritime activities, as well as the shortage of crew and engineers, are key drivers for change in the maritime sector. At the same time, there is a pull for growth, increased efficiency and profitability, while managing volatility in the markets. Moreover, the sector is critically important for global supply chains and security in a tense geopolitical situation. To demonstrate and prototype maritime AI solutions, the center will address a diverse and impactful set of use cases: Logistics, shipping and business transactions; Ship design and construction; Voyage planning and optimization; Condition monitoring and maintenance; Crew training; Maritime traffic and ship surveillance; Decarbonization and energy management; Autonomous ships and remote control. The research partners are the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), University of Oslo, Oslo School of Architecture and Design, Royal Norwegian Naval Academy, Norwegian Mapping Authority, MET and SINTEF Nordvest. There are about 30 user partners from the maritime sector, in addition to hundreds of members of the Maritime Forum, Blue Maritime, Ocean Autonomy, and Maritime CleanTech clusters. The center will be a hub, orchestrating the interfaces with research partners and user partners to facilitate collaboration, knowledge creation, dissemination, innovation, and sharing of knowledge. The Norwegian Maritime AI Center is funded by the Research Council of Norway and the partners for the period 2026-2030. items.title: PhD Position – Linking Above-Ground Plant Function to Root Dynamics
items.desc: Plant roots are essential for water and nutrient acquisition and play a key role in how crops respond to environmental stress. Yet, because roots are hidden in the soil, their development and activity remain difficult to observe – particularly under field conditions. Advances in plant phenotyping, on the other hand, allow us to characterize above- and belowground plant structure and function with increasing temporal resolution. Physiological measurements provide information about photosynthetic carbon assimilation, while sensor-based phenotyping captures dynamic changes in plant growth and stress responses. To what extent can available above-ground traits be related to root structure and function? At the Institute of Bio- and Geosciences – Plant Sciences (IBG-2) at Forschungszentrum Jülich, we are looking for a doctoral researcher to address this question within the PhenoRob – Robotics and Phenotyping for Sustainable Crop Production – research environment. Your Job The aim of your PhD project is to relate root dynamics to above-ground physiological and phenotypical measures and traits. You will investigate how photosynthesis, carbon allocation, shoot development and root growth are connected over time and how these relationships change in response to environmental conditions. To achieve this, you will combine experiments done under controlled conditions with field experiments. Complementary experiments will provide direct and non-invasive information about shoot and root structure and function. Using advanced imaging approaches such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET), you will follow root development and physiological processes over space and time. Together with measurements of photosynthetic performance, these experiments will help reveal how carbon assimilation and allocation are related to source-sink dynamics and subsequent root and shoot growth. By combining these complementary datasets, you will investigate whether measurable changes above ground can serve as indicators – and ultimately predictors – of dynamic processes in the hidden root system. Your tasks will include: Design and conduct plant experiments under controlled and field conditions Quantify temporal changes in plant structure and function using non-invasive approaches Investigate relationships between photosynthetic carbon assimilation, carbon allocation, and subsequent root and shoot growth Develop quantitative approaches to relate root development and stress responses to above-ground measurements Contribute experimental data to the parameterisation and validation of functional-structural plant models Present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed scientific journals The project will be highly collaborative and will connect expertise in plant physiology, root biology, phenotyping, sensing, imaging, data analysis and plant modelling within IBG-2 and the interdisciplinary PhenoRob research environment. Your Profile We are looking for a highly motivated candidate who combines scientific curiosity with an interest in experimental and quantitative plant science. Excellent Master's degree in plant sciences, biology, agricultural sciences, crop science, environmental sciences, bioengineering or a related discipline Motivation to combine controlled experiments with field-based plant research Interest in linking physiological processes with imaging and sensor-derived plant traits Experience in quantitative data analysis and statistics Experience with R, Python or comparable tools is advantageous Very good command of written and spoken English is required (at least B2 level according to the CEFR ), ideally supported by a certificate confirming the language level Experience with photosynthesis measurements, root phenotyping, plant imaging, MRI, PET, field phenotyping, remote sensing, image analysis, machine learning or plant modelling is an advantage, but not a prerequisite. items.title: PhD Position in Decoding Environmental History from Microorganisms for Living Sensors and Memory
items.desc: Help pave the future for living sensing systems by decoding microorganisms' encoding of environmental history. Job Description Background: Living microorganisms could transform how we sense and store information, replacing single-use electronics with inherently biodegradable systems that track environmental conditions over time. Even basic electronic sensing systems today require sensors, microcontrollers, memory, and batteries, and are often disposable. For example, temperature and humidity dataloggers used during food and vaccine transport become e-waste within weeks. Meanwhile, many species of microorganisms, such as the iridescent Flavobacteria, integrate environmental signals and store history structurally, all with minimal energy. Readout may be as simple as taking a photograph. Could these organisms replace conventional electronics and enable fully degradable, battery-less dataloggers? What's missing in realizing this future is our ability to interpret this biological record: we do not yet understand what the visual characteristics of organisms represent quantitatively, or how reliably we can recover that information. This PhD: We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to play a formative role in understanding how to decode environmental information from living microorganisms, in pursuit of living sensing and memory systems. This effort is truly trans-disciplinary, drawing on biodesign/biotechnology, machine learning, and interaction design. This project builds on groundwork already underway in our group but is meant to be shaped substantially by the candidate's own interests and expertise. The candidate will cultivate the living organism itself, characterize and model its visible responses to different environmental conditions, and develop and validate computational decoders that recover environmental history from an image of the living organism. Based on the found capabilities, the candidate will also design prototypes that incorporate living sensors, such as fully compostable, smart packaging for temperature and humidity monitoring for food, vaccines, or archival documents. The PhD candidate will be situated at the intersection of the Knowledge and Intelligent Design group and the Materializing Futures group in Sustainable Design Engineering (SDE), a department within the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering. Job Requirements We look for candidates who have: A Master's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Biodesign, Design Engineering, or a related field Experience in building and deploying machine learning or computer vision models Technical competencies in one or more of the following: bio-digital systems, biodesign, applied machine learning, computer vision, computational biology, and/or physical prototyping Experience or strong interest in biodesign and hands-on interaction with living organisms Experience or interest in conducting research with sound experimental design Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team, communicate effectively, and take initiative Prior publications and experience presenting at international conferences are assets but not requirements Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Industrial Design Engineering Matching the evolution of people with the speed of the revolution of technology. This is the focus of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering (IDE). Delft designers act as a bridge between advances in technology and the needs of people, organisations and society to create products, services and systems with purpose. IDE is a leader in design research across the application areas of mobility, sustainability and health, as well as its development of design tools and methods. A 350-strong research team and over 2,000 students work together in our inspiring hall, labs and studios. In close cooperation with industry, the public sector and NGOs we rehearse possible futures in research and education to design for a complex future. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , increasing from Promovendus gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. items.title: Doctoral researcher (PhD candidate) in energy informatics
items.desc: The Energy Informatics lab at Technische Universität Clausthal solicits expressions of interest for a doctoral researcher (PhD student) position. The position is on-site in Clausthal-Zellerfeld (Germany), full-time, remunerated up to TV-L E13, and offered for an initial duration up until 31 December 2028 with the possibility of a later contract extension. The position is part of the project " Innovative integrated energy concepts for rural areas (INITIAL) ," in which seven departments at four universities work towards the goal of creating and integrating simulation models for generation and demand in energy parks (featuring generators, consumers, and storages for electricity, hydrogen, and/or heat). The overall goal is to find the most grid-friendly operation mode for a given set of integrated components, while fostering acceptance by the general public at the same time. The contribution to be delivered by the successful candidate is the digital integration of models and the data-driven optimization of their modes of operation. Specific tasks Integrate existing simulation models of energy park components (such as hydrogen electrolyzers, PV and wind generators, and storage devices) Derive methodologies to emit control commands to reflect component dynamics (e.g., setpoint change latencies, or avoiding invalid operating regimes) Assess the relevance and importance of parameter forecasts on the overall system efficiency Communicate the scientific results achieved in conference and journal publications as well as presenting findings at project meetings Required prerequisites A very good university degree (M.Sc. or equivalent) in information technology, computer science, electrical engineering or a subject with a focus on technical computer science Very good communication skills, both written and spoken in English and ideally also in German Ability to work both independently and in a team Enjoy solving real-world problems and the interdisciplinary exchange with scientists Note that this is just a call for expressions of interest. Candidates expressing their interest on LinkedIn will be screened, and qualified candidates will be advised on how to submit their full application.

items.title: Doctoral Researcher (PhD) in Protein Synthesis
items.desc: A fully funded PhD position is available to study protein synthesis in the lab of Sarah O’Keefe at the Faculty of Biological and Environmental Sciences, University of Helsinki, Finland. About The Position We invite applications for a doctoral researcher position at the Viikki Campus in Helsinki, Finland. The doctoral researcher will work in the project Inhibiting Protein Synthesis – Old, New, Borrowed, Blue , funded by the Research Council of Finland. The doctoral researcher will be supervised by the Principal Investigator Sarah O’Keefe and co-supervised by Brendan Battersby. The successful candidate will complete an article-based PhD thesis and 30 ECTS credits of studies that are required for a PhD degree in Finland. The position is available and funded for 44 months from January 2027 , or as agreed. Project Description Proteins are key working molecules in all cells and their synthesis is an elaborate jigsaw puzzle. The early stages of protein synthesis include translation on ribosomes and the translocation of new polypeptides across, and their insertion into, membranes via translocons or insertases. New mechanistic insights are rapidly revolutionising our textbook models and bringing previously ‘undruggable’ protein synthesis machineries to the forefront of drug development. This doctoral project combines cellular and chemical biology, cell-free protein synthesis, cryoEM, gene editing and orthogonal high-throughput screening to discover breakthrough protein synthesis inhibitors and re-purpose existing ones. By expanding the chemical and biological space of protein synthesis and its inhibition, this research will develop new tools to probe how proteins are made and unlock new ways to treat human diseases. Why Work for Us? A collaborative, innovative and inclusive research environment. Training in cell culture, cell free protein synthesis, cryoEM, gene editing, high throughput screening, molecular biology, protein expression and purification, presenting, project management and writing. Access to cutting-edge infrastructures, including working closely the local cryoEM Unit, High Throughput Biomedicine Unit and Finnish Genome Editing Centre. International collaboration with Chemists and Computational Physicists (US, Japan and Finland). International mobility including conference attendance and short-term research visits at the University of Leeds (UK) to use new approaches for cryoEM sample preparation. As the first doctoral researcher in the lab, you will benefit from close, individualised mentorship and hands-on training from the Principal Investigator. You will also play a foundational role in shaping the lab’s core culture and scientific techniques as it grows. About The O’Keefe Lab We integrate biochemistry, cell biology, cryoEM and small molecules to unlock new mechanisms, methods and drug candidates of protein synthesis for the benefit of human health. To date, the Principal Investigator has discovered new protein synthesis inhibitors with anti-infective (bacteria, viruses, parasites) and anti-cancer utility, identified new mechanisms of protein biogenesis and visualised protein synthesis in action using cryoEM. Our research is highly interdisciplinary, drawing upon the Principal Investigator’s diverse career path in Medicinal Chemistry, Biochemistry and Cellular and Structural Biology in academic and industry settings. Supported by our collaborative network, we are committed to training and equipping lab members with the multidisciplinary skills needed to take their next career step. Selection Criteria You are ambitious, collegial, proactive and motivated to pursue multidisciplinary science research. You should have a Master’s degree (or be due to complete before the start date) in biology, biological sciences, biochemistry, pharmacy or another relevant field, including medicinal chemists with strong research experience and a commitment to switch fields. Competencies in cell culture, molecular biology, protein purification/expression and cryoEM will be learned during the project. Excellent written and spoken communication skills in English. The ability to work independently, problem solve, master new skills and work in a collaborative team. Merited criteria: research experience in industry or a research-intensive academic lab or knowledge of the protein synthesis field. The successful applicant will receive support in applying for the right to pursue a doctoral degree at the University of Helsinki, which should be obtained within the six-month probationary period. Salary and working hours The position is currently funded for a maximum of 44 months (3 years and 8 months, if commenced in January 2027). The starting gross monthly salary for a doctoral researcher is around 2500-2700 EUR and is based on job demand level 2 in the salary system for teaching and research personnel of Finnish Universities. The salary depends on the appointee’s qualifications and stage of doctoral studies and includes a personal performance component. The doctoral researcher should reside in Finland while employed by the University of Helsinki. The University assists employees from abroad with their transition to work and life in Finland. Finland is a member of the European Union, has high-quality free schooling (also in English), generous family benefits and healthcare. Helsinki offers an outstanding quality of life and Finland is consistently ranked among the world’s best countries for safety, work-life balance, education and family-friendliness. The University of Helsinki offers comprehensive occupational healthcare, flexible working hours, excellent sports facilities, staff training opportunities and support for international employees relocating to Finland. Read more about why the University of Helsinki is an excellent career choice . How To Apply Applications must be submitted via the University of Helsinki electronic recruitment system via ‘Apply now’ no later than 13th November 2026 (23:59 Helsinki time). Current employees at the University of Helsinki must submit their applications via the ‘Employee login’. Applications that are submitted via email, elsewhere, or after the closing date will not be evaluated. Excluding spellcheck and typo correction, the use of AI in application preparation will not be evaluated favourably. Applications should include the following documents as a single pdf called ‘lastname_firstname’ (in the field reserved for CV): A cover letter describing your motivation and suitability for the position (maximum 1 page). A curriculum vitae, including any publications or manuscripts in preparation. The names and contact details of two referees. A copy of your Master’s diploma. If you have not graduated at the time of applying, please describe your remaining studies and timeline to graduate before the starting date. A copy of your transcript of records, including completed courses and a grading system explanation. Succinct answers to the following: How does this PhD fit into your career vision and what are your alternatives to reach that goal? Based on your understanding of the project, what do you think the biggest obstacle is? Describe a time when a research task or project failed and how you approached the problem. What are your expectations for supervision, scientific training and professional development? Further Information Feel free to contact Sarah O’Keefe at sarah.okeefe@helsinki.fi . For support with the recruitment system can be obtained from University of Helsinki HR specialists at recruitment@helsinki.fi . A diverse and equitable study and work culture is important to us. That is why we do our best to promote an inclusive university community. We encourage all qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply for our positions.
