items.title: PhD Research Intern, Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research - 2027
items.desc: We are recruiting outstanding Research Interns to work on autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI! Intelligent machines that can perceive, reason, and safely interact with people and the physical world are rapidly becoming a reality. Self-driving cars, autonomous delivery and construction vehicles, mobile manipulators, and other robotic systems are moving closer to widespread deployment. However, fundamental research challenges remain before these systems can operate safely, reliably, and autonomously in complex, unfamiliar environments. For Example, How Can We Develop new training paradigms that use perception and interaction to train autonomous vehicle and robot policies in closed loop? Equip autonomous systems with online and offline assurances that meet the requirements of safety-critical applications? Enable vehicles and robots to navigate across new environments, tasks, and embodiments? Build systems that reason under uncertainty and interact safely and naturally with people and other agents? These are some of the exciting questions being explored by NVIDIA’s Autonomous Systems and Physical AI Research (ASPIRE) group. Our diverse, interdisciplinary team conducts foundational research spanning foundation model design, embodied reasoning, safety, closed-loop training and evaluation, and agentic workflows for Physical AI development. We also investigate related areas including decision-making under uncertainty, deep learning, reinforcement learning, simulation, and the verification and validation of safety-critical AI systems. Our focus is on fundamental research, and lab members are encouraged to publish their work and open-source their code. NVIDIA is known for its collaborative culture, and our researchers work closely with experts across the company in autonomous vehicles, robotics, perception, simulation, and machine learning. This creates opportunities to influence real-world products while retaining the freedom and bandwidth to conduct groundbreaking, publishable research. What You’ll Be Doing Designing and implementing cutting-edge techniques for autonomous vehicles, robotics, and physical AI. Conducting original research and publishing your results. Collaborating with research colleagues, internal product teams, and external researchers. Transferring technology you’ve developed to relevant product groups. What We Need To See Currently pursuing a PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field. Relevant research experience in autonomous vehicles, robotics, embodied AI, or autonomous systems. Strong knowledge of the theory and practice of vehicle or robot autonomy—or expertise in a related area, with a strong interest in applying your work to autonomous systems. A track record of research excellence, demonstrated through publications at leading conferences and journals—such as RSS, ICRA, CoRL, IJRR, NeurIPS, ICML, CVPR, TAC, etc.—and through other research artifacts such as open-source software. Exceptional Python programming skills; experience with C++ and parallel programming, such as CUDA, is a plus. Experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch. Strong communication and interpersonal skills are required, along with the ability to thrive in a dynamic, research-focused team. Are you intellectually curious, collaborative, and motivated to solve complex problems at the intersection of AI and the physical world? If so, you may be a great fit for NVIDIA. , , JR2024606

items.title: Stage Research Engineer : synthèse de programmes pour la génération 3D (PFE / M2 Recherche)
items.desc: Chat3D travaille sur la représentation paramétrique de la forme 3D par le langage : décrire un objet par du code plutôt que par une soupe de polygones. Cela repose sur deux chantiers : • l'entraînement de grands modèles de langage, en supervision puis en apprentissage par renforcement ; • la construction de juges 3D, capables d'estimer la justesse d'un objet produit et de servir de signal d'apprentissage. C'est un domaine où presque tout reste à établir : ce qu'un modèle doit émettre, ce qu'on sait mesurer d'une forme, et ce qui constitue un bon signal d'apprentissage pour s'en approcher. Le stage de recherche se focalise sur la contribution au pipeline d'apprentissage par renforcement qui permet à nos modèles de coder de la 3D. Le cadrage précis se discute à l'arrivée, selon ton profil et tes goûts, et nous sommes ouverts à une proposition personnelle alignée avec cette question. Dans tous les cas, le travail est pensé pour produire une contribution scientifique défendable : un protocole expérimental propre, des résultats falsifiables, un mémoire, et une publication possible. En pratique : • Encadrement : la supervision scientifique est assurée directement par le CTO (plus de 10 ans en ML appliqué, ex-CTO d'une startup de computer vision, publications ICCV / BMVC, un brevet US en estimation de profondeur, ancien encadrant de thèse CIFRE). • Durée : 5 à 6 mois, négociable jusqu'à 8. • Début : entre février et avril 2027, selon ton calendrier d'école. • Mois 1 et 2, cadrage : revue de littérature ciblée, définition du protocole expérimental, reproduction d'une première baseline. • Mois 2 à 4, expérimentation : itérations, mesures, ablations, analyse honnête des résultats y compris quand ils ne vont pas dans le sens attendu. • Mois 4 à 6, consolidation : rédaction du mémoire, restitution interne, démonstration. • Tout au long : un point hebdomadaire avec le CTO, des revues techniques régulières, et l'accès aux réunions produit et aux artistes pour comprendre le contexte d'usage réel. • Un vrai sujet de recherche, avec une contribution scientifique attendue, mesurable et défendable. Pas un stage « mets ce modèle en prod » déguisé. • Un encadrement scientifique serré par le CTO, en direct et chaque semaine. • Des moyens de calcul réels : tu auras du GPU pour tes expériences. • Lyon, ambiance startup, équipe tech resserrée où ton travail se voit. • 1 jour de télétravail par semaine. • Gratification de 1 200 à 1 400 € / mois selon profil. • Possibilité d'embauche en CDI à la fin du stage si le fit est bon. Indispensable : • Formation : dernière année d'école d'ingénieur (3A), M2 recherche, ou doctorant·e en césure, en CS / ML / vision / computer graphics. • Une vraie culture 3D. Tu sais ce que tu manipules : maillages, nuages de points, voxels, champs de distance signés ; topologie, normales, UV, matériaux. Tu as déjà ouvert un fichier 3D pour comprendre pourquoi il était cassé. C'est le point le plus discriminant de cette offre. • Rigueur expérimentale. Tu sais isoler une variable, construire une baseline, choisir ce que tu mesures, et tirer une conclusion honnête de résultats qui ne vont pas dans ton sens. Tu donnes toujours la taille de ton échantillon. • Solides bases en deep learning : tu as implémenté, entraîné et débuggé des modèles non triviaux, tu lis des papiers récents sans lutter. • Pratique sérieuse de PyTorch (ou équivalent), Python propre. • Une première expérience R&D tangible : stage en labo, projet de recherche encadré, contribution open source ML, publication étudiante. • Autonomie scientifique : tu creuses un sujet seul·e, tu identifies les bons papiers, tu sais quand demander de l'aide. • Bon niveau d'anglais scientifique. Les atouts qui font la différence : • un background geometry processing ou computer graphics académique (paramétrisation, remeshing, géométrie digitale, analyse de formes) ; • une expérience du post-training de LLM : apprentissage par renforcement, conception de fonctions de récompense, instrumentation d'évaluation ; • une expérience des métriques apprises et de leur validation contre du jugement humain ; • la pratique personnelle d'un outil DCC (Blender, Houdini, Maya) ; • une publication antérieure, ou une contribution open source significative ; • une sensibilité artiste, ou une pratique personnelle de la 3D, du jeu vidéo, de l'animation. • Étape 1, candidature : CV, et si tu en as, un lien vers tes travaux (dépôt de code, mémoire, publication, projets 3D). • Étape 2, premier échange : 30 minutes sur ton parcours et ce qui t'intéresse dans le sujet. • Étape 3, entretien scientifique : une heure de discussion sur un papier que tu as lu et un projet que tu as mené. Pas de test technique chronométré. On décide à l'issue de la troisième étape.

items.title: PhD Candidate in Access, Actors and Accountability: The Role of Researchers in AI Governance
items.desc: What is the role of researchers in the governance of AI systems and digital platforms? What legal exceptions and safeguards do researchers need to be able to play that role? And how can we organise productive interactions between researcher, policy makers, regulators, civil society and companies? Research and expertise have critical role in making sure that AI and digital technologies are safe, respectful of fundamental rights and beneficial to society, but we have yet to develop the legal and organisational frameworks to enable their work, while protecting their safety and academic freedom. If you want to help doing so, this position might be for you. Working at the UvA Join Us! Access, Actors and Accountability: The Role of Researchers in AI Governance Governing AI systems and digital platforms, identifying systemic risks and developing adequate policy responses is complex and requires research and expertise. In the new European Digital Framework, researchers are central stakeholder ins AI and platform governance, and regulations like the DSA and the AI Act, define prominent roles for them to produce evidence, audit big tech companies and public bodies, monitor the way AI technology impacts society and help to ensure transparency and accountability. At the same time, this role comes with new challenges for academic freedom, navigating dependencies on regulators and large technology companies, being meaningfully involved and heard, and sometimes even having to navigate issues around safety against personal attacks and threats to their safety. At the same time, the ability of independent researchers to study platforms and AI systems often depends on research exemptions and access rights, and so does the evidence base available to regulators. A good salary Your salary will be determined on the basis of your experience and seniority, in accordance with the Labour agreement. Your grading and therefore the amounts mentioned are based on full employment of 38 hours per week. 232 vacation hours We also offer parental leave, partner leave and social engagement leave. Through the Employment Conditions Menu Card, there are opportunities for even more vacation hours. Financial arrangements On top of your salary, you receive holiday allowance (8%) and a year-end bonus (8.3%). You build up a good pension with ABP. And in addition, we offer many other allowances and schemes. Career development and room for growth The UvA encourages you to continue to professionalise through training courses and open UvA lectures. Family matters Relocating to the Netherlands with your family? Find out about daycare, schooling, health insurance or employment options and support for your partner or spouse. Including the IDCN-network which provides support for your spouse through various training sessions, social activities, and networking events. All About This Vacancy This is what you will do This doctoral project examines the legal position of researchers under the DSA and AI Act, and the research exemptions, safeguards and policy processes needed to allow independent researchers to generate evidence for regulatory learning and anticipatory governance without eroding legality or academic freedom. This research combines doctrinal, normative and comparative research with interviews (with academics, policy makers, civil society and other societal stakeholders) and participatory research to co-design how research exemptions and researcher-regulator feedback loops can be designed and operationalised. The work will build an evaluative analysis of exemption scope and adequacy, a typology of enablers and obstacles to researcher–policy engagement, and concrete proposals how to enable policy research while protecting academic freedom. You will work on a legal PhD thesis at the Institute for Information Law (IViR), Amsterdam Law School, University of Amsterdam, as part of the REGULAIRE project. The PhD will provide the opportunity to contribute to the activities of the DSA Observatory, the AI, Media & Democracy Lab and the Amsterdam Law School Sectorplan initiative Democratic Digital Transformation (2026-2031) and offers a focused route into information law, platform and AI regulation. About REGULAIRE REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network bringing together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities to study how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Its projects examine how regulators sense emerging problems early, how balanced interventions encourage learning without overcorrection or underreaction, how such interventions alter institutional capacities, and how feedback can be institutionalised so that insights travel across organisations and jurisdictions. Across the network, regulatory learning means treating regulation as a learning architecture that generates, tests and refines knowledge about what works, rather than as one-off rulemaking. Each researcher joins an international cohort, receives supervision across institutions and takes part in three residential summer schools, methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and joint work with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations. Every project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment. The network is coordinated by Prof. Urs Gasser at the Technical University of Munich (TUM). More specifically, you are expected to: Refine the research questions and design with the supervision team, and prepare ethics, data-management and open-science materials. Collect, manage and analyse research data using the approved project-specific methods. Complete a doctoral thesis and related research outputs under the doctoral programme and the REGULAIRE plan. Take part in local and network-wide training, cohort activities, network reviews, dissemination and practitioner engagement, including three residential summer schools and monthly paper development seminars. Undertake the planned three-month intersectoral secondment with EDMO – The European Digital Media Observatory (EDMO), Florence, Italy. Contribute to the research and activities of the AI, Media & Democracy Lab and the DSA Observatory. Contribute to research integrity, equality and diversity, open science and FAIR data practices. What We Ask Of You A Master's degree (or an equivalent qualification giving access to doctoral studies) in law, political science, media and communication studies, or related legal, social science and interdisciplinary fields, completed by the start date. A demonstrable interest in studying the relationship of law to digital technologies and services; Skills or a demonstrable interest in qualitative research, such as interviews and participatory design. Excellent command of written and spoken English. Willingness to engage in international mobility, including the planned secondment and network-wide activities. Fulfilment of the MSCA eligibility conditions listed below. A creative mind and strong critical and analytical skills; Collegial attitude and capacity to work not only independently but also in teams; Ability and willingness to organize workshops, lectures, and similar events (demonstrable experience with these activities a plus). If the vacancy appeals to you, but you are doubting whether you might be THE person we are looking for, please do apply? We encourage all qualified applicants, including minorities, women, people with disabilities, and members of other groups underrepresented in academia. We wish to create a research group that consists of persons who each contribute in their unique way to the team. Complementarity and not homogeneity is what we are looking for. Supervision, training and mobility Your supervision team will consist of Supervision team: Prof. Natali Helberger (University of Amsterdam), Prof. Joris van Hoboken (University of Amsterdam), an external supervisor from the REGULAIRE project network, and a sectoral mentor at the anticipated secondment host. The secondment enables the candidate to observe how a research-based civil society organisation engages in policy research, challenges involved and possible best practices. The candidate will be part of a supervisory team consisting of the primary supervisor at the host institution, an academic co-supervisor at a partner institution in another country, and a sectoral mentor at the secondment host. Candidates meet the primary supervisor at least monthly and the full team at least four times per year; progress and training are recorded in a personal Career Development Plan. Network-wide training includes three residential summer schools (regulatory learning and foresight at TUM; methods and analytics at BI Norwegian Business School; academic writing and impact at the University of St. Gallen), monthly paper development seminars, and annual network reviews aligned with major community events. Candidates obtain a minimum of twenty ECTS through local and network-wide training, of which at least ten from network-wide provision. This Is What We Offer You A temporary contract for 38 hours per week for the duration of 4 years (the initial contract will be for a period of 12 months and after satisfactory evaluation it will be extended for a total duration of 4 years). The preferred starting date is January 1st 2027. This should lead to a dissertation (PhD thesis). We will draft an educational plan that includes attendance of courses and (international) meetings. We also expect you to assist in teaching undergraduates and master students. The gross monthly salary, based on 38 hours per week and dependent on relevant experience, ranges between € 3.204 to € 4.051 (scale P). This does not include 8% holiday allowance and 8,3% year-end allowance. The UFO profile 'PhD student' is applicable. The Collective Labour Agreement of Universities of the Netherlands is applicable. The UvA offers excellent possibilities for further professional development and education. What Else Do We Offer a position where own initiative and input are highly valued; an enthusiastic and dynamic team that is open to new colleagues; an inspiring academic and international working environment in the heart of Amsterdam. Your place at the UvA You will work in this team The University of Amsterdam is the largest university in the Netherlands, with the broadest spectrum of degree programmes. It is an intellectual hub with 39,000 students, 6,000 employees and 3,000 doctoral students who are all committed to a culture of inquiring minds. With over 5,000 students and more than 500 staff members, the Amsterdam Law School is one of the larger law faculties in the Netherlands. We educate lawyers who know how to apply the law effectively with the aim of making a real contribution to solving social problems. The Amsterdam Law School stands for progressive and trail-blazing education and research, for stronger legal institutions, solutions to social problems and a better and juster society. The Institute for Information Law (IViR), officially established in 1989, is one of the largest research centers in the field of information law in Europe, and one of the largest of its kind in the world. The Institute engages in cutting-edge research into fundamental and topical aspects of information law, and provides a forum for critical debate about the social, cultural and political aspects of regulating information markets. This is how we at the Amsterdam Law School view the role of law in a constantly changing (international) society. items.title: Doktorandin / Doktorand, Mitarbeiterin / Mitarbeiter in der Wissenschaft (w/m/d) - Teilzeit 80%
items.desc: Die Arbeit ist ein Teilprojekt innerhalb einer DFG-Forschungsgruppe, welche in Kooperation mit dem Fraunhofer-Institut für Werkstoffmechanik IWM (Freiburg) und fünf weiteren Forschungseinrichtungen durchgeführt wird. Ihr Arbeitsort wird das Fraunhofer IWM in Freiburg sein. Ihre Aufgaben Im Fokus dieses Teilprojektes steht die mikrostrukturbasierte Modellierung und numerische Analyse von Hochgeschwindigkeits-Scherschneidprozessen (HGSS) für hochfeste Blechwerkstoffe und deren Übertragung auf Prozessebene. Die im Werkstoff auftretende adiabatische Scherbandbildung spielt hier eine entscheidende Rolle. Für die Beschreibung der Wechselwirkung zwischen der Mikrostruktur, dem Prozess und der adiabatischen Scherbandbildung sollen geeignete Modellansätze weiterentwickelt und implementiert werden. Auf Basis umfangreicher Simulationsstudien werden zudem Methoden des maschinellen Lernens eingesetzt, um die Prozess-Struktur-Eigenschafts-Beziehungen zu korrelieren. Die Validierung der Modellansätze erfolgt durch den Abgleich anhand von experimentellen Daten auf der Mikroskala des Werkstoffs und auf Prozessebene. Ihr Profil Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master) in Maschinenbau, Materialwissenschaften, Computational Engineering oder eines vergleichbaren Fachgebiets Fundierte Kenntnisse in der Kontinuumsmechanik, Werkstoffmodellierung und finite Elemente Simulation Grundlegendes Verständnis der Zusammenhänge zwischen Mikrostruktur, plastischer Deformation und Werkstoffeigenschaften Kenntnisse in den Bereichen Kristallplastizität, mikrostrukturbasiere Materialmodellierung oder maschinellen Lernens sind von Vorteil Gute Programmierkenntnisse (z. B. Python, Fortran) inkl. ML-Bibliotheken sowie erste Linux-Erfahrung Erfahrung mit FEM-Solvern, vorzugsweise LS-DYNA HPC-Erfahrung von Vorteil Erwartet werden ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative zur Lösung komplexer wissenschaftlicher Fragestellungen, sowie das Interesse zur interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit in einem experimentell und numerisch ausgerichteten Forschungsverbund Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sowie verhandlungssichere Englischkenntnisse Wir bieten Forschung mit Wirkung : Arbeiten Sie an Themen von gesellschaftlicher Relevanz – in einem exzellenten wissenschaftlichen Umfeld, das Veränderungen möglich macht. Karriere und Entwicklung : Wir unterstützen Sie mit einer strukturierten Einarbeitung, vielfältigen Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten und individueller Förderung. So stärken wir Ihr persönliches Wachstum. Flexible Arbeitszeitgestaltung : Nutzen Sie Gleitzeit, mobiles Arbeiten und 30 Tage Urlaub für eine optimale Work-Life-Balance. Familienfreundlichkeit : Das Programm „KIT-Family +“ unterstützt Sie bei der Vereinbarkeit von Familie und Beruf – durch Kinderbetreuung, Ferienangebote, ein Eltern-Kind-Büro und Hilfe bei der Angehörigenpflege. Gesundheit : Unter dem Motto „Fit im KIT – mit Körper, Geist und Seele“ fördern wir Ihre Gesundheit mit Sportkursen und Angeboten zur psychischen Gesundheit. Individuelle Zusatzleistungen : Profitieren Sie von einer betrieblichen Altersvorsorge (VBL), einem monatlichen Zuschuss von 25 Euro zum Jobticket BW sowie vielfältigen Angeboten rund um Kultur und Freizeit. Arbeitsort Sonstige Eingruppierung EG 13 TV-L; die Eingruppierung erfolgt entsprechend den persönlichen und fachlichen Voraussetzungen. Vertragsdauer 3 Jahre Fachliche Auskünfte erteilt Ihnen gerne Dr. Alexander Butz alexander.butz@iwm.fraunhofer.de Dr. Hemanth Nallani hemanth.janarthanam.nallani@iwm.fraunhofer.de Bei allgemeinen Fragen zur Bewerbung wenden Sie sich bitte an Raquel Carrasco Sanchez Personalservice (PSE) raquel.carrasco@kit.edu +49 721 608-42016 Am KIT schätzen wir die Vielfalt unserer Mitarbeitenden - unterschiedliche Perspektiven und Hintergründe sind eine Bereicherung für unsere Arbeit. Wir freuen uns daher über alle Bewerbenden. Frauen sind besonders zur Bewerbung eingeladen. Bewerbungen von anerkannt schwerbehinderten Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt. items.title: PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints
items.desc: Ledig stilling PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid Ledig stilling PhD in Safe Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid Aalborg Ansøgningsfrist: 29.11.2026 Afdeling: Department of Electronic Systems Ref. nummer: 2026/1218 Ansættelsestype: Fuldtid The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a PhD stipend in the field of Safe Learning Based Multi-Robot Planning and Control under Connectivity Constraints within the general study programme Electrical and Electronic Engineering; starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The PhD Fellow will be based at the Automation and Control Section in Aalborg. In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk. Description of the position How can a team of autonomous robots operate safely and make progress when communication deteriorates, the environment is only partially known, and the team must continually reorganise? This PhD position addresses this challenge through research on safe and resilient planning, control, and coordination of heterogeneous robotic systems in demanding underground environments. The position combines scientific research with substantial hands-on engineering. You will develop and analyse new algorithms, implement robotic software, build realistic simulation and digital-twin environments, and carry out systematic experiments with physical robot platforms. We are looking for a researcher who enjoys connecting mathematical ideas to reliable real-world robotic systems. Description of the project The ROX6G EU Horizon project aims to develop autonomous robotic systems for exploring and collecting data in hazardous, poorly documented underground mines. Its heterogeneous robot teams combine exploration, mapping, sensing, and sampling with mobile, multi-hop 5G/6G connectivity. Because robots also act as communication nodes, they must adapt their movement and team roles to sustain communication without relying on fixed infrastructure installed throughout the mine. The project is coordinated by AAU. In addition, within ROX6G, AAU leads the activities on learning based multi-robot coordination and reconfiguration for connectivity preservation and on digital-twin generation and multimodal visualisation. The PhD candidate will contribute to both activities, collaborating with international partners across robotics, communications, sensing, and geological modelling. The main core of the PhD will focus on developing theoretical, algorithmic, and real-time implementation framework for on the fly autonomy of multi-robot control systems in uncertain and limited environments. In addition, methods will be evaluated through simulation, laboratory experiments, and project-level system integration and validation, with attention to safety, connectivity, and practical mission performance. Your work tasks The PhD fellow will be responsible for: Conducting research on safe and resilient learning based planning, control, and coordination of multi-robot systems operating under constraints and uncertainty. Actively contributing to the formulation and refinement of research questions within the doctoral project. Taking an active role in planning, implementing, and, when necessary, adapting the research plan. Designing, implementing, and evaluating the developed algorithms in realistic robotic simulation environments and on physical robotic platforms. Contributing to the development and implementation of digital twins by integrating robotic sensor data, to support real-time visualization, monitoring, and autonomous decision-making. Publishing research results in leading international journals and conferences, and presenting findings at project meetings and international scientific venues. Your competencies The successful candidate will hold a Master’s degree in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Control Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field, with a strong foundation in robotics, autonomous systems, planning, and/or control theory. We particularly value strong programming skills in Python and/or C++, familiarity with robotic software frameworks such as ROS/ROS 2, and demonstrated ability to implement, integrate, test, and troubleshoot robotic systems. Motivation for hands-on work with physical robot platforms, sensors, simulation, and experimental setups is important for this position. Experience with one or more of the following areas will be an advantage: multi-robot systems and graph-based coordination; safety-critical, robust, or optimisation-based control; autonomous navigation, localisation, simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM), or sensor fusion; simulation and digital-twin development using tools such as Gazebo, Isaac Sim, or Webots. Experience with data processing and visualisation, real-time robotic experiments, and research publications will also be considered positively. Applicants are not expected to have expertise in all these areas, but should be willing to learn and work across disciplines. You should be able to work independently and collaboratively in an international research environment, approach technical challenges in a structured and self-driven manner, and communicate clearly in written and spoken English. Qualification requirements PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1039 of August 27, 2013 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. Who we are The Department of Electronic Systems at Aalborg University (AAU) conducts internationally recognised research and education across digital technologies, including robotics, AI, control systems, communications, sound, and cybersecurity. Within the department, the Advanced Robotics & AI research group advances self-learning autonomous robotic systems for reliable operation in extreme environments. Our research strengthens robotic autonomy and resilience, enabling systems to operate safely and with minimal supervision in challenging settings. How to apply Your application must include the following: Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position Curriculum Vitae (CV) Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) Master thesis and/or relevant publications, if any Other relevant documents( e.g. one or two recommendation letters) The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost. Further information The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts. Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not. The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace. Read more about The Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design Salary and terms of employment The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”. Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen. items.title: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
items.desc: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology. We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1 st , 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences. Research environment The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research. The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad. The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology. Project description The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez . The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1 st , 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists. The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset. In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties. The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available. Qualifications Before the start date of September 1 st , 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study. The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required. The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required. For further information about the project, please contact: Anthony Vincent Fernandez Department of Psychology University of Southern Denmark (SDU) E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided. Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation): A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”. Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1 st , 2027. Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read. A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview. At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan. Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities. Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process. For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center. Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University . Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply. Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated [AF1] . Closing date January 15 th , 2027 We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date. Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students. The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order) Salary and Working Conditions at SDU PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement. Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98 per year. The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future. As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital. The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background. [AF1] I've removed the note about reference letters here since I will only request reference letters for those invited to interview. [AF2] To confirm, is this updated with the current rate?

items.title: Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), 3 positions, Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data
items.desc: The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website), funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. Your main duty as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for the doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). The positions will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff. The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month. items.title: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Understanding climate risks to global food security
items.desc: Tasks Investigate feedback mechanisms and processes behind acceleration in extreme weather trends Design targeted climate model experiments and analyse large ensembles to test conditions under which tail-specific feedbacks are triggered Apply explainable AI (XAI) and other advanced statistical methods to uncover non-linear interactions between physical drivers of extremes Evaluate how well climate models represent these tail processes against observations and reanalysis Investigate drivers, statistics and impacts of record-breaking events in current and future climates, in collaboration with the other group members Publish in leading journals, present at international conferences Help organise group events Co-supervise PhD students Profile Essential Master's degree (or equivalent) in climate science, atmospheric science, physics, geosciences, environmental science, statistics or a related field Programming skills (e.g. Python, R) and experience handling gridded or time-series data Strong motivation for independent, interdisciplinary research Good command of written and spoken English Advantageous Experience with climate model output, reanalysis data or extreme event analysis Knowledge of extreme value statistics, compound events or time-series methods Experience with agricultural modelling and agricultural datasets Experience with machine learning or causal methods Previous research experience, e.g. a Master's thesis in a related topic Our offer The position will begin on the 1st of January 2027 though some flexibility in start date is possible. Remuneration will follow the standard PhD salaries given in the Max Planck Society which correspond to 65% of EG 13 TvöD (Bund). The position includes 31 days of annual leave. We also offer attractive and family-friendly flextime and options for remote work. Additional benefits include an employer subsidy for public transport, access to training opportunities within the Max Planck Society, as well as language and health courses. The successful candidate can apply for admission to our graduate school “International Max Planck Research School for Modeling the Anthropocene”. The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more individuals with disabilities and especially encourages them to apply. We were honored with the TOTAL E-QUALITY award for the first time in 2023 for our commitment. Your application should include: A cover letter A CV of no more than 3 pages A summary of research interests with max. 2 pages If applicable a list of relevant scientific, peer-reviewed publications related to the position or a copy of the candidate’s MA/MPhil/MSc thesis Contacts of two referees Any relevant certificates Position remains open until filled. About us The Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (MPI-GEA) was founded in summer 2022 and is a dynamically growing, highly-interdisciplinary and international research institution. The research focuses on modeling and analyzing the interrelationships between biophysical and human-made systems, looking from the deep past to the future. The institute examines how humanity has driven the emergence of the Anthropocene – the period in which human activities began significantly impacting our planet’s climate and ecosystems – and identifying potential intervention points towards a more sustainable future. The Carl Zeiss Stiftung Independent Research Group on High-End Climate Risks (CZS-HECR) at MPI-GEA works towards an end-to-end understanding of worst-case climate outcomes, from unprecedented and compounding extremes to their societal impacts. The group combines fundamental physical process understanding rooted in climate physics and Earth System analyses, targeted climate model experiments, advanced statistics, including machine-learning- and explainable AI to deliver usable climate risk estimates under current and future climates for core societal sectors such as health, food, energy and finance. Doctoral researchers join an interdisciplinary team, and a broad international network are provided with highly competitive research conditions including generous support for travel and research visits. items.title: PhD Position: Biodiversity for Nature-Inclusive Dairy Farming
items.desc: Employment 0.8 - 1.0 FTE Gross monthly salary € 3,204 - € 4,051 Required background Research University Degree Organizational unit Faculty of Science Application deadline 22 November 2026 In this PhD position, you will develop integrated and innovative biodiversity monitoring and data analysis techniques to aid in the decision-making of businesses within the dairy sector for the benefit of biodiversity. Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses and healthy societies. A transition to a more nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands would be pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance. To properly assess the suitability and effectiveness of key performance indicators and the effects of management practices on local biodiversity, it is crucial to monitor, for example, breeding birds, bats, insect communities and soil life (depending on the KPI). By adapting and developing biomonitoring techniques programmes at dairy farms that are in line with long-running or recently developed monitoring schemes, you will utilise the full potential of datasets and methods to quantify biodiversity gains resulting from nature-inclusive farming as well as the potential for further biodiversity recovery. Novel instruments such as DIOPSIS smart insect cameras, LED buckets and bat loggers generate huge amounts of biodiversity data from across the Netherlands and can be used to detect and identify biodiversity automatically. National schemes like the breeding bird monitoring project, the butterfly monitoring scheme and the dragon fly monitoring scheme (standardised and coordinated by NGOs such as Sovon and Dutch Butterfly Conservation, and powered by thousands of citizen scientists) generate standardised long-term trends based on thousands of plots around the country. You will design novel, integrated analyses to quantify the effects on biodiversity from existing and new data while accounting for factors such as observers' bias, weather and surrounding landscape configuration. In this project you will: Bring coherence across the diverse monitoring systems and KPI developed so far and adapt sets of KPI's suited to peat soils. Document the relationships between different nature-inclusive measures taken by heterogeneous farm types, and the different aspects of biodiversity and ecosystem services considered. The precise type of monitoring and the number and locations of monitoring points will be decided in collaboration with stakeholders. Further develop effective and integrated monitoring to guide decision-making in businesses and develop reward schemes. Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time. Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate . At Radboud University, I can fully focus on expanding my expertise while learning from my peers and mentors. Noemí Segura-Solé PhD candidate in Microbial Ecology Read Noemí's story Does this sound like you? You have an MSc degree in Biology, Ecology, Environmental Sciences or a related discipline with an interest in social sciences. You have good communication and writing skills in both English and Dutch. You have designed scientific studies, and it would be advantageous if you have experience with writing scientific and non-scientific manuscripts for publication. You have an affinity for, and proven experience with, computer programming, statistical modelling and large datasets, and you know how to perform qualitative analyses based on quantitative data. You have an understanding of field work in practice, have a passion for biodiversity and are keen to absorb and share knowledge with others. You are a team player, eager to work on a truly interdisciplinary project. What we offer you We will give you a temporary employment contract (0.8 FTE 5- year contract - 1.0 FTE 4- year contract) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract) or 3.5 years (5-year contract). You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 from the fourth year onwards (salary scale P). You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus. You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20. Additional employment conditions Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. In addition, you receive a 34% discount on the sports and cultural activities at Radboud University as an employee. And, of course, we offer a good pension plan. We also give you plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes. Where you will be working The Department of Ecology at Radboud University is a dynamic, collaborative and interdisciplinary team. We are a young and ambitious group of ecologists committed to preserving and promoting biodiversity and ecosystem health. Our department brings together aquatic and terrestrial ecologists who focus on plants, animals and microorganisms and their interactions in a changing world. We are dedicated to conducting timely and innovative research that addresses both scientific and societal challenges. Your research will be integrated into ongoing studies in biodiversity research and applied ecology, with opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across departments. Dr Eelke Jongejans will be one of the two main supervisors for the project. The Radboud Institute for Biological and Environmental Sciences (RIBES) is committed to equality of opportunity, fairness and inclusivity, striving to be a place where everyone feels respected and valued, and creativity and innovation are fostered and encouraged. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ethnicities, sexual orientations, abilities and backgrounds, and particularly encourage those from underrepresented groups to apply. SoortenNL is an umbrella for organisations that collect and interpret biodiversity data from surveys and large monitoring schemes carried out by citizen scientists. It is both a social network and an information landscape. Dr Sander Turnhout of SoortenNL will be the co-supervisor of this project. In this interdisciplinary research project (DECISION: Dairy and Ecology: Co-Innovating buSIness Operations for Nature) you will closely collaborate with three other PhD candidates and a postdoctoral researcher working in animal sciences and social sciences at Wageningen University and Erasmus University. The research consortium also includes agribusinesses, financial businesses, farmer associations and governmental organisations. Faculty of Science The Faculty of Science (FNWI), part of Radboud University, engages in groundbreaking research and excellent education. In doing so, we push the boundaries of scientific knowledge and pass that knowledge on to the next generation. We seek solutions to major societal challenges, such as cybercrime and climate change and work on major scientific challenges, such as those in the quantum world. At the same time, we prepare our students for careers both within and outside the scientific field. Currently, more than 1,300 colleagues contribute to research and education, some as researchers and lecturers, others as technical and administrative support officers. The faculty has a strong international character with staff from more than 70 countries. Together, we work in an informal, accessible and welcoming environment, with attention and space for personal and professional development for all. Radboud University At Radboud University, we aim to make an impact through our work. We achieve this by conducting groundbreaking research, providing high-quality education, offering excellent support, and fostering collaborations within and outside the university. In doing so, we contribute indispensably to a healthy, free world with equal opportunities for all. To accomplish this, we need even more colleagues who, based on their expertise, are willing to search for answers. We advocate for an inclusive community and welcome employees with diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives. If you want to learn more about working at Radboud University, follow our Instagram account and read stories from our colleagues. Is this the job for you? Address your letter of application to Eelke Jongejans. In the application form, you will find which documents you need to include with your application. We look forward to receiving your application. The first interviews will take place on Wednesday 2 December. Any second interview will take place on Monday 7 December. You will preferably start your employment on 15 January 2026. items.title: PhD in Physics-informed generative AI for dynamic cardiac MRI
items.desc: The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers top-level education and research in one of the most relevant and exciting scientific disciplines of the 21st century: engineering health. In combining engineering and life sciences, through challenge-based learning and a multidisciplinary approach in collaboration with hospitals, industry and others, the department addresses the great challenges of the future, striving to improve healthcare and society as a whole. Introduction Do you want to make cardiac MRI safer for patients and the environment? Join PRIMA-CMR, a EuroTech Universities Alliance project between TU/e and the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and help to develop trustworthy generative AI that makes it possible to scan with far less contrast agent. Job Description Cardiac MRI gives unmatched insight into heart disease, but some of its most important exams depend on gadolinium-based contrast agents. Gadolinium can build up in the body, cannot be given to all patients, and is now an environmental pollutant. A large reduction in the dose would make cardiac MRI safer and available to more patients. At low doses, however, the images no longer contain enough signal for a reliable diagnosis. Current AI methods can make images that look realistic, but they cannot guarantee that what they show is real. We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate to develop new generative AI methods that recover diagnostic information from low-dose cardiac MRI in a reliable and trustworthy way. Your work will combine knowledge of MR imaging physics, patient-specific clinical information, and uncertainty quantification. The aim is a model whose outputs clinicians can trust, and which tells them when it is not certain. You will validate the methods on real clinical data together with our clinical partners. This PhD position is part of PRIMA-CMR, a collaborative project within the EuroTech Universities Alliance programme. You will be based at TU/e and spend six months at TUM in the group of prof. Julia Schnabel, which is a world leader in generative and multimodal AI. You will also work with international clinical and academic partners across Europe. This position is embedded in the Medical Image Analysis group, Department of Biomedical Engineering, TU/e. You will be supervised by dr. Cian Scannell, and co-supervised by prof. Julia Schnabel (TUM). Job Requirements A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Physics, Applied Mathematics, or a related field. Background in deep learning, with an interest in generative models. Knowledge of MRI physics, physics-based modeling, or inverse problems is a plus. Proficiency in Python and a deep learning framework such as PyTorch. A research-oriented attitude, analytical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Ability to work in an international, interdisciplinary team, and willingness to spend six months at TUM in Munich. Strong interest in medical imaging and cardiovascular disease. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In addition, we offer you: Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. items.title: PhD in Photonic Sensors for Light-Starved Applications
items.desc: The Department of Applied Physics and Science Education is a research-driven department housing high-quality educational programs, all featuring strong connections between research and education. Our research is clustered in three focal areas: Fluids, Bio and Soft Matter (FBSM); Plasmas and Beams (PB); and Nano, Quantum and Photonics (NQP). Our shared ambition is to equip the next generation of ‘engineers of the future’ with the knowledge and the skills they will need to impact science, innovation, and society, from regional to global scales. Introduction Are you passionate about cutting-edge semiconductor technology for solving real societal problems? Then this PhD position could be a fit for you. In this project you will push the limit of spectroscopic analysis by developing novel photonic chips working at ultralow light levels (down to femtowatts). These chips will form the core of sensors which are crucial for advancing healthcare and the energy transition. Job Description Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) allows characterizing materials and tissues, and it is widely used in industry. Our group has recently developed integrated spectral sensors, based on an advanced nanophotonic platform. These low-cost spectral chips, already commercialized by our spin-off MantiSpectra, provide detailed spectral information in the spectral region 900-1700 nm and allow measuring materials properties. However, they are based on reflection and therefore require a powerful light source to illuminate the object. Their application could be widely extended if they were sensitive enough to measure light emitted by a sample through fluorescence or Raman scattering. This requires pushing the limit of spectral sensing technology to combine spectral discrimination and detection at the femtowatt/low picowatt level, in a single device. To this aim the project will explore advanced device designs and fabrication methods, and collaborate with other TU/e research groups for the integration with low-noise amplification. The sensors will be fabricated at the NanoLab@TU/e cleanroom facility, using advanced semiconductor equipment. Their application to low-light sensing applications will also be explored during the project, in collaboration with industrial partners. Job Requirements A recent master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in Physics, Electrical Engineering or Materials Science. Candidates who obtained their Master degree more than two years ago will not be considered. A research-oriented attitude and strong interest and motivation for experimental work. Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team. Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students. Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level). Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. items.desc: The Department of Applied Physics and Science Education is a research-driven department housing high-quality educational programs, all featuring strong connections between research and education. Our shared ambition is to equip the next generation of ‘engineers of the future’ with the knowledge and the skills they will need to impact science, innovation, and society, from regional to global scales. Introduction Are you excited to solve technical challenges with a real-world application? Are you eager to build something truly unique in the world? Job Description Development of a pulsed electron source with extreme transverse bunch brightness, based on photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms, for time-resolved protein crystallography. Context: ERC-funded project “Cool T-ReX” Goal: Develop a unique and innovative instrument to enable time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons (and be the first in the world in doing so). Scientific relevance: Understanding how proteins function is crucial to improving medicine and unraveling processes that are fundamental to life. Time-resolved protein crystallography uniquely allows following the conformational change of a protein with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution, yielding a “molecular movie” of how the protein performs its function. This is currently only possible on large-scale X-ray facilities. In this project we will build the very first instrument that can make such movies through time-resolved protein crystallography with electrons rather than X-rays, on a laboratory-scale setup. Next, through collaboration with leading research groups in time-resolved protein crystallography, we will demonstrate the instrument’s capabilities in time-resolved crystallography experiments on photo-active proteins with medical relevance (and used in the field of optogenetics, awarded this year’s Nobel Prize in Medicine!). Your role: Drive the development of this unique instrument. You will build on our research group’s two decades of experience in building electron sources based on the photo-ionization of laser-cooled atoms. This technique has demonstrated electron pulses with record-low transverse temperatures, corresponding to a high transverse coherence, as needed for protein crystallography. In this project we will push this transverse coherence even further, making use of some of the unique capabilities of this source technology. The result will be an electron beam with a “transverse bunch brightness” that is three orders of magnitude beyond the current state of the art. To reach this ambitious goal, you will work with a team of experienced technicians, a second PhD student, a PostDoc, and the PI (Julius Huijts). We are part of the larger Coherence and Quantum Technology group in the Department of Applied Physics. Job Requirements A MSc degree in Applied Physics, Engineering Physics, Mechatronics with a strong physics component, or similar. You can work in a team, are open to new ideas, can communicate with people outside your own field. You take initiative, are able to organize your own work load. You have a background or a proven affinity with at least two of the following (please highlight this in your application): o Mechanical and optical design o Complex optical setups o Charged particle optics o Cold atoms o High vacuum o High voltage Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).
