items.title: Doctoral Researcher in Occupational Cancer Epidemiology (NordExCan) / Väitöskirjatutkija NordExCan-tutkimushankkeeseen
items.desc: Tampere University is a unique, boldly future‑oriented and evolving community, and one of Finland’s most multidisciplinary universities. At Tampere University, technology, health and society come together in a distinctive way. Our research groups and projects carry out interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral research that transcends organisational boundaries. Our community is international, with members from more than 80 countries. Read more at https://www.tuni.fi/en/tau The Faculty of Social Sciences and Health Sciences Unit (HES) at Tampere University invite applications for the position of Doctoral Researcher in Occupational Cancer Epidemiology for a fixed-term period of 3 years starting in January 2027 (or as agreed). The Health Sciences unit provides a collaborative setting with multidisciplinary and multimethodological strengths in population health, supporting rigorous and impactful doctoral research. Our doctoral programs in Health Sciences, Epidemiology and Public Health (IPPE), and Medicine offer a strong methodological and research environment for completing an ongoing doctoral project within established research groups at the Health Sciences Unit. The programs provide advanced training in key areas of population health, supporting high-quality publication-oriented research and researcher training. Job Description The doctoral researcher will join the research project “The Nordic Occupational Exposome and Cancer: Decades of Change, Mixtures, and Inequalities” (NordExCan) , led by Principal Investigator Dr. Subas Neupane. The project examines how occupational exposures change over working life and how these exposures, individually and in combination, are associated with cancer incidence, mortality, and inequalities in the Nordic countries. The research builds on the Nordic Occupational Cancer (NOCCA) cohort and Nordic job-exposure matrices, using occupational histories and population and cancer registry data from Finland, Sweden, Norway, Denmark, and Iceland. The doctoral researcher will mainly work on Work Package 1 , focusing on occupational exposure histories and their associations with cancer incidence. The work includes harmonising occupational and registry data, estimating cumulative and time-varying exposures, and examining the effects of exposure mixtures and changes in exposure over working life. The doctoral researcher will use epidemiological and statistical methods to investigate cancer risks, including differences by sex and socioeconomic position. Depending on the research needs, the doctoral researcher may also contribute to other work packages covering rare cancers, cancer survival, and causal pathways. The doctoral researcher will conduct research leading to a doctoral dissertation and contribute to scientific publications and conference presentations. The position also involves participating in project meetings and working closely with the Nordic research team. The research will be based on registry data analysed in secure environments using reproducible statistical methods. Qualifications A Master's degree in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, health sciences, data science, or a related field is required. The selected candidate must also meet the requirements for admission to a relevant doctoral programme at Tampere University. Applicants may be required to provide proof of English proficiency, such as IELTS or TOEFL scores, in accordance with the university's admission requirements. We are looking for a candidate with an interest in occupational and cancer epidemiology and good skills in quantitative research and statistical analysis. The candidate should be able to work independently and as part of a research team. Good written and spoken English skills are required. The selected candidate must also meet the requirements for admission to a relevant doctoral programme (Doctoral Programme in Health Sciences or International Doctoral Programme in Epidemiology and Public Health) at Tampere University. Previous experience in statistical programming, particularly R, and working with large-scale registry or longitudinal data will be considered an advantage. Experience in exposure assessment, survival analysis, or other epidemiological methods is also valuable. Familiarity with job-exposure matrices, time-varying exposures, multilevel models, or causal inference would be beneficial, but is not required. Previous experience with Nordic registry data is not required. We offer The position is fixed-term for 3 years starting in January 2027. A trial period of six months applies to all new employees at Tampere University. The salary will be based on the University Salary System. The salary of a doctoral researcher is at levels 2-4. In addition to the basic salary, a supplementary portion of the salary will be paid based on the appointee’s qualifications and experience. A typical starting salary is approximately 2 800 € / month. Most of the research will take place physically in Tampere, Finland. The appointee is expected to reside in Finland while employed by Tampere University. International staff are supported in relocating to Finland. Tampere University is an internationally renowned research university. We offer a wide range of staff benefits, such as occupational health care, flexible working hours, and excellent sports facilities on campus. Please read more about working at Tampere University. For more information about Tampere, please see Work In Tampere. For further information about Finland, please visit InfoFinland and This is Finland. How To Apply Please submit your application through our online recruitment system (link below). The closing date for applications is 15th November, 2026 (23:59 EET/UTC +2). Please Attach The Following Documents To Your Application Brief CV, (max. 3 pages including a list of publications. Short (max. 1 page) motivation letter describing research interests, relevant experience, and suitability for the position. Degree certificates and transcripts, and a brief description of previous research experience (a master’s thesis). Enquiries For further information about the position please contact Dr. Subas Neupane (subas.neupane@tuni.fi). Tampereen yliopisto hakee väitöskirjatutkijaa NordExCan-hankkeeseen kolmen vuoden sopimuksella. Tehtävä tarjoaa mahdollisuuden tehdä kansainvälisesti merkittävää tutkimusta työperäisten altisteiden, syövän ja terveyserojen yhteyksistä hyödyntäen ainutlaatuisia pohjoismaisia rekisteriaineistoja. Tutustu tehtävään, kelpoisuusvaatimuksiin ja hakuohjeisiin tarkemmin yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta. Hakuaika päättyy 15.11.2026.

items.title: Doctoral student in Material Science - Enable predictive design of 3D-shaped products based on pulp fibres
items.desc: Do you want to help create the next generation of sustainable 3D products from pulp fibres? In this Doctoral project, you will combine materials science, mechanics and multiscale characterisation to establish predictive design rules for transforming fibres into advanced products. You will contribute to research with the potential to replace fossil-based plastics with sustainable alternatives. About Us The Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering pushes the knowledge of chemistry and chemical engineering forward in a broad field of research and education. We offer an international environment, with scientific areas ranging from fundamental chemistry, health and medical technology, materials science, renewable energy, to chemical engineering processing, material recycling, nuclear chemistry, theory and modelling. The Division of Applied Chemistry We primarily focus on applied research, that is, research aimed at addressing societal challenges and that is ready for implementation either immediately or in the near future. Examples of application areas include fossil-free fuels and energy systems, electronic devices, health and technology, the utilisation of fibres and forest-based materials, and various forms of catalysis. About The Research Project Can pulp fibres be engineered into complex 3D products that rival conventional plastics? This Doctoral project aims to transform fibre-based manufacturing from trial-and-error development to predictive design. You will combine experiments, mechanical analysis and multiscale material characterisation to uncover how fibre properties govern deformability, damage, spring-back and shape retention in 3D forming processes. Who We Are Looking For The following requirements are mandatory: To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (120 credits) or an equivalent degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Fibre and Polymer Technology, Wood Technology, Engineering Physics, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology or a related field. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Documented experience from experimental research, thesis work, or industrial projects related to materials, mechanics, manufacturing, polymers, fibre-based materials, or modelling. Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret complex experimental data Ability to collaborate effectively and communicate clearly in multidisciplinary and international environments. The Following Experience Will Strengthen Your Application Experience with fibre-based materials, polymers, paper, packaging, or other sustainable material systems. Experience in experimental materials characterisation, mechanical testing, microscopy, image analysis, or related analytical techniques. Experience with data analysis, modelling, finite element methods, or programming (e.g. Python, MATLAB, or similar tools). Experience working in interdisciplinary teams and communicating scientific results in written reports or presentations. What You Will Do Take courses at an advanced level within the Chalmers graduate education system and actively participate in the research environment of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics, a Vinnova Competence Centre bringing together academia and industry. Conduct research aimed at understanding how fibre properties, material structure and processing conditions influence the formability of lignocellulosic materials into complex three-dimensional products. You will combine experimental studies, multiscale characterisation and data analysis to develop predictive design principles for fibre-based manufacturing. Develop your own scientific ideas and communicate research results through publications in international journals, presentations at conferences, and interactions with industrial partners. Collaborate with researchers from Chalmers, KTH and industrial partners within FibRe, contributing to the development of sustainable alternatives to fossil-based plastics. The position generally includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or other departmental duties corresponding to up to 20% of full-time employment. Contract terms The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start. The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years. The successful candidate will be employed by Chalmers University of Technology and enrolled in the doctoral education programme upon admission. A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026). Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn. The doctoral student will be part of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics, a VINNOVA Competence Centre involving close collaboration with academic and industrial partners and Area of Advance Production. What We Offer As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about working at Chalmers and our benefits for employees. A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg. Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg. Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence. We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities. If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in. Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here. Application procedure The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files. CV Personal letter A brief introduction about yourself. A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position. Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts. Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form. A background check may be conducted as part of the application process. Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview. We welcome your application no later than November 20 For Questions, Please Contact Prof. Anette Larsson anettel@chalmers.se We look forward to your application! Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position. *** Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society. Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

items.title: PhD scholarship in Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells - DTU Physics
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering? Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells , a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data. In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics. Responsibilities And Qualifications The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners. Successful candidates must document: Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE) Python programming skills Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar) Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . Assessment You will be assessed against the responsibilities and qualifications stated above and the following general criteria: Atomistic modelling and DFT experience Python programming experience Machine learning experience Knowledge of materials science, electrochemistry or catalysis Communication skills We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures . The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is from 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Alexander Bagger ( alexbag@dtu.dk ). You can read more about DTU Physics at https://physics.dtu.dk/ . If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time) . Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file . The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter, max 1 page) Curriculum vitae (max 2 pages) Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: PhD Position in Bacteria & Materials Interactions
items.desc: Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Biointerfaces Laboratory at Empa in St. Gallen is offering a PhD position in the field of antimicrobial biomaterials, microbiology, and bacteriophage therapy. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary research team developing innovative living hydrogel systems for the treatment of wound infections caused by antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria and biofilms. This project aims to create a new generation of injectable therapeutic hydrogels that combine beneficial probiotics and bacteriophages to simultaneously eradicate bacterial infections and promote tissue regeneration. With a strong translational focus, the project seeks to advance these living therapeutic systems toward clinically relevant solutions for wound infections and antimicrobial resistance. Your tasks You will contribute to the development of injectable, self-healing biomaterial-based hydrogels for the local delivery of probiotics and bacteriophages to wound sites. Your work will involve: Design and synthesis of injectable hydrogel systems Encapsulation and controlled delivery of probiotics and bacteriophages Engineering and characterization of phage-based antimicrobial strategies against pathogenic bacteria and biofilms Characterization and optimization of hydrogel properties and biological functionality Evaluation of tissue regeneration and the therapeutic potential of living therapeutics Elucidation of mechanisms of action and investigation of antimicrobial resistance evolution Your profile We are looking for a highly motivated and curious candidate with: A Master's degree in Biomaterials, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Chemistry, or a related field Strong interest in antimicrobial resistance, biomaterials, microbiology, or phage therapy Experience in one or more of the following areas: Microbiology and bacterial culture / Biofilm research / Biomaterials and hydrogels / Molecular biology or synthetic biology / Bacteriophages Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an interdisciplinary team Previous experience with phages, hydrogels, wound healing models, or antimicrobial testing is advantageous. Our offer A highly international and multidisciplinary research environment Access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure Scientific training spanning microbiology, biomaterials engineering, phage biology, and translational biomedical research Close collaboration with leading bacteriophage experts at ETH Zurich and opportunities to work across disciplines A stimulating work environment within one of Switzerland's leading research institutions Attractive employment conditions according to Empa regulations The position is available from November 2026 or after negotiation with a duration of four years. We live a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities - that's what counts. We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

items.title: Doktorand i arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL) med fokus på palliativ vård
items.desc: Högskolan Väst drivs av att göra skillnad. Genom vår utbildning och forskning vill vi bidra till innovation, en positiv samhällsutveckling och en hållbar värld. Vi är en modern högskola under stark utveckling och att samverka med omvärlden är prioriterat för oss. Högskolan Väst har ett av landets högsta söktryck och en hög andel av studenterna etablerar sig på arbetsmarknaden. Högskolan har 13 000 studenter och över 700 anställda. Vårt attraktiva campus ligger centralt i Trollhättan och är en plats där kunskaper, idéer, kulturer och människor möts. Vi jobbar aktivt för en inkluderande arbetsmiljö med jämställda förhållanden och sätter värde på de kvaliteter som mångfald tillför verksamheten. Vi som arbetar på Högskolan Väst gör skillnad varje dag. Vill du också det? Doktorand i arbetsintegrerat lärande med inriktning mot palliativ vård. Högskolan Väst söker nu en doktorand i arbetsintegrerat lärande till ett Kamprad-finansierat projekt inom forskningsgruppen NormAIL på Institutionen för hälsovetenskap. Centrala kunskapsområden i avhandlingsarbetet är arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL), vårdvetenskap och virtual reality (VR). Du intresserar dig för frågor om hur VR kan användas vid utbildning i palliativ vård för personal inom demensvård inom kommunal vård- och omsorg. Projektet fokuserar på hur digitala lärmiljöer kan stödja kompetensutveckling och bidra till att stärka personalens förmåga att möta komplexa vårdsituationer i den dagliga verksamheten. Det kan exempelvis handla om: • Hur VR och AI kan användas vid utbildning i palliativ vård för personer med demens inom kommunal vård- och omsorg. • Hur lärande inom palliativ vård påverkar vård och omsorg för personer med demens. • Hur utbildning med stöd av VR och AI påverkar bemötande av personer i livets slut. • Hur ett vetenskapligt förhållningssätt påverkar personal i kommunal vård och omsorg. Doktorandens vetenskapliga arbete i projektet Doktorandens vetenskapliga arbete kommer att genomföras inom ramen för ett forskningsprojekt med fokus mot palliativ vård i demensvård, inom kommunal vård och omsorg. Projektet tar sin utgångspunkt i de förändrade villkor som kommer med en åldrande befolkning och en pågående förskjutning av vården från slutenvård till kommunal vård och omsorg. Projektet undersöker hur virtual reality i kombination med en avatar kan stödja lärande och kompetensutveckling hos personal på ett särskilt boende för personer med demenssjukdom. En central fråga är hur denna form av lärande kan integreras i personalens arbete och hur erfarenheter från vårdpraktiken kan tas till vara. Doktorandprojektet syftar till att bidra till utvecklingen av framtidens utbildningsinsatser inom kommunal vård och omsorg, med särskilt fokus på palliativ vård och demensvård. Genom forskning med hög samhällsrelevans förväntas projektet generera kunskap som kan stärka kvaliteten i vården för äldre personer med komplexa vårdbehov. Projektet ska också bidra med kunskap om förutsättningarna för arbetsintegrerat lärande när ny teknik används för kompetensutveckling inom vård och omsorg. Ämnesområde: Arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL) Forskningsmiljö: Som doktorand vid institutionen för hälsovetenskap tillhör du forskarutbildningen inom AIL vid Högskolan Väst. Du blir verksam i en stark doktorand- och forskningsmiljö som ger möjlighet att förena perspektiv på lärande i arbetslivet med vårdvetenskapliga frågor inom palliativ vård och demensvård. Arbetsuppgifter: Forskarutbildningen innebär, förutom deltagande i forskarutbildningens kurser och andra aktiviteter, genomförande av ett självständigt avhandlingsarbete. Som doktorand ägnas anställningstiden framför allt åt forskarutbildning. En doktorand får dock i begränsad omfattning arbeta med utbildning och administration. Sådant arbete får, innan doktorsexamen har avlagts, inte omfatta mer än 20 % av full arbetstid (Högskoleförordningen 5 kap 2§). Eventuell institutionstjänstgöring (20 %) genomförs huvudsakligen inom undervisningsfältet omvårdnad/vårdvetenskap. Behörighetskrav: För att kvalificera sig för anställning som doktorand krävs att två behörighetskrav är uppfyllda: 1) grundläggande behörighet och 2) särskild behörighet. Grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå har den som: har avlagt examen på grund- och avancerad nivå, fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskild behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå i arbetsintegrerat lärande har den som har: Examen på avancerad nivå med relevans för forskarutbildningsämnet arbetsintegrerat lärande. Examensarbete omfattande minst 15 hp på avancerad nivå eller annat skriftligt arbete av motsvarande karaktär och omfång. Behörighetskraven kan uppfyllas av studier i Sverige eller utomlands. För denna anställning krävs dessutom: God förmåga att kommunicera muntligt och skriftligt på svenska och engelska. Meriterande för anställningen är följande kvalifikationer: Examen inom vårdvetenskap/omvårdnad Utbildning och arbetslivserfarenhet inom demensvård/ palliativvård Erfarenhet av VR och AI i kontexten lärande och/eller vård Tidigare vetenskaplig publicering Bedömningsgrunder: Urval bland sökande ska göras med hänsyn till förmågan att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildningen, vilket avser vetenskaplig kvalitet på tidigare arbeten samt förslag på avhandlingsinriktning, ämnets relevans och genomförbarhet i förhållande till arbetsintegrerat lärande (AIL). Vid bedömningen av projektets genomförbarhetgenomförbarhet kommer även sökandens kunskap och kompetens inom vårdvetenskap, demens, palliativ vård och VR/AI att väga tungt. Under punkt 3 i Allmän studieplan för utbildningen på forskarnivå i Arbetsinegrerat Lärande Dnr 2021/159 kan du läsa mer om behörighetskrav och bedömningsgrunder. Varaktighet och anställningsvillkor: En anställning som doktorand ska gälla tillsvidare, dock längst till en viss tidpunkt och aldrig längre tid än ett år efter avlagd doktorsexamen. Den första anställningen får gälla högst ett år. Anställningen får förnyas med högst två år i taget. Anställningen motsvarar fyra års heltidsstudier under maximalt åtta år (Högskoleförordningen 5 kap 7§). Ansökan Ansökan görs digitalt via Högskolan Västs rekryteringsverktyg Varbi via högskolans webbplats. Ansökan ska bestå av: CV/Meritförteckning Personligt brev innehållande: Intresse för forskningsämnet Tidigare erfarenhet av det föreslagna forskningsämnet och dess forskningsmetoder och vetenskapliga teorier Motiv till att bedriva forskarstudier Examensbevis för kandidat- och masternivå Examensarbete på avancerad nivå Kursförteckning/transcript över alla terminer för kandidat- och masterexamen på originalspråk samt i översättning En kort vetenskaplig reflektion (max två sidor exkl. referenser) med utgångspunkt i den projektbeskrivning som presenteras i utlysningen. Texten ska behandla och problematisera projektets övergripande syfte och ambition att bidra till utvecklingen av framtidens utbildningsinsatser inom kommunal vård och omsorg, med särskilt fokus på palliativ vård för personer med demenssjukdom. Reflektionen ska även beskriva hur ett arbetsintegrerat lärande kan stödja kompetensutveckling och bidra till att stärka personalens arbete samt hur projektet kan bidra till kunskapsutveckling inom AIL. Övriga handlingar som sökanden vill åberopa. Godkända skrivspråk gällande uppsatser, examensbevis, betyg och andra relevanta dokument är skandinaviska språk och engelska, eller översättningar till dessa språk. Vid översättning bifogas även originaltext. Om du har pågående studier på avancerad nivå kan du ansöka och därefter komplettera din ansökan med godkänt examensarbete, giltigt examensbevis och andra behörighetsdokument för sista dagen för ansökan. Din ansökan ska vara Högskolan Väst tillhanda senast 2026-11-11 . De underlag som inte kan skickas digitalt märks med ref.nr R 2026/170 och skickas till: HR-avdelningen Högskolan Väst 461 86 Trollhättan Sverige Institutionen för hälsovetenskap eftersträvar jämställdhet och mångfald inom samtliga yrkesgrupper. Vi välkomnar sökande med olika etniska och kulturella bakgrunder. För oss är det självklart med ett inkluderande arbetsklimat och att våra medarbetare kan kombinera arbete med ett aktivt föräldraskap. Välkommen med din ansökan! Vi undanber oss all direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av rekryteringsannonser.

items.title: Research Associate / Doctoral Candidate (f/m/d) at Psychosomatic Medicine
items.desc: Job description: Research Associate / Doctoral Candidate (m/f/d) at Psychosomatic Medicine and Developmental Neuroscience This position is available starting January 1, 2027, on a part-time basis (30 hours per week) for a fixed term of 3 years. Remuneration is based on the collective agreement for the public service of the federal states (TV-L) and, depending on personal qualifications, may be up to pay grade E13 TV-L. The position is affiliated with the Research Group Applied Developmental Neuroscience (Head: Prof. Dr. med. Stefan Ehrlich, PhD) as well as the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy (Head: Prof. Dr. med. habil. Vjera Holthoff-Detto). It is funded within the framework of the International Research Training Group (IRTG) 2773, in subproject P3, led by PD Dr. habil. Fabio Bernardoni, Dr. Delia Fuhrmann, and PD Dr. med. habil. Eva Mennigen. The International Research Training Group “Risks and Pathomechanisms of Affective Disorders” (IRTG 2773) is funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG). It is a structured international graduate program conducted in cooperation between the Technical University (TU) Dresden and the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience at King’s College London. The successful candidate will receive comprehensive supervision by an experienced scientific team, including participation in a structured curriculum. This curriculum covers topics from developmental neuroscience, child and adolescent as well as adult psychiatry, clinical and cognitive psychology, and in particular computational science. The program is complemented by training in key transferable skills, such as data management and the presentation of scientific results. A six-month research stay at King’s College London under the supervision of Dr. Delia Fuhrmann is planned as part of the curriculum. Subproject P3 focuses on identifying multimodal markers of psychopathology and analysing their topological and network-based longitudinal structure. Using repeated clinical, neuroimaging, genetic, immunological, and behavioural data, we will model latent dimensions of risk and resilience and examine their developmental trajectories in relation to the clinical manifestation of affective disorders. The project will employ advanced machine learning and multivariate data analysis methods, including canonical correlation analysis (CCA), topological data analysis, longitudinal network analysis, and other data-driven approaches. The long-term goal is to advance targeted prevention strategies and personalized interventions. The successful candidate will work in an interdisciplinary team of researchers and clinicians. Responsibilities also include supervising and mentoring research interns, student assistants, and medical students within the project. The results generated in the project are expected to be presented at international conferences and published in peer-reviewed scientific journals. Your profile: an excellent Master’s or Diploma degree in cognitive, computational, and/or affective neuroscience, psychology, psychiatry, or a related field; applicants from quantitatively oriented disciplines such as computer science, physics, statistics, data science, biometrics, or machine learning are explicitly encouraged to apply prior scientific experience, e.g., in statistical methods; ideally, initial efforts toward scientific publications as first or co-author basic programming skills (e.g., Linux/Unix shell scripting, Python, or MATLAB) and/or experience in the analysis of imaging data (FSL, SPM, FreeSurfer, or comparable tools) are advantageous but not mandatory strong interest in mental disorders excellent organizational skills good command of German (B1), both written and spoken very good command of English (C1), both written and spoken We offer: work in a leading medical environment in research, teaching, and clinical care, combined with a highly specialized workplace the opportunity to implement your own ideas and work in an innovative, interdisciplinary team Compensation: Based on the TV-L collective bargaining agreement in pay grade E13, plus an annual bonus, provided you meet the personal requirements Vacation: 30 days of paid vacation Professional Development: Extensive internal and external training and development opportunities to continuously strengthen your skills Company Culture: We value transparency, team spirit, and shared success. Celebrate with us at company gatherings or sporting events like the Rewe Team Challenge Mobility: A subsidy for a job ticket to make your commute eco-friendly and convenient Health: We promote your well-being with modern fitness and exercise programs at our health center, mental health programs, and a comprehensive workplace health management program Shopping benefits: Take advantage of employee discounts at our clinic pharmacy, exclusive corporate benefits, and other shopping portals Work-life balance: Our Family Office supports you with questions regarding daycare spots, vacation programs, and caring for family members. We also offer flexible work arrangements Please include the following documents with your application: Cover letter, CV including publication list, a copy of your degree certificate, and a transcript of records (i.e., the official list of completed courses including grades), as well as your secondary school leaving certificate (e.g., Abitur). If available, please also include letters of recommendation and proof of English and German language proficiency. For further information, please contact PD Dr. habil. Fabio Bernardoni by phone at +49 351 458-15245 or via email at fabio.bernardoni@ukdd.de .

items.title: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling
items.desc: Some features of our web site require JavaScript to function properly. Please enable JavaScript in your browser. Position PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling Employer The Department of Meteorology, Stockholm University The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University (MISU) conducts research and education spanning the atmosphere, ocean and physical climate sciences. MISU offers educational programmes at the Bachelor's, Master's and PhD levels. Our research addresses fundamental questions concerning the dynamics, physics, chemistry and biogeochemistry of the atmosphere and ocean relevant to weather and climate. MISU strives toward a broad representation of research within our scientific domain. We study questions originating from the deep ocean to the upper atmosphere and from the tropics to the poles. In this effort, we use and develop theory, statistical methods, and numerical models in close interplay with observations. We also develop and lead observational research using remote-sensing and in-situ measurements, including satellite missions and icebreaker expeditions to the Arctic. The department has around 60 employees and is embedded in a larger research environment, including the Bolin Centre for Climate Research, the Baltic Sea Centre and the Swedish e-Science Research Centre. The department is highly international, with over half of our employees coming from outside Sweden and both Swedish and English are used as working languages. We welcome and value diversity in our working environment. You can read more about us here: the Department of Meteorology. Homepage: https://www.su.se/english/divisions/department-of-meteorology Location Stockholm, Sweden Sector Academic Relevant divisions Atmospheric Sciences (AS) Ocean Sciences (OS) Type Full time Level Student / Graduate / Internship Salary Open Preferred Education Master Application deadline 3 November 2026 Posted 21 October 2026 Job Description Project description Clouds and their responses to varying environmental conditions are particularly important determinants of current climate and future climate change. However, the resolution of a typical climate model is far too coarse to explicitly represent processes of relevance to cloud formation. Those processes therefore need to be parameterized, or represented as functions of large-scale state variables. Such sub-grid scale parameterizations are associated with large uncertainties, and are also computationally expensive. This project focuses on novel ways to bridge between micro- and global scales, to improve climate model accuracy, efficiency and generalizability, and leverage modern computer architecture. We will explore the use of machine learning (ML) models trained on combinations of observational data and high-resolution simulations, as alternatives to empirical parameterizations of essential, unresolved sub-grid scale processes related to turbulence, cloud formation and aerosol-cloud interaction. The tasks will include deriving and training data-driven models, coupling them to a large-scale climate model, evaluating the results against observations and traditionally parameterized models, and using the ML-enhanced model to estimate climate-relevant quantities like cloud radiative effects and forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions. The work will be carried out in close collaboration with data scientists within the Swedish e-Science Research Centre, and contribute to development of methods with applicability also beyond climate science. The successful candidate will thereby develop their skills in atmospheric science and climate modelling, but also in data science and machine learning, and in communicating and collaborating within and across disciplines. Qualification Requirements In order to be admitted to postgraduate education, the applicant must have the general and specific entry requirements. The qualification requirements must be fulfilled before admission to the programme. You meet general entry requirements if you have completed a second-cycle degree, or completed courses equivalent to at least 240 higher education credits, of which 60 credits must be in the second cycle, or have otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. The specific entry requirements additionally require a minimum of 90 higher education credits in any of the fields of meteorology, oceanography, physics or chemistry; and at least 15 higher education credits in mathematics as well as a degree project of at least 15 higher education credits. At least 60 higher education credits of these courses must be on the second-cycle level. In addition, proficiency in English language, equivalent to English B in Swedish high school, is required. The specific entry requirements may also be fulfilled by a person who has otherwise acquired equivalent knowledge in Sweden or elsewhere. General syllabus for doctoral studies in atmospheric science and oceanography. Selection The selection between candidates who meet the entry requirements will be made with reference to their ability to benefit from the training. However, the fact that an applicant is deemed able to transfer credits from previous training or professional experience may not alone give the applicant priority over other applicants in the selection process. Admission decisions are made in accordance with current delegation policies. The assessment criteria for admission to the postgraduate programme in atmospheric sciences and oceanography are familiarity with the theory and applications of the subject, subject knowledge relevant to the research project, the ability to express oneself orally and in writing, proficiency in English, analytical ability, creativity, initiative, independence and the ability to work collaboratively. The assessment of the applicant’s ability in these respects are based on the relevance and results of completed higher education courses, the quality and scope of the independent project, references, interviews and a personal statement from the applicant describing their expectations of, and intentions regarding, the programme. Admission Regulations for Doctoral Studies at Stockholm University. About The Employment Starting date as per agreement. We offer a fixed-term employment as a doctoral student according to Chapter 5 of the Higher Education Ordinance (1993:100). The period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for four years. As a doctoral student, you should primarily devote yourself to your own doctoral education, but the employment may include work with education, research and administration to a limited extent (maximum 20 %). A new employment as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, the employment is then renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. Stockholm University strives to be a workplace free from discrimination and with equal opportunities for all. Contact For more information about the project, please contact professor Frida Bender, frida.bender@misu.su.se. For more information about the PhD programme, please contact the study director, Associate Professor Thorsten Mauritsen thorsten.mauritsen@misu.su.se. For information about the recruitment process and terms of employment, please contact Head of Administration Sara Engström, sara.engstrom@misu.su.se. Application Apply for the PhD student position at Stockholm University's recruitment system. Attach a personal letter and CV as well as the attachments requested in the application form. It is the responsibility of the applicant to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the job advertisement, and that it is submitted before the deadline. We kindly ask applicants to refrain from submitting AI-generated applications. The instructions for applicants are available at: How to apply for a position. Stockholm University contributes to the development of sustainable democratic society through knowledge, enlightenment and the pursuit of truth. How to apply Apply here: PhD student in Atmospheric Sciences and Oceanography, focus on ML-methods in climate modelling Go back

items.title: Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student)
items.desc: Login and apply The Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology, School of Computing The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in the field of Development of Data Science and AI for Spatial Data at the School of Computing on the Kuopio campus. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). Please find more information below and submit your application by 17 November 2026. Role and salary The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website), funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI. We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications. One Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will be recruited for each of the following three research topics: mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams) mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites. Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science. Your main duty as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for the doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies. The positions will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 February 2027 (or as agreed). The positions will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff. The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month. Our requirements and expectations We require you to be eligible for postgraduate studies; i.e., to hold a Master’s degree in a quantitative field (e.g., Data Science, Computer Science, Engineering, Geoinformatics, Statistics, or a related field) awarded by a university or by a university of applied sciences, or to have completed an applicable study programme abroad which in the awarding country gives eligibility for corresponding postgraduate education meet the student admission criteria for the LUMETO doctoral programme (Doctoral Programme in Science, Forestry and Technology, website) have a good command of written and spoken English. Students in the final stages of their Master’s degree may also apply provided that they complete their degree and deliver a copy of their degree certificate to the faculty by 15 December 2026. Applicants who do not yet have the right to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Eastern Finland are not required to apply for study rights at the application stage. If the applicant is selected for the position and applies for postgraduate study rights, the selection will be conditional until the right to pursue postgraduate studies in the faculty’s doctoral programme has been granted. The application for postgraduate study rights is submitted through the Studyinfo (Opintopolku) service. Other requirements good programming skills (e.g., Python/R) interest in machine learning and spatial data. The following will be considered an advantage experience with machine learning or deep learning (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) or strong motivation to learn these skills experience with Earth observation or geospatial data, desirable, but we encourage anyone with a strong willingness to learn to apply experience with cloud computing or collaborative software development (e.g., GitHub) is also welcome. Your benefits You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including the opportunity for flexible multi-location work excellent opportunities for professional development and continuous learning extensive occupational health care a broad selection of staff training staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services affordable sports services. Please read more in the Work at UEF section on our website. You will have an opportunity to work in meaningful as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community. Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the Life in Finland section on our website to learn more. How to apply? Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 17 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2). Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application CV (Template for CV, TENK web page) a list of publications (Instructions, Research Council of Finland Web page) copies of your academic degree certificates / diplomas, and copies of certificates / diplomas relating to your language proficiency, if not indicated in the academic degree certificates/diplomas a transcript of records a motivation letter (max. 1 page) describing your interest in the position and research project, your background, as well as your career aspirations and your motivation for engaging in doctoral-level research. In the cover letter, indicate your preferred topic(s), for example, by ranking the topics in order of preference or specifying whether you are applying for one or multiple topics. External evaluation will be used in the recruitment process. If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator's stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted. Questions? For further information on the position, please contact Professor Markku Tukiainen, email: markku.tukiainen@uef.fi, tel. +358 29 445 3653. For further information on the application procedure, please contact HR Specialist Iiris Korhonen, email: iiris.korhonen@uef.fi, tel. +358 29 4458161 or HR Specialist Noora Hämäläinen, email: noora.hamalainen@uef.fi, tel. +358 29 4458302. Haemme kolmea väitöskirjatutkijaa Itä-Suomen yliopistolle. Tehtävät sijoittuvat luonnontieteiden, metsätieteiden ja tekniikan tiedekuntaan tietojenkäsittelytieteiden laitokselle Kuopion kampukselle. Tehtävät alkavat 1.2.2027 (tai sopimuksen mukaan) ja ne täytetään kolmen vuoden määräajaksi. Tehtävissä tehtäväkohtainen palkanosa on vaativuustasoluokittelussa tasoilla 2–4. Lisäksi maksetaan henkilökohtaiseen suoriutumiseen perustuvaa palkanosaa, joka on 6–50 % tehtäväkohtaisesta palkanosasta. Tehtävissä edellytetään hyvää englannin kielen taitoa. Lue tarkemmat tiedot tehtävistä ja hakuohjeet yllä olevasta englanninkielisestä ilmoituksesta. Jätäthän hakemuksesi englanniksi. Hakuaika tehtäviin päättyy 17.11.2026. The Faculty of Science, Forestry and Technology operates on the Kuopio and Joensuu campuses of the University of Eastern Finland. The mission of the faculty is to carry out internationally recognised scientific research and to offer research-education in the fields of natural sciences, forestry and technology. The faculty invests in all of the strategic research areas of the university. The faculty’s environments for research and learning are international, modern and multidisciplinary. The faculty has approximately 2,650 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students and some 440 postgraduate students. The number of staff amounts to 650. The University of Eastern Finland (UEF) is the most multidisciplinary university in Finland. Our university employs approximately 3,200 employees, and our community includes approximately 17,000 degree students and 16,000 adult education students. Our campuses are located in Joensuu and Kuopio. We represent the world’s cutting edge of research in many fields and produce research-based knowledge, which is made openly available to benefit everyone. Learn more about our university at www.uef.fi/en. Read also about UEF as a working community and employer and the career stories of our employees. items.title: PhD Position F/M Detecting Dangerous Browser Extensions to Protect the Security and Privacy of Web Users
items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Doctorant A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle Inria is the French National Institute for Research in Digital Science, of which the Inria Côte d'Azur University Center is a part. With strong expertise in computer science and applied mathematics, the research projects of the Inria Côte d'Azur University Center cover all aspects of digital science and technology and generate innovation. Based mainly in Sophia Antipolis, but also in Nice and Montpellier, it brings together 47 research teams and nine support services. It is active in the fields of artificial intelligence, data science, IT system security, robotics, network engineering, natural risk prevention, ecological transition, digital biology, computational neuroscience, health data, and more. The Inria Center at Université Côte d'Azur is a major player in terms of scientific excellence, thanks to the results it has achieved and its collaborations at both European and international level. Contexte et atouts du poste The PhD position is funded by the French National Research Agency (ANR). It is part of Aurore Fass' ANR JCJC project "EXPELLIARMUS: Disarming Dangerous Browser Extensions to Protect the Security and Privacy of Web Users". EXPELLIARMUS, aims to develop methods to "disarm" dangerous extensions to better protect the security and privacy of Web users. More specifically, it will detect, understand, and mitigate dangerous browser extensions through an interdisciplinary approach combining computer science, human factors, and legal analysis. EXPELLIARMUS will deliver a systematic taxonomy of dangerous extension behaviors, open-source datasets and detection tools, as well as actionable recommendations for users, browser vendors, developers, and regulators. The PhD student will be part of the research team led by Dr. Nataliia Bielova (https://www-sop.inria.fr/members/Nataliia.Bielova/index.html) at the Inria Centre at Université Côte d’Azur at the French Riviera. The PhD student will be supervised by Dr.-Ing. Aurore Fass (https://aurore54f.github.io/). Note that a PhD in France typically lasts 3 years. Mission confiée Context on Browser Extension Security Given the central role of the Web in our daily lives and its overall impact on society and economy, it is crucial that Web pages and browser extensions assure the security and privacy of their large user base. Browser extensions have become an integral part of the modern Web ecosystem. The most popular desktop browser Chrome lists 280k browser extensions [1] (totaling almost 3 billion active users) in its official gallery, the Chrome Web Store [2]. Browser extensions enable users to enhance and customize their browsing experience: typically, extensions offer additional functionality to Web users, such as ad blocking (e.g., AdBlock), grammar checks (e.g., Grammarly), or password management (e.g., LastPass). To operate, browser extensions need elevated privileges compared to Web pages. Browser extensions can access sensitive user data, such as cookies or browsing history, and they can interact with arbitrary websites and other extensions [3, 4, 5]. While a compromised or malicious Web page is in itself troublesome, a malicious or vulnerable browser extension is much more powerful, as an attacker can leverage an extension's elevated privileges to cause more harm [3]. In particular, browser extensions can exfiltrate sensitive user data [6], track users online [7], or propagate unwanted software [8]. Detecting such threats at scale remains a challenge, as the extension ecosystem is particularly large, diverse, and continuously evolving. Limitations of existing work Abundant prior work attempted to detect some classes of dangerous extensions [9], e.g., malicious [10], vulnerable [3], or fingerprintable extensions [11]. However, related works have major limitations. Existing works analyze only hundreds of extensions [12], are outdated (e.g., 2012–2015 [8, 13, 14, 15]), have limited scalability and necessitate significant manual effort [16, 4], lack a clear characterization of what a dangerous behavior is [14]; and finally, only a small minority thereof is open source, as we have highlighted in [10]. Besides, existing machine learning-based detectors are opaque, they lack interpretability and explainability. It is therefore critical to design automated, large-scale, and reliable security and privacy analyses of browser extensions that have the potential to be deployed in the real world. References : [1] chrome-stats. Chrome extension statistics. https://chrome-stats.com/chrome/stats [2] Google. Chrome Web Store. https://chromewebstore.google.com [3] Aurore Fass , Dolière Francis Somé, Michael Backes, and Ben Stock. DoubleX: Statically Detecting Vulnerable Data Flows in Browser Extensions at Scale. In ACM CCS, 2021. Code repository: https://github.com/Aurore54F/DoubleX [4] Dolière Francis Somé. Empoweb: Empowering web applications with browser extensions. In IEEE S&P, 2019. [5] Jianjia Yu, Song Li, Junmin Zhu, and Yinzhi Cao. Coco: Efficient browser extension vulnerability detection via coverage-guided, con- current abstract interpretation. In ACM CCS, 2023. [6] Quan Chen and Alexandros Kapravelos. Mystique: Uncovering information leakage from browser extensions. In ACM CCS, 2018. [7] Michael Weissbacher, Enrico Mariconti, Guillermo Suarez-Tangil, Gianluca Stringhini, William Robertson, and Engin Kirda. Ex-ray: Detection of history-leaking browser extensions. In ACSAC, 2017. [8] Xinyu Xing, Wei Meng, Byoungyoung Lee, Udi Weinsberg, Anmol Sheth, Roberto Perdisci, and Wenke Lee. Understanding malvertising through ad-injecting browser extensions. In TheWebConf, 2015. [9] Sheryl Hsu, Manda Tran, and Aurore Fass . What is in the Chrome Web Store? Investigating Security-Noteworthy Browser Extensions. In ACM AsiaCCS, 2024. [10] Ben Rosenzweig, Valentino Dalla Valle, Giovanni Apruzzese, and Aurore Fass . It's not easy: Applying supervised machine learning to detect malicious extensions in the chrome web store. In ACM Transactions on the Web (TWEB), 2026. Code repository: https://github.com/its-not-easy/tweb25/tree/main [11] Shubham Agarwal, Aurore Fass , and Ben Stock. Peeking through the window: Fingerprinting browser extensions through page-visible execution traces and interactions. In ACM CCS, 2024. Code repository: https://github.com/raider-ext/raider [12] Nicholas Carlini, Adrienne Porter Felt, and David Wagner. An evaluation of the google chrome extension security architecture. In USENIX Security, 2012. [13] Nav Jagpal, Eric Dingle, Jean-Philippe Gravel, Panayiotis Mavrommatis, Niels Provos, Moheeb Abu Rajab, and Kurt Thomas. Trends and lessons from three years fighting malicious extensions. In USENIX Security, 2015. [14] Alexandros Kapravelos, Chris Grier, Neha Chachra, Christopher Kruegel, Giovanni Vigna, and Vern Paxson. Hulk: Eliciting malicious behavior in browser extensions. In USENIX Security, 2014. [15] Kurt Thomas, Elie Bursztein, Chris Grier, Grant Ho, Nav Jagpal, Alexandros Kapravelos, Damon Mccoy, Antonio Nappa, Vern Paxson, Paul Pearce, Niels Provos, and Moheeb Abu Rajab. Ad injection at scale: Assessing deceptive advertisement modifications. In IEEE S&P, 2015. [16] Nikolaos Pantelaios, Nick Nikiforakis, and Alexandros Kapravelos. You’ve changed: Detecting malicious browser extensions through their update deltas. In ACM CCS, 2020. Principales activités Objectives of the PhD The broad objective of this PhD is to develop new automated tools to detect dangerous browser extensions , with a specific focus on malicious extensions. While the majority of prior work focuses on Chrome, we also want to study dangerous extensions on other browsers, such as Firefox and Edge, since we showed that the same malicious extensions can be published on multiple galleries [1]. Objective 1 : Generate a large-scale dataset of browser extensions. Establish a systematic and comprehensive taxonomy of dangerous browser extension behaviors. Objective 2 : Design novel, automated, and explainable methods to detect dangerous browser extensions, combining JavaScript static and lightweight dynamic analyses, predictive machine learning, and Large-Language Models. Provide interpretable and continuously adaptable detection models. Objective 3 (in collaboration with a postdoctoral researcher, to be recruited): Assess how different stakeholders (i.e., platform maintainers, developers, and users) understand and manage the underlying security and privacy risks of browser extensions. Keywords : Web Security & Privacy, Browser Extensions, Dangerous Behavior Detection, Code Analysis, Applied Machine Learning, (Human Factors). References : [1] Abdullah Hassan Chaudhry, Valentino Dalla Valle, and Aurore Fass . Two Heads are Better Than One: Analysing Browser Extensions Across Stores. In MADWeb (workshop co-located with NDSS), 2026. Code repository: https://github.com/abdchau/two-heads-are-better Compétences Skills : A successful candidate for a PhD: should have a strong background in Computer Science ( Master degree or equivalent); with a major ideally in Cybersecurity ; their research interests should be in Web Security, Web Privacy, or Web Measurements . We are looking for a motivated student with: solid programming skills in python ; (at least) a basic background in Web Security & Privacy ; students with prior knowledge with Web-development technology (e.g., JavaScript), browser extensions, and browser architecture will be given priority; some basic knowledge of Machine Learning is a plus; proficiency in spoken and written English is a must ( C1 level or higher); French knowledge is not necessary (note that English is the default language in the team); we expect the student to be curious, creative, and have a strong willingness to learn and improve . Avantages Subsidized meals Partial reimbursement of public transport costs Leave: 7 weeks of annual leave + 10 extra days off due to RTT (statutory reduction in working hours) + possibility of exceptional leave (sick children, moving home, etc.) Possibility of teleworking and flexible organization of working hours Professional equipment available (videoconferencing, loan of computer equipment, etc.) Social, cultural and sports events and activities Access to vocational training Employer-sponsored health insurance plan Rémunération Gross salary per month: 2300 € 36-month fixed-term contract Informations générales Ville : Sophia Antipolis Centre Inria : Centre Inria d'Université Côte d'Azur Date de prise de fonction souhaitée : 2027-04-01 Durée de contrat : 3 ans Date limite pour postuler : 2026-11-22 Attention : Les candidatures doivent être déposées en ligne sur le site Inria. Le traitement des candidatures adressées par d'autres canaux n'est pas garanti. L’autorisation d’accès à une zone est délivrée par le chef d’établissement, après avis ministériel favorable, tel que défini dans l’arrêté du 03 juillet 2012, relatif à la PPST. Un avis ministériel défavorable pour un poste affecté dans une ZRR aurait pour conséquence l’annulation du recrutement. It operates a 3.4 km-long X-ray laser, which produces X-rays of unique quality for studies in physics, chemistry, the life sciences, materials research and other disciplines. The diverse scientific facilities at European XFEL enable scientists from across the globe to carry out a wide range of experimental techniques. For our EXPLODE group we are looking for a PhD student - Microstructural Dynamics of Fusion Targets (f/m/d) - 29,25 hours/week The Position This PhD project is funded by the BMFTR as part of the "EXPLODE" (Experimental X-ray Platforms for Optimisation and Diagnosis of inertial fusion Energy) research group and is focused on developing X-ray imaging diagnostics together with the HED- HiBEF instrument. The BMFTR Project code is 13F1044 for the project "Experimentelle Röntgenplattformen zur Optimierung und Diagnose der Trägheitsfusion" (EXPLODE). Contribute to the development and application of X-ray imaging methods for the investigation of laser-driven, fusion-relevant targets. Analyse experimental data and help establish robust, well-documented workflows for the evaluation of X-ray imaging measurements. Support the preparation, fabrication and characterisation of nanostructured targets for experiments. Assist with the planning, preparation and execution of experiments at European XFEL and other facilities, including beamtime applications. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists. The Advanced Multilayer X-ray Optics group at CFEL is one of the leading research groups developing novel X-ray lenses and gratings with nanometre control. As part of a collaborative project between Hamburg and Trento we plan to combine these elements with attosecond-duration X-ray laser pulses to image, understand and ultimately control electron dynamics in molecular systems. We are looking for a highly motivated PhD student to develop an attosecond X-ray interferometer to measure ultrafast responses of materials and molecules and to help create movies of electron dynamics for the first time. items.title: PhD position: High-Throughput Development of Chemical Conversion Treatment for Light Metals
items.desc: Beginn der Ausschreibung 21.10.2026 Ende der Ausschreibung 03.11.2026 Institut bzw. Bereich Institut für Oberflächenforschung Standort Geesthacht Aluminium and magnesium alloys are key to lighter vehicles, aircraft, drones and consumer goods but only if they are safe and durable, reliably protected against corrosion. Chemical conversion coatings are one of the most effective and commercially successful ways to do this. They protect the metal and help paint adhere to it. Yet finding better, environmentally friendly formulations is still largely a matter of trial and error. The number of possible formulations is virtually infinite, so we do not test them one by one. At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data, we run a robotic high-throughput testing platform combined with machine learning for AI-assisted discoveries. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a PhD student in the quickly developing field of high-throughput and robotic experimentation in materials science. The position is part-time (19,5 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg). We value diversity and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply. items.desc: Vacature ID: 16964 Functie categorie: PhD-posities Aanstellingsomvang in uren min: 38 Aanstellingsomvang in uren max: 38 Standplaats: Leiden Solliciteren kan tot en met: 11 januari 2028 The Institute of Environmental Sciences CML and Faculty of Science is looking for: PhD Researcher Excited to explore how population decline and changing demographic structures redefine urban planning, where and what we decide (not) to build, and what this means for resource demand and the environment? Key responsibilities The primary objective of this PhD project is to advance understanding of how spatial population distribution, demographic change (including aging population and smaller households), and urban form jointly shape future resource demand and GHG emissions. The project will evaluate core trade-offs, balancing the efficiency gains of urban density against the rise in vacant buildings and underutilized infrastructure caused by regional depopulation. Ultimately, the research will inform urban and regional development strategies to minimize net land take and GHG emissions, while catering to the needs of changing populations across the rural-urban continuum. As a PhD researcher on this project, you will: Develop high-resolution activity demand models for the building energy and transport sectors under future spatially refined European demographic projections. Integrate demand projections with material flow and life-cycle models to quantify future energy requirements, material intensity, and GHG emissions. Evaluate adaptive re-use and circular strategies for vacant buildings and underutilized transport infrastructure in depopulating or aging regions. Design integrated spatial planning scenarios that combine built environment transformations with transport infrastructure investments to support low resource and emission development pathways across population change and urban/rural contexts Where you will work Leiden University is situated between Amsterdam (36 km) and The Hague (15 km) and was founded in 1575, making it the oldest university in the Netherlands. It houses around 35,000 students originating from 112 nationalities, facilitated by approximately 8,000 staff. The Institute of Environmental Science (CML) at Leiden University offers a vibrant and supportive community of scientists committed to the challenges of sustainability. CML distinguishes itself for its attention to professional development in coordination with the interests of its scientists. As such, there are plenty of opportunities to learn new skills, expand your knowledge, collaborate across disciplines, and experiment in a friendly environment fully embodying academic freedom across all career levels. The core focus of CML is to perform research and education in the interdisciplinary field of Environmental Sciences. CML focuses on the sustainable use of natural resources and preservation of natural capital and biodiversity. CML has a culture of mutual support and collaboration between researchers. CML has two Departments: Industrial Ecology (CML-IE) and Environmental Biology (CML-EB). Presently, about 150 fte (including postdocs and PhDs) are employed at CML. CML further collaborates with TU Delft and Erasmus University in the Leiden-Delft-Erasmus Centre for Sustainability (LDE-CfS), and with the Naturalis Biodiversity Centre. The Institute of Environmental Sciences (CML) is positioned in the Faculty of Sciences. The Faculty of Science is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expanding fundamental knowledge by curiosity and looking beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science and to make a contribution to addressing the major societal challenges of the future. The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelor’s and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2.800 staff and almost 6000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together. For more information, see www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science . Information about CML can be found at www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/science/environmental-sciences .
