items.title: PhD Student Positions on Networked Physical AI Multi-Agent Systems
items.desc: The Networked Systems Lab of the Universidad Miguel Hernández (UMH) de Elche (Spain) offers several fully-funded PhD positions in Networked Physical AI Multi-Agent Systems. Successful candidates will work in an internationally recognized research group with extensive collaborations in academia and industry, publish in top-tier journals and conferences, contribute to active projects (and proposals) and have opportunities for international collaborations. The Networked Systems Lab (formerly UWICORE laboratory) is internationally-recognized for its research on wireless networking for connected and automated mobility and smart manufacturing. The laboratory is actively involved in EU and national projects, standardization and R&D contracts with industrial partners. Some of the PhD projects will be carried out in collaboration with industrial partners in the US. The laboratory is located in the Mediterranean coast of Spain (Elche) and is part of the Department of Communications Engineering of the Universidad Miguel Hernández (UMH) and of the Institute for Engineering Research (I3E) of Elche. Tasks Future Physical AI systems will be characterized by large populations of autonomous embodied agents – including collaborative robots and connected autonomous vehicles– operating in shared physical environments. Unlike today's agentic AI systems, which primarily execute predefined workflows in structured and well-defined digital environments, future Physical AI agents will have to perceive, reason and act under unstructured and continuously evolving real-world conditions and objectives. This calls for a fundamental rethinking of how agents interact, requiring intelligence and semantic and task-oriented networking to be co-designed so that agents can collaboratively construct meaningful representations of the physical world, reason over existing (shared) context and knowledge, and adapt their networking and interactions to efficiently accomplish individual and collective tasks. Our lab is offering several PhD positions on research at the intersection of Physical AI, multi-agent systems, and 6G networks. The research will focus on developing solutions that enable autonomous agents to perceive, reason, network, and collaborate effectively in dynamic real-world environments. The research may also include interactions between embodied agents and agents at the 6G edge-cloud continuum infrastructure, as well as AI-network-control co-design. Research will initially be framed in collaborative mobile robotics and connected automated mobility, while developing scientific foundations that generalize to a broader range of cyber-physical systems. Specific research topics will be discussed during the interviews, and they can be co-defined with selected candidates based on their background, expertise, and research interests. The positions are for three years and will start as soon as possible. The positions are fully funded according to the Spanish PhD employment scheme and include full social security benefits. Requirements Candidates should hold (or be close to completing) a Master’s degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical, Electronic, or Telecommunications Engineering (or related disciplines). Strong interest or experience in one or more of the following topics is required: Artificial Intelligence, Physical AI, autonomous systems (e.g., mobile robotics and connected and automated vehicles), multi-agent systems, networking, 6G. Candidates should have good programming skills (e.g., C++ and/or Python) as well as good theoretical foundations and strong critical thinking skills. Experience with popular machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) or simulation environments is considered a plus, but not required. Previous research experience or publications are positively considered but are not required. Good English writing and speaking skills as well as curiosity, self-motivation, and team-working attitude are essential.

items.title: Doctoral student in Explainable Machine Learning for Nuclear Safeguards
items.desc: Are you excited to push the boundaries of artificial intelligence in nuclear technology? Join us as a doctoral student to explore the advanced frontier of AI-driven nuclear safeguards and enhance global nuclear safety and security. About us The Reactor Physics, Modelling and Safety group at Chalmers develops advanced methods for modelling, simulation, monitoring and safety analysis of current and next-generation nuclear reactors. Combining expertise in reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear safeguards, diagnostic techniques and machine learning applied to nuclear technology, the group conducts both fundamental and applied research in collaboration with national and international partners across academia and industry. We are part of the Division of Subatomic, High Energy and Plasma Physics, at the Department of Physics and Astronomy, offering a dynamic and stimulating working environment. About the research project Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models are powerful tools for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection. However, their architectural and optimization complexity renders them black boxes, posing a challenge when making critical decisions, such as classifying SNF as either consistent or inconsistent with declared information. In this doctoral research, you will investigate an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework to enable transparency in ANN models and their predictions for SNF inspection, bridging high-performing machine learning with transparent nuclear verification. Who we are looking for The following requirements are mandatory: To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or equivalent. You have strong written and verbal communication skills in English. You have background/experience in at least one of the following areas: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Explainable AI, Reactor Physics, Nuclear Safeguards. You have a solid background in computational methods and strong programming skills (e.g., in Python). You thrive in a collaborative environment and take responsibility for your work. You have a strong analytical mindset and enjoy complex challenges. for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted. What you will do Conduct doctoral research focused on exploring, testing, and evaluating an Explainable AI (XAI) framework for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection. Integrate various XAI methods and study semantic layers to aggregate predictions into actionable explanations for safeguards inspectors. Leverage XAI insights to guide ANN model architectures, optimize training strategies, and strengthen model robustness. Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate research results through peer-reviewed journal publications and conference presentations. Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Nuclear Engineering. The position generally also includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours. Contract terms The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start. items.title: Doctoral Student in Environmental Bioengineering
items.desc: Doctoral Student in Environmental Bioengineering 100%, Zurich, fixed-term The Environmental Microfluidics Group of Prof. Roman Stocker in the Institute of Environmental Engineering is seeking a dynamic and motivated doctoral student with an engineering background for a project on how bacterial chemotaxis accelerates plasmid transfer, including the spread of antibiotic resistance. The position is funded by a recently awarded SNSF grant, and the project is a joint effort with Prof. Jonasz Slomka at the University of Warsaw. This position will be based in the laboratory of Prof. Roman Stocker. Project background Bacterial conjugation, the contact-dependent transfer of plasmids between cells, speeds up bacterial evolution and is a major route for the spread of antibiotic resistance in the environment, which in turn poses a global health threat. Aquatic environments are full of microscale chemical hotspots, such as the nutrient-rich 'phycosphere' around phytoplankton and sinking marine particles, and chemotactic bacteria are known to find and accumulate rapidly at these locations. This project will test the hypothesis that this accumulation enhances plasmid spreading in the environment, contributing to a cutting-edge view of the role of antibiotic resistance in nature. The project seeks to study when, where and how strongly this enhancement operates across different chemical hotspots, fluid flows and bacterial strains, and what it means for the spread of antibiotic resistance among aquatic bacteria. Job description This is a primarily experimental PhD at the interface of engineering and microbiology. The student will: Design, build and characterize new instrumentation to couple existing chemotaxis assays to controlled shear systems. This includes mechanical design, 3D ing, control systems and integration with a fluorescence microscope. Run chemotaxis and conjugation experiments with bacterial donors and recipients of plasmids and a range of chemoattractants, with the opportunity to learn and use advanced techniques such as flow cytometry and plate-reader-based plasmid transfer quantification. Image and track fluorescently labeled bacteria and chemical plumes in shear flow, and analyze the data with quantitative image- and data-analysis pipelines. Test clinically relevant bacteria and freshwater (e.g. lake) bacteria, to assess the potential for chemotaxis-driven spread of resistance in the environment. Contribute data to mathematical models of plasmid spread. Profile We are looking for a hands-on, skilled and curious engineer who loves to build new tools and is interested in using them to answer fundamental scientific questions. Ideal candidates hold an MSc degree in bioengineering, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, environmental engineering, physics or a related discipline, and have some (not necessarily all) of the following skills: Practical experience in prototyping and manufacturing, for example CAD, 3D ing, machining (strongly preferred). Experience with control systems and instrumentation, for example motor control, sensors, microcontrollers, and automation or data-acquisition code (Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW or similar) (preferred). Openness to gain experience in the microbiology laboratory: bacterial cultures, sterile technique, plate readers and flow cytometry. Familiarity with microscopy, image analysis, fluid mechanics or microfluidics (beneficial but not necessary). Fluency in English (oral and written), enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international team, and the drive to pursue scientific excellence (required). You will be guided by Prof. Roman Stocker and by members of his lab with extensive experience in microbiology, experimental techniques and environmental processes. You will have the opportunity to work in a cutting-edge, fast-paced research environment, interact with researchers from many different disciplines (engineers, physicists, microbiologists, oceanographers, chemists, mathematicians), gain technical experience across diverse research approaches and interact with world-class collaborators. Workplace Workplace We offer ETH Zurich is a family-friendly employer with excellent working conditions. You can look forward to an exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits. We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values, ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future. Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application by December 15th, 2026, including the following documents: Curriculum vitae Cover letter (max one page, including brief motivation, research interests and possible start date) Full transcript from undergraduate studies (both Bachelor and Masters, including grades) Copy of Master’s or Bachelor’s thesis (PDF) At least two reference letters Further information about The Stocker Lab can be found on our Website. Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr Stefano Ugolini, gugolini@ethz.ch (no applications). Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered. We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

items.title: PhD position NCCR Genesis: combining remote and in-situ life detection techniques
items.desc: NCCR Genesis: background The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) and the Division for Space Research and Planetary Sciences (WP) at the University of Bern invite applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis. The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress. Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch. Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups. Project description Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life. This PhD project will investigate for the first time the combination of remote life sensing techniques using circular spectro-polarimetry with in situ laser-based mass spectrometry measurements, both designed for the detection or signatures of life. The work will mainly involve experiments in the lab, using cell cultures of a range of strains (including anaerobic cultivation of microorganisms) and various classes of organic molecules relevant to Solar System environments. These studies will be complemented by targeted field measurements of soil material containing microorganisms and low abundant organics that are relevant candidates for extinct/extant life on Mars or in the icy moons of the solar system. The results of this endeavour will reveal the potential of combining life detection methods at different scales that will be key to define optimal strategies for future life-detection missions, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus or future NASA mission to Mars. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics. Profile We are looking for a creative and motivated candidate, a team player, with a MSc degree in physics, chemistry, or biology. Willingness to learn microbiological techniques is essential; prior wet lab experience is an asset. No prior expertise in optics is required; training will be provided, though a basic understanding of polarization, vacuum technology and/or mass spectrometry is a plus. Excellent oral and written skills in English are a requirement. What we offer The position is based at the Centre for Space and Habitability, which strives to investigate key questions in space sciences through interdisciplinarity. The team collaborates tightly with various national and international partners. This includes for example the Microbiology Laboratory of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements on microorganisms will be conducted. Laser-based mass spectrometry on organics will be conducted at the Space Research and Planetary Sciences division of the University of Bern, which is closely collaborating with colleagues at NASA Ames Research Center, USA. The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities. The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. Ample funding for travel, publications and computing resources will be available. Child allowance and maternity/paternity leave are offered. Assistance with visa procedures is available for international candidates. Additionally, the CSH offers career advice, mentorship, and teaching opportunities. Application and Contact Questions about the position? Queries should be addressed to: Prof. Dr. Brice-Olivier Demory (brice-olivier.demory@unibe.ch) and PD Dr. Andreas Riedo (andreas.riedo@unibe.ch) who will jointly supervise the PhD student. Questions about the application? items.title: PhD position NCCR Genesis: remote sensing of microorganisms in extreme environments
items.desc: NCCR Genesis: background The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) at the University of Bern invites applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis. The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress. Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch. Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups. Project description Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life. This PhD project will investigate the impact of icy-moon environmental conditions on the detectability of selected bacteria in ice/salt mixtures rapidly exposed to vacuum, extremely low temperatures and high-radiation levels. For this purpose, a high-sensitivity spectro-polarimeter will be interfaced with a temperature-vacuum chamber. Additionally, an electron gun and a UV light source will be used to investigate the incidence of harsh conditions on bacterial samples deposited on ice as a proxy for icy moon conditions. The study will also investigate whether spectro-polarimetry could probe fundamental structures in the microorganisms such as cofactors or proteins in the near UV. The project will thus investigate the detectability of fundamental biosignatures relevant to a wider range of microorganisms. This effort will inform the preparation of future life-detection missions in our Solar System, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus. The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team (lead: Prof. Brice-Olivier Demory) with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics. Profile We are looking for a creative and motivated candidate, a team player, with a MSc degree in physics or engineering. Prior expertise in optics is an asset and a basic understanding of polarisation is a plus. Excellent oral and written skills in English are a requirement. What we offer The position is based at the Centre for Space and Habitability, which strives to investigate key questions in space sciences through interdisciplinarity. Our team collaborates tightly with the Microbiology Laboratory (Prof. Pilar Junier) of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements are conducted. The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities. The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. Ample funding for travel, publications and computing resources will be available. Child allowance and maternity/paternity leave are offered. Assistance with visa procedures is available for international candidates. Additionally, the CSH offers career advice, mentorship, and teaching opportunities. Application and Contact Questions about the position? Queries should be addressed to : Prof. Dr. Brice-Olivier Demory (brice-olivier.demory@unibe.ch) Questions about the application? Applications are invited from all nationalities and should consist of: a 2-page cover letter detailing your interest in joining the group and in the PhD topic a CV official transcripts of your Bachelor's and Master's degrees, as well as contact details of three referees (references will only be requested for short-listed candidates). Application materials should be submitted in a single PDF file to info.csh@unibe.ch with "NCCR Genesis PhD2 position" in the subject line. The review of the applications will start immediately and will continue until the position is filled.

items.title: Promotion - Foundation Models und Agentic AI für die industrielle Automatisierung
items.desc: Unternehmensbeschreibung Bei Bosch gestalten wir Zukunft mit hochwertigen Technologien und Dienstleistungen, die Begeisterung wecken und das Leben der Menschen verbessern. Unser Versprechen an unsere Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter steht dabei felsenfest: Wir wachsen gemeinsam, haben Freude an unserer Arbeit und inspirieren uns gegenseitig. Willkommen bei Bosch. Die Robert Bosch GmbH freut sich auf deine Bewerbung! Stellenbeschreibung Die industrielle Automatisierung steht an einem Wendepunkt. Foundation Models bieten eine beispiellose Generalisierung und Anpassungsfähigkeit – doch ihr Einsatz in realen Produktionsumgebungen bedeutet, sich harten Randbedingungen stellen zu müssen: Latenzen im Mikrosekundenbereich, deterministisches Verhalten, funktionale Sicherheitszertifizierungen und Legacy-Infrastrukturen, die sich nicht ohne Weiteres ersetzen lassen. Zu deinen Aufgaben gehört die Untersuchung, wie Foundation Models in der industriellen Realität nutzbar werden. Hierfür entwickelst du innovative Anpassungs-, Validierungs- und Deployment-Methoden. Du bringst diese Modelle in die Fertigung, die Prozessindustrie und in cyber-physische Systeme, wobei du Latenz, Determinismus und Sicherheit als nicht verhandelbare Größen berücksichtigst. Außerdem widmest du dich den Kernfragen, wie Foundation Models eine begrenzte, vorhersagbare Leistung erbringen können, ohne an Fähigkeiten einzubüßen. Du erarbeitest Lösungen, wie sich Foundation Models mit etablierten industriellen Sicherheits- und Automatisierungsstandards (z. B. IEC 61131, IEC 61508) vereinbaren lassen. Nicht zuletzt erweiterst du Brownfield-Automatisierungsplattformen um die Fähigkeiten von Foundation Models und schaffst so neue Möglichkeiten für die Industrie. Qualifikationen Ausbildung: abgeschlossenes Master-Studium in Informatik, Elektrotechnik, Automatisierungstechnik, Robotik, Mechatronik oder vergleichbar Erfahrungen und Know-how: starker theoretischer und praktischer Hintergrund in Machine Learning und Deep Learning; solides Verständnis von Konzepten der industriellen Automatisierung, Steuerungssystemen sowie Echtzeit- oder Embedded-Umgebungen; fundierte Programmierkenntnisse in Python und C++; Vertrautheit mit Standards der funktionalen Sicherheit (IEC 61508, ISO 13849) sowie formalen Verifikations- oder Validierungsmethoden; nachgewiesene Erfahrung beim Deployment und der Optimierung von KI-Modellen auf Edge-Geräten, Embedded-Hardware oder ressourcenbeschränkten Plattformen; Kenntnisse in Modelloptimierungstechniken wie Quantisierung, Pruning, Knowledge Distillation oder beschleunigter Inferenz (Accelerated Inference); praktische Erfahrung mit SPS-Umgebungen, industriellen Kommunikationsprotokollen (OPC UA, PROFINET, EtherCAT) oder industriellen Echtzeitplattformen sind wünschenswert Persönlichkeit und Arbeitsweise: du bringst ein tiefes Interesse an der Anwendung von Foundation Models in industriellen oder cyber-physischen Systemen mit und es gelingt dir, komplexe Forschungsfragen methodisch zu bearbeiten Sprachen: fließendes Englisch in Wort und Schrift und gute Deutschkenntnisse Zusätzliche Informationen https://www.bosch-ai.com www.bosch.com/research Die finale Vergabe des Promotionsthemas obliegt deiner Hochschule als zentrale Anlaufstelle für deine Promotion. Beginn: nach Absprache Bitte sende uns deine aussagekräftigen Bewerbungsunterlagen (inkl. Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse und Links zum GitHub- oder Kaggle-Account) zu. Vielfalt und Inklusion sind für uns keine Trends, sondern fest verankert in unserer Unternehmenskultur. Daher freuen wir uns über alle Bewerbungen: unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Behinderung, Religion, ethnischer Herkunft oder sexueller Identität. Sie haben Fragen zum Bewerbungsprozess? Celina Dannecker (Personalabteilung) +49 711 811 21346 Sie haben fachliche Fragen zum Job? Daniel Ewert (Fachabteilung) mailto:daniel.ewert@de.bosch.com Work beginnt hier: Jetzt bewerben!

items.title: PhD Candidate in Explainable AI (xAI) for Capsule Endoscopy
items.desc: About The Position NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim. This position will be in Gjøvik, Norway. At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world. You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here. Video: https://youtu.be/Xt-yHCN5QS0 Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network CAPTURE, collaborate with academic, healthcare, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on wireless endoscopy. As part of the CAPTURE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting. The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027. Your immediate leader will be the unit leader of Colourlab. About The Project The CAPTURE project is an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) through developments in computer vision and artificial intelligence. The project aims to improve image-based diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment by developing methods that reduce clinicians’ workload, enhance imaging quality, and support more accurate and timely diagnoses. CAPTURE combines research with a strong focus on doctoral training, preparing a new generation of researchers to work at the interface of technology and medicine. The consortium brings together expertise from academia, industry, and hospitals, ensuring that the research is both scientifically rigorous and clinically relevant. The project focuses on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), reflecting its growing prevalence in Europe. As many of the methods developed have broader applicability, the project will also consider other gastrointestinal diseases. These goals will be achieved through the recruitment and training of 15 doctoral candidates in an international and intersectoral environment, providing interdisciplinary expertise across the technical, clinical, and applied aspects of WCE. Duties of the position Automated approaches for pathology detection using WCE are generally based on recent AI models. These models often result in black-box decisions. For a clinician to use these systems, the basis for diagnostic decision should be clearly explained. The PhD candidate will help develop explainable AI (XAI) methods for automated diagnostic decision systems to enhance the explainability and actionability of their predictions for doctors. The candidate will also evaluate the generated explanations with medical doctors to assess their relevance, usefulness, and importance in clinical settings. Key responsibilities Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above Academic publications and popular science dissemination Participate in the Colourlab research group Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the CAPTURE partner institutions and contribute to CAPTURE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures. Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to Robert Gordon University, UK and Technical University of Darmstadt, Germany. Close collaboration with hospitals for assessing methods developed in PhD project Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must have experience with computer vision and machine learning. You must have excellent programming skills in Python with exposure to popular deep learning libraries like PyTorch or Tensorflow. At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible. You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position. You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Preference may be given to candidates with: Experience with computer vision, medical image processing, self-supervised learning or learning in low-data regimes. Experience with statistical signal processing and pattern recognition will be counted positive. Experience with pretrained representation models, transfer learning and xAI. Knowledge of robustness analysis in computer vision applications. Knowledge of explainable AI, uncertainty estimation, calibration, out-of-distribution detection, adversarial robustness, or causal analysis. Experience with causal inference, counterfactual explanations, or uncertainty quantification in deep learning Evidence of scientific writing, publications, a strong master's thesis, research software, or relevant open-source contributions. Excellent analytical and communication skills. Ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary environment. Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Show strong motivation for research and a willingness to engage deeply with challenging scientific questions. Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them. Present and discuss your research with other professionals. Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback. Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity. Show curiosity and a strong motivation for the subject. Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions. Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed. Communicate, present, and collaborate effectively, including explaining technical ideas clearly and presenting research results to interdisciplinary audiences and project partners. Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As an employee in Norway, the successful candidate will normally be a member of the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme, which provides access to public healthcare and social security benefits in accordance with applicable legislation and regulations. As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance and Mobility Allowance. In addition, a family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 3 years. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed. About The Application The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English. Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. Incomplete applications will not be prioritised. The Application Must Include Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees CV Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Doc

items.title: PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys
items.desc: Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon The Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon conducts cutting-edge international research for a changing world: Around 1,000 employees contribute to the tackling of climate change, the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range. Institute of Material and Process Design The Institute of Material and Process Design is dedicated to the sustainable and ecological development of innovative materials and manufacturing processes, especially for the transportation sector and medical technology. To this end, materials are tailored and manufacturing processes are designed to conserve resources – from the modeling of material behavior to the development of the material to the finished component. PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys Reference code: 1057 - 2026/WD 1 Commencement date: as soon as possible Work location: Geesthacht Application deadline: November 12th, 2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. items.desc: Die Technische Informationsbibliothek (TIB) ist eine Stiftung öffentlichen Rechts des Landes Niedersachsen. Mit rund 600 Beschäftigten und einem Etat von circa 60 Millionen Euro ist sie eine der größten Informationsinfrastruktureinrichtungen in Deutschland. Als Deutsche Zentrale Fachbibliothek für Technik und Naturwissenschaften sichern wir mit unseren zukunftsweisenden Dienstleistungen die infrastrukturellen Voraussetzungen einer qualitativ hochwertigen Informations- und Literaturversorgung für Forschung in Wissenschaft und Industrie. Mit dem Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) arbeiten wir daran, den Austausch und die Nutzung wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse im digitalen Zeitalter zu revolutionieren. Die TIB, Programmbereich D, Open Research Knowledge Graph, sucht für die Forschungsgruppe Data Science & Digital Libraries (Prof. Dr. Sören Auer) zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:n Wissenschaftliche:n Mitarbeiter:in / Doktorand:in für Natural Language Processing (NLP) und kausale KI (m/w/d) Die Stelle ist für die Dauer der Projektlaufzeit von drei Jahren befristet. Die Einstellung erfolgt vorbehaltlich der finalen Bewilligung der Mittel durch den Drittmittelgeber Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Die regelmäßige Wochenarbeitszeit beträgt 39,80 Stunden (Vollzeit). Der Arbeitsplatz ist grundsätzlich für Teilzeitbeschäftigung geeignet. Mobiles Arbeiten ist unter Berücksichtigung dienstlicher Erfordernisse in begrenztem Umfang möglich. Die Eingruppierung erfolgt in die Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. Aufgaben Die Stelle ist Teil des Projekts EcoAIRE - AI-assisted hypothesis assessment in invasion biology and the restoration of freshwater ecosystems under fragmented and heterogeneous ecological evidence im Förderprogramm Leibniz-Kooperative Exzellenz. Das Projekt verbindet die Expertise der TIB in der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache und der wissenschaftlichen Wissensrepräsentation mit der ökologischen Expertise des Leibniz-Instituts für Gewässerökologie und Binnenfischerei (IGB) sowie der Expertise des Deutschen Forschungszentrums für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) in der kausalen Modellierung. An der TIB liegt Ihr Forschungsschwerpunkt auf der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache zur Extraktion wissenschaftlicher und kausaler Informationen. Sie entwickeln Methoden, die wissenschaftliche Evidenz in strukturierte, maschinenverarbeitbare Repräsentationen von Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Unsicherheiten und kausalen Zusammenhängen überführen. Dabei geht Ihre Forschung über die Extraktion einzelner Fakten hinaus: Sie modellieren, wie wissenschaftliche Befunde zusammenhängen und unter welchen Bedingungen wissenschaftliche Aussagen gelten. Darauf aufbauend erforschen Sie kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern. Dazu gehören Simulationen, interventionsbasierte Schlussfolgerungsverfahren und die Bewertung von Hypothesen unter veränderten Bedingungen. Ihre Tätigkeit umfasst Sie entwickeln ein multimodales Rahmenwerk, das heterogene wissenschaftliche Wissensquellen - darunter Publikationen, Bilder, ergänzende Informationen, Datensätze und weitere Forschungsartefakte - in strukturierte Repräsentationen zur Hypothesenbewertung integriert und dabei die Herkunft der Informationen nachvollziehbar berücksichtigt. Sie entwickeln sprachmodellbasierte und agentenbasierte Methoden, um Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Evidenz, Unsicherheiten sowie kausale oder mechanistische Zusammenhänge quellenübergreifend zu extrahieren, zu vereinheitlichen, aufeinander abzustimmen und zusammenzuführen. Sie erforschen kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern, um Interventionen zu simulieren und zu untersuchen, inwieweit sich Hypothesen auf veränderte Bedingungen übertragen lassen. Sie entwickeln Evaluationsrahmenwerke, die unterschiedliche Qualitätsaspekte der KI-gestützten Hypothesenbewertung erfassen. Dazu gehören Verfahren auf Grundlage fachlicher Expertenbewertungen sowie Ansätze, bei denen große Sprachmodelle als Bewertungsinstanz eingesetzt werden („LLM-as-a-judge“). Sie veröffentlichen Ihre Forschungsergebnisse auf Konferenzen und in Fachzeitschriften mit Peer-Review-Verfahren in den Bereichen NLP, Semantic Web, künstliche Intelligenz und maschinelles Lernen. Zudem wirken Sie an Projektberichten und der Verbreitung der Forschungsergebnisse mit. Profil Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master oder gleichwertiger Abschluss) in Informatik oder einem eng verwandten Fachgebiet, beispielsweise Künstliche Intelligenz (Artificial Intelligence), maschinelle Sprachverarbeitung (Natural Language Processing), maschinelles Lernen (Machine Learning), Data Science oder Computerlinguistik. Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Forschung oder Softwareentwicklung mit Python sowie praktische Kenntnisse moderner Methoden der Softwareentwicklung, beispielsweise Git-basierter Zusammenarbeit, automatisierter Tests und reproduzierbarer Experimente. Nachweisbare praktische Erfahrung mit transformerbasierten Modellen und großen Sprachmodellen, einschließlich der Nutzung von Frameworks wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers oder vergleichbaren Technologien für NLP-Anwendungen. Praktische Erfahrung in der Entwicklung agentenbasierter KI-Workflows oder von Multiagenten-KI-Workflows, einschließlich Werkzeugnutzung, strukturierter Ausgaben, Orchestrierung oder iterativer Verarbeitungspipelines für Schlussfolgerungen. Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens dem Niveau C1 für die wissenschaftliche Kommunikation, Zusammenarbeit und Publikationstätigkeit. Wünschenswerte Qualifikationen Erfahrung mit der Feinabstimmung oder Anpassung großer Sprachmodelle und/oder dem Aufbau fortgeschrittener RAG-Pipelines unter Verwendung von Technologien wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Sentence Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex, FAISS, Qdrant oder vergleichbaren Werkzeugen. Dazu zählen embeddingbasierte Informationssuche, Reranking, Vektorsuche und strukturierte Generierung. Kenntnisse der kausalen Modellierung und kausalen Inferenz, beispielsweise kausaler Graphen, struktureller Kausalmodelle oder interventionsbasierter Schlussfolgerungsverfahren. Erfahrung mit Semantic-Web-Technologien. Fachkenntnisse in der Ökologie, insbesondere der Süßwasserökologie, Invasionsbiologie oder Renaturierungsökologie, oder Erfahrung in der Mitarbeit an interdisziplinären wissenschaftlichen Projekten. Wir bieten Unser Ziel ist es, die Bereitstellung und Nutzung von Forschungsdaten und -informationen immer wieder neu zu überdenken und zu innovieren. Wir bieten ein intellektuell inspirierendes Umfeld mit unternehmerischer Denkweise, eingebettet in eine führende technische Universität und eines der größten Informationszentren der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Mit dem Forschungszentrum L3S der Leibniz Universität Hannover, eines der weltweit führenden Forschungsinstitute im Bereich Web & Data Science, besteht dabei im Rahmen des Leibniz Joint Lab Data Science & Open Knowledge eine enge Kooperation. Nicht zuletzt legen wir Wert auf ein offenes und kreatives Arbeitsklima, in dem es Spaß macht zu arbeiten. Darüber hinaus bieten wir einen gemeinwohlorientierten Arbeitsplatz im öffentlichen Dienst auf der Grundlage des TV-L mit einer Vergütung nach der Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. eine Sonderzahlung zum Jahresende sowie 30 Tage Urlaub im Jahr bei einer Fünf-Tage-Woche sowie zusätzliche freie Tage an Heiligabend (24.12.) und Silvester (31.12.). einen flexiblen Arbeitsplatz in Zeit und Raum mit Angeboten zur Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie wie u. a. mobiles Arbeiten und flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodellen (Gleitzeit). einen modernen Arbeitsplatz in zentraler Lage von Hannover mit einem kollegialen, attraktiven und vielseitigen Arbeitsumfeld. einen Arbeitgeber mit breit gefächertem Fort- und Weiterbildungsangebot, einer betrieblichen Gesundheitsförderung und Altersvorsorge für den öffentlichen Dienst (VBL). Beschäftigtenrabatt in den Mensen des Studentenwerks Hannover sowie vergünstigte Möglichkeit zur Nutzung der vielseitigen Angebote des Hochschulsports Hannover. eigenverantwortliche und zukunftsorientierte Tätigkeiten, die Abwechslung bieten und Raum für persönliche Entwicklung lassen. die Finanzierung der erforderlichen Ausstattung sowie von Reisen zu Konferenzen und Forschungsaufenthalten. die Mitarbeit in einem nationalen Forschungs- und Innovationsprojekt. ein breites Spektrum an Forschungsinfrastrukturen und Technologiekomponenten, auf denen Sie aufbauen können. Dazu gehören TIB AIssistant, der Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG), ORKG Ask sowie Forschungssoftware aus dem SciKnowOrg-Ökosystem. Important note Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered. LNKD1_DE

items.title: CIFRE - Cosmic rays robustness - H/F
items.desc: At STMicroelectronics, we believe in the power of technology to drive innovation and make a positive impact on people, businesses, and society. As a global semiconductor company, our advanced technologies and chips form the hidden foundation of the world we live in today. When you join ST, you will be part of a global business with more than 115 nationalities, present in 40 countries, and comprising over 50,000 diverse and dedicated creators and makers of technology around the world. Developing technologies takes more than talent: it takes amazing people who understand collaboration and respect. People with passion and the desire to disrupt the status quo, drive innovation, and unlock their own potential. Embark on a journey with us, where you can innovate for a future that we want to make smarter and greener, in a responsible and sustainable way. Our technology starts with you. YOUR ROLE Since 2000, wide-bandgap materials, especially silicon carbide, have been progressively introduced into power electronic circuits. Owing to their higher critical electric field compared with silicon, high-voltage unipolar devices such as Schottky diodes and MOS transistors have been developed, replacing silicon bipolar devices, including fast bipolar diodes and IGBTs, with significantly reduced switching losses. The resulting improvement in power efficiency reduces cooling requirements and enables a smaller overall system footprint, making the adoption of wide-bandgap devices particularly advantageous in applications with stringent constraints on size and weight, such as spacecraft and avionics. For these applications, high tolerance to cosmic rays is obviously expected. On the ground, higher power efficiency is also crucial for electrical vehicle deployment as it increases driving range, and for smart-grid applications that require very high voltage devices (> 2000V). Here again, cosmic ray robustness, especially neutrons, is essential to meet the very low failure rates expected in the automotive sector and to avoid complex maintenance in smart-grid applications. Since 2004, cosmic rays impact on silicon carbide devices has been extensively studied. In addition to the well-known single event burnout (SEB), also observed in silicon power devices, silicon carbide devices have been shown to exhibit a new cumulative degradation mechanism reported as single-event leakage current (SELC). No consensus has yet been reached within the scientific community regarding its cause. In This Context, You'll Be Responsible For Defining models to be implemented in cosmic-ray simulations for silicon carbide devices. Performing simulations on existing diode structures to validate the simulation setup. This activity will benefit from an ongoing study engaged with the french national center for space studies (CNES), which will provide with heavy-ion robustness results from different diode structures. Studying the reverse characteristics of damaged diodes and request analyses (either electrical or structural ones) to understand the mechanisms involved. Simulating new diode structures to improve cosmic-ray robustness. Thesis location STMicroelectronics Tours RADIAC team at IES (University of Montpellier) Your Skills & Experiences Master degree in semiconductor physics, condensed-matter physics, or particle-matter interaction, B2 English level and finite-elements simulation experience would be appreciated. ST is proud to be one of the 17 companies certified as a 2025 Global Top Employer and the first and only semiconductor company to achieve this distinction. ST was recognized in this ranking thanks to its continuous improvement approach and stands out particularly in the areas of ethics & integrity, purpose & values, organization & change, business strategy, and performance. At ST, we endeavor to foster a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we do not tolerate discrimination. We aim to recruit and retain a diverse workforce that reflects the societies around us. We strive for equity in career development, career opportunities, and equal remuneration. We encourage candidates who may not meet every single requirement to apply, as we appreciate diverse perspectives and provide opportunities for growth and learning. Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) is woven into our company culture. To discover more, visit st.com/careers.

items.title: PhD in Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models
items.desc: Introduction Are you interested in the communication networks behind modern AI systems? Would you like to combine mathematical modeling with experiments on programmable network hardware to make AI infrastructure faster and more energy-efficient? In this PhD project, you will develop models and orchestration methods for the networks that connect GPUs during large language model inference. Are you our next PhD candidate in high-performance AI networking? Job Description Your research challenge Large language models rely on powerful computing infrastructure to generate responses. When inference is distributed across multiple GPUs, these devices must continuously exchange intermediate results. Network congestion and communication overhead can therefore limit performance and increase energy consumption, even when substantial computing resources are available. In the project Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models (COIL) , you will investigate how analytical network models can support the design and operation of AI clusters. The project combines network performance modeling, optimization, and experimental research, giving you the opportunity to connect mathematical foundations with practical challenges in AI infrastructure. You will develop fast, composable analytical models using Network Calculus, a mathematical framework for analyzing communication networks. These models will capture interactions between inference traffic, network architecture, and mechanisms such as flow control and congestion feedback. They will provide bounds on communication latency and buffer requirements, complemented by energy estimates based on measurement-calibrated power models. Building on these models, you will explore how architectural choices—including network topology, link bandwidth, and parallelization strategies—affect performance and energy consumption. You will develop tools that help cluster designers evaluate promising configurations efficiently. You will also investigate how the models can guide runtime decisions, such as workload placement, prioritization, routing, or resource reservation. A focused prototype will demonstrate how model-informed decisions can improve the operation of an existing network. Experimental validation will be an integral part of your research. You will use measurements from AI infrastructure and conduct reproducible experiments on programmable networking testbeds. Technologies of interest include Ethernet-based AI networks, emerging Ultra Ethernet mechanisms, P4-programmable switches, and SmartNICs. Finally, you will evaluate the results from the testbeds on real AI infrastructure in collaboration with our partner SURF. Through this combination of theory, software development, and experimentation, you will contribute to more responsive and energy-efficient AI infrastructure. The project also offers opportunities to share your findings with networking standardization communities and to release research tools and experimental results openly. An interdisciplinary and international environment You will conduct your research under the main supervision of Prof. Lisa Maile who leads the Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) lab. NoMaD is part of the Electronic Systems group in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your supervision will also include partners from the Advanced Models by Open Research and Engineering (AMOR/e) Lab of Computer Science and the Model-Based Design Lab from Electrical Engineering. The position is funded through the EuroTech programme, which promotes research collaboration between leading technical universities across Europe. As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Prof. Georg Carle and his research group on Network Architectures and Services at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) . As part of this collaboration, you will spend six-month in Munich with the group at TUM , where you will gain hands-on experience with programmable network hardware and reproducible experimental infrastructure. Job Requirements Essential qualifications A master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong mathematical background, demonstrated by excellent performance in mathematically rigorous courses, additional mathematics electives, a mathematics minor or specialization, or substantial mathematical work in a thesis or research project. Good programming skills and an interest in developing research software and experimental tools. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, initiative, and creativity. An interest in high-performance networking and AI infrastructure, and motivation to apply mathematical methods to computer networks and distributed systems. A strong team spirit and enthusiasm for working in an international, collaborative, and socially engaging environment. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. Willingness to spend at least six months at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) as part of the project. Desirable Qualifications A solid foundation in computer networks or distributed systems. Experience with Network Calculus, network simulation, mathematical optimization, or GPU communication. Experience with programmable networking technologies, such as P4 or SmartNICs. Selection procedure Interviews and a scientific presentation will be part of the selection procedure. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. The Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) Lab develops mathematical models, tools, and protocols for reliable and efficient communication networks. Its research connects formal analysis with practical implementation, covering technologies such as Time-Sensitive Networking, Ultra Ethernet, and beyond-5G networks. Applications range from connected vehicles and industrial automation to large-scale AI infrastructure. By combining analytical methods with simulation and hardware experiments, the lab translates theoretical insights into practical network designs and resource-management solutions. NoMaD is part of the ES group, which develops methods for designing electronic, embedded, and cyber-physical systems with predictable performance, timing, reliability, and energy consumption. With about 12 full-time and 5 part-time professors and ~45 post-docs, PhDs, and EngD students, the group’s expertise spans model-driven engineering, system architectures, software, and digital circuits. This provides an interdisciplinary environment for your research, connecting network modeling and optimization with broader challenges in computing and system design. The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field. Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed. Visit our website for more information about the application process. You can also contact Kevin Caris, HR advisor, k.t.caris@tue.nl. Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video. Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page. Application We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a: Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and qualifications for the position. Curriculum vitae, including a list of your publications and the contact information of three references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application. A transcript of your BSc and MSc studies. A sample of your academic or technical writing in English where you are the first authors. For example, a research paper, thesis chapter, or report, of which you are the primary author. items.title: PhD - Benchmarking Robotic Tactile Sensors
items.desc: The Manipulation and Touch Lab at Imperial College London has funding to support a home PhD student on the topic of Benchmarking Contemporary Tactile Sensors . The project will be supervised by Dr Ad Spiers, an Associate Professor of Robotics and Machine Learning. The Manipulation and Touch Lab is part of the Intelligent Systems and Networks research group and the Imperial Robotics Forum. Project Summary: Increasing interest in robotic manipulation has led to recent an explosion in the variety of (commercial and experimental) tactile sensing platforms, which vary in transduction techniques, fabrication methods and processing approaches. While all sensors have their pros and cons, there is currently no clear documentation to allow these sensors to be directly compared, particularly when diverse use cases are considered. Comparative benchmarking has become an important topic in robotic manipulation within the last decade or so, leading to such efforts as the YCB object set, COMPARE ecosystem and NIST task boards. Clearly, a similar effort would be beneficial for tactile sensing, though the scope and details of such benchmarks are currently unclear. The developments of relevant and rigorous sensor tests will be the focus of this PhD, which will be actualised via high-precision robotic test equipment and access to multiple tactile sensors from various manufacturers. We anticipate this research to generate protocols and datasets that will be shared with the international robotics research community, as we have done with our past research outputs. The Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Imperial has a long and proud history of world-class research and innovation. It ranked the 1st in the UK (Engineering) in REF 2021 based on the proportion of world-leading research (4*). Funding: The PhD studentship is fully funded for and includes home-level tuition fees, a tax-free stipend for three and a half years at the UKRI London rate (approximately £23,805 per year for 2026/27), and support for research expenses and travel to conferences. The post is only open to home applicants. Qualifications: Applicants are expected to hold either a Bachelor’s (2:1 or higher) and Master’s (Merit or higher) or Integrated Master’s (Merit or higher) in relevant subjects. How to Apply: To make initial enquiries about the position, please send an email to Dr Ad Spiers ( a.spiers@imperial.ac.uk ) with the subject line ‘MTL Tactile PhD’. For queries regarding the application process, please contact eee.pgadmissions@imperial.ac.uk . Applications must be made via the departmental portal (https://www.imperial.ac.uk/electrical-engineering/study/phd/). Applications received via email will be discarded. Early applications are encouraged as recruitment is on a rolling basis. Candidates must be able to start at one of the department’s fixed entry points (January, April, July, or September). Preference will be given to candidates who can start their studies at an earlier entry point. Closing Date: March 31st 2027 About Imperial EEE: Imperial College London is the UK’s only university focussed entirely on science, engineering, medicine and business and we are consistently rated in the top 10 universities in the world. Additional information on the PhD programme in the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering can be found here. The Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering at Imperial has a long and proud history of world-class research and innovation. It ranked the 1st in the UK (Engineering) in REF 2021 based on the proportion of world-leading research (4*). We are committed to equality and valuing diversity. We are also an Athena SWAN Silver Award winner, a Stonewall Diversity Champion, a Two Ticks Employer, and are working in partnership with GIRES to promote respect for trans people. items.title: PhD Candidate in Colour and Image Enhancement for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
items.desc: About The Position Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network CAPTURE, collaborate with academic, healthcare, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on wireless endoscopy. As part of the CAPTURE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting. The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027. Your immediate leader will be the unit leader of Colourlab. About The Project About the Capture project The CAPTURE project is an EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) through developments in computer vision and artificial intelligence. The project aims to improve image-based diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment by developing methods that reduce clinicians’ workload, enhance imaging quality, and support more accurate and timely diagnoses. CAPTURE combines research with a strong focus on doctoral training, preparing a new generation of researchers to work at the interface of technology and medicine. The consortium brings together expertise from academia, industry, and hospitals, ensuring that the research is both scientifically rigorous and clinically relevant. The project focuses on inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), reflecting its growing prevalence in Europe. As many of the methods developed have broader applicability, the project will also consider other gastrointestinal diseases. These goals will be achieved through the recruitment and training of 15 doctoral candidates in an international and intersectoral environment, providing interdisciplinary expertise across the technical, clinical, and applied aspects of WCE. About The PhD Project The overall objective of the PhD project is to improve the diagnostic quality and reliability of Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) image data through advanced colour correction, contrast enhancement, and consistent visualisation. Specific Objectives Are To develop methods for combined colour correction and contrast enhancement of WCE image and video data; define a colour palette and suitable reference target for gastrointestinal imaging; establish measurement protocols and guidelines for accurate and reproducible colour acquisition; quantify inter-device variability among WCE systems and determine whether device-specific or general calibration models are required; develop objective and subjective methodologies for evaluating colour fidelity, image quality, and perceptual improvements; apply psychometric and statistical methods to validate the proposed methods; develop a display visualisation pipeline for consistent and perceptually accurate presentation of WCE images across different viewing conditions. Duties of the position Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate. Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above. Academic publications and popular science dissemination. Participate in the Colourlab research group. Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person across the CAPTURE partner institutions and contribute to CAPTURE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures. Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (STH) and University of Granada (UGR). Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment Required Selection Criteria You must have experience with imaging, colour science, colour metrology, image processing, or medical imaging, Very good programming skills. At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible. You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information. You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, imaging science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis. Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position. You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works. Excellent oral and written communication skills in English. This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network CAPTURE, collaborate with academic, healthcare, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on wireless endoscopy. As part of the CAPTURE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations.
