items.title: PhD in Multifunctional Polymer Composites
items.desc: Introduction Are you inspired to push the limits of polymeric materials for lighter and smarter defense platforms? Join us to develop a new generation of 3D-printed composite panels that shield electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact. Job Description We are offering 2 PhD positions within project VALOR, an ambitious, interdisciplinary collaboration between academia, industry and government partners. The project aims to develop a new generation of lightweight composite panels that both shield sensitive electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact events, helping to make defense platforms safer and more resilient. Naval ships, drones and military vehicles increasingly depend on electronic radar, communication and navigation systems that must be protected against electromagnetic interference and radar detection . Today, this is mostly done with metals, which block practically all wave power with only a thin layer. However, they add weight, corrode, and reflect electromagnetic waves, making platforms easier to detect. Project VALOR tackles this challenge by merging two fields that have so far been developed separately: absorption-based electromagnetic shielding and impact-resistant sandwich structures . By combining 3D-printed architected nanocomposite materials with predictive modelling into one integrated design strategy, the project will construct a design framework for panels that are able to both carry loads and absorb electromagnetic waves, with a performance that can be tailored to specific (defense) applications. Your role We Are Recruiting Two PhD Candidates Who Will Work As a Team Throughout The Project, I.e. From Material Screening To Design And Testing Of Larger Scale Panel Demonstrators. Both Candidates Will Conduct a Combination Of Experimental And Numerical Work And Collaborate Closely With Industrial Partners Within The Consortium. More Specifically PhD 1 focuses on mechanics and manufacturing: 3D printing nanocomposite lattice materials, fabricating composite facesheets, conducting mechanical tests, constructing and validating mechanical finite element models. PhD 2 focuses on electromagnetic testing and design: formulating polymer nanocomposite materials and characterizing their electromagnetic behaviour, designing and testing absorbing architected nanocomposite structures, conducting electromagnetic shielding simulations. Your team and network You will join the Processing and Performance of Materials section in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at TU/e. The group has around 20 PhD and post-doctoral researchers working on how processing, structure and properties connect in polymers and polymer-based composite materials. The group is known for its integrated experimental-numerical approach to tailor the performance of these materials. You will have access to state-of-the-art computational facilities and laboratories dedicated to rheology, polymer processing (incl. additive manufacturing) and mechanical testing. You will be supervised by Frederik Van Loock (project leader), Ruth Cardinaels and Tom Engels. Job Requirements PhD 1 – Mechanics and manufacturing We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with the following qualifications: A master’s degree (or equivalent) with excellent grades in Mechanical Engineering with a specialization in mechanics of materials / solid mechanics. A strong interest in combining experimental work with numerical modelling. Enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary team and with industrial and defense partners. A research-oriented mindset: critical thinking is your second nature. Good communication skills and fluency in English, both spoken and written (C1 level). Experience with one or more of the following areas is a plus: mechanical characterization of polymer-based materials, finite element simulations of mechanical behaviour of polymer-based materials, 3D printing of polymers, polymer and composite processing. PhD 2 – Electromagnetic testing and design We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with the following qualifications: A master’s degree (or equivalent) with excellent grades in Engineering (Mechanical or Electrical), Materials Science or Applied Physics, with a specialization in materials. A strong interest in combining experimental work with numerical modelling. Enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary team and with industrial and defense partners. A research-oriented mindset: critical thinking is your second nature. Good communication skills and fluency in English, both spoken and written (C1 level). Experience with one or more of the following areas is a plus: electromagnetic characterization of polymer-based materials (e.g. vector network analysis, waveguide measurements), electromagnetic simulations (e.g. full-wave finite element modelling), 3D printing and processing of polymers. Why Join? Work within the multidisciplinary Processing and Performance of Materials group Work at the forefront of advanced materials research in collaboration with industry leaders. Combine material formulation, characterization, and computation in a multidisciplinary team. Get trained to use cutting-edge experimental and numerical simulation facilities. Contribute to the development of advanced multi-functional and 3D printed composite panels that make defense platforms more safe and resilient. Work in an international working environment and present your work at international conferences. Conditions of Employment A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station. In Addition, We Offer You Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment. Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)). In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary. Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time. As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%. High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process. An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care. Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate. We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training. An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs. A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme) for international candidates. On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment. Build on your career at TU/e! About Us We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video. Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here. The Department of Mechanical Engineering department conducts world-class research aligned with the technological interests of the high-tech industry in the Netherlands, with a focus on the Brainport region. Our goal is to produce engineers who are both scientifically educated and application-driven by providing a balanced education and research program that combines fundamental and application aspects. We equip our graduates with practical and theoretical expertise, preparing them optimally for future challenges. Information Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more? Please contact the hiring manager Frederik Van Loock, f.v.loock@tue.nl. Visit our website for more information about the application process. You can also contact HRServices.me@tue.nl. Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video. Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page. Application We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a: Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and qualifications for the position. Curriculum vitae, including a list of your publications and the contact information of three references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application. Complete overview of grades obtained (bachelor & master degree). Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications. We look forward to receiving your application and will screen it as soon as possible. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled. Please note You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

items.title: PhD position Secure multi-stakeholder 6G orchestration
items.desc: Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications. Job Description Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge. 6G services will no longer run in a single place. They will be built from software functions that are placed, scaled, and moved across devices, base stations, edge sites, and central clouds, often owned and operated by different parties. This PhD project designs, builds, and evaluates the management and orchestration (MANO) systems that make this multi-stakeholder continuum secure and dependable. The research question is how orchestration can decide across infrastructure that cannot be fully trusted. The project addresses how hardware roots of trust are discovered, allocated, and carried across migration, how a node is attested continuously while it serves traffic, how split AI workloads are placed without exposing model or data across trust boundaries, and how orchestration decisions are made auditable. The work extends open-source orchestration platforms and is validated on FNS experimental infrastructure in collaboration with industrial partners. You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos. Job requerements Become part of an expansive ecosystem shaping the development of 6G. You will benefit from training in 5G and beyond networks, AI, and software development. Plus, you will gain exclusive access to (1) a state-of-the-art testbed where theory meets real-world application, and (2) an ecosystem that cultivates entrepreneurial endeavours. Are you ready to challenge yourself? We're seeking candidates who have, or are about to receive, a Master-of-Science degree in a relevant computer science discipline and who like to combine theory with practice. Proficiency in English is essential, as you'll collaborate within a diverse, international community. For more details on our admission requirements, please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission. We’ll evaluate based on your academic record, interviews, and possibly assignments. While a strong background in the field is crucial, what matters as well is your creative flair, motivation, and above all, your passion for comprehensive research! TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context. At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. Challenge. Change. Impact! Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact dr. Nitinder Mohan, via n.mohan@tudeft.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 Nov 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter Copies of your BSc and MSc degrees and transcripts. You can address your application to dr. Nitinder Mohan. Applications will be evaluated as they come in,so please apply as soon as possible. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. Recruitmentcode 6Gflagship

Um mit unseren Innovationen das Tempo vorzugeben und Großartiges zu ermöglichen. Denn hinter jedem erfolgreichen Unternehmen stehen eine ganze Menge faszinierender Menschen. Die Mitarbeitenden von ZEISS arbeiten in einem offenen und modernen Umfeld mit zahlreichen Entwicklungs- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten. Unsere Kultur ist geprägt von Expertenwissen und Teamgeist. All das wird getragen durch die besondere Eigentümerstruktur und das langfristige Ziel der Carl-Zeiss-Stiftung: Wissenschaft und Gesellschaft gemeinsam voranzubringen. Heute wagen. Morgen begeistern. Vielfalt ist ein Teil von ZEISS. Wir freuen uns unabhängig von Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung, Alter sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität auf Ihre Bewerbung. Jetzt bewerben! In weniger als 10 Minuten. Enabler für kleinere, leistungsfähigere und energieeffizientere Mikrochips Arbeiten, wo das Morgen entsteht. Rund 80 Prozent aller Mikrochips weltweit werden mit ZEISS Technologien gefertigt. Als Herzstück eines jeden elektronisch gesteuerten Systems sind sie aus unserem Alltag nicht mehr wegzudenken – egal ob im Smartphone, im Smart Home oder in Smart Factories. In der Gruppe Systems Engineering Mechanical Design entwickeln wir komplexe Sondermaschinen von Grund auf. und Englischkenntnisse auf B2-Niveau sowie von Vorteil erste Erfahrung in der fachlichen Koordination Wir bieten Important note Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for items.title: Master's Theses "Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security"
items.desc: The AIT Austrian Institute of Technology is Austria’s largest Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) . We aim to transform scientific excellence into innovation with impact. Together with our partners, we develop technologies and solutions for a sustainable, resilient, and digitalised future, strengthening Europe’s competitiveness and technological sovereignty. Our international teams combine cutting-edge research with strong implementation expertise to create measurable value for industry and society. Our Center for Digital Safety & Security invites applications for master’s theses at our location in Vienna (Giefinggasse, 1210). At the Center for Digital Safety & Security, we conduct research into a wide range of key technologies such as distributed IT systems, the Internet of Things (IoT), cybersecurity, data science, artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain technologies, quantum and photonic technologies, wireless systems (6G) and digital solutions for crisis and disaster management. Our Research Field Cyber Security , which forms part of the Cyber Security & Communication Technologies Competence Unit, specialises in applied research in the field of digital security and is pioneering the development of highly innovative concepts, algorithms and systems for anomaly detection, cyber-threat analysis, penetration testing and cryptography. Using our groundbreaking technologies, we simulate modern ICT and OT infrastructures as well as cyber-attacks. Master's Theses "Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence for Cyber Security" CENTER FOR DIGITAL SAFETY & SECURITY We are looking for motivated and enthusiastic master’s students to join our team for a period of six to eight months . The ideal candidate has a solid background and a strong interest in one or more areas relevant to cyber security, such as (1) data science and data analysis, (2) software development and systems engineering, or (3) machine learning and artificial intelligence. You will work closely with our senior researchers to further develop and enhance open-source solutions for areas such as log-data analysis for intrusion detection, cyber threat intelligence processing, and the dynamic provisioning of complex IT infrastructures. Guided by our interdisciplinary team, you may apply modern data-driven methods to process, analyse, and interpret log data for indications of cyber attacks. Alternatively, you may focus on natural language processing (NLP) techniques and large language models (LLMs) for the automated processing and analysis of cyber threat intelligence feeds. As a cyber security enthusiast, you will contribute directly to our projects, academic publications, and open-source code bases , helping to strengthen the European cyber security ecosystem . You will further develop your scientific research skills and have the opportunity to exchange ideas with leading experts and experienced researchers in the field. You will gain first-hand insights into how a research organisation collaborates with customers and industry partners to address real-world cyber security challenges. Your qualifications as an Ingenious Partner: Master’s student at an Austrian university in Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering, or a related field. Basic knowledge of relevant technologies and methods in the Cyber Security area. A conscientious, independent working style and a high degree of reliability. For prototype development, experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage, depending on the specific thesis topic: Python-based implementations, including data structures, machine learning libraries, mathematics, and statistics Security monitoring technologies, technical artefacts of cyber attacks, and their analysis Log data analytics, data science methods, and data visualization techniques A good understanding of common network protocols, Linux operating systems, and their application in modern enterprise environments Linux user-space and kernel-space development, including C programming and kernel internals Automated deployment and system integration, including system design, C, Python, Linux scripting, and Ansible Application of large language models (LLMs) and artificial intelligence (AI), including evaluation harnesses, prompting strategies, and their application in cyber security Strong interest in applied research questions and real-world challenges from industry High level of motivation and a collaborative, team-oriented mindset. Good written and spoken English and German skills What to expect: Duration of the internship: 6-8 months Start date: There is flexibility concerning the start-date A remuneration of EUR 1.379,60 gross per month for 20 hours per week. In addition to our company benefits, we offer flexible working conditions and work experience in a highly innovative environment. As a research institution, we are familiar with the supervision and implementation of final theses and are looking forward to supporting you accordingly. At AIT, we create an inclusive and family-friendly working environment that promotes equal opportunities and actively strengthens diversity across our workforce and in leadership positions. Among other initiatives, we are committed to increasing the proportion of women in our company and therefore particularly welcome applications from female applicants. items.title: Doctoral Researcher, SmartSpaces project, Centre for Wireless Communications
items.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are now looking for a Doctoral Researcher to join the Centre for Wireless Communications unit at the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering, University of Oulu. The Centre for Wireless Communications (CWC) counts about 250 experts working in four research groups. The research topics are selected to create scientific knowledge and engineering solutions with high impact, to train professionals and to enable resilient, sustainable, and secure connectivity and networks. The vision is to stay among world leading academic communities, and conduct research on wireless communications and technologies for future 6G networks. About the job The doctoral researcher will contribute to the SmartSpaces project, funded by the Research Council of Finland in collaboration with research partners at Rice University, USA. The research will focus on enabling wireless systems to sense and interpret their surroundings and provide secure, efficient spatial awareness services. Particular emphasis will be placed on mathematical modelling, optimization, and algorithm development for integrated sensing and communication. Topics of interest include: RF radar signal processing Backscattering Resource allocation and scheduling. Query-driven and task-oriented sensing. Machine learning for adaptive sensing and network operation. Combining RF and acoustic sensing to improve spatial awareness. Secure and trustworthy sensing, including authentication and resilience against eavesdropping, spoofing, and jamming. Efficient representations of sensed environments, including compact digital twins and the management of sensing information. The main duties of a doctoral researcher are related to undertaking original academic research in several of the above topics towards the award of a joint doctoral degree, accompanied by the publication of results in high-impact journals and conference venues, and thorough, transparent, and insightful collaboration with the whole research team. Who are you? You are required to have: A master’s or equivalent degree in Electrical and Communications Engineering, Computer Sciences, or related fields, with top grades. Skills and motivation for doctoral studies. Excellent verbal and writing communication skills in English. Additionally, to succeed and enjoy the position, you are expected to have: A strong background in Mathematics Excellent programming skills Aptitude for working both independently and as part of a team Aptitude for developing strong productive relationships At least one of the following prerequisite skills: wireless communications/networking convex optimization signal processing machine learning RF radars You must apply for the right to study for a doctoral degree at the beginning of your employment in accordance with the requirements of the University of Oulu Graduate School (UniOGS). What we offer The support of an experienced and enthusiastic team with whom you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture, and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and your close ones in settling into Oulu. We have an HR Excellence in Research -quality label, which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, an excellent education system, and a competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Salary The position is fixed-term for 3 years, starting as soon as possible. The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (a maximum of 50 % of the job-specific component). The starting gross salary will be approximately 2800-2900 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6 months is applied to the position. How to apply? Interested? items.title: PhD Position F/M Collusion in Agentic Systems
items.desc: Le descriptif de l’offre ci-dessous est en Anglais Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Doctorant A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle The Inria Saclay-Île-de-France Research Centre was established in 2008. It has developed as part of the Saclay site in partnership with Paris-Saclay University and with the Institut Polytechnique de Paris . The centre has 40 project teams , 27 of which operate jointly with Paris-Saclay University and the Institut Polytechnique de Paris; Its activities occupy over 600 people, scientists and research and innovation support staff, including 44 different nationalities. Contexte et atouts du poste The recruited student will work in the FairPlay team. FairPlay is a joint team between Inria, ENSAE and Criteo with around 8 permanent researchers and 15 PhD students/postdocs from all three partners institution. The team is bi-localized, hosting at CREST (on the Polytechnique campus) but working from Criteo HQ in Paris once a week. Mission confiée Agentic systems are increasingly present: agents make decisions or tasks. They may interact for that with other agents, which opens the possibility of collaboration, but also potentially of collusion. This was observed in the past in algorithmic pricing systems. The objective of the PhD is to analyze these questions theoretically using game theory and learning theory. Principales activités Main activities: conduct research on fairness in online algorithms Additional activities: document the results through publications and talks Compétences Technical skills and level required : A strong background in mathematics, in particular in probability and online learning. L’autorisation d’accès à une zone est délivrée par le chef d’établissement, après avis ministériel favorable, tel que défini dans l’arrêté du 03 juillet 2012, relatif à la PPST. Un avis ministériel défavorable pour un poste affecté dans une ZRR aurait pour conséquence l’annulation du recrutement. Politique de recrutement : Dans le cadre de sa politique diversité, tous les postes Inria sont accessibles aux personnes en situation de handicap. Contacts Équipe Inria : FAIRPLAY Directeur de thèse : Loiseau Patrick / patrick.loiseau@inria.fr L'essentiel pour réussir The successful candidate should have high motivation for research work and a taste for societal and security questions. A propos d'Inria Inria, l'institut national de recherche dans les sciences et technologies du numérique, est en appui de l’État pour les stratégies nationales de recherche et d’innovation du numérique en tant qu'Agence de programmes. items.title: Stage - Synthèse et vérification de propriétés fonctionnelles pour les systèmes embarqués F/H
items.desc: Lieu : Meyreuil, France Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. Nos engagements, vos avantages Notre savoir-faire technologique Notre attention portée à l’équilibre des collaborateurs Un environnement inclusif et bienveillant Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu (Thales Solidarity, indice CAC 40 ESG…) Votre quotidien En nous rejoignant à Meyreuil, à proximité d'Aix-en-Provence, vous intégrez un site regroupant l’ensemble des activités de conception de circuits intégrés pour l'identité et et la sécurité numériques. Lors de ce stage, vous développez une méthodologie automatique pour générer des propriétés de vérification fonctionnelle à partir d'une source unique fiable. Vous appliquez cette méthode sur un processeur open-source, afin de simplifier et fiabiliser la vérification des composants tels que processeurs, SoC ou accélérateurs cryptographiques. L’objectif est de réduire le temps, les erreurs et la dérive entre documentation et code, un problème fréquent dans la conception, particulièrement dans un contexte industriel intégrant l’IA. Pour ce faire vous avez à : concevoir une méthodologie automatique pour générer des propriétés de vérification à partir d’une source unique, cohérente avec le code RTL et la documentation. Cette source servira à définir des contrats fonctionnels aux différents niveaux d’abstraction, depuis l’architecture (jeu d’instructions) jusqu’aux modules RTL. Le stage inclut la prise en main des langages de propriété et des techniques basées sur les grands modèles de langage, la définition de la source unique, la génération et la validation des propriétés sur un CPU open-source, ainsi que l’évaluation de l’intégration dans le flux de vérification. Vous gagnez en expertise dans les méthodes formelles et l’IA générative appliquées au matériel, en travaillant sur un projet industriel avec un support expert. Votre profil Vous préparez un diplôme dans le domaine informatique, électronique ou génie informatique, avec une spécialisation en conception numérique ou systèmes embarqués ou équivalent de niveau Bac +5 et vous avez de l'expérience sur : une bonne maîtrise du flot de conception numérique (RTL), des connaissances en assertions SVA/PSL une bonne connaissance des architectures de processeur, Les plus : des connaissances de vérification formelle, des bases d’IA notamment avec de grands modèles de langage (prompting, génération de code), des connaissances en environnement de simulation/UVM. De la curiosité, de l'autonomie, un attrait pour la recherche dans un contexte qui évolue vite sont des atouts que l’on vous reconnait ? Alors cette mission est faite pour vous ! Tous nos stages sont conventionnés et soumis à une gratification dont le montant est déterminé selon votre niveau d’études. Thales, entreprise Handi-Engagée, reconnait tous les talents. La diversité est notre meilleur atout. Postulez et rejoignez nous !

items.title: PhD Student
items.desc: Ihre Aufgaben Your tasks Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil. Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses. Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility. Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico. Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings. Ihre Qualifikationen Your qualifications Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field. Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided. Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning. Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English. Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite. Wir bieten We offer A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration. Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise. An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences. Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies. Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified. Weitere Informationen This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration. The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. Combining in vivo electrophysiology, computational neuroscience, and generative modeling, the project investigates how acoustic signals can be transformed into spatiotenporal light patterns for stimulation via the optical cochlear implant under development at IAN and EKFZ-OT. Your application Please submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable. We look forward to receiving your application! Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.

items.title: PhD: new methodologies for RSV infection and immunity
items.desc: Bilthoven Universitair Master 36 uur Schaal 8 / €3.333 - €4.457 (bruto) Onderzoek / wetenschap, Medisch / verzorging Solliciteer voor 9 november 2026 Dit ga je doen Are you an MSc graduate in viro-immunology and keen to help replace traditional animal testing? As a PhD researcher within a new European consortium, you will advance, standardize, and qualify a cutting-edge human cell-based model to evaluate RSV immunity. Working alongside leading scientists and regulators across Europe, you will deepen your expertise in advanced methodologies like single-cell RNA sequencing while shaping non-animal approaches in vaccine research. This role offers a clear path to complete your PhD thesis, publish high-impact literature, and build an international network at the intersection of science and public health. Developing Advanced Human Epithelial Models for RSV Traditionally, research into respiratory virus infection and immunity has relied on small animal models and in vitro cultures of immortalized cell lines. Bridging these experimental systems, differentiated primary human epithelial cell culture models are gaining ground, but their use in vaccine research remains limited due in part to a lack of immunological components and standardization of these models. We have recently developed a novel virus neutralization model for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This virus causes considerable morbidity and mortality in infants and older adults, and first-generation preventive strategies have recently become available. Our novel neutralization model builds upon the previously established air–liquid interface respiratory epithelial transwell model, which includes functional multiciliated and mucus-producing goblet cells. Your responsibilities Within a new European consortium, you will apply the RSV neutralization model as a use case to advance its standardization and qualification as a new approach methodology (NAM) in collaboration with regulatory partner institutes in the UK and Germany. In addition, you will dive deeper into the possibilities of this model to provide insights into population variability as well as viral escape mutants. With this project, you will contribute to the implementation of novel in vitro methodologies that will increase our understanding of antiviral mucosal immunity and reduce the need for animal experiments. Your role will involve: Co-design of a standardization plan for the RSV neutralization model, in collaboration with (regulatory) consortium partners, including technical transfer of the model to partner sites. Performing extensive cell culture work including viral infections at BSL-2/ML-II biosafety level, aimed at standardization and further exploration of the RSV neutralization model. Various molecular biological and virological techniques, including (confocal) microscopy, virus titration, RT-qPCR, single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunoassays. Systematic literature reviewing of available and ongoing studies related to the use of in vitro models of respiratory viral infection and immunity. Analyze and interpret data, publish in peer-reviewed scientific journals, present the results in the institute as well as at (inter-)national conferences and prepare a PhD thesis based on your findings. Participate in a team of virologists, immunologists, bioinformaticians and regulators at RIVM and collaborating institutes to share and discuss the results of your studies. About the RIVM department The Center for Immunology of Infectious Diseases and Vaccines (IIV) at RIVM serves as the government's knowledge center in the field of immunology of infectious diseases and vaccines. The core mission of IIV is to provide information and advice on vaccine effectiveness, vaccination strategies, and immune responses to infectious diseases, supporting government policy and informing the public. Research at IIV focuses on optimizing the effectiveness and safety of current and future vaccination programs, immunosurveillance, age-related efficacy of immune responses, and identifying correlates of protection. Within IIV, the Department of Immune Mechanisms - Immunological Models (IIM) employs immunological models to support the core mission of IIV. You will be part of IIM, an international, dynamic, and highly motivated team of approximately 20 scientists and technicians at various stages of our careers, united by a strong drive to advance immunological research for the benefit of public health. We combine expertise in virology, immunology, and bioinformatics, and we believe in the power of collaboration and teamwork. About the PhD programme The intended start date is February 1st, 2027. The PhD programme lasts four years. Your appointment is initially for one year. At the end of the first year, an evaluation takes place according to the standard procedure. If this evaluation is positive, the appointment will be extended by three years. During the PhD research, your salary is set as follows according to Functiegebouw Rijk (FGR): First year: €3,333.81, according to scale 8, step 0. Second year: €3.741,48, according to scale 8, step 5. Third year: €3.984,50, according to scale 8, step 7. Fourth year: €4.132,76, according to scale 8, step 8. How to apply and more information You can address your application to IIM manager Jørgen de Jonge. Do you have any questions before applying? Please contact project leader Puck van Kasteren (+316 311 423 91), she is more than happy to answer your questions. We look forward to hearing from you. In the event of substantial interest in this vacancy, we may invite a larger group of candidates for a short 15-minute online interview, including a brief pitch and two or three predefined questions Dit krijg je Schaal 8 €3.333 - €4.457 (bruto) Arbeidsovereenkomst voor bepaalde tijd 4 jaar 36 uur Het salaris is gebaseerd op een werkweek van 36 uur. Dit bieden we nog meer Naast het salaris ontvang je een Individueel Keuzebudget (IKB). Het IKB bestaat uit geld (16,50% van je bruto jaarsalaris) en tijd. Met het IKB maak jij de keuzes die bij jou passen en kun je een deel van je arbeidsvoorwaarden zelf samenstellen. Je kunt er bijvoorbeeld voor kiezen om een deel van je maandinkomen te laten uitbetalen wanneer jij dat wenst. Ook kun je dit budget omzetten in verlof en andersom of besteden aan fiscaal vriendelijke doelen. De Rijksoverheid hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en loopbaanontwikkeling en biedt daarvoor tal van mogelijkheden. Tot de secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden behoren onder meer verschillende studiefaciliteiten, bedrijfsfitness, volledige vergoeding van je OV-reiskosten woon-werkverkeer en gedeeltelijk betaald ouderschapsverlof. Dit vragen wij Your profile To be successful in this position, you bring the following knowledge and experience: An MSc in biomedical sciences, biology, medicine, or a related discipline, preferably focused on infection and immunity. Background in infection and immunity or a related field, preferably with previous experience in cell culture work and virological methods (such as titration or neutralization assays). Strong analytical capacity to systematically review literature, interpret multifaceted datasets, and translate findings into rigorous scientific publications and your PhD thesis. High autonomy and initiative to independently plan, drive, and adapt your daily research activities. Clear communication skills in English, allowing you to articulate research outcomes effectively to diverse audiences. A collaborative mindset to align naturally with an international, multidisciplinary team of scientists, regulators, and laboratory technicians. Bij het RIVM hebben we één van de beste cao's van Nederland, namelijk die van de Rijksoverheid. Naast een goed salaris hebben we aantrekkelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden zoals een Individueel Keuzebudget van 16.5 % van je bruto jaarsalaris waarover je zelf de regie hebt. Je kunt iedere maand een deel laten uitbetalen of extra vrije dagen kopen of verkopen. Daarnaast bieden we fiscale voordelen om bijvoorbeeld je studieschuld af te lossen. Ook zijn we een mantelzorgvriendelijke organisatie. Meer weten? Lees er meer over onder de kop ‘overige arbeidsvoorwaarden’. Hier kom je te werken Over RIVM RIVM: deskundig, betrouwbaar en onafhankelijk Als Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu (RIVM) zijn we een deskundige, betrouwbare en onafhankelijke adviseur voor overheid, professionals en burgers. Ons doel: een gezonde bevolking en een duurzame, veilige en gezonde leefomgeving. We bewaken gezondheid, ziekten, de kwaliteit van de leefomgeving én het milieu. Daarvoor doen we onderzoek en we verzamelen kennis voor toegankelijke informatie en toepasbare adviezen. Het RIVM zorgt voor een goede geboortescreening, het bestrijden van infectieziekten en heeft een centrale rol bij het Rijksvaccinatieprogramma en de bevolkingsonderzoeken. We onderzoeken wat er nodig is voor goede zorg, een gezonde leefstijl, veilige producten en een veilige en gezonde leefomgeving. Ook dragen we bij aan het voorkomen, bestrijden en beheersen van incidenten en crises. Terwijl we druk de verhuizing voorbereiden naar een prachtig nieuw gebouw op het Utrecht Science Park, werken we op ons huidige hoofdkantoor in Bilthoven met ongeveer 3000 collega’s aan al onze adviezen, rapporten, factsheets en publicaties. Daarbij laten we ons leiden door de vragen van vandaag én morgen. We doen ons werk midden in de maatschappij. Trots zijn we op onze organisatie waar iedereen welkom is. Als kennisinstituut van de overheid willen we een afspiegeling van de samenleving zijn. Naast talent, ervaring en motivatie maken ook aspecten van identiteit zoals leeftijd, geaardheid, culturele achtergrond of arbeidsbeperking, onze organisatie rijker, innovatiever én leuker. Met deze verschillende achtergronden, perspectieven en inzichten werken wij samen aan een nog beter resultaat! Het RIVM zet zich in om medewerkers in dienst te nemen die onder de doelgroep van de Wet Banenafspraak vallen. Meer informatie hierover vind je op de website van de Rijksoverheid. Bij het RIVM ben je welkom zoals je bent. Wij zijn ervan overtuigd dat diversiteit in een team de samenwerking en de uitkomst sterker maakt. items.title: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy
items.desc: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy Join TU Delft and the EU-funded OPERA consortium. Push the frontier of general-purpose AI for robotics and tackle the fundamental tension between long-horizon reasoning and real-time safety guarantees. Job description Robots that operate for long periods among people must plan beyond the next few seconds while staying safe. They need to predict how their surroundings and the people in them will evolve, know how reliable these predictions are, and adapt their plans when the predictions fail. In the EU-funded OPERA project, TU Delft contributes to General-Purpose AI for robotics by developing methods that combine fast, reactive behavior with more deliberate reasoning, planning, and decision-making. In this PhD position, you will develop planning and decision-making methods that let robots act safely and reliably over long time horizons when their knowledge of the environment and of the people around them is incomplete. The research sits at the intersection of model-based planning and control and learning-based models, and addresses the trade-off between safety, performance, and real-time computation. You will formulate the methods and analyze their guarantees and failure modes. This research is connected to OPERA's tasks on GPAI-powered planning and decision-making, on long-term reasoning in human-centered environments, and on adaptive human-robot and robot-environment interaction. Depending on your background, the work may draw on optimal control and model predictive control, motion planning, probabilistic modeling and estimation, or learning-based methods. The emphasis is on methods with a clear formulation and well-understood failure modes, validated in simulation and on real robots. You will work in the Cognitive Robotics Department at TU Delft under the supervision of Prof. Robert Babuška and Dr. Laura Ferranti, and you will be embedded in the Reliable Robot Control Lab (https://r2clab.com/). You will collaborate with OPERA partners across Europe on simulation, perception, and the OPERA open-source toolbox. Job requirements The ideal candidate for this PhD position has a strong background in control, optimization, or motion planning and is motivated by the question of how robots can plan safely and reliably over long time horizons. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds who want to work at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. You have: An MSc degree in Systems and Control, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong interest in safe planning and decision-making for robots, at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. A passion for rigorous, theoretically grounded research, combined with an eagerness to validate ideas in simulation and on real robots. Strong analytical and mathematical skills, in particular in optimization, probability and statistics, and dynamical systems. Excellent communication skills and proficiency in English (written and verbal), as required for academic publication and international collaboration. You are particularly encouraged to apply if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Hands-on experience implementing optimization-based planners or controllers (e.g., model predictive control with acados or CasADi) in C++ or Python. Safe or robust control and planning under uncertainty. Learned dynamics or prediction models, model-based reinforcement learning. Uncertainty quantification, probabilistic or Bayesian modeling, state estimation. Long-horizon or hierarchical planning, prediction of human or multi-agent behavior. Real-robot deployment with ROS or ROS 2. As part of OPERA, you will travel to meet and collaborate with the project’s European partners and attend regular consortium meetings. We particularly encourage applications from women and other underrepresented groups, as we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive research environment. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. . Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3059 - €3881 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information For more information, please reach out to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska [l.ferranti@tudelft.nl, r.babuska@tudelft.nl] Please do not use LinkedIn and other channels for applications or inquiries. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 15 November 2026 upload the following documents: A letter of motivation explaining why you are the right candidate for this project An updated cv Exam transcipts from your Bachelor and Master A copy of your MSc thesis, or draft MSc thesis (or a link to access it) You can address your application to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: #EUfunded This is an EU funded project, named OPERA, with project number 101298363, within program HORIZON/HORIZON-CL4-2025-04-DIGITAL-EMERGING-07 You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. Faculty/Department: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering Salary range: €3059 - €3881 Hours per week: 38-40 FTE: 1,0 Submission is possible until: 15 Nov 2026 ID job: 3993

items.title: PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps
items.desc: Career Vacant positions Job vacancy PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps About the position SINTEF Energy is announcing two PhD candidate positions within the field of thermal engineering and industrial heat supply utilizing High Temperature Heat Pumps (HTHPs). Both positions are within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled by the doctoral program at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and have supervisors at both SINTEF and DTU Construct. About the project The activity is coordinated within the HeatMinds MSCA-DN by Brunel University in London, UK. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 18 partners across Europe. This integrated project aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates to make a step change in accelerating the development and deployment of industrial HTHPs to support the decarbonization of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres, and industrial actors, advanced models and design tools will be developed that contribute to the advancement of these efforts. HeatMinds will tackle highly connected research questions, namely what are the optimum and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs, and supporting energy policy frameworks? HeatMinds will establish a roadmap for deploying IHTHP technology to support the decarbonisation of several key industries. The other project partners recruiting PhD students are Brunel University (UK), City St. Georges University (UK), University of Seville (Spain), Technical University of Denmark, and SINTEF Industry. One of the PhD projects hosted by SINTEF Energy is titled “Multiscale design and optimization of ejectors integrated within novel IHTHP architectures” and addresses the potential for improved energy efficiency achieved by using ejectors. The project also addresses the coupled and multiscale challenges associated with optimal design and integration, and focuses on the use of natural working fluids. On the one hand, the analysis and design of optimal heat pump cycles is typically carried out using simple lumped or one-dimensional models. On the other hand, accurate component performance and design requires more detailed analysis methods, such as CFD, that present a challenge for how complex and coupled systems should be designed. This project includes elements of: Evaluation of two-phase ejector component integration strategies within high temperature heat pump applications, considering system constraints and ejector performance trade-offs. Component design and optimization using computational fluid dynamics. Exploration of multi-fidelity and multiscale modelling methods that may include surrogate modelling approaches for coupled cycle analyses. Evaluation of proposed efficient reduced-order ejector performance models that could be directly implemented to ejector dimensioning tools and/or automation algorithms. Comparison to experimental test results. SINTEF Energy, along with the partners in HeatMinds, hold significant experience and expertise in the analysis, design, and experimental testing of two-phase ejectors integrated in refrigeration and heat pump applications. DTU Construct additionally has an extensive track record working with two-phase flow, turbomachinery, and design optimization. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with SINTEF colleagues as well as with HeatMinds partners. The project includes an international secondment to Danfoss (Denmark), to gain practical insight into industrial R&D for ejector components and systems. Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondment with HeatMinds partners. Participate in relevant conferences, workshops, and training activities. Be flexible and prepare to adjust to activities and project focus as the PhD project progresses if needed. Complete the doctoral education. Participate actively in the relevant SINTEF Energy research groups’ activities. Required selection criteria You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree[JD1.1]. Master’s students in their final year can apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (average grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential Must meet the admission requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Please see https://www.dtu.dk/english/education/phd for more information for specific requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Excellent written and spoken English. MSCA Mobility Rule: At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date of the position. The appointment is to be made in accordance with SINTEF’s guidelines for recruitment positions and the academic regulations set by DTU Construct. Background (mandatory) Strong mechanical engineering fundamentals with a focus on thermal and fluid flow phenomena Foundations of computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods, and heat and mass transfer Thermodynamic cycle analysis Fundamentals of programming Additional background that will be valued in the selection process: Optimisation methods and/or surrogate modeling for component and system design Multiphase flow and phase change modelling Familiarity with experimental methods and model validation Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity for the subject. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and motivation for the position. We offer An exciting and challenging research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network with excellent opportunities to collaborate within international research groups and industry. A dynamic, creative, and inclusive working environment. Access to cutting edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. Salary and conditions The employment period is three years, funded through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. About the application The application must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter). Curriculum vitae. Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale. Names and contact information of two references. Applications without the required documentation will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, disability, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. Contacts Joshua Render Dowdell, Researcher. Email: , phone +47 484 05 669 Petter Nekså: Chief Scientist. Email: , phone: +47 926 06 519 Elisa Magnanelli, Research Manager. Email: , phone +47 944 32 692 Unit SINTEF Energy Research Work place Trondheim Application due 22/11/2026 SINTEF Energi AS leverer forskningsbaserte løsninger og tjenester som skaper verdier hos kundene, både nasjonalt og internasjonalt. SINTEF Energi AS er en del av konsernet SINTEF. SINTEF er en uavhengig og allmennyttig forskningsstiftelse hvor ingen eiere kan ta ut utbytte. Økonomiske overskudd investeres i vitenskapelig utstyr og kompetanse. About SINTEF SINTEF is one of Europe’s largest research institutes, offering specialist multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of technology and the natural and social sciences. SINTEF is an independent foundation that since 1950 has generated innovation by means of research and development projects for the private and public sectors both in Norway and overseas. SINTEF has 2,100 employees from 80 countries and an annual turnover of more than NOK three billion. SINTEF invests any profits into further research and innovation. Our vision: Technology for a better society.

items.title: CDTNet PhD Fellow
items.desc: Job Description Summary For this position, we are looking for a talented and ambitious doctoral candidate to join CDTnet, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network dedicated to transforming cardiovascular medicine through Digital Twins. Digital Twins are personalised virtual models that combine biomedical data, artificial intelligence, physiological modelling, and clinical knowledge to improve the diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of cardiovascular disease. Through CDTnet, 15 doctoral candidates will work at leading universities, hospitals and industry partners across Europe while receiving world-class interdisciplinary training. This fully-funded three-year position will be hosted in Oslo, Norway with secondments in Norway, Spain and the UK. GE Healthcare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world. Job Description Project Description Heart valve disease affects millions of people worldwide and relies heavily on medical imaging for diagnosis, treatment planning and patient follow-up. Echocardiography is the most widely used imaging technique for assessing valve function, but the development of reliable artificial intelligence tools for image analysis is often limited by the availability of large, high-quality, annotated datasets. Creating and annotating such datasets is expensive and time-consuming, creating a significant barrier to innovation. This project will investigate how generative artificial intelligence can be used to improve the assessment of mitral valve diseases in particular mitral regurgitation. The doctoral candidate will develop novel methods analysing different echocardiography data modalities such as b-mode or colorflow and investigate how generating synthetic echocardiographic images can support automated image analysis tasks, such as valve segmentation and the assessment of mitral valve regurgitation. Attention will be given to understanding how patient-specific information can be incorporated into generative models to improve accuracy, consistency and clinical relevance. Working at the interface of artificial intelligence, medical imaging and cardiovascular medicine, the candidate will evaluate how generated synthetic data can improve the performance and robustness of machine-learning models when compared with training approaches utilising real world data alone. The project will make use of both proprietary clinical datasets and publicly available resources. Ultimately, the developed methods will be integrated into clinical software and evaluated as part of a prospective study of automated mitral valve assessment. The project provides a unique opportunity to contribute to the next generation of AI-enabled cardiac imaging technologies within a leading industrial research environment, while benefiting from close collaboration with academic and clinical partners across Europe. Planned Secondments Oslo University Hospital, Norway (3 months): retrospective analysis of mitral valve regurgitation and validation of automated assessment methods. IDIBAPS, Barcelona, Spain (2 months): design and implementation of a prospective clinical study for automated mitral valve assessment. King's College London, United Kingdom (2 months): investigation of how mechanistic cardiovascular models can complement machine-learning approaches. Desirable Project-Specific Qualifications and Skills We are looking for a highly motivated and solution-oriented applicant with a strong machine learning background. The ideal candidate will have: Master’s degree (equivalent to a minimum of 120 ECTS credits) preferably in machine learning, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics/electrical engineering. Other degrees can also be considered given that the candidate has formal competence in machine learning and/or image analysis/computer vision. Foreign completed degrees (M.Sc.-level) must correspond to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system A solid background in modern deep learning, machine learning, mathematics, linear algebra, and/or statistics is also required Solid knowledge and documented experience with programming in Python and relevant machine learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) Fluent oral and written communication skills in English Experience with medical image analysis and echocardiography is a plus Inclusion and Diversity GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer where inclusion matters. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. Behaviors We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership – always with unyielding integrity. Total Rewards Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support. #LI-MG1 Additional Information Relocation Assistance Provided: No
