items.desc: 15.09.2022, Academic staff We are an active and lively research group that is passionate about science. We are working in an environment that may best be characterized by the passion to accomplish something new—complemented by teamwork and fostering personal relationships. From assistants, students, researchers, and postdocs to professors; we are all working hand in hand, and are highly committed and engaged with our work. We know how to celebrate our successes, but also how to get through setbacks together! In the next months, we are going to extend our research group at the Technical University Munich (www.tum.de). Accordingly, we are currently searching for Ph.D. Students to join our team on Logic Synthesis! Our Research In Our Group, We Conduct Scientific Work On Design Automation For Various Technologies And Develop Algorithms And Software Tools Dedicated To Accelerating Research On Multiple Levels. We Are Working At The Intersection Of Computer Science, Physics, And Material Science To Push The Limits Of Atom-scale Manufacturing With Corresponding Design Automation Methodologies. Our Research Is Mainly Focused On (but Not Limited To) The Following Topics Logic synthesis under technology constraints Placement & Routing for technology-independent layout generation Clocking and data synchronization Layout validation and verification Technology mapping and optimization To learn more about the details of our previous work, check out our website and open-source implementation which is publicly available on GitHub. Your Profile We are looking for team players who are willing to learn and explore new topics while advancing the scientific field. Your main task will be the development, conceptualization, and eventual implementation of new logic synthesis and design automation, simulation, and verification methods and software for emerging computing technologies. Our focus on interdisciplinary partnerships and networks will enable you to meet many interesting people (at places all over the world) and present your work at top-notch conferences and journals in our domain. You should have completed your Master's/Diploma studies with top grades in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Mathematics, Electrical Engineering, or a similar subject. Most importantly, you should be creative, passionate about research, driven by curiosity, and able to think outside of the box. You will need strong coding skills, ideally in both modern C++ and Python, to design highly performant algorithms. Solid knowledge in the areas of logic synthesis, algorithmics, and optimization problems, as well as experience with SAT/SMT solvers, ABC, Yosys, mockturtle, and similar tools is a big bonus. Join O ur Team While we are obviously interested in your CV and background (if applicable, please also add your list of publications, projects, cooperations, etc. as well as your GitHub profile), most importantly, however, tell us what motivates you to join our team and work on emerging computing technologies. items.title: Doktorand (m/w/d) im Bereich KI-gestützte Steuerungscodegenerierung für industrielle Anwendungen
items.desc: Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter, Doktorand (m/w/d) im Bereich KI-gestützter Steuerungscodegenerierung für industrielle Anwendungen Speicherprogrammierbare Steuerungen (SPS) bilden das Rückgrat industrieller Automatisierung, ihre Programmierung findet jedoch häufig manuell und damit zeitintensiv statt und wird meist durch Domänenexperten statt Softwareingenieuren geleistet. Die resultierende Steuerungssoftware erreicht selten die Qualitätsstandards moderner Softwaretechnik, muss aber über Jahrzehnte gewartet und wiederverwendet werden. Generative KI verspricht hier einen erheblichen Hebel, doch heutige Ansätze erzeugen isolierte Codefragmente aus kurzen Prompts – ohne Anlagenwissen, ohne Bezug zum physikalischen Prozess und ohne belastbare Prüfung der Funktionalität und der Safety-Anforderungen. Am ISW erforschen wir Methoden zur SPS-Codegenerierung für sicherheits- und qualitätskritische industrielle Anwendungen. Hierfür wurde bereits ein Multi-Agenten-Ansatz entwickelt und erfolgreich erprobt, der spezialisierte Generierungs- und Validierungsschritte miteinander kombiniert. Aufbauend darauf soll untersucht werden, wie sich qualitätsgesicherter, wartbarer und wiederverwendbarer SPS-Code für den industriellen Einsatz automatisiert erzeugen lässt. Ziel ist es, das Agentennetzwerk zu einer Engineering-Lösung weiterzuentwickeln, die SPS-Code auf Industrieniveau erzeugt, diesen auf Sicherheitsanforderungen hin validiert und die systematische Wiederverwendung erprobter Softwareartefakte ermöglicht. Hre Zukünftigen Themenschwerpunkte Analyse benötigter Engineering-Artefakte oder Guidelines Weiterentwicklung eines Multi-Agenten-Systems zur Orchestrierung und mehrstufigen Generierung und Validierung von Steuerungscode. Automatisierte Unit- und Integrationstests und Einbindung in die Virtuelle Inbetriebnahme Automatisiertes Wissensmanagement zur strukturierten Erfassung von Prozesswissen und anlagenspezifischen Code-Artefakten als Grundlage für SPS-Code Planung und Durchführung von Hackthons und anderen Lehrangeboten Planung und Teilnahme an interdisziplinären AI-Software-Projekten Etablierung eines Systems zur Verifikation der Sicherheitsanforderungen Methode zur Validierung Rekombinierten Codes Ihr Profil Sie haben Ihr Masterstudium in Mechatronik, Autonome Systeme, Software Engineering, Informatik, Computional Linguistics oder einer verwandten Fachrichtung mit sehr guten Leistungen abgeschlossen. Erfahrungen in der Softwareentwicklung und der Entwicklung von KI-Applikationen oder Agentennetzwerken. Sie bringen erste Erfahrungen oder starkes Interesse an der Steuerungstechnik oder SPS-Programmierung mit. Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse befähigen Sie, im nationalen und internationalen wissenschaftlichen und industriellen Umfeld zu kommunizieren. Institutssprache ist deutsch. Wir Bieten Ihnen Hoher Anwendungsbezug und praxisnahe Forschung im Spannungsfeld von Steuerungstechnik und KI Möglichkeit zur Promotion in einem aktuellen und hochrelevanten Forschungsthema Interdisziplinäre Forschung mit moderner Infrastruktur Teilnahme an nationalen und internationalen Konferenzen Ein Sprungbrett für Ihre Karriere in Industrie oder Wissenschaft Interdisziplinäre wissenschaftliche Betreuung durch Univ.-Prof. Dr. rer. nat. habil. A. Wortmann (ISW) und Prof. Dr.-Ing. Morozov (IAS) Die Universität Stuttgart möchte den Anteil der Frauen im wissenschaftlichen Bereich erhöhen und ist daher an Bewerbungen von Frauen besonders interessiert. Schwerbehinderte werden bei gleicher Eignung vorrangig eingestellt. null

items.title: Doktorand IT (m/w/d)
items.desc: Die Technische Universität Dresden (TUD) zählt als Exzellenzuniversität zu den leistungsstärksten Forschungseinrichtungen Deutschlands. Sie begreift Diversität als kulturelle Selbstverständlichkeit und Qualitätskriterium einer Exzellenzuniversität. Entsprechend begrüßen wir alle Bewerberinnen und Bewerber, die sich mit ihrer Leistung und Persönlichkeit bei uns und mit uns für den Erfolg aller engagieren möchten. An der Fakultät Informatik, Institut für Künstliche Intelligenz , ist an der Professur für Computational Logic im Rahmen des Sonderforschungsbereichs/Transregio 248 „Foundations of Perspicuous Software Systems“ zum 01.01.2027 , vorbehaltlich vorhandener Mittel, eine Stelle als wiss. Mitarbeiterin bzw. Mitarbeiter / Doktorandin bzw. Doktorand (m/w/d) (bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen E 13 TV-L) bis 31.12.2030 (Beschäftigungsdauer gemäß WissZeitVG) zu besetzen. Es besteht die Gelegenheit zur eigenen wissenschaftlichen Weiterqualifikation (i. d. R. Promotion). Der Informatik-SFB/Transregio 248 legt die fundamentalen wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen für cyber-physische Systeme der Zukunft, die ihre Funktionalität und ihr Verhalten erläutern (sogenannte Perspicuous Systems). Erforscht wird eine tiefgehende und anwendbare Theorie von Erklärungen aller Facetten des Systemverhaltens sowie deren Erschließung durch visuelle und verbale Erläuterungen für verschiedene Nutzergruppen. Weitere Informationen unter www.perspicuous-computing.science. Als Mitglied der TUD werden Sie Teil eines erfolgreichen, interdisziplinären und internationalen Teams erfahrener Forschender. Erforschung und die Entwicklung von Methoden zur strukturierten, interaktiven Revision von Wissensbasen und Ontologien, von den theoretischen Grundlagen über komplexitätstheoretische Bewertung bis hin zur Implementierung und Evaluation. items.title: PhD position in Development and Implementation of Advanced HIV-1 reservoir diagnostics for a Biomedical laboratory scientist
items.desc: Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The project is based within the research team of Maarten van De Klundert, which is part of senior professor Anders Sönnerborgs activities at the department of Medicine, Huddinge, Centrum of Infectious Medicine – Clinical Infectious Disease. The team has a strong research focus on HIV-1. The PhD position is based at ANA Futura Laboratory, Campus Flemingsberg, a modern and international research environment with access to advanced infrastructure and opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration. The position will be closely integrated with the clinical microbiology laboratory at Karolinska University Laboratory, the National Reference Laboratory for HIV-1 and Retroviruses. You will work in a collaborative environment involving researchers with complementary expertise in molecular virology, HIV-1 immunology, and bioinformatics. The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student The PhD position is part of the national Graduate School: Biomedical Laboratory Scientists for Excellence – Future Educators in Health and Medical Care, (BioLabX). Therefore, only graduated Biomedical laboratory scientists are eligible to apply for the position In this doctoral project, you will investigate the HIV-1 reservoir in clinical samples from people living with HIV-1. It is closely connected to an ongoing clinical cohort at Department of Infectious Diseases, Karolinska University Hospital, and combines established clinical sampling with molecular and bioinformatic analyses of HIV-1 proviruses. You will establish and optimise workflows for the analysis of HIV-1 proviral DNA to characterise HIV-1 proviral sequences with respect to genetic diversity, viral subtype, drug-resistance mutations, hypermutation, and other sequence features. For data analysis, you will use advanced bioinformatics and phylogenetic analysis. You will also be involved in biobanking of all incoming samples, and later characterise immunological characteristics of selected study participants, for instance by FACS analysis, ELIspot assays, assessing HIV reactivation and more. In addition to mandatory courses specific to the PhD education at Karolinska Institutet, the BioLabX program includes a shared course package consisting of two subject-specific doctoral courses. The program also comprises a seminar series, workshops, and annual retreats that are mandatory for the doctoral students. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. Eligibility requirements for doctoral education In order to participate in the selection for a doctoral position, you must meet the following general (A) and specific (B) eligibility requirements at latest by the application deadline. It is your responsibility to certify eligibility by following the instructions on the web page Entry requirements (eligibility) for doctoral education. A) General eligibility requirement You meet the general eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you: have been awarded a second-cycle/advanced/master qualification (i.e. master degree), or have satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the advanced/second-cycle/master level, or have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.* Follow the instructions on the web page Entry requirements (eligibility) for doctoral education. *If you claim equivalent knowledge, follow the instructions on the web page Assessing equivalent knowledge for general eligibility for doctoral education. B) Specific eligibility requirement You meet the specific eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you: - Show proficiency in English equivalent to the course English B/English 6 at Swedish upper secondary school. Follow the instructions on the web page English language requirements for doctoral education. Verification of your documents Karolinska Institutet checks the authenticity of your documents. Karolinska Institutet reserves the right to revoke admission if supporting documents are discovered to be fraudulent. Submission of false documents is a violation of Swedish law and is considered grounds for legal action. (A) and (B) can only be certified by the documentation requirement for doctoral education. Skills and personal qualities The successful candidate is required to have: A strong interest in HIV research, molecular virology and translational biomedical research. Good analytical skills and an ability to interpret experimental and quantitative data. Excellent ability to speak, read and write in English. A degree in Biomedical Laboratory Science or an equivalent degree The following qualifications are desirable: Experience of experimental laboratory work in molecular biology, microbiology, virology or a related field. Experience with DNA and RNA sequencing, especially NGS and phylogeny. Basic programming and/or bioinformatic experience, for example in R, Python or related tools, and working in linux environments. Experience working with immunological methods and assays, such as PBMC isolation, FACS, ELIspot, intracellular cytokine staining (ICS) etc. Particular emphasis will be placed on the applicant's motivation for doctoral studies, scientific curiosity and analytical ability. Terms and conditions The doctoral student will be employed on a doctoral studentship maximum 4 years full-time. Application process Submit your application and supporting documents through the Varbi recruitment system. Use the button in the top right corner and follow the instructions. We prefer that your application is written in English, but you can also apply in Swedish. Your application must contain the following documents: - A personal letter and a curriculum vitae - Degree projects and previous publications, if any - Any other documentation showing the desirable skills and personal qualities described above - Documents certifying your general eligibility (see A above) - Documents certifying your specific eligibility (see B above) Selection A selection will be made among eligible applicants on the basis of the ability to benefit from doctoral education. The qualifications of the applicants will be evaluated on an overall basis. Karolinska Institutet uses the following bases of assessment: - Documented subject knowledge of relevance to the area of research - Analytical skill - Other documented knowledge or experience that may be relevant to doctoral studies in the subject. All applicants will be informed when the recruitment is completed. KI applies a salary scale when setting salaries for doctoral students. Links: Maarten van De Klundert´s team Anders Sönnerborg´s research group Department of Medicine, Huddinge Want to make a difference? Join us and contribute to better health for all

items.title: Synthèse de Carbon Dots par voie solvothermale pour des applications optoélectroniques H/F
items.desc: Ce projet est consacré au développement de nanoparticules de carbone, appelées Carbon-Dots (CDs) fonctionnalisés durables synthétisées par chimie de manière douce. Une application potentielle de ces matériaux sera la détection de rayonnement béta après intégration dans un dispositif de scintillation plastique. Dans ce cadre, le (la) postdoctorant(e) intégrera le Laboratoire LNAR et sera en charge de la synthèse par voie douce hydro/solvothermale de CDs de taille et morphologie contrôlées, de l'intégration de ces nanoparticules dans un dispositif de scintillation plastique, de l'étude et de l'optimisation des propriétés de luminescence des CDs ainsi que des scintillateurs. Intégré(e) à l'équipe R&D, en interaction avec les équipes de recherche et d'analyse, le (la) postdoctorant(e) sera accompagné(e) dans la prise en charge des actions suivantes : Développement d'un processus synthétique optimisé permettant de préparer des CDs et CDs fonctionnalisés Intégration des CDs à une matrice polymère pour étude de scintillation Caractérisation complète par IR, XRF, XPS, HR-TEM, SEM, DLS, EDS, UV-vis et photoluminescence. Évaluation de scintillation du dispositif. Ce poste offre un excellent cadre de recherche en science des matériaux. Une collaboration est prévue avec le Laboratoire d’étude des technologies du Numérique et des Procédés Avancés (LNPA), pour la réalisation des mesures de scintillation. Moyens / Méthodes / Logiciels Bureautiques (pack office), Word, PowerPoint et Excel Profil du candidat Diplôme préparé : Bac+8 Spécialité du diplôme préparé : Chimie et physico-chimie Compétences techniques et/ou spécifiques : chimie de synthèse Localisation du poste Site Marcoule Localisation du poste France, Occitanie, Gard (30) Ville Bagnols sur Cèze Critères candidat Langues Anglais (Intermédiaire) Diplôme préparé Bac+8 - Doctorat scientifique Formation recommandée Chimie et physico-chimie Demandeur Disponibilité du poste 03/11/2025

items.title: PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials
items.desc: Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Laboratory for Acoustics/Noise Control is an international team of scientists and engineers active in the fields of vibroacoustics, environmental acoustics, and psychoacoustics. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements. Mechanical waves and vibrations are traditionally controlled using linear devices with fixed properties. In this PhD project, the student will explore a new generation of nonlinear resonators whose dynamic behaviour changes with vibration amplitude, enabling functionalities that are not achievable with conventional designs. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. The goal is to develop efficient models and design rules for nonlinear metamaterials capable of adaptive vibration isolation, frequency conversion, and non-reciprocal wave propagation. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative Swiss-French project involving Empa, ETH Zurich, and LAUM. Your tasks As doctoral candidate within this project you will work on highly nonlinear building blocks for vibrational metamaterials. Specific tasks to achieve the challenging results include Develop analytical and numerical models for strongly nonlinear resonators exhibiting nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia effects. Design, simulate, and optimize novel resonator concepts based on inertia amplification, bilinear stiffness, and multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics. Manufacture and experimentally characterize resonator prototypes using vibration testing, laser vibrometry, and modal analysis techniques. Investigate nonlinear phenomena such as internal resonances, frequency conversion, bifurcations, and nonlinear energy transfer. Create reduced-order models and efficient simulation tools for the design of nonlinear metamaterials and wave-control devices. Disseminate research results through publications in leading journals, presentations at international conferences, and collaboration with project partners at ETH Zurich and the Université du Mans. Your profile If you recognize yourself in the story below, then you have the profile that fits the project and the research group: I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics, obtained no longer than four years ago and performed above average in comparison to my peers. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some experience with at least one of the following: structural and/or nonlinear dynamics, numerical modelling techniques (finite element method), or experimental methods in acoustics. I have a profound interest for these topics. As a researcher I perform research in a structured and scientifically sound manner. I read technical papers, understand the nuances between different theories and implement and improve methodologies myself. In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors which steer the direction of my research. It's important for me to work as an active team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and being inspired by my colleagues. During my PhD I want to grow towards more independence, e.g. representing the research group on project meetings and conferences. I see these events as an occasion to disseminate my work to an audience of international experts and research colleagues, and to learn about the larger context of my research and the research project. Our offer We offer a fully funded 4-year PhD position at Empa. The candidate will also be enrolled as a PhD student at the ETH Zürich, co-supervised by Dr. Paolo Tiso. The core of the PhD project will be conducted at Empa with at least one research secondment in Le Mans and intense collaboration with the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETHZ. Besides ample occasions to develop yourself in a scientific and/or industrial direction offered by the research group, further doctoral training for PhD candidates is provided in the framework of the Doctoral School . Starting date is February 2027 or upon mutual agreement. You stay in a vibrant environment centrally in Europe. Empa has its main campus in Dübendorf, located close to Zürich and 20 minutes by tram from Zurich International Airport. Zurich is one of the cities with the highest quality of life worldwide, welcoming to non-German speaking people and with ample opportunities for social, cultural, and outdoor activities. We foster a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities. Our commitment is documented in our Diversity Action Plan and refers to specific goals, which are implemented and further developed on a regular basis. You don't meet every single requirement? We are aware that particularly women and individuals from minority backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. However, we also value motivation, commitment and a willingness to learn. If you see yourself in this role, we would love to receive your qualified application, even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements. We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

items.title: PhD Position: Safe Planning and Decision-Making under Uncertainty for Long-Horizon Robot Autonomy
items.desc: Join TU Delft and the EU-funded OPERA consortium. Push the frontier of general-purpose AI for robotics and tackle the fundamental tension between long-horizon reasoning and real-time safety guarantees. Job Description Robots that operate for long periods among people must plan beyond the next few seconds while staying safe. They need to predict how their surroundings and the people in them will evolve, know how reliable these predictions are, and adapt their plans when the predictions fail. In the EU-funded OPERA project, TU Delft contributes to General-Purpose AI for robotics by developing methods that combine fast, reactive behavior with more deliberate reasoning, planning, and decision-making. In this PhD position, you will develop planning and decision-making methods that let robots act safely and reliably over long time horizons when their knowledge of the environment and of the people around them is incomplete. The research sits at the intersection of model-based planning and control and learning-based models, and addresses the trade-off between safety, performance, and real-time computation. You will formulate the methods and analyze their guarantees and failure modes. This research is connected to OPERA's tasks on GPAI-powered planning and decision-making, on long-term reasoning in human-centered environments, and on adaptive human-robot and robot-environment interaction. Depending on your background, the work may draw on optimal control and model predictive control, motion planning, probabilistic modeling and estimation, or learning-based methods. The emphasis is on methods with a clear formulation and well-understood failure modes, validated in simulation and on real robots. You will work in the Cognitive Robotics Department at TU Delft under the supervision of Prof. Robert Babuška and Dr. Laura Ferranti, and you will be embedded in the Reliable Robot Control Lab (https://r2clab.com/). You will collaborate with OPERA partners across Europe on simulation, perception, and the OPERA open-source toolbox. Job Requirements The ideal candidate for this PhD position has a strong background in control, optimization, or motion planning and is motivated by the question of how robots can plan safely and reliably over long time horizons. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds who want to work at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. You have: An MSc degree in Systems and Control, Robotics, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field. A strong interest in safe planning and decision-making for robots, at the intersection of planning, control, and learning. A passion for rigorous, theoretically grounded research, combined with an eagerness to validate ideas in simulation and on real robots. Strong analytical and mathematical skills, in particular in optimization, probability and statistics, and dynamical systems. Excellent communication skills and proficiency in English (written and verbal), as required for academic publication and international collaboration. You are particularly encouraged to apply if you have experience in one or more of the following areas: Hands-on experience implementing optimization-based planners or controllers (e.g., model predictive control with acados or CasADi) in C++ or Python. Safe or robust control and planning under uncertainty. Learned dynamics or prediction models, model-based reinforcement learning. Uncertainty quantification, probabilistic or Bayesian modeling, state estimation. Long-horizon or hierarchical planning, prediction of human or multi-agent behavior. Real-robot deployment with ROS or ROS 2. As part of OPERA, you will travel to meet and collaborate with the project’s European partners and attend regular consortium meetings. We particularly encourage applications from women and other underrepresented groups, as we are committed to building a diverse and inclusive research environment. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Mechanical Engineering From chip to ship. From machine to human being. From idea to solution. Driven by a deep-rooted desire to understand our environment and discover its underlying mechanisms, research and education at the ME faculty focusses on fundamental understanding, design, production including application and product improvement, materials, processes and (mechanical) systems. ME is a dynamic and innovative faculty with high-tech lab facilities and international reach. It’s a large faculty but also versatile, so we can often make unique connections by combining different disciplines. This is reflected in ME’s outstanding, state-of-the-art education, which trains students to become responsible and socially engaged engineers and scientists. We translate our knowledge and insights into solutions to societal issues, contributing to a sustainable society and to the development of prosperity and well-being. That is what unites us in pioneering research, inspiring education and (inter)national cooperation. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Mechanical Engineering. Do you want to experience working at our faculty? These videos will introduce you to some of our researchers and their work. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3059 - €3881 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information For more information, please reach out to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska [l.ferranti@tudelft.nl, r.babuska@tudelft.nl] Please do not use LinkedIn and other channels for applications or inquiries. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 15 November 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: A letter of motivation explaining why you are the right candidate for this project An updated cv Exam transcipts from your Bachelor and Master A copy of your MSc thesis, or draft MSc thesis (or a link to access it) You can address your application to Laura Ferranti and Robert Babuska. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: #EUfunded This is an EU funded project, named OPERA, with project number 101298363, within program HORIZON/HORIZON-CL4-2025-04-DIGITAL-EMERGING-07 You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

items.title: PhD in experimental physics: how do you make the first antimatter molecule?
items.desc: Your function When a proton meets a hydrogen atom, the pair can emit a photon and stay together as H₂⁺. This is how the first molecules formed after the Big Bang, and it is one of the proposed routes to the first antimatter molecule, yet it has never been measured. In the NWO Vidi project SAMURAI, you will study these collisions one quantum state at a time: instead of colliding atoms, we use lasers to prepare a hydrogen molecule at the moment of a collision and watch it fall apart. You will be part of a small group in which experiment and theory go hand in hand. Your duties excite H₂ with two tunable extreme-ultraviolet lasers (60–205 nm), built in our lab and unique in the Netherlands, and image the fragments with velocity-map imaging aim for the first spectroscopic observation of the excited electronic states of H₂⁺, calculated by Edward Teller in his PhD thesis in 1930 and never seen since trap H₂⁺ ions and use millimetre waves and magnetic fields to control how they come apart work towards the first measurement of radiative association: joining a cold proton and a cold hydrogen atom with light, next to a crystal of laser-cooled Be⁺ ions compare your data with multichannel quantum-defect theory and scattering calculations, and contribute to the theory yourself if you like develop your skills in lasers and nonlinear optics, ultrahigh vacuum, electronics, CAD design and scientific programming present your results at international conferences and publish them in peer-reviewed journals Your profile an MSc degree (or close to completing one) in physics, physical chemistry or a related field affinity with quantum mechanics and atomic, molecular and optical physics, and an interest in lasers and electronics good command of spoken and written English most important: you are curious, enjoy building things that work, like working in a team, and want to spend four years on a question nobody has answered yet As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset. We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements. What do we offer? Education A challenging position in a socially engaged organisation. At VU Amsterdam, you contribute to education, research and service for a better world. And that is valuable. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of minimum € 3.204,00 (PhD) and maximum € 4.051,00 (PhD) gross per month, on a full-time basis. This is based on UFO profile PhD candidate. The exact salary depends on your education and experience. a position for at least 0.8 FTE. Your employment contract will initially last 1 year. Afterwards, the possibility of expansion exists. We also offer you attractive fringe benefits and regulations. Some examples: A full-time 38-hour working week comes with a holiday leave entitlement of 232 hours per year. If you choose to work 40 hours, you have 96 extra holiday leave hours on an annual basis. For part-timers, this is calculated pro rata. 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% end-of-year bonus contribution to commuting expenses group insured for partial disability with employer contribution of 50% of the premium optional model for designing a personalized benefits package About Us Quantum Metrology and Laser Applications (QMLA), LaserLaB Amsterdam The Quantum Metrology and Laser Applications group in the Department of Physics and Astronomy is a very international group of some 20 strongly collaborating senior and junior scientists. The group carries out precision measurements on atoms and molecules, using advanced laser techniques and methods to cool their motion. It shares the infrastructure of LaserLaB Amsterdam, with lasers ranging from ultrastable to ultrafast, connected to atomic clocks and frequency combs. The aims are to test fundamental theories such as quantum electrodynamics, to determine fundamental constants such as the proton-to-electron mass ratio, and to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Molecular Ions group Within QMLA, the Molecular Ions group led by Dr. Max Beyer studies the simplest molecules there are, with one, two, three and four electrons: H₂⁺, H₂, He₂⁺ and He₂. These systems are simple enough to be calculated with extreme precision, so every measurement is a direct test of theory, and we do both: experiments and ab initio, quantum-defect and scattering calculations. In the lab we laser-cool molecules, trap ions and use light from across the electromagnetic spectrum, from the extreme ultraviolet through the visible and infrared to millimetre waves. More at www.molecularions.com (https://www.molecularions.com/). Faculty of Science Working at the Faculty of Science means collaborating with students, lecturers and researchers who are focused on their field, yet have a broad view of the world. We are proud of a positive and inclusive workplace culture within the faculty, where we work together with great energy and a pragmatic attitude to tackle social challenges. At the Faculty of Science, scientists and students work on fundamental and complex societal issues for a sustainable, healthy and just future. From forest fires to big data, from obesity to malnutrition, from helium to the universe and from genetics to medicine: our education and research cover the full breadth of science, from molecules to mankind. Our academic education and research are highly experimental, technical and interdisciplinary in nature. That is why we collaborate extensively with leading scientific institutes and industry. The faculty has more than 8,000 students studying in one of the 39 programms and employs more than 1,400 staff across 10 scientific departments, making us one of the largest science faculties in the Netherlands. Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam stands for values-driven education and research. We are open-minded experts with the ability to think freely - a broader mind. Maintaining an entrepreneurial perspective and concentrating on diversity, significance and humanity, we work on sustainable solutions with social impact. By joining forces, across the boundaries of disciplines, we work towards a better world for people and planet. Together we create a safe and respectful working and study climate, and an inspiring environment for education and research. Learn more about our codes of conduct (https://vu.nl/en/about-vu/more-about/code-of-conduct-vu-amsterdam) We are located on one physical campus, in the heart of Amsterdam's Zuidas business district, with excellent location and accessibility. Over 6,150 staff work at the VU and over 31,000 students attend academic education. Diversity Diversity is the driving force of VU Amsterdam. VU wants to be accessible and receptive to diversity in disciplines, cultures, ideas, nationalities, beliefs, preferences and worldviews. We believe that trust, respect, interest and differences lead to new insights and innovation, to sharpness and clarity, to excellence and a broader understanding. We stand for an inclusive community and believe that diversity and internationalisation contribute to the quality of education, research and our services. Therefore, we are always searching for people whose backgrounds and experience contribute to the diversity of the VU community. Interested Do you want to be the one who makes this measurement? Then we look forward to your application. Please include: a detailed CV a cover letter describing your background, motivation and skills (max. 1 page) transcripts with all your grades from your BSc and MSc studies your MSc thesis, or a draft if it is not finished yet your diploma(s) the names and contact details of two references Applications will be considered until the position is filled. items.title: PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps
items.desc: Hjem Karriere i SINTEF Ledige stillinger Ledig stilling PhD Candidate (MSCA) in multiscale ejector design and optimization within high temperature heat pumps About the position SINTEF Energy is announcing two PhD candidate positions within the field of thermal engineering and industrial heat supply utilizing High Temperature Heat Pumps (HTHPs). Both positions are within the frame of a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN). The candidate will be employed by the Energy Use Department to carry out the doctoral project described below, enrolled by the doctoral program at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), and have supervisors at both SINTEF and DTU Construct. About the project The activity is coordinated within the HeatMinds MSCA-DN by Brunel University in London, UK. The HeatMinds project is officially launched in October 2026 and holds a consortium of 18 partners across Europe. This integrated project aims to conduct collaborative research while training fifteen doctoral candidates to make a step change in accelerating the development and deployment of industrial HTHPs to support the decarbonization of heat supply in the process industry. Supported by leading universities, research centres, and industrial actors, advanced models and design tools will be developed that contribute to the advancement of these efforts. HeatMinds will tackle highly connected research questions, namely what are the optimum and sustainable cycle arrangements, component designs, and supporting energy policy frameworks? HeatMinds will establish a roadmap for deploying IHTHP technology to support the decarbonisation of several key industries. The other project partners recruiting PhD students are Brunel University (UK), City St. Georges University (UK), University of Seville (Spain), Technical University of Denmark, and SINTEF Industry. One of the PhD projects hosted by SINTEF Energy is titled “Multiscale design and optimization of ejectors integrated within novel IHTHP architectures” and addresses the potential for improved energy efficiency achieved by using ejectors. The project also addresses the coupled and multiscale challenges associated with optimal design and integration, and focuses on the use of natural working fluids. On the one hand, the analysis and design of optimal heat pump cycles is typically carried out using simple lumped or one-dimensional models. On the other hand, accurate component performance and design requires more detailed analysis methods, such as CFD, that present a challenge for how complex and coupled systems should be designed. This Project Includes Elements Of Evaluation of two-phase ejector component integration strategies within high temperature heat pump applications, considering system constraints and ejector performance trade-offs. Component design and optimization using computational fluid dynamics. Exploration of multi-fidelity and multiscale modelling methods that may include surrogate modelling approaches for coupled cycle analyses. Evaluation of proposed efficient reduced-order ejector performance models that could be directly implemented to ejector dimensioning tools and/or automation algorithms. Comparison to experimental test results. SINTEF Energy, along with the partners in HeatMinds, hold significant experience and expertise in the analysis, design, and experimental testing of two-phase ejectors integrated in refrigeration and heat pump applications. DTU Construct additionally has an extensive track record working with two-phase flow, turbomachinery, and design optimization. The work will be conducted in close collaboration with SINTEF colleagues as well as with HeatMinds partners. The project includes an international secondment to Danfoss (Denmark), to gain practical insight into industrial R&D for ejector components and systems. Duties of the position Publish scientific articles and contribute to dissemination activities. Engage in collaboration and secondment with HeatMinds partners. Participate in relevant conferences, workshops, and training activities. Be flexible and prepare to adjust to activities and project focus as the PhD project progresses if needed. Complete the doctoral education. Participate actively in the relevant SINTEF Energy research groups’ activities. Required Selection Criteria You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree[JD1.1]. Master’s students in their final year can apply, but the degree must be completed and documented before 1 January 2027. Strong academic record (average grade B or better) or demonstrated research potential Must meet the admission requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Please see https://www.dtu.dk/english/education/phd for more information for specific requirements for the PhD program at DTU Construct. Excellent written and spoken English. MSCA Mobility Rule: At the time of employment, the candidate must not have lived, worked, or studied in Norway for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the start date of the position. The appointment is to be made in accordance with SINTEF’s guidelines for recruitment positions and the academic regulations set by DTU Construct. Background (mandatory) Strong mechanical engineering fundamentals with a focus on thermal and fluid flow phenomena Foundations of computational fluid dynamics, numerical methods, and heat and mass transfer Thermodynamic cycle analysis Fundamentals of programming Additional background that will be valued in the selection process: Optimisation methods and/or surrogate modeling for component and system design Multiphase flow and phase change modelling Familiarity with experimental methods and model validation Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently and take initiative. Plan and carry out research systematically. Collaborate effectively in multidisciplinary teams. Show strong motivation and curiosity for the subject. Communicate clearly and constructively with colleagues. Emphasis will be placed on personal suitability and motivation for the position. We offer An exciting and challenging research project within an international MSCA Doctoral Network with excellent opportunities to collaborate within international research groups and industry. A dynamic, creative, and inclusive working environment. Access to cutting edge facilities and interdisciplinary training. Career development and mentoring through the HeatMinds network. Salary and conditions The employment period is three years, funded through the EU Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Grant HeatMinds. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. The position is conditional on external funding. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. About The Application The Application Must Include A letter motivating the application (cover letter). Curriculum vitae. Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale. Names and contact information of two references. Applications without the required documentation will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, race, disability, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. Contacts Joshua Render Dowdell, Researcher. Email: joshua.dowdell@sintef.no, phone +47 484 05 669 Petter Nekså: Chief Scientist. Email: Petter.Neksa@sintef.no, phone: +47 926 06 519 Elisa Magnanelli, Research Manager. items.title: Doktorand i elektroteknik med inriktning cybersäkerhet
items.desc: Beskrivning av verksamheten Avdelningen för säkerhets- och nätverkssystem inom Institutionen för elektro- och informationsteknik arbetar brett med forskning inom krytografi, datasäkerhet samt trådlåsa- och fasta näterk. Avdelningen bedriver flera forskningsprojekt genom olika samverkansplattformar, arrangerar forskningskonferenser och seminarier, vilket synliggör forskningen och dess resultat. Forskningsplattformarna används även till att skapa tvärvetenskapliga projekt, bidrar till nationella och internationella forskningsnätverk, vilket gör att avdelningen erbjuder en dynamisk forskningsmiljö. Vi söker nu en ny doktorand för arbete inom cybersäkerhet och mjukvaruteknik i ett projekt finnasierat av strategiska forskningsstiftelsen, SSF. Att vara doktorand Som doktorand är du både antagen som student och anställd vid Lunds universitet. Som forskarstuderande tränas du i ett vetenskapligt förhållningssätt. Det kan kort beskrivas som att du får övning i att tänka kritiskt och analytiskt, att du får lösa problem självständigt med hjälp av rätt metodval och du får en forskningsetisk medvetenhet. Dessutom ges möjlighet för dig som doktorand att arbeta med projekt, att utveckla dina ledaregenskaper och din pedagogiska förmåga. Under hela din studietid guidas du av handledare. Forskarstudierna avslutas med en avhandling och doktorsexamen. Mer om att vara doktorand vid LTH på lth.se. Projektbeskrivning Du kommer att arbeta i projekt RESIST och främst bidra till området skydd av distribuerad AI. RESIST är i samarbete med Linköpings universitet, Örebro universitet och forskningsinstitutet RISE och är ett multidisciplinärt forskningscentrum som arbetar med det snabbt växande området att ta fram förutsättningar och tekniker för att skydda framtidens AI-baserade system. Centrumet leds av Linköpings universitet med Lunds universitet som partner. Arbetsuppgifter Du kommer framförallt att ägna dig åt din forskarutbildning, vilket innefattar såväl deltagande i forskningsprojekt som forskarutbildningskurser, seminarier och konferenser. De huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifterna är att bedriva forskning och undervisning i gränslandet mellan cybersäkerhet och mjukvaruteknik. Forskningen är inriktad på området automatiserade principer för att analysera programkod. Detta innefattar hur man med hjälp av AI-modeller kan analysera och korrigera mjukvara så att den inte innehåller svagheter. Exempelvis har det visat sig att AI-generad kod ofta har stora säkerhetsbrister. För att man skall kunna använda AI-genererad kod inom tillämpningar med hög säkerhet, behöver därför kodgenereringen göras mycket mer robust. Det ingår i arbetsuppgifterna att utvärdera existerande tekniker ur ett säkerhetsperspektiv och att hitta principer för automatisk analys och kodkorrigering. Fallstudier och experimentbaserad forskning förväntas vara centrala forskningsmetoder i doktorandprojektet. I arbetsuppgifterna ingår det även medverkan i undervisning och annat institutionsarbete (dock max 20% av arbetstiden). Kvalifikationer För att kunna antas och anställas som doktorand behöver du uppfylla kraven nedan. Behörighetskrav Grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå uppfyller du som har: avlagt examen på avancerad nivå eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå eller på något annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskild behörighet för elektroteknik uppfyller du som har: minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå med relevans för ämnesområdet, eller civilingenjörsexamen inom datateknik, elektroteknik, informations- och kommunikationsteknik, medicin och teknik, teknisk fysik, teknisk matematik eller teknisk nanovetenskap. Övriga krav För att tillgodogöra sig den aktuella forskarutbildningen krävs även: Mycket goda programmeringskunskaper. Erfarenhet av att arbeta med komplexa dator- och kommunikationssystem. God förmåga till självständigt arbete och förmåga att formulera och angripa vetenskapliga problem. God förmåga till skriftlig och muntlig kommunikation. God samarbetsförmåga. Mycket goda kunskaper i engelska, i tal och skrift. Meriterande För Den Aktuella Forskarutbildningen Är Följande Meriterande Avslutade kurser och/eller examensarbete inom datasäkerhet. Dokumenterad erfarenhet av principer för mjukvaruutveckling. Dokumenterad erfarenhet av mjukvaruutveckling. Dokumenterad erfarenhet av tekniker för artificiell intelligens. Dokumenterad erfarenhet av undervisning och kommunikation. Industriell erfarenhet. items.title: Doctoral student in Web and Emerging Applications Security
items.desc: Join a world-leading research environment at the Chalmers Security and Privacy Lab and help shape the future of web, software, and AI security. As a doctoral student, you will contribute to cutting-edge cybersecurity research while working closely with internationally recognized researchers. This position offers an excellent opportunity to develop as an independent researcher and make an impact on secure and trustworthy digital systems. Software is often the root cause of vulnerabilities in modern computing systems. We develop principled concepts and mechanisms to ensure robust security and privacy for software. You will be supervised by Prof. Andrei Sabelfeld (Wallenberg Scholar and recipient of awards from ERC, SSF, VR, WASP, Google, Amazon, Facebook, and OpenAI, as well as the Chalmers Doctoral Supervisor of the Year award). About Us The Department of Computer Science and Engineering, a joint department of Chalmers and the University of Gothenburg, spans the breadth of computing disciplines. Our internationally visible research, strong industry links and diverse environment create a collaborative setting where ideas grow into real impact. At the division of Computing Science, we advance secure and trustworthy software and systems, spanning foundations, programming languages, tools and practical methods that help shape dependable digital infrastructures. About The Research Project You will contribute to one of our research projects on Web and Emerging Applications Security. Our research tracks include: Web application crawling and security scanning (Black Widow, Black Ostrich, and Spider-Scents) Security and privacy of browser extensions (FakeX and CodeX) JavaScript server-side sandboxing (SandTrap) Data minimization in Trigger-Action Platforms (minTAP and LazyTAP) Security and privacy of agentic and AI-integrated systems (ongoing research area) Promotional video of our research on securing web applications Who We Are Looking For The following requirements are mandatory: To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (masterexamen) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree (magisterexamen) of 60 credits* in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a closely related field Strong written and verbal communication skills in English Documented research interest and/or achievements in cybersecurity and/or privacy Ability to work independently and analytically to solve complex research problems for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted. The Following Experience Will Strengthen Your Application A Master's thesis or research-oriented project in language-based security, web security, or systems security Experience with program analysis, formal methods, or AI/LLM-based systems Publications, open-source security tools, or participation in security competitions (CTFs) and bug bounty programs What You Will Do Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate School of Computer Science and Engineering Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours Conduct research within one of the tracks above Design, implement, and evaluate security analysis tools and prototypes, such as crawlers, scanners, sandboxes, data minimizers, and extension analyzers Publish and present results at cybersecurity venues Contract terms The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start. The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years. A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026). Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn. What We Offer As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about working at Chalmers and our benefits for employees. A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg. Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg. Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence. We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities. If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in. Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here. Application procedure The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files. CV Personal letter A brief introduction about yourself and your track record. A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position. A brief description of your future goals and research focus. Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts. Documented evidence of relevant work, if available, such as (links to) research papers, project reports, and software repositories. Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form. A background check may be conducted as part of the application process. Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview. We welcome your application no later than November 27, 2026. For Questions, Please Contact Professor Andrei Sabelfeld andrei@chalmers.se We look forward to your application! Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position. *** Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society. Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

Ämnes- och projektbeskrivning Genom Wallenberg AI, Autonomous Systems and Software Program (WASP) erbjuder vi nu en ny doktorandtjänst inom området tillämpad kryptografi. WASP är Sveriges största enskilda forskningsprogram någonsin, en betydande nationell satsning på strategiskt motiverad grundforskning, utbildning och rekrytering av forskare. Programmet behandlar forskning kring artificiell intelligens och autonoma system som samverkar med människor, anpassar sig till sin omgivning genom sensorer, information och kunskap, och bildar intelligenta system-av-system. Mer om WASP (wasp-sweden.org). De huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifterna för doktorandanställningen är att bedriva forskning och undervisning inom området tillämpad kryptografi. Forskningen är inriktad mot det bredare området för integritetsbevarande kommunikation och outsourcing av beräkningar. Kommunikation över internet är sårbar för övervakning och censur. Integritetsbevarande kommunikationstekniker (t.ex. Tor, Nym, Snowflake) gör det möjligt för användare att kringgå sådan övervakning och censur. Forskningsområdet omfattar att designa, analysera och implementera sådana system; dessutom förväntas studier av olika attacker och motåtgärder ingå i forskningsmetoden. Integritetsbevarande outsourcing av beräkningar gör det möjligt för användare att lägga ut beräkningsuppgifter på en molnserver utan att servern får kännedom om användardata eller ens vilken typ av beräkningar som utförs. Det finns olika tekniker för sådan integritetsbevarande outsourcing av beräkningar, såsom Trusted Execution Environment (t.ex. Intel SGX) och full homomorfisk kryptering (TFHE, BGV). Vidare kan de specifika funktionerna/uppgifterna vara föremål för attacker, och att identifiera attacker och motåtgärder förväntas ingå i forskningen. Forskningsmetoden kommer att vara en kombination av systemstudier, design och experimentell forskning. Das Projekt wird vom Forschungsteam «Auditory Pathway» am Hearing Research Laboratory des ARTORG Centers for Biomedical Engineering Research der Universität Bern in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Universitätsklinik für Hals-, Nasen- und Ohrenkrankheiten am Inselspital durchgeführt. Cochlea-Implantate sind hochwirksame Neuroprothesen, die Menschen mit hochgradigem Hörverlust ermöglichen, wieder Klänge wahrzunehmen und Sprache zu verstehen. Wie gut das Sprachverstehen nach der Implantation gelingt, ist individuell sehr unterschiedlich: Bei rund einem Viertel der Patientinnen und Patienten bleiben die Ergebnisse hinter den Erwartungen zurück, und verlässliche Prognosen zum individuellen Nutzen eines Cochlea-Implantats vor der Operation fehlen bislang. Hinweise deuten darauf hin, dass neben dem Hörorgan auch die Verarbeitung und Vernetzung im Gehirn eine wichtige Rolle spielen. Die SOUND Study untersucht, wie sich diese Erkenntnisse für individuellere Prognosen nutzen lassen. Das erwartet Sie Im Rahmen der SOUND Study untersuchen Sie die zentralen Hörbahnen mithilfe neuester bildgebender Verfahren. Im Fokus stehen die funktionelle Nahinfrarotspektroskopie (fNIRS) und spezialisierte Magnetresonanztomografie-Sequenzen (MRT) Sie führen neurobildgebende, audiologische und klinische Daten zusammen und wenden statistische Verfahren sowie Machine Learning an, um Muster zu erkennen, die mit dem späteren Sprachverstehen zusammenhängen Ihre Ergebnisse diskutieren und interpretieren Sie gemeinsam mit Fachpersonen aus der Neuroradiologie sowie mit klinischen und technischen Expertinnen und Experten Das bringen Sie mit Masterabschluss in Elektrotechnik, biomedizinischer Technik, Physik oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet Praktische Erfahrung in der Signalverarbeitung Erfahrung in der medizinischen Bildanalyse oder Interesse, sich in dieses Gebiet einzuarbeiten; Kenntnisse in Datenanalyse oder Machine Learning sind von Vorteil Interesse an klinischer Forschung und an der Arbeit mit Patientinnen und Patienten sowie Freude an der interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

items.title: Doktorand (m/w/d) im Bereich Robotik & KI: Fertigung nachhaltiger Faserverbundbauteile
items.desc: Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter, Doktorand (m/w/d) im Bereich Robotik & KI: Fertigung nachhaltiger Faserverbundbauteile Robotisch gefertigte Faserverbundstrukturen eröffnen große Potenziale für ressourceneffiziente und nachhaltige Baukomponenten, insbesondere beim Einsatz biobasierter Naturfasern wie Flachs. In der Praxis ist der Weg zur reproduzierbaren, serientauglichen Fertigung jedoch anspruchsvoll: Naturfasern zeigen chargen- und umgebungsbedingte Schwankungen, die zu Abweichungen im Faserverlauf, Qualitätsstreuungen und erhöhter Nacharbeit führen können. Für robuste Prozesse braucht es daher eine durchgängige, digitale Prozessüberwachung, die Abweichungen während der Fertigung erkennt und der Robotik eine schnelle, zielgerichtete Reaktion ermöglicht. Am ISW erforschen und entwickeln wir dafür Algorithmen und Softwarebausteine, die kamerabasierte Inline-Bildverarbeitung, KI-gestützte Anomalieerkennung und Echtzeit-Integration in die Robotersteuerung verbinden. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf der intelligenten Auswertung von Sensordaten und der Online-Anpassung des Wickelpfads bzw. robotischer Bewegungs-/Ablageparameter, um Material- und Prozessschwankungen automatisch zu kompensieren. Ziel ist ein robustes, selbstüberwachendes robotisches Wickelverfahren mit stabiler Bauteilqualität, als Grundlage für wirtschaftliche und nachhaltige Faserverbundbauteile. Wir Bieten Ihnen Hoher Anwendungsbezug und praxisnahe Forschung im Spannungsfeld von Robotik, KI und nachhaltiger Fertigung Möglichkeit zur Promotion in einem hochaktuellen Thema Interdisziplinäre Forschungsarbeit mit moderner Robotik-, Sensorik- und Software-Infrastruktur Ein Sprungbrett für Ihre Karriere in Industrie oder Wissenschaft Ihre Zukünftigen Themenschwerpunkte Zusammengefasst Entwicklung und Integration einer Inline-Bildverarbeitung (Kamerasysteme am Roboter) zur Erfassung von Faserverlauf und Qualitätsmerkmalen während des Wickelns Konzeption und Umsetzung KI-basierter Anomalieerkennung zur Detektion/Klassifikation von Qualitätsabweichungen in Bilddaten Aufbau einer Daten- und Softwarepipeline für Training, Test und Deployment Entwicklung einer Echtzeitfähigen Kopplung von Bildauswertung/KI mit Robotik Implementierung von Methoden zur Online-Pfadanpassung / Pfadkorrektur auf Basis der Sensordaten und experimentelle Validierung am Demonstrator Ihr Profil Sie haben Ihr Studium in Technischer Kybernetik, Mechatronik, Maschinenbau, Autonome Systeme oder einer verwandten Fachrichtung mit guten Leistungen abgeschlossen oder sind gerade dabei es abzuschließen Sie bringen erste Erfahrung oder starkes Interesse in mindestens einem der Bereiche Computer Vision/Bildverarbeitung, Machine Learning, Robotik-Softwareentwicklung, Regelung/Echtzeit-Systeme mit Sie arbeiten strukturiert, eigenständig und gerne interdisziplinär. items.title: PhD: Mechanisms of HIV-induced neurodegeneration (MCSA)
items.desc: Job description About the project MERIT (MEtabolic Reprogramming in viral pathogenesis: from Infection to Therapeutic innovations) is an EU-funded MSCA training programme aimed at better understanding how viruses affect the human body. Coordinated by Dr. Adithya Sridhar, Assistant Professor, and Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt, Professor of Pediatric Infectious diseases, from the OrganoVIR Labs at Amsterdam UMC (location AMC), this project brings together 7 academic institutions and 12 associated partners from across Europe. Within MERIT, researchers will take a new, holistic approach that focuses on infections and host metabolism to unravel virus-induced metabolic reprogramming and its impact on human health. The project’s objective lies in understanding the complex interplay between viruses and host cells, focusing on metabolic reprogramming, and long-term consequences of infection. This will be achieved by combining three methodological pillars: human organoids, integrative and spatial omics, and advanced microscopy. About the role Despite effective combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), individuals living with HIV experience neurocognitive impairments, collectively known as HIV-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). The neuropathological changes observed in HAND are also found in neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), such as Alzheimer’s disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, and Parkinson’s disease. A common link between HAND and NDDs is disrupted lipid metabolism, with HAND patients exhibiting increased amyloid-beta deposition. Clinical data suggest that TDP-43 proteinopathy may contribute to HAND, further linking it to NDDs. This project aims to explore these connections using iPSC-derived microglia-embedded brain organoids. By characterising lipid profile changes following HIV infections and investigating TDP-43 proteinopathy, we seek to identify potential mechanisms underlying HAND. At the Amsterdam UMC in the Netherlands, MERIT is looking for a Doctoral Candidate (DC) to work on Work Packages 1 and 2. As DC7, your objectives are: to characterise lipidomic profiles of HIV-infected brain organoids compared to healthy organoids; to assess and alter TDP-43 proteinopathy in HIV-infected organoids. You will be guided during your research project by Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt and Dr. Renata Vieira de Sá at the OrganoVIR Labs at the Amsterdam UMC, Netherlands. You can apply for this position until 30 October 2026 . Applications submitted after this date will not be considered. Profile a motivated PhD candidate with an academic qualification (MSc or MD, or close to completion) in one of these disciplines: in (bio)medical sciences, biology, cell biology, biotechnology, or a closely related field and has a solid foundation in molecular and cellular biology as well as immunology expertise in one or more of the following fields: virology, (3D) cell culture, tissue engineering. experience with experimental laboratory techniques relevant to the field, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary research team. excellent oral and written communication skills in English (minimum C1/C2 CEFR level) have not resided/carried out work or studies in the Netherlands for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before 1 April 2027 (transnational mobility rule). Our offer A contract with Amsterdam UMC for 36 hours per week for 4 years (probation of 6 months). The opportunity to work on large-scale and in-house research with motivated colleagues from all over the world. Planned secondments in International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology (ICGEB) & Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC). Training in safety and biosecurity aligned with international best practices. You will be trained in hazard identification, containment, incident reporting, and dual-use/gain-of-function issues. An opportunity to take part in a tailor-made pre-MBA programme to develop entrepreneurial and commercial skills and other network-wide training opportunities including conferences and courses, a Personal Development Plan, non-academic coaching, and workshops on topics including ethics and sustainability and AI/LLM. Classification in salary scale OIO: € 3,217 to € 4,077 gross for full-time employment (depending on experience). In addition to a good basic salary, we offer 8.3% end-of-year bonus. Calculate your net salary here. 100% reimbursement for public transport travel costs and, for private transport, €0.18 per km up to a maximum of 40 km each. Do you prefer walking or cycling? Take advantage of our good bike scheme. About the workplace Amsterdam UMC, location AMC, houses the university hospital and the medical faculty of the University of Amsterdam, as well as several research institutes. The OrganoVIR Labs is uniquely embedded within both the Department of Medical Microbiology and Infection Prevention (MMI) and the Department of Pediatrics and is affiliated with the Amsterdam Immunity and Infection Institute (AIII), Amsterdam Reproduction and Development (AR&D), and Emma Centre for Personalized Medicine (Emma CPM). This multidisciplinary positioning fosters close collaboration between fundamental, translational, and clinical research. OrganoVIR Labs has access to various advanced facilities including level 3, state-of-the-art molecular biology and culture facilities and access to high-throughput sequencing. Through its integration with the Department of Pediatrics, OrganoVIR Labs also benefits from extensive clinical expertise in the care of children with a broad spectrum of acute and chronic conditions. The department’s multidisciplinary approach and extensive clinical expertise support the translation of research findings into improved outcomes for pediatric patients. About the role The antiviral functions of the mitochondrial antiviral signalling protein in viral RNA detection and interferon response come at the cost of metabolic reprogramming and dysfunction. Mitochondrial changes during enterovirus infections include redistribution of mitochondria, disruption of calcium homeostasis, and generation of mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS). items.title: PhD: Implementation strategies for safe virus research in EU labs (MCSA)
items.desc: Job description About the project MERIT (MEtabolic Reprogramming in viral pathogenesis: from Infection to Therapeutic innovations) is an EU-funded MSCA training programme aimed at better understanding how viruses affect the human body. Coordinated by Dr. Adithya Sridhar, Assistant Professor, and Prof. Dr. Dasja Pajkrt, Professor of Pediatric Infectious diseases, from the OrganoVIR Labs at Amsterdam UMC (location AMC), this project brings together 7 academic institutions and 12 associated partners from across Europe. Within MERIT, researchers will take a new, holistic approach that focuses on infections and host metabolism to unravel virus-induced metabolic reprogramming and its impact on human health. The project’s objective lies in understanding the complex interplay between viruses and host cells, focusing on metabolic reprogramming, and long-term consequences of infection. This will be achieved by combining three methodological pillars: human organoids, integrative and spatial omics, and advanced microscopy. About the role The project aims to bridge the gap between biosafety guidelines and everyday laboratory practice by strengthening the implementation of safety measures. Using an implementation science approach, the project will systematically identify behavioural, social, and organisational determinants of compliance, and translate these into tailored, context-sensitive implementation strategies. Through qualitative and mixed methods research (e.g. literature reviews, interviews, questionnaires including discrete choice experiments or vignettes, and observations) the project will map the key drivers and barriers of safety behaviour. Building on these insights, it will explore how these determinants shape the mechanisms through which implementation strategies work, and under which conditions they are most effective and sustainable. In close collaboration with laboratory staff, including doctoral candidates and supervisors, suitable implementation strategies will be selected and tailored to local workflows, resources, and safety culture, and subsequently piloted in real-world laboratory settings. Ultimately, the project aims to enhance biosafety, research quality, and public trust in high-risk pathogen research. At the Amsterdam UMC in the Netherlands, MERIT is looking for a Doctoral Candidate (DC) to work on Work Package 2. As DC2, your objectives are: to identify behavioural, social, and organisational determinants of compliance with safety measures through literature review, interviews, questionnaires (discrete choice models or vignettes), and observations; to explore how these determinants influence mechanisms through which implementation strategies work; to work together with laboratory staff, DCs and supervisors to select and tailor implementation strategies; to pilot and evaluate these strategies in real-world laboratory settings across multiple EU institutions, focusing on their feasibility, acceptability, and appropriateness and their potential to strengthen compliance with biosafety practice. You will be guided during your research project by Dr. Rosa van Mansfeld, Dr. Mireille Dekker and Dr. Adithya Sridhar. You can apply for this position until 30 October 2026 . This PhD studentship is part of the ReIMAGINE[Life] programme, a major initiative funded by Prostate Cancer UK that aims to transform prostate cancer diagnosis and risk stratification through the integration of molecular, imaging, and clinical data. Working within the Treatment Resistance Team led by Professor Gerhardt Attard, you will analyse and integrate large-scale multi-omics datasets, including genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic data, alongside imaging and clinical information. You will develop innovative computational approaches and predictive models to improve risk stratification, disease monitoring, and patient outcomes.
