items.title: Promotion Informatik (m/w/d)
items.desc: Die Technische Universität Dresden (TUD) zählt als Exzellenzuniversität zu den leistungsstärksten Forschungseinrichtungen Deutschlands. Sie begreift Diversität als kulturelle Selbstverständlichkeit und Qualitätskriterium einer Exzellenzuniversität. Entsprechend begrüßen wir alle Bewerberinnen und Bewerber, die sich mit ihrer Leistung und Persönlichkeit bei uns und mit uns für den Erfolg aller engagieren möchten. An der Fakultät Informatik, Institut für Künstliche Intelligenz , ist an der Professur für Computational Logic im Rahmen des Sonderforschungsbereichs/Transregio 248 „Foundations of Perspicuous Software Systems“ zum 01.01.2027 , vorbehaltlich vorhandener Mittel, eine Stelle als wiss. Mitarbeiterin bzw. Mitarbeiter / Doktorandin bzw. Doktorand (m/w/d) (bei Vorliegen der persönlichen Voraussetzungen E 13 TV-L) bis 31.12.2030 (Beschäftigungsdauer gemäß WissZeitVG) zu besetzen. Es besteht die Gelegenheit zur eigenen wissenschaftlichen Weiterqualifikation (i. d. R. Promotion). Der Informatik-SFB/Transregio 248 legt die fundamentalen wissenschaftlichen Grundlagen für cyber-physische Systeme der Zukunft, die ihre Funktionalität und ihr Verhalten erläutern (sogenannte Perspicuous Systems). Erforscht wird eine tiefgehende und anwendbare Theorie von Erklärungen aller Facetten des Systemverhaltens sowie deren Erschließung durch visuelle und verbale Erläuterungen für verschiedene Nutzergruppen. Weitere Informationen unter www.perspicuous-computing.science. Als Mitglied der TUD werden Sie Teil eines erfolgreichen, interdisziplinären und internationalen Teams erfahrener Forschender. Aufgaben Die wesentlichen Aufgaben der Stelle sind die wiss. Erforschung und die Entwicklung von Methoden zur strukturierten, interaktiven Revision von Wissensbasen und Ontologien, von den theoretischen Grundlagen über komplexitätstheoretische Bewertung bis hin zur Implementierung und Evaluation. Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt hierbei auf Grundlagenforschung im Bereich beschreibungslogischer und regelbasierter Ontologiesprachen und deren Erweiterung zur Beschreibung kontextualisierten Wissens mithilfe von Standpunktlogik. Qualifikationsprofil wiss. Hochschulabschluss in der Fachrichtung Informatik oder verwandt vertiefte Kenntnisse in Theoretischer Informatik, vorzugsweise in Wissensrepräsentation und Logik sehr gute Grundkenntnisse in Mathematik strukturierte Arbeitsweise Fähigkeit, Projekte selbstständig voranzubringen und mit allen Beteiligten zu kommunizieren ausgezeichnetes schriftliches und mündliches Ausdrucksvermögen in Englisch gute Programmierkenntnisse und Interesse an experimentellen Aufgaben erwünscht Deutschkenntnisse auf mittlerem Niveau (ab Niveau B1 nach GER) erwünscht Wir bieten interessante und vielfältige Tätigkeit in einem Forschungsverbund zu einem hochaktuellen Thema flexible Arbeitszeiten 30 Urlaubstage pro Jahr (innerhalb einer 5-Tage-Woche) umfangreiches Angebot zur Fort- und Weiterbildung Gesundheitsvorsorge und Sportangebote der TUD ermäßigtes Jobticket (auch als Deutschlandticket) Teilnahme an der zusätzlichen Altersversorgung im öffentlichen Dienst über die VBL

items.title: PhD Researcher (m/f/d): Understanding climate risks to global food security
items.desc: Scientist Jena Developmental and Evolutionary Biology & Genetics Immunobiology and Infection Biology & Medicine Earth Sciences and Climate Research Social Sciences Linguistics Job Offer from October 23, 2026 The Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology (MPI-GEA) was founded in summer 2022 and is a dynamically growing, highly-interdisciplinary and international research institution. The research focuses on modeling and analyzing the interrelationships between biophysical and human-made systems, looking from the deep past to the future. The institute examines how humanity has driven the emergence of the Anthropocene – the period in which human activities began significantly impacting our planet’s climate and ecosystems – and identifying potential intervention points towards a more sustainable future. The Carl Zeiss Stiftung Independent Research Group on High-End Climate Risks (CZS-HECR) at MPI-GEA works towards an end-to-end understanding of worst-case climate outcomes, from unprecedented and compounding extremes to their societal impacts. The group combines fundamental physical process understanding rooted in climate physics and Earth System analyses, targeted climate model experiments, advanced statistics, including machine-learning- and explainable AI to deliver usable climate risk estimates under current and future climates for core societal sectors such as health, food, energy and finance. Doctoral researchers join an interdisciplinary team, and a broad international network are provided with highly competitive research conditions including generous support for travel and research visits. Candidate tasks Analyse the physical drivers and statistical properties of compounding and record-breaking extreme weather events using observations, reanalysis and climate model output Investigate the role of climate change in past, present and future agricultural losses including seasonal changes, the timing and sequencing of single and multi-hazards, Develop and apply statistical methods for agricultural impact attribution Write and publish your research as a doctoral thesis and papers in international journals Present results at conferences and group events, and take part in training such as Summer Schools and Workshops Your qualification Essential Master's degree (or equivalent) in climate science, atmospheric science, physics, geosciences, environmental science, statistics or a related field Programming skills (e.g. Python, R) and experience handling gridded or time-series data Strong motivation for independent, interdisciplinary research Good command of written and spoken English Advantageous Experience with climate model output, reanalysis data or extreme event analysis Knowledge of extreme value statistics, compound events or time-series methods Experience with agricultural modelling and agricultural datasets Experience with machine learning or causal methods Previous research experience, e.g. a Master's thesis in a related topic Our offer The position will begin on the 1st of January 2027 though some flexibility in start date is possible. Remuneration will follow the standard PhD salaries given in the Max Planck Society which correspond to 65% of EG 13 TvöD (Bund). The position includes 31 days of annual leave. We also offer attractive and family-friendly flextime and options for remote work. Additional benefits include an employer subsidy for public transport, access to training opportunities within the Max Planck Society, as well as language and health courses. The successful candidate can apply for admission to our graduate school “International Max Planck Research School for Modeling the Anthropocene”. The Max Planck Society is committed to employing more individuals with disabilities and especially encourages them to apply. We are also committed to encouraging diversity and actively challenging biases based on gender, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion and other components of identity. We were honored with the TOTAL E-QUALITY award for the first time in 2023 for our commitment. The Max Planck Society supports the compatibility of family and career and is certified according to the "berufundfamilie" (“job and family”) audit. Your application should include A cover letter A CV of no more than 3 pages A summary of research interests with max. 2 pages If applicable a list of relevant scientific, peer-reviewed publications related to the position or a copy of the candidate’s MA/MPhil/MSc thesis Contacts of two referees Any relevant certificates Position remains open until filled. Contact for more information Application portal Dr. Kai Kornhuber Email: kornhuber@gea.mpg.de

items.title: Doctoral Researcher for Low-Cost Production Drones/UAVs (Fixed Wing)
items.desc: 11.02.2026, Academic staff The TUM Chair of Aircraft Design is looking for a doctoral researcher in the field of Aircraft Design for Low-Cost Production of Drones/UAVs (fixed wing). The research is conducted in a joint project with industry and TUM IWB to develop decision support for future design designs for fixed wing UAVs. Besides research activities you will also contribute to the lectures and organizational tasks of the chair as well as supporting general aircraft design activities in the field of UAVs. About Us As member of the Department of Aerospace and Geodesy at the Technical University Munich the Chair for Aircraft Design is focusing on the design of manned and unmanned aircraft. The research is dedicated to the areas of „scenario analysis, future trends and technologies“, „aircraft design for civil and military operations“ and „operational analysis and evaluation“. The combination of these research focus areas provides an ideal platform for interdisciplinary research in simulation and experimental validation, including experimental flight testing. Requirements The actual developments show an increasing demand on high production numbers of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV)/drones. This extends well beyond the classical consumer eVTOL design into the field of fixed wing drones, even with hundreds of kg Take-Off Weight. Funded by industry and in a collaborative project with the Chair of Innovative Production Systems (TUM IWB) we target for an experimental decision support system trading performance driven with production tailored optimization UAV design. Besides the UAV design also new production concepts shall be investigated. You should hold a MSc. or Dipl. degree in aerospace or mechanical engineering well above average and you should have experience in designing, building and testing/flying of UAV concepts or model airplanes. Fundamental knowledge of the key disciplines in aerospace engineering and especially in aircraft design is required. Expertise in building and testing of model and scale aircraft is favoured. You should be interested in cooperation with other groups, bring good communication and writing skills in English to publish scientific papers. Due to security restrictions only applications from EU citizens will be considered. Tasks The chair is involved in multiple research projects focussing on novel UAV solutions for a variety of civil and military applications. It would be your task perform the joint project with industry and TUM IWB to develop decision support for future design designs for fixed wing UAVs. Besides research activities you will also contribute to the lectures and organizational tasks of the institute as well as supporting general aircraft design activities in the field of UAVs. We provide A full-time researcher position featuring a fixed-term contract with a salary in accordance with the German state regulated public service salary scale (TV-L E13) TUM is an equal opportunity employer. TUM aims to increase the proportion of women and therefore particularly welcomes applications by women. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given priority consideration given comparable qualifications. Application Please file your complete application before 27. February 2026 via Email or mail to: Technische Universität München Lehrstuhl für Luftfahrtsysteme Boltzmannstr. 15 85748 Garching bei München +49 89 289 15981 Sekretariat.lls@ed.tum.de The position is suitable for disabled persons. Disabled applicants will be given preference in case of generally equivalent suitability, aptitude and professional performance. Data Protection Information When you apply for a position with the Technical University of Munich (TUM), you are submitting personal information. With regard to personal information, please take note of the Datenschutzhinweise gemäß Art. 13 Datenschutz-Grundverordnung (DSGVO) zur Erhebung und Verarbeitung von personenbezogenen Daten im Rahmen Ihrer Bewerbung. (data protection information on collecting and processing personal data contained in your application in accordance with Art. 13 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)). By submitting your application, you confirm that you have acknowledged the above data protection information of TUM. items.title: SD-26142 PhD CANDIDATE IN SOCIAL CRITERIA DRIVEN ABSOLUTE ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY ASSESSMENT
items.desc: Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 48 months Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact. The Environmental Sustainability Assessment and Circularity (SUSTAIN) Unit conducts cross‑disciplinary research to support the transition toward a more sustainable, resilient, and healthy society. SUSTAIN combines expertise in environmental sciences, circular economy, risk and safety assessment, and sustainable innovation to address complex challenges related to human and environmental health, climate change, and resource efficiency, developing knowledge, methods, and transferable software for the simulation and comprehensive sustainability assessment of socio-economic systems. Its purpose is to foster sustainable eco-innovation, through products and technologies, as well as support sustainability-oriented policy implementation and behavioural change to promote decarbonisation transitions. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? The world faces a convergence of crises that are transforming the conditions for human development. Climate instability, ecosystem degradation, and the overuse of natural resources have reached critical levels, while social inequality, political fragmentation, and technological disruption are reshaping societies. Traditional notions of economic competitiveness, centred on growth and productivity, are being redefined to include social resilience, inclusiveness, and ecological integrity. Responding to this “polycrisis” requires new pathways that reconcile prosperity with planetary and social limits. Luxembourg offers a particularly illustrative example of these tensions. The country enjoys one of the highest income levels globally and a dynamic financial and business environment that sustains its reputation for economic success. Yet this prosperity depends strongly on cross-border commuting, which creates mobility challenges and environmental stress. Escalating housing prices have made access to affordable living increasingly difficult, displacing a significant share of the workforce beyond national borders. The reliance on imported energy leaves households and firms vulnerable to external shocks. Although Luxembourg’s welfare model and social dialogue remain robust, they are under pressure from rising costs of living, widening inequalities, and growing demands on public services. Environmentally, Luxembourg’s footprint per inhabitant ranks among the largest worldwide, driven by high consumption and land-use pressures that push the country beyond sustainable limits. Meeting these intertwined challenges calls for coordinated transformations that bridge sectors, disciplines, and scales. Economic and social progress must be reframed within the concept of a Safe Operating Space—an area in which human well-being is achieved without breaching environmental boundaries. The objective is to steer innovation, governance, and everyday practices toward forms of competitiveness that are compatible with sustainability, rather than in conflict with it. The Doctoral Training Unit C-SOS (Competitiveness within a Safe Operating Space) is designed to cultivate researchers capable of analysing and fostering such transformations. It brings together an interdisciplinary consortium to train 12 PhD candidates in the assessment and design of inclusive and sustainable development trajectories. The programme equips them with conceptual and methodological tools to connect environmental sustainability, social well-being, and economic dynamics into integrated frameworks for decision-making. Its ambition is to inform socio-economic policies, encourage responsible industrial and technological innovation, and contribute to more equitable and resilient societies. Luxembourg provides an ideal environment for this initiative, combining strong expertise in sustainability science and policy analysis. The DTU is a collaboration between researchers at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), the University of Luxembourg (UL) and the Urban Development and Mobility Department at the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER). The consortium also includes the National Statistics Office (STATEC). In this DTU, 12 scientists will train 12 PhD students over six years (from January 2027), each obtaining a PhD from UL’s doctoral schools. As part of the C-SOS Doctoral Training Unit, in this PhD you will integrate concepts from Post-Growth, Sufficiency and Doughnut Economics into the downscaling of planetary boundaries, leveraging good examples of application to territories and cities. Possible research questions include: how to couple ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system? How to define social foundation? How to allocate the carrying capacity based on social foundation?. You will be embedded in the SUSTAIN unit at LIST and enrolled as a doctoral candidate at the University of Luxembourg. You will work closely with a diverse cohort of 12 PhD researchers across the social, economic, and environmental sciences, contributing to a shared research agenda on how Luxembourg can thrive within its fair share of planetary limits You will be mainly in charge of: Conducting a systematic review and critical assessment of existing carrying capacity allocation and planetary boundary downscaling approaches, spanning economic and emission based allocation methods, sufficiency based approaches, and Doughnut Economics frameworks Developing a methodological framework for coupling ecological limits and social foundation as an interdependent system, integrating Post-Growth, Sufficiency, and Doughnut Economics concepts into the downscaling of planetary boundaries Applying the framework to Luxembourg and comparable small territories under a range of allocation scenarios, drawing on Green Deal technology targets, context specific Decent Living Standards, and provisioning systems, producing environmental ceiling estimates grounded in social foundation thresholds Building and maintaining a dynamic system model enabling the testing of individual and combined allocation approaches, valuing social outcome generation per unit of environmental impact across relevant planetary boundary dimensions Collaborating with other C-SOS doctoral researchers, in particular those working on social foundation, Quality of Life, and economic systems, to ensure that allocation approaches rest on socially realistic and empirically coherent definitions of social foundation Publishing results in peer reviewed journals and presenting at international conferences Contributing to C-SOS training activities, workshops, and stakeholder engagement events Is Your profile described below? Are you our future colleague? Apply now! Education Master's degree (or equivalent) in a quantitative discipline relevant to environmental sustainability, such as: industrial ecology, environmental engineering, environmental or ecological economics or computational social science Solid academic grounding in Planetary Boundaries, Doughnut Economics, Post Growth or degrowth literature Familiarity with Decent Living Standards and Quality of Life frameworks Experience and skills Proficiency in Python for building and maintaining modular research tools Experience with dynamic system modeling or willingness to develop this quickly Comfort with multiregional input output analysis or similar economy wide modeling approaches Statistical and data analysis skills for working with large environmental and social datasets Experience with prospective LCA or scenario-based sustainability modelling is an asset Intellectual curiosity and genuine interest in the intersection of environmental science, economics, and well-being economy Capacity to work both independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team Strong analytical and scientific writing skills Language skills Fluency in English, both oral and written. National and Greater Region languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) are an asset, other languages welcome. Your LIST benefits An organization with a passion for impact and strong RDI partnerships in Luxembourg and Europe that works on responsible and independent research projects Sustainable by design, empowering our belief that we play an essential role in paving the way to a green society Innovative infrastructures and exceptional labs occupying more than 5,000 square metres, including innovations in all that we do An environment encouraging curiosity, innovation and entrepreneurship in all areas Personalized learning programme to foster our staff’s soft and technical skills Multicultural and international work environment with more than 60 nationalities represented in our workforce Diverse and inclusive work environment empowering our people to fulfil their personal and professional ambitions Gender-friendly environment with multiple actions to attract, develop and retain women in science 32 days’ paid annual leave, 11 public holidays, 13-month salary, statutory health insurance Flexible working hours, home working policy (not remote) and access to Digital lunch vouchers Apply online Your application must include: A motivation letter oriented towards the position and detailing your experience A scientific CV with contact details List of publications, if applicable) Contact details of 2 references Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by email will not be considered. Application procedure and conditions We kindly request applicants to provide their nationality for statistical purposes only, as part of our commitment to promoting diversity and ensuring equal opportunities in our workforce. This information will be kept confidential and will not be used for any discriminatory purposes. LIST is dedicated to maintaining an inclusive work environment and is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to attracting, hiring, and retaining a diverse workforce. All applicants will be considered for employment without discrimination based on national origin, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, religion, age, or disability. Applications will be continuously reviewed until the position is filled. An assessment committee will thoroughly evaluate applications, adhering to guidelines designed to ensure equal opportunities. The primary criteria for selection will be the alignment of the applicant's existing skills and expertise with the requirements mentioned above. As part of our recruitment process, the selected candidate might be subject to a background check in accordance with applicable laws and institutional policies. For the purposes of the position and in accordance with applicable legislation, the successful candidate may be requested to provide a recent criminal record certificate. PhD additional information: Supervisor at LIST: Dr. Enrico Benetto Work location: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), Belvaux, Luxembourg PhD enrolment: University of Luxembourg, Belval, Luxembourg Please note that university enrolment fees, currently set at 400 EUR per semester (as of July 2025) must be covered by the successful applicant. Your master diploma must be recognized in Luxembourg. items.title: PhD in AI-Assisted Generative Design and Optimization of Compliant Mechanisms (F/M/D) 100%
items.desc: Facing the challenges of our time - Help us grow and be more impactful! Your mission Help create engineering tools that combine mechanics, computation and AI to make the design of complex optomechatronic systems faster, more rigorous and more reusable. CSEM and the Engineering Design and Computing Laboratory of ETH Zurich are seeking a doctoral researcher to investigate how AI and advanced computational methods can support the design of high-performance optomechatronic systems. The research will be anchored in compliant mechanisms, where performance emerges from tightly coupled geometry, material behaviour, actuation, sensing, manufacturing and verification constraints. The ambition is not to treat AI as a black box. You will develop scientifically grounded methods that combine physics-based models, simulation data and engineering knowledge, and make their predictions traceable, testable and useful to engineers. Research focus The project will build on the outcomes of Guilain Lang’s doctoral thesis, “CAM2S2: Compliant AM Mechanisms Systematic Synthesizer” [link to the online thesis], which established a systematic framework for translating requirements into compliant mechanism designs. The new research will critically assess and selectively reuse, adapt or extend the methods and tools developed in CAM2S2, without being constrained to retain the complete existing framework. From this foundation, it will develop and validate AI-assisted methods to derive engineering insight from requirements, explore broader solution spaces and generate reusable models for mechanism and optomechatronic system design. The exact thesis plan will be refined with the selected candidate and the supervisors. Expected research directions include: AI-assisted interpretation of requirements to identify critical design drivers, sensitive parameters, conflicts and uncertainty. Traceable use of scientific literature and CSEM engineering knowledge, including models, test results and lessons learned. Inverse and multi-objective design methods that connect required performance to geometry, material choices and manufacturing constraints. Extension of mechanism synthesis beyond a limited set of topologies, including variable cross-sections and alternative manufacturing routes. Physics-informed surrogate or reduced-order models for nonlinear stiffness, stress, buckling, parasitic motion and other key mechanism properties. Automated generation of design-of-experiment campaigns using finite element models and computational methods. Implementation and validation on representative compliant optomechatronic demonstrators. Your responsibilities Formulate focused research questions and establish robust benchmarks against existing analytical, numerical and engineering workflows. Develop computational models, algorithms and research software with reproducible data and version control practices. Design numerical experiments, critically assess model validity and quantify uncertainty. Work closely with specialists in mechanics, systems engineering, AI, manufacturing and testing at CSEM and ETH Zurich. Validate selected methods against higher-fidelity simulations and experimental evidence. Publish in leading peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences. Transfer useful methods into engineering tools and document them so that they can be understood, challenged and reused. Your profile Know-how Essential Master's degree in microtechnology or mechanical engineering, computational science and engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, robotics, or a closely related field. Strong foundation in computational mechanics and numerical modelling, including finite element analysis. Understanding of the architecture and development of multidisciplinary optomechatronic or mechatronic systems. Ability to develop and assess computational methods beyond routine use of commercial FEM software. Solid programming skills, preferably in Python and/or a compiled scientific-computing language. Rigorous scientific reasoning, independence, creativity and the ability to communicate clearly in written and spoken English. Strong assets Background in machine learning, artificial intelligence or data-driven modelling, with the ability to connect these methods to physical systems. Experience with surrogate modelling, optimisation, uncertainty quantification, reduced-order modelling, differentiable simulation or scientific machine learning. Knowledge of compliant mechanisms, nonlinear structural mechanics, mechanism synthesis or topology optimisation. Experience in design for additive manufacturing. DfAM is a major advantage, although the project will not be limited to DfAM. Experience with CAD, parametric modelling, experimental validation or the development of engineering software. What we offer A doctoral project at the intersection of fundamental methods and demanding real-world engineering applications. Joint supervision by CSEM and Prof. Kristina Shea's Engineering Design and Computing Laboratory at ETH Zurich. Access to CSEM expertise, engineering heritage, simulation and test capabilities in precision mechanisms and optomechatronic systems. A multidisciplinary and international environment with close interaction between researchers and engineers. The opportunity to publish scientific results while translating research into methods with direct engineering value. Attractive employment conditions and access to the ETH Zurich doctoral ecosystem, subject to the applicable admission and approval requirements. CSEM mission and values We believe in a future that is imagined, shared, and created TOGETHER. At CSEM, we don’t just innovate, we envision technologies that shape tomorrow. Since 1984, our purpose has remained constant: to harness science and technology for the benefit of society. Today, with over 650 people across Switzerland, we remain committed to our mission: to develop and transfer world-class solutions in digital technologies, precision manufacturing, and sustainable energy systems. In doing so, we empower Swiss industry to innovate and remain competitive. Our strength is the excellence of our people. We believe that strong values support the successful development of our organization as well as the harmonious and balanced development of all our employees. We are A unique place between research and industry at the cutting edge of new technologies An innovative, non-profit, and employee-driven company A dynamic, multidisciplinary, and multicultural environment A solar team focused on enabling solutions to energy challenges for a sustainable world Working@CSEM means Being part of a passionate community Flexibility, attractive working conditions, and opportunities of development Benefit from a management style based on trust & feedback Please submit: A concise motivation letter explaining why this research question fits your background and ambitions. Curriculum vitae, degree certificates and academic transcripts. A short description or link to one research, software or engineering project that best demonstrates your contribution. Contact details for at least two academic or professional referees. In your motivation letter, briefly describe how you would combine physics-based simulation and machine learning without losing traceability or engineering credibility. Applications will be evaluated on scientific potential, depth of fundamentals, evidence of independent problem solving and alignment with the interdisciplinary nature of the project. The position will be primarily based at CSEM in Neuchâtel. The doctoral researcher will also spend time at ETH Zurich, as required by the research activities and the collaboration with the Engineering Design and Computing Laboratory. The project will be conducted as an external doctoral thesis under ETH Zurich supervision, subject to formal university approval and admission. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity. We look forward to receiving your complete application file via (CV, cover letter, certificates & diplomas) our job page. Preference will be given to professionals applying directly.

items.title: Phd Position In Quantum Computing Technology At Ifae
items.desc: Open Position PhD position in Quantum Computing Technology at IFAE Opening Date: October 6, **** Closing Date: Until Filled Ref: IFAE*******_QCT_PhDStudent About IFAE The Institut de Física d'Altes Energies (IFAE) is a public consortium of the Generalitat de Catalunya, the Autonomous Government of Catalonia, and the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB, a public university) whose main objective is to carry out research and to contribute to the development of high energy physics from a theoretical, experimental and technological point of view. IFAE has the status of a "University Institute" attached to the UAB and its premises are within the campus of the University. About The Quantum Computing Technology Group In ****, IFAE started a new line on quantum computation with superconducting circuits, the Quantum Computing Technology group, to study the implications of this emerging technology in different areas of particle physics. The Quantum Computing Technology (QCT) group at IFAE hosts a complete laboratory to perform experiments controlling superconducting qubits, including dilution refrigerators, and instrumentation for microwave signal generation and acquisition. The group also has access to a metal evaporator exclusively used to produce superconducting quantum devices. The QCT group has already demonstrated coherent control of superconducting qubits and is developing its own program on coherent quantum annealing through the EuroQHPC-Integration program. In parallel, a line of operating qubits as detectors is being carried out within the Quantera project QRADES. In addition, the QCT group is a partner in the EU SUPREME consortium to realize the implementation of a European foundry of superconducting quantum devices. Required Skills And Evaluation Criteria The successful candidate will be expected to have: A Master's degree (or equivalent) in quantum physics. Prior experience with superconducting qubits, operation of dilution refrigerators, qubit-compatible control electronics (microwaves, fast pulsing, low noise signal processing), or device fabrication in cleanroom environments will be highly valued. A good level of English, with (optional but valued) international experience. The evaluation criteria and their weighting for the submitted applications will be the following: Background knowledge in physics and quantum physics, particularly in superconducting qubits 30 Background knowledge in qubit-compatible laboratory techniques, including software programming 30 Background knowledge in cleanroom and fabrication techniques 30 High level of English, internationalization 10 What will be your role? The candidate will join one of the teams at QCT group, and they will be trained in superconducting qubit device design and fabrication techniques, as well as laboratory methods in cryogenics, microwave engineering, signal processing and coding. Offered contract Employment contract for practical training (maximum 6 month) + Predoctoral Contract (4 years). The position will correspond to "Researcher Technician" in a 6-month contract, and Predoctoral Researcher (R1) in a 4-year contract within the professional categories of the IFAE. Full-time contract (40h/week). Salary: In accordance with the IFAE salary scales applicable to the position. The selected candidates are expected to join the IFAE as soon as possible. Work with exciting experimental science. Travelling to scientific singular infrastructures. Opportunity to gain experience learning first?hand. Personal growth, innovation, and learning every day. Equal Opportunity and Diversity IFAE is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity in the workplace and social integration of people with a disability. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates. People from groups that are typically underrepresented in the labour market in general and in Science and Engineering in particular, such as women, minorities, or people with a disability, are particularly encouraged to apply. A Selection Committee will evaluate the received applications. If more than one candidate seems equally suitable for the position, the Selection Committee will arrange an on?line interview with each one of them as part of the Selection process. In compliance with article 121 of the Spanish Public Sector Legal Regime Act, staff with a pre-existing relationship with the Consortium administration (Generalitat de Catalunya and Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona) will have priority in the awarding of the position. You may contact Pol Forn (******) for any questions related to this job opening.

items.title: CDD - Doctorant CIFRE (H/F/X) - Tribologie & Science des Matériaux : Durabilité des tribofilms vers une meilleure prédiction des performances des lubrifiants
items.desc: Contexte et environnement Rejoignez TotalEnergies et participez à un projet de recherche innovant mené en partenariat avec le Laboratoire de Tribologie et Dynamique des Systèmes (LTDS) de l'École Centrale de Lyon. Dans un contexte d'amélioration continue des performances énergétiques et environnementales, la compréhension des mécanismes de frottement et d'usure constitue un enjeu majeur pour le développement des futures générations de lubrifiants. En conditions sévères de lubrification, certains additifs contenus dans le lubrifiant réagissent avec les surfaces frottantes pour former un tribofilm permettant de contrôler le frottement et l'usure de l’interface. Cette thèse CIFRE a pour objectif d'identifier des descripteurs mécaniques, physico-chimiques et interfaciaux robustes permettant de relier les propriétés et la durabilité des tribofilms aux performances tribologiques observées. Les résultats contribueront à améliorer la discrimination des formulations et la prédictivité des méthodes d'évaluation des lubrifiants, afin d'accélérer le développement de formulations innovantes. Le doctorant évoluera au sein d'un environnement mêlant recherche académique et recherche industrielle, avec une présence répartie entre le Centre de Recherche de Solaize et le LTDS à Écully. Activités À ce titre, vos principales missions consistent à : Contribuer scientifiquement à la diminution de la consommation énergétique ; Définir et mettre en œuvre les protocoles expérimentaux nécessaires pour générer des tribofilms dans des conditions contrôlées ; Réaliser des essais tribologiques sur différentes formulations et différents matériaux ; Caractériser les surfaces, interfaces et tribofilms à l'aide de techniques avancées de caractérisation ; Exploiter, analyser et interpréter les résultats expérimentaux obtenus ; Étudier la robustesse, la variabilité et l'évolution des propriétés des tribofilms au cours des sollicitations tribologiques, afin de mieux comprendre les mécanismes qui gouvernent leur durabilité et les performances associées ; Développer des descripteurs robustes et exploitables permettant d'améliorer la discrimination des formulations et la prédiction des performances des lubrifiants ; Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de TotalEnergies et du LTDS ; Présenter l'avancement de vos travaux lors de réunions scientifiques et techniques ; Valoriser les résultats au travers de publications et de participations à des conférences nationales et internationales ; Rédiger et soutenir une thèse de doctorat à l'issue des travaux de recherche. Profil du candidat Titulaire ou prochainement diplômé d' un Master 2 ou d'un Diplôme d'Ingénieur en tribologie, science des matériaux, mécanique, physico-chimie ou dans un domaine lié aux surfaces et aux interfaces , vous souhaitez vous engager dans un projet de recherche appliquée au sein d'un environnement combinant excellence académique et recherche industrielle. Vous justifiez idéalement d' une première expérience en laboratoire de recherche ou en R&D (stage de fin d'études, projet de recherche, année de césure), au cours de laquelle vous avez réalisé des travaux expérimentaux et participé à l' analyse de résultats scientifiques . Vous avez : Une bonne connaissance de la science des matériaux et des phénomènes liés aux surfaces et interfaces ; Un intérêt marqué pour la tribologie, les phénomènes de frottement, d'usure et de lubrification ; Une expérience pratique des manipulations expérimentales en laboratoire ; Des compétences en analyse et traitement de données scientifiques ; Une bonne maîtrise de l'anglais scientifique, à l'écrit comme à l'oral ; Idéalement, une expérience en techniques de caractérisation des matériaux ou des surfaces (AFM, Raman, XPS, nanoindentation ou techniques similaires). Vous appréciez le travail expérimental et le travail en équipe. Vous êtes capable d'évoluer dans un environnement multidisciplinaire à l'interface entre mécanique, matériaux et physico-chimie et souhaitez contribuer à des travaux de recherche à fort impact industriel.

items.title: SD-26141 PhD STUDENT IN CONSUMPTION-BASED FOOT-PRINTING OF COMPETITIVENESS POLICIES
items.desc: Fixed term contract | Belvaux | 48 months Are you passionate about research? So are we! Come and join us The Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST) is a leading Research and Technology Organisation (RTO) that drives innovation for the economy and society in Luxembourg and beyond. With cutting-edge expertise in Natural, Built, Industrial environments, Space, AI, Security and defence technologies. LIST bridges scientific excellence and applied research to design solutions that address real-world challenges and create positive impact. The Environmental Sustainability Assessment and Circularity (SUSTAIN) Unit conducts cross‑disciplinary research to support the transition toward a more sustainable, resilient, and healthy society. SUSTAIN combines expertise in environmental sciences, circular economy, risk and safety assessment, and sustainable innovation to address complex challenges related to human and environmental health, climate change, and resource efficiency, developing knowledge, methods, and transferable software for the simulation and comprehensive sustainability assessment of socio-economic systems. Its purpose is to foster sustainable eco-innovation, through products and technologies, as well as support sustainability-oriented policy implementation and behavioural change to promote decarbonisation transitions. Do you want to know more about LIST? Check our website: https://www.list.lu/ How will you contribute? The world faces a convergence of crises that are transforming the conditions for human development. Climate instability, ecosystem degradation, and the overuse of natural resources have reached critical levels, while social inequality, political fragmentation, and technological disruption are reshaping societies. Traditional notions of economic competitiveness, centred on growth and productivity, are being redefined to include social resilience, inclusiveness, and ecological integrity. Responding to this “polycrisis” requires new pathways that reconcile prosperity with planetary and social limits. Luxembourg offers a particularly illustrative example of these tensions. The country enjoys one of the highest income levels globally and a dynamic financial and business environment that sustains its reputation for economic success. Yet this prosperity depends strongly on cross-border commuting, which creates mobility challenges and environmental stress. Escalating housing prices have made access to affordable living increasingly difficult, displacing a significant share of the workforce beyond national borders. The reliance on imported energy leaves households and firms vulnerable to external shocks. Although Luxembourg’s welfare model and social dialogue remain robust, they are under pressure from rising costs of living, widening inequalities, and growing demands on public services. Environmentally, Luxembourg’s footprint per inhabitant ranks among the largest worldwide, driven by high consumption and land-use pressures that push the country beyond sustainable limits. Meeting these intertwined challenges calls for coordinated transformations that bridge sectors, disciplines, and scales. Economic and social progress must be reframed within the concept of a Safe Operating Space—an area in which human well-being is achieved without breaching environmental boundaries. The objective is to steer innovation, governance, and everyday practices toward forms of competitiveness that are compatible with sustainability, rather than in conflict with it. The Doctoral Training Unit C-SOS (Competitiveness within a Safe Operating Space) is designed to cultivate researchers capable of analysing and fostering such transformations. It brings together an interdisciplinary consortium to train 12 PhD candidates in the assessment and design of inclusive and sustainable development trajectories. The programme equips them with conceptual and methodological tools to connect environmental sustainability, social well-being, and economic dynamics into integrated frameworks for decision-making. Its ambition is to inform socio-economic policies, encourage responsible industrial and technological innovation, and contribute to more equitable and resilient societies. Luxembourg provides an ideal environment for this initiative, combining strong expertise in sustainability science and policy analysis. The DTU is a collaboration between researchers at the Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), the University of Luxembourg (UL) and the Urban Development and Mobility Department at the Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research (LISER). The consortium also includes the National Statistics Office (STATEC). In this DTU, 12 scientists will train 12 PhD students over six years (from January 2027), each obtaining a PhD from UL’s doctoral schools. As part of the C-SOS Doctoral Training Unit, in this PhD you will develop a quantitative policy toolbox that estimates, across multiple planetary boundary dimensions (e.g. climate change, water and land use, biodiversity), what a given policy measure actually delivers — individually and in combination — for Luxembourg and the Greater Region. You will be embedded in the SUSTAIN unit at LIST and enrolled as a doctoral candidate at the University of Luxembourg. You will work closely with a diverse cohort of 12 PhD researchers across the social, economic, and environmental sciences, contributing to a shared research agenda on how Luxembourg can thrive within its fair share of planetary limits You will be mainly in charge of: Conducting a systematic review and critical assessment of existing multiregional input-output (MRIO) analysis based projection methods and demand-side modelling approaches (taxation/subsidies, bans, income elasticities, rebound effects) Developing a methodological framework for the prospective quantification of environmental impacts of policy scenarios, integrating input-output analysis, scenario modelling, and micro-economic methods Applying the framework to Luxembourg and the Greater Region under a range of beyond-growth and climate policy scenarios (e.g. carbon fee-and-dividend schemes, ICE phase-out, 4-day workweek, housing construction codes, mobility subsidies), producing quantitative footprint estimates at territorial scale Building and maintaining an open, modular, Python-based policy toolbox enabling the testing of individual and combined policy measures and their environmental outcomes across all relevant planetary boundary dimensions Collaborating with other C-SOS doctoral researchers — in particular those working on social foundation and economic systems — to ensure that policy scenarios are grounded in socially realistic and economically coherent assumptions Publishing results in peer-reviewed journals and presenting at international conferences Contributing to C-SOS training activities, workshops, and stakeholder engagement events Is Your profile described below? Are you our future colleague? Apply now! Education Master's degree (or equivalent) in a quantitative discipline relevant to environmental sustainability, such as: industrial ecology, environmental engineering, environmental or ecological economics, data science applied to sustainability, or computational social science Solid academic grounding in at least one of the following: life cycle assessment, input-output economics, environmental accounting, or integrated assessment modelling Experience and skills Strong Python programming skills are essential; experience with data science workflows, large dataset handling, and reproducible research practices (e.g. version control with Git) is highly valued Multiregional input-output (MRIO) analysis and knowledge of environmentally-extended input-output (EEIO) models are required; familiarity with EXIOBASE or FIGARO is an asset Experience with prospective LCA or scenario-based sustainability modelling is an asset Ability to translate complex policy questions into quantitative modelling frameworks — bridging the gap between policy intent and measurable environmental outcomes Intellectual curiosity and genuine interest in the intersection of environmental science, economics, and public policy Capacity to work both independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary team Strong analytical and scientific writing skills Language skills Fluency in English, both oral and written. National and Greater Region languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) are an asset, other languages welcome Your LIST benefits An organization with a passion for impact and strong RDI partnerships in Luxembourg and Europe that works on responsible and independent research projects Sustainable by design, empowering our belief that we play an essential role in paving the way to a green society Innovative infrastructures and exceptional labs occupying more than 5,000 square metres, including innovations in all that we do An environment encouraging curiosity, innovation and entrepreneurship in all areas Personalized learning programme to foster our staff’s soft and technical skills Multicultural and international work environment with more than 60 nationalities represented in our workforce Diverse and inclusive work environment empowering our people to fulfil their personal and professional ambitions Gender-friendly environment with multiple actions to attract, develop and retain women in science 32 days’ paid annual leave, 11 public holidays, 13-month salary, statutory health insurance Flexible working hours, home working policy (not remote) and access to Digital lunch vouchers Apply online Your application must include: A motivation letter oriented towards the position and detailing your experience A scientific CV with contact details List of publications, if applicable) Contact details of 2 references Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by email will not be considered. Application procedure and conditions We kindly request applicants to provide their nationality for statistical purposes only, as part of our commitment to promoting diversity and ensuring equal opportunities in our workforce. This information will be kept confidential and will not be used for any discriminatory purposes. LIST is dedicated to maintaining an inclusive work environment and is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to attracting, hiring, and retaining a diverse workforce. All applicants will be considered for employment without discrimination based on national origin, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, religion, age, or disability. Applications will be continuously reviewed until the position is filled. An assessment committee will thoroughly evaluate applications, adhering to guidelines designed to ensure equal opportunities. The primary criteria for selection will be the alignment of the applicant's existing skills and expertise with the requirements mentioned above. As part of our recruitment process, the selected candidate might be subject to a background check in accordance with applicable laws and institutional policies. PhD additional information: Supervisor at LIST: Dr. Thomas Gibon Work location: Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology (LIST), Belvaux, Luxembourg PhD enrolment: University of Luxembourg, Belval, Luxembourg Please note that university enrolment fees, currently set at 400 EUR per semester (as of July 2025) must be covered by the successful applicant. Your master diploma must be recognized in Luxembourg. Please refer to: https://www.uni.lu/en/admissions/diploma-recognition/ and https://guichet.public.lu/fr/citoyens/enseignement-formation/etudes-superieures/reconnaissance-diplomes.html Hired PhD candidates must self-register at the university of Luxembourg and cover all associated fees. A B2 English certificate is mandatory; see University of Luxembourg's accepted certificates list, IELTS or TOEFL, unless your Master degree was fully tau

items.title: PhD Student (m/f/d) |Community ecology, stone tool use and social behavior in gracile capuchin monkeys
items.desc: Young Researchers Radolfzell / Konstanz Developmental and Evolutionary Biology & Genetics Behavioral Sciences Microbiology & Ecology Job Offer from October 23, 2026 The Max Planck Institut of Animal Behavior at its sites in Konstanz and Radolfzell offers an international, interdisciplinary, and collaborative enviroment that opens up unique research opportunities. The goal of our basic research is to develop a quantitative and predictive understanding of the decisions and movements of animals in their natural environment. The Ecology of Animal Societies at the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior would like to fill PhD Student (m/f/d) 100 % - Community ecology, stone tool use and social behavior in gracile capuchin monkeys with a flexible starting date in summer / autumn 2027 . This position is fully funded for a period of 4 years. The workplace will be in Konstanz, Germany. Our Group The Inheritance and Social Learning across Scales (ISLaS) group investigates how extragenetic modes of inheritance– namely cultural transmission via social learning and the ecological inheritance of home ranges and territories— affect and are affected by social behavior, ecology, and genetic evolution. We aim to integrate quantitative theory with reproducible Bayesian statistical modeling grounded in an appreciation for natural history. Our work integrates theory and tools from cultural evolution, animal behavior, population biology, spatial ecology, and the quantitative social sciences. We are based out of Konstanz, Germany, but our group does field research in Panama, Costa Rica, Colombia, Mozambique, and California. Our current group has projects focused on the adaptive significance of tool use, parasitology, social behavior and ecology in capuchin monkeys, methods development in social network analysis, and computer vision tools for studying longitudinal behavior and population demography using camera traps. We prioritize theoretical and methodological rigor and embracing uncertainty over prestige, and are sympatheticto many social and methodological calls for science reform (i.e. reproducible, open science and in-country field-partnerships and collaboration). Project Details We will hire one student for one of two possible projects: [A] Community Ecology of Stone Tool Use in Gracile Capuchins This project will focus on combining field experimentation and data collection, analyzing existing data, and analytical or agent-based modeling to tackle varying questions related to stone tool use by white-faced capuchin monkeys (Cebus imitator) living in the archipelago of Coiba National Park, Panama. Most of these groups are unhabituated and highly terrestrial, so camera trapping is central to our research. Field work may consist of a few 2 week trips or longer multi-month stays in Panama depending on the nature of the project. Linking Tool-Use Behavior to Below-ground Ecological Processes Promises and Pitfalls of Capuchin Tool-use to Heterospeciﬁcs The Metapopulation Ecology of Stone Tool Sites [B] Multi-site comparisons of the social behavior, ecology, and/or movement of gracile capuchin monkeys (genus Cebus) This project is opened up to a motivated and independent PhD student with systems expertise in Cebus trying to answer broad scale questions about the social behavior, population demography, community ecology, movement ecology or any other aspect of Cebus behavior, evolution, and ecology. A desire to develop indirect approaches to measure these biological or environmental traits (camera trapping, remote sensing, biological samples) is a plus. Potential students may work within our study systems in Panama, or foster collaboration between long-term studies where they have previous research experience and support from senior collaborators. The project should dovetail with long-term research goals of our group and yield within group collaborations. Qualifications REQUIRED: Applicants are required to have a Masters degree in any scientific discipline including biology, ecology, anthropology, archaeology, or the quantitative sciences and have some previous field research experience. DESIRED: The candidate should be enthusiastic about integrating observational and/or experimental field collected data with quantitative approaches in Bayesian data analysis, causal inference, or theoretical modelling. Broad thinking and a desire to link fields and questions across disciplines is a plus. Previous field research experience in remote environments, the desire to conduct field research in the tropical Americas, and the ability to work and communicate in a cross-cultural context is highly desirable. Prior experience with programming (e.g. in R, Python, Julia, Mathematica, NetLogo, etc.) and an enthusiasm for tackling challenging problems is also highly desirable.Researchers with systems expertise, who feel they may be lacking in quantitative skills are encouraged to apply as well if they are willing to put in considerable effort to develop them with the group’s guidance. The student will be expected to proactively co-develop and implement research ideas to move the project forward, thus a high degree of independence, and ability to know when to ask for help if needed, is crucial. The working language of the group is English, the ability to speak Spanish is desirable, and German language skills are not a requirement. Applicants who are shortlisted for interviews are strongly encouraged to talk to current lab members and alumni to feel out if a PhD position in the group is a mutually beneficial fit. Our Offer The student will join the Inheritance and Social Learning across Scales (ISLaS) research group led by Dr. Brendan Barrett (he/him) and integrated within the Department for the Ecology of Animal Societies. They will work closely with a team of collaborators both within the department, outside of the department and at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute in Panama. The University of Konstanz and the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior together form a thriving research community representing a global hotspot for behavioral ecology, collective behavior, and animal movement research, including the Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behavior. The student will join the International Max Planck Research School for Quantitative Behaviour, Ecology and Evolution from lab to field (IMPRS-QBEE), a cooperative doctoral program between the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior and the University of Konstanz. The successful candidate will join a supportive, international, and interdisciplinary research team, with access to strong academic and career mentorship, the ability to participate in coursework and conferences, and opportunities for growth as both a computational and field biologist. The position is fully funded for 4 years (TVöD salary scale E-13, 65%). The Max Planck Society endeavors to employ more severely disabled people. Applications of severely disabled persons are expressly welcome. The Max Planck Society strives for gender and diversity equality. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. How to apply Are you interested? Then we are looking forward to receiving your application by December 1, 2026 through IMPRS Online portal. Please Include The Following Application Materials Curriculum vitae (CV) Contact information for 2 references Letter of motivation Research Statement (2 pages, excluding references) Research interests: Describe your main research interests, how they developed, and how they relate to the research we do in our group. (½ page) Research proposal: Spend some time exploring our groups prior publications or relevant literature. Then, choose one of the potential project directions listed above (A or B) and describe 1-2 specific biological questions you would like to ask or hypotheses you would like to test within the scope of the project. Explain the theoretical framework and/or analytical approach(es) you would use to address your question(s). Include a mock figure (can be hand drawn) of what your results might look like, and an interpretation of your potential findings (1-2 pages). ( NOTE: this section is an opportunity for you to develop your ideas and demonstrate how you would address scientific questions with quantitative approaches. It is not meant as a full-fledged PhD proposal, and you will not be expected to carry out the exact project you propose should you join our team!) Code example: If possible please provide an example of some code you have written, with a brief explanation of what it does (you can also link to publicly-accessible repository). The code does not have to relate to animal behavior, but it should be written by you and be something you can explain to others if needed. AI Declaration: For transparency (and not penalization), indicate if you used AI in drafting your application, and if so describe briefly how you used it. Academic transcripts for your BSc and MSc degrees. Transcripts can be unofficial at this stage – official records will be required before acceptance. Questions about this position should be addressed to Dr. Brendan Barrett (bbarrett@ab.mpg.de).

items.title: PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys
items.desc: Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon The Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon conducts cutting-edge international research for a changing world: Around 1,000 employees contribute to the tackling of climate change, the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range. Institute of Material and Process Design The Institute of Material and Process Design is dedicated to the sustainable and ecological development of innovative materials and manufacturing processes, especially for the transportation sector and medical technology. To this end, materials are tailored and manufacturing processes are designed to conserve resources – from the modeling of material behavior to the development of the material to the finished component. PhD position on Physics-Guided Digital Twin Development for Composition-Process-Structure-Property Modeling of Magnesium Alloys Reference code: 1057 - 2026/WD 1 Commencement date: as soon as possible Work location: Geesthacht Application deadline: November 12th, 2026 The Institute of Material and Process Design at the Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon is offering a 4-year PhD position in the field of computational materials engineering, machine learning, and digital twins for advanced lightweight materials. The focus of the PhD project will be the development of a physics-guided digital twin framework for magnesium alloys by integrating experimental characterization, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, precipitation modeling, and machine learning approaches to establish quantitative composition-process-structure-property relationships. Building upon recently developed machine-learning approaches for structure-property prediction in extruded magnesium alloys, the project aims to advance toward a next-generation Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) framework capable of predicting microstructure evolution and resulting mechanical properties across previously unseen processing conditions and material states. The candidate will work closely with interdisciplinary teams combining expertise in magnesium alloy development, thermomechanical processing, crystal plasticity, phase-field modeling, machine learning, and advanced experimental characterization. The objective of the project is to bridge the gap between purely data-driven materials modeling and mechanistic microstructure simulations by combining crystal plasticity, dynamic recrystallization, precipitation kinetics, and machine learning into a unified digital-twin framework. The resulting methodologies shall enable accelerated alloy and process design by leveraging experimentally validated physics-guided surrogate models with improved extrapolation capabilities beyond the limits of conventional machine-learning approaches. This work directly contributes to the digital transformation of materials development and manufacturing technologies for future lightweight engineering applications. Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. Aufgaben development of physics-guided machine-learning models for composition-process-structure-property relationships in magnesium alloys combination of crystal plasticity, phase-field, items.title: Wissenschaftliche:r Mitarbeiter:in / Doktorand:in für Natural Language Processing (NLP) und kausale KI (m/w/d)
items.desc: Die Technische Informationsbibliothek (TIB) ist eine Stiftung öffentlichen Rechts des Landes Niedersachsen. Mit rund 600 Beschäftigten und einem Etat von circa 60 Millionen Euro ist sie eine der größten Informationsinfrastruktureinrichtungen in Deutschland. Als Deutsche Zentrale Fachbibliothek für Technik und Naturwissenschaften sichern wir mit unseren zukunftsweisenden Dienstleistungen die infrastrukturellen Voraussetzungen einer qualitativ hochwertigen Informations- und Literaturversorgung für Forschung in Wissenschaft und Industrie. Mit dem Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG) arbeiten wir daran, den Austausch und die Nutzung wissenschaftlicher Erkenntnisse im digitalen Zeitalter zu revolutionieren. Die TIB, Programmbereich D, Open Research Knowledge Graph, sucht für die Forschungsgruppe Data Science & Digital Libraries (Prof. Dr. Sören Auer) zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt eine:n Wissenschaftliche:n Mitarbeiter:in / Doktorand:in für Natural Language Processing (NLP) und kausale KI (m/w/d) Die Stelle ist für die Dauer der Projektlaufzeit von drei Jahren befristet. Die Einstellung erfolgt vorbehaltlich der finalen Bewilligung der Mittel durch den Drittmittelgeber Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Die regelmäßige Wochenarbeitszeit beträgt 39,80 Stunden (Vollzeit). Der Arbeitsplatz ist grundsätzlich für Teilzeitbeschäftigung geeignet. Mobiles Arbeiten ist unter Berücksichtigung dienstlicher Erfordernisse in begrenztem Umfang möglich. Die Eingruppierung erfolgt in die Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. Aufgaben Die Stelle ist Teil des Projekts EcoAIRE - AI-assisted hypothesis assessment in invasion biology and the restoration of freshwater ecosystems under fragmented and heterogeneous ecological evidence im Förderprogramm Leibniz-Kooperative Exzellenz. Das Projekt verbindet die Expertise der TIB in der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache und der wissenschaftlichen Wissensrepräsentation mit der ökologischen Expertise des Leibniz-Instituts für Gewässerökologie und Binnenfischerei (IGB) sowie der Expertise des Deutschen Forschungszentrums für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) in der kausalen Modellierung. An der TIB liegt Ihr Forschungsschwerpunkt auf der Verarbeitung natürlicher Sprache zur Extraktion wissenschaftlicher und kausaler Informationen. Sie entwickeln Methoden, die wissenschaftliche Evidenz in strukturierte, maschinenverarbeitbare Repräsentationen von Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Unsicherheiten und kausalen Zusammenhängen überführen. Dabei geht Ihre Forschung über die Extraktion einzelner Fakten hinaus: Sie modellieren, wie wissenschaftliche Befunde zusammenhängen und unter welchen Bedingungen wissenschaftliche Aussagen gelten. Darauf aufbauend erforschen Sie kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern. Dazu gehören Simulationen, interventionsbasierte Schlussfolgerungsverfahren und die Bewertung von Hypothesen unter veränderten Bedingungen. Ihre Tätigkeit umfasst Sie entwickeln ein multimodales Rahmenwerk, das heterogene wissenschaftliche Wissensquellen - darunter Publikationen, Bilder, ergänzende Informationen, Datensätze und weitere Forschungsartefakte - in strukturierte Repräsentationen zur Hypothesenbewertung integriert und dabei die Herkunft der Informationen nachvollziehbar berücksichtigt. Sie entwickeln sprachmodellbasierte und agentenbasierte Methoden, um Hypothesen, Variablen, Kontextinformationen, Evidenz, Unsicherheiten sowie kausale oder mechanistische Zusammenhänge quellenübergreifend zu extrahieren, zu vereinheitlichen, aufeinander abzustimmen und zusammenzuführen. Sie erforschen kausale und von Weltmodellen inspirierte Ansätze für wissenschaftliches Schlussfolgern, um Interventionen zu simulieren und zu untersuchen, inwieweit sich Hypothesen auf veränderte Bedingungen übertragen lassen. Sie entwickeln Evaluationsrahmenwerke, die unterschiedliche Qualitätsaspekte der KI-gestützten Hypothesenbewertung erfassen. Dazu gehören Verfahren auf Grundlage fachlicher Expertenbewertungen sowie Ansätze, bei denen große Sprachmodelle als Bewertungsinstanz eingesetzt werden („LLM-as-a-judge“). Sie veröffentlichen Ihre Forschungsergebnisse auf Konferenzen und in Fachzeitschriften mit Peer-Review-Verfahren in den Bereichen NLP, Semantic Web, künstliche Intelligenz und maschinelles Lernen. Zudem wirken Sie an Projektberichten und der Verbreitung der Forschungsergebnisse mit. Profil Abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Master oder gleichwertiger Abschluss) in Informatik oder einem eng verwandten Fachgebiet, beispielsweise Künstliche Intelligenz (Artificial Intelligence), maschinelle Sprachverarbeitung (Natural Language Processing), maschinelles Lernen (Machine Learning), Data Science oder Computerlinguistik. Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Forschung oder Softwareentwicklung mit Python sowie praktische Kenntnisse moderner Methoden der Softwareentwicklung, beispielsweise Git-basierter Zusammenarbeit, automatisierter Tests und reproduzierbarer Experimente. Nachweisbare praktische Erfahrung mit transformerbasierten Modellen und großen Sprachmodellen, einschließlich der Nutzung von Frameworks wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers oder vergleichbaren Technologien für NLP-Anwendungen. Praktische Erfahrung in der Entwicklung agentenbasierter KI-Workflows oder von Multiagenten-KI-Workflows, einschließlich Werkzeugnutzung, strukturierter Ausgaben, Orchestrierung oder iterativer Verarbeitungspipelines für Schlussfolgerungen. Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens dem Niveau C1 für die wissenschaftliche Kommunikation, Zusammenarbeit und Publikationstätigkeit. Wünschenswerte Qualifikationen Erfahrung mit der Feinabstimmung oder Anpassung großer Sprachmodelle und/oder dem Aufbau fortgeschrittener RAG-Pipelines unter Verwendung von Technologien wie PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Sentence Transformers, LangChain, LlamaIndex, FAISS, Qdrant oder vergleichbaren Werkzeugen. Dazu zählen embeddingbasierte Informationssuche, Reranking, Vektorsuche und strukturierte Generierung. Kenntnisse der kausalen Modellierung und kausalen Inferenz, beispielsweise kausaler Graphen, struktureller Kausalmodelle oder interventionsbasierter Schlussfolgerungsverfahren. Erfahrung mit Semantic-Web-Technologien. Fachkenntnisse in der Ökologie, insbesondere der Süßwasserökologie, Invasionsbiologie oder Renaturierungsökologie, oder Erfahrung in der Mitarbeit an interdisziplinären wissenschaftlichen Projekten. Wir bieten Unser Ziel ist es, die Bereitstellung und Nutzung von Forschungsdaten und -informationen immer wieder neu zu überdenken und zu innovieren. Wir bieten ein intellektuell inspirierendes Umfeld mit unternehmerischer Denkweise, eingebettet in eine führende technische Universität und eines der größten Informationszentren der Leibniz-Gemeinschaft. Mit dem Forschungszentrum L3S der Leibniz Universität Hannover, eines der weltweit führenden Forschungsinstitute im Bereich Web & Data Science, besteht dabei im Rahmen des Leibniz Joint Lab Data Science & Open Knowledge eine enge Kooperation. Nicht zuletzt legen wir Wert auf ein offenes und kreatives Arbeitsklima, in dem es Spaß macht zu arbeiten. Darüber hinaus bieten wir einen gemeinwohlorientierten Arbeitsplatz im öffentlichen Dienst auf der Grundlage des TV-L mit einer Vergütung nach der Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L. eine Sonderzahlung zum Jahresende sowie 30 Tage Urlaub im Jahr bei einer Fünf-Tage-Woche sowie zusätzliche freie Tage an Heiligabend (24.12.) und Silvester (31.12.). einen flexiblen Arbeitsplatz in Zeit und Raum mit Angeboten zur Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Familie wie u. a. mobiles Arbeiten und flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodellen (Gleitzeit). einen modernen Arbeitsplatz in zentraler Lage von Hannover mit einem kollegialen, attraktiven und vielseitigen Arbeitsumfeld. einen Arbeitgeber mit breit gefächertem Fort- und Weiterbildungsangebot, einer betrieblichen Gesundheitsförderung und Altersvorsorge für den öffentlichen Dienst (VBL). Beschäftigtenrabatt in den Mensen des Studentenwerks Hannover sowie vergünstigte Möglichkeit zur Nutzung der vielseitigen Angebote des Hochschulsports Hannover. eigenverantwortliche und zukunftsorientierte Tätigkeiten, die Abwechslung bieten und Raum für persönliche Entwicklung lassen. die Finanzierung der erforderlichen Ausstattung sowie von Reisen zu Konferenzen und Forschungsaufenthalten. die Mitarbeit in einem nationalen Forschungs- und Innovationsprojekt. ein breites Spektrum an Forschungsinfrastrukturen und Technologiekomponenten, auf denen Sie aufbauen können. Dazu gehören TIB AIssistant, der Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG), ORKG Ask sowie Forschungssoftware aus dem SciKnowOrg-Ökosystem. Important note Please be advised that a valid work permit for Germany is required for non-EU citizens. Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered. LNKD1_DE

Full Time Edinburgh Posted 4 days ago Website CDT in Machine Learning Systems, University of Edinburgh About The CDT Machine Learning has a dramatic impact on our daily lives built on the back of improved computer systems. Systems research and ML research are symbiotic. Modern systems research targets the ubiquitous need for efficient ML. ML research, conversely, is directly affected by how methods will be deployed. Furthermore, systems research increasingly explores ML methods to improve systems, and ML research develops such methods. Major gains are made when the development of ML and systems are symbiotic and co-optimized. This is relevant across a broad spectrum of industries: in-car systems, medical devices, phones, sensor networks, condition monitoring systems, high-performance compute, and high-frequency trading. This CDT develops researchers with expertise across the systems-ML stack. This makes a cohort-based programme vital, treating ML Systems as a holistic discipline. Cohort interaction, and integration, give students real experience across multiple systems, approaches and methodologies. Company engagement is an integral part of the programme with built-in internships alongside entrepreneurship training. The PhD programme in Machine Learning Systems positions students for strong, ethically aware technical careers, developing the next generation of leaders. Students will develop foundational research skills in Computer Systems, Machine Learning, Hardware, Sensors and Control, Programming and Integrated Machine Learning Environments, AI Ethics, and Leadership and Entrepreneurship. At the end, all students will have extensive experience of real-world deployment and optimization of machine learning methods. Candidate’s profile An Ideal Candidate Would Typically Have a strong degree or higher qualification in a relevant field (e.g. computer science, mathematics, engineering, physical sciences, economics or any other field where evidence is provided of sufficient computing and mathematical background) solid experience of programming, machine learning methods and ideally deep learning environments (e.g. pytorch) or a computer systems background CDT studentships The CDT has a minimum of 10 fully-funded studentships available for September 2027 entry. Studentships include stipend, fees and research costs for 4 years. Home students will receive an enhanced stipend thanks to the Government TechFirst Scheme, in return of some additional requirements around widening participation and wider engagement with the TechFirst programme. As a UKRI-funded CDT, application is open to all UK/EU/non-EU citizens providing they meet the University PhD entry requirements. However, the number of students with international fees status that can be recruited is restricted (about 3 per year). An indication of the fees status categories, entry requirements and further details on eligibility criteria can be found on our website. Why Edinburgh? The University of Edinburgh is one of the best research-intense Universities in the world. The School of Informatics that hosts the CDT is consistently ranked among the world’s top 30 computer science departments. In 2026 QS World University Ranking by Subject, it is ranked 22nd for Computer Science and Information System, and 30th for Data Science and AI. The CDT students will be hosted in the state-of-the-art Informatics Forum in the heart of Scotland’s capital, consistently considered one of the most desirable places to live in the world. How To Apply The deadline for first-stage applications is 14th December 2026, 23:59. We accept applications from Home applicants until 15th March 2027, pending studentships availability.
