items.desc: Das Institut für Medizinische Informatik und Biometrie (IMB) ist Teil der Medizinischen Fakultät Carl Gustav Carus der Technischen Universität Dresden. Die Forschungsschwerpunkte des Instituts liegen in den Bereichen medizinische Biometrie, Bioinformatik, Systembiologie/-medizin inklusive der mathematischen Modellierung sowie in der medizinischen Informatik. Neben diesen wissenschaftlichen Tätigkeitsfeldern bietet das IMB verschiedene Dienstleistungen (z. B. Beratungs- und Weiterbildungsangebote im Bereich der medizinischen Datenwissenschaften) für Mitarbeitende und Studierende der Medizinischen Fakultät und des Universitätsklinikums Dresden an. Die Stelle ist Teil des von der Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG) geförderten interdisziplinären Forschungsprojekts „Virtuelle Nische: Computer-gestützte Modellierung und Simulation der zeitlichen-räumlich Dynamik hämatopoetischer Stammzellen in ihrer lokalen Mikroumgebung“. Kernziel des Projektes ist die Entwicklung und Anwendung eines mathematischen Modells, das die zeitlich‑räumliche Organisation hämatopoetischer Stamm‑ und Vorläuferzellen in ihrer lokalen Wachstumsumgebung im Knochenmark beschreibt. Das angestrebte verbesserte Verständnis der zugrundeliegenden Prozesse ist sowohl für offene grundlagenwissenschaftliche Fragestellungen der Stammzellbiologie als auch für zukünftige medizinische Anwendungen von zentraler Bedeutung. Aufgaben Entwicklung mathematischer Modelle zur Beschreibung zellulärer Dynamiken Implementierung der Modelle in einer geeigneten Programmierumgebung Simulation zellulärer Dynamiken innerhalb komplexer 3D-Strukturen Anwendung des Computermodells als virtuelle Brücke zwischen in vitro- und in vivo-Studien Systemische Analyse und Interpretation experimenteller Daten im Kontext komplexer biologischer Interaktionen Enge interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit mit experimentell arbeitenden Teams an der TU Dresden und kooperierenden Laboren im europäischen Ausland Profil abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (M.Sc., Diplom oder Vergleichbares) im Fach Mathematik, Physik, Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften (mit biologischem/technologischem Schwerpunkt) oder einer verwandten Disziplin sehr gute oder exzellente Studienleistungen ausgeprägtes Interesse an interdisziplinären Aufgaben, speziell an der Anwendung mathematischer/informatischer Methoden in der Biologie/Medizin solide Programmiererfahrung (z. Wir Suchen In der Fakultät III - Wirtschaftswissenschaften, Wirtschaftsinformatik und Wirtschaftsrecht -, Nachwuchsgruppe ENACT - Exploring New Assemblies of Communities & Smart Technologies in Urban Spaces, suchen wir zum 01.04.2027 eine/n wissenschaftliche/n Mitarbeiter/in zu folgenden Konditionen: 100 % = 39,83 Stunden Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L Befristung: zunächst 3 Jahre; eine Verlängerung um weitere 18 Monate ist möglich Die von Dr. Judith Dörrenbächer geleitete fünfjährige Nachwuchsgruppe ENACT untersucht, wie smarte und autonome Technologien soziale Begegnungen im öffentlichen Raum unterstützen können. Sie verbindet Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), Design Research und künstlerische Forschung mit spekulativen und performativen Ansätzen. Sie arbeitet eng mit dem Forum Freies Theater (FFT) Düsseldorf und internationalen Künstler:innen zusammen. Ihre Aufgaben Entwicklung und Durchführung eines eigenständigen Promotionsprojekts im Bereich Research through Design mit Schwerpunkt auf Speculative Design und sozialer Interaktion im urbanen Raum Zusammenarbeit mit Künstler:innen im Artist-in-Residence-Programm am FFT Düsseldorf und Verbindung von Design Research und künstlerischer Forschung Konzeption und Durchführung spekulativer, partizipativer und performativer Forschungs- und Gestaltungsformate Qualitative und gestaltungsorientierte Erforschung sozialer Begegnungen im urbanen Raum Planung, Durchführung und Auswertung empirischer Studien Veröffentlichung und Präsentation der Forschungsergebnisse in internationalen wissenschaftlichen Kontexten Mitarbeit an gemeinsamen Aktivitäten der Nachwuchsgruppe und am Transfer in Öffentlichkeit und Praxis Ihr Profil: Sehr guter wissenschaftlicher Hochschulabschluss (Master oder vergleichbar) in Human-Computer Interaction, Interaction Design, Design, Design Research oder einem verwandten Fach Interesse an sozialen Interaktionen, urbanen Räumen und zukünftigen Technologien Kenntnisse und/oder praktische Erfahrungen mit qualitativen, partizipativen oder gestaltungsorientierten Forschungsmethoden Interesse an Speculative Design, Design Fiction und/oder performativen Designmethoden Interesse an der Zusammenarbeit mit Künstler:innen und Praxispartner:innen in einem transdisziplinären Forschungsumfeld Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Gute Deutschkentnisse sind von Vorteil Selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise sowie ausgeprägte Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeit Erfahrungen im wissenschaftlichen Schreiben und/oder wissenschaftliche Publikationen sind von Vorteil Unser Angebot: Förderung der eigenen wissenschaftlichen oder künstlerischen Qualifizierung nach dem Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz (z.B. items.title: Doktorand*in für Promotion Prozessentwicklung Kunststofftechnik E-Motor
items.desc: Life is always about becoming… Im Leben geht es darum, sich auf eine Reise zu begeben, um die beste Version unseres zukünftigen Selbst zu werden. Während wir Neues entdecken, stellen wir uns Herausforderungen, meistern sie und wachsen über uns hinaus. Bewerben Sie sich bei Mercedes-Benz und finden Sie den Aufgabenbereich, in dem Sie Ihre Talente individuell entfalten können. Dabei werden Sie von visionären Kolleginnen und Kollegen unterstützt, die Ihren Pioniergeist teilen. Bei uns einzusteigen bedeutet, Teil eines globalen Teams zu werden, dessen Ziel es ist, die begehrenswertesten Automobile der Welt zu bauen. Together for excellence. Stellennummer: MER00049OI Aufgaben Du hast ein ingenieur- oder naturwissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium abgeschlossen und möchtest kunststofftechnische Verarbeitungsverfahren für automobile Elektroantriebe weiterentwickeln? Du arbeitest gerne an der Schnittstelle zwischen Vorentwicklung, Produktion, Werkstofftechnik und Qualität? Dann erwartet Dich ein Promotionsvorhaben zu kunststofftechnischen Fertigungsprozessen für den Stator eines Elektromotors. Wir vom Team der Prozessentwicklung für elektrische Antriebe sind Teil des Planungs- und Produktionstechnologiezentrums für den Antriebsstrang am Standort Untertürkheim. Wir stellen in Zusammenarbeit mit den anderen Teams die neuesten und innovativsten Technologien im Produktionsumfeld zur Verfügung und sichern den Reifegrad bis zur Serieneinführung ab. In unserem Team werden neben vielen fertigungstechnischen und messtechnischen, auch weiterführende Fragestellungen aus dem Entwicklungs- und Qualitätsbereich bearbeitet. Zudem entwickeln wir innovative Fertigungsverfahren und Prozesse für hochwertige Powertrain-Anwendungen. Im Rahmen eines Technologieprojektes für zukünftige Antriebssysteme suchen wir eine*n Doktorand*in mit dem Fokus der Weiterentwicklung von Fertigungstechnologien in der Kunststofftechnik. Deine Aufgaben umfassen unter anderem: Stand der Technik zu polymerbasierten Stator Baugruppen und Isolationskonzepten analysieren Fertigungsprozesse wie Spritzgießen, Extrusion, Imprägnieren und Pressen entwickeln Thermoplaste, Duroplaste und Faserverbundwerkstoffe werkstoff- und prozessgerecht auslegen Versuchsreihen mittels Design of Experiments planen, durchführen und auswerten Prozess-, Werkzeug- und Qualitätsdaten korrelieren sowie robuste Prozessfenster ableiten Werkstoffe mittels DSC, TGA, DMA, TMA und Rheometrie charakterisieren Prozessinduzierte Defekte und Schädigungsmechanismen analysieren Bauteilqualität, Zykluszeit, Materialeffizienz und Industrialisierbarkeit optimieren Ergebnisse dokumentieren, publizieren und mit Fachbereichen sowie Universität abstimmen Die Tätigkeit kann ab Februar 2027 beginnen. Einstellungsvoraussetzung ist die Betreuung des Promotionsvorhabens durch einen Hochschullehrenden. Die Auswahl einer entsprechenden Betreuungsperson obliegt dem Promovierenden. Profil Studium: Sehr gut abgeschlossenes Master- oder Diplomstudium der Kunststofftechnik, Polymertechnik, Leichtbau, Maschinenbau oder vergleichbar mit kunststofftechnischem Schwerpunkt sowie erfüllte Promotionsvoraussetzungen Fachkenntnisse: Fundierte Kenntnisse und praktische Erfahrung in der Kunststoffverarbeitung, insbesondere Spritzgießen; Erfahrung mit Extrusion, Duroplasten, Insert-Molding, Verguss- oder Faserverbundverfahren ist von Vorteil Analytik: Praktische Erfahrung mit DSC, TGA, DMA, TMA und Rheometrie; Kenntnisse in Mikroskopie oder mechanischer Prüfung sind wünschenswert Methoden und IT: Erfahrung mit DoE und statistischer Datenanalyse; sicherer Umgang mit MS Office, Kenntnisse in CAD, Python oder Prozesssimulation sind von Vorteil Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift Persönliches: Analytische, selbstständige und strukturierte Arbeitsweise, Labororientierung, Qualitätsbewusstsein, Kommunikationsstärke und Teamfähigkeit Sonstiges: Bereitschaft zur Arbeit im Technikum und Labor sowie Führerschein Klasse B Zusätzliche Informationen: Promoviere im Mercedes-Benz Konzern! Profitiere von unserem Know-how, einem internationalen Expertise-Netzwerk, Forschungsmaterialien, Arbeitseinblicken und einer persönlichen Betreuung durch Mentorinnen und Mentoren – zusätzlich zu Deiner Hochschule. Weiterführende Informationen findest Du hier. Wir freuen uns auf Deine Online-Bewerbung mit Lebenslauf und Zeugnissen. Ein Anschreiben ist optional. Bitte vergiss nicht, im Online-Formular Deine Dokumente als "relevant für diese Bewerbung" zu markieren und beachte die maximale Dateigröße von 5 MB. Schwerbehinderte und gleichgestellte Bewerbende sind herzlich willkommen! Die Schwerbehindertenvertretung (sbv-untertuerkheim@mercedes-benz.com) unterstützt Dich gerne im Bewerbungsprozess. People Solutions hilft Dir bei Fragen zum Bewerbungsprozess gerne weiter. Du erreichst uns per E-Mail über myhrservice@mercedes-benz.com oder telefonisch unter 0711/17-99000 (Mo-Fr 10-12 Uhr & 13-15 Uhr). Unfortunately, applications without a valid work permit and sufficient German language skills may not be considered. LNKD1_DE

items.title: Phd Candidate In Business And Technology
items.desc: Company Description Western Balkans University (WBU) is a higher education institution based in Tirana, Albania, offering fully English-taught programs. The university has a distinct focus on Medicine, Medical Sciences, Technology, Economy, and Innovation, preparing students for modern, interdisciplinary careers. WBU fosters an international learning environment, encouraging collaboration between academic staff, researchers, and students. The institution emphasizes research, practical learning, and innovation, creating opportunities for emerging scholars to contribute to regional and global development. Role Description The PhD Candidate in Business and Technology will be engaged in advanced academic research, focusing on topics at the intersection of business management, digital transformation, innovation, and emerging technologies. Day-to-day responsibilities include conducting literature reviews, designing research methodologies, collecting and analyzing data, and preparing research papers for conferences and journals. The candidate will participate in seminars, workshops, and departmental meetings, and may support teaching activities such as assisting in undergraduate or master’s courses and supervising student projects. Collaboration with academic supervisors and research teams to develop and refine the dissertation project will be a key component of the role. This is an on-site role located in Albania, requiring regular presence at Western Balkans University and active participation in the campus research community. Qualifications Strong foundation in business, management, economics, or a related field, with interest in technology and innovation. Demonstrated research skills, including literature review, research design, data collection, and quantitative and/or qualitative analysis. Excellent academic writing and communication skills in English, with the ability to present complex ideas clearly. Ability to work independently and collaboratively, manage time effectively, and meet research and academic deadlines. Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Business, Economics, Technology Management, or a related discipline; prior research experience is an advantage. Familiarity with digital tools and platforms used in research and teaching (e.g., statistical software, reference management tools, learning management systems). Motivation to contribute to interdisciplinary projects and to the academic development of Western Balkans University. Strong ethical standards, critical thinking skills, and commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

items.title: Doktorand Biotechnologie (m/w/d)
items.desc: Das Universitätsklinikum Düsseldorf (UKD) ist das größte Krankenhaus in der Landeshauptstadt und eines der wichtigsten medizinischen Zentren in NRW. Die 9.300 Mitarbeiterinnen und Mitarbeiter in UKD und Tochterfirmen setzen sich dafür ein, dass jährlich über 45.000 Patientinnen und Patienten stationär behandelt und 270.000 ambulant versorgt werden können. Das UKD steht für internationale Spitzenleistungen in Krankenversorgung, Forschung und Lehre, sowie für innovative und sichere Diagnostik, Therapie und Prävention. Patientinnen und Patienten profitieren von der intensiven interdisziplinären Zusammenarbeit der 60 Kliniken und Institute. Die besondere Stärke der Uniklinik ist die enge Verzahnung von Klinik und Forschung zur sicheren Anwendung neuer Methoden. Am UKD entsteht die Medizin von morgen. Jeden Tag. Die Medizinische Fakultät der Heinrich-Heine-Universität Düsseldorf ist ein Spitzenzentrum der forschenden Medizin. Ihre Projekte und Verbünde in Grundlagen- und klinischer Forschung werden u.a. von der Deutschen Forschungsgemeinschaft, den Landes- und Bundesministerien und der EU gefördert. Die Klinik für Kardiologie, Pneumologie & Angiologie sucht zum 01.02.2027 einen Wissenschaftlichen Mitarbeiter / naturwissenschaftlicher Doktorand (m/w/d), Teilzeit (TV-L 13, 65%, 3 Jahre) Die Anstellung erfolgt im Rahmen der Arbeitsgruppe von Prof. Dr. med. Amin Polzin in der Sektion für Herzinsuffizienz. Die Arbeitsgruppe besteht aus einem internationalen Team von medizinischen und naturwissenschaftlichen Mitarbeitenden unterschiedlicher Professionen. Als Teil des Teams, werden Sie in der grundlagenwissenschaftlichen Forschung arbeiten. Hier untersuchen Sie u.a. das genetische Risiko eines Myokardinfarktes. Aufgaben Was sind Ihre Aufgabenschwerpunkte? Durchführung experimenteller Tiermodelle Molekularbiologische Analyse von Geweben Bioinformatische Datenanalyse Aktive Mitarbeit über Ihr eigenes Projekt hinaus Eigene wissenschaftliche Weiterqualifikation (Promotion) Qualifikationsprofil Was erwarten wir? Abgeschlossenes naturwissenschaftliches oder veterinärmedizinisches Hochschulstudium oder angrenzenden Fachgebieten Kenntnisse über Versuchstierkunde (Maus/Ratte) - EU Tätigkeit A (früher FELASA B) setzen wir voraus Neugier und starkes Interesse an rigoroser, methodischer Grundlagenforschung Sehr gute mündliche sowie schriftliche Ausdrucksfähigkeit in Deutsch und Englisch Was bringen Sie zusätzlich mit? Begeisterungsfähigkeit für neue Aufgaben Selbstständige Lösungsfindung bei komplexen Frage- und Problemstellungen Freundliche und situationsgerechte Kommunikationsfähigkeiten Wir bieten Was bieten wir? Möglichkeit Ihre Aufgaben im Bereich der akademischen Medizin in einem dynamischen Umfeld eigenverantwortlich zu gestalten Raum für Eigenverantwortlichkeit, Kreativität und persönliche Entwicklung Möglichkeit der Teilnahme an wiss. Konferenzen umfangreiche Fort- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten Der Vertrag wird mit der Heinrich-Heine-Universität geschlossen. Die Heinrich-Heine-Universität Düsseldorf strebt eine Erhöhung des Frauenanteils an. Bewerbungen von Frauen werden bei gleicher Eignung, Befähigung und fachlicher Leistung daher bevorzugt berücksichtigt, sofern nicht in der Person eines Mitbewerbers liegende Gründe überwiegen. Die Heinrich-Heine-Universität vertritt das Prinzip Exzellenz durch Vielfalt. Sie hat die „Charta der Vielfalt“ unterzeichnet und erfolgreich am Audit „Vielfalt gestalten“ des Stifterverbandes teilgenommen. Sie ist als familiengerechte Hochschule zertifiziert und hat sich zum Ziel gesetzt, die Vielfalt ihrer Mitarbeiter*innen zu fördern. Die Bewerbung geeigneter Schwerbehinderter und gleichgestellter behinderter Menschen im Sinne des SGB IX ist erwünscht. Der Arbeitsbereich ist für die Besetzung mit Teilzeitkräften grundsätzlich geeignet.

items.title: Junior Quantum Engineer (PhD candidate)
items.desc:
At IQM, we build world-leading quantum computers for the well-being of humankind. We design systems to tackle computational challenges beyond the practical limits of classical machines. Our work sits at the edge of science and engineering. It's complex, demanding, and deeply collaborative. We turn deep research into reliable, full-stack systems that drive discoveries in fields like medicine, energy, and technology, reshaping how the world computes.
 This position is part of QuBriC , the first European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network dedicated entirely to QEC. You will join an international cohort of doctoral researchers and collaborate with leading academic and industrial partners, including research visits at Chalmers (Gothenburg) and INRA (Paris) .
 Join the team that gives quantum a heartbeat.
 The work 
 The PhD project focus on successfully implementing and testing quantum error correction (QEC) protocols on hardware efficient quantum processors (QPU). You will have access to IQM co-design architecture QPU to benchmark QEC codes efficiency on those QPUs.
 Joining our QEC Operations team, you will combine Python development, experiments on superconducting quantum processors and data analysis to improve and demonstrate QEC performance. You will develop calibration procedure and fundamental operations such as qubit reset and leakage reduction units. Working with quantum and software engineering teams, you will also contribute to the control software that makes these experiments possible.
 Your IQM Team Leader will guide your engineering work, while your PhD supervisor will guide your academic research. Alongside your contributions to IQM’s QEC roadmap, you will write scientific publications, present your findings and complete the activities required by your host university.
 What you’ll actually do 
 Implement, run and analyze experiments for fundamental QEC operations, including qubit reset and leakage reduction.
 Execute QEC capability benchmarks and demonstration experiments, and report findings clearly and accurately.
 Develop features in our quantum computer control software in collaboration with quantum and software engineering teams.
 Support QEC calibration of research and customer quantum processors under guidance, working with calibration and service teams to establish useful workflows.
 Keep up with relevant scientific developments and bring new knowledge into the team’s experimental work.
 Write publications, prepare conference presentations and contribute to university activities, grant reporting and research outreach as part of your PhD.
 What we’re looking for 
 A master’s degree, or equivalent skills, in a field relevant to quantum computing research and development, with excellent academic grades.
 A solid understanding of quantum information processing and quantum computing, including the basic concepts of quantum error correction.
 An understanding of superconducting qubits and quantum processing units.
 Python software engineering skills, including language features, environments, testing, documentation and version control.
 Experience conducting laboratory experiments in quantum science or technology through your studies, research projects or equivalent experience.
 An ability to solve problems with guidance and turn your work into documented code, methods and results that others can use.
 Clear written and spoken communication, a collaborative approach and a commitment to reporting technical results accurately.
 No prior professional experience beyond your university education is required.
 The applicant cannot be in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of the recruitment. 
 Additional information 
 Mobility rule: To fulfil the Marie Skłodowska-Curie mobility rules, you must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Germany for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your date of recruitment.
 The applicant cannot be in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of the recruitment.
 Duration : The position is funded for three years with expecting starting date in January.
 Gross monthly salary range: 5000 € - 5833 €.
 Work location: Munich, Germany.
 Why IQM? 
 Full-stack quantum computing: From quantum hardware to software layers and beyond, we build across the full-stack.
 High-performance playground: We aim high, and we know sustainable performance only works when life outside work does too—hybrid setups, flexible hours.
 Never the smartest: You won’t always be the smartest person in the room. Neither will we. Expect to learn constantly - from each other and beyond with IQM’s Learning Hub, LinkedIn Learning, and a team-based L&D budget.
 Approachable leadership: Flat hierarchy, direct access. Feel free to approach any leaders. They're friendlier than they look!
 The sweet spot: Big enough to matter. Small enough to move fast. Growing between a startup and a corporation. We’re in the phase where top performers get noticed.
 Bigger than IQM: Our people build know-how for the entire quantum ecosystem. We publish papers, run hackathons, and help shape a market that's still being defined.
 The future of computing won’t build itself. You might be one of the few who do. 
 Meet our people and learn more about IQM on our stories page.

The Department of Biology, research group “Animal Ecology” led by Prof. Dr. Anne Mupepele, is currently accepting applications for a position offered in collaboration with Dr. Felix Fornoff, Chair of Nature Conservation and Landscape Ecology, Faculty of Environment and Natural Resources, University of Freiburg. The position is a third-party-funded part-time position (65% of the regular working hours) as Research Assistant (Doctoral Researcher/PhD) is available from 1 February 2027, subject to the approval of funding, for a fixed term of three years. The position will be classified in pay grade E 13 of the Collective Agreement for the Public Service of the State of Hesse (TV-H). The ‘BeeConn’ project (Bee Genetic Connectivity Across Landscapes: Insect Translocation and Population Establishment for Ecological Restoration), funded under the Biodiversa+ call ‘BiodivConnect’, addresses three key challenges in pollinator restoration: 1. the successful translocation and establishment of pollinator species, 2. the restoration of genetic diversity and gene flow through connected stepping-stone habitats and 3. the development of stakeholder-supported strategies for long-term restoration. The project includes additional partners in Sweden and Poland. The PhD project will contribute to all three objectives, with a primary focus on the successful translocation of ground-nesting bees and assessing genetic connectivity across different landscapes in collaboration with the Polish partners. The position is shared between Marburg and Freiburg. Ideally, the first 1.5 years will be spent in Marburg and the second 1.5 years in Freiburg. This offers a unique opportunity to gain insights into two different research groups and to change working environment. The PhD will be formally completed in Marburg and the candidate will be supervised equally by Prof. Anne Mupepele and Dr. Felix Fornoff, throughout the entire duration of the project. Deviations from this scenario, for example, due to personal preference for one of the two locations or to better balanced work and family life, are possible upon agreement. Tasks: Development of a PhD project addressing the scientific questions raised by BeeConn, in particular the extent to which different translocation methods for ground-nesting wild bees can contribute to the recovery of populations, and the extent to which this is influenced by various abiotic factors such as soil substrate. Further the question of how habitat connectivity affects genetic exchange between populations of cavity-nesting wild bees Academic services in the field of research, including the drafting and publication of peer-reviewed academic articles, as well as the presentation of research findings at working group seminars and at academic conferences The position is limited to a time period deemed adequate for the completion of a doctoral degree. As part of the assigned duties, there will be ample opportunity to conduct the independent scientific research necessary for the completion of a doctorate. The limitation complies to Section 2(1) of the German Academic Fixed-Term Contract Act (WissZeitVG). Profile: A completed academic degree (Diplom, Master’s or equivalent) in biology, nature conservation, environmental sciences, bioinformatics or a related field Experience with – or a willingness to acquire – computer-based data collection and analysis methods (e.g. statistics in R) Ability to cope with challenging tasks during fieldwork Organisational skills, e.g. for fieldwork Strong communication skills and the ability to work as part of a team Excellent written and oral presentation skills in English, as well as sufficient knowledge of German or a proven willingness to acquire it, in order to navigate interactions with authorities and landowners, as well as everyday life in Germany, with confidence Knowledge of entomology, particularly regarding wild bees, is an advantage Willingness to collaborate with geneticists and social scientists (interdisciplinary), as well as with farmers (transdisciplinary) A Class B driving licence and a willingness to travel to fieldwork locations are desirable Disposition toown scientific qualification (e.g. a doctorate project in ecology) is expected. We offer: Regular exchanges with other research groups, particularly through integration into a research network – both at the University of Marburg and Freiburg and through collaboration with the four other partners in the BeeConn project: the National Research Institute of Animal Production (Poland), the Institute of Animal Systematics and Evolution of the Polish Academy of Sciences (Poland), the University of Gothenburg (Sweden) and Halmstad University (Sweden) Free use of public transport in Hesse (Landesticket) Company pension scheme (VBL) We actively support the professional development of junior researchers by the offers of Marburg Research Academy (MARA), the International Office and the Higher Education Didactics Office. Contact for more Information Anne Mupepele / Felix Fornoff +49 6421-28 23386 / +49 761-203 67790 mupepele@uni-marburg.de / felix.fornoff@nature.uni-marburg.de We support women and strongly encourage them to apply. items.title: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue
items.desc: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue Shape the future of nanoparticle safety and design. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue. Job description We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University. Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles. Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed. The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target. SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package. As a PhD candidate, you will: Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference. Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up. Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted. Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue. You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects. You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster. The intended start date is January 2027. Job requirements MSc in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, systems biology, or a closely related quantitative field. Demonstrated experience building and solving ODE or dynamical systems models. Demonstrated experience with Bayesian inference in a probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. Strong scientific programming in Python. Please point us to a repository. Excellent written and spoken English. Preferred qualifications: Continuous optimization or optimal control. Causal inference or counterfactual reasoning. Surrogate modelling, Gaussian processes, or emulation. Physiologically based pharmacokinetic modelling or systems pharmacology. Experience packaging and documenting scientific software. No background in toxicology, nanomaterials, chemistry or biology is required. TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference. For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future. At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward. Faculty Technology, Policy & Management The Faculty of TPM provides an important contribution to solving complex technical-social issues, such as energy transition, mobility, digitalisation, water management and (cyber) security. TPM does this with its excellent education and research at the intersection of technology, society and policy. We combine insights from both engineering and social sciences as well as the humanities. TPM develops robust models and designs, is internationally oriented and has an extensive network of knowledge institutions, companies, social organisations and governments. . Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, via s.azimirashti@tudelft.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 29 November 2026 upload your CV, a brief cover letter, a one-page research statement, and a link to a code repository you have built. items.desc: 9th November 2026 Languages English English English Do you want to contribute to the development of knowledge, insight and solutions that are relevant to society and working life today and in the future? PhD Research Fellow in Hydropower generators securing electricity supply and grid resilience Welcome to USN The University of Southeastern Norway (USN) ranks as the country's fourth largest higher education institution. We are a vibrant community of approximately 18,000 students and 1,900 employees. ... (Video unable to load from YouTube. Accept cookie and refresh page to watch video, or click here to open video) About the position The Faculty of Technology, Natural Sciences and Maritime Sciences (TNM) has a vacancy for a temporary 100 % position as PhD Research Fellow in “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” from January 1st 2027. The position is a part of the FME SecurEL center, and it is funded by the Research Council of Norway and USN. The position is located at the Department of Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, and Cybernetics and reports to the Head of Department. The position will be working in the research group, “Electrical Power Systems” (EPS). The place of employment is Porsgrunn. The employment period will be four years full time, and there is a premise for employment that the PhD Research Fellow is enrolled in USN’s PhD-program in PhD in Technology within three months of accession in the position. The four-year full-time period will consist of 75 % research duties and 25 % teaching duties. About the PhD-project and SecurEL This PhD position “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” will be associated with Work Package 1 (WP1) on Security of Electricity Supply in SecurEL. The overall objective for the PhD work is to investigate the role of hydropower generators in managing the security of electricity supply in evolving regional distribution grids. The work of the PhD candidate will be integrated with the ongoing work being carried out by the research partners in WP1. In the initial phase, the supervisors, the candidate (based on the candidate's profile), and research partners in SecurEL will work together to identify the comprehensive research questions to be addressed to meet the overall objective of the PhD work. Some potential specific research objectives: Model the coordination and interactions between power producers and system operators (DSOs and TSO) in scenarios for the transition of distribution grids. Quantify the importance of hydropower production and its interoperability in managing security of supply and grid stability. Explore the interplay between different aspects of security of supply (energy availability, power capacity, reliability of supply and voltage quality), as well as power flow balancing, and dynamic system integration) in regional distribution grids. Investigate how generator characteristics such as capabilities for fault-ride through, island mode transition, and black start impact the vulnerability and resilience of the grid, in particular considering islanded grid operation. Develop vulnerability indicators related to power production and control for increasing situational awareness. Read more about the Centre and its research at the website https://www.securel.no Qualifications Eligibility Requirements: A master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree (120 ECTS). Documented proficiency in English (Nordic applicants may submit their high school diploma as documentation). Applicants with a strong background in STEM fields (e.g., electrical power engineering, control system engineering, physics or environmental engineering, mathematics (Operations research) or computer science or machine learning). The master’s thesis must be included in the application. Some of the teaching duties are in Norwegian language. Documented level of Norwegian or Scandinavian language skills at minimum B2 level are required. Ideal Candidate: Ability to collaborate and work effectively in an international and interdisciplinary research environment. Demonstrates experience or strong interest in modelling, programming, systems thinking, and qualitative/quantitative research methods. Documented programming experience for example GitHub project on MATLAB, Python, Julia, Javascript. Experience in mathematical modeling, control engineering, and optimization is a distinctive advantage. Possesses a strong academic record, with relevant experience in either industry or academia. Has prior professional experience and a solid understanding of workplace responsibilities and expectations, which will be considered a key advantage. Shows a deep interest in interdisciplinary research, is capable of independent work, and actively engages with the supervision team to foster collaborative research. For admission to the PhD-program the weighted average grade is B or higher is usually required. The applicant must have gained the degree within the start date of the position, so applicants in the last semester of their master’s degree are also encouraged to apply. items.title: PhD position in Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory
items.desc: ICFO is offering a PhD position to highly motivated student who wish to start their scientific career in a friendly and stimulating environment. The successful candidate will be joining the Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory group led by Prof. Dr. Oriol Romero-Isart . Our PhD-program brings together top-level training and teaching for young scientists , benefiting from the extensive course offerings of local universities and focused instruction by ICFO professors, in a stimulating, international and interdisciplinary environment . PhD-students have the opportunity to take advantage of our network of excellence , consisting in partners of national and international research institutes and universities, as well as industrial partners in the field. The successful candidate will join a research project funded by a “la Caixa” Junior Leader Fellowship at ICFO. The project, “Tabletop Tests of Fundamental Physics with Levitated Nanoparticles,” will be carried out within the Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory group Macroscopic Quantum Optics Theory group led by Prof. Dr. Oriol Romero Isart and aims to explore how levitated quantum optomechanical systems can be used to investigate fundamental questions in physics, including the search for new fundamental interactions, dark matter, and signatures of the quantum nature of gravity. Main Tasks and Responsibilities The candidate will conduct theoretical research at the intersection of quantum optics, quantum information, and fundamental physics. Their work will involve developing analytical and numerical tools to model quantum systems and designing experimentally feasible protocols for precision sensing and tests of fundamental physics. Eligibility To be eligible for the position, candidates must: Have an internationally-recognized Master-equivalent degree, The degree must be completed by the start of your prospective PhD at ICFO, at the latest, and must be in a field of science and engineering related to the ICFO research activities. Degrees issued within the European Higher Education Area (EHEA) must have an equivalent to 300 ECTS, out of which a minimum of 60 ECTS must have been obtained in postgraduate studies. Please, if in doubt regarding your academic eligibility, contact us at jobs@icfo.eu Candidates who have already been awarded a PhD are not eligible to apply. Have an excellent academic record, previous research experience and a strong commitment for scientific research. Have a high working knowledge of English. ICFO is an equal opportunity employer. Candidates are selected exclusively on merit and potential on the basis of submitted application material. No restrictions related to disabilities, citizenship or gender apply to ICFO positions. ICFO abides by the principles of openness, efficiency, transparency, supportiveness, and international comparability as stated in the European Charter for Researchers and the European Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers. Candidates with disabilities or other special needs are strongly encouraged to apply to the program. ICFO will provide all possible assistance to ensure the candidate’s application is fairly assessed. Candidates who have extenuating circumstances that may explain gaps in the academic career or other potentially negatively evaluated aspects of their application are invited to volunteer, if they wish, personal information that the selection panel may consider in their evaluation. Such information may include details of family obligations, severe illness or disability, refugee situation, etc. If the selection panel decides to shortlist a candidate based in part on such extenuating circumstances, it may require the candidate to provide reasonable supporting documentation. Conditions ICFO PhD positions are offered for a period of 4.5 years. The conditions of the positions awarded in the scope of the ICFO PhD fellowship program are as follows: Initial contract for a period of up to 6 months (referred to as the “initial trainee period”), while being pre-admitted to the PhD program, with an explicit follow-up/ renewal procedure at the end of this first stage. Note that in certain circumstances the initial trainee period might be shortened or not offered. During this period, students already take part in the ICFO working environment, join a research group, and work with their supervisor to define a research project. After the initial training period, students are formally enrolled in a PhD Program with a local university (as a general rule, the UPC PhD in Photonics program administered by ICFO), and the full PhD Fellowship activated. Fellowships are offered for periods of three years, renewable for an additional fourth year, and are formalized via a PhD-contract. Continuity and renewal are subject to satisfactory performance in the PhD studies and related research activities, evaluated annually by the Thesis Director and the ICFO PhD Committee. ICFO offers a standard salary level for PhD Students of €27.257,83 gross annual salary. This applies to both the 6-months Trainee Period and the 4-years PhD Period. The starting date will be discussed with the Group Leader by selected candidate. All fellowships include medical care coverage and work accident insurance through the Spanish Social Security system, providing access to the Spanish public health care system. As part of the fellowship, ICFO will provide budget as deemed necessary and with the corresponding approval from the corresponding Group/Team Leader to enable the PhD fellow to complete his/her assigned research project. This budget is managed by the Group/Team leader, and will include consumables and other materials, training and other related costs, such as registration fees, travel and subsistence costs for participation in national or international events, conference, meetings, schools, and/or other training activities. Additionally, a family allowance is also available on request and after corresponding approval for people with family charges in the terms described in the corresponding policy. To apply , suitable candidates are requested to submit (in English) online the following material: A Cover Letter addressing research interests and motivation for application, as well as specific indication of ICFO research group of interest, A Curriculum Vitae, including contact details, Scanned copies of the complete (Bachelor and Master equivalent) official academic transcripts in English or Spanish, Scanned copies of the degree certificates, if available at the time of application, Holders of degrees issued within European Higher Education Area outside Spain shall also submit the European Diploma supplement, if available. If not submitted during the application, this will be compulsory to be submitted in further steps of the selection process. Holders of degrees issued in outside European Higher Education Area shall submit documentation that explicitly indicate equivalence of degree and/or admissibility in a PhD program in the country where it was issued. If not submitted during the application, this will be compulsory to be submitted in further steps of the selection process. Examples of documents we accept are: Official document or website from the degree granting university Academic transcript including this explicit description Letter or certificate from faculty, school or department, addressed to ICFO on official letter-head, signed by a person responsible for admissions into the PhD program If available, scanned copy of standardized test results (GRE, TOEFL, etc.). Note that submission of test results is optional, but they can be particularly helpful for evaluating candidates with degrees obtained outside the European Higher Education Area. The names and contact details of 2 referees. Extenuating circumstances (optional; 1-page max). Candidates may submit a statement regarding any career interruptions (care of dependents, birth of children, etc.) or any other aspects, which will be taken-into-account in evaluating their applications. Candidates may contact jobs@icfo.eu for formal enquiries regarding the application. Selection process All students admitted into the ICFO PhD program must pass through a selection process involving the evaluation of submitted documents, an eligibility and admissibility check and an interview with a selection committee. ICFO Selection Committees are appointed in line with the recommendations of European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers, in terms of gender balance, diversity of discipline, expertise and necessary competence for a proper evaluation and assessment of the candidates. Selection committee interviews include a presentation of the candidate’s background, research interests and motivations, followed by questions from the committee. Candidates may explain their experience, highlight their achievements, and describe their career aspirations and relevant personal or professional details. Candidates invited to the interviews receive detailed guidelines about the selection process and the interview day. A dedicated, external and independent Appeals Panel will be established to rule on the outcome of appeals from the applicants. At all stages of the process, candidates may contact the Talent Attraction Team via jobs@icfo.eu; for complete information about the PhD Admissions process at ICFO, please see https://www.icfo.eu/studies/phd-program/ Data Protection In accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Organic Law 3/2018, ICFO informs applicants that their personal data will be processed exclusively for recruitment purposes. items.title: Doktorand i bioinformatik med fokus på AI-baserad dataanalys inom precisionsmedicin
items.desc: Skövde Referensnummer HS 2026/672 Högskolan i Skövde är en central och ledande aktör för utbildning, forskning och samverkan som stödjer omställningen för en hållbar framtid – regionalt, nationellt och internationellt. Våra 12 000 studenter och 460 medarbetare skapar förutsättningar för samhällets digitala transformation och hållbar samhällsutveckling genom högkvalitativ utbildning och forskning inom valda områden. Välkommen till ett levande campus mitt i Skaraborg. Om oss Institutionen för biovetenskap vid Högskolan i Skövde bedriver forskning och utbildning av hög internationell standard.Vi har väl utvecklade former för nationell och internationell samverkan mellan utbildning, forskning, näringsliv och övriga samhället. Institutionen för biovetenskap siktar på att vara en nationell nod inom biovetenskap. Som doktorand kommer du att ingå i forskargruppen för translationell bioinformatik, som har lång erfarenhet av att utveckla metoder och verktyg för storskalig dataanalys inom livsvetenskaperna. Forskningsarbetet kommer huvudsakligen att inriktas på utveckling av nya metoder för precisionsmedicin, med särskilt fokus på bioinformatiska metoder för analys av storskaliga omikdata. Arbetet innefattar forskning inom förklarbar AI och modelltolkning, där experimentellt arbete kombineras med avancerade bioinformatiska och AI-baserade analystekniker. Projektet är ett samarbete mellan akademi och industri inom forskningsprofilen ”AI-driven precisionsmedicin” som finansieras av Stiftelsen för kunskap- och kompetensutveckling. Arbetet kommer att bedrivas vid Högskolan i Skövde och Sahlgrenska Universitetssjukhuset i Göteborg. Som doktorand kommer du ha din tjänst inom Bioinformatik som på Högskolan i Skövde definieras som studier och utveckling av datorbaserade metoder och verktyg för analys, modellering, representation, och bearbetning av biomolekylära data. Doktorsexamen kommer att avläggas inom medicin i samarbete med Göteborgs Universitet. Din roll De huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifterna består av att bedriva forskning, utföra institutionsrelaterade tjänster samt hantera tillhörande administrativa uppgifter. Ytterligare arbetsuppgifter kan komma att ingå i befattningen. Behörighet För tillträde till forskarutbildning på forskarnivå krävs grundläggande och i förekommande fall den särskilda behörighet som är fastställd i den allmänna studieplanen för forskarutbildningsämnet. Grundläggande behörighet till forskarutbildning på forskarnivå har den som: avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller på annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat motsvarande kunskaper. Särskild behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå i medicinsk vetenskap har den som: med godkänt resultat fullgjort kurs engelska B/6 eller bedöms ha förvärvat motsvarande kunskaper genom tidigare studier (bedömningen görs i enlighet med Universitets- och högskolerådets rekommendationer). Bedömningsgrunder Vid bedömningen fästs särskild vikt vid dokumenterade kvalifikationer avseende: God förmåga att tillgodogöra sig utbildning på forskarnivå. God samarbetsförmåga och god förmåga att arbeta såväl självständigt som i grupp. Förmåga att planera, organisera och uppnå uppsatta mål. Praktisk laboratorieerfarenhet av molekylärbiologiska metoder, exempelvis qPCR och western blot. Erfarenhet av statistik, bioinformatik och datavisualisering med hjälp av R, Python och Nextflow. Erfarenhet av högpresterande beräkningar (High-Performance Computing, HPC), TensorFlow, PyTorch och Keras för tillämpningar inom djupinlärning, samt praktisk erfarenhet av användning av variationell autokodare (variational autoencoders) och förklarbar AI (Explainable AI), exempelvis metoder som SHAP och integrerade gradienter (Integrated Gradients). Kunskap om analys av omikdata, inklusive single-cell RNA-sekvensering (single-cell RNA-seq) och proteomik. Vid denna anställning kommer stor vikt att fästas vid erfarenhet av högpresterande beräkningar (High Performance Computing, HPC), TensorFlow, PyTorch och Keras för tillämpningar inom djupinlärning, samt praktisk erfarenhet av användning av variationell autokodare (variational autoencoders) och förklarbar AI (Explainable AI), exempelvis metoder som SHAP och integrerade gradienter (Integrated Gradients). Anställningsform: Anställningen är en visstidsanställning fram till och med avlagd doktorsexamen, dock längst 4,5 år. Anställningens omfattning är 100 %, varav 90 % forskarstudier och 10 % institutionstjänstgöring. Lön utgår enligt lokalt avtal om lönestege för forskarstuderande. Endast den som antas eller redan har antagits till en utbildning på forskarnivå får anställas som doktorand. Sista ansökningsdatum: 16 november 2026 Diarienummer: Ref nr HS 2026/672 Kontaktuppgifter: Upplysningar om anställningen lämnas av avdelningschef Henrik Thilander (henrik.thilander@his.se) och projektledare Jane Synnergren (jane.synnergren@his.se). Facklig information lämnas av Anders Johansson (Saco-S) eller Maria Carlstedt (ST). Samtliga personer nås via Högskolans växel 0500-44 80 00. Ansökan Du söker anställningen via vår hemsida, www.his.se/jobb genom att klicka på ”Ansök” . Där kan du även läsa mer oss Högskolans rekryteringsprocess samt vilka förmåner du har som medarbetare hos oss. Välkommen med din ansökan! Till din ansökan ska följande dokument bifogas: Personligt brev inklusive en intressebeskrivning engelska där du redogör för dina forskningsintressen och förväntningar på forskarutbildningen CV Intyg, betyg och övriga merithandlingar du som sökande vill åberopa Examensbevis och betygsutdrag Examensarbete på magister- eller masternivå Eventuella publikationer Kontakta HR-avdelningen på hr-specialister.hr@his.se om du har publikationer som inte kan bifogas elektroniskt direkt i ansökan. Publikationerna ska vara högskolan tillhanda senast en vecka efter sista ansökningsdatum. Länk till den här sidan https://www.his.se/mot-hogskolan/jobba-hos-oss/lediga-jobb/?rmpage=job&rmjob=1165&rmlang=SE

items.title: Doctoral Position in Environmental Microbiology
items.desc: Doctoral Position in Environmental Microbiology 100%, Zurich, fixed-term The Environmental Microbiology group led by Prof. Marie Schölmerich at the Department of Environmental Systems Science, ETH Zurich, invites applications for a fully funded 4 year Doctoral Position. Our group explores the fascinating world of anaerobic microbiology from the global to the microscopic scale. This project investigates the physiology and bioenergetics of alkaliphilic methanogenic archaea. Project background The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress. Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website. NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups. Job description Alkaline environments such as soda lakes and serpentinising vents are candidate sites for the emergence of life on Earth and potential habitats on ocean worlds like Enceladus Methanogenic archaea are the main biological source of the greenhouse gas methane Some methanogenic archaea can thrive under alkaliphilic conditions where conventional energy conservation reaches its limits This Doctoral project seeks to investigate what limits the growth of alkaliphilic methanogens, how they conserve energy and acquire carbon at high pH, and which signatures distinguish their methane from abiotic methane The work combines anaerobic cultivation, physiology and biochemistry Profile MSc (or equivalent) in microbiology, environmental sciences or a related field Experience in anaerobic cultivation and/or protein biochemistry is an advantage Curiosity about fundamental questions and enthusiasm for experimental work and excellent communication skills in English Workplace Workplace We offer Opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research with the potential for high impact in the field of environmental microbiology Encouraging and collaborative research environment A Doctoral Position in a national, interdisciplinary network linking microbiology with geochemistry, planetary science and origin-of-life research Training in anaerobic microbiology, bioenergetics, and omics A fundamental research question with direct relevance to astrobiology and the methane cycle Support for career goals through conference travel and workshops Exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits We value diversity and sustainability In line with our values, ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future. Curious? So are we. We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents: Cover letter CV including publication list Diploma and Transcript of Records Contact details of two references Further information about the Environmental Microbiology Group in the Department of Environmental Systems Sciences can be found on our website. Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Marie Schölmerich, marie.schoelmerich@usys.ethz.ch (no applications). Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered. The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026. We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

items.title: PhD Student in Philosophy in SNSF-Project CREST-AI
items.desc: Digital Society Initiative PhD Student in Philosophy in SNSF-Project CREST-AI 80 % Start of employment November 1, 2026 or by agreement, temporary We invite you to apply for a two-year funded PhD position in philosophy whose research output will be directly relevant to building the next generation of expert-layperson simplification AI. As a PhD student, you will contribute to the research project «Countering Epistemic, Semantic and Technological Asymmetry in AI-Human Collaboration Focusing on Expert-Layperson Simplification (CREST-AI)» funded by the SNSF at the University of Zurich's Digital Society Initiative (DSI) under the supervision of Dr. Reto Gubelmann. The main philosophical reference point will be Neo-Kantian conceptions of rational autonomy, which will be brought to bear on the epistemically challenging situation of being on the receiving end of expert-layperson simplification settings, directly shaping the technology developed in the project. The Digital Society Initiative (DSI) aims to shape the digital transformation of science and society and thus to strengthen Zurich as a center of research and business. Your responsibilities Conducting research in the Context of WP 1 of Project CREST-AI Writing a doctoral dissertation Participating in scientific conferences and public outreach activities Supporting the PI in managing the project, organizing conferences and preparation of research proposals to national and international funding agencies Your profile Excellent MA in Philosophy, preferably with an emphasis on Kantian thought. Information on your application Please submit your application at your earliest convenience; the position will remain open until filled. Your application should include: your CV, motivation letter (specify your research interests and how they relate to the topic of the research project), academic record (include additional education or coursework if applicable), contact information of two references and a writing sample (a paper or chapter from your Master's thesis). items.title: PhD Candidate in Sociology
items.desc: Jacobs Center for Productive Youth Development PhD Candidate in Sociology 80 % Start of employment February 2027 or by arrangement, temporary Professor Robin Samuel's research group at the Jacobs Center for Productive Youth Development and the Department of Sociology at the University of Zurich investigates how the interplay between digital and physical social spaces shapes how young people grow up. Its research focuses on social inequalities, everyday socialization processes, and their role for the development of children and adolescents, while integrating a biopsychosocial perspective. Your responsibilities Develop and pursue independent research questions as part of an article-based doctoral dissertation comprising three empirical papers. Contribute to the design, implementation and analysis of a longitudinal study supplemented by diary, geo-spatial and experimental data. Conduct additional analyses of secondary data. Apply and further develop quantitative analytical methods in collaboration with an experienced postdoctoral researcher. Present and publish research findings and contribute to interdisciplinary collaboration at the Jacobs Center. Co-supervise Bachelor's and Master's theses in sociology. Your profile A Master's degree in sociology or a related social science discipline by the start of employment. Strong interest in sociological questions concerning socialization, childhood and adolescence, social inequalities, and digital and physical living environments. Very good quantitative methodological skills and experience with R or Python; knowledge of longitudinal analysis is an advantage. Interest in deepening your expertise in advanced quantitative methods, especially longitudinal, experimental and spatial analyses. Very good academic communication skills in German and English. An independent, analytical and meticulous working style, and enjoyment of interdisciplinary collaboration and academic exchange. Information on your application Please submit your application as a single PDF file containing the following documents: (1) A motivation letter (maximum two pages) outlining your research interests, motivation to pursue a PhD, and fit with the research group. In particular, explain how you would contribute to Professor Robin Samuel's research agenda through your own research questions, theoretical perspectives and methodological skills. (2) An academic CV detailing your education, previous research experience, quantitative methods and software skills, any publications and conference contributions, and the names and contact details of two to three academic referees. (3) Degree certificates and transcripts for your Bachelor's and Master's studies. If your Master's degree is not yet complete, please submit a current transcript. (4) Two academic writing samples (e.g., a Master's thesis, academic publications, manuscripts or seminar papers). For co-authored work, please briefly indicate your contribution. items.title: PhD Position in Neuroimaging, LLM, Genetics and Cross-species comparison
items.desc: Your function Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison. The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization. A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience . You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining. You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence. Your duties analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity integrate genetics with neuroimaging perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows collaborate with researchers within the Connectome Lab, CNCR and international research networks present your findings at national and international scientific meetings write scientific manuscripts contribute to teaching activities where appropriate Your profile MSc degree in neuroscience, neuroimaging, genetics, biomedical engineering, physics, computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics, psychology, biology, or a related quantitative discipline. Hands-on experience with computational analysis is important. Ideally, you have experience with several of the following: structural MRI and cortical reconstruction, including FreeSurfer Genetics (GWAS) diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI), tractography and structural connectivity resting-state fMRI and functional connectivity analysis FSL and other commonly used neuroimaging software packages Experience with AI / LLM processing and quality control of neuroimaging datasets connectome and network neuroscience analyses Strong interest in and experience with scientific programming is essential. You should have experience with Python, MATLAB, R, Bash and/or comparable languages , and be comfortable working with computational analysis pipelines. Experience with one or more of the following would be an advantage: large-scale neuroimaging datasets such as UK Biobank, HCP or comparable resources comparative or cross-species neuroimaging brain atlases, surface-based analysis and registration machine learning or multivariate statistics high-performance computing version control and reproducible research workflows network science and computational modelling We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy working with complex data, think critically about methodology, and are motivated to develop strong computational and neuroimaging expertise. You should also: have a strong interest in neurodiversity and/or evolution be able to work independently while enjoying collaboration within a multidisciplinary team have good analytical and problem-solving skills have a good command of written and spoken English be motivated to learn new neuroimaging and computational techniques support open and reproducible science and be willing to share tools and data with the wider scientific community As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset. We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements. What do we offer? Education A challenging position in a socially engaged organisation. At VU Amsterdam, you contribute to education, research and service for a better world. And that is valuable. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of minimum € 3.204,00 (PhD year 1) and maximum € 4.051 (PhD year 4) gross per month, on a full-time basis. This is based on UFO profile PhD candidate. a 4-year PhD position (initial 1-year contract, extended by 3 years following positive evaluation). We also offer you attractive fringe benefits and regulations. Some examples: a full-time 38-hour working week comes with a holiday leave entitlement of 232 hours per year. If you choose to work 40 hours, you have 96 extra holiday leave hours on an annual basis. For part-timers, this is calculated pro rata. 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% end-of-year bonus solid pension scheme (ABP) contribution to commuting expenses optional model for designing a personalized benefits package About Us Research environment You will join the Connectome Lab of prof Van den Heuvel at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Our research focuses on understanding the architecture of the human brain and how its network organization relates to cognition, individual variation, brain disorders and evolution. You will work in a multidisciplinary team of PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and students with backgrounds spanning neuroimaging, network neuroscience, genetics, artificial intelligence, computational neuroscience and psychology. The project is embedded within the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR) , providing a highly interdisciplinary research environment and opportunities for collaboration within VU Amsterdam and with national and international research groups. Faculty of Science Working at the Faculty of Science means collaborating with students, lecturers and researchers who are focused on their field, yet have a broad view of the world. We are proud of a positive and inclusive workplace culture within the faculty, where we work together with great energy and a pragmatic attitude to tackle social challenges. At the Faculty of Science, scientists and students work on fundamental and complex societal issues for a sustainable, healthy and just future. From forest fires to big data, from obesity to malnutrition, from helium to the universe and from genetics to medicine: our education and research cover the full breadth of science, from molecules to mankind. Our academic education and research are highly experimental, technical and interdisciplinary in nature. That is why we collaborate extensively with leading scientific institutes and industry. The faculty has more than 8,000 students studying in one of the 39 programms and employs more than 1,400 staff across 10 scientific departments, making us one of the largest science faculties in the Netherlands. Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam stands for values-driven education and research. We are open-minded experts with the ability to think freely - a broader mind. Maintaining an entrepreneurial perspective and concentrating on diversity, significance and humanity, we work on sustainable solutions with social impact. By joining forces, across the boundaries of disciplines, we work towards a better world for people and planet. Learn more about our codes of conduct (https://vu.nl/en/about-vu/more-about/code-of-conduct-vu-amsterdam) We are located on one physical campus, in the heart of Amsterdam's Zuidas business district, with excellent location and accessibility.
