items.title: Doctoral researcher in computational genomics for predictive medicine
items.desc: The Barrett lab at the University of Helsinki is recruiting a doctoral researcher (PhD student) in computational genomics for predictive medicine. We are jointly affiliated with the ELLIS Institute Finland , the Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM) , and the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Helsinki. We analyze multiomic data to discover, understand, and measure mechanistically meaningful subtypes of complex human diseases. We believe that characterizing diseases not by their observed clinical phenotype, but by their molecular and biological endotype, will enable better treatment for patients. This long-held ambition in biomedicine is now poised to be realized due to: National research biobanks that collectively include millions of individuals with matched biosamples and detailed electronic health records. Large and growing multiomic data sets in samples from these biobanks, including genomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and transcriptomics. New machine learning and AI methods to build multiomic models that stratify disease risk, progression, and treatment response by molecular endotypes. Find examples of research areas and possible projects on our website. Responsibilities Design and implement a PhD research project on a topic related to computational genomics for predictive medicine. Carry out the research project: propose hypotheses, write code, think about and discuss results, and interpret findings. Collaborate closely with other members of the team, other researchers at the ELLIS Institute and University of Helsinki, and international partners. Share scientific results via publications and presentations at local and international conferences, and contribute more broadly to open science (e.g. via pre-prints and open source software). Contribute to mentoring and training the next generation of scientists. Qualifications, Experience, And Skills These items are most important for this role. We expect candidates to fulfill most of these: Motivation to work collaboratively on hard scientific problems with a pragmatic focus on getting things done. Master’s degree in computational biology, data science, bioinformatics, or a related discipline (exceptional candidates may be considered coming straight from a bachelor’s). Proficiency in programming for data analysis in either Python or R. Research experience in computational biology and/or data science. Excellent written and spoken English. Any of the following are nice experience to have, but not essential. Please don’t be put off if you don’t have these: Working in high-performance or cloud compute environments. Working on machine learning problems (e.g. with frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow). Research with health care and/or genomics data. Developing software in a small team environment with code review and version control. Using agentic AI tools (e.g. from Anthropic and OpenAI) while still retaining your own thinking process (see here for more about how we use AI). What We Offer This is an opportunity to be one of the first members of a newly established laboratory led by Professor Jeffrey Barrett, who has over 20 years’ experience leading genomics research teams. You will benefit from hands-on supervision from Professor Barrett as well as active participation in the intellectual environments at both FIMM (genomics and molecular medicine) and the ELLIS Institute (fundamentals of applied AI). Our team has access to biobank data sets which cumulatively include 2 million individuals (FinnGen, UK Biobank, All of Us, Estonian Biobank). We have access to both local supercomputer facilities as well as extensive cloud computing resources. We also routinely generate new ’omics data in samples available from the Finnish biobank network. The position is for a fixed term, with a maximum duration of four years. A trial period of six months will be applied. The salary is based on the salary system of the Finnish universities . The starting salary is typically around 2600-2850 EUR per month, depending on the appointees’ qualifications and experience, and rises gradually as the PhD work progresses. The University of Helsinki offers comprehensive services to its employees, including occupational health care, support in access to high quality sports facilities, and many opportunities for professional development. Standard Finnish pension benefits are provided for university employees. How To Apply Please submit your application through the University of Helsinki recruitment system by November 19 , 2026. Your application should include: A one-page cover letter describing why you’re interested in this role. Please don’t use AI for this! It’s important to explain in your own voice. CV, including publications and github link if applicable Contact information for two references For more information regarding the position or the research goals of the group, please contact Jeff at jeffrey.c.barrett(at)helsinki.fi. More information A diverse and equitable study and work culture is important to us. That is why we do our best to promote an inclusive university community. We encourage all qualified applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply for our positions. Click this link to read about accessibility and inclusivity at our University. JOIN US TO BUILD A BETTER WORLD – TOGETHER! #HelsinkiUniCareers The Institute for Molecular Medicine Finland (FIMM) is an international research unit focusing on human genomics and personalized medicine at the Helsinki Institute of Life Science (HiLIFE) of the University of Helsinki - a leading Nordic university with a strong commitment to life science research. As part of Academic Medical Center Helsinki in Meilahti campus FIMM collaborates locally with the Faculty of Medicine, Helsinki University Hospital and National Institute for Health and Welfare. FIMM is part of the Nordic EMBL Partnership for Molecular Medicine, composed of the European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL) and the centres for molecular medicine in Norway, Sweden and Denmark, and the EU-LIFE Community. ELLIS (European Laboratory for Learning and Intelligent Systems) is a major European initiative in AI with a mission to strengthen Europe’s AI landscape by connecting top researchers, attracting talent, and fostering strategic collaborations. ELLIS unites leading machine learning researchers in Europe and operates as a multi-centric, pan-European AI Lab, currently spanning 47 research sites. ELLIS Institute Finland was launched in 2025 and is the second institute in the ELLIS network , partnering with Finnish universities. We develop machine learning through fundamental research, with a particular focus on the fundamentals of applied AI: making machine learning more widely and effectively applicable, and better at working with people. AI for Research is one part of this focus. Our faculty works across a broad range of areas, including data-efficient probabilistic machine learning, generative modelling, amortized inference, interactive and cooperative machine learning, and transformative multidisciplinary collaboration. The institute will have a small number of strategic focus areas and the first one is AI for Health, spearheaded by a project to build a nationwide foundation model to support better decision-making in healthcare.

items.title: PhD position 6G-Native Distributed Intelligence for Physical AI
items.desc: Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications. Job Description Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge. How can 6G enable resource-constrained Physical AI by dynamically distributing and adapting AI workloads across embedded devices, the edge, and the cloud, while jointly orchestrating communication, computation, and sensing under strict latency, reliability, and resource constraints? The project will investigate resource-aware 6G-native distributed AI techniques such as collaborative and split inference, adaptive model partitioning and selection, computation offloading, and cross-layer resource orchestration. A particular focus will be on how 6G can enable Physical AI systems to adapt to changing network, compute, sensor, and energy conditions while maintaining predictable performance. You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos. Job requerements Become part of an expansive ecosystem shaping the development of 6G. You will benefit from training in 5G and beyond networks, AI, and software development. Plus, you will gain exclusive access to (1) a state-of-the-art testbed where theory meets real-world application, and (2) an ecosystem that cultivates entrepreneurial endeavours. Are you ready to challenge yourself? We're seeking candidates who have, or are about to receive, a Master-of-Science degree in a relevant computer science discipline and who like to combine theory with practice. Proficiency in English is essential, as you'll collaborate within a diverse, international community. For more details on our admission requirements, please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission. We’ll evaluate based on your academic record, interviews, and possibly assignments. While a strong background in the field is crucial, what matters as well is your creative flair, motivation, and above all, your passion for comprehensive research! TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context. At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. Challenge. Change. Impact! Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact Dr Qing Wang, via qing.wang@tudelft.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 Nov 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter Copies of your BSc and MSc degrees and transcripts. You can address your application to Dr Qing Wang. Applications will be evaluated as they come in,so please apply as soon as possible. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. It plays a key role in scientific and technological policy in Spain by carrying out research in all fields of knowledge. CSIC produces ~20% of the national scientific output and is liste the 1st organization in Spain, the 3rd in H2020 (917 projects) and the 2nd in Horizon Europe (612 projects). It is also a main actor in the ERC programme (161 projects signed as Host Institution), the EIT’s, KIC’s, and International Programmes like LIFE and INTERREG. CSIC coordinates key infrastructures (ESFRI, EOSC), promotes Open Science, and holds the HR Excellence in Research award. The successful candidate will join the Instituto de Geociencias (IGEO, Madrid), a Joint Research Center of CSIC and UCM. IGEO gathers employees and resources from both institutions and carries out cutting-edge multidisciplinary research in different topics related to climate. This multidisciplinary character embraces the study of the Earth System, from the core to the stratosphere, in order to solve scientific problems in Earth Sciences within the framework of scientific collaborations with other research organizations and industry, at both national and international levels. Homepage: https://www.igeo.ucm-csic.es/ Location Madrid, Spain Sector Academic Relevant divisions Atmospheric Sciences (AS) Climate: Past, Present & Future (CL) Natural Hazards (NH) Type Full time Level Student / Graduate / Internship Salary approximately €1,655 net per month, depending on personal tax circumstances, with full Spanish Social Security coverage and standard employee benefits. Required education Master Application deadline Open until the position is filled Posted 26 October 2026 Job Description The Physics of Climate and Climate Change group at the Instituto de Geociencias (IGEO, CSIC–UCM) in Madrid invites applications for a: PhD researcher, 100% to join the project ADAPT-X – AI-Driven AnticiPated aTtribution of eXtreme events (ref. 2025-T1/ECO-36122 ), funded by the Comunidad de Madrid through the César Nombela Talent Attraction Programme. The position is offered for 4 years , starting in Spring 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. ADAPT-X investigates how AI-based weather prediction models can be used to improve the prediction and climate-change attribution of extreme events such as heatwaves, heavy precipitation, droughts and severe storms. Recent AI weather models can produce skilful global forecasts at a fraction of the computational cost of conventional numerical weather prediction systems, opening new possibilities for large forecast ensembles and event-based climate attribution. The PhD researcher will evaluate the predictive skill of AI weather models for extreme events and examine how well they represent the atmospheric processes associated with them. The work will include factual and counterfactual forecast experiments, in which AI models are initialized under present-day and pre-industrial climate conditions to quantify the influence of anthropogenic climate change on individual events. The candidate will also investigate how the imposed climate-change signal evolves during the forecast, assess the physical consistency of the resulting response using dynamical and thermodynamic diagnostics, and compare AI-based attribution with physics-based numerical weather prediction simulations, including NWP experiments for selected events. The successful candidate will join the Physics of Climate and Climate Change group at IGEO-CSIC and the STREAM research group at UCM , with access to GPU and high-performance computing resources and opportunities for international collaboration and research stays. Requirements: Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a Master’s degree giving access to a PhD programme in atmospheric sciences, meteorology, climate science, physics, applied mathematics, environmental sciences, computer science, data science, or a related quantitative field. Good scientific programming skills, particularly in Python, are required. Experience with atmospheric dynamics, numerical modelling, machine learning, or large meteorological datasets would be advantageous. Full description of the offer here: https://bernatj.github.io/assets/pdf/PhD_offer_ADAPTX.pdf How to apply Applications and deadline: Please send a single PDF including (i) CV, (ii) a one-page motivation letter, (iii) academic transcripts, and (iv) contact details of two potential referees to bernatji@ucm.es, with the subject “ADAPT-X PhD application – [Candidate name]” , by 31 December 2026 . items.title: PhD Position Bayesian Modeling and Counterfactual Methods for Nanoparticle Transport in Human Tissue
items.desc: Shape the future of nanoparticle safety and design. Join TU Delft as a PhD researcher using Bayesian and counterfactual modelling to predict nanoparticle transport in human tissue. Job Description We are looking for a PhD candidate to build the computational model at the center of a European project on nanoparticle transport in human tissue. You will join the research group of Dr. Sepinoud Azimi, working within the SYNERGIE project (Horizon Europe), a consortium of thirteen partners including Fraunhofer, Roche, the Karolinska Institute, University Hospital Aachen, Mimetas, Ruhr University Bochum and Maastricht University. Small particles from the environment have been detected in human blood, placenta and brain tissue, but it is still not clear what they do there. Dose-response data for humans does not exist and animal studies have not transferred well, and as a result there is no exposure limit for these particles. Part of the reason prediction is so hard is that a particle changes as it moves through the body. It acquires a layer of proteins, it aggregates with other particles, and depending on the material it may partly degrade, so that the particle reaching a given tissue is not the same object that was administered or characterised at the start. Most transport models do not account for this. They treat the particle as fixed, which means they are predicting the fate of something that has already changed. The same difficulty affects engineered nanoparticles for drug delivery, and it is one of the reasons so few of them reach their intended target. SYNERGIE is building a platform of nine human tissue-on-chip models that can be connected to follow a particle through uptake, circulation and storage. TU Delft leads the in silico work package. As a PhD candidate, you will: Build a mechanistic model of how particles move between nine human tissues, and calibrate it against experimental data using Bayesian inference. Work out which physical and chemical properties of a particle decide where it ends up. Develop methods that go beyond prediction: for a particle that behaves badly, what is the smallest change that would fix it, and when should that answer not be trusted. Release the model as open-source software and support its use in regulatory dialogue. You will also contribute to teaching in the department and to the supervision of BSc projects. You will work alongside a postdoctoral researcher and PhD candidates on related problems, and interact with experimental partners across the SYNERGIE consortium. You will have access to the DelftBlue high-performance computing cluster. The intended start date is January 2027. Job Requirements MSc in applied mathematics, computational science, physics, systems biology, or a closely related quantitative field. items.title: PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials
items.desc: Beschreibung Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Laboratory for Acoustics/Noise Control is an international team of scientists and engineers active in the fields of vibroacoustics, environmental acoustics, and psychoacoustics. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements. Mechanical waves and vibrations are traditionally controlled using linear devices with fixed properties. In this PhD project, the student will explore a new generation of nonlinear resonators whose dynamic behaviour changes with vibration amplitude, enabling functionalities that are not achievable with conventional designs. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. The goal is to develop efficient models and design rules for nonlinear metamaterials capable of adaptive vibration isolation, frequency conversion, and non-reciprocal wave propagation. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative Swiss-French project involving Empa, ETH Zurich, and LAUM. PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials Your tasks As doctoral candidate within this project you will work on highly nonlinear building blocks for vibrational metamaterials. Specific tasks to achieve the challenging results include Develop analytical and numerical models for strongly nonlinear resonators exhibiting nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia effects. Design, simulate, and optimize novel resonator concepts based on inertia amplification, bilinear stiffness, and multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics. Manufacture and experimentally characterize resonator prototypes using vibration testing, laser vibrometry, and modal analysis techniques. Investigate nonlinear phenomena such as internal resonances, frequency conversion, bifurcations, and nonlinear energy transfer. Create reduced-order models and efficient simulation tools for the design of nonlinear metamaterials and wave-control devices. Disseminate research results through publications in leading journals, presentations at international conferences, and collaboration with project partners at ETH Zurich and the Université du Mans. Your profile If You Recognize Yourself In The Story Below, Then You Have The Profile That Fits The Project And The Research Group I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics, obtained no longer than four years ago and performed above average in comparison to my peers. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some experience with at least one of the following: structural and/or nonlinear dynamics, numerical modelling techniques (finite element method), or experimental methods in acoustics. I have a profound interest for these topics. As a researcher I perform research in a structured and scientifically sound manner. I read technical papers, understand the nuances between different theories and implement and improve methodologies myself. In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors which steer the direction of my research. It's important for me to work as an active team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and being inspired by my colleagues. During my PhD I want to grow towards more independence, e.g. representing the research group on project meetings and conferences. I see these events as an occasion to disseminate my work to an audience of international experts and research colleagues, and to learn about the larger context of my research and the research project. Our offer We offer a fully funded 4-year PhD position at Empa. The candidate will also be enrolled as a PhD student at the ETH Zürich, co-supervised by Dr. Paolo Tiso. The core of the PhD project will be conducted at Empa with at least one research secondment in Le Mans and intense collaboration with the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETHZ. Besides ample occasions to develop yourself in a scientific and/or industrial direction offered by the research group, further doctoral training for PhD candidates is provided in the framework of the Doctoral School. Starting date is February 2027 or upon mutual agreement. You stay in a vibrant environment centrally in Europe. Empa has its main campus in Dübendorf, located close to Zürich and 20 minutes by tram from Zurich International Airport. Zurich is one of the cities with the highest quality of life worldwide, welcoming to non-German speaking people and with ample opportunities for social, cultural, and outdoor activities. We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

items.title: PhD In-flight aeroelastic measurements & modelling for scaled experimental a/c (m/v/x)
items.desc: Functieomschrijving Join a cutting-edge PhD in experimental flight testing and advanced optical measurement technology to help shape the future of sustainable flight! Background Recently, the use of scaled flight testing has received interest at NLR and multiple other research institutions in Europe to fill the gap between ground testing and full-scale flight testing. Scaled flight tests of radically new aircraft concepts can provide early stage validation data of flight dynamics and complex interdisciplinary topics such as aero(servo)elasticity . Because these topics are very challenging to address in ground testing, validation data would typically only be obtained at the later stages of a design processes when large prototypes are flown. Insights into these topics stemming from scaled flight tests at earlier design stages can be critical enablers to accelerate innovation in aerospace. Currently, a gap exists between the highly sophisticated measurement instruments focused on producing a maximal amount of information that are used in ground testing and the specialized equipment with a focus on reliability and accuracy in difficult measurement circumstances that has been developed for large-scale flight testing. Previous projects that were focused on advanced in-flight measurement techniques have made large steps towards making modern measurement instruments, often optical and/or laser-based measurement techniques, applicable in-flight. However, existing research work focused on large-scale industrial flight testing. The recent interest on the topic of scaled flight testing results in a need to develop advanced measurement techniques specifically for smaller scale experimental flight testing. This type application is of high interest for advanced measurement techniques because the uncertainties are larger than in industrial testing, creating a more urgent need for more comprehensive and detailed measurement data. Furthermore, understanding the possibilities and limitations of scaled flight testing for aeroelastic phenomena and the application of digital twins can improve the value of the results. Project Description Ultra-high aspect ratio wings, with or without truss, are often featured on novel aircraft configurations for future sustainable aircraft. Such wings exhibit different structural characteristics than wings on current aircraft types. The differences become even more pronounced when the fuel source is switched to hydrogen because the hydrogen fuel tanks cannot be carried in the wing. This means that the development of such new wings will have considerable consequences for the entire aircraft design, resulting in novel configurations. Novel configurations are also envisioned for other aircraft concept ideas, such as wings carrying batteries, distributed propulsion on wings, etc. Addressing the design challenges of these novel aircraft designs can be supported by scaled flight testing. Among the tests performed with such scaled experimental aircraft, the complex topic of aeroservoelasticity at the intersection of aerodynamics, flight dynamics, structural dynamics and control, stands out as highly relevant and challenging. It requires efficient and robust measurement techniques applied in flight and a detailed understanding of the validity of results for characterizing the multi-disciplinary problems addressed, such as aeroelastic aircraft state estimation, gust sensing, and load alleviation, where state-of-the art pointwise measurements encounter limitations that could be overcome by global optical measurement techniques. Optical measurement techniques promise to improve in-flight capabilities significantly but require further maturation in the relevant test environment, which is targeted in this PhD project. Furthermore, the assessment of the scaling possibilities and limitations is supported with a simulation environment in which digital twins of the scaled and full-scale aircraft provide substantiation of accuracies and validity of results. The maturation is achieved in a combination of ground tests (e.g. the wind tunnel) for developing and refining the envisioned measurement approach and flight testing (e.g. the Diana 2 scaled glider platform) for validating its performance. Your profile Master’s degree in aerospace engineering or an equivalent study; Hands-on experience with complex measurement technology; Experience or affinity with (experimental) flight testing; Strong background in programming, using MATLAB and/or Python or other relevant programming languages; Collaborative and self-directed, and receptive to constructive feedback; Good communication skills for spoken and written English. Knowledge of Dutch is desirable but not mandatory; Ability to learn independently and passion for research. What we offer you You will receive a 4-year research contract from NLR Amsterdam and will join the Flight Test and Certification department. In addition, you will be enrolled in the Doctoral Education programme of the Graduate School at Delft University of Technology (TU Delft), i.e. an excellent team of supervisors and academic staff. At the start of your assignment your working week will ideally be divided into: 4 days in Amsterdam, 1 days in Delft. In Addition To All This, We Offer No fewer than 45 days off (with full-time employment) so that you can also fully enjoy your free time in addition to your challenging job; A fixed end-of-year bonus of 8%; A contribution towards your healthcare costs; Extra paid parental leave; The possibility to work from home. Working at NLR? Royal NLR has been a knowledge organization with the will and ambition to innovate for over 100 years. Based on that motivation, we make the world of aviation and space travel safer, more sustainable, more efficient and effective and stand for groundbreaking innovations. We employ more than 1000 passionate professionals, from aircraft engineers to psychologists and from mathematicians to application experts. NLR stands for an inclusive and diverse organization where everyone feels welcome, safe, valued and respected. Would you like to know more? Please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/en/ae/research/ae-graduate-school for more information on the graduate school. Don't hesitate to contact Frank Bax (recruiter) via frank.bax@nlr.nl or Skype! Would you like to apply? Great, we are curious about you! Send your motivation letter and CV via the apply button! A pre-employment security screening VGB-C is a requirement. For more information about the screening, please visit the AIVD website. Acquisiton is not appreciated.

items.desc: Beschreibung Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Für unser Forschungsprojekt SOUND suchen wir eine:n PhD-Doktorand:in, die/der anhand neuester neurobildgebender Verfahren sowie klinischer Daten untersucht, wie sich das Sprachverstehen nach einer Cochlea-Implantation besser vorhersagen lässt (*Predicting Speech Perception Outcomes in Cochlear Implant Candidates Using Neuroimaging Data*). Das Projekt wird vom Forschungsteam «Auditory Pathway» am Hearing Research Laboratory des ARTORG Centers for Biomedical Engineering Research der Universität Bern in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Universitätsklinik für Hals-, Nasen- und Ohrenkrankheiten am Inselspital durchgeführt. Cochlea-Implantate sind hochwirksame Neuroprothesen, die Menschen mit hochgradigem Hörverlust ermöglichen, wieder Klänge wahrzunehmen und Sprache zu verstehen. Wie gut das Sprachverstehen nach der Implantation gelingt, ist individuell sehr unterschiedlich: Bei rund einem Viertel der Patientinnen und Patienten bleiben die Ergebnisse hinter den Erwartungen zurück, und verlässliche Prognosen zum individuellen Nutzen eines Cochlea-Implantats vor der Operation fehlen bislang. Hinweise deuten darauf hin, dass neben dem Hörorgan auch die Verarbeitung und Vernetzung im Gehirn eine wichtige Rolle spielen. Die SOUND Study untersucht, wie sich diese Erkenntnisse für individuellere Prognosen nutzen lassen. Das erwartet Sie Im Rahmen der SOUND Study untersuchen Sie die zentralen Hörbahnen mithilfe neuester bildgebender Verfahren. items.title: Doktorand AI-Aided Product Development - Prozessintelligenz und Wissensmanagement (w/m/d)
items.desc: Stellenbezeichnung: Doktorand AI-Aided Product Development - Prozessintelligenz und Wissensmanagement (w/m/d) Startdatum der Ausschreibung: 05.10.26 Zu Besetzen Ab 01.02.2027 Dienstort Stuttgart – mit Reisebereitschaft nach München Dein Arbeitsumfeld Wir bei MAN Truck & Bus sind Teil eines starken internationalen Teams und einer der führenden europäischen Nutzfahrzeughersteller und Anbieter von Transportlösungen. Zusammen mit den Marken Scania, Volkswagen Truck & Bus und International gehören wir zur TRATON GROUP. Als Teil dieses Verbundes stehen wir vor großen Herausforderungen: Unsere Fahrzeuge werden immer autonomer und vernetzter, um emissionsärmer unterwegs zu sein. Dafür arbeiten wir an nachhaltigen Lösungen. Eine Karriere bei MAN Truck & Bus bietet unzählige Möglichkeiten, sich an diesem Wandel zu beteiligen. Der Kunde an erster Stelle, Respekt, Teamgeist, Verantwortung und Verschwendung vermeiden – das sind unsere Unternehmenswerte, die wir bei MAN leben. Zieh mit uns an einem Strang. Als Teil unseres globalen Teams von über 36.000 Mitarbeitenden wirst du Zukunftsvisionen mit uns gemeinsam Wirklichkeit werden lassen. Wir sehen Individualität unserer Mitarbeitenden als Stärke an und freuen uns über vielfältige Bewerbungen von Personen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen. Falls du während deiner Bewerbung Unterstützung benötigst, melde dich bitte bei uns. Dein Heimatbereich „Engineering Strategy“ verantwortet die strategische Weiterentwicklung unserer Forschung und Entwicklung: von der Entwicklungsstrategie über die Prozess- und Methodenlandschaft bis hin zur Frage, wie Künstliche Intelligenz in der Nutzfahrzeugentwicklung echten Mehrwert schafft. KI-Werkzeuge entwickeln sich derzeit schneller, als Entwicklungsorganisationen sie sinnvoll integrieren können. Der limitierende Faktor ist dabei selten das Modell, sondern die Qualität, Struktur und Zugänglichkeit der zugrundeliegenden Prozess-, Wissens- und Datenbasis. Genau hier setzt deine Promotion an: Du entwickelst eine methodische Vorgehensweise, mit der sich KI-Tools für die Entwicklung systematisch identifizieren, bewerten und einführen lassen. Die Forschungsarbeit entwickelt ein erweiterbares AI-Aided Process Tool auf Basis eines maschinen- und menschenlesbaren Metamodells sowie ein Verfahren zur systematischen Verknüpfung von Prozessanforderungen und KI-Fähigkeiten. Ziel ist die kontinuierliche Optimierung unserer Prozesslandschaft durch den zielgerichteten Einsatz von KI. Deine Ergebnisse validierst du an realen Anwendungsfällen – von der KI-gestützten, kontextspezifischen Wissensbereitstellung für Mitarbeitende bis zur datenbasierten Identifikation von Optimierungspotenzialen. Du arbeitest eng mit Prozessverantwortlichen, IT und Engineering Fachbereichen zusammen, um praxisnahe Anforderungen in wissenschaftliche Fragestellungen zu überführen und umgekehrt Forschungsergebnisse in die industrielle Anwendung zu bringen. Bei dieser Forschungsarbeit handelt es sich um ein Kooperationsprojekt mit der Universität Stuttgart, an der auch deine Promotion erfolgt. Dein Dienstort ist Stuttgart; für die Zusammenarbeit mit den Entwicklungsbereichen und für Prozessaufnahmen vor Ort bringst du Reisebereitschaft an unseren Entwicklungsstandort München mit. Die Anstellung erfolgt als wissenschaftliche(r) Mitarbeiter(in) mit der Möglichkeit zur Promotion; die Projektlaufzeit beträgt 36 Monate. Deine Aufgaben Analyse bestehender Entwicklungsprozesse und ihrer Dokumentation sowie Identifikation systematischer Lücken Strukturierung, Harmonisierung und Überführung heterogener Prozess- und Wissensdokumentationen in das entwickelte Metamodell sowie Aufbau einer maschinenlesbaren Wissensbasis Entwicklung eines Metamodells und eines standardisierten Erhebungsschemas für maschinen- und menschenlesbare Prozess- und Wissensdokumentation Skalierte Erhebung und Aufbau einer strukturierten Prozesswissensbasis inklusive Aufwandsmessung Entwicklung einer Fähigkeits-Taxonomie der KI-Landschaft und eines reproduzierbaren Verfahrens zur Auswahl und Bewertung von KI-Tools Konzeption, Umsetzung und kontrollierte Evaluation von Demonstratoren (KI-gestützter Wissenszugang, Prozessoptimierung) Dokumentation, Evaluierung und Ergebnisse sowie Ableitung einer Nutzen-Aufwand-Betrachtung Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse in internationalen Zeitschriften und entsprechenden Konferenzen Deine Qualifikationen Guter Masterabschluss, der zur Promotion berechtigt, in Maschinenbau, Data Science, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Informatik, Wirtschaftsinformatik oder verwandten Studiengängen Gute Sprachkenntnisse in Deutsch und Englisch Interesse am wissenschaftlichen Arbeiten mit hohem Anwendungsbezug Erfahrung im Bereich Produktentwicklung, Prozessmodellierung (z. B. BPMN) oder Wissensmanagement Kenntnisse im Bereich Künstliche Intelligenz, insbesondere Large Language Models, RAG- oder Knowledge-Graph-Ansätze Erfahrung mit empirischen Methoden (Interviews, Beobachtung, qualitative Inhaltsanalyse, Nutzerstudien) von Vorteil Programmierkenntnisse in Python Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsstärke und Freude an der Arbeit mit unterschiedlichen Fachbereichen Selbstständige, strukturierte Arbeitsweise sowie Reisebereitschaft nach München Dein Ansprechpartner Dr.-Ing. Florian Reichelt, Engineering Strategy, MAN Truck & Bus SE Luca Möderl, Engineering Strategy, MAN Truck & Bus SE

items.title: Doktorand i numerisk simulering av turbulent värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor
items.desc: Om arbetsplatsen Doktoranden kommer att vara anställd vid Institutionen för Energivetenskaper vid Lunds tekniska högskola (LTH), Lunds universitet, och tillhöra avdelningen för värmeöverföring. Forskningsmiljön bedriver forskning inom strömningsmekanik, värmeöverföring och beräkningsströmningsmekanik, med särskilt fokus på numerisk modellering och simulering av turbulenta strömmar och tekniska tillämpningar. Doktoranden kommer att arbeta i en forskningsmiljö som förenar grundforskning med tillämpningar av direkt relevans för industrin. Projektet genomförs i nära samarbete med Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB och RISE. Det ger möjlighet att arbeta i gränslandet mellan grundforskning, avancerade numeriska metoder och industriellt relevanta problem. Doktoranden får tillgång till expertis inom beräkningsströmningsmekanik (CFD), turbulens, värmeöverföring, numeriska metoder och högprestandaberäkningar. Arbetet innebär omfattande användning av högprestandaberäkningsresurser, både GPU- och CPU-baserade. Att vara doktorand Som doktorand är du både antagen som student och anställd vid Lunds universitet. Som doktorand får du vetenskaplig skolning. Du tränas i att tänka kritiskt och analytiskt, lösa problem självständigt med lämpliga metoder och utveckla en medvetenhet om forskningsetik. Du får också möjlighet att arbeta i projekt och utveckla ditt ledarskap och din pedagogiska förmåga. Under hela utbildningen får du handledning. Doktorandutbildningen avslutas med en avhandling och doktorsexamen. Ämnes- och projektbeskrivning Ytråhet påverkar turbulent strömning, väggfriktion och värmeöverföring i många tekniska system. Det är viktigt att förstå och kunna förutsäga dessa effekter inom en rad tillämpningar, bland annat energisystem, termisk hantering och transporter. Trots den praktiska betydelsen är det fortfarande en utmaning att förutsäga turbulent värmeöverföring över realistiska skrovliga ytor med god noggrannhet, särskilt när arbetsmediets egenskaper och de relativa tjocklekarna hos impuls- och värmegränsskikten varierar. Målet med doktorandprojektet är att fördjupa den fysikaliska förståelsen av samspelet mellan ytråhet, turbulens och värmeöverföring samt omsätta förståelsen i förbättrade tekniska modeller. Forskningen kommer främst att använda högupplösta numeriska simuleringar, däribland direkt numerisk simulering (DNS) och storvirvelsimulering (LES). Olika CFD-program kommer att användas beroende på problem och önskad noggrannhet, bland annat OpenFOAM, CaNS och nekRS. Simuleringarna kommer i stor utsträckning att använda moderna högprestandaberäkningsresurser med både GPU:er och CPU:er. Projektet undersöker hur ytråhet påverkar turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring för olika fluider och termiska förhållanden. Särskild uppmärksamhet ägnas åt samspelet mellan råhetsgeometri, turbulenta strukturer samt impuls- och värmegränsskikt, även när de termiska gränsskiktens och impulsgränsskiktens relativa tjocklek skiljer sig åt. Data från de högupplösta simuleringarna ska användas för att identifiera relevanta fysikaliska mekanismer och skalningssamband samt stödja utvecklingen av reducerade modeller och tekniska modeller för värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor. Det omfattar förbättrade modeller och korrelationer som lämpar sig för Reynoldsmedelvärdesbaserade Navier–Stokes-simuleringar (RANS). Det övergripande målet är att knyta samman grundläggande turbulensfysik, högupplösta numeriska simuleringar och beräkningsmodeller som kan användas vid teknisk konstruktion. Projektet genomförs i nära samarbete med Siemens Energy AB, Ericsson AB, TRATON AB och RISE. Samarbetet ger möjligheter till vetenskapligt utbyte och kontakt med forskare och ingenjörer som arbetar med industriella tillämpningar av turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring. Arbetsuppgifter Du ägnar huvuddelen av din arbetstid åt forskarutbildningen, som omfattar deltagande i forskningsprojekt samt forskarutbildningskurser, seminarier och vetenskapliga konferenser. En central del av arbetet är att genomföra och analysera högupplösta numeriska simuleringar av turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor. Du använder CFD- och högprestandaberäkningsramverk, exempelvis OpenFOAM, CaNS och nekRS, på CPU- och GPU-baserade system. Du ska ha erfarenhet av jämförbara simuleringsverktyg och högprestandaberäkningssystem (HPC); erfarenhet av de specifika program som används i projektet är meriterande. Arbetsuppgifterna omfattar Genomföra DNS- och LES-simuleringar av turbulent strömning och värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor med OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS eller jämförbara ramverk för CFD och vetenskapliga beräkningar. Förbereda, köra, validera och analysera simuleringar på GPU- och CPU-baserade högprestandaberäkningssystem. Undersöka hur ytråhetens geometri och egenskaper påverkar turbulent impuls- och värmeöverföring. Undersöka effekterna av fluidernas egenskaper och termiska förhållanden, inklusive olika förhållanden mellan impuls- och värmegränsskiktens tjocklek. Bearbeta, analysera och visualisera stora datamängder, identifiera fysikaliska mekanismer och ta fram skalningssamband utifrån DNS- och LES-data. Utveckla reducerade modeller, korrelationer och förbättrade RANS-modeller för turbulent värmeöverföring över skrovliga ytor. Bedöma och validera de utvecklade modellerna mot högupplösta numeriska data och, när sådana finns, experimentella data. Samarbeta med forskare vid Lunds universitet och med projektets industri- och forskningspartner. Presentera forskningsresultat vid projektmöten, vetenskapliga konferenser och internationella workshoppar. Skriva vetenskapliga artiklar för publicering i internationella sakkunniggranskade tidskrifter och bidra till doktorsavhandlingen. Arbetet kan innebära resor inom Sverige och internationellt för projektmöten, besök hos forsknings- och industripartner, konferenser och forskningssamarbeten. Arbetsuppgifterna kan även omfatta undervisning och annat institutionsarbete, dock högst 20% av arbetstiden. Behörighetskrav En sökande uppfyller de allmänna behörighetskraven till utbildning på forskarnivå om personen: har avlagt examen på avancerad nivå, eller har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller på något annat sätt, i Sverige eller utomlands, har förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper. Särskilda krav För att kunna genomföra den aktuella forskarutbildningen krävs även följande: Masterexamen eller motsvarande inom maskinteknik, teknisk fysik, flygteknik, energiteknik, tillämpad matematik, beräkningsvetenskap eller ett annat ämne som är relevant för projektet. Goda kunskaper i strömningsmekanik, CFD och turbulenta strömmar samt relevanta kunskaper i värmeöverföring. Ett omfattande forskningsprojekt eller examensarbete inom CFD, turbulens, värmeöverföring eller ett närliggande område. Dokumenterad förmåga att självständigt sätta upp, genomföra, felsöka, validera och analysera numeriska simuleringar. Förmågan ska styrkas genom forskningserfarenhet och inte enbart genom kursarbete. Erfarenhet av vetenskaplig programmering i ett relevant språk, till exempel C/C++, Fortran och Python eller Matlab. Praktisk erfarenhet av att köra beräkningssimuleringar på HPC-system. Förmåga att planera och genomföra forskningsuppgifter med begränsad löpande handledning, kritiskt analysera resultat och tydligt kommunicera slutsatser. Mycket goda kunskaper i engelska, både i tal och skrift. Meriterande kvalifikationer Följande kvalifikationer är meriterande för den aktuella forskarutbildningen: Erfarenhet av DNS eller LES, väggbegränsad turbulens, turbulent värmeöverföring, ytråhet eller konvektiv värmeöverföring. Erfarenhet av CFD eller ett ramverk för högupplösta simuleringar, till exempel OpenFOAM, CaNS, nekRS eller motsvarande forskningskod. Erfarenhet av parallellberäkningar eller GPU-accelererade vetenskapliga beräkningar. Kunskaper i RANS, väggmodellering eller termisk turbulensmodellering. Forskningserfarenhet utöver masterexamensarbetet, till exempel som forskningsassistent eller forskningsingenjör. Erfarenhet av att presentera eller publicera forskningsresultat eller av att samarbeta med industrin. Du behöver inte ha erfarenhet av alla program som används i projektet. Däremot ska du ha visat att du självständigt kan bedriva beräkningsforskning med ett jämförbart ramverk för CFD eller vetenskapliga beräkningar. Du förväntas kunna bidra från ett tidigt skede med stöd av tidigare erfarenhet av numeriska simuleringar och HPC. Vi erbjuder Lunds universitet är en statlig myndighet. Som anställd får du särskilda förmåner, generös semester och fördelaktiga tjänstepensionsvillkor. Läs mer om att arbeta på Lunds universitet. Anställningsvillkor Anställningen är en tidsbegränsad heltidsanställning med start så snart som möjligt. Forskarutbildningen vid LTH omfattar fyra års heltidsstudier. Om du har undervisning eller andra arbetsuppgifter vid institutionen förlängs anställningen i motsvarande omfattning. Doktorandanställningar regleras i högskoleförordningen (1993:100), 5 kap. 1–7 . Läs mer om att vara anställd som doktorand på Lunds universitet. Övrigt Doktoranden förväntas ha regelbunden kontakt med projektets akademiska partner och industripartner. Tjänsten kan därför omfatta besök hos partnerorganisationer och deltagande i projektmöten, workshoppar och konferenser i Sverige och utomlands. Ansökan Ansökan ska vara skriven på engelska och innehålla: CV och personligt brev där du beskriver varför du söker forskarutbildningen och det aktuella forskningsprojektet samt hur din utbildningsbakgrund, forskningserfarenhet och dina intressen anknyter till CFD, turbulens och värmeöverföring. Kopior av utfärdade studieintyg och/eller examensbevis. Handlingarna ska styrka att du uppfyller de allmänna och särskilda behörighetskraven till forskarutbildningen och har de ämneskunskaper som krävs för doktorandprojektet. Studieutdrag med genomförda kurser och betyg. En kopia av masterexamensarbetet eller, om arbetet inte är färdigt, en sammanfattning av det pågående arbetet och beräknat datum för färdigställande. Övriga handlingar som du vill åberopa, till exempel vetenskapliga publikationer, tekniska rapporter, konferensbidrag, rekommendationsbrev eller annat material som visar relevant forskningserfarenhet. Kontaktuppgifter till minst två referenspersoner som kan kontaktas under rekryteringsprocessen. Välkommen med din ansökan.

items.desc: An der Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Institut für Geographie ist folgende Stelle zu besetzen: Wissenschaftliche/-r Mitarbeiter/-in (Doktorand/-in) (m/w/d/x) in der Geographie – Erfassung sozioökonomischer Auswirkungen von Klimaextremen Stellenausschreibung vom 26.10.2026 Kennziffer 147/2026 Vergütung Entgeltgruppe 13 TV-L Befristung 3 Jahre, Qualifizierungsplanung Umfang 75 % einer Vollbeschäftigung, ein geringerer Zeitumfang ist möglich Beginn März 2027 Die 1409 gegründete Universität Leipzig gehört zu den großen, forschungsstarken und medizinführenden Universitäten in Deutschland. Mit ihren rund 30.000 Studierenden und mehr als 5.000 Beschäftigten in 14 Fakultäten prägt sie das Leben in der pulsierenden und weltoffenen Stadt Leipzig. Die Universität Leipzig bietet ein dynamisches und international geprägtes Arbeitsumfeld sowie attraktive und vielfältige Arbeitsmöglichkeiten in Forschung, Lehre, Transfer, Infrastruktur und Verwaltung. Die Promotionsstelle ist Teil des Projekts „CASCADE - Cascading impacts of climate extremes: new perspectives for interlinking Earth System Sciences in Leipzig“ zu zusammengesetzten und kaskadierenden Auswirkungen von Klimaextremen. CASCADE untersucht, wie Hochwasser und Dürren Gesellschaft und Umwelt beeinflussen, und verbindet großskalige Datenanalysen mit einer systemischen Perspektive auf Mensch-Umwelt-Wechselwirkungen. Unser Wissen über die Auswirkungen von Klimaextremen ist nur so gut wie die Daten, die sie erfassen. Ziel des Promotionsprojekts ist es, Verzerrungen (Biases) in Impact-Datenbanken und in der Forschung zu Klimafolgen aufzudecken und ein umfassenderes Bild der Auswirkungen von Hochwasser und Dürren auf globaler Ebene zu schaffen. Dazu wird die/der Promovierende bestehende Datenbanken (z. B. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, EM-DAT) in einem gemeinsamen Ereignis-, Impact- und Raumbezug verknüpfen und harmonisieren sowie an der Entwicklung eines mehrsprachigen, nachrichtenbasierten Impact-Datensatzes mitwirken, der Lücken in bestehenden Quellen schließen soll. Mit unabhängigen globalen Gefahren- und Expositionsdaten als Referenz analysiert das Projekt, wo und für welche Auswirkungen die Quellen übereinstimmen, wie sich die berichteten Schadensausmaße unterscheiden und wie die Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass ein Ereignis überhaupt erfasst wird, von der Intensität der Gefahr, der Exposition, den sozioökonomischen Bedingungen, der Sprache und der Medienpräsenz abhängt. Das Projekt profitiert von einer engen Zusammenarbeit mit dem Helmholtz-Zentrum für Umweltforschung (UFZ). Sie arbeiten in einem interdisziplinären Team an der Schnittstelle von Geographie, Klimarisikoforschung und Data Science. Das sind Ihre Aufgaben Verknüpfung und Harmonisierung textbasierter und etablierter Impact-Datenbanken (z. B. ROUGE, Wikimpacts, nachrichtenbasierte Daten, EM-DAT) in einem gemeinsamen globalen Ereignis-, Impact- und Raumbezug Vergleichende Analyse, wo, wann und für welche Impact-Arten die Datensätze übereinstimmen oder voneinander abweichen, mit globalen Gefahren- und Expositionsdaten als unabhängiger Referenz Analyse der geographischen, sozioökonomischen und sprachlichen Faktoren, die die Sichtbarkeit von Auswirkungen in verschiedenen Datenquellen bestimmen Entwicklung eines kombinierten, verzerrungsbewussten globalen Bildes der Auswirkungen von Hochwasser und Dürren Mitwirkung an der Entwicklung und Validierung eines mehrsprachigen, nachrichtenbasierten Impact-Datensatzes mithilfe von Natural Language Processing (NLP) und großen Sprachmodellen (LLMs) Veröffentlichung der Ergebnisse in internationalen begutachteten Fachzeitschriften, Präsentation auf wissenschaftlichen Konferenzen sowie offene Bereitstellung von Code und Daten Das bringen Sie mit abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (z. B. Master) oder gleichwertiger Abschluss in Geographie, Computational Social Sciences, Digital Humanities, Umwelt- oder Erdsystemwissenschaften, Katastrophenrisikoforschung oder einem eng verwandten Fach Erfahrung in der Datenanalyse, insbesondere in der Zusammenführung und Harmonisierung heterogener Datensätze erforderlich, z. B. nachgewiesen durch die Masterarbeit, Forschungsprojekte oder Berufserfahrung ausgezeichnete Programmierkenntnisse erforderlich (z. B. Python, R) Erfahrung in der Analyse räumlicher Daten erforderlich, z. B. räumliche Statistik Interesse an Klimarisiko-, Naturgefahren- oder Katastrophenforschung, z. B. nachgewiesen durch Lehrveranstaltungen oder die Masterarbeit sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift erforderlich (mindestens Sprachniveau B2) Erfahrung mit oder nachweisbares Interesse an Natural Language Processing (NLP) oder großen Sprachmodellen wünschenswert, z. B. durch Lehrveranstaltungen oder Projekte Das bieten wir Ihnen eine abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit mit hoher Eigenverantwortung im dynamischen Umfeld einer großen Universität Zusammenarbeit in einem freundlichen, unterstützenden und motivierten Team flexible Arbeitszeiten und Mobile Arbeit zur besseren Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Privatleben eine zielgerichtete Personalentwicklung in allen Phasen Ihres Berufslebens mit Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten vielfältige Angebote des betrieblichen Gesundheitsmanagements eine Vergütung gemäß Tarifvertrag der Länder inklusive Jahressonderzahlung und betrieblicher Altersvorsorge ein vergünstigtes Personennahverkehrsticket (z. B. das Deutschlandticket als Jobticket) umfangreiche Verpflegung in den Mensen und Cafeterien des Studentenwerks Leipzig Forschung, Lehre, Transfer, Infrastruktur und Verwaltung brauchen Perspektivenvielfalt. Die Universität setzt sich deshalb für Diversität und Chancengerechtigkeit ein. Ihre Bewerbung ist bei uns willkommen, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Nationalität, Religion, kultureller und sozialer Herkunft, Alter oder sexueller Orientierung. Die Universität strebt eine Erhöhung des Anteils von Frauen in verantwortlicher Position an und bittet deshalb qualifizierte Frauen ausdrücklich um ihre Bewerbung. items.title: CIFRE - Panel Level Package (PLP) development : interfaces characterization - H/F
items.desc: Chez STMicroelectronics, nous sommes convaincus que la technologie est un moteur d’innovation et a un impact positif pour les entreprises, les personnes et la société. En tant qu’acteur mondial des semiconducteurs, nos technologies de pointe et nos composants électroniques sont invisibles mais au cœur du monde d’aujourd’hui. Rejoindre ST, c’est intégrer une entreprise internationale riche de plus de 115 nationalités, présente dans 40 pays, et rassemblant plus de 50 000 talents passionnés et engagés, tous unis par la volonté de créer et d’inventer la technologie de demain. Innover demande bien plus que des compétences techniques : cela nécessite des personnes inspirantes, qui savent collaborer avec respect et enthousiasme. Des collaborateurs animés par la passion, prêts à remettre en question le statu quo, à faire avancer l’innovation et à révéler leur plein potentiel. Venez vivre cette aventure avec nous et contribuez à construire un futur plus intelligent et plus durable, en alliant responsabilité et innovation. Notre technologie commence avec vous. A propos de vos missions En microélectronique, la technologie Panel-Level Packaging (PLP) repose sur la réalisation d'empilements complexes associant différentes couches fonctionnelles, notamment organiques, métalliques et d'encapsulation. La fiabilité de ces architectures dépend non seulement des propriétés de chaque matériau, mais également de la qualité des interfaces qui les séparent. Celle-ci dépend des choix réalisés lors de la fabrication : température de dépôt, préparation de surface, rugosité des couches, utilisation de promoteurs d’adhérence… Néanmoins, à ce jour, les mécanismes physiques et mécaniques à l'origine de l'adhérence entre ces matériaux restent à préciser, tout comme leur évolution sous sollicitation mécanique ou thermomécanique. De fait, des défauts d'interface, une adhérence insuffisante ou l'apparition de contraintes locales sont autant de paramètres pouvant favoriser l'amorçage et la propagation de délaminations, susceptibles de compromettre l'intégrité de l'empilement. Une meilleure compréhension des relations entre les caractéristiques des interfaces, les propriétés mécaniques des couches et les mécanismes d'endommagement apparaît donc essentielle pour fiabiliser les procédés et orienter la conception des empilements. Cette thèse vise à développer une approche expérimentale et numérique permettant de caractériser les interfaces des empilements PLP, de comprendre leur comportement mécanique et d'identifier les paramètres gouvernant leur tenue et leur endommagement. Il s'agira notamment de dépasser la seule mesure de l'adhérence pour étudier le rôle de la morphologie des interfaces, des propriétés mécaniques locales et des mécanismes de déformation et de rupture dans la réponse globale de l'empilement. Une première partie portera sur la caractérisation des interfaces et de leur état initial, notamment par tomographie aux rayons X, Microscopie Électronique à Balayage (MEB) et, lorsque cela sera pertinent, microscopie à force atomique (AFM). Une attention particulière sera accordée à la morphologie des interfaces, à la présence de défauts et à l'influence des traitements de surface. Une seconde partie sera consacrée au développement et à l'adaptation d'essais mécaniques permettant de solliciter spécifiquement les interfaces. Parmi les essais envisagés, les essais DBC (Double Cantilever Beam) et les essais de flexion 4 points sur éprouvette entaillée semblent être particulièrement adaptés. Le couplage des sollicitations mécaniques à des observations in situ sous MEB ou tomographe permettra de relier les réponses mécaniques mesurées aux mécanismes d'endommagement observés. Une approche multi-échelle sera développée afin de relier les propriétés mécaniques des constituants au comportement des interfaces. L'indentation instrumentée pourra être utilisée pour caractériser localement les propriétés mécaniques des couches, en tenant compte des effets de l'épaisseur, du substrat et de la proximité des interfaces. Grâce à cette technique il est également envisagé d’estimer l’adhérence et la résistance à la délamination par la technique d’indentation par supercouche (superlayer indentation technique). Enfin, la confrontation des caractérisations structurales et des essais mécaniques permettra d'établir des relations entre les paramètres de procédé, l'état initial des interfaces, les modes de rupture et la résistance à la délamination. Les résultats attendus contribueront à établir une méthodologie expérimentale de caractérisation de la tenue des interfaces et à proposer des critères permettant d'orienter le choix des traitements de surface et des architectures multicouches. Ce sujet de thèse est le fruit d’une collaboration entre le laboratoire de mécanique Gabriel Lamé et STMicroelectronics et pourra bénéficier des outils expérimentaux et des compétences de deux plateformes de l’Université de Tours : le CERMEL et le CERTeM. A propos de vous Bac +5 en Physique/Matériaux / chimie, connaissance des procédés de la microélectronique, connaissance en physique des semi-conducteurs, rigueur scientifique, autonomie, persévérance. ST est fière d’être certifiée parmi les 17 entreprises mondiales « Global Top Employers 2025 » et d’être la première et unique entreprise de semi-conducteurs à recevoir cette distinction. ST a été distinguée dans ce classement grâce à sa démarche d’amélioration continue, se démarquant notamment par son engagement en matière d’éthique et d’intégrité, de sens et de valeurs, d’organisation et de gestion du changement, ainsi que par sa stratégie commerciale et ses performances. En France, ST a également obtenu la labélisation Happy Trainee 2025. Nous cultivons un environnement de travail inclusif et diversifié, où la discrimination n’a pas sa place. Notre ambition est de recruter et de fidéliser des talents reflétant la richesse des sociétés dans lesquelles nous évoluons. Nous nous engageons à l’équité dans le développement des carrières, les opportunités professionnelles et la rémunération. Chez ST, nous encourageons les candidats qui ne remplissent pas forcément tous les critères à postuler, car nous croyons en la richesse des parcours variés et offrons de réelles opportunités d’apprentissage et d’évolution. La diversité, l’équité et l’inclusion sont des valeurs fondamentales qui façonnent notre culture d’entreprise. Pour découvrir toutes nos opportunités, rendez-vous sur st.com/careers.

items.title: Thèse "Sonde micro-endoscopique pour l’histologie Raman stimulée" (H/F)
items.desc: Nouveau Physique des lasers, atomes et molécules VILLENEUVE D ASCQ Nord CDD Doctorant 36 mois BAC+5 This offer is available in English version Cette offre est ouverte aux personnes disposant d’un titre leur reconnaissant la qualité de travailleur handicapé ou travailleuse handicapée. L'offre en un coup d'oeil L'unité Physique des lasers, atomes et molécules Type de Contrat CDD Doctorant Temps de Travail Complet Lieu de Travail 59658 VILLENEUVE D ASCQ Durée du contrat 36 mois Date d'Embauche 01/01/2027 Rémuneration La rémunération est d'un minimum de 2300,00 € mensuel Postuler Date limite de candidature : lundi 16 novembre 2026 23:59 Description du Poste Sujet De Thèse Sonde micro-endoscopique pour l’histologie Raman stimulée Votre Environnement de Travail Les techniques d'endoscopie sont essentielles pour le diagnostic, la stadification et le traitement des cancers épithéliaux. Pour de nombreux cancers, elles sont souvent le seul moyen d'accéder directement au site tumoral. Cependant, les tissus précancéreux présentent parfois des modifications subtiles indétectables visuellement. La détection endoscopique du cancer souffre de deux principales faiblesses : (1) la sensibilité limitée des marqueurs fluorescents couramment utilisés et (2) le besoin de biopsies et d'analyses histologiques, qui retardent la chirurgie et la prise de décisions. Le projet de thèse vise à développer une sonde optique miniature pour l'histologie Raman stimulée capable de fournir des images tissulaires en temps réel, en concordance étroite avec l'histologie classique (coloration H&E). Cette approche ambitionne de permettre une détection précoce et moins invasive des cancers gastro-entérologiques, ainsi que d'explorer son potentiel pour la détection des cancers urologiques et l'évaluation peropératoire des marges tumorales. Nous proposons une approche novatrice combinant la microscopie Raman stimulée (SRS), des fibres à cœur creux de dernière génération et avec les technologies les plus avancées d'assemblage de sondes miniatures micro-endoscopiques fibrées. L'objectif est de développer une sonde endoscopique SRS permettant de réaliser une histologie Raman stimulée en temps réel. Les développements viseront des applications en cancers gastro-entérologiques et urologiques, avec une validation sur des tissus biologiques pertinents en lien avec des partenaires cliniciens. La thèse se déroulera au laboratoire PhLAM de l'Université de Lille, sous la direction d'Alexandre Kudlinski, en étroite collaboration avec Hervé Rigneault (Institut Fresnel, Aix-Marseille Université) et la société Lightcore Technologies (basée à Lille et Marseille). Le sujet de thèse est à forte dominante expérimentale dans le domaine de l’optique, des fibres optiques et des lasers ultra-brefs. Des compétences en pilotage d’instruments, en électronique, en conception optique (notamment avec des logiciels tels que Zemax) et en traitement d’images seront appréciées. Le candidat devra manifester un réel intérêt pour l’optique expérimentale, faire preuve d’autonomie, d’initiative et d’une bonne capacité à résoudre des problèmes pratiques. items.title: PhD position
items.desc: PhD position (m/w/d) on the Natural ecology and evolution of C. elegans at Kiel University, Germany Well-motivated and highly-qualified students from all countries are welcome to apply. We are looking forward to your application for a PhD position to join the Schulenburg group in Kiel in the beautiful landscape of Northern Germany. Application deadline: 4 November 2026 . The PhD position is for 3,5 years with a possible extension for another 6 months. It is based in the Schulenburg group (https://evoecogen-kiel.de/). The PhD project aims at understanding how the model nematode C. elegans interacts with other organisms in its natural environment, ranging from the interaction with microbes up to predators and parasites. C. elegans is one of the best studied model organisms in the life sciences, yet there is still very little understanding of its natural ecology, and especially the interaction with other organisms, even though this natural context sets the stage for full appreciation of the nematode’s gene functions. Based on the observation of such interactions in nature, the project will then further study selected interaction types in the lab, taking advantage of the tools available for this model organism, thereby allowing us to generate new insights on the evolution as well as the genetic basis of ecologically relevant biotic interactions. The position will be integrated within the graduate school on Translational Evolutionary Research (https://transevo.de/), providing numerous opportunities for exchange with colleagues working on related topics. Necessary competences and qualifications: · Master of Science or equivalent · Master thesis or equivalent in the field of Evolutionary Biology or Genetics · Competences and experiences in experimental laboratory work with invertebrate animals · Knowledge in statistics · English language skills at level C1 Beneficial competences: · Competences and experience in experimental research with the nematode C. elegans · Competences and experience in performance of evolution experiments · Competences and experience in genome sequence data analysis · Experiences in the application of advanced statistics (multivariate statistics, GLMs) · Publication(s) from earlier research work For enquiries regarding the position and research topic please contact Prof. Dr. Hinrich Schulenburg: hschulenburg@zoologie.uni-kiel.de Applications should be sent by email as a single PDF to Hinrich Schulenburg (hschulenburg@zoologie.uni-kiel.de). Applications should include: (1) A letter of motivation (max. 2 pages, Arial 11, line spacing 1.15). In your motivation letter, please explain how your background fits the required profile and how your research interests align with the group research focus. (2) Curriculum vitae. (3) Master certificate (or current grades transcript in case of ongoing studies)

items.title: PhD position 6G resilience planning
items.desc: Join the Dutch 6G flagship project to help shape the future of communications. Job Description Join the frontier of innovation in 6G: the future of mobile networks technology! In the Netherlands, a unique alliance of 60 top-notch ICT companies, semiconductor firms, and research institutions has united to spearhead specific aspects of 6G: (1) software antennas, (2) AI-driven network software, and (3) groundbreaking 6G applications. Join us as a PhD student in this prestigious Future Network Services (FNS) flagship project, where research and entrepreneurial pursuits converge. With 6G expected to support mission-critical services, such as autonomous mobility, remote healthcare, and industrial automation, network operators must be able to anticipate, quantify, and mitigate risks arising from both internal and external factors. To address this need, through this PhD project, you will develop a risk profiling and resilience advisory system for 6G networks. This system will continuously compute a comprehensive risk profile for network infrastructure and operations, providing actionable recommendations for resilient network planning, evolution, and disaster recovery. You’ll be joining an internationally diverse and thriving team, providing ample opportunities for riveting sparring and knowledge sharing. Fostering a highly collaborative and friendly atmosphere, we will give you all the support you need to develop and grow. Moreover, as a valued member of the FNS consortium, you can collaborate with various partners in pursuit of integrating your AI/ML techniques into the various 6G PoCs and demos. Job requerements Become part of an expansive ecosystem shaping the development of 6G. You will benefit from training in 5G and beyond networks, AI, and software development. Plus, you will gain exclusive access to (1) a state-of-the-art testbed where theory meets real-world application, and (2) an ecosystem that cultivates entrepreneurial endeavours. Are you ready to challenge yourself? We're seeking candidates who have, or are about to receive, a Master-of-Science degree in a relevant computer science discipline and who like to combine theory with practice. Proficiency in English is essential, as you'll collaborate within a diverse, international community. For more details on our admission requirements, please visit https://www.tudelft.nl/onderwijs/opleidingen/phd/admission. We’ll evaluate based on your academic record, interviews, and possibly assignments. While a strong background in the field is crucial, what matters as well is your creative flair, motivation, and above all, your passion for comprehensive research! TU Delft (Delft University of Technology) Delft University of Technology is built on strong foundations. As creators of the world-famous Dutch waterworks and pioneers in biotech, TU Delft is a top international university combining science, engineering and design. It delivers world class results in education, research and innovation to address challenges in the areas of energy, climate, mobility, health and digital society. For generations, our engineers have proven to be entrepreneurial problem-solvers, both in business and in a social context. At TU Delft we embrace diversity as one of our core values and we actively engage to be a university where you feel at home and can flourish. We value different perspectives and qualities. We believe this makes our work more innovative, the TU Delft community more vibrant and the world more just. Together, we imagine, invent and create solutions using technology to have a positive impact on a global scale. That is why we invite you to apply. Your application will receive fair consideration. Challenge. Change. Impact! Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science The Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science (EEMCS) brings together three scientific disciplines. Combined, they reinforce each other and are the driving force behind the technology we all use in our daily lives. Technology such as the electricity grid, which our faculty is helping to make completely sustainable and future-proof. At the same time, we are developing the chips and sensors of the future, whilst also setting the foundations for the software technologies to run on this new generation of equipment – which of course includes AI. Meanwhile we are pushing the limits of applied mathematics, for example mapping out disease processes using single cell data, and using mathematics to simulate gigantic ash plumes after a volcanic eruption. In other words: there is plenty of room at the faculty for ground-breaking research. We educate innovative engineers and have excellent labs and facilities that underline our strong international position. In total, more than 1000 employees and 4,000 students work and study in this innovative environment. Click here to go to the website of the Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science. Conditions of employment Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met. Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%. As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills. The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged. Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit, Coming to Delft Service, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A Dual Career Programme is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands. Additional Information If you would like more information about this vacancy or the selection procedure, please contact prof.dr.ir. Fernando Kuipers, via f.a.kuipers@tudelft.nl. Application procedure Are you interested in this vacancy? Please apply no later than 1 Nov 2026 via the application button and upload the following documents: CV Motivational letter Copies of your BSc and MSc degrees and transcripts. You can address your application to prof.dr.ir. Fernando Kuipers. Applications will be evaluated as they come in,so please apply as soon as possible. Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements. Please note: You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post. As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about knowledge security. Please do not contact us for unsolicited services. Recruitmentcode 6Gflagship
