items.desc: Mise en ligne le 2026-10-27 Type de contrat : Thèse Niveau de formation : BAC +8 Expérience : Débutant Spécialité(s) : Ingénierie / Expertise / Recherche Pays / Région : France / Ile-de-France Département : Seine et Marne (77) Ville : Moret-sur-Loing Description de l'offre EDF R&D, avec ses 2000 chercheurs, a pour missions principales de contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance des unités opérationnelles du groupe EDF, d'identifier et de préparer les relais de croissance à moyen et long termes. EDF R&D met en œuvre une politique volontariste de partenariat en France et à l’international notamment dans les pays où le Groupe est présent. Vous souhaitez associer mécanique des matériaux, simulation numérique et intelligence artificielle pour répondre à des enjeux industriels ? -> Rejoignez EDF Recherche et Développement dans le cadre d’une thèse CIFRE consacrée à la réduction de modèle par apprentissage profond pour les calculs en plasticité cristalline. La poursuite de l’exploitation des centrales nucléaires au-delà de 60 ans nécessite des outils avancés pour justifier la tenue mécanique des composants. Pour les matériaux métalliques, leur comportement dépend notamment de la microstructure, c’est-à-dire de l’organisation des grains qui les constituent. Les simulations en plasticité cristalline permettent de représenter ces grains et leurs interactions pour mieux comprendre les déformations et les mécanismes de rupture. Elles restent toutefois coûteuses en temps de calcul, ce qui limite l’étude de microstructures et de sollicitations variées. L’objectif de cette thèse est de développer des modèles réduits fondés sur l’apprentissage profond pour accélérer ces simulations, tout en conservant une précision adaptée aux grandeurs étudiées et en respectant les lois physiques. Vos principales missions seront les suivantes : Étudier les méthodes de réduction de modèle et d’apprentissage profond adaptées à la plasticité cristalline. Constituer et exploiter des jeux de données issus de simulations de référence, couvrant différentes microstructures, propriétés des matériaux et sollicitations mécaniques. Développer des modèles capables de prédire les grandeurs mécaniques recherchées, en intégrant des contraintes physiques pour améliorer leur fiabilité. Comparer les approches en matière de précision, de coût de calcul et de capacité à traiter des configurations non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage. Appliquer les méthodes à des cas représentatifs des besoins industriels et valoriser les résultats dans des publications scientifiques. Deux pistes seront particulièrement explorées : des réseaux de neurones apprenant directement la relation entre les données du problème et la réponse mécanique, et des approches hybrides associant réduction par projection et corrections non linéaires apprises. Principalement numérique, cette thèse se situe à l’interface entre mécanique des matériaux, mathématiques appliquées et apprentissage automatique. Elle contribuera au développement d’outils plus rapides pour comprendre le comportement des matériaux à l’échelle de leur microstructure. Poste basé sur le site EDF Lab Les Renardières à Moret sur Loing (77). Profil souhaité Vous êtes titulaire, ou prochainement titulaire, d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master bac +5 en mécanique, mathématiques appliquées ou calcul scientifique. Vous disposez de bonnes bases en méthodes numériques et en programmation scientifique, notamment en Python. Vous avez un intérêt marqué pour la mécanique des matériaux et l’apprentissage automatique. Une première expérience en simulation mécanique ou en apprentissage profond serait appréciée. Qualités attendues pour mener les travaux de thèse : Curiosité scientifique, Rigueur, Autonomie, Goût du travail en équipe, Sens de l'organisation (la thèse étant un projet de 3 ans). Vous savez présenter clairement vos résultats et disposez d’un niveau d’anglais vous permettant de lire et de rédiger des publications scientifiques. Le dossier de candidature doit comporter : un curriculum vitae détaillé ; une lettre de motivation ; relevés de notes de votre diplôme de master ou d’ingénieur des années n, n-1 et n2 ; lettres de recommandations et les noms, les coordonnées d’au moins deux personnes pouvant être contactées pour recommandation. Les avantages : Vous pourrez bénéficier des activités sociales de l’entreprise. Vous aurez une prime d’intéressement et une couverture sociale. Vous serez remboursé(e) de 75% de votre abonnement de transport en Ile de France. La diversité alimente notre performance. Dans le groupe EDF, accueillir des personnes en situation de handicap fait partie de notre ADN. Notre objectif est d’ouvrir nos portes à toutes les compétences, toutes les énergies et toutes les personnalités sans exclusion. Le poste proposé est donc ouvert à toutes et à tous.

items.title: PhD Position in Neuroimaging, LLM, Genetics and Cross-species comparison
items.desc: Your function Do you enjoy working with complex neuroimaging data, large datasets and computational methods? Do you want to work at the intersection of genetics, neuroimaging, neuroscience, neurodiversity and cross-species analyses? We are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the Connectome Lab at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam The Connectome Lab at the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR), Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, is seeking a PhD candidate in Neuroimaging, Genetics and Cross-species comparison. The project aims to understand how variation in brain anatomy and connectivity contributes to the remarkable diversity of the human brain, and how these features relate to principles of brain evolution. We will combine large-scale human neuroimaging datasets with comparative datasets across species to investigate variation in brain structure, connectivity and functional organization. A central goal is to understand which aspects of brain organization are highly conserved, which show substantial variation between individuals, and which features may have emerged or expanded during human brain evolution. The project therefore brings together neuroimaging, connectomics, neurodiversity, comparative neuroscience and computational neuroscience . You will work with large structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets and develop and apply computational approaches to quantify variation in brain organization across individuals, populations and species. There is particularly attention for the use of LLM in data mining. You will be part of the computational neuroimaging Lab led by Prof. Martijn van den Heuvel and work in an interdisciplinary environment with researchers from neuroimaging, computational neuroscience, genetics, psychology, psychiatry and artificial intelligence. Your duties analyse large-scale structural MRI, diffusion MRI and resting-state fMRI datasets develop and apply pipelines for cortical reconstruction, tractography, functional connectivity and connectome analysis investigate individual variation and neurodiversity in brain structure and connectivity integrate genetics with neuroimaging perform comparative analyses of human and non-human brain organization in the context of brain evolution integrate findings across different neuroimaging datasets and imaging modalities develop and apply computational and statistical approaches for analysing brain networks contribute to reproducible and open neuroimaging workflows collaborate with researchers within the Connectome Lab, CNCR and international research networks present your findings at national and international scientific meetings write scientific manuscripts contribute to teaching activities where appropriate Your profile MSc degree in neuroscience, neuroimaging, genetics, biomedical engineering, physics, computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics, psychology, biology, or a related quantitative discipline. Hands-on experience with computational analysis is important. Ideally, you have experience with several of the following: structural MRI and cortical reconstruction, including FreeSurfer Genetics (GWAS) diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI), tractography and structural connectivity resting-state fMRI and functional connectivity analysis FSL and other commonly used neuroimaging software packages Experience with AI / LLM processing and quality control of neuroimaging datasets connectome and network neuroscience analyses Strong interest in and experience with scientific programming is essential. You should have experience with Python, MATLAB, R, Bash and/or comparable languages , and be comfortable working with computational analysis pipelines. Experience with one or more of the following would be an advantage: large-scale neuroimaging datasets such as UK Biobank, HCP or comparable resources comparative or cross-species neuroimaging brain atlases, surface-based analysis and registration machine learning or multivariate statistics high-performance computing version control and reproducible research workflows network science and computational modelling We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy working with complex data, think critically about methodology, and are motivated to develop strong computational and neuroimaging expertise. You should also: have a strong interest in neurodiversity and/or evolution be able to work independently while enjoying collaboration within a multidisciplinary team have good analytical and problem-solving skills have a good command of written and spoken English be motivated to learn new neuroimaging and computational techniques support open and reproducible science and be willing to share tools and data with the wider scientific community As a university, we strive for equal opportunities for all, recognising that diversity takes many forms. We believe that diversity in all its complexity is invaluable for the quality of our teaching, research and service. We are always looking for talent with diverse backgrounds and experiences. This also means that we are committed to creating an inclusive community so that we can use diversity as an asset. We realise that each individual brings a unique set of skills, expertise and mindset. Therefore we are happy to invite anyone who recognises themselves in the profile to apply, even if you do not meet all the requirements. What do we offer? A challenging position in a socially engaged organisation. At VU Amsterdam, you contribute to education, research and service for a better world. And that is valuable. So in return for your efforts, we offer you: a salary of minimum € 3.204,00 (PhD year 1) and maximum € 4.051 (PhD year 4) gross per month, on a full-time basis. This is based on UFO profile PhD candidate. a 4-year PhD position (initial 1-year contract, extended by 3 years following positive evaluation). We also offer you attractive fringe benefits and regulations. Some examples: a full-time 38-hour working week comes with a holiday leave entitlement of 232 hours per year. If you choose to work 40 hours, you have 96 extra holiday leave hours on an annual basis. For part-timers, this is calculated pro rata. 8% holiday allowance and 8.3% end-of-year bonus solid pension scheme (ABP) contribution to commuting expenses optional model for designing a personalized benefits package About us Research environment You will join the Connectome Lab of prof Van den Heuvel at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Our research focuses on understanding the architecture of the human brain and how its network organization relates to cognition, individual variation, brain disorders and evolution. You will work in a multidisciplinary team of PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers and students with backgrounds spanning neuroimaging, network neuroscience, genetics, artificial intelligence, computational neuroscience and psychology. The project is embedded within the Center for Neurogenomics and Cognitive Research (CNCR) , providing a highly interdisciplinary research environment and opportunities for collaboration within VU Amsterdam and with national and international research groups. Faculty of Science Working at the Faculty of Science means collaborating with students, lecturers and researchers who are focused on their field, yet have a broad view of the world. We are proud of a positive and inclusive workplace culture within the faculty, where we work together with great energy and a pragmatic attitude to tackle social challenges. At the Faculty of Science, scientists and students work on fundamental and complex societal issues for a sustainable, healthy and just future. From forest fires to big data, from obesity to malnutrition, from helium to the universe and from genetics to medicine: our education and research cover the full breadth of science, from molecules to mankind. Our academic education and research are highly experimental, technical and interdisciplinary in nature. That is why we collaborate extensively with leading scientific institutes and industry. The faculty has more than 8,000 students studying in one of the 39 programms and employs more than 1,400 staff across 10 scientific departments, making us one of the largest science faculties in the Netherlands. Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam stands for values-driven education and research. We are open-minded experts with the ability to think freely - a broader mind. Maintaining an entrepreneurial perspective and concentrating on diversity, significance and humanity, we work on sustainable solutions with social impact. By joining forces, across the boundaries of disciplines, we work towards a better world for people and planet. Together we create a safe and respectful working and study climate, and an inspiring environment for education and research. Learn more about our codes of conduct We are located on one physical campus, in the heart of Amsterdam's Zuidas business district, with excellent location and accessibility. Over 6,150 staff work at the VU and over 31,000 students attend academic education. Diversity Diversity is the driving force of VU Amsterdam. Therefore, we are always searching for people whose backgrounds and experience contribute to the diversity of the VU community. Interested Are you interested in this position and do you believe that your experience will contribute to the further development of our university? items.title: PhD Assessing Social Sustainability in Short Food Supply Chains
items.desc: Your job Are you interested in how law and policy can make agri-food systems fairer and more socially sustainable? Do you enjoy combining legal analysis with empirical research and engaging with farmers and other food-system actors? Join the Law Group at Wageningen University & Research as a PhD candidate in the Horizon Europe project SOCIAL AGRI. Social issues such as working conditions, farmer wellbeing, migrant worker integration and gender equality remain insufficiently captured in EU agricultural data and policy frameworks. This makes social costs and inequalities difficult to assess and address. SOCIAL AGRI aims to close this gap by collecting evidence on social conditions in agriculture, assessing their economic implications, and translating the findings into practical legal and policy instruments to make social sustainability a measurable and actionable dimension of European agricultural policy. You will contribute to this objective through an in-depth socio-legal study of short food supply chains (SFSCs) in the Netherlands. You will investigate how different SFSC models operate, how EU and Dutch law and policy shape their development, and how their organisation affects social sustainability, including working conditions, inclusion, community relationships and the distribution of value. Combining legal analysis with empirical research, you will use methods such as semi-structured interviews and stakeholder engagement activities, depending on the research design. You will identify legal and regulatory barriers to socially sustainable practices and explore how law and policy could better support their development. Working with other project partners, you will also contribute to developing and assessing SOCIAL AGRI’s social-sustainability indicators. Your findings will inform the project’s comparative analysis and help translate evidence on social performance into feasible policy recommendations and legal instruments, including potential regulatory approaches and contractual provisions. Your duties and responsibilities include: Develop and carry out a PhD research plan aligned with SOCIAL AGRI, with a clear focus on the Dutch short food supply chain case study and its contribution to the project’s evidence-to-policy pathway. Analyse relevant EU and Dutch legal and policy frameworks affecting short food supply chains and social sustainability in agriculture. Collect and analyse empirical evidence on the social conditions and relationships within Dutch short food supply chains, using appropriate qualitative methods. Contribute to the development actionable legal and policy instruments, including policy recommendations and model regulatory or contractual provisions, in collaboration with the wider consortium and relevant stakeholders, and of social-sustainability indicators. Contribute to comparative research, collaboration and dissemination within SOCIAL AGRI, interdisciplinary teamwork, project meetings, workshops and academic publications, while actively participating in the academic life of the Law Group. You will work here The research is embedded within the chair Law Group.The Law Group is a vibrant, dynamic, intercultural research community that is closely integrated into the Department of Social Sciences. It has a critical, socio-legal orientation, and excels in interdisciplinary research. It collaborates closely with a range of global partners. The focus of the group’s work is detailed in its most recent Chair Plan. You will work under the supervision of Dr Mirta Alessandrini, who is responsible for the SOCIAL AGRI Dutch case study, Dr Edwin Albals, and Dr Inga Winkler. You will also collaborate with colleagues and researchers from the wider SOCIAL AGRI consortium. Your qualities You are curious, analytically minded and motivated to conduct independent research on the legal and social dimensions of agri-food systems. You are comfortable working across disciplines, engaging with people outside academia, and managing your research independently. You have excellent organisational and time-management skills and can balance different tasks and priorities effectively. To meet the requirements of the role, you have: A completed Master level degree in law, agricultural economics, food studies, rural sociology, social sciences or a closely related discipline. Candidates from various disciplinary backgrounds are welcome to apply, provided they demonstrate affinity with the legal and policy dimensions of agri-food systems. A good understanding of the EU legal and policy context. Experience with qualitative research methods, such as semi-structured interviews or focus groups and with multi-stakeholder processes or clear evidence of the ability to develop these skills. Strong analytical, academic writing and communication skills, with fluency in both Dutch and English. The ability to work independently and collaborate effectively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment. For this position your command of the English and Dutch language is expected to be at C1 level. Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here. We offer Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment. A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include: Partially paid parental leave; working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance; there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee; a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%; excellent pension scheme. In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team. The gross salary for the first year is € 3.204,- per month rising to € 4.051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help. You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment. Coming from abroad Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees. Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account, dual career programs or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands. Important information For more information about the position, please contact Dr Mirta Alessandrini, Assistant Professor of Agri-Food Law, via mirta.alessandrini@wur.nl . Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Noorien Abbas, Corporate Recruiter, via recruitment.ssg@wur.nl . Ready to apply? You can apply directly using the apply button on the vacancy page on our website which will allow us to process your personal information with your approval. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered. To apply, please send the following documents: Complete and up-to-date curriculum vitae (max. 2 pages); Motivation letter (max. 1 page). A writing sample, such as a master’s thesis chapter or academic paper (max 3 pages). The maximum length of the documents must not exceed 6 pages . If it exceeds, applications will not be considered. Additional files such as grades and transcripts are not required during this stage and will not be considered. You can apply up to and including 17 November 2026. The first interviews will be scheduled soon after the closing date. Additional information form For this position, you must fill in a mandatory form which will allow us to have a comprehensive view of your qualifications and better assess your fit for it. You can access the form using the link below: PhD Assessing Social Sustainability in Short Food Supply Chains – Fill out form Your prompt response will ensure that your application continues to move forward in the evaluation process. We assure you that the information provided will be kept confidential and used solely for this application process. Welcome, safe, and valued Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization. We are The mission of Wageningen University & Research is “To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life”. Under the banner Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen University and the specialised research institutes of the Wageningen Research Foundation have joined forces in contributing to finding solutions to important questions in the domain of healthy food and living environment. With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. The unique Wageningen approach lies in its integrated approach to issues and the collaboration between different disciplines. Read the 5 reasons why your future colleagues enjoy working at WUR and watch the video below to get an idea of our green campus! We will recruit for the vacancy ourselves, so no employment agencies please. However, sharing in your network is appreciated.

items.title: PhD Research Fellow in Hydropower generators securing electricity supply and grid resilience
items.desc: University of South-Eastern Norway Kjølnes Ring 56, 3918 Porsgrunn Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel PhD Research Fellow in Hydropower generators securing electricity supply and grid resilience Type ansettelse Åremål, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk Søk senest mandag 9. november Welcome to USN The University of Southeastern Norway (USN) ranks as the country's fourth largest higher education institution. We are a vibrant community of approximately 18,000 students and 1,900 employees. Video: https://vimeo.com/898549899/60305e2540 About the position The Faculty of Technology, Natural Sciences and Maritime Sciences (TNM) has a vacancy for a temporary 100 % position as PhD Research Fellow in “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” from January 1st 2027. The position is a part of the FME SecurEL center, and it is funded by the Research Council of Norway and USN. The position is located at the Department of Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, and Cybernetics and reports to the Head of Department. The position will be working in the research group, “Electrical Power Systems” (EPS). The place of employment is Porsgrunn. The employment period will be four years full time, and there is a premise for employment that the PhD Research Fellow is enrolled in USN’s PhD-program in PhD in Technology within three months of accession in the position. The four-year full-time period will consist of 75 % research duties and 25 % teaching duties. About the PhD-project and SecurEL This PhD position “The role of hydropower generators in securing electricity supply and enhancing grid resilience” will be associated with Work Package 1 (WP1) on Security of Electricity Supply in SecurEL. The overall objective for the PhD work is to investigate the role of hydropower generators in managing the security of electricity supply in evolving regional distribution grids. The work of the PhD candidate will be integrated with the ongoing work being carried out by the research partners in WP1. In the initial phase, the supervisors, the candidate (based on the candidate's profile), and research partners in SecurEL will work together to identify the comprehensive research questions to be addressed to meet the overall objective of the PhD work. Some potential specific research objectives: Model the coordination and interactions between power producers and system operators (DSOs and TSO) in scenarios for the transition of distribution grids. Quantify the importance of hydropower production and its interoperability in managing security of supply and grid stability. Explore the interplay between different aspects of security of supply (energy availability, power capacity, reliability of supply and voltage quality), as well as power flow balancing, and dynamic system integration) in regional distribution grids. Investigate how generator characteristics such as capabilities for fault-ride through, island mode transition, and black start impact the vulnerability and resilience of the grid, in particular considering islanded grid operation. Develop vulnerability indicators related to power production and control for increasing situational awareness. Read more about the Centre and its research at the website https://www.securel.no Qualifications Eligibility Requirements: A master’s degree equivalent to a Norwegian master’s degree (120 ECTS). Documented proficiency in English (Nordic applicants may submit their high school diploma as documentation). Applicants with a strong background in STEM fields (e.g., electrical power engineering, control system engineering, physics or environmental engineering, mathematics (Operations research) or computer science or machine learning). The master’s thesis must be included in the application. Some of the teaching duties are in Norwegian language. Documented level of Norwegian or Scandinavian language skills at minimum B2 level are required. Ideal Candidate: Ability to collaborate and work effectively in an international and interdisciplinary research environment. Demonstrates experience or strong interest in modelling, programming, systems thinking, and qualitative/quantitative research methods. Documented programming experience for example GitHub project on MATLAB, Python, Julia, Javascript. Experience in mathematical modeling, control engineering, and optimization is a distinctive advantage. Possesses a strong academic record, with relevant experience in either industry or academia. Has prior professional experience and a solid understanding of workplace responsibilities and expectations, which will be considered a key advantage. Shows a deep interest in interdisciplinary research, is capable of independent work, and actively engages with the supervision team to foster collaborative research. The project proposal will be included in the assessment of the applicant’s competence. The final project description and work plan will be prepared in consultation with the supervisor(s) during the first three months of the employment period. Learning is integrated into network control to support decisions about scheduling, routing and resource allocation. For example, an urgent clinical alert should reach its destination promptly even when links are congested and patients are moving. The project also develops distributed and federated learning methods that adapt to connectivity, available resources and clinical priorities. Network control and distributed learning are designed together, so that the network supports learning and learning remains effective when communication is constrained. The methods are evaluated in remote patient monitoring and hospital-at-home scenarios. This position focuses on network protocols and their control at the MAC, network, transport and cross-layer levels, combined with machine learning. It does not cover hardware, antennas, circuits or physical-layer signal processing, and is not a general data-science position. Applicants must document relevant computer-networking knowledge and experience. Research areas Learning-based network control, including scheduling, link selection, routing and resource allocation in wireless and edge networks. Reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning for distributed network decision-making. Graph and hypergraph representation learning of network state, including temporal graph neural networks. Network- and urgency-aware distributed and federated learning, adapting the exchange of data and model updates to network conditions and clinical priorities. Evaluation through network simulation and emulation, and with real remote patient monitoring data. Resonsibilities Develop and evaluate learning-based methods for urgency-aware network control and network-aware distributed learning. Implement and test the methods using network simulation or emulation and real monitoring data. Publish in leading networking and machine-learning venues and complete a PhD at the University of Oslo, Faculty of Medicine. Coursework or project experience in machine learning, and good programming skills in Python. A weighted average grade of B or better on the master’s degree, as required by the University of Oslo. A master’s thesis graded B or better (Norwegian grading scale or equivalent). Preferred qualifications Experience with reinforcement learning or graph neural networks. Experience with network simulation or emulation tools, such as ns-3, OMNeT++ or Mininet. Publications or a master’s thesis combining networking and machine learning. Language Requirements Applicants who are not proficient in a Scandinavian language must document English proficiency through one of the following: TOEFL: at least 600 (paper-based) or 92 (internet-based); IELTS Academic: at least 6.5, with no section below 5.5; Cambridge CAE/CPE: grade A or B. items.title: PhD Student/ Research Assistant (f/m/d)
items.desc: The Chair for Embedded Systems (CES) at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT) invites applications for a Doctoral Researcher (f/m/d) position on Adaptive, Secure, and Energy-Efficient Edge AI Processors . The position aims to develop an adaptive Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and to integrate it into a complete System-on-Chip (SoC) platform for efficient, reliable, and secure edge AI. A central challenge is to exploit runtime-configurable precision, approximate computing, and early-exit inference to meet strict energy, performance, real-time, and security requirements. The research spans hardware architecture, FPGA prototyping, ASIC implementation, hardware/software co-design, and system-level execution. Research Focus The successful candidate will contribute to research in the following interconnected areas: Adaptive NPU architectures – runtime-configurable processing elements, systolic arrays, mixed-precision data paths, approximate arithmetic, and reliability monitoring. SoC integration, FPGA and ASIC design – RISC-V-based SoC integration, RTL design and verification, FPGA prototyping, system bring-up, PPA evaluation, technology-aware optimization, and post-silicon validation. Cross-layer hardware/software optimization – joint exploration of hardware and neural-network parameters, dynamic precision and approximation, early-exit execution, workload mapping, scheduling, and energy-aware runtime management. Hardware security and trusted execution – security monitoring, hardware roots of trust, measured boot, platform attestation, memory isolation, and protection against side-channel attacks. Personal Qualifications A very good Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. A background or strong interest in FPGA/ASIC design and hardware/software co-design , ideally complemented by knowledge of computer architecture, embedded systems, edge AI, real-time systems, or hardware security. Experience with C/C++, Python, RTL design (Verilog/VHDL/SystemVerilog), Linux, or hardware design and simulation tools is advantageous. Strong motivation for independent research, teamwork, and fluent written and spoken English. Starting Date Expected from January 2027. Application Process Please send your application, including a cover letter, CV, and copies of relevant certificates and academic transcripts, to henkel@kit.edu with the following email subject line: Application for NPU Researcher Position – Last Name, First Name We encourage applications from candidates of diverse backgrounds. Recognized severely disabled applicants will be given preference if equally qualified.

items.title: Doctoral student in equitable AI for breast cancer screening and risk prediction
items.desc: Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The doctoral student will be based at the Department of Oncology-Pathology, Karolinska Institutet, within the Computational Breast Imaging Group led by Associate Professor Fredrik Strand. The group is internationally recognized for the development and evaluation of AI for breast cancer imaging and precision medicine, combining expertise in radiology, machine learning, and biostatistics. It comprises PhD students, research engineers, research assistants, postdoctoral researchers, and collaborating senior clinicians in radiology, pathology, oncology, and surgery. The group has active national collaborations (KTH, Lund University, the Institute for Future Studies, and several groups at KI) and international collaborations (among others UC Berkeley, UCSF, University of Hawaii, and University of Barcelona). Available infrastructure includes high-performance computing, GDPR-compliant secure storage, and the VAI.B platform, which holds multi-region Swedish screening mammography data linked to cancer outcomes. The doctoral student will be supervised by Apostolia Tsirikoglou, PhD, research specialist and lead AI scientist in the group, as main supervisor, together with Associate Professor Fredrik Strand, head of the group and principal investigator of the project, as co-supervisor. The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student This PhD project investigates whether AI systems used in population-based mammography screening perform equitably across population groups, and how inequities can be reduced. AI is entering breast cancer screening both as detection support and as risk prediction to guide screening intervals and supplemental imaging. Systems developed on specific populations may perform differently for groups that were underrepresented in their development, and screening outcomes already differ by country of birth and socioeconomic status. Evidence on equitable performance is therefore needed before AI is adopted at scale. The project uses a large multi-region Swedish screening dataset with radiologist assessments, cancer outcomes from the National Quality Register for Breast Cancer, and demographic and socioeconomic data from Statistics Sweden. The doctoral student will evaluate commercial and in-house AI cancer detection systems and AI risk prediction models across subgroups defined by country of birth and socioeconomic status, compare AI with radiologist performance in the same groups, and, in a later phase, develop and evaluate fairness-aware models that reduce identified disparities while maintaining clinical performance. The doctoral student is expected to take an active and increasingly independent role in study design, cohort construction and register linkage, statistical analysis, running and evaluating AI systems on imaging data, model development, writing scientific publications, and presenting results at international conferences. The doctoral education includes courses in epidemiology, biostatistics, machine learning, and AI fairness. Where needed, competence in deep learning model development will be built during the project under supervision. What do we offer? A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. Eligibility requirements for doctoral education In order to participate in the selection for a doctoral position, you must meet the following general (A) and specific (B) eligibility requirements at latest by the application deadline. It is your responsibility to certify eligibility by following the instructions on the web page Entry requirements (eligibility) for doctoral education. A) General eligibility requirement You meet the general eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you: have been awarded a second-cycle/advanced/master qualification (i.e. master degree), or have satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the advanced/second-cycle/master level, or have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.* Follow the instructions on the web page Entry requirements (eligibility) for doctoral education. *If you claim equivalent knowledge, follow the instructions on the web page Assessing equivalent knowledge for general eligibility for doctoral education. B) Specific eligibility requirement You meet the specific eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you: - Show proficiency in English equivalent to the course English B/English 6 at Swedish upper secondary school. Follow the instructions on the web page English language requirements for doctoral education. Verification of your documents Karolinska Institutet checks the authenticity of your documents. Karolinska Institutet reserves the right to revoke admission if supporting documents are discovered to be fraudulent. Submission of false documents is a violation of Swedish law and is considered grounds for legal action. (A) and (B) can only be certified by the documentation requirement for doctoral education. Skills and personal qualities Necessary: A master's degree (or equivalent) in bioinformatics, biostatistics, or a related quantitative field Programming skills for data processing and analysis Knowledge of statistical and epidemiological methods Strong analytical ability and interest in interdisciplinary research at the intersection of AI, medicine, and health equity Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team Excellent written and spoken English Desirable/advantageous: Experience with population-based register data and record linkage, preferably Swedish national registers Experience with cohort construction and subgroup analyses in large health datasets Experience with large-scale processing of medical imaging data or evaluation of AI systems on clinical data Interest in health equity, fairness in AI, and responsible implementation of AI in healthcare Terms and conditions The doctoral student will be employed on a doctoral studentship maximum 4 years full-time. Application process Submit your application and supporting documents through the Varbi recruitment system. Use the button in the top right corner and follow the instructions. We prefer that your application is written in English, but you can also apply in Swedish. Your application must contain the following documents: - A personal letter and a curriculum vitae - Degree projects and previous publications, if any - Any other documentation showing the desirable skills and personal qualities described above - Documents certifying your general eligibility (see A above) - Documents certifying your specific eligibility (see B above) Selection A selection will be made among eligible applicants on the basis of the ability to benefit from doctoral education. The qualifications of the applicants will be evaluated on an overall basis. Karolinska Institutet uses the following bases of assessment: - Documented subject knowledge of relevance to the area of research - Analytical skill - Other documented knowledge or experience that may be relevant to doctoral studies in the subject. All applicants will be informed when the recruitment is completed. KI applies a salary scale when setting salaries for doctoral students. Apply at the latest 17th November . Die Bereitschaft zur akademischen Qualifikation wird vorausgesetzt. Die Stelle ist grundsätzlich teilzeitgeeignet. Die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik am Institut für Informatik der TU Clausthal forscht im Bereich des modernen Hardware-Entwurfs, mit dem Ziel leistungsfähiger sowie energie- und ressourceneffizienter Rechnersysteme. Einen Schwerpunkt bildet die Prozessorentwicklung, von Erweiterungen der offenen RISC-V-Architektur bis zu neuartigen Prozessorkonzepten. Weitere Themen sind Hardware für neuronale Netze und Approximate Computing. Unsere Forschung umfasst die gesamte Designkette von der Logiksynthese bis zur Implementierung auf FPGAs; dabei nutzen und erweitern wir moderne Hardwarebeschreibungssprachen wie Chisel und Clash. Sie interessieren sich für Rechnerarchitektur und Hardwareentwurf und möchten promovieren? Dann unterstützen Sie die Arbeitsgruppe Technische Informatik in einem der folgenden Themenbereiche: Prozessorentwicklung: Die Arbeitsgruppe forscht an RISC-V Prozessoren und deren Erweiterungen sowie an neuartigen Prozessorarchitekturen, die ohne klassische Register auskommen. items.title: PhD scholarship in computational modelling of protein and nutrient bioavailability of microbial foods - BRIGHT
items.loc: Kongens Lyngby, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
items.desc: Job Description Are you fascinated by how the food we eat shapes our microbiome and metabolic health? Excited by the prospect of determining how nutritious are microbial foods? Eager to work in a cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research environment tackling major food-system challenges? Then join us as our new PhD Student in computational modelling of protein and nutrient bioavailability of microbial foods! This position sits within BRIGHT’s Microbial Foods mission. You will help developing computational tools to predict the nutritional value of alternative proteins and nutrients. Our goal is to predict how well a protein or microbial food is digested, absorbed and assimilated in humans, so that foodstuffs can be tailored for a nutritious and sustainable diet without compromising taste and texture. You will build the computational model at the heart of our mission, combining protein language model embeddings with nutritional composition, proteomics and metabolomics data into a multi-modal AI/ML system that predicts digestibility and bioavailability of proteins as well as the bioavailability of micronutrients and food-derived bioactives. The position is fully computational, and you will work with a talented team of scientists generating the in vitro and clinical data that will train and validate your model. Responsibilities And Qualifications Responsibilities: Review the state-of-the-art in protein bioavailability, covering digestion, absorption and assimilation, with a focus on microbial foods Build a multi-modal AI/ML model that predicts protein digestibility and bioavailability, combining protein language model embeddings with nutritional composition data and benchmarking against DIAAS and ileal digestibility datasets Create and curate a database of selected microbial foods, for example, Yarrowia lipolytica and Aspergillus spp. Model proteolytic digestion and the absorption of peptides and amino acids and small molecules including transporter-mediated uptake Test and refine the model against proteomics and metabolomics data for single microbial proteins and whole microbial cells Retrain the model with in vitro digestion data and with clinical trial data generated by our experimental partners Apply the model to the computational redesign of microbial foods for improved bioavailability, and release it as an open-source tool Report your research results in peer-reviewed scientific publications and international conferences Collaborate within BRIGHT as well as our local, national and international networks Disseminate your results through scientific publications, public engagement and social media Teach and supervise MSc and BSc students Qualifications: MSc in bioinformatics, computational biology, machine learning, computer science, food science or a related area Advanced programming experience in Python Experience with machine learning, including deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch Excellent English proficiency in written and oral form Excellent communication and social skills for working within an interdisciplinary research team Strong analytical skills and ability to work independently Preferred qualifications but not mandatory: Experience with protein language models or other sequence-based representation learning Familiarity with protein digestion, nutrition or food science, including metrics like DIAAS and PDCAAS Experience working with proteomics or metabolomics data Experience with data curation and building structured databases, and an interest in open-source software development You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education . We offer DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility. Salary and appointment terms The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures The period of employment is 3 years. The position is full time. The preferred starting date is 1st April 2027 (or sooner according to mutual agreement). You can read more about career paths at DTU here . Further information Further information may be obtained from Carlos Acevedo-Rocha: cargac@dtu.dk More information about BRIGHT: https://bright.dtu.dk/ If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark . Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “ PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar ” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include: A letter motivating the application (cover letter) Curriculum vitae Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale One letter of reference, with referee’s email and phone number You may apply prior to ob­tai­ning your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position. BRIGHT Mission 2: Microbial Foods BRIGHT Mission 2 aims to build an AI-powered framework for the rational design of microbial foods that meet four targets: consumer acceptance, health, sustainability and scalability. The first phase focuses on two fungal chassis, Aspergillus and Yarrowia, characterizing more than 500 prototypes through multi-omics, sensory analysis, life-cycle assessment and safety testing. Predictive models for flavor, texture, nutrition and process scale-up are trained iteratively through active learning. The scientific scope spans strain engineering, adaptive laboratory evolution, solid- and liquid-state fermentation, sensory and consumer research, and pre-clinical and clinical evaluation of safety, bioavailability and cardiometabolic health, in collaboration with national and international partners. BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829 DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

items.title: Thèse CIFRE: Réduction de modèle par deep learning pour la plasticité cristalline F/H
items.desc: EDF R&D, avec ses 2000 chercheurs, a pour missions principales de contribuer à l'amélioration de la performance des unités opérationnelles du groupe EDF, d'identifier et de préparer les relais de croissance à moyen et long termes. EDF R&D met en œuvre une politique volontariste de partenariat en France et à l’international notamment dans les pays où le Groupe est présent. Vous souhaitez associer mécanique des matériaux, simulation numérique et intelligence artificielle pour répondre à des enjeux industriels ? > Rejoignez EDF Recherche et Développement dans le cadre d’une thèse CIFRE consacrée à la réduction de modèle par apprentissage profond pour les calculs en plasticité cristalline. La poursuite de l’exploitation des centrales nucléaires au-delà de 60 ans nécessite des outils avancés pour justifier la tenue mécanique des composants. Pour les matériaux métalliques, leur comportement dépend notamment de la microstructure, c’est-à-dire de l’organisation des grains qui les constituent. Les simulations en plasticité cristalline permettent de représenter ces grains et leurs interactions pour mieux comprendre les déformations et les mécanismes de rupture. Elles restent toutefois coûteuses en temps de calcul, ce qui limite l’étude de microstructures et de sollicitations variées. L’objectif de cette thèse est de développer des modèles réduits fondés sur l’apprentissage profond pour accélérer ces simulations, tout en conservant une précision adaptée aux grandeurs étudiées et en respectant les lois physiques. Vos principales missions seront les suivantes : Étudier les méthodes de réduction de modèle et d’apprentissage profond adaptées à la plasticité cristalline. Constituer et exploiter des jeux de données issus de simulations de référence, couvrant différentes microstructures, propriétés des matériaux et sollicitations mécaniques. Développer des modèles capables de prédire les grandeurs mécaniques recherchées, en intégrant des contraintes physiques pour améliorer leur fiabilité. Comparer les approches en matière de précision, de coût de calcul et de capacité à traiter des configurations non utilisées pendant l’apprentissage. Appliquer les méthodes à des cas représentatifs des besoins industriels et valoriser les résultats dans des publications scientifiques. Deux pistes seront particulièrement explorées : des réseaux de neurones apprenant directement la relation entre les données du problème et la réponse mécanique, et des approches hybrides associant réduction par projection et corrections non linéaires apprises. Principalement numérique, cette thèse se situe à l’interface entre mécanique des matériaux, mathématiques appliquées et apprentissage automatique. Elle contribuera au développement d’outils plus rapides pour comprendre le comportement des matériaux à l’échelle de leur microstructure. Poste basé sur le site EDF Lab Les Renardières à Moret sur Loing (77). Vous êtes titulaire, ou prochainement titulaire, d’un diplôme d’ingénieur ou d’un master bac +5 en mécanique, mathématiques appliquées ou calcul scientifique. Vous disposez de bonnes bases en méthodes numériques et en programmation scientifique, notamment en Python. Vous avez un intérêt marqué pour la mécanique des matériaux et l’apprentissage automatique. Une première expérience en simulation mécanique ou en apprentissage profond serait appréciée. Qualités attendues pour mener les travaux de thèse : Curiosité scientifique, Rigueur, Autonomie, Goût du travail en équipe, Sens de l'organisation (la thèse étant un projet de 3 ans). Vous savez présenter clairement vos résultats et disposez d’un niveau d’anglais vous permettant de lire et de rédiger des publications scientifiques. Le dossier de candidature doit comporter : un curriculum vitae détaillé ; une lettre de motivation ; relevés de notes de votre diplôme de master ou d’ingénieur des années n, n-1 et n2 ; lettres de recommandations et les noms, les coordonnées d’au moins deux personnes pouvant être contactées pour recommandation. Les avantages : Vous pourrez bénéficier des activités sociales de l’entreprise. Vous aurez une prime d’intéressement et une couverture sociale. Vous serez remboursé(e) de 75% de votre abonnement de transport en Ile de France. La diversité alimente notre performance. Dans le groupe EDF, accueillir des personnes en situation de handicap fait partie de notre ADN. Notre objectif est d’ouvrir nos portes à toutes les compétences, toutes les énergies et toutes les personnalités sans exclusion. Le poste proposé est donc ouvert à toutes et à tous.

items.title: Ph.D. Candidate in Reinforcement Learning for Project Scheduling Problems
items.desc: About The Position Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? As a PhD Candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, in and outside academia. The position will specifically focus on Reinforcement Learning for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP). The Ph.D. candidate will be a member of the group of Civil Engineering and Geomatics at NTNU and will tightly cooperate with other Ph.D./post-docs in projects (such as HEU-CIRCULess) and research groups at the department. The Ph.D. position will offer opportunities to develop high-quality research within the field of digitalization of circular construction. Your immediate leader will be the Head of Department. Duties of the position Develop learning-based algorithms or methods for deterministic scheduling optimization problems with the aim of achieving competitive performance against state-of-the-art approaches. Extend the developed framework to scheduling under uncertainty. Investigate how the proposed learning-based methods can be extended to uncertain and dynamic project environments. Improve the scalability of learning-based scheduling methods and evaluate generalization, robustness, and computational performance. Disseminate research outcomes. Publications in relevant high quality peer-reviewed journals are needed. Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above Academic publications and popular science dissemination Participate in the research group Civil Engineering and Geomatics Research group Civil Engineering and Geomatics - NTNU Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment. Required Selection Criteria You must have a relevant master’s degree in Computer Science and technology, computer system engineering or equivalent. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Experience in reinforcement learning, GNN, etc. You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education. You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phiv Applicants must have fluent skills in both written and oral English. Non-English native speaker applicants who do not have master in Europe must provide evidence of good English language skills, written and spoken. The following tests can be used as such documentation: TOEFL, IELTS or Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) or Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE). Minimum scores are: TOEFL: 600 (paper-based test), 92 (Internet-based test); IELTS: 6.5, with no section lower than 5.5 (only Academic IELTS test accepted); CAE/CPE: grade B or A. In extraordinary circumstances, formal documentation of language skills can be relinquished. In such cases, the candidate’s language skills will be assessed in a personal interview. PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”. The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position. Preferred Selection Criteria Academic publication in relevant field. Experience in programming skills, and artificial intelligence. Personal characteristics To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: Work independently The applicant must be motivated to work closely with teams and external partners Work constructively under pressure or in the face of adversity Show curiosity and strong motivation for the subject Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities. We offer An exciting job with an important mission in society Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues Working capital that can be used to implement the project Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK) Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2) As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits. Diversity Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. Salary and conditions In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,-per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. The employment period is 3 years for the doctoral work. For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Engineering https://www.ntnu.edu/studies/phiv within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment. As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them. For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis. The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed. About The Application The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English. Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request. The Application Must Include Transcripts for Bachelor's and Master's degrees Diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees Copy of Master's thesis Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages) Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page) Possibly publications etc. other relevant research work Possibly certificates CV Names and contact information of three relevant referees If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation. When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates. NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission). General information A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted. If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply. If you have any questions about the position, please contact Yongping Liu (Associated professor), email yongping.liu@ntnu.no. If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR Advisor Kristine Rognlid Hagaseth, e-mail: kristine.r.hagaseth@ntnu.no. items.title: Doctoral Researcher, Space Physics, Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory
items.desc: The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles. We are now looking for a Doctoral Researcher to join us at the Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory (SGO), University of Oulu. SGO operates internationally recognized geophysical measurement networks and research infrastructures, supporting research on space weather, the near-Earth environment, and Arctic geophysics. The position is part of the SafeEarth research programme, funded by the Research Council of Finland. The doctoral researcher will contribute to improved understanding of the space weather phenomena and their impacts on critical technological infrastructure and society. About the job Space weather driven by solar activity can produce disturbances in the Earth's upper atmosphere and magnetic environment, creating natural hazards that are particularly pronounced at high latitudes. Understanding these processes is essential for improving resilience against space weather impacts on society and infrastructure. As a doctoral researcher, you will pursue postgraduate studies leading to a doctoral degree while advancing your own doctoral thesis within the SafeEarth research programme. The successful candidate will be based at the University of Oulu's Linnanmaa campus in Oulu, Finland. In this position, you will be expected to: analyse observations from the Sodankylä Geophysical Observatory's measurement networks, with a particular focus on auroral imaging data and related geophysical observations study the physical processes linking aurora and space weather impacts in the near-Earth environment contribute to the development of new scientific understanding of natural hazards associated with space weather and their implications for society publish research results in international scientific journals and present your work at conferences collaborate with researchers across the multidisciplinary SafeEarth consortium and participate in other activities of the research group What we offer We offer you a supportive academic environment in a community of committed scholars with whom you can share your expertise and grow as an expert. Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture, and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits. Development and career options of the big organization. Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us. Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and your close ones in settling into Oulu. We have an HR Excellence in Research -quality label, which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers. Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, an excellent education system, and a competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu. Who are you? To succeed in this position, we expect you to have: A degree in space physics, physics, astronomy, atmospheric sciences, data science, geophysics, or another relevant field. Applicants should meet the admission requirements of the University of Oulu Graduate School (UniOGS) by the beginning of their doctoral studies. A strong interest in space weather, the upper atmosphere, auroral phenomena, or geomagnetic disturbances. items.title: PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials
items.desc: Empa 100% Académique: Doctorant Zürich & Schaffhouse Description Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain. The Laboratory for Acoustics/Noise Control is an international team of scientists and engineers active in the fields of vibroacoustics, environmental acoustics, and psychoacoustics. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements. Mechanical waves and vibrations are traditionally controlled using linear devices with fixed properties. In this PhD project, the student will explore a new generation of nonlinear resonators whose dynamic behaviour changes with vibration amplitude, enabling functionalities that are not achievable with conventional designs. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. The goal is to develop efficient models and design rules for nonlinear metamaterials capable of adaptive vibration isolation, frequency conversion, and non-reciprocal wave propagation. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative Swiss-French project involving Empa, ETH Zurich, and LAUM. PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials Your tasks As doctoral candidate within this project you will work on highly nonlinear building blocks for vibrational metamaterials. Specific tasks to achieve the challenging results include Develop analytical and numerical models for strongly nonlinear resonators exhibiting nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia effects. Design, simulate, and optimize novel resonator concepts based on inertia amplification, bilinear stiffness, and multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics. Manufacture and experimentally characterize resonator prototypes using vibration testing, laser vibrometry, and modal analysis techniques. Investigate nonlinear phenomena such as internal resonances, frequency conversion, bifurcations, and nonlinear energy transfer. Create reduced-order models and efficient simulation tools for the design of nonlinear metamaterials and wave-control devices. Disseminate research results through publications in leading journals, presentations at international conferences, and collaboration with project partners at ETH Zurich and the Université du Mans. Your profile If You Recognize Yourself In The Story Below, Then You Have The Profile That Fits The Project And The Research Group I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics, obtained no longer than four years ago and performed above average in comparison to my peers. I am proficient in written and spoken English. During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some experience with at least one of the following: structural and/or nonlinear dynamics, numerical modelling techniques (finite element method), or experimental methods in acoustics. I have a profound interest for these topics. As a researcher I perform research in a structured and scientifically sound manner. I read technical papers, understand the nuances between different theories and implement and improve methodologies myself. In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors which steer the direction of my research. It's important for me to work as an active team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and being inspired by my colleagues. During my PhD I want to grow towards more independence, e.g. representing the research group on project meetings and conferences. I see these events as an occasion to disseminate my work to an audience of international experts and research colleagues, and to learn about the larger context of my research and the research project. Our offer We offer a fully funded 4-year PhD position at Empa. The candidate will also be enrolled as a PhD student at the ETH Zürich, co-supervised by Dr. Paolo Tiso. The core of the PhD project will be conducted at Empa with at least one research secondment in Le Mans and intense collaboration with the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETHZ. Besides ample occasions to develop yourself in a scientific and/or industrial direction offered by the research group, further doctoral training for PhD candidates is provided in the framework of the Doctoral School. Starting date is February 2027 or upon mutual agreement. You stay in a vibrant environment centrally in Europe. Empa has its main campus in Dübendorf, located close to Zürich and 20 minutes by tram from Zurich International Airport. Zurich is one of the cities with the highest quality of life worldwide, welcoming to non-German speaking people and with ample opportunities for social, cultural, and outdoor activities. We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.
